## 2. Trust model and threat model

### 2.1 Purpose and scope

This section sets the adversary model, trust boundaries, server visibility, key custody, the "private from us" statement and metadata list, and invariants I-1..I-20 for every section; §5-§18 own mechanisms, §21 abuse, §22 tests.

### 2.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-TRUST-1 | Storage and the sequencer hold no group secret or key | PLAN.md:221 |
| R-TRUST-2 | Servers see only ciphertext and published small header values, except D-SMTP-19's report and role-mail intake (mx-4; D-TRUST-4); "end-to-end encrypted" comes with a malicious-server threat model and the unaudited-cryptography disclosure | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:745, :927-933; owner directive; [owner decision 119](#od-119) |
| R-TRUST-3 | Signed membership stops a breached server from adding a reader | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:745; [owner decision 3](#od-3) |
| R-TRUST-4 | TLS keys stay in the listening sidecar; tlsedge never terminates | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:699; X1 |
| R-TRUST-5 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges and exit only through customer exits; sidecar-bound agent tokens last ≤1 h and stay out of agents' environments | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:689; sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:139; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |
| R-TRUST-6 | Untrusted content cuts egress. New recipients need approval. One switch revokes reach | sidecar/design/improve.md:126-127; sidecar/design/pitch5.html:729 |
| R-TRUST-7 | Admins see actions, not transcripts; session contents open only when shared, while in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates by default; authors see admin reads | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:640; owner decisions [126](#od-126), [170](#od-170) |
| R-TRUST-8 | Client tokens never administer networks. Revocation is forward-only | [R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md) §3 item 3; PLAN.md:327 |

### 2.3 What exists today

- **Encryption.** connect defaults to Off (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:788), the sdk to Opportunistic (sdk/device_local_provider.go:258), and ControlId traffic is never encrypted (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:3671-3686).
- **AUTHZ1** (§7.3): on non-Embed networks any client token mints a network login through `/auth/code-create`, and same-user processes read the network credential in `.auth_state` (sdk/local_state_auth.go:28-36) and in the extension's `chrome.storage.local` (extension/src/background/index.ts:134).
- **Missing:** members, signed membership, customer keys, a metadata list, and ur.network's DS, CAA and SPF records (dig, 2026-11-03).

### 2.4 Assets and boundaries

Assets: content (files, sessions, mail, burner logins), keys and credentials, authority (config repo, approvals, record), names, metadata, shared reputation, availability.

```text
TB1 device:  sidecar daemon (keys, plaintext), harness and agents as one OS user (owner decision 47);
             an app's VPN component, a network process, with only forwarding's keys and the config's
             contents (owner decision 197; §18.6);
             for a cloud agent (owner decision 49), the sandbox operator (the VM host, its snapshot store
             and its egress proxy), whose VM snapshot holds the keys and whose TLS-terminating proxy would
             see service tokens, is inside the device boundary, like the OS;
             web: script running in a decrypting page's origin, Cloudflare's altered page script included,
             is inside the plaintext boundary (EX7); keys and tokens stay in §18.8's key origin, which is
             served direct (owner decision 211);
             the daemon stops tool misuse, not same-user reads; other users and the LAN are outside
TB2 members: trusted for granted content; admins admit alone and change authority under k of n
             (owner decision 110), but add no reader to a member's owner-bound repos without that
             member's consent (owner decision 126); admin vs author key domain (X20); a member whose
             device is designated as a network-scope search indexer sees the queries members' phones
             send it over the team repos it answers, as an owner's indexer sees those over a repo the
             owner shared (owner decisions 175, 178); no device is designated by default (owner
             decision 177)
TB3 servers: behind connect e2e (I-3); untrusted for content and authority
outside:     CAs, CT logs and search, DoH resolvers, IP-listing feeds, mailbox providers, Stripe,
             APNs/FCM, model providers, other tenants (§2.8 ext-*)
```

### 2.5 Server visibility matrix

| Service (§2.8 rows) | Where encryption ends; what stays sealed |
|---|---|
| connect, tlsedge, certs (connect-*, tls-*, cert-*) | At each sidecar (I-3, X1) |
| smtpedge, mxedge (smtp-*, mx-*) | At the destination MX or the receiver (X6, X7); mx-4 excepted (§2.8's statement) |
| evs, gkm (evs-*, gkm-*) | On readers' devices; names, contents, keys; gkm sees members and wrap recipients as sidecar ids (owner decisions [72](#od-72), [114](#od-114), [115](#od-115), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) |
| api, sockets, dns (api-*, sock-*, dns-*) | No content passes; policy text and internal names stay sealed (owner decisions [67](#od-67), [72](#od-72)); DNS records are public |

### 2.6 Key custody

| Key | Holder | Who can misuse it |
|---|---|---|
| ClientKey, identity and local root keys; tokens, auth codes | Device keychain (§5); device files; a browser's key origin (§18.8) | Holder, same-user agents and a cloud agent's sandbox operator; tokens administer until the P0's stages (§7.4) |
| AdminSet (Owner, Admin, Network and IT admin), approval, presence and recovery keys | Holders' devices (§7, §16); recovery codes offline ([owner decision 62](#od-62)) | Holder; authority statements need k signers, target excluded, k = 1 when n ≤ 2 ([owner decision 110](#od-110)); a recovery code counts as one of k after a vetoable 72 h ([owner decision 127](#od-127)) and admits its member's devices, with an admin cosign when `self_admit` is off, and under a binding the compromise cascade restored only after that vetoable 72 h ([owner decision 149](#od-149); §7.9) |
| MLS secrets, repo and path keys, the socket-name key | Readers' devices; agents', and in the config and team directory groups member devices past a network's first 1,000, by X-Wing wraps (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182); §10); each member's recovery key by RecoveryWraps ([owner decision 62](#od-62)); wraps as ciphertext | Readers; every admitted sidecar, agents included, reads the config's policy, AdminSet, the emails policy names, `K_sock` and share signers' seeds (owner decisions [6](#od-6), [67](#od-67); below), and in a team the directory ([owner decision 171](#od-171)); removed readers for generations held and path tokens until rotation (evs-11); holders of a Delegation's reader key (its agents, reaped ones and ephemeral ones past their own `not_after` included, and copies of its auth key) until the key drops (§10.5 lists when), and a copy of the whole auth key, which holds the signing seed, admitting fresh agents, each with its own wraps once the key has dropped, until the Delegation ends (§7.9's delegation row); a recovery code's holder with its member's login or the operator's help, for every generation wrapped to it, at once and whatever the window or a veto, until `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` or a cascade void of its binding (§7.9) |
| An app's forwarding key, forwarding reader key and forwarding clients' keys (§5.5, §18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)) | Its VPN component's own store (§5.9), generated there and never exported | That process, or a compromise of it: forwarding as its sidecar through that sidecar's grants, and the config generations wrapped to its reader key, until its forwarding Delegation ends at a `DelegationRevoke`, a newer one or its sidecar's revocation (§7.9); never mail, another evs repo, an MLS leaf secret, or the sidecar's identity, client, reader or recovery keys |
| A bridge share's ShareKey, ShareSigner seeds and table key K (§17.9) | The ShareKey in the accepting network's approving admin's owner-bound `secret`; each config generation's seed in its `BridgeShareSigner` config file; K in the sharing network's config (`bridge/share-grant/`), so every reader of that config holds it, and with every holder of the invite's code | The secret's readers (§8.5), a removed one until the share is revoked; every config reader, agents included, one its network's policy denies too on an operator-minted contract (§8.11), a removed one until a later ShareCert reaches the host, at most 7 days (§2.10); K's holders read the share's sealed tables, never its traffic |
| TLS, DKIM and mail-host keys | Each listening, sending or receiving device (D-TLS-6, [owner decision 36](#od-36), D-MAIL-4) | Holder; receivers see their hosts' mail in transit |
| Platform keys: JWT, OAuth, key history, ACME, DNSSEC, registrar, platform mail, evs receipt MACs | api's issuer, certs, the dns edge, mxedge, evs, vault | Insiders or hijackers: tokens, EX1, EX2, EX6 and URnetwork's mail |
| Release signing keys | Offline two-person key over `SHA256SUMS`; code signing (§4.10); no GPG key, since no apt or yum repository ships ([owner decision 213](#od-213)) | Holders; the build pipeline |

### 2.7 Client-id-to-key binding and ghost members

The server creates client ids and serves their keys (`/key/<id>`, server/api/route_authz.go:248), so a malicious one could add a ghost peer, substitute a key at first contact, or pass off its own KeyPackage or external commit as a member's new device (RFC 9750 §8.4.3).

Mitigations (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [113](#od-113)): config-repo admissions chain to the genesis key that invites and auth keys carry (§7.9), so clients refuse underived peers, readers, rules and membership commits, leaving a breached server only denial or delay, within §2.8's exposure bound; `Hello` bindings and safety numbers stop first-contact substitution (EX5, EX6).

### 2.8 "Private from us"

Statement (D-TRUST-4): *URnetwork's servers never receive plaintext content or keys, in any mode, except `rpt.bringyour.com`'s report and role-mail listener, which terminates TLS, parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23), seals the raw bytes to the network mail key and persists no plaintext (mx-4, §14.8). They see the values listed below. URnetwork builds no prospective collection ([owner decision 93](#od-93)) but could be compelled to record these values from now on (§21.9).*

An active or compelled operator keeps:

- **EX1.** Certificates in URnetwork zones ([owner decision 39](#od-39)); CT watch (D-TRUST-6); CAA `accounturi` excludes Team custom domains in strong mode only (customer A and AAAA, or an ALIAS flattening only those), and a weak-mode custom host (a CNAME into an operator zone) stays exposed (§12.8); the canary probe that catches an ALIAS also flattening CAA is URnetwork's own (certs), the ordering desktops repeating only the walk, so against a compelled operator such an ALIAS is as exposed as weak mode, the CT watch (D-TLS-8) its remaining control.
- **EX2.** Forged TLSA, CAA, MX, DKIM or MTA-STS records in URnetwork-signed zones ([owner decision 69](#od-69)); zone watch (D-TRUST-9).
- **EX3.** Interception of inbound mail from senders validating neither DANE nor MTA-STS, undetected; labeled "opportunistic" unless REQUIRETLS or a listed enforcing operator makes it "validated" (owner decisions [98](#od-98), [135](#od-135); §15.5), a match mxedge can fake (§2.18); an operator listed only for MTA-STS makes burner mail "validated" though burner domains publish no policy; the operator list is an operator-reputation inference, and REQUIRETLS records only the final hop's requirement, never that URnetwork did not read the message (§15.5).
- **EX4.** A send the user allowed to an unauthenticated MX ([owner decision 38](#od-38)), labeled "readable by an active URnetwork edge".
- **EX5.** Trust on first use of a genesis key no invite or auth key carried ([owner decision 5](#od-5)); safety numbers, 60 decimal digits over the genesis's SHA-256 and the device's identity key, shown as 12 groups of 5 (§5.6's safety row; [owner decision 281](#od-281)); a code-only recovered device, which has no admitter, commits, wraps, seals or signs nothing until the config head its RecoveryWrap, or under a binding a cascade void restored the ReaderWrap it is given (§7.9's restored order), opens chains to a genesis its RecoveryBind's `genesis_sig` signs under the key its code derives (§7.9's anchor), so the recovery public keys every config reader and rotator holds let no server fake that genesis; a server can forge the wrap or the ReaderKey gkm serves, but not a head that chains to that genesis.
- **EX6.** connect key substitution at first contact until M2's admission check (§6.4); first-use pins.
- **EX7.** Code URnetwork ships: signed releases ([owner decision 77](#od-77)) and labeled decrypting web pages ([owner decision 76](#od-76)); undetected; any script in a decrypting page's origin reads views while it runs (§18.8). Cloudflare terminates https://ur.io, so it sees page requests and can alter page script, and through it request views while that script runs, never the key origin's code, key or token, since `sidecar.ur.io` is served direct (§19.5's W10; [owner decision 211](#od-211)). The key origin serves only a promoted build, whose loader and `sidecar.wasm` the release's signed `SHA256SUMS` lists, so anyone can compare the served bytes, though no browser checks them on load (§18.8; [owner decision 221](#od-221)). For `ur`, GitHub alone cannot ship a client, since `install.sh` checks the release against the offline key's signed sums, but ur.io serves both that script and its pin, so ur.io alone can ship one to a new script install, or hand it an older signed release; the script prints the key's fingerprint and the repository path that publishes it, for a user who compares (§4.10; [owner decision 264](#od-264)).
- **EX8.** URnetwork login as the `members` audience authority ([owner decision 42](#od-42)); undetected (§13.7).

**Exposure bound** ([owner decision 129](#od-129)): a writer learns of a withheld Remove at its first HeadCheck with a device that holds it, or with a peer that relays it as `proven` or `unverified` within 8 hops of a holder (D-TRUST-10, §6.4); with the withholding proof it stops at once, and without it the pin stays UNVERIFIED, so, as with no consistent witness, the writer stops sealing shared-group content at `ServiceSettings.witness_bound_hours` (default 72 h, 24-168 h). Exposure is unbounded across a split, where the server leaves no HeadCheck path of up to 8 hops between a holder and the writer, including when every device that holds the Remove is offline, and in own groups, where writers only alarm: personal networks, and with them the v0 pilot ([owner decision 102](#od-102)), have no bound.

**Also disclosed:**
- Burner linkability (§15.9).
- No fork detection without a shared pin.
- I-10's no-policy allow-all, in product copy too ([owner decision 120](#od-120)).
- §2.18's unaudited cryptography.
- A head reader's trust in evs for which writer-signed version, or a refused push's writer-signed entry that was never a version, is current at its first pin, for a path it never read or no longer remembers (its sealed read record evicted, or its pin past the budget; [owner decision 209](#od-209)) and, after a re-pin past §11.9's 4 MiB catch-up budget (shown as `verified since <time>`), for every path, HeadCheck confirming the pin, not those versions (§11.9).
- A shredded repo's statements and ciphertext in shared batches up to 26 h past key destruction (§11.12).
- P0 safety work runs at once whatever its volume ([owner decision 186](#od-186)), so a wave of it on one metadata cluster, legal within every network's rates, holds that cluster's evacuation from when it empties the write budget's bucket until the wave ends (§11.13; [owner decision 190](#od-190)): each bound in this list that rests on hourly evacuation, the 26 h ones, stretches meanwhile (§11.21).
- Erasure paced, at the storage limit or while spent, by each eraser's daily closure allowance, which §21 never cuts below its floor: an entry's own keys go at once, while its derived fields (`i/` entries and search-index copies) stay openable to their key holders, masked from search, for up to the wait §11.13 and §15.7 state from the erasure's closure bytes, not a fixed time per message, and longer while a ref's full erasure set holds back the erasure's CUT (§11.12's cut row); an erasure whose eraser's device is lost waits for another device that may finish it (§11.12's reconcile row; [owner decision 146](#od-146)).
- Versionless content (§11.7): a writer may turn versioning off for a path, except in config and mailcfg repos, on git-mode and creates-only refs and, through a repo admin's lock, in a locked repo, after which each replaced version's content is purged about a minute after its replacement (staged content with its batch, at most 26 h; evs-12), beyond recall, while its signed statement keeps its hash, padded size, time and signer; the setting shows the server which paths are versionless and which hold the search index ([owner decision 168](#od-168)); under a hold, versionless content that existed at placement stays until the hold ends.
- Dropped history (§11.7, §11.13): a repo admin may drop a path's history on a file-mode ref outside config and mailcfg repos, after a 7-day window in which any repo admin can cancel, or at once with `now`; in an owner-bound repo only its owner drops or cancels (owner decisions [126](#od-126), [183](#od-183)); each dropped version's statement keeps its hash, time and signer, and its content goes beyond recall; inline content stays as unserved ciphertext in packs until a later compaction, unscheduled ([owner decision 247](#od-247)), and in slot-keyed repos is unreadable at once; under a hold the content stays until the hold ends, while the drop reads, lists and bills as finished ([owner decision 184](#od-184)); deleted blocks persist on the drives until overwritten (evs-28).
- Search (§11.14, §16.10): no query or result reaches a server; an ephemeral sidecar's first sync of a repo's index and any device's fetch of a repo's all partition at "search more" show evs that and when the device searched, never what (desktops and indexers, syncing in the background, show neither); each opened hit, and each candidate `ur search --verify fetch` opens, is an ordinary document read, so their set shows evs a query-dependent access pattern (evs-26); an app host's "search more" that a designated indexer answers goes end to end to that device, which sees the query (another member's device only for team repos or a repo that member shared, the app naming that member first), while relays see when each search and page runs, in fixed sizes, connect's stored reports show each window's fixed floor rather than its pages, its contract rows a search's time only when the search fails over or re-establishes a session lost in the foreground, and evs sees nothing (connect-5; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [176](#od-176), [178](#od-178), [188](#od-188), [191](#od-191)).
- The team directory (§16.11): in a team network every admitted sidecar, agents and the audit reader included, reads each member's run titles, projects and branches unless the member opts out ([owner decision 170](#od-170)), and the name and description of every general and record repo unless its owner marks it private or revokes its announcement ([owner decision 181](#od-181)), a revocation hiding the name from honest readers at once and destroying its copies' keys once a directory admin's device runs its erasure request, so a modified reader can open them until then; at M6 an item's earlier announce entries stay readable to every admitted sidecar after its withdrawal or revocation, until their 30 days or a directory admin's erasure, since a stream takes creates only; evs learns per sidecar when its runs start, end and move, and per access request which requester asked which approvers' devices (evs-27).

Feedback (sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:11) and hosted models are out of scope.

**How the list moves** ([owner decision 252](#od-252)). The published file, `metadata_list.yml`, is the block below, byte for byte (§22.7): a row changes here, in a design-records fold, and `make metadata` copies it. A fold that adds a row adds, in the same commit, the row's `planned` line in `testdata/metadata/fields.yml`, at the milestone that first serves its value, since the row and its line are one fact; a new §4 id's evidence line in `check/` lands the same way. Ahead of a fold, a code track may add an owner-answered row's words to the file through an entry in `check/`'s list of additions that names the question holding the answer, and where no owner wording exists it marks the field `pending` in its metadata rows instead; when a fold writes the words here the entry leaves, the guard failing while the design and an entry both hold the line. So the public list is this block plus named owner additions, never a hand edit.

# Each row gives service, store (tables, Redis families, object families, logs or memory),
# sees, why, ttl, and owner: the section that designs the value and states its ttl. Withdrawn rows keep
# their ids so citations resolve. Public: this list ships in DESIGN.md on the public sidecar repo (owner
# decisions 117, 118; §4.11) as D-TRUST-4's versioned document.
# File cluster: evs and gkm keep all durable state as objects in unversioned buckets, with no Postgres rows
# (owner decision 2); Redis holds only rebuildable soft state and verified caches (owner decision 136: evs-8,
# evs-24, gkm-10, api-7's {acl_}e); no backup of key slots or wraps (owner decision 90); no off-site copy
# (owner decision 94); the metadata tier grows by whole clusters, never pools, each repo placed on one at
# its creation (owner decision 145; evs-25).
# Postgres: sidecar tables, with the network, user and client rows they name, go to their own daily off-site
# dump, kept 14 days, tables whose ttl here is at most 7 d excluded, so a row outlives its ttl, or its hold,
# by at most 14 d; tables that exist today also sit in the main dumps for about 4 months (ops-2, D-TRUST-7);
# the primary's physical working copies hold every table but the UNLOGGED edge records for at most 7 d (ops-2).
# Redis: sidecar families (§19.7) stay out of the rdb bundles (D-OPS-16); other families sit in them for
# about 8 months (ops-3).
# Holds (owner decision 133; api-14, evs-19): a preservation hold keeps one network's in-scope rows and
# objects that exist at placement until its kind's deadline: 90 d, renewable once, or 1 year for a §2258A
# report (api-14). Its scope is the network or 1 to 16 repo ids, server rows always held at the network
# (owner decision 527). TTL sweeps, GC, drop jobs and gkm's reconciler skip them, and copied_rows copies what
# drops or is overwritten on its own: rows of partitions that drop whole (tls-3, smtp-3, mx-2), connect-1's
# contract rows naming a client of the network (owner decision 529), the rows a network's or client's deletion
# removes, in its own transaction, the deletion reading as done (owner decision 526), and the in-scope Redis
# soft state existing at placement (evs-8's lease fields, gkm-10's acks); evs-7's and ops-1's 7-day logs stay
# outside every hold. It collects nothing new, and users' shredding (--now, the 7-day timer, per-entry erasure)
# always proceeds, a hold keeping only the ciphertext a shred leaves (§11.12); a drop is no user's shredding,
# and its deletions wait with no sign of the hold (owner decision 184; evs-19).
# gkm rows give §10.6's visible values, as owner decision 115 confirmed them.
connect-1:
  service: connect (relays, residents) and api's contract service
  store: transfer_contract, contract_close, contract_close_report (existing); the Redis contract-hole projection (existing)
  sees: source and destination client ids; contract ids; a relayed sidecar contract's payer_network_id, which its one INSERT sets (§20.6); ProvideMode (Network, Service, FriendsAndFamily); roles, principal, source subject and source network, the contract class (control or data; §6.4) and the subject's WindowDelegation (subject, window client and key, target, expiry, share, its signer, the subject's identity key or its forwarding Delegation's key, and a share's ShareCert with its config generation, ShareSigner key and expiry, §17.9), all sealed in every mode (C13); per-party close reports (client, contract, bytes and the time each was received, a checkpoint at each idle receive-sequence exit among them), which pair the two clients; the contract-hole projection's client pairs
  why: route, authorize, settle and meter transfers; issue Service only for Find-recorded pairs (§6.10.1), and control contracts only between two admitted sidecars of one network, neither revoked, parked nor suspended, for witnesses (§6.4, §8.10); debit relayed bytes (owner decision 10)
  ttl: contracts expire within 60 min; resolved ones go at the contract horizon, 35 to 91 d by its runtime control (server/model/contract_horizon_reaper.go, server.ContractRetention), from the partition cutover with their week; while the reaper is off, paid ones (shares) 7 d after payout and unpaid ones (Network, Service) at 300 d (server/model/subscription_model.go:47-52); a contract the reaper's keep rules hold stays until they clear; close-report evidence at the same horizon (server/db_contract_close_evidence_horizon.go); projection keys with their contract, and in ops-3's bundles; a hold's copy excepted (api-14), the horizon reaper, the close-evidence horizon and the weekly partition drops waiting only while a hold placed before their range's end has an unfinished copy (owner decision 529)
  owner: §6.10
connect-2:
  service: connect relays (residents)
  store: memory
  sees: per frame, the outer source and destination client ids, size, timing, sequence and acks; per-peer handshake certificates and public keys; sidecar payloads only as ciphertext (Required, I-3); ControlId frames unsealed (connect-4); for a same-network pair on P2P, which no network runs until SidecarProtocolSettings.EnablePeerP2p is turned on (default off; owner decision 296), relays see no frames of that pair, and the two sidecars learn each other's public addresses through ICE
  why: carry and acknowledge transfers; set up e2e sessions (§6.9)
  ttl: relay memory while in flight; no frame or dial record (§21.9)
  owner: §6.9
connect-3:
  service: lb, connect residents
  store: memory; network_client_connection and network_client_location (existing; server/db_migrations.go:603-615, :689-697)
  sees: client IP and port of each transport (H1 wss, H3, DNS-tunneled carriers); per transport, as for every client today, a row with client and connection ids, connect and disconnect times, the resident's host, service and block, a SHA-256 of the client's /29 or /56 under a fixed pepper (server/ip.go:84-97), its port, IP version and family intent, and the location and network type its address maps to
  why: carry the transport; connection state and location; the ephemeral reaper's disconnect time (api-4)
  ttl: addresses in memory while connected, never logged in the clear (I-13, R-OPS-4), the lb's access log holding no client address; rows until 8 h after disconnect (server/taskworker/work/network_client_work.go:93), and in ops-2's main dumps about 4 months; URnetwork can invert the hash, whose pepper never rotates
  owner: §19.8
connect-4:
  service: connect residents; api (sync routes, long-poll)
  store: Redis {scp_<clientId>} ver (hash), hint (stream, MAXLEN ~256) and n (counter); long-poll cursors in memory
  sees: per client, topic versions and hints for core, team, sock, tls, mail, dns, gkm, gkm:<group_id> and evs:<repo_id>, each hint at most 256 B of server-held ids, kinds and versions or client-sealed bytes, never content; PushReset (at most 48 versions); which client syncs which topic, and when; core, mail and tls versions are writers' clock times, and team's the authorization log position (§6.8's registry)
  why: real-time push (X8 (b), owner decision 17); resync after gaps (§6.8); an unsigned raise of core's minimum secure version is a denial under I-4, never stored state, which a device bounds by its own compiled version (§6.4; owner decision 295)
  ttl: Redis keys 1 h (EXPIRE 3600 NX), outside the Redis bundles (D-OPS-16); versions live in their owners' stores; a poll cursor for one 25 s hold
  owner: §6.8
connect-5:
  service: connect relays (residents) and api's contract service, for §11.14's remote search (owner decision 175)
  store: none new; what connect-2's relay memory and connect-1's contract rows and close reports hold for the Network contracts, both directions, between an app host and an indexer it asks
  sees: per frame, the app host's and the indexer's client ids, size, timing and acks, every search request a 4,016 B body and every reply the requester's steps times 16,384 B, failures after parsing included; so when each "search more" and each further page runs, how many pages a search takes, and how long the indexer took to answer; from connect-1, the pair's contracts and close reports as for any peer's, so api's retained rows show when a phone searched through an indexer and how many 20 KiB exchanges it took, the that and when evs-26 concedes for "search more" (owner decision 609, which reverses owner decisions 176, 188 and 191); never a query, term, filter, repo named, hit, snippet or result count, all sealed end to end (I-3, I-19)
  why: phones ask a designated indexer (owner decisions 175, 178) instead of downloading all partitions, which evs-26 would otherwise show
  ttl: relay memory while in flight (connect-2); contract rows and close reports as connect-1, at the contract horizon, 35 to 91 d, and at most 300 d while its reaper is off
  owner: §11.14
api-1:
  service: api
  store: account, sign-in and payment tables (existing); network_idp_identity
  sees: user id, verified email or phone, sign-in methods, IdP identities (idp_id, sub), payment methods and balances, tier, verification state (network_verified, §21.7), cached as 0 or 1 in api-13's {sq_<network_id>}verified for 60 s with a 5 s in-process tier, Pro's two windows (ProCacheTtl, ProLocalCacheTtl)
  why: sign-in, SSO, billing; the verification gate for public names and internet mail (owner decision 96)
  ttl: the account's life; IdP identities until removed (§7.11); existing tables also sit in the main dumps about 4 months (ops-2)
  owner: §7.6
api-2:
  service: api, dns
  store: network (existing; network_name), network_name_reclaim (existing), network_team, dns_label
  sees: network_id, network_name and its reclaim tombstones; the opaque label and the opt-in alias (owner decision 14), each with kind and state (live, retiring, tombstoned), and dns_label.certified_time, set by certs when a chain naming the alias is issued or registered; team settings; the team's SCIM bearer's SHA-256, while SCIM is on
  why: naming and routing (§12.5); takeover protection (I-14)
  ttl: labels and aliases never deleted (tombstoned), a changed alias retiring 90 d first (D-DNS-10); released names held 24 h (§7.12); team settings for the network's life (§7.5)
  owner: §12.5
api-3:
  service: api
  store: network_member, network_invite, network_idp, network_domain, network_scim_change; Redis {address_<hash>} attempt histories (existing; the ones every Public route's limit uses, under POST /auth/sso-discover's own key prefix)
  sees: members (member_id, user, email, role, reauth_deadline, pending JIT state); invitations (hashed token, email, role, expiry); IdP configuration (issuer, client, vault-encrypted secret); verified domains (domain, TXT challenge, verification and daily check times), with each domain's acme_token, public in the customer's CNAME (§13.8's delegated DNS-01); SCIM changes awaiting an admin (Team v1); discovery attempts per caller address hash, for 10 minutes (POST /auth/sso-discover's per-address limit, 30 in 10 minutes, keyed by the address's peppered hash; no domain or address held); IdP sign-in flows in progress (state, nonce, PKCE verifier, IdP, network, the signed-in user that began one; 10 min, taken once)
  why: sign-in, roles and SSO (§7.5, §7.6); groups, tags, device names and admissions live only in the config repo (owner decision 46); discovery's limit bounds the IdP fetches a Public route makes api do
  ttl: members until removed; invitations until accepted or expired, at most 30 d; IdP rows until removed; domains, with their acme_token, while verified, dropped after 7 failed days; SCIM changes at most 7 d; discovery attempt histories 10 min, a family that exists today and so also sits in ops-3's bundles
  owner: §7.6
api-4:
  service: api; connect (contract gate); taskworker (the ephemeral reaper)
  store: network_client (existing), network_client_owner, network_client.acl_subject_client_id, network_client_lease; proxy_device_config (existing hosted mark)
  sees: each client's id, network, parent (source_client_id), device_spec, create and auth times; owner rows (owner user, member, sponsor, auth key, tagged, ephemeral, admin_refused, strict_exp, acl_enforcing, declares_no_egress, forward_only, and the 32-byte ClientKey public key that enrollment named, written once); acl_subject_client_id; each ephemeral client's lease (seen_time, its newest poll, written at most once per 300 s) and the SHA-256 of its close capability; the hosted-device mark
  why: enrollment and token refusal (§7.4), contract gates (§8.10), client counting (§20.8); reaping ephemeral clients by their newest disconnect (connect-3) and lease, or at once by a close beacon's capability (§18.8)
  ttl: the client's life (top-level clients deactivated after 30 idle days and deleted 30 days later, children after 30 days unseen, §5.3); ephemeral clients, with no connection open, 30-36 min after their last poll and 35-36 min after their last disconnect (a 35 min threshold checked every 60 s), or at once on a close beacon (§7.7, §18.8); owner and lease rows go with their client
  owner: §7.7
api-5:
  service: api
  store: sidecar_identity, sidecar_identity_binding
  sees: sidecar_id, network_id, identity public key and algorithm, status, create and revoke times; append-only bindings (generation, client_id, client public key, dual signatures, time); identity lookups (GET /sidecar/identity/<sidecar_id>, with its pages of older bindings, and GET /sidecar/identity?client_id=, caller and target; the internal POST /sidecar/identity/clients, by which gkm and other hosts without Postgres turn sidecar ids into client ids for §6.8's hints, logs no per-target record)
  why: durable identity across the reaper; peer binding checks (§5.5, §6.4); git committer resolution (owner decision 81)
  ttl: never reaped; deleted with their network; lookups only in ops-1's logs
  owner: §5.15
api-6:
  service: api; connect residents; owning services; the push sender (taskworker)
  store: sidecar_push_token (with slot, the Redis hash slot of the client's {scp_} tag, rev, the row's revision, and removed_time; a removed token's row kept as a tombstone); Redis {scp_<clientId>}tok, {scp_<clientId>}tokrev, {scp_<clientId>}ack, {scp_<clientId>}live, {scp_<clientId>}hb, {wake_<clientId>} counters, {wake_<sidecarId>}, {wakeq_<shard>}, {tokgen_<n>} (taskworker's 16,384 per-slot sentinels)
  sees: each client's APNs or FCM token and platform, its row's revision and, after the client's removal, when it was removed; per Redis hash slot, the run_id of the master that served it at its last reconcile; wake requests (POST /sidecar/wake, caller and target device of one member); whether a client's resident is live, and whether its stack acked each wake-class hint; whether an HTTP-only client polled in the last 300 s; wake triggers (client, topic, version, hint id, due time); per wake the platform, token, topic class (mail, team, evs, core) and version, send time and vendor result
  why: content-free phone wakes from v0 (owner decision 88; §18.7, §19.4); the liveness of HTTP-only hosts, whose poll marker gates the reaper's lease row (api-4; §6.8, §7.10)
  ttl: tokens until replaced, or removed by an empty POST, on APNs 410 or FCM UNREGISTERED or with their client, each removal leaving a tombstone row (client_id, rev, slot; no token) and its tokrev, kept while the client lives and deleted 24 h after its removal; live markers 90 s, poll markers 300 s; no wake event stored (§18.7); token projections while the token lives; sentinels with no TTL, compared by taskworker's 60 s pass and rewritten when it reconciles their slot, outside the rdb bundles (D-OPS-16); acks 1 h; counters and the hourly wake key at most 1 h, triggers dropped after 60 s, metrics by platform, topic and result only (§19.4)
  owner: §18.7
api-7:
  service: api (verifier, token exchange) and every gate (CreateContract, sockets, tlsedge, certs, dns, smtpedge, mxedge, evs, gkm)
  store: proj/<network_id>/<n>/_ and projrows/<network_id>/<sha256>/_ (the first metadata cluster); network_acl_head; Redis {acl_<networkId>}v, {acl_<networkId>}e (owner decision 136's verified read cache, n -> AuthEntry bytes from the newest base on) and {acl_<networkId>}q (the append limiter's counters; §7.9); while a site-loss restore runs, Redis {acl_<networkId>}r (members' devices' re-seed uploads and the resumed marker; §7.9, QD-724)
  sees: "the authorization log's signed id-only entries (position, chain digest, kind, time), whose base headers carry the config_version, config head hash, folded_through, rows hash, rows_byte_count and threshold, the repos whose key holders the base's own config head change shrinks, and each base header's tail verdicts (which of the entries since its fold took effect, and which completed a proposal); the network's Genesis (its network, config repo, owner member and sidecar, the owner's identity public key and time); and rows (members with roles and their recovery bindings newest first (key hash, reason) for the membership's life, sidecar admissions with identity keys, admission, revocation and park positions, the signer and position of each admission, AdmissionConfirm, OwnerConfirm, Delegation, recovery binding and key registration (§7.9's cascade), capabilities and each member device's live_since (the config leaf rank), member or opaque tag ids, ephemeral flags, expiry and sponsors, each admission's time (the time of the entry it took effect at), every confirmation's signer and position with whether it lifted a park, and the span each compromise cascade held a sidecar in P (from and until positions), Delegations' signing and reader public keys, tag ids, max_admits and admissions, expiry, key drops and ends, and a forwarding Delegation's sidecar and host client id and key (owner decision 197), with its reader key's digest and supersession position, never the key itself (owner decision 202), registered presence and SSH public keys with member and purpose, Team scope labels, open authority proposals with their signers, windows and kinds, the applied-id ring (the first 16 bytes of each applied statement's id with its position), each indexer designation folded into the projection rows while it holds, with its signer and position and its IndexerSet header's nonce, 16 random bytes the entry already shows (owner decision 634), and the id-level settings self_admit and scim_signer (owner decision 205)) and their AclRows (has_document; opaque tag and group atoms mapped to member and sidecar ids, an atom's id being 16 random bytes the config's sealed tables hold beside its name, derived from no key; a tag atom's owners as member ids (QD-172); derived atoms for the selectors no table names, each over a member, sidecar, client or network id, a role or a principal, values the server already holds, and a target naming a legacy client by its id (QD-170); rules with targets and, apart from them, via subjects (QD-764), actions, whether a rule limits ports (never which), socket token paths, during a K_sock rotation the previous key's beside the current key's until the head that clears the previous key, which links the two for as long as those rows are kept, at least 30 days (owner decision 334), public names, audiences, publish rules' application modes (http or raw) and raw link grants' client-certificate SPKI SHA-256, which a requested grant's GrantActivate also shows (§8.4, §13.7, §16.6), and expiries; request rules with approver atoms (autogroup:dst-owner among them) and counts, expiry bounds and evidence channels, and the document's default evidence channels for an action no request rule names; the Suspends a fold keeps (subject, suspend id, signer, its class and position), activated and revoked grant ids with the time each is kept until, an activated grant as a rule with its source rule's id (QD-079), and a share's grant with the other network as its source (owner decision 346); repos with kind, a general repo's group or admin inbox marker (QD-102), owner member, the owner's consented sidecar ids, folded access log with its versioning lock (its rules stay sealed), each repo admin's add position and a removed one's removal position until a later base drops it, the newest RepoDelete's entry time and signer, each EvsShare's signer, position and expiry, holders_shrunk_at and its time, and for each general repo every RepoPrefixRules entry (its position, time and signer, the generation its rules are sealed to and their padded length, 48 B and a multiple of 256 B; never a rule, a subject or a prefix; owner decision 345); BridgeRows egress modes and each approved route in force by its ids (route id, advertiser and the route rules it serves; QD-764); the audit reader and its AuditOptIn); statements with their types, headers (signer's pin, nonce, expiry) and signatures, presence countersignatures with evidence and act path: member admissions with their roles, Delegations, admissions by an admin and scoped admissions by a member's consented device or recovery key (owner decisions 112, 126), revocations (reason, and since_n for a compromise or a leak), OwnerConfirms and AdmissionConfirms, recovery bindings and rebinds as ids (member, signer, reason, the new and replaced recovery Ed25519 keys' hashes), the rest, X-Wing key and genesis signature included, sealed, authority proposals, cosigns and vetoes, recovery-signed ones, each with a recovery-signed statement's recovery Ed25519 public key in its Signed.key_id (§6.9), included (owner decision 127), grant activations and revocations, each activation showing its canonical action's kind, version and scope and the fields §16.8's server row lists, a requested dial or route grant's prefixes and ports only sealed (owner decisions 220, 457), suspensions and unsuspensions, EvsShares, repo access-log statements, SponsorSets, key registrations, each presence key's with the new key's own proof (its signature and WebAuthn evidence) and an empty attestation, since clients request attestation none, so no create ceremony's client data, authenticator model or vendor certificate chain (owner decision 608, which reverses owner decisions 455 and 553), indexer designations as ids (signer, subject, scope, retire; services sealed; owner decision 150), and bridge statements as ids (kind, signer, subject, rule id, expiry; an egress statement's mode and a withdrawal's, reset or drain; an approved route's advertiser and rules) with sealed bodies; ApprovalDeliveries as their signer, requester_sidecar_id and size, the decision or cancel they carry sealed to the requester (§16.8; owner decision 447); a team directory approval's grant only as its RepoGrant, EvsShare or GrantActivate, naming no request (§16.11); api's ticks: reaped ephemeral sidecar ids and activated proposal ids; admissions under a member outside its consented ids show its parked devices (owner decision 126); together, the reach graph; each network's newest position and statement and base counts per minute and day for the append limits; the config repo itself only as evs ciphertext; after a site loss, until the network's log resumes, each uploading sidecar's newest re-seed upload (the Signed Genesis, the entries and bases' rows it keeps, verbatim, or a phone's position and chain digest pins, all of it what the log itself shows), the order the uploads came in, the position the adopted run was written through, and the position of the base that resumed the log"
  why: one order for every authorization change; server gates without policy text or names, owner consent included (owner decisions 5, 72, 126; §7.9, §8.8); the cache, written only by api after each append and checked by readers against their pins, spares cluster reads and decides nothing; after a site loss, two members' uploads that reach different api instances adopt, and re-seed mode ends for each network at its resumed marker (§7.8, §19.10; QD-724)
  ttl: entries from §7.9's retention point, min(the previous base, the newest base's folded_through + 1), for the network's life, re-uploaded verbatim by devices after a site loss at unchanged positions (§7.9, §19.10); a network newer than both dumps at a Postgres restore takes the deleted-network path, its proj/ and projrows/ objects deleted with the last of its repos' shreds (§19.10); older entries, and rows no retained base names, 30 d after the newer base; network_acl_head with its network; {acl_}v 48 h after its last change; {acl_}e 10 min after the network's last append; {acl_}q 25 h; {acl_}r 24 h after its last write or the last token exchange that read its resumed marker, its uploads dropped when the network's resume base lands
  owner: §7.9
api-8:
  service: api
  store: network_admin_event, network_audit_webhook
  sees: admin events (per-network seq, actor, action, target, result, request id, hash chain; no client IP), DNS user and key writes included; the custom-certificate events of DESIGN-DETAILS 17.2.14, naming a host, a device and a time; SIEM webhook endpoints and deliveries; each webhook's signing key, HMAC-SHA256 of the vault resource network_audit_webhook_key over a fixed domain string and the webhook's id, answered once when the webhook is added and never stored

api-9:
  service: api; CreateContract
  store: network_acl_share, network_bridge_share
  sees: "invites (hashed 256-bit code, uses, 7-day window, inviting and accepting networks); bridge shares (share_id, both network ids, target and alias tables sealed under a key the code derives and the server cannot, versions, accept status: active, refused as too large or refused for no space, §17.9); the paying (dialing) network"

  service: api and the server gates (sockets, dns, certs, tlsedge, smtpedge)
  store: memory at the gate; approval_use; inside api-7's statements
  sees: server-gated ApprovalDecisions (format version, approval id, request hash, payload hash, decision, uses, expiry, approver member, evidence channel (device, presence or harness), SSHSIG, evidence hash, signer key, the requester sidecar id (the bearer's own) and the approver's projection pin) with the canonical action's kind, version and scope and the fields that gate already sees (host, port, audience, expiry, and a dns action's name, type, value and ttl), a requested dial or route grant's prefixes and ports only sealed (owner decision 220), each carried by a GrantActivate or presented with its action; ApprovalCancels (approval id, signer); per use, in approval_use, its index, effect key (a hash, the action's Idempotency-Key; none on a cancelled use), state (done or cancelled), result, time and the decision's expiry; run and agent ids, recipients and previews stay sealed

api-11:
  service: api (issuer auth.bringyour.com)
  store: network_auth_key, network_oauth_client, account_api_key (scopes, expiry, creator), auth_code (api_key_id), admin_token_use; Redis {dpop_<client_id>} (proof jti), {oauthdev_<device_code_sha256>} and {oauthuser_<user_code>} (device authorizations); Redis enrollment attempt histories; api's service log
  sees: auth keys (hashed secret, creator, tags, expiry, uses, ephemeral, pre-approved); network OAuth clients (hashed secret, scopes, creating member); API-key scopes, expiry and creator; token exchanges (client, subject client, sidecar, member, audience, scope such as repo:<id>:rw, projection version, act, the DPoP key); DPoP proofs' jti and key thumbprints; admin tokens (member, scopes, command digest, 1 h) and their uses (jti, member, command digest, result, time); edge logins for members audiences (member, network, published origin, time, nonce); device authorizations in progress (device code's SHA-256, user code, the ur-cli request with its DPoP key thumbprint and command digest, poll times, and once approved the user, network and sign-in time; 10 min, taken once); enrollment attempts per auth key and per caller address hash, for 10 minutes (§7.8's limits; keyed by the key's id and the address's peppered hash, no address held)
