  owner: §7.8
api-12:
  withdrawn: bridge rules, the overlay /16, LAN prefixes and port maps live in the config repo (owner decision 5); gates see api-7's ids and egress modes
api-13:
  service: api, taskworker; the edges (leases); evs (usage batches); CreateContract (relayed reservations); sockets and the other gate services with no database, which read limits and the over-limit list from api's internal gate routes (§8.9, §20.14; QD-055)
  store: transfer_balance.tier, network_sidecar_limit, network_quota_state, network_service_usage, service_debit_journal, service_usage_batch, stripe_meter_report (with version, attempts and next_time), team_subscription; Redis {sq_<network_id>} (rates, the connected_sidecar sorted set and the verified flag); Redis network_tier_versioned:<network_id> (the tier, cached 60 s); lease reservations, and relayed sidecar contracts' reservations made at CreateContract (§20.6), in escrow's per-balance Redis reservations (existing), and {escrow_<balance_id>}approx_floor
  sees: each network's tier; limit overrides (key, value, a reason citing an ops change or §21 case); quota state (stored bytes, storage_over, spent time); daily usage per network and meter (edge leases, evs transfer, relayed bytes, seats, the Team overages, and the transfer overage's helper rows team_credit_window and team_credit_running, which GET /network/usage hides; §20.9); debit journal rows (usage, balance, meter, bytes, batch, applied); usage batches (batch id, producer, window start, applied time); Stripe meter reports (network, meter, day, identifier, value, state, version, attempts, next send); each Team's Stripe subscription and customer ids, billing anchor, start and end (owner decision 199); rate counters, among them each erasing sidecar's closure bytes for the day (owner decision 146); every connected sidecar client, each marked client scored by its expiry ms and refreshed on the resident poll as {np_}connected is, counted by one ZCOUNT from now at enrollment and connect ({sq_<network_id>}connected_sidecar); each network's network_verified as 0 or 1 ({sq_<network_id>}verified); edge leases (network, meter, reservations of 64 MiB to 1 GiB, 16 to 256 MiB on Community); per relayed contract its reservation, grant and settled bytes; each balance's lowest credit shown in the last 2 min
  why: quotas, transfer-balance debits (owner decision 10), Team billing (owner decision 92; §20)
  ttl: counters 48 h, the connected set's key refreshed to 48 h at each write; the verified flag 60 s; tier cache 60 s; daily usage and meter reports 13 months; debit rows until applied; usage batches 24 h; overrides until lifted; quota state and Team subscription rows until their network is deleted; a lease's own reservation tokens 15 min, extended while it lives, and a carved debit's 24 h until its flush releases it (owner decision 517); relayed reservations until closed, settled or expired; a balance's shown floor 2 min, in ops-3's bundles as escrow's existing keys are
  owner: §20.14
api-14:
  service: api (abuse role), the taskworker abuse worker
  store: abuse_case, abuse_action, abuse_appeal, network_abuse_state, abuse_legal_hold (keyed by network, case and part), abuse_access_log, legal_request; the task tables pending_task and finished_task (existing), for each hold's end pass; the abuse and legal-request mailboxes' sealed copies, off site (§21.10); Redis {address_<hash>} attempt histories (existing; the ones every Public route's limit uses, under POST /abuse/report's own key prefix)
  sees: abuse cases (category, target host, label or network, join keys, reporter class, and a reported URL's path and query until the case's first review ends), actions (kills, halts, suspensions, cap tightening, and platform-wide breaker levels as rows with no network) and appeals with reviewers' reasons, with a reviewer id, the staff member's opaque id and never a customer's, on each read, review and appeal decision, and the legal and engineering ids that sign a production off; each network's standing; holds (network, case, part, kind, scope, which is the network or 1 to 16 repo ids, and place, report, renew and expire times) and their copied_rows and copy_state, the in-scope records that drop or are overwritten on their own, namely rows of partitions that drop whole (tls-3, smtp-3, mx-2), connect-1's contract and close rows naming a client of the network, copied at placement (owner decision 529), the api-1, api-4, api-5 and network_acl_head rows a network's or client's deletion removes, copied in that deletion's own transaction (owner decision 526), and the Redis soft state existing at placement (evs-8's lease fields, gkm-10's acks), never evs-7's or ops-1's 7-day logs, in parts of at most 16 MiB of compressed rows, part 0 the hold itself; for each hold it ends, its sweep pass's network, scope's repo ids and placement and end times in the pass's task rows (owner decision 206); legal requests (instrument, country, accounts, productions, sealing orders); every abuse-role read; reporters' third-party data only until the join, never a reporter's address or free text, of which only an appeal's own reason is stored (§21.8; owner decision 207); report attempts per caller address hash, for the window (POST /abuse/report's per-address limit, 30 an hour, keyed by the address's peppered /29 or /56 hash; no address held; owner decision 536); each action and lift, and each hold's placement, renewal and end, as it commits, MACed under a vault key and sealed to an HPKE key whose private half is kept offline before it leaves api or taskworker, and mailed to the abuse or the legal-request mailbox at one provider outside URnetwork's Postgres and clusters, which, as SES, sees only each record's sender, time and size (§21.10; owner decisions 208, 535)
  why: abuse handling, legal process and preservation (§21; owner decision 133); reviewers judge the page reported; a restore re-applies what the mailboxes hold (§19.10); the report limit bounds the cases a Public route opens
  ttl: "cases, actions and appeals 13 months after the case's last close (§21.10), a reported URL's path and query only until the case's first review ends, at most its review clock; legal requests, productions and the access log 3 years; holds, with their copied rows, until their kind's deadline: 90 d plus one 90 d renewal, or 1 year for a §2258A report (§21.9); a hold pass's task rows until the pass runs, then 24 h, or 7 d while its post retries, and in ops-2's main dumps about 4 months, as tables that exist today; the mailboxes' records, an action's kept as api-14's actions and a hold's until its expire_time; report attempt histories the window, 1 h, a family that exists today and so also sits in ops-3's bundles; standing only while current"
  owner: §21.10
api-15:
  service: api
  store: network_acl_ack
  sees: per client, the projection version it applied and when (POST /acl/ack)
  why: propagation targets and drift alarms (§8.9)
  ttl: 7 d
  owner: §8.9
sock-1:
  service: sockets
  store: Redis {sg_<network_id>_<h16(name)>} (listener fields m, r, i and e, and x, a removal's tombstone; version v) and its lease-ordered ZSET (suffix ix)
  sees: network_id; the name as a token path (16 B a segment, HMAC under a key from the config repo's K_sock, owner decision 67) or, for tls/, smtp/ and ur/, in plaintext; per listener the sealed name, client_id, listen_id, protocol, version, ALPN, application mode (http or raw), weight, max_streams, flags (exclusive, affinity, serving, draining), reported in-flight and issued counts, ejection state and its Signed claim (the sidecar's identity key); per tls/ listener the custom hosts and aliases it is certified for, and the names it holds an ACME claim for with the claim sequence; per lease the listener's sidecar_id, the authorization log position it was admitted at and the set_version of the page that wrote it; for 10 min after a removal for cause (60 s after an unlisten), the listener's client_id with the position and set version of the removal; the group version
  why: Find, scheduling and sampling (§9.5-§9.8); a tombstone refuses a later write admitted below the removal's position or from an older set
  ttl: 45 s lease renewed by heartbeat; ejections at most 300 s; tombstones 10 min after a removal for cause or the client's removal, 60 s after an unlisten; a K_sock rotation's dual registration, until rotated_at_ms + 10 min by each listener's clock, links old and new token paths; outside the Redis bundles (D-OPS-16)
  owner: §9.5
sock-2:
  service: sockets
  store: memory; per-dialer fields in sock-1's hash
  sees: each Find's dialer client, network and sidecar id, which its service token names (owner decision 588; edges add their K client ids and name no sidecar), token path or edge name, a dial's protocol, minimum version and offered ALPN ids, the server name of a dial that came by a custom host or an alias, affinity key (tlsedge's keyed /24 or /48 hash, never stored), the authorization log position that allowed it (§7.9), chosen listeners, grant id, issued tickets, a ur/ ticket naming its dialer's sidecar id for the listener's subject (owner decision 560), and the failed tickets a retry reports; each dialer's issued share and exclusions; reported accept timeouts; per-source registration and Find rates for the control-plane bound (memory; D-SOCK-15)
  why: admission, scheduling and outlier ejection (§9.6, §9.7)
  ttl: the request; tickets 30 s; dialer shares and exclusions at most 300 s; no per-dial record (D-SOCK-9)
  owner: §9.6
sock-3:
  service: sockets writes; CreateContract reads
  store: Redis {svc_<listener_client_id>}, keyed by the pair's non-edge end in every namespace, so {svc_<sidecar dialer client_id>} for a ur/ pair (owner decision 298)
  sees: Service-contract pairs, field the edge's platform client (the dialer, or for a ur/ pair the edge listener a sidecar dials), value the grant expiry; the authorization log position at which a listener's pairs were last removed, for 10 min
  why: CreateContract issues Service only for a pair Find recorded (§6.10.1, C9); the removal's floor refuses a pair written at an older position
  ttl: "the grant's expiry, at most 15 min past the listener's last accepted registration (ur/: its service's grant length, 60 min by default and 125 min for ur/smtpedge, refreshed per Find); deleted on revocation or the last edge unlisten, which does not reach a ur/ pair under its dialer's key, so that pair ends at its ttl; the floor 10 min"
  owner: §9.6
sock-4:
  service: sockets
  store: Redis {sn_<network_id>}names
  sees: a network's registered token paths and edge names, with sealed names, for listing; the authorization log position of the network's newest revocation sweep, for 30 s
  why: GET /socket/list; clients unseal names locally (owner decision 67); one process a network and position claims the sweep (§9.8)
  ttl: entries leave with their leases; the sweep's claim 30 s
  owner: §9.8
sock-5:
  service: sockets
  store: Redis {sc_<client_id>}set
  sees: a client's set_version and registered entries
  why: idempotent full-set calls; removal on the client's removal signal (§9.5, §9.8)
  ttl: 5 min after the client's last call
  owner: §9.8
evs-1:
  service: evs; gkm reads it
  store: repo/<repo> (metadata cluster)
  sees: repo_id; kind (general, record, config, team_record, mailcfg, vault, mailbox, secret; directory, one per team network); owner member of an owner-bound kind; state (keying, active, deleted, shredding, shredded, each with time, signer and deletion id); object format (1, or 2 from a repo's first push carrying a format-2 value, such as a versionless file or a DROP; §11.6); sealed display name; its network, from the projection, stored at creation and never changed, kept in the shredded tombstone (§11.12)
  why: lifecycle, kind rules, the lifecycle check every push reads, deletion and restore (owner decision 82)
  ttl: "the repo's life; a deleted repo, a repo of a network newer than both dumps at a Postgres restore included (§19.10), is shredded after 7 d, or at once with now, under a preservation hold too: slot/, then its gkm objects, {gka_} acks and recovery wraps, then every other object (a hold defers only this step, over unreadable ciphertext that evacuation still moves from shared batches into packs and parcels), none of which a fold, evacuation or gkm write that began earlier re-creates; then repo/<repo> becomes a shredded tombstone for the network's life (owner decision 133; §11.12)"
  owner: §11.8
evs-2:
  service: evs
  store: the ref_id inside head/, log/, idx/, pmap/ and pidx/ keys, pb/ records and {evsl_} lease fields; EvsPush fields
  sees: ref ids, HMAC-SHA256 of the ref name under a key from RK_1 (never names; guessable names testable by holders of RK_1, §11.5); each ref's kind (shared, owned, deposit), mode (git, file), owner sidecar_id and overlay base; deposit refs' ids, the first 16 B of SHA-256(repo_id ‖ sidecar_id), which name their depositor; the erasure ref's kind and id, the first 16 B of SHA-256 of a fixed label and repo_id (§11.6), which names that ref as the repo's erasure ref
  why: ownership and ref rules; record refs refuse FORCE and DELETE; git-mode refs commit only on their tip (owner decision 141; §11.8)
  ttl: as the ref's head and history (evs-3, evs-12, evs-14)
  owner: §11.6
evs-3:
  service: evs; taskworker writes evacuation fences (GC raises none; owner decision 203), source drops and collection windows (§11.6, §11.7, §11.13)
  store: head/<repo>/<ref> (metadata cluster); a verified copy in Redis {evsh_<repo_id>} for 10 min (evs-24); the host capability in a fresh single-ref read reply
  sees: "the commit point; version v, chain C_v, sealed ref name, whether the responding host supports EXACT_HEAD on a file-mode push, overlay base, whether a committed DELETE left it a tombstone (deleted), path epoch with its listed sources, any due epoch and a mapper's creation block with its end (block_until_ms); the authorization pin (AuthPin: projection version n and chain A_n, §7.9) and generation pin (group, generation, C_g) of the newest commit; a window of the last 64-127 versions' entries (push id, statement hash prefix, the batch place of its statement and payload, an 8-byte digest of its changed token paths, flags, one marking a push that replaced or removed versionless versions and one a DROP push; at most 255 while folds lag); the chain before the window, the newest folded version (folded_through) and the time of its last write; the fence counter, the writer's clock at the newest evacuation fence (fence_ms), and any seal lease; an ingester's CONSUME mark (consumed_through, the version through which its deposits are consumed: the highest at or below which its newest CONSUME found no unconsumed deposit, never falling), which a deposit's head in a push's answer or refusal repeats, so its depositor, a receipt-only reader included, learns beside its own version and chain when its deposits were ingested (§11.12); up to 8 refusal records, each a refused push id's first 8 bytes, its statement hash's first 2, the refusal's code and when the record lapses (until: the statement's time bound plus 1 s), and the writer's clock at the newest refusal fence (refused_ms); for a refused push that would have created its ref, a placeholder head at version 0 holding only those records, and for a ref that evacuation fences before its first commit, one holding only its fence and fence_ms (owner decision 203); on a ref holding a search index, its index_epoch, the version of its newest CUT (§11.12); the marker collection (EvsCollect: done, the removal version through which markers are collected; the latest window's through, its newest removal version, and until_ms, its end, 30 s after it opens; §11.7)"
  why: If-Match commits; readers trust only committed push ids; hints to subscribers (§11.8, §11.10); collection windows keep folds from writing over the markers taskworker is deleting, so no DELETE removes a newer entry (owner decision 148; §11.7); the DROP bit lets evs refuse pushes citing a version a drop in the window lists (owner decision 173; §11.8); refusal records keep a refusal true for every later attempt of its push id, however late it reaches evs (§11.8's outcomes); the index epoch refuses an index push built before an erasure's CUT (§11.12, §11.14)
  ttl: the ref's life, a DELETE leaving a tombstone head and a refused or fenced creation a placeholder head, which stays as a tombstone does; a refusal record until the first head write after it lapses; older versions page into log/ (evs-14); the host capability is computed for that reply only
  owner: §11.8
evs-4:
  service: evs; the segment cluster
  store: seg/<repo>/<segment_id> (segment cluster)
  sees: segment id (SHA-256 of its bytes), Padmé-padded size up to 8 MiB, 32 B public header (format, flags, repo_id, generation), uploader client and sidecar, upload time, whether it came as an erasure's closure upload (?closure=1); upload receipts (repo, segment id, padded size, upload time, uploader sidecar, whether its header is a kind-5 header), MAC'd by evs under its receipt key id, held by the client and returned with its push; the ranges each client reads, which for the search index's files show evs-26's view; kind-5 (versionless) segments, each one record of one version of one path, its 48 B header also naming its introducing push, uploaded with a receipt or written at evacuation from a staged copy in its push's batch (evs-22), and when each is deleted, about a minute after its version's replacement commits, which the change history already dates; which kind-1 segments only executed drops' listed versions name, and when the drop's job deletes each (evs-28); for a git-mode push, which of its new segments no entry version names, so the padded size of the history blobs it carried (owner decision 237)
  why: storage, quota, GC (§11.6, §11.13)
  ttl: "while a retained push names it, in an entry version or, for a git-mode push's history segments, in its new-objects list, then 7 d, a deposit's version retained until a committed CONSUME removes it; a record-class repo's expired segments, keyless, until a later GC, unscheduled (owner decision 246); an upload no committed push adopted: deleted 49-75 h after its upload, once evacuation has settled every batch that could adopt it (owner decision 203); a kind-5 segment until about a minute after the push replacing its version commits, at most ~26 h when its committing process failed (evacuation's sweep), at its marker's collection when its removing push did not list it (evs-11), or, existing at a hold's placement, until the hold ends (§11.13); a kind-1 segment that only executed drops' listed versions name, though their pushes stay: deleted after its drop's window (7 d, or with now 25 h 12 min to 26 h 12 min, once evacuation's horizon has passed by 12 min the time evs saw the drop committed; owner decisions 204, 397) once evacuation's horizon has passed its LastModified + 24 h + 2 min, unless a hold covering the repo keeps it until the hold ends or a pack until a later compaction, unscheduled (owner decision 247), and never served once the job's delete set names it (§11.13)"
  owner: §11.13
evs-5:
  service: evs
  store: slot/<repo>/<slot_id> (metadata cluster)
  sees: "slot id, up to 64 wrapped object keys (ciphertext), each wrapped key's generation, in clear beside it, size up to 8 KiB, times; deposit keys HPKE-wrapped to the drop key; ERASE statements (signer, slot ids and key indexes, time); in slot-keyed repos (record-class repos, group inboxes), slots that only one versionless path's versions name, each holding that path's one key, and their deletion; slots that only executed drops' listed versions name, and their deletion by the drop's job (evs-28); each slot's origin, in object metadata: the push id, statement hash prefix, ref, signer sidecar, base version, path epoch and mode of the statement that created it, or a re-seed's mark; all of it also in that push's record (evs-12); each new slot's body as its push brought it, a one-part push's in its payload and a push in parts' in its seal request, never in a part, which evs writes to slot/ and keeps in no record (QD-806, QD-819)"
  why: per-entry erasure for record-class repos and mail (owner decision 61); a drop's slot deletions (owner decision 173)
  ttl: until erased (rewritten at once without the erased keys, under a preservation hold too; owner decision 133), consumed (a deposit's, by its CONSUME; evs-6) or shredded with the repo; a refused or dead push's own slots until evacuation finds it dead, at most about 26 h after its batch, a slot stored within 2 s of that or after it staying, or, while evacuation's delete of them is off, in the release that brings slot origins, until the repo is shredded (§11.8, §11.13; owner decision 255); never backed up (owner decision 90); owner devices' mirrors keep sealed copies until their next sync after an erasure (§11.13); a versionless path's slot until about a minute after no retained version names it (its removal, or a fresh key at a CLOSURE, a rekey or its first write after a reader's removal; §11.7), at most ~26 h when its committing process failed, at its marker's collection when its removing push did not list it (evs-11), or, existing at a hold's placement, until the hold ends (§11.13); a slot that only executed drops' listed versions name, as evs-4's kind-1 segments (§11.13)
  owner: §11.12
evs-6:
  service: evs
  store: deposit-ref entries in evs-11's, evs-12's, evs-4's and evs-5's objects
  sees: deposits (entries under random ids, padded size, time, the depositor through its deposit ref, MailDeposit headers sealed), each with a slot; a member's device that deposits same-network mail into another member's mailbox, so that those two members exchanged mail and when (§8.5; owner decision 333); receipt deposits by readers of owner-bound repos, at most 4 KiB each and 256 a day per repo (§16.8); the CONSUME that deletes them and their slots
  why: write-only deposits from receivers and headless agents (§11.12, §15.7); read receipts (§16.8)
  ttl: until a reader with rw consumes them; unconsumed deposits are lost with the site (§2.18)
  owner: §11.12
evs-7:
  service: evs
  store: evs's service log
  sees: request log; caller ids, route, repo and ref ids, ranges and slots read, bytes, status, time; a read's pin version, the version of a path it asks for, whether it asks for a fresh head and the ref versions of the DROP pushes whose bodies it holds (§11.9); each answer's retry delay, a push's outcome where evs cannot say it committed, and a framed reply's end; for the search index's files, evs-26's view; drop dry runs and drop listings by route, DROP pushes and their cancels as pushes (evs-28)
  why: rate limits, abuse, debugging; attests audit-member reads (§16.8)
  ttl: 7 d
  owner: §11.8
evs-8:
  service: evs
  store: Redis {evsl_<repo_id>} (holder, ref, path epoch, prefix -> expiry) and {evsl_<repo_id>}v; {evsc_<client_id>} (repo ids, by last subscribe or renewal ms); each lease's expiry, which GET /evs/v1/subscriptions returns as EvsSubscription.expires_ms (owner decision 408)
  sees: per client, the repos, refs, path epochs and up to 16 token prefixes it follows, each lease's expiry, and which repos it subscribed to or renewed in the last 7 d, with when
  why: change notification (PLAN.md:55; owner decision 2); the per-client repo cap (§11.10)
  ttl: 7 d after the last renewal, each lease renewed once it is over 24 h old, never on a reconnect (§11.10); {evsc_} members dropped 7 d after their last subscribe or renewal, or at a DELETE of the client's last lease on the repo, the key expiring 8 d after its last write; soft state outside the rdb bundles, re-created by holders after a loss (owner decision 136); a hold's copy of the lease fields excepted (api-14), {evsc_} needing none since the lease fields hold the same facts
  owner: §11.10
evs-9:
  service: evs and taskworker's drop jobs report; api stores; taskworker's nightly pass counts
  store: api-13's rows, through ServiceHost.Quota.ReportUsage; Redis {evsn_<night>} (the nightly pass's per-shard sums)
  sees: in 60 s usage batches, transfer bytes per caller network and stored-byte deltas per repo network, a drop job's as it deletes included; the over-limit list evs reads every 5 s; a quota refusal's retry delay and whether a purchase lifts its limit; per night, each shard job's stored-byte sum per network and which shards of which metadata clusters reported, which a closing job writes as each network's count once all have (owner decision 198)
  why: soft storage quotas and transfer debits (owner decisions 2, 10; §20.6)
  ttl: as api-13; stored bytes counted nightly by §20.7's stored rule (§11.13); {evsn_} 48 h, outside the rdb bundles (D-OPS-16), a night that some shard never finished, or whose sums Redis lost, leaving the old count
  owner: §11.13
evs-10:
  service: "the file cluster (MinIO: the metadata clusters and the segment cluster); taskworker's write-budget governor"
  store: every object in every bucket, and D-OPS-20's settle bookkeeping on each drive (each version's xl.meta, a DELETE's copy under .minio.sys/settle/); Redis {nvb_<set>} and {nvb_<cluster>}
  sees: every evs, gkm, place/, proj/, projrows/, rev/ and hold/ object key with its size, checksum, times and access pattern, and no object metadata but an idx/ entry's state while its head lists sources (evs-11) and a slot/ object's origin (evs-5), on an NVMe metadata cluster (one 8-drive PM9A3 set at EC:4, owner decisions 116, 136-139; a repo's objects on the cluster its place/ names, owner decision 145) or the HDD segment cluster (EC:8; owner decision 116); requests come only from evs, gkm, api and taskworker over the LAN, never from clients (D-OPS-4); per metadata set, the write budget's bucket level, floored at zero, calibration, allowance and accounts, its prepaid P2 wallet, each process's 5 s report (queued P1 and P2 priced bytes, priced bytes issued by class (P1, unfunded P2, funded P2) and in flight, the funded backlog by P2 rank, credit moved and spent, P0 bytes by kind), a per-cluster at_limit flag the budget loop sets at 80% summed raw use or 70% inodes, and the P0 figures, P0's forgiven excess among them, and liabilities §19.8 exports, and per segment cluster, its drive operations a second and measured capacity (§19.6's hdd row) and each evs process's 5 s count of the segments stored for it since its start, which the hdd loop sums into §19.8's hdd_puts (owner decision 257), all from drive counters and process totals, with no network or repo id; in each version's xl.meta its write's settle id (x-minio-internal-settle-id, the key lock's random id, linked to nothing outside the cluster), and for each DELETE what it took, ciphertext and xl.meta, in .minio.sys/settle/<id>-<hash of the key>/ on each drive, as a revert needs (§19.6's settle row)
  why: durable ciphertext storage (X13; owner decisions 18, 21, 94, 116); drive endurance (owner decision 140; §11.13)
  ttl: each object's own row; deletes and overwrites keep no prior version (unversioned buckets); no off-site copy (owner decision 94); request logs as ops-1; {nvb_} 15 s, but the write budget's saved bucket level, wallet and counter readings 48 h after the loop's last write; a settle id with its version; a DELETE's settle copy from the DELETE until the sweep removes it, at least 2 min after and longer while the key is held, never past §11.12's 10 min stragglers' pass, which §19.6 checks the sweep's interval against
  owner: §19.6
evs-11:
  service: evs; taskworker's path-epoch copy and marker collection (§11.6, §11.7)
  store: idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<t1>/.../<tn>.e, and orphan markers at idx/<repo>/<ref>/_o/<r>-<ids digest>.e outside every epoch (metadata cluster)
  sees: "path index; tokens t_i = HMAC-SHA256(K_path_p, t_(i-1) ‖ name_i)[:16], so keys show the tree's shape (depth, fan-out, files per directory) and per-file change history, and one path has one token on every ref of a repo within a path epoch; each entry's up to four committed versions, folded from committed pushes (the newest with its inline body), each with the place of its change in its own statement's list (leaf_part, leaf_index; owner decision 200), and no pending versions (entry version, push id, base version, previous push id and committed version, layout, time, kind, padded size, versioning setting (0 kept, 1 versionless, 2 the search index's; owner decision 168), sealed fields, chain locators (kind 5, staged or not, for versionless versions) and slot ids, or an inline body up to 16 KiB); a DROP's fold leaving a path's entry only its through_version, with the drop mark {drop_id, through_version}, which path-epoch copies carry; for each path a removal at r removes, a removed directory's current-epoch entries below it included, a removed-entry marker {removing push id, r, the path's version: one past its last, its change's place} (§11.7), with, for a versionless file its removing push did not list, the kind-5 segment and slot ids its collection deletes; while the head lists sources, each entry's state in its object metadata, which reads HEAD at a path's prefixes: carried (from the source it names), fresh (new to the current epoch since the cut-over) or removed (its marker); per directory a name table of child tokens, kinds, a carried row's source epoch (§11.6) and individually sealed names padded to 64 B steps, with its newest folded delta's place and the version the table is folded through (names_through); at most 4,096 children and 448 KiB of name table; an orphan marker {removing push id, r, token path, kind-5 segment and slot ids} for carried ids a fold's re-creation or a copy would otherwise drop, collected as a marker is (§11.7)"
  why: one-round-trip head reads, sparse fetch, prefix LIST, token-prefix subscriptions (owner decision 2); markers, written If-Match (If-None-Match on a 404) only over an entry holding an older version, so no repeated, queued or late removal fold writes over a newer entry, and a creation's entry version is max(its push's effective base version, a standing removal's) + 1, an overlay's base counting its chain's base versions (§11.7), so a path's versions never restart (owner decision 148); the drop mark keeps a listed version from being cited again (owner decision 173)
  ttl: the path's life; a marker until a re-creation's fold replaces it or, once folded_through >= r + 64 (a base range past the removal, so no push based before it can commit) and the head lists no source, taskworker's nightly pass deletes it in a collection window (evs-3; §11.7); a source epoch's markers are deleted unmoved when its copy ends (§11.6); up to four folded committed versions, older ones dropping at the next fold (§11.7). Never names or cross-repo equality (K_path is per repo); holders of a K_path, a removed reader included, can test guessed names created before the next path epoch, which every removal makes due within 24 h (owner decision 585), no source-epoch token of a later name reaching the server but one first sent within 5 s of the cut-over (§11.6)
  owner: §11.7
evs-12:
  service: evs
  store: push, part, seal and reseed records in pb/ batches (metadata cluster; evs-22), then in pack/ (evs-16) or hp/ (evs-23)
  sees: "Signed EvsPush cleartext (repo_id, ref_id, ref kind and mode, owner sidecar_id, push_id, base version and chain, changes of token path, base entry version and entry hash, at most 1,024 entry writes a part, sealed-metadata hash, generation, path epoch, projection version and chain (the auth pin), the generation pin (group id, generation, commitment), a Merkle root and count over the changes with covering token prefixes when they are not inline, the new-objects hash (segment ids with padded sizes and upload days, new slot ids, listed in the payload), a PATH_EPOCH's map source version and chain and tail hash, while sources stand a source-paths hash, an ERASE's or CLOSURE's erased-list hash (a CLOSURE's equals the ERASE's that follows it, so evs links the re-keyed path to that erasure), a DROP's drop_sha256, signer sidecar_id, client_id, time, flags FORCE, DELETE, BASE, IMMUTABLE, CONSUME, PATH_EPOCH, ERASE, CLOSURE, DROP, CUT or COMPLETION, the EXACT_HEAD flag binding the signed base version and chain at commit, a CONSUME's consumed_through (§11.12), an index push's or CUT's index_epoch (the version of the newest CUT it follows), path-map hash, part count and part hashes); per part (up to 1,024), its EvsPushPart and the head version evs checked it at; cleartext entry versions; a PATH_EPOCH payload's tail moves (old and new token paths), which link created paths across epochs as evs-15's maps do; while sources stand, the payload's source paths: each change's token path in every listed source that may hold it, never for a name created since the cut-over (§11.6); sealed commit metadata; inline records; repo admins' EvsReseed statements (repo, ref, re-seeded version and chain, incident id; §19.10); with evs-3 and evs-14, the push DAG and per-file change history (token, time, uploader, padded size); which records one evs process wrote together within 20 ms; per entry version its versioning setting and kind-5 locators; the new-objects list's staged marks and the staged segments' bytes (ciphertext, one record padded to at most 16 KiB each); removals listing each versionless file below a removed directory or deleted ref; each record's purge candidates (segment and slot ids, derived by evs) and a purge list's mark past 2,048 ids or the record's 1 MiB, a part's record listing instead what its versions replaced, whole, marked replaced (§11.13); DROP payload bodies (drop id, action, a cancel's drop id and version, not_before_ms, preview id, and per path lineage its token path in each epoch with their map parts, through_version, boundary, count and list hash) with their listed entry hashes, names and reasons sealed in commit metadata"
  why: commits, multi-part pushes, history, GC, audit, re-seeding (§11.8)
  ttl: "history, the repo's life by default; record-class repos per §16.8's retention through BASE; in batches 25-26 h, then packed hourly once a repo's aged material reaches 256 KiB, else held in parcels until 7 d (owner decision 136; evs-23); dead and duplicate records, and a shredded repo's unless a hold keeps them (evs-19), until their batch is evacuated: at most 26 h after the batch was written; staged bytes leave with their batch, at most 26 h, written to seg/ (evs-4) while their version is retained, else dropped, never into packs or parcels; a replaced versionless version's statement and entry version stay as history; a dropped version's statement stays as history, and its entry version stays served unless its chain names an inline record, in which case both stay stored, never served again, until a later compaction, unscheduled (§11.13; owner decision 247)"
  owner: §11.8
evs-13:
  service: evs, gkm
  store: memory (verified per request)
  sees: capability tokens (aud evs or gkm, scope repo:<id> with role deposit, r, rw or admin, or recovery:<member_id> for an unadmitted device's own recovery wraps at gkm (§7.8), projection version, client, subject client, sidecar and member ids, act), 15 min, verified offline against api's svc- keys; during a site-loss restore (sidecar.yml's reseed), only admin tokens for the re-seed routes, to sidecars the restored rows list under their network's admins (§7.8, §19.10)
  why: authorization without Postgres (owner decision 2; §7.8, §11.8)
  ttl: 15 min; never stored; issuance as api-11
  owner: §11.8
evs-14:
  service: evs
  store: log/<repo>/<ref>/<n> (metadata cluster)
  sees: "history pages; versions 64n to 64n+63: their Signed EvsPush statements, DROP pushes and their cancels included, and each version's window entry (as evs-3), and C at the page's ends"
  why: settle push ids past the head's window; history for replaying readers (§11.8)
  ttl: history, the ref's life; packed with evs-12's records after 24 h, or with a small repo's other aged material at 7 d (owner decision 136; evs-16)
  owner: §11.8
evs-15:
  service: evs
  store: pmap/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<map_sha256>/<part>/_ (metadata cluster)
  sees: Signed EvsPathMap parts (repo, ref, path epoch, part numbers, the source head each map covers, moves of old token path to new token path with names re-sealed, and every live path's token in each source epoch), up to 8 MiB each, and their signer; they link every moved path's tokens across epochs
  why: path-key rotation on removal (owner decision 2 item 9; §11.6); keyed by the map's hash, so a mapper whose source left the window uploads a fresh map
  ttl: the committed map, the ref's history; the epoch's other maps deleted once it commits, and an uncommitted one above the head's epoch by the nightly pass once evacuation's horizon has passed its oldest part's upload + 24 h + 2 min, 49-75 h after it (§11.6; owner decision 203)
  owner: §11.6
evs-16:
  service: evs; taskworker packs
  store: pack/<repo>/<pack_id> (segment cluster)
  sees: packs of log pages and push, part and seal records, older than 24 h, packed hourly once a repo's aged material reaches 256 KiB, else once its oldest is 7 d old (owner decision 136), with their SHA-256; reads by range
  why: keep history older than 24 h off the metadata cluster (owner decision 136; §11.13, §19.6)
  ttl: history
  owner: §11.13
evs-17:
  service: evs
  store: pidx/<repo>/<ref>/<v_first>-<pack_or_parcel_id> (metadata cluster)
  sees: a pack's or parcel's offsets for the versions and log pages it holds (a parcel holds no log pages), the record kinds it holds, the segment ids its records introduce, and each record's place in the batch it left (§11.8's EvsPlace)
  why: find packed or parceled history (§11.13); one entry per container, so a pack's entries never collide with its parcels'
  ttl: as its pack or parcel; a parcel's entries go with it, after its pack's entries exist (§11.13)
  owner: §11.13
evs-18:
  service: api writes; evs, gkm and sockets read
  store: rev/<network_id>/<kind>/<subject_id>/_ (the first metadata cluster)
  sees: revocation objects for a client, sidecar or member; a JWS under api's svc- keys with subject, not_before, reason and time
  why: void 15-minute tokens on removal, deactivation, suspension or revocation (owner decision 2; §7.8)
  ttl: 20 min after its last write; after a site loss api re-creates live ones from its tombstones (§19.10)
  owner: §7.8
evs-19:
  service: api writes; evs, gkm and taskworker read
  store: hold/<network_id>/<case_id>/_ (the first metadata cluster)
  sees: preservation holds mirrored from abuse_legal_hold (network, kind, scope, case id, place_time and expiry), as unsigned UTF-8 JSON (§21.9), a scope being the network or 1 to 16 repo ids, each covering that repo's objects on every cluster and its gkm group (owner decision 527)
  why: the server's TTL sweeps, retention, GC and gkm's reconciler skip held networks' in-scope objects, and evacuation moves their batch records, a shredding repo's included, into packs and parcels that nothing deletes while the hold stands; user-initiated shredding (--now, the 7-day timer, slot erasure) always proceeds, and the versionless purge keeps in-scope content that existed at placement while purging content created since (owner decision 133); a drop is no user-initiated shredding, and holds keep its deletions waiting, silently (owner decision 184; §21.9)
  ttl: "its kind's deadline: 90 d, renewable once, or 1 year for a §2258A report (api-14)"
  owner: §21.9
evs-20:
  withdrawn: no upload markers; evs MACs a receipt the client returns with its push (evs-4; §11.13)
evs-21:
  service: evs, taskworker
  store: spidx/<repo>/<n>/_ (metadata cluster)
  sees: offsets of segments moved into a pack (reserved, empty in v0)
  why: packed segments stay addressable by id (§11.13)
  ttl: as its pack
  owner: §11.13
evs-22:
  service: evs; taskworker evacuates
  store: pb/<yyyymmddhh>/<mm>/<instance>-<seq> (metadata cluster)
  sees: batches; per batch the writing evs process's id, sequence and time, and evs-12's records with each one's repo, ref, push id, signer, type (push, part, seal, reseed) and offsets; which records one process wrote within 20 ms; inside records, staged versionless segments and purge candidates (evs-12); the batch format (1, or 2 when it holds either)
  why: "group commit: one write per batch instead of per push (owner decision 140; §11.8)"
  ttl: until hourly evacuation, at most 26 h, a bound §11.13's write budget keeps under load by serving evacuation of batches past 25 h first within P2, except while P0 holds the bucket empty (owner decision 186), when evacuation waits and batches stay until the wave ends, evacuation then restarting, oldest first, as the bucket refills (owner decision 190); deleted whole (§11.13)
  owner: §11.8
evs-23:
  service: taskworker writes; evs reads
  store: hp/<repo>/<parcel_id> (metadata cluster)
  sees: a small repo's records older than 24 h, with their offsets; its log pages wait at log/ until a pack takes them
  why: keep small repos' aged history on NVMe until it reaches 256 KiB or 7 d, without tiny HDD objects (owner decision 136)
  ttl: until packed, 7 d after its oldest record's commit plus at most an hour; shredded with the repo
  owner: §11.13
evs-24:
  service: evs
  store: Redis {evsq_<repo_id>} (push sequence), {evsh_<repo_id>} (verified head cache)
  sees: each repo's push sequence; copies of its heads (evs-3), their ETags and cache times, and the sequence value each ref's last commit raised, which GET .../refs?moved_after= reads (§11.9)
  why: hint versions without a repo/ write per push; fewer cluster reads (owner decision 136; §11.10)
  ttl: the sequence 30 d after its last commit, restarting above every earlier value after a loss; a head copy served only within 10 min of its own cache time, the hash expiring 10 min after the repo's last write; outside the rdb bundles (D-OPS-16)
  owner: §11.10
evs-25:
  service: evs creates it; evs and gkm resolve and cache it
  store: place/<repo_id> (the first metadata cluster)
  sees: which metadata cluster holds a repo's objects and its gkm group's, and its creator's sidecar_id, set once at the repo's creation (If-None-Match decides a race)
  why: the metadata tier grows by whole clusters while each repo keeps one commit point (owner decision 145; §11.8, §19.6)
  ttl: as repo/<repo> (evs-1)
  owner: §11.8
evs-26:
  service: evs (pushes, head reads, listings and range reads, §11.8, §11.9) and its service log (evs-7)
  store: none new; what evs-3's head windows, evs-12's push records, evs-11's entries, evs-4's segments and range reads and evs-7's request log hold for the search index's files, which their versioning value 2 (owner decision 168) makes recognizable (evs-11)
  sees: from pushes, which paths hold each repo's index (one versionless directory per indexed file-mode ref, or the ur/index ref), each indexed push's staged head overwrite, whose padded size step shows roughly how much text it indexed, a shard rewrite per ~128 KiB of entries, a bulk removal and shard rewrites once a bucket length (the roll-up, rarely with one newer bucket's shard and manifest rewritten to take a promoted entry), CUTs and CLOSUREs at erasure (a CUT's staged rewrite of its ref's erasure set, whose padded size steps with the documents its pending erasures hold, and a 409 INDEX_EPOCH for each index push it outdates), and on ur/index companion pushes trailing content pushes by up to a minute on 1 KiB blocks, else five minutes (owner decision 172); from reads, per client, which index files of which repos and refs it reads, at which versions and ranges, and when; so which repos it keeps searchable, whether it keeps a repo's all partition (desktops and indexers at each roll-up they do not reproduce; phones in background windows on Wi-Fi while charging, and a browser tab while open on Wi-Fi while charging, where its browser reports both (§18.4)), and, for an ephemeral sidecar's first sync of a repo or any fetch of all at "search more" that no indexer answered (a phone or browser tab that has not kept all, an ephemeral sidecar or a cloud agent), that its person or agent searched, and when; a "search more" an indexer answers shows evs nothing (connect-5); the documents it opens soon after, and the candidates `ur search --verify fetch` opens, as ordinary reads whose set follows the query; nothing else of a query, term, candidate, result or result count, since index files are fetched by sync position, all whole in a fixed order, documents only when opened, and nothing is compressed across documents (I-19)
  why: search runs only on devices, over whole downloaded partitions, so no server takes part in a query (owner decisions 151, 154, 166)
  ttl: as evs-3, evs-4, evs-11, evs-12 and evs-7 (7 d); nothing beyond them
  owner: §11.14
evs-27:
  service: evs (pushes, head reads, listings, range reads) and its service log (evs-7)
  store: none new; what evs-3, evs-4, evs-5, evs-8, evs-11, evs-12 and evs-7 hold for a team's directory repo
  sees: from the directory's format 2 (before it, announce entries in each writer's stream show the same timing), per announcing sidecar one card path, and per general or record repo, and any repo announced explicitly, one repo path, an announcement or a private marker padded alike, each token stable within a path epoch, a new repo's path first written by its creating device just after the creation, so linkable to it; each card version's signer, time and padded size in 2 KiB steps, so when each sidecar's runs start, end, change claims and renew (hourly while a run moves) and when its worker item renews (daily), never which run, title, project or branch; a revocation as a repo path's rewrite (before format 2, a newer announce entry) and an erasure_request entry in the revoker's stream, then a CLOSURE and ERASE on the directory's erasure ref (before format 2, ERASEs of the earlier entries) that a directory admin's device signs, as it signs every directory erasure, whose erased keys and rewritten index files show which writers' entries or documents named the repo; per access request, a notice created, rewritten at each decision, a denial's as an approval's, and removed under a token prefix that every request to one target shares, with the leases of that target's approvers' clients on it and of the requester's clients on its own path, so which requester asked which approvers, when, which approvers' devices decided it and when, and when it closed; request, decision, erasure request and coordination entries as stream records (signer, time, padded size); which clients read the directory, and when, with each sync's moved-stream listing and the streams it read (§11.9); nothing of an announcement's or a request's content or reason, and of a repo path's repo or a request's target only what the roles api-7 shows for the path's signers or the request's approvers narrow, though an approval's grant, which api-7 shows at the decision (RepoGrant, EvsShare) or at the requester's activation (GrantActivate), shows the approval and links the notice's prefix to its repo or worker
  why: one team directory (owner decisions 170, 171, 181); approvers are notified by lease (§11.10)
  ttl: as evs-3, evs-4, evs-5, evs-8, evs-11, evs-12 and evs-7; entries by the directory's retention, announce entries 30 d after a newer entry or file for their item or the item's expiry, a live repo item's newest copy kept, and the rest 400 d, expiry erasing their keys (§16.11)
  owner: §16.11
evs-28:
  service: evs appends; taskworker runs the dry runs and jobs (§11.13)
  store: drops/<repo>/_ (the repo's metadata cluster, at most 64 KiB beside held drops' entries and held jobs' records); dropscan/<repo>/<id>/<f> (segment cluster; f one of snap, cand, list, mark, del, held, ask, res); Redis {evsd_<repo_id>}
  sees: "per drop: its id, ref, DROP push id, version and place, not_before_ms, the time evs saw it committed, state (pending, cancelled, executing with phase and progress, held, observed, done, refused with reason), freed and held bytes, and the dry run it names; per dry run: the token paths and lists it was asked about, its snapshot and results (candidate segment and slot ids with sizes, which of them other versions name, inline and packed bytes), its state and progress, and per path whether the client's list matched, whether its lineage is linked and by which map parts, the resolved count, and young bytes; per job, the running one's and each held one's (owner decision 654): its owner instance and lease, the drops it covers, its round and that round's horizon, its snapshots (each ref's version), cursor, counters, and candidate, mark, delete and held sets, per covered drop the entry hashes of its listed versions, sorted, each with a flag for an inline record, in its list files, and in its first snapshot file whether a listed version renamed a path (its push removed one path and created another citing its kind-5 content) and whether one copied across refs (its chain named a reuse source of another ref), two booleans the observe report counts (owner decision 513); for format 2, what a read answers for a version a drop holds or took or collection removed: its read state (collected, drop pending, dropped), the drop's id, not_before_ms and version; per cancelled or refused drop, a 17 B void record {drop_id, state}"
  why: a resumable deletion job and a dry run for the drop-history action, after its cancellable window, with no metadata write per push (owner decisions 173, 183)
  ttl: drops/ entries at most 30 d after their drop or dry run ends, ended ones leaving sooner, oldest first, when a write would pass 64 KiB, but never one whose DROP committed under 27 h ago, and a held drop's entry staying until its deletions finish, unlisted once 30 d have passed from its move to held, or at once where the 64 KiB bound would evict its done twin (owner decisions 643, 654), and a held job's record until its round after the holds ends it; a void record for the repo's life; dropscan/ files 30 d after their job or dry run ends, but a job's list files, its listed versions' entry hashes, and its first snapshot file, snap-0, its covered drops' ids, versions, places and seen_ms, which stay for the repo's life (§11.13; owner decisions 398, 570); {evsd_} hints until taken, outside the rdb bundles; all three deleted with the repo at its shred (§11.12's phase 5)
  owner: §11.13
evs-29:
  service: evs
  store: reseed/<repo>/<ref> (the repo's metadata cluster)
  sees: "after a site loss, per ref the Signed EvsReseed statements its repo admins filed: repo_id, ref_id, the re-seeded head's version and chain, the recovery's incident id, and the signing sidecar"
  why: a reader whose pin lies above every surviving copy accepts the shorter history only under a repo admin's EvsReseed, shown as a loss (§11.13, §19.10; QD-725)
  ttl: the ref's life; deleted with the repo at its shred (§11.12's phase 5)
  owner: §11.13
evs-30:
  service: xops writes it at provisioning; evs's, gkm's and taskworker's hosts read it (server.FileClusters, a HEAD every 30 s with the block's own credentials)
  store: sentinel/_ (one fixed key in each file cluster's bucket)
  sees: a constant body; no network, repo, user or client id
  why: "readiness: each cluster's sentinel readable (§19.4; owner decision 258)"
  ttl: the cluster's life; written once, never rewritten
  owner: §19.6
gkm-1:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/repo/<repo_id>/<seq>; gkm/<group_id>/owner and gkm/<group_id>/epoch/0 (metadata cluster); gkm/dkey/<network_id>/<delegation_id>
  sees: GroupForm chain (repo_id, group_id, previous group, generation, signer, and the signer's auth pin when it signs (owner decision 368)); epoch 0 (network_id, cipher suite 0x0010 (owner decision 44), creator); each group's owner marker (repo_id, network_id), written first at a creation or re-form, through which alone gkm resolves the group (owner decision 201); and each forwarding Delegation's reader public key, by delegation_id, which gkm and every rotator check against its row's digest (owner decision 202)
  why: one accepted commit per epoch; re-forming; one repo to a group; sealing to forwarding Delegations (§10.5)
  ttl: life of the repo, epoch 0 while epoch/0 exists; an owner marker until the repo's shred, a re-seed's form writing it again; a forwarding Delegation's reader key until 24 h after the Delegation ends or is superseded
  owner: §10.6
gkm-2:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/<group_id>/epoch/<n> (metadata cluster)
  sees: epoch objects; group_id, epoch, content type, generation, auth pin, size, time, uploader sidecar_id; the commit as PrivateMessage ciphertext; GenWrap; at most 16 leaves, the sealed GroupInfo and the generation that seals it
  why: ordering; the write gate
  ttl: 30 d, then until every leaf acking in the last 30 d has applied it; never the newest epoch
  owner: §10.6
gkm-3:
  withdrawn: no roster delta in the clear (owner decision 59); membership shows only as sidecar ids in gkm-4, gkm-5, gkm-7 and gkm-10, as in api-7
gkm-4:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/kp/<sidecar_id>/<ref>, gkm/kp/<sidecar_id>/<ref>.claim, gkm/rk/<sidecar_id> (the first metadata cluster)
  sees: "KeyPackages (init and leaf HPKE keys, signature key, credential: sidecar_id, identity key and its algorithm, suite, not_after, admission hash, signature); claims (group, claimer, target); ReaderKeys (owner decision 114)"
  why: asynchronous adds; wrapped readers
  ttl: KeyPackages until claimed, or 90 d; claims 90 d; ReaderKeys until replaced or past their not_after, at most 7 d
  owner: §10.6
gkm-5:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/<group_id>/welcome/<n> (the repo's metadata cluster), gkm/welcome/<sidecar_id>/<group_id>/<n> (the first)
  sees: Welcome objects and pointers, the pointers keyed by recipient, group and epoch and naming the KeyPackageRef the Add used (owner decision 363); recipient sidecar_ids and KeyPackageRefs in the clear; secrets and GroupInfo encrypted
  why: deliver joins
  ttl: until every recipient has acked, at most 90 d
  owner: §10.6
gkm-6:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/<group_id>/epoch/<n> (external commits)
  sees: external commits, for resync and recovery only (PublicMessage); the joiner's leaf and credential, its removed old leaf, their ExternalInit and Remove proposals and their UpdatePath's public keys and encrypted path secrets
  why: offline catch-up and recovery
  ttl: as gkm-2
  owner: §10.6
gkm-7:
  service: gkm
  store: "gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>, gkm/<group_id>/genpack/<k> (§10.16's gen packs, from §19.9's gen trigger: gen/<256k+1> to gen/<256k+256> verbatim, those gen/ objects then deleted), gkm/<group_id>/group-info, gkm/<group_id>/wrap/<g>/<c8>/<recipient>/<k8> (metadata cluster)"
  sees: key ladder; GenRotates (group, generation, parent and own commitments, cause, auth pin, time, holders hash, the count of its staged and recovery wraps, signer; GenLink and leaf-wrap ciphertexts; the drop public key and its expiry where the kind takes deposits); GroupInfo pointers and, above 16 leaves, sealed GroupInfo and the generation it names; staged and late wraps (group, generation, commitment, recipient sidecar_id or delegation_id and the SHA-256 of the key sealed to, staged or late, a late one's auth pin and time, ciphertext, signer; owner decisions 114, 144, 182)
  why: ladder, resync, deposits; wrapped readers
  ttl: life of the repo, a gen pack's GenRotates as gen/'s; GroupInfo until superseded; wraps until the next generation's exist, staged wraps of a lost claim 24 h, a recipient's wrap to an older key 30 d after one to a newer key exists
  owner: §10.6
gkm-8:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm/recovery/<member_id>/<group_id>/<g>/<c8>/<b8> (metadata cluster)
  sees: recovery wraps (member_id, group_id, generation, the 8-byte prefix c8 of the generation's commitment, which gkm-7 shows whole, an 8-byte prefix of the binding's Ed25519 key hash, which the authorization log already shows, HPKE ciphertext); the bindings are §7.9's RecoveryBind config records, not gkm objects
  why: recovery after losing every device
  ttl: until a RecoveryRebind replaces them or the repo is deleted; staged ones of a lost claim 24 h
  owner: §10.6
gkm-9:
  service: gkm
  store: gkm's service log
  sees: request log; client, route, group, time, bytes (GroupInfo requests included)
  why: rate limits, abuse
  ttl: 7 d
  owner: §10.6
gkm-10:
  service: gkm
  store: Redis {gka_<group_id>}
  sees: acks in Redis {gka_<group_id>}; group_id, sidecar_id, newest applied epoch, time; written at most daily
  why: retention
  ttl: overwritten by the leaf's next ack; 31 d after its last write; deleted with its group's gkm objects at a shred (§11.12); soft state outside the rdb bundles, lost with Redis, after which gkm deletes no epoch for 30 d; a hold's copy excepted (api-14)
  owner: §10.6
tls-1:
  service: lb (stream split, port 80 redirect), tlsedge
  store: memory, with a snapshot of the label and custom-host maps and the suspensions, read through tlsedge's restricted Postgres role at start and then every 5 s (owner decision 495); a 30 s negative cache; the lb's generated custom-host split map (active custom hostnames, public through SNI and CT; §13.4)
  sees: per TCP 443 connection (and 8443, 8883 and 5671; owner decision 121) the SNI, which the lb's ssl_preread split and tlsedge read (owner decision 34), the whole ClientHello (ALPN list, ECH presence, size), the accepting port, setup timing, record sizes and bytes per direction, the chosen listener; on port 80, the Host and request line of plaintext requests, answered with a redirect to https; the sidecar subprotocol's framing of each stream with a listener, its Envelope, Chunk, Error and Stream* fields (ids, codes, offsets, windows, retry times and versions), in which StreamOpen.target holds only the <net>:<name> socket or service target the edge already routes by and early_data only bytes of the connection it already carries
  why: route by SNI without terminating (X1); caps; absorb scans; no plaintext path to tlsedge (§13.4, §13.5)
  ttl: connection memory; negative cache 30 s; the lb writes no access-log line for *.<root> names (I-13); tls-3 holds the only records
  owner: §13.5
tls-2:
  service: lb, tlsedge
  store: memory; Redis {vhk}tls:<yyyymmdd>, the fleet's daily visitor-hash key
  sees: visitor IP and port (PROXY v1 or v2 from the lb); per-process cap keys per /64 or /32, with /48 and /24 aggregates (HMAC under a per-process key rotated daily); the fleet-shared daily key of tls-3's hash and Find's affinity key, 32 random bytes the day's first process creates, from which k_record and k_affinity derive by HKDF-SHA256
  why: caps (§13.9); the keyed /24 or /48 affinity key to Find (sock-2); TlsEdgeOpen.client_ip to the listener over a sealed stream
  ttl: memory, never logged (I-13); cap keys rotate daily; the daily key 25 h (SET NX EX 90000, UTC dates), outside the rdb bundles (D-OPS-16), a process that cannot reach Redis using a random key of its own for that day
  owner: §13.4
tls-3:
  service: tlsedge
  store: tls_connection_record (hourly partitions), tls_connection_day
  sees: connection records (network_id, host from SNI, connection_id, start, duration, bytes, a /24 or /48 hash, HMAC-SHA256 under k_record from tls-2's fleet-shared daily key, I-13); daily counts per network and host
  why: abuse joins by connection_id (§21.8), the keyed hash linking one visitor's connections within a day; per-host bytes (§13.6, §13.9)
  ttl: records dropped at 24 h, after any §21.9 hold has copied out its network's rows (owner decision 133); daily counts 13 months; URnetwork can invert the hash until its key expires, 25 h after its date begins
  owner: §13.15
tls-4:
  service: tlsedge, api, the abuse worker
  store: network_tls_suspension; Redis {tes_<network_id>} and its trigger {tes_<network_id>}n; lease spends (api-13); the published-names list, drawn from api-7
  sees: payload bytes per network (meter tls lease spends); kill-switch entries (a host or all the network's hosts, reason, until); the published-names list, active publish grants (host, port, label or alias, audience, expiry), which §21.6 checks hourly against Web Risk
  why: billing (owner decision 10); takedown and abuse checks without inspection (owner decision 41; §13.9, §21.6)
  ttl: lease spends as api-13; a suspension until its case lifts it, a downgrade's renewal lifts it (§20.7), or its until time passes, then deleted with its keys, the case keeping the action (api-14); a name leaves the list when its grant expires or is revoked (Community publishes at most 7 d)
  owner: §13.9
cert-1:
  service: certs (taskworker), api
  store: network_tls_cert, network_tls_account, network_tls_custom_spend, network_tls_name_backoff; Redis {tcb_<ca>_<registered_domain>} (a sorted set of the last 7 days' new-set orders)
  sees: cert_id, network_id, client_id, sidecar_id, identifier-set hash, SPKI hash, the identity-key attestation, the CSR (public key and names), CA, account URI, profile, serial, validity, ARI window, state and successor, the time of its latest state; issued chains until 30 d after expiry or revocation, and a requested revocation's reason; Team custom-domain chains and queued CSRs (v1); each CA's and registered domain's new-set orders of the last 7 days; per custom row its host and domain, the ACME order's URL, the claim sequence, whether it is an ARI renewal, and a reason; per domain the account's URI, CA, key sequence, the current and next key's thumbprints (public) and the ids of the secret repos holding the key file; the lock's holder sidecar, purpose, row and lease; rate-limit holds; each ordering desktop's last poll time; per custom host and registered domain the times of orders, certificates and failed authorizations of the last 16 days; per URnetwork-zone name and CA, its failure backoff (the count of consecutive failed authorizations since its last success there and the next allowed attempt time). Never the account key
  why: order, renew and revoke certificates for device-held keys (owner decision 39; §13.8)
  ttl: 30 d after expiry, revocation or failure; budget entries 7 d, the key 7 d after its newest order, rebuilt from network_tls_cert on loss; the account row with its domain; spends 16 d; poll times 7 d; a name's failure backoff until a success at its CA, or 8 d past its next allowed attempt
  owner: §13.8
cert-2:
  service: CAs (Let's Encrypt, GTS, ZeroSSL) and public CT logs
  store: external, public
  sees: every SAN, that is <net>.<root>, *.<net>.<root>, live aliases and Team scope labels (owner decision 40), and Team custom domains' names; never hosts under a wildcard; URnetwork's ACME accounts; DNS-01 lookups through dns-2; for a Team custom domain the customer's ACME account, its key changes, every order and revocation, and the public address each ordering desktop reaches the CA from
  why: CA rules
  ttl: permanent and public
  owner: §13.8
dns-1:
  service: dns (API blocks and edges)
  store: dns_root (with custom_host_map_version and restore_incident_id), network_dns_zone, network_dns_record, network_dns_host_suspension, dns_zone_journal, network_dns_custom_host, dns_custom_host_map, dns_custom_host_map_applied, dns_restore_incident, dns_canary_verdict, dns_ns; Redis {dns}serial:<root>; edge snapshots, and after a reload the snapshot it replaced; a restore's incident record and admin events (api-8)
  sees: system and user records (A, AAAA, CNAME, TXT, MX, SRV, wildcards), DKIM selectors and keys, TLSA per receiver key and the hashes of the caller's own published keys a key-record write retires (retire_spki_sha256; §15.5, owner decision 443), CAA, null MX, direct-MX addresses, replying burners' selector records and the MX, A and AAAA copies at their labels, until the PSL listing (owner decision 79; §12.7), each Team network's delegated _domainkey.<domain> apexes (§14.6; owner decision 623), challenge TXT values, strong-mode probes' CAA canaries (the customer's pin plus a nonce; §12.8), custom-host maps with each custom host's state (pending, active, or withheld while a downgrade keeps a web host out of the map; §20.7, QD-840), CAA mode (strong or weak), full-chain check result, map version and readiness (§12.8); the map's versions and digests, and each lb interface's reported version, digest and nginx master and its route probes' results (§13.4); the sending lb addresses, listed in _spf.<root> and named in their reverse zones by PTRs under bringyour.com (owner decision 124); zone suspensions (network, reason, until) and host suspensions (network, host, creation time; §12.9), each record's creation time, an expiring record's expiry and a withheld record's withheld time; the journal of diffs; serials; each user or key write also as an admin event (api-8); after a restore, the RRsets (network_id, owner, type) that differ between an edge's replaced snapshot and the restored zone, and the custom hosts W1's regeneration adds or drops (§12.6), and each reclaimable name's CT leaf SHA-256; each lb interface's public addresses, router flag and the health an edge derives from its probes; each monitor source's canary verdict (source, serial, ok, time), overwritten in place; each NS's state, stopped time and reason; each network's report token, public in _dmarc
  why: serve the zones and the sending addresses' reverse zones; takedown (§21); DNS data is public by nature (CONVENTIONS §0)
  ttl: records while published, withdrawn at once when their network is deleted (§12.5); a delegated _domainkey.<domain> apex with the verified domain's row (api-3); PTRs while smtpedge.yml lists their address; challenges and canaries at most 1 h; journal 7 d; custom-host map versions 7 d, and interface reports while the interface is in the lb inventory; suspensions until Restore or their until time; {dns}serial projects dns_root (§19.7); a replaced snapshot until the restore step has its diff, at most 24 h after the reload, and deleted at once after a reload that is not a restore's; a restore's lists 400 d, in its incident record as in admin events (api-8); canary verdicts overwritten in place; NS rows while dns.yml lists the NS; report tokens with their network_dns_zone row
  owner: §12.6
dns-2:

smtp-1:

smtp-2:
  service: smtpedge
