
**F8. A harness recording work through MCP** (X20 and approvals: owner decisions [25](#od-25), [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [80](#od-80), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142)).

```text
   harness      daemon       evs          approver
1  |--ur mcp--->|            |            |
2  |--hooks---->|            |            |
3  |            |--records-->|            |
4  |--O tool--->|--request-->|            |
5  |            |            |--hint----->|
6  |            |<--decision--------------|
7  |<--result---|            |            |
8  |            |--coverage->|            |

1  the harness spawns `ur mcp --agent a` (bare `ur` does the same when stdin is not a terminal), which
   relays to the daemon over a Unix socket that checks the peer uid; tools take a `network` argument
   defaulting from the project's `.ur` file, else the daemon's only network, and refuse otherwise
   (§5.8; owner decisions 23, 57, 84; §5 D-CORE-9; §16 D-MCP-2)
2  hooks call `ur hook` (at most 300 ms, fail open) and the daemon tails the transcript; it redacts
   secrets, then seals (§16 D-MCP-5)
3  vault entries form a signed per-writer chain with a key slot per entry, written as in F2; each
   RecordEntry is sealed whole, and owned refs in record repos refuse FORCE and DELETE (owner decisions
   25, 61; §16 D-MCP-6; Q-ARCH-9 (a)). A device the author has not consented to only deposits into
   the author's vault (owner decision 126; §8.5). Team-record entries go by drop key (§10 D-KEYS-8)
4  an outward (O) tool, such as tls_publish or mail_send to a new recipient, writes an ApprovalRequest
   and returns pending (§16 D-MCP-4)
5  an evs hint and a content-free phone wake notify the approver (owner decision 88; §16.8)
6  the approver's identity key on another device, or a presence key, signs the ApprovalDecision; a
   single-device user approves in the harness's own prompt, which in a tainted run counts only where
   the matching `requests` rule names harness evidence, or with a presence prompt. The record labels
   the evidence type, and a network policy may demand stronger evidence; no decision needs an SSHSIG
   (owner decision 279), and no approval comes by email (owner decisions 75, 80, 142; §16.6)
7  the daemon executes only if the decision's hash matches its own canonical payload and the decision
   names this sidecar, reserving the use before the effect (§16 D-MCP-4, D-MCP-11, D-MCP-12); once
   the run is tainted, no standing grant or approved recipient passes, and it refuses as stale a
   decision whose request was untainted, Authorize filing a tainted request, though a use reserved
   before the taint completes (§16.6's TS1; §5.4); a requested grant activates once, as a
   `GrantActivate` carrying the decision under its fixed `grant_id` (§16.6, §8.8; §8 D-ACL-7; owner
   decisions 3, 74)
8  at run end, a coverage entry lists every gap (§16.8)
```

**F9. Remove a member** (X3 and X12 as in F1 and F3; owner decisions [59](#od-59), [64](#od-64), [83](#od-83), [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [129](#od-129), [144](#od-144)). Actors: an admin; api; the removed member's devices; gkm; a remaining writer leaf; evs.

```text
   admin        api          removed      gkm          writer       evs
1  |--remove--->|            |            |            |            |
2  |--revocation, into the config repo----------------------------->|
3  |            |--cut off-->|            |            |            |
4  |            |            |            |--pending-->|            |
5  |            |            |            |<--commit---|            |
6  |            |            |            |            |--write---->|

1  member-remove, remove-client or SCIM deprovisioning: one api transaction removes the member,
   deactivates the member's own clients, revokes their tokens and logs an admin event; tagged agents
   the member enrolled stay, with their tags' grants, and admins may reassign their sponsorship (owner
   decision 83; §7.10, D-TEAM-10)
2  the admin's device signs the revocation into the config repo, where members read it; one admin
   signature suffices, except that removing an AdminSet member, or their devices, is an authority
   statement needing k of n, the target never counting (owner decisions 3, 5, 110; §7.9). Its
   projection v' closes the write gate of every repo the member read (§11.8)
3  api, sockets and the edges refuse the tokens at once; evs and gkm, which verify tokens offline,
   honor the signed revocation object in the cluster and drop the subject's scope with their newest
   verified projection, and tokens lapse within 15 min (§7.8, §8.9); connect closes the clients within
   90 s; their listeners, publishes, forwards, DKIM selectors and certificates end (owner decisions 2,
   36; §13.8; I-15)
4  gkm hints pending on the per-client gkm topic of each group's writers, the revoking device first
   (owner decision 113; §6.8; §10.6, KF4)
5  a writer leaf commits the Remove with a path, as a PrivateMessage whose clear authenticated_data
   carries only GkmCommitHeader (generation, auth pin), with no roster delta; members derive the
   change from the config repo at v' and reject a Remove without the signed revocation (owner
   decisions 59, 113; §10.9); then any writer rotates, claiming gen/<g+1> after staging its wraps
   (§10.5). In the config group the revocation's signer, when it is a leaf, may commit the Remove even
   if not a config writer (owner decision 128). No wrapped device commits a Remove: agents never do,
   and in the config group neither do member devices past its first 1,000, so a wrapped signer
   rotates and the next leaf commit removes the target (owner decisions 114, 144; §7.9); an agent's
   revocation is a new generation not wrapped to it, which any writer writes (owner decision 114). gkm
   stores the commit and the gen/ claim with If-None-Match: * (owner decision 2; §10 KF4)
6  the gate reopens at g+1: writes use generation g+1 and a rotated path key with an old-to-new token
   map, and the first write to each file is a full checkpoint (owner decisions 2, 64); new names in
   general, config and mailcfg repos wait until that map lands (§11.6). The removed party keeps what
   it already decrypted (§10.8). Until a writer, agents included, claims g+1, pushes get 412 (§11.8);
   until a writer leaf commits the Remove, no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds the removed leaf
   (§10.5). A server withholding the Remove delays it within §2.8's exposure bound, which a split it
   makes by dropping traffic defeats: shared-group writers without a consistent witness alarm at 24 h
   and stop at witness_bound_hours (default 72 h), while rotations, Removes and revocations never stop
   (owner decision 129; D-TRUST-10)
```

**F10. Burner lifecycle** (X6 residual Q-MAIL-3: [owner decision 32](#od-32); launch at M8, receive-only until F5 ships: owner decisions [34](#od-34), [35](#od-35)).

```text
   app          evs          receiver     mxedge       smtpedge
1  |[label]     |            |            |            |
2  |--mailcfg-->|--hint----->|            |            |
3  |            |            |<--mail-----|            |
4  |--reply, as F5, once outbound ships--------------->|
5  |--burn----->|--hint----->|            |            |
6  |            |            |--550 RCPT->|            |

1  the app's sidecar role generates <blabel>, a word-number label such as otter-4821, that avoids the
   network's published hosts and burned labels; the address is <name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>, and an
   alias in place of <net> shows the network's name (owner decision 32; §15.9)
2  the label goes into the signed mailcfg, written as in F2, and receivers learn it from the hint; the
   wildcard MX *.<net>.<root> -> mx.<net>.<root> covers it, so it has no DNS record, no quota use and
   no server state (§15 D-MAIL-7)
3  inbound mail arrives as in F6 with SNI mx.<net>.<root>, so mxedge routes by network, and the
   receiver checks RCPT against mailcfg (§15.5)
4  a reply goes as in F5 from <name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>, flagged BURNER, with Received and client
   headers removed (§15.10); smtpedge checks that the From domain lies in the network's zone; until
   <root> is on the PSL, a burner that replies gets its own DKIM selector and MX records, which
   publish its label: guessable and visible in DKIM headers, not walkable under §12.6's compact denial
   (owner decision 79 accepted walkable; owner decision 35; §15.9-15.10)
5  burn is local: the label is marked burned in mailcfg and never reissued (owner decision 32)
6  receivers answer 550 5.1.1 for it from then on; for a receive-only burner nothing changes in DNS or
   on the server. Correspondents can link a network's burners through <net> (owner decision 32;
   §15.9)
```

**F11. Search, and find agents working on a task** (owner decisions [10](#od-10), [23](#od-23), [63](#od-63), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142), [150](#od-150) and [151](#od-151)-[157](#od-157), [166](#od-166), [170](#od-170)-[172](#od-172); v1). Actors: the writer, another agent (in a team network, another member's); evs; the network's indexer, if one is designated; the searching daemon with its index cache; an agent in a harness.

```text
   writer       evs          indexer      daemon       agent
1  |--claim---->|            |            |            |
2  |            |--hint------------------>|            |
3  |            |<--sync latest-----------|            |
4  |            |            |            |<--search---|
5  |            |            |            |--page 1--->|
6  |            |<--roll-up--|            |            |
7  |            |<--all, by position------|            |
8  |            |            |            |--groups--->|
9  |            |<--read, receipt first---|<--open-----|

1  the writer's run claims its task (record_append, kind claim: its text and targets): in a team
   network the claim joins the run's announcement in the team directory, indexed in the push that
   writes its card (§16.11; owner decisions 170, 171); in a personal network it is a vault entry whose
   index entry follows on the vault's ur/index in the writer's next companion push, at most a minute
   later on 1 KiB XFS blocks, else five minutes (owner decision 172); a head keeps one entry per
   document (§11.14; §16.8, §16.10; owner decisions 151, 153)
2  in a personal network as F2 steps 5-6, a daemon that follows a record stream only for search
   holding a whole-ref lease on its ur/index (§11.10); in a team network the daemon instead syncs the
   directory at each search or view, coalesced to 30 s, every 15 min while it serves a harness
   session, else hourly (§5.4; §16.11, §18.4)
3  the daemon replays the ref's statements after its pin and fetches the changed index files into its
   sealed cache, checking each against its entry version's content_sha256, by sync position, never by
   query; from the directory's changed cards it derives their writers' index heads, fetching a head,
   and alarming, only where the derived one differs from its entry version's content_sha256 (§5
   D-CORE-16; §11.14; §16 D-MCP-20)
4  search_agents("rate limiter", since 7d): the scope is the session's network (`.ur`), every repo this
   sidecar reads by §8's local evaluation, the team directory included (§16.11), less secret, config,
   mailcfg and deposit-only repos, unconsented owner-bound repos and repos whose index is off (owner
   decisions 23, 126; §16 D-MCP-21)
5  phase 1: both latest buckets at once, the newest version winning by document key; doc-table fields
   confirm header matches, and the daemon's plaintext confirms the rest where it holds it, else they
   stay possible; hits group by (sidecar, agent label), active groups first, then the newest;
   untrusted hits and the directory's announcements, requests and decisions return as stubs, so the
   run stays untainted (I-9; owner decision 142; §16 D-MCP-22 to D-MCP-24, D-MCP-29)
6  once per bucket length the indexer, else the first writer after the bucket expires, rolls the
   expired bucket into all under a per-ref lock and drops it; the expired bucket answers until the
   roll-up lands (owner decisions 150, 153, 157)
7  desktops and indexers fetch the changed all shards in the background; an ephemeral or cloud daemon
   fetches every all shard it lacks, whole and youngest first, only for `more`; downloads debit the
   transfer balance (owner decisions 10, 154)
8  phase 2's hits follow phase 1's under the same cursor, so a returned page is never revised (§16
   D-MCP-25)
9  opening a hit is a read as in F2 step 7, which checks a possible hit; an EvsShare or audit reader of
   an owner-bound repo deposits a read receipt first (§16 D-MCP-18; owner decisions 63, 126)
```

**F12. A phone's "search more" answered by an indexer** (owner decisions [10](#od-10), [126](#od-126), [150](#od-150), [151](#od-151)-[155](#od-155), [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178); v1). Actors: an app host's sidecar, the phone; connect relays; a designated search indexer, the member's own or, for team repos, a network-scope one; evs.

```text
   phone        relays       indexer      evs
1  |--Hello, HeadCheck------>|            |
2  |[search own]|            |            |
3  |--SearchRequest--------->|            |
4  |            |            |[verify]    |
5  |<--SearchReply-----------|            |
6  |[merge]     |            |            |
7  |--next page------------->|            |
8  |--read, on open---------------------->|

1  at foreground, where the network designates a search indexer (none by default, owner decision 177)
   and the phone's mode is on, its default, the phone sends Hello to its first-choice own search
   indexer, or to another member's once that member's notice is answered, on the pair's Network
   contract: data where reach allows, else the `control` class, which carries SEARCH only to a sidecar
   advertising Hello feature bit 0; it checks the indexer's designation, admission and identity
   binding in its own state, and runs HeadCheck if due (§6.4, D-PROTO-21; §18.7, D-SDK-27)
2  keystrokes search the phone's own buckets and any cached all (§11.14); nothing leaves the phone
3  "search more": the scope by §16.10's rules, its repos split by §11.14's eligibility, own indexers
   first; an owner-bound repo goes only to its owner's consented devices (owner decision 126), and a
   team repo that no own indexer serves to one network-scope search indexer, another member's device
   only after the app has named that member once (§18.4's notice); each request is one 4,016 B body
   naming at most 64 repos (owner decision 175)
4  the indexer checks the requester and each repo in its own state (§8.5, §8.12), pins its cached
   snapshot and verifies candidates newest first against the text it holds, inside its remote budget
   and outside every MCP session and run, fetching nothing from evs, api or gkm (§5.8, D-CORE-17;
   I-19)
5  one 16 KiB step, failures after parsing included: verified hits, each repo's coverage and pinned
   (v, C_v), and checked_through_ms
6  the phone compares equal-version chains as HeadCheck does, merges by doc key, keeps its own
   confirmed hits, collapses possible matches the checked span disproves, and labels the hits that
   indexer verified "verified by <device>" (§11.14; §18.5)
7  each further page, on scroll, in the same sizes; relays see only each request's and reply's time and
   fixed size, connect accounts the pair's contracts like any peer's, and every byte debits the transfer
   balance (owner decisions 10, 609; §2.8 connect-5)
8  opening a hit is a read as in F2 step 7, whose text the phone checks, a mismatch alarming and naming
   the indexer; with no designated indexer answering, the default, step 3 falls back to a download of
   all as in F11 step 7, by sync position under §18.4's metered rule, and owner decision 155's
   possible matches
```

**F13. Announce, find and request** (owner decisions [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [126](#od-126), [142](#od-142), [161](#od-161), [169](#od-169)-[171](#od-171), [179](#od-179)-[182](#od-182); v1). Actors: member A's daemon and run; evs; member B's daemon and agent; the repo admin's device.

```text
   A's daemon   evs          B's daemon   B's agent    repo admin
1  |--announce->|            |            |            |
2  |            |<--sync-----|            |            |
3  |            |            |<--find-----|            |
4  |            |            |<--request--|            |
5  |            |<--file-----|            |            |
6  |            |--hint, wake------------------------->|
7  |            |<--grant, decision--------------------|
8  |            |--decided-->|            |            |
9  |--ended---->|            |            |            |

1  at SessionStart A's daemon announces A's run within 10 s, `claims` being auto in a team network
   unless A opted out, per member or project, and renews it hourly while the run moves: an `announce`
   entry in A's directory stream at M6, A's card on the `cards` ref from the directory's format 2
   (§16.11); it carries the run's who (member, sidecar, agent label, harness), what (its redacted
   title, claims and state) and where (the repo id and, if the repo is announced, its name and branch,
   else `private`), and nothing else of the session leaves A's vault (owner decisions 126, 170, 171;
   I-20)
2  B's daemon syncs the directory by sync position (I-19) at each search or view, coalesced to 30 s,
   every 15 min while it serves a harness session, else hourly (§5.4, §18.4); it reads it through the
   directory's own MLS group, in which the first 1,000 live member devices are leaves and later ones
   and agents read by wraps (owner decision 182; §10.4), and ignores, with an alarm, any item not
   signed and pushed under §16.11's path rules by an admitted writer, consented where it is a member
   device (I-EVS-14)
3  B's agent looks for active runs on its task: `directory_list` at M6, a local filter over the folded
   state, and `search_agents` from M10 (owner decision 169); both return directory stubs, attested and
   identifier fields without prose, so B's run stays untainted (I-9; owner decision 142)
4  B's agent calls `directory_request` for read on A's repo, which the directory announced at its
   creation (owner decision 181) or shows only by its id and `private`; as an O-tier tool it passes
   §5.4's Authorize, which builds an `access_request` action and waits for member B's endorsement:
   harness evidence in an untainted run, device or presence in a tainted one (owner decisions 74, 75,
   142)
5  B's daemon files the request entry in B's directory stream, then a notice under the repo's prefix
   q/<repo_id>/, which names no approver (§16.11)
6  evs hints the repo admin's devices, which lease that prefix (§11.10); §18.7 wakes their phones from
   M8, and a desktop raises SidecarEvent access_request (§5.4)
7  a person, on /dev/tty or in an app and never through MCP, signs the RepoGrant into the repo's access
   log, the decision entry and the notice's rewrite to decided (owner decision 8; §8.8); an owner-bound
   repo's requests reach only its owner, whose consented device decides by EvsShare (owner decision
   126). A request to a worker asks to dial the services it announces (owner decision 179), and its
   owner, or a tagged sidecar's sponsor, approves as autogroup:dst-owner (owner decision 180; §8.4)
8  B's daemon reads the decision, verifies the grant at its log position and records the outcome in
   B's vault; KF3 then seats the subject's devices in the repo's group, member devices as leaves and
   agents by wraps (§10.7), and an approved worker request activates once, as a GrantActivate (§16.6)
9  at SessionEnd A's daemon marks the run ended, or handed off: a newer announce entry at M6, a card
   rewrite from format 2, whose replaced version is purged a minute later (owner decision 161);
   readers show the run ended for 24 h
```

### 3.9 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hosted sidecar (X14 b) | no install | keys and plaintext on servers | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03; [owner decision 26](#od-26)) |
| Edge termination of customers' TLS or mail | filtering, coverage | plaintext at URnetwork | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Server-compiled ACL slices | per-client rules only | a breached server could forge rules | superseded (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6)) |
| Bulk evs over the exchange | one transport | contract per pair; 16 KiB frames | rejected (§6, §11) |

Owners weigh the rest: a sidecar on the device client (§5.11), a sealed client index (§11.16), agents as MLS leaves (§8.13), per-network addresses (§15.11), and Redis or MinIO pools for the metadata tier (§19.12; owner decisions [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145)).

### 3.10 Decisions proposed

**D-ARCH-1 (proposed).** This document writes `<root>` for X4's user-name root (ur.network; [owner decision 13](#od-13)), `<net>` for X5's immutable network label ([owner decision 14](#od-14); PLAN.md:25's `<me>`), which an opt-in alias may replace in user-facing names, `<host>` for a zone-relative host and `<blabel>` for a burner's generated label, so a burner domain is `<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, served by the mail host `mx.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 32](#od-32)); `<me>` appears only inside PLAN quotations. The front matter carries it. *Why:* one value, one spelling; no mechanism changes.

**D-ARCH-2 (proposed).** The architecture has the six planes of 3.5 and no others; a new carrier needs an owner's decision, as the dns edge and phone wakes had (owner decisions [71](#od-71), [88](#od-88)), and a checkpointer's own HTTPS call to a witness its log admin named is ruled none ([owner decision 214](#od-214)). *Why:* §6 D-PROTO-3, D-PROTO-5, D-PROTO-6 and §11 D-EVS-1 already split traffic this way, and §19 and §22 need one map.

**D-ARCH-3 (proposed).** F1-F13 implement the directive and the owner decisions each names, and are redrawn when a decision changes. They are §22.7's scenarios: S1-S3 are F1-F3, S4 is F9, S5-S9 are F4-F8, S10 is F10, S11 is F11, S12 is F12 and S13 is F13, with S3 and S4 in device form (§10 KF2, KF4) from M2 and member form at M6. *Why:* OUTLINE §22 asks for tests "mirroring §3", and tests of superseded flows test the wrong system.

**D-ARCH-4 (proposed).** Each flow names the owner decisions it implements. G0's assembly check (§23.8) maps every owner decision to the section text that implements it, and fails on a decision without such text, a citation of a withdrawn D- item, a decided question shown as open, or a Q- option the owner has not chosen presented as the design, unless it is an open question's recommendation marked "(proposed; Q-...)". *Why:* the owner's decisions arrived in rounds while sections were drafted and reviewed; only a mechanical check keeps the body, the decision list and §22's scenarios in step.

### 3.11 Open questions

None open. The 2026-11-03 design-review round, not human peer review, closed these, so peer reviewers may reopen them.

**Q-ARCH-1 (closed 2026-11-03).** Q-PROTO-3 (b), adopted by [owner decision 11](#od-11): Service mode (C9) for edges, FriendsAndFamily (C13) for shares; applied in §6.10.1.

**Q-ARCH-2 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), confirmed by [owner decision 39](#od-39): certs proxies CSRs and alone writes DNS-01 in URnetwork zones; an `accounturi` pin appears only in Team customers' own CAA records; applied in §12.8, §13.8.

**Q-ARCH-3 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): smtpedge splices mail for an MX on mxedge's router interfaces to mxedge over the host LAN, TLS still sidecar to sidecar; applied in §14.4.

**Q-ARCH-4 (withdrawn).** The directive is a requirement (CONVENTIONS §0); ruled-out modes appear only as Alternatives or Departures rows. Q-MAIL-7 goes with it.

**Q-ARCH-5 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), with wakes in v0 ([owner decision 88](#od-88)); applied in §18 (tokens, payloads), §19 (sender) and §2.8.

**Q-ARCH-6 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), confirmed by [owner decision 4](#od-4): no sidecar shares the device client, which runs Opportunistic; applied in §5.5 and Q-PROTO-2.

**Q-ARCH-7 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a), at M4 ([owner decision 85](#od-85)): C14's `UpgradeMux.SetLocalZone` and a `ur tun` resolver answer private names; applied in §12.9, §17.

**Q-ARCH-8 (closed 2026-11-03).** (c): an ephemeral reap is §7.10's removal; it starts a new generation only where the agent held a key that no live Delegation still delivers (§10.5; [owner decision 114](#od-114)); headless sidecars read the config and otherwise only deposit, by §8.5's kind defaults, unless a grant or EvsShare names them, which §8.6's ceiling enforces for ephemeral ones ([owner decision 6](#od-6)); applied in §7.7, §8.

**Q-ARCH-9 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): RecordEntries are sealed whole, record repos' owned refs refuse FORCE and DELETE, and readers find gaps by chain pins; applied in §11.8, §16.8.

Disagreements raised elsewhere are settled there: Q-EVS-3, Q-TLS-6, Q-MCP-5 and Q-MAIL-8 closed in the same round, and owner decisions [2](#od-2), [34](#od-34), [70](#od-70), [75](#od-75) and [86](#od-86) decided Q-EVS-1, Q-MAIL-1, Q-DNS-6, Q-MCP-3 and Q-BRIDGE-6.

### 3.13 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the maps, planes, topologies with the indexer's definition and fallbacks (3.6), F1-F13 (§22.7's scenarios, D-ARCH-3), the service summary, the closure register (3.11) and the decision trace (D-ARCH-4).
- **Consumes:** §1-§23 and the owner's decision record (front matter).
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, Tables, Services and config:** none new.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**

### 3.14 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sections lag the directive or the owner's decisions, so §22's scenarios test superseded flows | High | High | decision citations in flows; D-ARCH-4's check at G0 (§23.8); I-18 |
| A removed leaf stays in a repo's MLS tree until a writer leaf commits its Remove ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | Medium | Low | §10.15's row |
| Outbound mail waits on sound BDAT and DATA preamble proofs | High | High | burner email launches receive-only (F6, F10); both proofs sit on the mail team's critical path (owner decisions [9](#od-9), [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)) |
| A site or Hurricane Electric outage stops every flow and both nameservers; losing the site loses server-held data | Medium; Low | Critical | accepted (owner decisions [94](#od-94), [123](#od-123)); an out-of-hours rota pages from M3 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); mail senders retry (§15.3); devices re-seed from local copies and Postgres rows from D-OPS-18's daily off-site dump (§19.10); record repos and their slots mirror to an indexer where one is designated (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [150](#od-150), [177](#od-177)) |
| P0 safety work (revocations and their rotations, Removes, shreds, erasures) runs at once whatever its volume ([owner decision 186](#od-186)), so a wave of it on one metadata cluster, legal within every network's rates, wears its drives, stops its pushes and evacuation while it lasts and keeps its forgiven excess as wear ([owner decision 190](#od-190)), as §11.21's P0 row states | Low | High | §11.21's P0 row |
| Repos stay on the cluster placed at creation until a later move tool, so the first metadata cluster's writes can outgrow its set ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) | Medium | High | §11.13's write budget refuses the heaviest network first ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); new repos go to the next cluster from §19.9's triggers; §19.9's cohorts row tracks each cluster's own growth, builds the move tool before the earliest projected exhaustion and, until it exists, holds a full cluster to maintenance (507 CLUSTER_FULL) |

### 3.15 Phasing

§23 orders milestones (X15): after the shared M0-M2, recURd and mail run as two tracks ([owner decision 9](#od-9)). F1 needs §5 and §7's P0 with 7-day sidecar tokens (M1; owner decisions [45](#od-45), [103](#od-103), [131](#od-131)), then the config repo (M2; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [112](#od-112)-[114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)); F2 needs §10, §11's v0a and v0b and the PM9A3 metadata set, whose benchmark gates format 1 on drive writes per push (M2; [owner decision 140](#od-140)), then the production cluster (M3); F8 adds §16 (M3). Member-level F3 and F9 arrive with Team at M6 ([owner decision 102](#od-102)); their device forms (§10 KF2, KF4) run from M2. F7 needs C5, C6a, C13 and C14 (M4), Linux first, and C18 for cross-network invites (M6). F4 needs C9, the dns edge, the 443 SNI split and ports 8443, 8883 and 5671 (M5; [owner decision 121](#od-121)). F6 needs mxedge on port 25, DNSSEC and TLSA (M7), with phone wakes from M8's app hosts ([owner decision 88](#od-88)). F10 launches burner email receive-only at M8, once the owner accepts M7's census loss ([owner decision 34](#od-34); D-MAIL-9). F5 and burner replies wait for M9's sound BDAT and DATA proofs (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)). F11 and F2's versionless steps need §11's format 2, with the index, at M10 (owner decisions [163](#od-163), [169](#od-169)), behind its computed drive-write gate ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); F11 reaches other members' claims in the team directory and the team record's run cards once M6's exist. F12's serving side ships at M10, its app-host steps at the later of M10's and M8's exits and its team-indexer steps at the later of M10's and M6's; F13 runs at M6 on format 1's record streams, its phone wakes from M8 and its cards and search steps at M10 (D-PHASE-11). Edges and mail start dark in main ([owner decision 91](#od-91)). recURd needs F1, F2 and F8, then F7; burner email needs F6 and F10, then F5.

## 4. Repositories, code placement, branches, and build

### 4.1 Purpose and scope

This section decides where code lives and how it is built, branched, versioned, published and shipped, including X9's connect changes, operator-core's host contract ([owner decision 251](#od-251)), where the build's operations commands live ([owner decision 274](#od-274)) and the checkout's documents. Components are §5-§18, deployment §19, tests §22, milestones §23.

INTERNAL and unlicensed before [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip, it is now PUBLIC, its README stating MPL-2.0, whose full text is the first `sidecar` commit (4.9); connect, sdk, server, sn (`urfoundation/sn`), build, warp and extension are PUBLIC too, config, vault and xops PRIVATE, mmm INTERNAL. An unclassified service exits 64 (build/all/deploy-rollout.zsh:37-39). At that date all touched repos but sidecar, config and vault shared one commit-msg hook, which 4.9 copies into those three and minio. With no hosted CI, policy lives in Go tests, a leg per shipped build (sdk/dependency_boundary_test.go:81-92).

- Of this module's packages, the root imports only `protocol` and `protocol/bridge`, std-and-protobuf packages, as connect's root imports `connect/protocol` (Q-REPO-3). `protocol` imports `protocol/bridge`, never the reverse, so a type both use is declared only in `protocol/bridge` (4.9). The root never imports `device/`: `cli/` (`ur tun`, `ur bridge`) and sdk's `DeviceLocal` wire `device.Bridge` to the root's `BridgeState`, so Apple's network extensions, the `ios_extension` leg, link of the root only §18.10's forwarding files and of `protocol` only its config, acl, evs and gkm descriptors (D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)). Beyond this repository the root's first-party imports are connect and operator-core's `operator` package, which imports connect ([owner decision 251](#od-251)).
- **Build tags.** Desktop-only code (the OS tun, §17.10; installers; the macOS keychain, §5.10) lives in `cli/` or carries `!ios && !android && !sdk_mobile_bind`. Package connect links gVisor into every importer through its untagged tun.go (connect/tun.go:38-47), so root files that use package connect (client generations and `SidecarEnv`, `Subprotocol` and streams, remote search, sockets dial and listen, the bridge, tls and smtp listeners) carry `!sidecar_http`, as do the engine host interfaces (`host_*.go`), since no hosted server engine runs in the page Worker, whose search engine needs none. The rest, §5.4's events, actions, binding and `Sign` included, uses the root's `Id`, `Logger`, `MonitorValue` and `CallbackList`, and reaches api through the net/http `SidecarApi` (bearer plus DPoP signer), in both legs; connect-facing files convert at that boundary. The root's `Id` is an alias of operator-core's (4.5), which imports connect, on every leg but the `sidecar_http` one, where it stays the root's own `[16]byte` type, a build-tag twin of id.go (id_http.go) whose methods and encodings are identical to operator-core's and which a test holds to them: the page Worker runs no engine and takes no `Env`, so nothing on that leg needs operator-core, the leg links no connect package or gVisor, and §4.7 fails one that does (§18.10; [owner decision 276](#od-276), amending 251 for this one leg). `make size` then measures that leg at about 57.8 MB unstripped, so D-SDK-19's 41,943,040 B goal stays a recorded slip and its miss rule's 74,965,628 B gate stands (§18.10). The `ios_extension` leg links operator-core beside the connect it links through `device/`, and the owner revisited §18.10's 6 MiB extension budget ([owner decision 215](#od-215)) with that leg's measurement, as [owner decision 251](#od-251) foresaw: with the replaying config head reader on the leg it rose to 7.5 MiB ([owner decision 491](#od-491)).
- **The `ios_extension` leg's files.** `check/` seeds the leg from the Forwarder's files, every root `bridge_forward*` file among them, and regenerates its list (check/testdata/ios_extension_leg.txt), which is exactly the Forwarder's and the compiler's closure (§18.10; [owner decision 197](#od-197)), so a Forwarder file tagged out by mistake fails closed. The closure also takes each file outside it whose `init` sets a hook a closure file declares, and what that file needs, but for a short reviewed list of deliberate seams, each with its reason, which `check/` skips ([owner decision 596](#od-596)): the eight registration files tagged `!ios_extension` whose hooks the forwarding role does not serve, `evs_read_provenance.go` (so a read on the leg gives no provenance and the leg links no agent-subkey check), `directory_card.go`, `directory_format2.go`, `directory_removal.go`, `directory_revoke.go`, `identity_cleanup.go`, `record_agent_body.go` and `evs_read_erased.go`, whose `init` gives a read its judge of keys gone from their slots, so off the leg a key a committed ERASE destroyed reads as erased, while on the leg, which reads only the config repo that no ERASE touches and links no ERASE reader, a key gone from its slot still alarms tamper ([owner decision 665](#od-665)), so the list names only what the leg links, and the rule's guard holds for every other `init`. The seed rule is not narrowed for a file it takes wrongly: a file of the sidecar role never carries the Forwarder's prefix, so the role's forwarding setup is bridge_setup_forward.go and its port forwards bridge_daemon_forward.go, and a declaration the closure needs from a file tagged `!ios_extension` moves into a file of the closure, as `EvsGitEmptyTreeOid` moved to evs_git_object.go, the tag staying ([owner decision 275](#od-275)).

### 4.5 Placement and the sidecar/server split

| Component | sidecar | server and other repos |
|---|---|---|
| Host contract ([owner decision 251](#od-251)) | the `<svc>service` engines and any `Sidecar` core a server process runs take an `Env`; sidecar's stores, over the db it grants | operator-core: the interfaces and shared value types, fakes in `coretest`; server/core implements the `Env` |
| Core, subprotocol, MCP, `ur` (§5, §6, §16) | root, protocol/, mcp/, cli/ | api routes (§5, §7) |
| Push (§6.8, §18.7; owner decisions [17](#od-17), [88](#od-88), [104](#od-104)) | `push_`; `pushservice`: publishers, long-poll, wake sender | connect residents, api, taskworker, respectively |
| Access control (§8; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6)) | `acl_`: parser and compiler, run by each device for itself and by the writer of each config head for `AclRows`; gates use only the `AclRows` evaluator | the signed id-only projection: storage, routes, gates |
| sockets (§9) | `socket_`, `socketsservice` | server/cli/sockets |
| gkm (§10) | `mls_`, `gkm_`, `gkmservice` | server/cli/gkm from v0 (D-OPS-2); reconciler in taskworker |
| evs (§11) | `evs_`, `evsservice` | server/cli/evs; GC, packing, drop jobs and the metadata write budget's loop in taskworker (§19.4) |
| File cluster (§19.6; [owner decision 195](#od-195)) | `ServiceHost.Blobs`, an interface only | `urnetwork/minio`, a public fork, holds D-OPS-20's build and MinIO's AGPL source; no module here imports it, and server's Blobs client is minio-go, Apache-2.0 (server/blob.go) |
| dns (§12) | `dns_`, `dnsservice` | server/cli/dns on the dns edge ([owner decision 71](#od-71)) |
| tlsedge, certs (§13) | `tls_`, `tlsedgeservice`, `certsservice` | server/cli/tlsedge; taskworker |
| smtpedge (§14) | `smtp_`, `smtpedgeservice`, `smtpproof` | server/cli/smtpedge |
| mail, mxedge (§15) | `mail_`, `mxedgeservice` | server/cli/mxedge |
| bridge (§17) | `bridge_` (the compiler builds `BridgeState`, in the daemon or an app's VPN component); `device/` (the forwarding role's packet side); `protocol/bridge` | sdk DeviceLocal imports `device/` (sdk/device_local.go:5707, 5800); connect C5, C18 |
| Operations commands ([owner decision 274](#od-274)) | none: 4.7's license list and layering let no command here link server's model or an engine package | server/sidecarctl, one binary for every operations command this build adds (`certs swap` and `renew`, `dns census`, `restoring`, `restore` and `ceremony`, `evs purge-turn-on`, `sidecar restore`, `network sidecar-limit`, the abuse commands), beside the model code its commands call and under server's own dependency, license and layering rules; `bringyourctl`'s and `warpctl`'s existing commands stay where they are, and the customer-facing `ur admin` commands in `ur` |

The host contract is operator-core's `Env` (operator-core/env.go), the root factory of every service an extension uses ([owner decision 251](#od-251)). An extension holds service instances that an `Env` creates, never a package-level service function or global service state, unlike server's own shared-namespace functions (`server.Db`, `server.Tx`, its Redis and blob helpers), on purpose, but for operator-core's one process-wide `Env` ([owner decision 593](#od-593)): `SetGlobalEnv(env Env)` sets it and `GlobalEnv() Env` answers the one last set, or, before any set and after `SetGlobalEnv(nil)`, which tests use to restore, an `Env` whose every accessor refuses with an error wrapping `ErrNotGranted`, never a nil. Every service process the server repo launches builds its `Env` at startup through server/core's `NewProcessEnv`, under `ProcessGrants`, which names each such process, and sets it before it serves. Engines that take an `Env` or a `ServiceHost` keep taking it; only the code server calls with no `Env` of its own reads the global one, sidecar/work and sidecar/handler (below). server/core implements it, wrapping server's existing services, those functions and the sidecarhost, evshost, dnshost, mxedgehost and quotahost packages, and passes it to sidecar's server-hosted code, the `<svc>service` engines and any `Sidecar` core a server process runs, which take the `Env` or the instances they need. Device-side code (`ur daemon`, the apps, their VPN components) takes no `Env` and keeps its own settings and local stores.

```go
// operator-core/env.go, package operator: what a hosting process supplies. Engines never import server, so
// go-redis, minio-go, pgx and prometheus stay out of sidecar and operator-core.
type Env interface { // each accessor answers its service or a typed not-granted error, never a nil
	Db() (Db, error)                             // granted only where the process allows: evs and gkm get none
	Redis() (Redis, error)                       // cas, incr, scripts, TTLs, hash-tagged keys; evs and gkm keep
	                                             // only soft state they rebuild there (owner decision 136);
	                                             // keyspace events only via the shared subscriber, never per
	                                             // client, the pattern that melted the cluster on 2026-07-15
	                                             // (server/model/peer_model.go:32-37)
	Blobs() (BlobStore, error)                   // the segment bucket and each metadata cluster's bucket, by
	                                             // cluster id, the first holding place/ (owner decision 145):
	                                             // If-Match and If-None-Match puts, streamed put, ranged get,
	                                             // prefix list, delete (X13)
	Authenticator() (Authenticator, error)       // jwt -> Principal (server/session)
	Quota() (Quota, error)                       // reserve, commit, release (§20)
	Metrics() (Metrics, error)                   // prometheus in server
	Tasks() (Tasks, error)                       // once-keyed jobs (taskworker)
	Push() (Push, error)                         // server to client (X8)
	ServiceClient() (ServiceClientSource, error) // jwt and urls for the engine's connect client
	// and ServiceHost's other members, Clock (below), ClockCheck (§19.6), Gates (ServiceGates, §19.11's
	// gates, which server implements over CurrentSidecarConfig), Budget (§11.13's write budget) and Abuse
	// (§21.7), beside the domain interfaces through which server-owned data (networks, clients, accounts)
	// reaches an extension
}

// The injected clock, on every leg. ServiceHost.Clock and SidecarSettings.Clock hold it, nil meaning real
// time; the root's Clock and sidecartest.Clock alias it.
type Clock interface {
	Now() time.Time
	After(timeout time.Duration) <-chan time.Time
	AfterFunc(timeout time.Duration, function func()) (stop func() bool)
}

// What each engine a server/cli/<svc> hosts hands back. The host wraps it with readiness, /status, stats and
// PROXY-unwrapped listeners and serves the shape it is handed, never asking by type assertion; pushservice's
// types run inside existing services instead. An engine package states its shape, as
// var _ operator.HttpEngine = (*EvsEngine)(nil); smtpedge, which listens on nothing (§14.9), is an Engine.
type Engine interface {
	Ready() bool // its stores reachable and its state loaded, §19.4's ready column
	Drain()      // takes no new work; returns once work in flight ends or its own bound passes
	Close()
}
type HttpEngine interface {
	Engine
	Handler() http.Handler // one handler for every route of the service
}
type StreamEngine interface { // tlsedge, mxedge
	Engine
	Serve(listener net.Listener) error // once per listener, each on its own goroutine
}
```

Each process grants the db only where its role allows. evs and gkm get none and keep durable state only in `Blobs` (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [19](#od-19), [21](#od-21)): a repo's metadata objects and its gkm group's live on the metadata cluster that the repo's create-only `place/<repo_id>` on the first cluster names, which the engines resolve and cache ([owner decision 145](#od-145); §11.8). The db mirrors server's helpers (server/db.go) as instance methods: callback-style `Db` and `Tx` whose implementation owns retries (serialization failures, lock timeouts), the isolation and read-before-begin options, `Query`, `Exec` and `Batch`, `Rows` that scan into standard types and `Id`, named args and temp tables, all in operator-core's own types with no pgx type; server/core adapts server's pgx helpers to it. Sidecar owns its SQL: its stores (`SmtpEdgeStore`, …) live in sidecar over the granted db and touch only sidecar's own tables, server's T3 harness testing them over server/core's db (§22.4); server-owned data reaches them through operator-core's domain interfaces; and sidecar's operator-core `Extension`, its migrations and its engines' constructors over an `Env`, is what server/core iterates, running the migrations, so hosting another extension is one import and one registration. A store answers a context that ended as an error and never re-raises the db's done panic into the engine's own goroutine, which no handler would catch: the adapters over server's helpers for tlsedge's, mxedge's and smtpedge's stores and the abuse SMTP sink recover every raised value, an ended context included, and return it, since a store call past its timeout or an engine's context ending mid-flush is an ordinary failure every engine retries, and a slow Postgres must not end an edge process (QD-1090).

operator-core's `Id` is server.Id moved: `type Id connect.Id`, with server.Id's database/sql, JSON and Hash marshalling and its parsing, formatting and comparison delegating to connect. Its pgx codec stays in server/core; `server.Id` and the root's `Id` alias it, the root's on every leg but the page Worker's, which keeps a twin (4.4; [owner decision 276](#od-276)); the generators stay where they are, server's `NewId` over `connect.NewId` and the root's on crypto/rand. Its JSON decode refuses everything server.Id or the root's `Id` refused before the seam: server.Id's null and length refusals keep server's words, and an unquoted value, a separator other than a dash and bad hex answer `ErrInvalidId` without echoing input (I-13), every refusal matching `operator.ErrInvalidId`; a well-formed id decodes as before, encodings are byte-identical, and the Scanner and Valuer stay server's exactly, so server accepts fewer malformed inputs than it did, none of which a conforming encoder produces ([owner decision 276](#od-276)). The other value types server shared move with it (`ByteCount`, `NanoCents`, the blob object records, the sentinel errors); server-internal types stay in server.

Until the build's review phase moves the call sites (4.18), sidecar and server keep Go type aliases of the moved types and sidecar keeps `ServiceHost`, so other sections' `ServiceHost.<member>` names stay valid, each naming the `Env` accessor of that name, and sidecar's stores and migrations stay in server, which implements them over Postgres.

**Server-hosted packages ([owner decision 594](#od-594)).** The move lands sidecar's server-hosted code, beside its engines, in four packages that mirror server's own: sidecar/model (tables and queries), sidecar/controller (logic), sidecar/work (taskworker's work) and sidecar/handler (api's handlers). Every exported function of model and controller takes the `Env` (`operator.Env`) as its first argument and reaches Postgres, Redis, blobs and the other host services only through it, never through server's package-level functions; work and handler, which server's taskworker and router call with no `Env`, take `operator.GlobalEnv()` and pass it down. server keeps the hosting: its service mains set the global `Env`, its router mounts sidecar/handler, its taskworker registers sidecar/work, and its migration runner applies sidecar's schema.

- **Imports:** besides this repository's modules, connect with its replaced forks and operator-core are the only first-party modules a sidecar module requires ([owner decision 251](#od-251)), operator-core/coretest only in the test leg; never proxy or the userwireguard it requires (proxy/go.mod:9-10), so `ur proxy add` (cli/UI.md:39-41) runs in `cli/` on §17's userspace `connect.Tun`.
- **Third-party:** `dependencies.yml` lists each module with SPDX id, reason and leg (client, engine, cli, test), operator-core's on every leg and operator-core/coretest's on the test leg alone. Allowed: MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, MPL-2.0 and X11, read as MIT's text plus only its no-advertising clause, which lets src.agwa.name/tlshacks, connect's ClientHello parser on every connect leg, through as a license of its own with no per-module exception ([owner decision 271](#od-271)); refused: GPL family, SSPL, BUSL, custom, unlicensed. Initial: protobuf v1.36.11, x/crypto, docopt-go, pires/go-proxyproto, go-sdk v1.7.0 for mcp/ and go-winio v0.6.2 for §5.8's pipe (server/go.mod:30, 67), purego v0.11.2 for the macOS Keychain (Apache-2.0), wireguard's tun (MIT) for `cli/`'s OS tun (§17.10); in the test leg, `mlsinterop/`'s peers [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Patched libraries.** §15's mail libraries need changes their upstreams do not carry, so each lives in `third_party/` as a module under its upstream path, behind the replaces above, with a URNETWORK.md naming the upstream tag and the patch, as server/third_party/pgx does. `third_party/go-smtp` keeps D-MAIL-3's `ServeConn(conn, ServeConnOptions{AfterStartTls: true})` and adds `ServeTlsConn(conn *tls.Conn) error` over it. The release fixture builds the root at its tag with no replaces (4.9), which links upstream go-smtp, so the root names no fork-only symbol: mail_smtp_serve.go reaches `ServeTlsConn` only through a local interface assertion on `*smtp.Server`, which fails against upstream's server, and `mailSmtpServe` then refuses, closed. `third_party/mox` holds only the packages `dkim`, `dmarc` and `spf` need, with `mlog`'s three counters removed so prometheus stays out of every leg, and both of mox's license files; `dependencies.yml` lists github.com/mjl-/mox as `MIT AND MPL-2.0` and github.com/mjl-/adns. Upstream's mox API is a superset, so it needs no seam and `mailAuthVerifiers` stays the one (§15.5). If an upstream takes its patch the replaces and the assertion go; upstreaming is an external action.
- **Versions:** shared modules match connect, sdk and server, because an uncoordinated bump fails server's `-mod=readonly` build (server/README.md:12); protobuf follows §18.10; golang.org/x/text follows §11.14's normalizer 1: one module version on every leg, at least v0.43.0, which every module of connect, sdk, sdk/build, server and sn now requires, so no bump is owed; what remains is `make check`'s rule below, and from M10 any x/text bump is a new normalizer and a rebuild (§11.14). The floor is v0.43.0 because v0.40.0 and gomobile's v0.41.0, which connect, sdk and sdk/build held on 2026-11-05, have an NFC that wrongly composes 19,960 two-rune strings (every two-rune string checked under go1.27.3, 2026-11-05), U+05D2 U+0307 into U+105C9 and U+10044 U+0307 into U+1E0A among them, which v0.43.0 normalizes correctly under the same reported Unicode version, 17.0.0 (v0.40.0 and v0.41.0 key recomposition on runes clipped to 16 bits, .gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.40.0/unicode/norm/forminfo.go:217).
- **Go.** Every go.mod of connect, sidecar, sdk, server and sn names go 1.27.4, moved from 1.27.3 in one coordinated change for GO-2026-6859, an HTTP/1 server crash in net/http that `make check`'s govulncheck rule fails; `check/` accepts no advisory, the build images' Go base and server's lock.yml `go` line follow, with a re-pin, and the toolchain comes through the module proxy, checked against Go's checksum database. D-TEST-15's one-toolchain rule holds, since x/text chooses its tables by go1.27, which a patch release does not change. Two measurement harnesses stay on go1.27.3 so their frozen baselines stay comparable: server's competition evaluator (server/connect/sim-latency's image digest, GOVERSION guards and toolchain-policy test, server/competitionagent and server/cli/competitionsubeval) and the tests repo's perf runner (tests/runner/perf, whose h1 diagnostic requires a go1.27.3 producer and preflight manifest). ### 4.8 Branches and cross-repo pinning

- **Branches.** Every repo the work touches gets a `sidecar` branch at M0 (§23.4; [owner decision 196](#od-196)), on its normal remote, public where the repo is ([owner decision 118](#od-118)); the extension and apps only if the owner opts in. `urnetwork/minio`, the new fork that holds D-OPS-20's build, is a sibling checkout with its own `sidecar` branch, and the owner creates its GitHub repo before any push ([owner decision 195](#od-195)). operator-core, whose GitHub repo the owner created, is a sibling checkout too, its `sidecar` branch opened with the seam ([owner decision 251](#od-251)). The `tests` repo has one as well, opened from `main` locally, so its fixtures can change with the build. `main` stays production-ready (build/README.md:5); in minio, whose upstream calls it `master`, that branch plays `main` ([owner decision 270](#od-270)).
- **Pins.** server@sidecar's lock and build@sidecar's submodules pin the same `sidecar` commits of sidecar and operator-core, which server's source-graph tests confirm.
- **Merge, never rebase.** A rebase orphans pinned commits and skips the commit-msg hook (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:17-18). Merge `main` in weekly and before each gate, in the order connect, operator-core, sidecar, sdk, sn, server, warp/config/vault/xops/mmm/minio, build, tests, re-pinning each time. minio's weekly merge in is a no-op while its upstream stays archived; xops pins a commit of the fork in place of playbook-minio-clusters.yml's `minio_commit`, and that commit is on the public fork before a host runs it, as [owner decision 195](#od-195) keeps the AGPL source in one public place ([owner decision 270](#od-270)).
- **To `main`** at each milestone's Gn-out (§23.8): every touched repo, server and sdk included, in that order, once the pinned set passes its checks, migrations are additive and release-compatible (connect/CODESTYLE.md:85-89), connect's default-off changes lead and the code is dark (D-OPS-10). Branch migrations stay pending until their own Gn-out registers them (D-OPS-6), so one track's merge never applies the other track's group, and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118); §23.9).
- **What a Gn-out merges** ([owner decision 268](#od-268)). Each gate's pinned commit set is recorded when its local checks are reported, and an approved Gn-out merges that set, never the tip, in the order above; a later milestone's merge brings the rest, and a group's migration registration (D-OPS-6) is the one commit on top of the set. Before any recorded commit reaches connect's `main`, the merge runs `check/`'s `TestX9ReadyForMain` for the gate, which refuses a landed change that no default-off test pins and a row due by the gate whose marker has not landed; no hand-picked commit set replaces the recorded one. [Owner decision 609](#od-609) withdraws C19, and with it the gate under which every Gn-out merge of connect waited for FS-125's sweep, reversing that part of [owner decision 268](#od-268).
- **The closed source graphs** ([owner decision 267](#od-267)). server's competition and sn's release gates each list the repositories they build from, and both take sidecar in one change landing with M0's Gn-out, before server and sn merge to `main`: sn's as a fourteenth release repository with a new `sidecar_go_source_hash`, the competition's as an eleventh repository, `sidecar`, last in every list and keyed `sidecar` in sim-latency.yml, with an additive migration. The evaluator takes it through new producer releases, as minimum-work and work-coverage were added: six programs beside the historical ones (evaluator-sidecar.sh, evaluator-minimum-work-sidecar.sh, evaluator-work-coverage-sidecar.sh and a prepare-round-baseline program for each), new dependency maps, and a selector `source_graph_policy` in the round's settings, the preparation config, the completion receipt and the future-epoch policy, whose value `sidecar/1` means the eleven repositories and whose omission the ten, an empty, null or unknown value refused. The historical producers and their pins stay byte for byte, but for one entry the owner named: the controller's pin of evaluator-work-coverage.sh is corrected to the tree's file, the ten-repository competition's qualified release, from which the sidecar producer is cut. sim-latency's source ledger stays strict: once the eleven-repository release is in use every epoch and generation pins sidecar and a ledger of the ten is refused, so the release opens only with a new ledger, at a season boundary or by an explicit re-baseline, never midway through a season. The owner qualifies the release on the evaluator hosts together with 4.7's go1.27.4 re-qualification; until then the evaluator stays at ten repositories and fails closed on a server commit that needs sidecar, so server's `main` is not a competition epoch's source in between.

### 4.9 Generation, targets, versions, license, style

- **Protobuf:** `protocol/Makefile` runs `protoc -I=. --go_out=. --go_opt=paths=source_relative protocol/*.proto protocol/bridge/*.proto` from the repo root, so files register as `protocol/<name>.proto` and `protocol/bridge/<name>.proto` in package `urnetwork.sidecar`; sdk and server link connect's and sidecar's packages, and a duplicate path or name panics at init (protobuf@v1.36.11/reflect/protoregistry/registry.go:42, 128, 152), so `config.proto`, `acl.proto` and `directory.proto` import the types 4.4 lists for `protocol/bridge`, never redeclare them. `tool` pins protoc-gen-go v1.36.11, and output is committed. The sections' `proto` fences are the wire: protocol's fence test holds every declaration to its fence in DESIGN.md and RECORD.md, and a field the code declares ahead of a fold sits in that test's additions lists (protocol/design_unfenced_test.go) until a design-records fold writes it into its fence and, in the same commit, drops its line there, touching only those entries; a fence never moves ahead of the code ([owner decision 273](#od-273), beside 252's rule for a new row or §4 id).
- **Mobile, wasm, C ABI:** gomobile binds only sdk (§18.3). `make size` gates from v0: the `ios_extension` leg (`device/`, `protocol/bridge` and the root's forwarding files; D-SDK-20) fails if sidecar adds over §18.10's budget, 7.5 MiB stripped (owner decisions [197](#od-197), [215](#od-215), [491](#od-491)), and the `sidecar_http` js leg is measured unstripped from M2 against §18.10's 41,943,040 B goal and miss rule (D-SDK-19). No C ABI: desktop apps use the `ur` daemon (§5) or sdk's generated ABI (sdk/cgo/gen/gen.go).
- **Versions.** Development paths stay unversioned, as connect's and sdk's do; the release runs their steps (build/all/run.sh), which §22.4's release fixture checks:
