### 4.10 CLI distribution

| OS | Artifacts and signing | Path |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | one `.pkg` and one `.tar.gz` per architecture, no universal binary, of a Developer ID bundle, `ur.app`, id `network.ur.cli`, with a provisioning profile and hardened runtime (D-CORE-12), claiming both app groups, `6BGU69Q742.group.network.ur` and `6BGU69Q742.group.com.bringyour.urnetwork`, so a direct-download app reaches the daemon's app-group socket; notarized and stapled (run.sh's notarize step) | `/usr/local/lib/ur/ur.app`, with `/usr/local/bin/ur` and `/usr/local/bin/git-remote-ur` as links to its executable |
| Linux | `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.pkg.tar.zst` (nfpm) and `.tar.gz`, direct downloads through `install.sh`'s verified path, with no apt or yum repository, GPG key or repository host ([owner decision 213](#od-213); updates: proposed, Q-REPO-6) | `/usr/bin/ur`; the script uses `/usr/local/bin/ur` |
| Windows | `.zip` holding `ur.exe`, a copied `git-remote-ur.exe`, `LICENSE` and a README naming the folder and the PATH step, with no `wintun.dll` ([owner decision 222](#od-222)); winget later; signtool SHA-256 with a timestamp (windows/app/SIGNING.md:17), the step failing when no signing thumbprint is set, unlike windows/app/build.ps1 | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\URnetwork\ur.exe` |

- **`git-remote-ur`** ships beside `ur` in every package as a link to the same binary, which dispatches on argv[0] (a copy in the Windows zip); git runs it for `ur://` URLs from PATH (gitremote-helpers(7); §11.11), so Windows users add the zip's directory to PATH. **`git-credential-ur`** ships the same way: a local credential helper that `ur mount add` and `ur mount share` configure (§11.11's binding).
- **Artifacts.** `ur-<version>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` and `.pkg`, `ur_<version>_<arch>.deb`, `ur-<version>.<rpmarch>.rpm`, `ur-<version>-<pkgarch>.pkg.tar.zst` and `ur-<version>-windows-<arch>.zip`, following build/all/linux/README.md's spellings: 14 files for the six targets.
- **Build.** `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath` with `GOEXPERIMENT=greenteagc` and `-ldflags "-w -s"`, as run.sh's `sn_cli_release` builds release binaries, from `cli/`'s module, archive times from `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (server/cli/api/Makefile:1, 4); macOS's keychain goes through purego (D-CORE-12).
- **Release integrity.** Signing is the gate ([owner decision 77](#od-77)), and a release is promoted, not every build signed ([owner decision 264](#od-264)). Every release runs a VirusTotal scan (run.sh's `virustotal`) and builds `ur`'s artifacts and an unsigned `SHA256SUMS` as ordinary assets of its GitHub release, run.sh waiting for no one. When both holders of the offline two-person Ed25519 key (§2.6) pick a release, they SSH-sign its sums offline, under namespace and identity `ur-release`, and a commit on mmm publishes `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.sig` and `latest.json` under `https://ur.io/recurd/ur/`; `latest.json` is listed in the signed sums, and `ur-promote.zsh` never moves it backward. No private key touches the build host, a repo or vault. The public key is published at `sidecar/RELEASE-KEY.pub` and `https://ur.io/recurd/release-key.pub`; before the key exists neither file does, and `install.sh` refuses. `install.sh` on ur.io (mmm's branch from M0, §23.4; owner decisions [15](#od-15), [16](#od-16), [196](#od-196)) pins the key, reads `latest.json`, verifies signature and checksum (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`, OpenSSH 8.1+), fetches the artifacts from the GitHub release and refuses on any failure. What holds: GitHub alone cannot ship a client, but ur.io serves both the script and its pin, so ur.io alone can, to a new script install (§2.8 EX7), and a fresh install cannot tell an older signed pair from the newest, so ur.io could roll a new install back to an older signed release. `install.sh` prints the key's fingerprint and the repository path that publishes it, so a careful user can compare, and nothing more is built; notarization and Authenticode remain second checks on the macOS and Windows artifacts. From M4 the sums also list the key origin's loader and `sidecar.wasm`, which `sidecar.ur.io` serves only from a promoted build (§18.8; [owner decision 221](#od-221)).
- **Proving key sets ([owner decision 266](#od-266)).** `smtpproof`'s setup transcripts, about 0.9 GiB a key set, ship in no package, and its proving keys are published nowhere: a host that sends mail fetches the key set its release pins, by hash, from ur.io at idle, as §14.5 says, with no token and no account, checks the transcripts against the circuits its own build compiles and derives its proving keys from them before it uses one (§14.9; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 3, 3.2.7), about 0.9 GiB fetched and 4 GiB kept. §2.8's smtp-7 lists what that path's host sees, the fetching address above all, which marks a prover host ([owner decision 253](#od-253)). The cut of the proof's 20 shapes to what M7's census justifies is met without the census: eleven shapes of one domain size, none sized by a guess about recipients ([owner decision 433](#od-433)).
- **Harness configs (§16)** use `ur`'s absolute path, since GUI-launched hosts lack the shell PATH ([MCP debugging](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2025-03-26/tools/debugging.md)). v0 has no self-updater.

### 4.11 The documents in the sidecar checkout

The checkout holds documents only, on `main` (§4.3): at the root, README.md (its images in `design/readme/` and `design/mocks/previews/`), DESIGN.md with its reviews (DESIGN-REVIEW1.md to DESIGN-REVIEW3b.md and DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md) and with DESIGN-DEFER.md, which documents every deferred decision, one entry each, and is generated with DESIGN.md from `design/source/` ([owner decision 587](#od-587)), FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md and `research_notes/`; under `design/`, the business and input documents: PLAN.md, product.md, the pitches (pitch1.html to pitch5.html, with PDFs of the last three), the market notes (market.md, market2.md, gap.md, improve.md, improvements4.md, sentiment2.md), two overview PDFs, a saved IETF draft (d.html), mocks/, reports/ (among them the Tailscale, agent-work-record and 2026-11-05 search-index reports), design-research/ (the sheets behind DESIGN.md's research links) and cold5/'s outreach drafts. All of it is public as it is, history included, the move into `design/` kept as renames (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)), so DESIGN.md's citations (`sidecar/design/pitch5.html`, `sidecar/design/market2.md`, `sidecar/design/reports/Encrypted repo search index formats.md`) resolve publicly, and its research links point into `design/design-research/`. Code starts on the `sidecar` branch (§4.8). The `ur` command sketch, cli/UI.md, sits outside every repository; a copy goes to `design/UI.md`, and its spellings then replace the build's own for the pass-change and lock commands, `--replace`, the recovery login and the daemon's `--port`, each a one-line rename; until the copy is there the build keeps the spellings §5 states ([owner decision 265](#od-265)).

### 4.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scrub, then publish a filtered clone (D-REPO-8 as drafted) | Business material stays private | A second repository, a rewrite and a path allowlist | Rejected ([owner decision 117](#od-117)) |
| `/v2026` in development paths | One identity in every build | Breaks connect's and sdk's convention and consumers' v0.0.0 requires; the rewrite already publishes `/v2026` | Rejected (D-REPO-1) |
| `cli/` in the root module | One module | The root requires `smtpproof`, whose requirements then enter every consumer's graph, sdk's legs included | Rejected (D-REPO-2; [owner decision 104](#od-104)) |
| Host interfaces declared in sidecar (`ServiceHost`), each engine's store implemented by server | No new repository | Sidecar's SQL and migrations live in server; each extension declares a host of its own | Rejected (D-REPO-3; [owner decision 251](#od-251)) |
| The root keeps its own `Id` on every leg, operator-core's converting to it | The page Worker links no connect package | Two id types at every boundary between sidecar, operator-core and server | Not taken, but for the page Worker's leg, which meets no such boundary and keeps a twin (owner decisions [251](#od-251), [276](#od-276)) |
| Package-level service functions, as server has (`server.Db`, `server.Tx`) | No factory to pass | One shared namespace per process, so no host can give an extension instances of its own | Rejected ([owner decision 251](#od-251)) |
| Sign every release's `SHA256SUMS` | Every release installable through `install.sh` | An offline two-person signature cannot gate a pipeline that runs unattended and almost daily | Rejected: promotion ([owner decision 264](#od-264)) |
| The operations commands in a module of this repository (`sidecar/sidecarctl`) | Beside the engines they operate | 4.7's license list and layering let no command here link server's model or an engine package, so `dns census`, `evs purge-turn-on` and `sidecar restore` could not be built | Rejected: server/sidecarctl ([owner decision 274](#od-274)) |
| Narrow the `ios_extension` leg's seed rule, or untag a file, when the rule takes a file wrongly | No rename or move | A Forwarder file tagged out by mistake no longer fails closed | Rejected ([owner decision 275](#od-275)) |
| The mlswg's vectors fetched at test time, none committed | No unlicensed bytes in the repository | A fetch in every test run, and a history rewrite for the files already landed | Rejected ([owner decision 263](#od-263)) |

§23.10 rejects D-REPO-9's private mirrors ([owner decision 118](#od-118)).

### 4.13 Decisions proposed

**D-REPO-1 (proposed).** Use §4.7's go.mod, its two patched mail libraries as modules under `third_party/` behind replaces, §4.9's proto naming, an unversioned development path, and the release rewrite to `/v2026` that connect and sdk use (§4.9), which keeps `third_party/` beside the rewritten tree ([owner decision 278](#od-278)). *Why:* §4.3's replace and lock rules, protobuf's init-time panic, and the release convention; Go accepts a v2026 tag only on a `/v2026` path, which only the release tree has.

**D-REPO-2 (proposed).** Use §4.4's tree: MLS in root `mls_*` files ([owner decision 43](#od-43)), server-only engines in `<svc>service` packages ([owner decision 104](#od-104)), the forwarding role's packet side in the leaf `device/` over `protocol/bridge`, which alone declares the types it parses, linked in apps' VPN components with only the root's forwarding files (D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)), connect-facing and engine-host root files under `!sidecar_http` (D-SDK-19), test peers only in `mlsinterop/`; `cli/` and `smtpproof/` are nested modules the root never requires; the core services' interfaces and the value types server and sidecar share in the operator-core repository's `operator` package, which imports connect, with their fakes and conformance suites in its test-only `coretest` module ([owner decision 251](#od-251)). *Why:* CODESTYLE groups files by prefix (connect/CODESTYLE.md:49-62); owner rule 1; a message declared twice panics at init, and importing connect links gVisor; test peers must not raise consumers' versions, and a root requirement reaches every consumer's module graph; server imports sidecar, so what both need lives in a module below both.

**D-REPO-3 (proposed).** Engines live in sidecar and take operator-core's `Env`, the root factory of every service they hold, which server/core implements over server's services; server hosts each one, and sidecar owns its SQL over the db an `Env` grants, registering its migrations through operator-core's `Extension`, and its other server-hosted code lives in its model, controller, work and handler packages, whose model and controller functions take the `Env` first and whose work and handler, which server calls with no `Env`, read the one each service process sets at startup (§4.5; Q-REPO-1; owner decisions [251](#od-251), [593](#od-593), [594](#od-594)). *Why:* logic and its persistence stay in sidecar, URnetwork-only infrastructure stays behind interfaces ([owner decision 48](#od-48)), and service instances from one factory, never a shared namespace, let any host supply an extension's services.

**D-REPO-4 (proposed).** Enforce §4.7 with `make check` and §4.9's v0 `make size` gate; ship no binding or C ABI. *Why:* no hosted CI exists, sidecar must be checked as the bindings build it, and a cgo file would enter gomobile's macOS slice.

**D-REPO-5 (proposed).** X9 changes are generic, additive, off by default and wire-compatible, tested in connect and merged to connect `main` first. *Why:* connect serves every client.

**D-REPO-6 (proposed).** Consumers wire sidecar and operator-core as §4.7 lists, the forks' replaces included, server's competition graph and sn's release gates take sidecar ([owner decision 267](#od-267)), and branches follow §4.8, a Gn-out merging its gate's recorded commit set ([owner decision 268](#od-268)). *Why:* the gates fail closed, pins must stay reachable (owner rule 4), and migration versions are positions.

**D-REPO-7 (proposed).** License, style, hook and distribution per §4.9 and §4.10, with sums the two holders sign offline when they promote a release ([owner decision 264](#od-264)). *Why:* the open-source promise, the owner's commit rule, and GitHub alone must not be able to ship a client; ur.io, which serves both `install.sh` and its pin, alone can, to a new script install, which §4.10 and §2.8's EX7 state.

**D-REPO-8 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 117](#od-117): no scrub, archive, filtered clone or path allowlist; the repo keeps its documents and history.

**D-REPO-9 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): no private mirrors; every `sidecar` branch uses its repo's normal remote and merges to `main` at each Gn-out.

### 4.14 Open questions

**Q-REPO-1.** How do PLAN.md:5-7's repos split a service? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 19](#od-19)):** (a), a sidecar engine that server hosts and backs with its stores (D-REPO-3). **Amended by owner 2026-11-15 ([owner decision 251](#od-251)):** the engine takes operator-core's `Env`, which server/core implements over server's services; sidecar owns its SQL over the db an `Env` grants and registers its migrations through operator-core for server/core to run, and server-owned data reaches it through operator-core's domain interfaces (4.5). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-2.** [X9] Which connect changes may land on connect's `sidecar` branch? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 22](#od-22)):** (b), §4.6's dispositions, as owner decisions [85](#od-85), [86](#od-86) and [176](#od-176) amend them. *Residual:* C17, for the extension's streaming Worker only, after §18's spike.

**Q-REPO-3.** May `protocol/` be an exception to connect/CODESTYLE.md:26? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 52](#od-52)):** (a), with a `make check` test that `protocol/` and `protocol/bridge` import nothing else from sidecar (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-4.** When does sidecar go public, and with which documents? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 (owner decisions [117](#od-117), [118](#od-118)):** now, as it is (§4.11), superseding the scrub and later publication of owner decisions [51](#od-51) and [107](#od-107); nothing waits for publication (§4.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-5.** Should server-only engines live in the root (PLAN.md:13)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 104](#od-104)):** (b), child packages, and (d), a nested module for the X7 prover (§4.4); `cli/` is a nested module too, so the root never requires the prover (§4.7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-REPO-6.** How do Linux users update `ur`, now that v1 ships no apt or yum repository, so `apt upgrade` and `dnf upgrade` never reach it ([owner decision 213](#od-213))? *Options:* (a) they re-run `install.sh`, whose verified path checks the offline key's signature, or fetch the next `.deb` or `.rpm`, so no update reaches a Linux host by itself; (b) apt and yum repositories later, signed at promotion by a second offline two-person GPG key, their trees under ur.io/recurd through mmm; (c) a self-updater in `ur` that checks the same signed `SHA256SUMS`. *Recommendation:* (a) for v1, the owner deciding at v1's exit review whether Linux users need (b). *Blocks:* nothing before v1's channels (M6). *Decider:* owner.

### 4.15 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:13** ("all service code goes in the root"): engines live in `<svc>service` child packages and the X7 prover in a nested module, so no mobile or wasm build links them ([owner decision 104](#od-104); Q-REPO-5), and the forwarding role's packet side in the leaf `device/`, so the iOS extension links of the root only its forwarding files (Q-SDK-5, closed by peer review; D-SDK-20; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **PLAN.md:9-21** (the tree) stands; `cli/` carries its own go.mod so the prover's requirements stay out of consumers' module graphs ([owner decision 104](#od-104)).

### 4.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the tree and modules, operator-core's `Env` with its db, domain interfaces, engine contract and `Extension` (`ServiceHost` and the aliases until the review phase's sweep), the X9 rows, the checks, §4.8's and §4.11's rules, §4.9's release rewrite, and §4.10's install paths (§11, §16).
- **Consumes:** server/core's `Env` over server's services and host packages ([owner decision 251](#od-251)); §6 (X8; §6.4's requester feature bit), §10 (X12), §11 (X19; placement; §11.14's normalizer 1, which x/text follows), §13 (X1), §17 (X18; C5's dial fence and per-flow idle, `WindowDelegation`, C18's alias map), §18 (X14; `sidecar_http`, `device/`), §19's gates and pending migrations (D-OPS-6), §22.4's `sidecar_testhooks` and release fixture, §23's milestones.
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, tables:** none (routes: C11).
- **Services and config:** §4.5's server column, server/sidecarctl included; operator-core's repository and `sidecar` branch; lock.yml; build/.gitmodules; run.sh; `ur-promote.zsh`; deploy-rollout.zsh; dependencies.yml; on ur.io, `install.sh`, `recurd/ur/`, `recurd/release-key.pub` and the key set path.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §6 adds no protobuf `service` blocks; §6, §9-§15 and §19 follow §4.5's placement, their engines taking an `Env` and, from the review phase's move, keeping their SQL in sidecar, which §22.4's T3 tests over server/core's db ([owner decision 251](#od-251)); §6.9, §7.9, §8.8 and §17 declare what `device/` parses only in `protocol/bridge`'s `signed.proto`, `auth.proto` (§8.8's `GrantRevoke`, `Suspend` and `Unsuspend` included) and `bridge.proto`, which `config.proto`, `acl.proto` and `directory.proto` import (4.4); §5.4 and §18.10 keep connect out of the `sidecar_http` leg, whose `Id` is the root's own twin ([owner decision 276](#od-276)), and §18.10 excludes `host_*.go` (4.4); §15.5 reaches the forks only as 4.7 states, and §14.5 fetches its key sets as 4.10 states; §10, §11 and §19 keep each repo's metadata on the cluster its `place/` object names ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); §5.8 and §11.11 define `git-remote-ur`'s daemon mode; §17, §2.10 and §22 cover C18, and §2.8's connect-5 states what remote search leaves visible, C19 being withdrawn ([owner decision 609](#od-609)); §23.9 merges every touched repo at each Gn-out.

### 4.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engine or root code bloats the iOS extension, which since [owner decision 197](#od-197) links the root's forwarding files | Medium | High | `<svc>service` packages; the leaf `device/` and the `ios_extension` leg's file and descriptor lists; `make size` at the budget [owner decision 491](#od-491) set |
| With the root's `Id` an alias of operator-core's, operator-core enters the iOS extension's leg; the page Worker's `sidecar.wasm`, which keeps a twin `Id` and links no connect, still measures about 57.8 MB unstripped against D-SDK-19's 41,943,040 B goal | High | Medium | The extension's leg re-measured, the owner revisiting [owner decision 215](#od-215)'s budget with it ([owner decision 251](#od-251)), which [owner decision 491](#od-491) raised to 7.5 MiB; the goal's slip recorded under the miss rule's 74,965,628 B gate, and a test holding the twin to operator-core's `Id` ([owner decision 276](#od-276)) |
| ur.io serves a new script install an altered `install.sh` with its own pin, or an older signed release | Low | High | `install.sh` prints the key's fingerprint and the repository path that publishes it; `latest.json` is in the signed sums and `ur-promote.zsh` never moves it backward; §2.8's EX7 names the case; notarization and Authenticode on macOS and Windows |
| Branches drift from mains that release almost daily | High | Medium | Weekly and per-milestone merges; pending migration groups (D-OPS-6) |
| A secret or AI-attributed message on a public branch stays served by hash (https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/removing-sensitive-data-from-a-repository, read 2026-11-03) | Low | Medium | The hook in every clone (connect/.githooks/commit-msg:23-27); `--scan` before each push and at each Gn-out (§23.8); secrets only in vault |
| A Go release breaks purego, leaving macOS pass-only | Low | High | Pinned version; a Keychain round trip in `make check`; cgo fallback |
| A tagged consumer resolves two sidecar module paths or registers a descriptor twice | Low | High | 4.9's rewrite; §22.4's release fixture |

### 4.18 Phasing

- **v0, before code (M0):** LICENSE, the hook, the root's and `cli/`'s go.mod, dependencies.yml and `make check` on sidecar's `sidecar` branch, merged at M0's Gn-out (DESIGN.md and the documents are on `main` already, 708bb45); M0's branches; the lock entry, the release step and its fixture.
- **The operator-core seam ([owner decision 251](#od-251)), now:** operator-core with ServiceHost's interfaces moved over, the `Env`, the db interface and the shared value types, Go type aliases left in sidecar and server so existing code compiles unchanged, and server/core building the `Env` over the existing host packages; new code takes the `Env`, and every service process server launches sets the global one at startup ([owner decision 593](#od-593)). In the build's review phase, the pass of reviews and fixes after the draft of M0-M10: the call sites, sidecar's SQL and migrations moving from server into sidecar's model, controller, work and handler packages (4.5; [owner decision 594](#od-594)), and the fakes' move into `coretest`. The move is planned now, as an inventory of the sidecar branch's server-side files with the package each goes to and the server imports each drops, in ordered move tracks that run as a barrier once the draft lanes drain, after the owner's choices from the complexity review of 2026-11-17, so that code they drop is not moved.
- **v0, first usable:** §4.6's M1, M4 and M5 rows; the first hosted engine; signed `ur` packages; the `make size` gate; `sidecar_http`'s import rule (M1) and size measure (M2); `device/` and its `ios_extension` rule, with the root's forwarding files (M4; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).
- **v1:** C18 (M6); C20 (M7; [owner decision 269](#od-269)); 4.7's x/text rule on ahead of M10's index code, every module being on v0.43.0 already; Homebrew and winget; [no apt or yum repository](DESIGN-DEFER.md#repo-apt-yum-repositories), `.deb` and `.rpm` staying direct downloads ([owner decision 213](#od-213); Q-REPO-6). **Later:** [C4](DESIGN-DEFER.md#repo-c4-browser-carrier) with §18's worker, and [C17](DESIGN-DEFER.md#repo-c17-js-connect-build) for that streaming Worker if its spike needs it.
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#repo-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Blocking:** M0's `make check` blocks the first consumer pin; C13 blocks C18; C20 blocks M7's `strict_chain`; C19 is withdrawn, so nothing waits for its sweep ([owner decision 609](#od-609)).

## 5. The Sidecar core: identity, keys, lifecycle, local state

### 5.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sidecar.Sidecar` (lifecycle, components, events, the outward-action gate); the client identity (X10); the client side of login, enrollment, pairing, admission, owner consent, refresh, revocation and AUTHZ1; and the daemon, local IPC, local state, keys, recovery and platform variants. §6 owns the subprotocol; §7 enrollment routes, auth keys, OAuth, the AUTHZ1 server fix and config records; §8 policy; §10 MLS; §11 evs; §16 MCP and approvals; §18 hosting; §20 counting.

### 5.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-CORE-1 | Import connect only | PLAN.md:7 |
| R-CORE-2 | Hold "an authenticated jwt, connect client, api, and encryption key" | PLAN.md:14 |
| R-CORE-3 | The CLI speaks stdio MCP by default | PLAN.md:19-20 |
| R-CORE-4 | Run in the sdk, the apps, and the extension's web worker | PLAN.md:28 |
| R-CORE-5 | The git identity is the sidecar client id | PLAN.md:59 |
| R-CORE-6 | `--instance`; `ur login/logout/status/daemon/install-daemon/uninstall-daemon` | cli/UI.md:10-19 |
| R-CORE-7 | A keychain encoded with a pass; changing the pass re-encodes it | cli/UI.md:82-85 |
| R-CORE-8 | Any number of in-daemon agents, free, with their bytes debited (pitch5's "never metered" changes) | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:844, :849; owner decisions [4](#od-4), [10](#od-10) |
| R-CORE-9 | `ur connect --token`; "Log in with URnetwork" | sidecar/design/mocks/recurd-app.html:712, :930 |
| R-CORE-10 | Agent tokens ≤1 h, key-bound, never in the agent's environment | sidecar/FEEDBACK-SYSTEM.md:139; §2 I-7 |
| R-CORE-11 | No sidecar credential can administer the network | §2 I-6 |
| R-CORE-12 | Identities survive the client reaper | server/model/network_client_model.go:4179, :4199 |
| R-CORE-13 | Settings-owned tunables; a `Logger` with connect's methods; pure Go for wasm; mobile budgets | connect/CODESTYLE.md:140-151, :179-182; [R:sdk-clients](design/design-research/sdk-clients.md) §3 |
| R-CORE-14 | Outward actions need an I-8 approval from every entry point | §2 I-8; [owner decision 75](#od-75) |

| R-CORE-18 | Each network's search index cache stays sealed on the device, is fetched by sync position, holds no query, and is deleted with the content or access it derives from | [owner decision 166](#od-166); §11 D-EVS-26 |

### 5.3 What exists today

**connect**
- `BringYourApi` has `AuthNetworkClient(Sync)`, `RemoveNetworkClient` and `GetClientKey`, but no refresh (connect/api.go:20-62, :256-330, :548-570). `NewClient` (connect/transfer.go:2267) takes a `ClientKeySeed` (:1657-1663) and `ClientAuth` (connect/transport.go:348-364).
- `ClientKeyManager.Sign` signs without a label (connect/transfer_key.go:221-229), and the key history does not stop an operator malicious from first contact (connect/transfer_key_history.go:22-26). The ClientKey is plain Ed25519 from a 32-byte seed (connect/transfer_key.go:127-129).
- Package connect's untagged tun.go imports gVisor (connect/tun.go:38-50), so a file using any connect type, even `Id` (connect/id.go:15), `Logger` (connect/log.go:41), `MonitorValue` or `CallbackList` (connect/util.go:74, :220), links the IP stack.

**server**
- A client token creates only its own children (`source_client_id`, server/model/network_client_model.go:191, :374-394). A child is exempt from the client caps (:535, :757-779), never becomes a peer (connect/transfer.go:17611-17617) and ends with its parent (server/session/by_jwt.go:679-700).
- The reaper deactivates a top-level client after 30 idle days and deletes it 30 days later, and deletes a child after 30 days unseen (server/model/network_client_model.go:4179, :4199, :4467). One resident serves each client id and instance (server/model/network_client_resident_model.go:62-68).
- `/auth/code-create` escalates a client token (server/api/route_authz.go:123), and expiry is not enforced (server/session/AUTH.md:229; §7.3); a removed client's tokens stop at once (server/session/AUTH.md:197). `GET /auth/refresh` takes a bare Client token (route_authz.go:115), and `POST /network/auth-client` (OwnClient) mints and reissues client tokens (:132), neither with a proof of possession.

**Missing:** everything below.

### 5.4 Sidecar: fields, settings, lifecycle, components

```go
// Every leg: sidecar.go, settings.go and the root's id, log and monitor files import no connect package, so
// §18.10's sidecar_http leg links them (§4.4) and no connect package, its Id being the root's own twin of
// operator-core's (owner decision 276). Sidecar is safe for concurrent use.
type Id = operator.Id // operator-core's: server.Id moved, type Id connect.Id with its marshalling (§4.5;
                      // owner decision 251); connect-facing files convert: connect.Id(id); NewId stays here, on
                      // crypto/rand

type Logger interface { // connect.Logger's methods (connect/log.go:41); connect-facing files adapt it
	Info(args ...any)
	Infof(format string, args ...any)
	Warningf(format string, args ...any)
	Errorf(format string, args ...any)
	V(level int32) Verbose // Verbose: Enabled(), Info, Infof
}

// MonitorValue[T comparable] and CallbackList[T any]: the root's copies of connect/util.go:74, :220.

type SidecarApi struct { // net/http: bind, refresh, the exchange and the sidecar routes (§7-§20)
	stateLock  sync.Mutex
	byJwt      string                                        // the authenticated jwt
	dpopSigner func(method, url, ath string) (string, error) // the ClientKey's proof (§7.4), by crypto/ed25519
	transport  http.RoundTripper // connect leg: dials by its ClientStrategy's ConnectSettings().DialContext
	                             // (connect/net_http.go:777, connect/net.go:232), egress-bound as
	                             // connect/net_http.go:3663-3668 requires; sidecar_http: net/http's fetch
}

type Sidecar struct {
	host           SidecarHost // Store(); KeyStore() (nil: pass only); TokenSource() (nil: D-CORE-8's refresher)
	settings       *SidecarSettings
	sidecarApi     *SidecarApi
	state          *MonitorValue[SidecarState] // Locked → Unenrolled ⇄ Offline ⇄ Online (5.6); a locked
	                                           // store → Locked (5.9); only a verified SidecarRevoke → Revoked
	eventCallbacks *CallbackList[SidecarEventFunction]

	stateLock sync.Mutex
	keychain  *keychain        // nil while locked; holds this network's root key R_n (5.9)
	identity  *SidecarIdentity // ids and identity public key
	leg       *sidecarLeg      // declared per leg: !sidecar_http, a BringYourApi on the same jwt, the components
	                           // and one connect.Client per client generation; sidecar_http, the long-poll (§6.8)
}

type SidecarAction struct { // every outward action (I-8)
	Kind      SidecarActionKind // tls/ or smtp/ publish or listen; forward; expose; egress change; invite or share;
	                            // alias create or delete; agent-config write or delete in a shared repo (§16.5);
	                            // DNS user record set or delete; mail to a non-member with no approved-recipient
	                            // record (§15.7's rcpt/; owner decision 280), or to any non-member in a tainted
	                            // run; an access request through the team directory (§16.11; CanonicalAction
	                            // version 3); payment; a restore; a TL4 allowance for a recipient domain (§14.4).
	                            // On the wire one verb a value (§16.8): 1 publish,
	                            // 2 listen, 3 forward, 4 expose, 5 egress_change, 6 invite, 7 share,
	                            // 8 alias_create (burners too, §15.8), 9 alias_delete, 10 agent_config_write,
	                            // 11 agent_config_delete, 12 dns_set, 13 dns_delete, 14 mail_send,
	                            // 15 access_request, 16 payment, 17 restore, 18 mail_tls_unauthenticated (owner
	                            // decision 436), new kinds appending; publish and
	                            // listen cover tls/ and smtp/ alike, since host and socket_name say which
	Canonical []byte            // built by the daemon; payload_sha256 = SHA-256(Canonical)
	Risk      SidecarRisk       // 1 normal, 2 high, the wire's values (§16.8); every action is normal: no policy
	                            // field and no classifier raises one, and no decision needs an SSHSIG, in v0 and
	                            // every milestone until a customer asks (owner decision 279)
	RunId     *Id               // a decision binds (approval_id, run_id, agent_id) and authorizes at most
	AgentId   *Id               // `uses` distinct actions, each once (§16 D-MCP-11)
	Effect    SidecarEffect     // live, set by the caller: what Authorize runs once the use is reserved (§16.6)
	Outcome   *SidecarOutcome   // set by Authorize
}

type SidecarEffect interface { // one outward action's effect, idempotent per effectKey, which is empty under a
	// standing grant, where no ledger row is kept
	Run(ctx context.Context, effectKey []byte) (effectRef []byte, err error)
}
type SidecarOutcome struct { // what a use's effect came to (§16.6)
	State     string // done, not_done or uncertain
	EffectRef []byte // the component's reference to what it did
}
// A kind's lookup reads only the stored action, so a restart reconciles a reserved use with no caller alive; a
// kind with no registered lookup is refused before its Reserve.
type SidecarEffectLookup func(ctx context.Context, canonical []byte, effectKey []byte) (*SidecarOutcome, error)

type SidecarEvent struct { // AddEventCallback, `ur status`, the sdk listener (§18.5), ur://acl/grants
	Kind        SidecarEventKind // state, approval_pending, member_added, member_removed, key_changed, refused,
	                             // admission_alarm, recovery_rebind, recovery_window, recovery_unseen (5.6),
	                             // admissions_near_cap: on admin devices, from 90% of config_admissions' cap, with
	                             // §7.10's cleanup list,
	                             // head_alarm (§6.4); index_mismatch, index_malformed (§11.14); search_alarm: an
	                             // indexer's hit that its text disproves, or a local hit it omitted (§11.14);
	                             // history_drop: a drop's state changed (§11.7); access_request: an approver's
	                             // pending directory request, and access_decided: the requester's, with its
	                             // outcome; directory_erasure: a repo owner's revocation still waiting for the
	                             // directory's erasure runner past 24 h, then done (§16.11); erasure: an erasure
	                             // this device runs or may finish changed state (§11.12); mail_send: an internet
	                             // send's outcome for a recipient domain changed (§14.5); evs_conflict: §11.11's
	                             // restart row left a local conflict ref, an ordinary event; evs_alarm: storage
	                             // that fails a reader's or writer's check (EvsAlarm); evs_gap: a re-pin past
	                             // §11.9's budget (VerifiedSince); record_alarm: the record's and the directory's
	                             // reader alarms (RecordAlarm; §16); credential_store: an enrolled daemon found a
	                             // readable network by_jwt in a host store (5.6), with no path or value, ur status
	                             // naming the store kind; ct_alarm: §13's CT watch, Evidence[0] the leaf's
	                             // SHA-256; mail_receiver_alarm: D-MAIL-15's (§15); bridge_alarm (§17); key_changed:
	                             // gkm serves under this sidecar's id a ReaderKey it never signed (§10.5's
	                             // readerkey row; owner decision 358)
	State       SidecarState
	Reason      SidecarStateReason // Unenrolled: expired, refused, parent_lost, session_ended, keystore_lost;
	                               // Offline: subprotocol_store_failed, the damaged sealed file in the
	                               // network's subprotocol store a generation could not start on (5.9's
	                               // Failed; owner decision 616); Revoked: signed (§18.5's GetStateReason)
	GroupId     *Id // membership kinds: the §10 group
	SidecarId   *Id // membership kinds: the leaf or wrapped reader; admission_alarm: the admitted sidecar;
	                // recovery_rebind: its signer; recovery_unseen: the recovered device; head_alarm: the peer,
	                // nil for a fork evs shows; index alarms, history_drop and evs_alarm: the signer;
	                // search_alarm: the indexer; record_alarm: the writer or signer; mail_receiver_alarm: the
	                // receiver
	RepoId      *Id    // index alarms, search_alarm, history_drop, directory_erasure, erasure, evs_conflict,
	                   // evs_alarm, evs_gap, record_alarm, mail_receiver_alarm
	RefId       *Id    // index alarms, history_drop, evs_alarm, evs_gap; evs_conflict: the local conflict ref
	Path        string // index alarms: the alarmed path; history_drop: its first listed path (§18.5's Drops
	                   // lists all); evs_conflict, evs_alarm: its path; a path local to this device, never
	                   // logged (I-13)
	DropId      *Id              // history_drop
	DropState   SidecarDropState // history_drop: pending, cancelled, executing, done (a held drop reads done,
	                             // owner decision 184), refused, or invalid: it failed this device's checks (§11.7)
	NotBefore   time.Time        // history_drop: its window's end (owner decision 183)
	SearchAlarm SidecarSearchAlarm // search_alarm: mismatch (an opened hit's text disproves it) or omission (a
	                               // local confirmed hit that no page of the checked span returned)
	RequestId   *Id // access_request, access_decided: the directory request; directory_erasure: its erasure request
	Outcome     string // access_decided: approved, denied, cancelled or expired; directory_erasure: pending or done
	SendId      *Id // mail_send: the send, whose outcomes §18.5's GetSendResult reads
	ApprovalId  *Id
	HeadAlarm   SidecarHeadAlarm // head_alarm: fork (two pins that disagree; a head evs serves that does not
	                             // extend this device's pin is one, SidecarId nil and Evidence this device's
	                             // RefHead and evs's), withheld (PROOF OF WITHHOLDING), unverified, unwitnessed
	                             // (24 h without a consistent witness; 1 h for a revocation it signed), or
	                             // rollback: a push reset presenting a durable topic below the version this
	                             // client holds (§6.8; owner decision 300), SidecarId nil and Evidence the
	                             // two TopicVersions as protobuf bytes, the held one first
	Evidence    [2][]byte        // head_alarm: my pin and the peer's or api's, as §6.5 encodes them (AuthPin,
	                             // GroupHead, GenHead or RefHead); recovery_rebind at a void: the AuthPins
	                             // at which keychain.wrap was sealed to the voided binding and re-sealed (5.9);
	                             // ct_alarm: [0], the leaf's SHA-256; key_changed: [0], the foreign key's SHA-256
	EvsAlarm    SidecarEvsAlarm  // evs_alarm, a closed set: missing_segment, tamper (a failed entry hash, AEAD,
	                             // oid or statement), version_rule (off §11.7's rule), epoch_overdue (a writer
	                             // 1 h past due_by_ms) or prefix_rule (Later, with 8.8's rules)
	VerifiedSince time.Time      // evs_gap: the time of the newest re-pin past §11.9's budget, which the pin
	                             // record holds; EvsRepo.VerifiedSince(refId) answers it later, zero when
	                             // nothing was skipped
	RecordAlarm SidecarRecordAlarm // record_alarm, a closed set of 14: chain_gap, chain_fork, bad_entry (RECORD.md
	                             // section 5.4's steps 1-4, section 5.5's steps 1-3, 5 and 6), depositor_kind,
	                             // early_removal (a BASE or ERASE taking an entry before keep_days, or a class 7
	                             // entry), path_rule, parked_writer, over_cap, over_limit (§16.11's limits row),
	                             // id_reuse, bad_erasure (an ERASE, CUT or CLOSURE from another signer, or an
	                             // erasure_request that fails its check), bad_decision, log_check (RECORD.md
	                             // section 10.2) and moderation, which apps show as a notice; head_alarm stays
	                             // HeadCheck's, index_mismatch the index's and evs_alarm storage tampering's
	BridgeAlarm string           // bridge_alarm: block_conflict (§17.4), share_holder_removed (§17.9),
	                             // principal_mismatch (§17.9's verify), state_unverified (§17.8), block_refused
	                             // (D-BRIDGE-16) or, from a VPN component, narrowing_overdue (§18.10's memory row,
	                             // backing off to daily; owner decision 487)
	Erasure     *SidecarErasure  // erasure: its id, state and what is left (§11.12, §11.13's wait)
}

type SidecarErasure struct { // §11.12's erasure as its eraser's device, or a device that may finish it, sees it
	ErasureId   Id
	State       string    // fenced: its CUTs committed, its documents masked and unpublishable, its own keys
	                      // gone with the first ERASE; rewriting; waiting: a 429 for its allowance or turn, or
	                      // room for its CUT in a ref's full erasure set (§11.12's cut row);
	                      // done: every key destroyed; stalled: no device that may finish it is running
	ObjectsLeft int64     // rekey objects not yet re-keyed (§11.13's wait row)
	BytesLeft   int64     // their closure bytes
	NextTry     time.Time // the last 429's retry_after_ms; zero when none waits
	Finish      time.Time // §11.13's bound from BytesLeft, the allowance and the turns; zero below the limit
}

type SidecarStatus struct { // Status(): `ur status`, §18.5's GetState and GetStateReason
	State       SidecarState
	Reason      SidecarStateReason
	Generation  int64     // the bound client generation (5.5)
	WitnessedAt time.Time // the newest consistent HeadCheck witness (§6.4); zero: none yet
	Unverified  [][]byte  // the open UNVERIFIED auth pins (§6.4), as AuthPin bytes; empty: none
	CtWatchDegraded bool  // §13's CT watch cannot run as it should
	Lines       []string  // one line a condition, such as an unmirrored log or a waiting erasure, filled by each
	                      // component through the core's status seam and printed by `ur status` as is; nothing
	                      // parses them
}

type SidecarIdentityBinding struct { // 5.5; signed by the ClientKey and the identity key
	NetworkId, SidecarId, ClientId Id
	Generation                     int64 // 1 for a sidecar_id's first binding, then n+1 for every new client:
	                                     // re-enrollment, pairing, fallback (5.8)
	ClientPublicKey                []byte
	IdentityPublicKey              []byte
	IssuedAt                       time.Time
}
// On the wire, in protocol/bridge/auth.proto: SidecarIdentityBinding{network_id = 1, sidecar_id = 2,
// client_id = 3, generation = 4 (int64), client_public_key = 5, identity_public_key = 6, issued_at_ms = 7 (int64)},
// carried as SignedSidecarIdentityBinding{body = 1, client_signature = 2, identity_signature = 3}, body being the
// first message's bytes. Each signature is Ed25519 over §6.9's signed bytes with SIGNED_SIDECAR_BINDING = 0x1A01:
// purpose binding-client by the ClientKey, binding-identity by the identity key. Verifiers check the received body
// bytes, never a re-marshal. Hello.binding and POST /sidecar/bind carry the marshalled wrapper, and 5.15's
// signatures column stores those bytes verbatim, since the table's other columns cannot rebuild them.

type SidecarSettings struct { // validate refuses every number that is not positive, on every leg, so zero is
	// never unlimited or off; only a field tagged settings:"zero" gives zero a meaning, which its comment states:
	// Search.CacheByteCount (in memory), AutoLockTimeout (never), IdleExitTimeout (never)
	Instance, ApiUrl, PlatformUrl, AuthUrl, AppVersion string
	EvsUrl, GkmUrl, SocketsUrl, DnsUrl                 string // every url empty in DefaultSidecarSettings, so
	                             // NewSidecar refuses until its host sets them from §18.9's embedded host table,
	                             // the one copy of these names (§19.4's; owner decision 282)
	Connect               *SidecarConnectSettings      // client generations (below)
	ProtocolSettings      *SidecarProtocolSettings     // §6.6
	TokenRefreshSettings  *SidecarTokenRefreshSettings // sdk's schedule (sdk/device_token_manager.go:20-27, :266-275): jti-drawn 0.4-0.5 window, 5 min floor, 15 min retry
	KeychainSettings      *SidecarKeychainSettings     // Argon2id parameters, pass attempts (5 per 10 min) and
	                             // AutoLockTimeout: 10 min with no request on any local socket (control, mcp, hook,
	                             // git), never while 5.8's busy rule holds; zero never locks (5.9; owner decision 284)
	LocalSettings         *SidecarLocalSettings        // sockets; IdleExitTimeout: 10 min, zero never exits, counted
	                             // only by an auto-spawned daemon (5.8); RequestTimeout: 30 s for a local request's
	                             // own work, a person's wait (a /dev/tty confirmation, the daemon's presence
	                             // prompt) running under its method's own bound, and git-mode streams and MCP
	                             // sessions keeping theirs (Mcp.CallTimeout); FirstPort: 17000 (5.8);
	                             // EventRingEventCount and EventWaitTimeout: 5.8's events method
	Mcp                   *SidecarMcpSettings          // §16
	Ingest                *SidecarIngestSettings       // §16.7
	Record                *SidecarRecordSettings       // §16.8
	Search                *SidecarSearchSettings       // §16.10; 5.9's index cache; §11.14's remote search
	Directory             *SidecarDirectorySettings    // §16.11
	ComponentQueueMessageCount, ComponentQueueByteCount int // 256 envelopes, four of §6.6's 64-message peer
	                             // queues; 1 MiB, 256 envelopes in their 4 KiB pool class, a reassembled body
	                             // counting by its size, so one 256 KiB body takes a quarter of the queue
	MemoryBudgetByteCount int64 // contains §6's process-wide reassembly, idempotency and credit caps; proving
	                            // (§14) sits outside it, under the injected prover's own MemoryMaxByteCount
	                            // (2,496 MiB: two loaded shapes and one proof in flight, kept by counting and a
	                            // collection after each proof; owner decision 647; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section
	                            // 3, 3.2.8):
	                            // SmtpSenderSettings.ProverConcurrency defaults to 1, and a host records p/ only
	                            // after Prover.Measure finishes inside that bound, one that cannot recording
	                            // none and only queueing
	StreamChunkByteCount  int
	Log                   Logger // nil: connect.DefaultLogger() (glog), adapted; sidecar_http: none unless set
}

type SidecarSearchSettings struct { // §16.10's limits, 5.9's cache and §11.14's remote search; defaults only from
	// DefaultSidecarSettings(), which hosts adjust per class as sdk's applyMobileLowMemoryClientSettings does
	// (sdk/mobile_memory_policy.go:332; §18.4); a daemon designated for search (§7.9) applies CacheByteCount
	// 16 GiB and MemoryBudgetByteCount 192 MiB (owner decision 175)
	CacheByteCount         int64            // 4 GiB; 0 keeps the cache in memory (ephemeral sidecars)
	MemoryByteCount        int64            // 64 MiB of decoded index state, inside MemoryBudgetByteCount; app
	                                        // and page hosts set §18.4's smaller working sets
	VersionCacheByteCount  int64            // 256 KiB of 5.9's version-table pages a process, inside MemoryByteCount
	BackgroundByteCount    int64            // 1 GiB a day a network of sync downloads
	MoreByteCount          int64            // 1 GiB a call
	AllPolicy              string           // §18.4's mode for all: background (desktops, indexers), on_demand
	                                        // (ephemeral, cloud)
	HintCoalesce           time.Duration    // 1 min a repo, on the leading edge: a quiet interval's first hint
	                                        //   fetches at once (§16.10; owner decision 450)
	CursorTimeout          time.Duration    // 10 min idle, local and remote cursors
	HeadRefreshInterval    time.Duration    // 10 min: at most one forced head refresh a repo
	NonWriterSyncInterval  time.Duration    // 15 min: a reader that is not a writer syncs an owner-bound index
	                                        // at most this often (§16.10's receipts)
	SessionSearchCount     int              // 2 at once a session
	SessionSearchRate      SidecarRate      // 5 a second, burst 10, a session
	SessionCursorCount     int              // 16 open a session, the oldest dropped
	DaemonSearchCount      int              // 4 local searches at once
	PageCpu                time.Duration    // 2 s of CPU a page, local or remote
	PageCandidateCount     int              // 1,000 candidates verified a page
	TooBroadCandidateCount int              // 20,000 candidates in a partition answer too_broad
	PageByteCount          int              // 64 KiB of MCP results a page
	RemoteMode             string           // "on" until the person picks on, own or off (5.9's state)
	RemoteTimeout          [2]time.Duration // 3 s unmetered, 5 s metered without a first page, then the next
	                                        // indexer
	RemoteServe            bool             // answer remote searches once designated: true on daemon hosts,
	                                        // false on app hosts
	RemoteSearchCount      int              // 4 remote searches computing at once, beside DaemonSearchCount
	RemoteQueueCount       int              // 16 waiting, each at most RemoteQueueTimeout, else
	                                        // RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
	RemoteQueueTimeout     time.Duration    // 1 s
	RemoteCpuPerMinute     time.Duration    // 30 s of CPU a minute for all remote work
	RemoteCursorCount      int              // 64 open remote cursors, the oldest dropped
	RemoteRequesterRate    SidecarRate      // 30 a minute, burst 10: per requester at an indexer, and per
	                                        // indexer at a requester
	RemoteOwnAskCount      int              // 2 own indexers a search asks at once (§11.14's order row)
	RemoteSkipTimeout      time.Duration    // 2 min: a failed indexer is not asked (D-SDK-27)
	RemoteOnlineTimeout    time.Duration    // 10 min: how long a HelloResult, Pong or page keeps an indexer
	                                        // online, and the own indexer that answered last first
	RemoteRefusedTimeout   time.Duration    // 10 min: a repo an indexer refused in coverage is not asked of it
	RemoteServedTimeout    time.Duration    // 24 h: 5.9's memory of which repos each indexer served
	RemoteMismatchCount    int              // 3 mismatches from one indexer within RemoteMismatchInterval, 24 h,
	RemoteMismatchInterval time.Duration    // void its claims and skip it for RemoteDistrustTimeout, 24 h
	RemoteDistrustTimeout  time.Duration    // (§11.14's merge row)
	SkewGuard              time.Duration    // 40 min: evs's time check both ways (§11.8's 5b), which bounds a
	                                        // fold; a value of the format, changed on no side alone
	PinRingCount           int              // 64 (version, chain) pairs kept a ref, to match a coverage's pin
	RetainFactor           int              // 2: a retained bucket lives at most 2 of its windows past its
	                                        // roll-up
	ResyncInterval         time.Duration    // 1 h: §11.14's resync
	SyncRoundCount         int              // sync rounds at once a network: 4 on daemon hosts, 1 on app hosts
	                                        // and page Workers
	SyncRetryInterval      time.Duration    // 30 s, doubling to ResyncInterval: a round that failed on a read
	                                        // (these fourteen: DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.1)
	ServedRecordTimeout    time.Duration    // 30 d: an owner's indexer keeps 5.9's served records, by their day
	ServedRecordCount      int              // 8,192 served rows at most, the oldest days dropped first: a last
	                                        // bound that ordinary use and one abusive reader never reach (owner
	                                        // decision 294)
	CompanionInterval      time.Duration    // 5 min on every host: the companion push's cadence (§11.14); 1 min once
	                                        // D-TEST-11's M2 run fixes 1 KiB blocks; no server signal carries it
}

// 5.6's revocation of another of this member's devices (D-CORE-20), on every leg, a read_only or ephemeral
// caller answering REVOKE_NOT_CAPABLE: ur devices revoke confirmed on /dev/tty, a remote-mode app's control calls
// (5.8) and §18.5's SidecarApprovals reach it, never MCP
type MemberDevice struct { // Devices(): this member's admitted sidecars, this one first
	SidecarId  Id
	Name       string    // its config device name
	This       bool      // the calling sidecar, which signs out instead
	ReadOnly   bool      // a page Worker (§18.8)
	Ephemeral  bool      // a quick burner
	State      string    // live, pending (suspended while its revocation awaits cosigns), parked, stale (§10.9
	                     // removed its leaf as stale from every group this device is a leaf of that seated it,
	                     // at least one) or revoked
	AdmittedAt time.Time
	LastChange time.Time // its newest leaf change in a group this device is a leaf of, its credential's
	                     // not_after less 90 days in that group's tree (§10.9); zero: none seen
}
type DeviceRevokeItem struct { // one row of a plan
	Effect   string // park, void, stands, reseal (5.9's backup rule) or key (offered for KeyRevoke)
	Kind     string // what the row names: device, delegation, recovery_binding, key, evs_share, grant, ...
	Id       []byte // an Id's 16 bytes, a recovery_binding's 32-byte key hash or a key's key_id (§6.9)
	Name     string // a device's or key's name, or an EvsShare's repo
	Position uint64 // the entry that carries it
}
type DeviceRevokePlan struct {
	PlanId     Id     // the first 16 B of SHA-256 over the target and its revocation state, the reason, since_n,
	                  // Signatures, Presence and the key item ids, never a statement header (5.6's sign)
	SidecarId  Id
	Name       string // the target's config device name
	Reason     string // "lost" or "compromise", SidecarRevoke's reasons (§7.9)
	SinceN     uint64 // compromise: where P starts (5.6), with its entry's time
	SinceTime  time.Time
	Items      []DeviceRevokeItem
	Signatures int  // counted signatures needed: 1, or k for an AdminSet member's device, this one counting once
	Presence   bool // set from the log, never by the caller: RevokeDevice needs presence (5.6's approval)
}
type DeviceRevokeError struct { // every refusal of the two calls below
	Code     string // 5.6's REVOKE_ codes
	Position uint64 // REVOKE_PARKS_SELF: the entry that puts this sidecar in P
}

	sinceN uint64) (*DeviceRevokePlan, error) // sinceN 0: the proposed position, which needs a loss time (5.6's
	// plan; owner decision 292); lost ignores both

	// presence: the host's check over the act's countersigned bytes (§7.9's presence row), returning §6.9's

	// only while the plan's Presence is unset; revokeKeyIds: the plan's key items the person left selected;
	// proposalId: §7.9's 32-byte proposal_id, set while k > 1 pends

// The search engine, search_*.go on every leg, and search_remote_*.go, which asks and serves §11.14's remote
// search, where connect links; §16.10's tools and `ur search` call it, and §18.5's SidecarSearch wraps it.
type SearchRequest struct {
	Text         string              // §16.10's query
	Repos        []Id                // empty: every readable repo with its index on (never secret, config, mailcfg)
	Scope        SearchScope         // SearchCached (default: buckets and any cached all), SearchLatest, SearchAll:
	                                 // the partitions; §16.10's breadth is SearchBreadth (SearchBreadthRepo,
	                                 // SearchBreadthNetwork, SearchBreadthAll), §22.4's oracle parameter
	                                 // sidecartest.SearchScope, a struct holding one of each, and search.proto's
	                                 // scope keeps its own 1 and 2
	Since, Until time.Time           // zero: unbounded
	Fuzzy        bool                // near hits even when 3 or more exact hits exist
	Filters      []SearchFieldFilter // §16.10's doc-table filters: from, subject, agent, run, kind, path prefix
	IncludeSpam  bool                // mail the device's join marks spam, which a search otherwise leaves out, and
	IncludeTrash bool                //   trash likewise (§15.7, §16.10's include; owner decision 444)
	AllowMetered bool                // scope all may fetch past §18.4's 25 MiB on a metered link
	Remote       string              // "": the network's remote mode (5.9's state); "off": this search stays local
	PageSize     int                 // default 50
}
type SearchHit struct {
	Repo, Ref  Id
	Path       string         // or a derived document's registered name (§11.14)
	Version    uint64
	Time       time.Time
	Signer     Id             // the document version's writer, for grouping by agent (§16.10)
	Fields     []SearchField  // display fields: title or subject, from, and kind-specific ones
	Snippet    string         // verified hits: around the match; mail: i/'s snippet; else empty
	State      SearchHitState // SearchVerified, SearchConfirmed, SearchPossible, SearchNear, SearchUnmatched (a
	                          // local possible or near hit an indexer's checked span disproved, §11.14's merge)
	Partition  SearchPartition
	Correction string         // SearchNear: the corrected term
	By         string         // "": this device; else the answering indexer's config name (§11.14)
}
type SearchProgress struct {
	Searched, Total          int       // partitions
	FetchBytes, FetchedBytes int64     // scope all: bytes still to fetch, and fetched so far
	Uncovered                int       // changes not yet searchable
	Waiting                  string    // "", "metered", "offline", "update"
	CoveredFrom              time.Time
	Remote, FallbackReason   string    // §18.5's remote states and fallback reasons
	RemoteBy                 *Id       // the indexer asked, or the one a notice names
}
// SearchStatus and SearchIndexer carry §18.5's SidecarSearchStatus and SidecarIndexer fields.
func (self *Sidecar) Search(ctx context.Context, request *SearchRequest) (*SearchStream, error)
func (self *SearchStream) Next() (page []SearchHit, progress SearchProgress, done bool, err error) // replaces the last
func (self *Sidecar) GetSearchStatus(repoId *Id) (*SearchStatus, error) // search_status (§16.10), GetStatus (§18.5)
func (self *Sidecar) SetSearchConditions(unmetered, charging, lowPower bool) // the host's reports (§18.7)
func (self *Sidecar) SetSearchForeground(foreground bool) // the app's lifecycle and a page Worker's tab visibility
                                                          // (§18.7); unreported counts as background
func (self *Sidecar) RunSearchBackgroundSync(ctx context.Context) error // an OS window, ctx's deadline its budget
                                                                        // (§18.5's budgetMillis); resumes next time
func (self *Sidecar) SetSearchPolicy(repoId *Id, mode string) error // nil repoId: every repo; "": the host default
func (self *Sidecar) DropSearchCache(repoId *Id) error              // nil repoId: every repo; 5.9's state stays;
                                                                    // resets the sync's loaded manifest, plan and
                                                                    // versions of each dropped ref, so its next
                                                                    // round fetches again (owner decision 599)
// remote search's requester side, on app hosts only (§18.4; CLI and browser requesters are Later):
func (self *Sidecar) GetSearchIndexers() []SearchIndexer                      // those that may answer, own first
func (self *Sidecar) SetSearchRemote(mode string) error                       // on, own or off (5.9's state)
func (self *Sidecar) AcknowledgeSearchIndexer(memberId *Id, allow bool) error // the notice; false sets own

// !sidecar_http files only, with the client generations, streams, sockets, bridge, tls and smtp listeners and
// the engine host interfaces (host_*.go), as §4.4 says; the sidecar_http leg declares SidecarConnectSettings
// empty and NewSidecar without components.
type SidecarConnectSettings struct {
	ClientStrategySettings    *connect.ClientStrategySettings
	ClientSettings            *connect.ClientSettings // Required, no P2P; provides Network, plus Service while on tls/ or smtp/ (§13.6) and FriendsAndFamily while sharing (§8.11); never Public (§6)
	PlatformTransportSettings *connect.PlatformTransportSettings
}

type SidecarComponent interface {
	Name() string                 // "evs", "sockets", "mail", "bridge", "tls"
	Attach(env *SidecarEnv) error // per client generation; returns promptly
	Close()
}

type SidecarEnv struct { // immutable; Ctx ends with the generation
	Ctx         context.Context
	Client      *connect.Client
	Api         *connect.BringYourApi
	SidecarApi  *SidecarApi
	Identity    *SidecarIdentity
	Secrets     SidecarSecrets // keychain namespace
	Store       SidecarStore   // component directory, streaming I/O
	Subprotocol *Subprotocol   // §6: inline, zero-wait handlers; streams
	Authorize   func(ctx context.Context, action *SidecarAction, decision *bridge.Signed) error // the gate: takes
	                                                    // the same action, its Effect included, and sets its Outcome
	Log         Logger
}

func NewSidecar(ctx context.Context, host SidecarHost, components []SidecarComponent, settings *SidecarSettings) (*Sidecar, error)
func (self *Sidecar) Pair(ctx context.Context, childJwt string) error // 5.8: same network, new ClientKey, generation n+1;
	// before anything is sent, childJwt must name this network and carry both the strict_exp and the admin_refused
	// claim (§7.4; D-CORE-7; owner decision 291)
func (self *Sidecar) AddComponent(component SidecarComponent) (func(), error)
```

**Lifecycle.** Per client generation, `run()` builds the client, registers §6's id 21842, handles §6's `core` push, and calls `Attach` outside `stateLock`; in the `sidecar_http` leg a generation is its long-poll (§6.8), which carries `core`, and no component attaches: §18.10's kept files run on `SidecarApi` and the keychain. Complete envelopes go to their component's bounded, zero-wait queue, which drops and counts when full (connect/CODESTYLE.md:119). `StreamData` fills per-stream buffers bounded by §6.7's credit instead, since stream bytes cannot be dropped (:123); an overrun resets the stream with PROTOCOL. Callbacks never block or call `CloseAndWait` (:171).

**Outward-action gate (I-8).** Every outward method calls `Authorize`, which passes under an active approved grant (§8) or a §16.6 decision that passes its spend check ([owner decision 75](#od-75)), reserving the use durably before the effect (§16 D-MCP-11); otherwise it writes an `ApprovalRequest`, emits `approval_pending` and returns pending. `Authorize` runs the effect itself: under a decision, §16.6's steps 1 to 6 with the action's `Effect`; under a standing grant, the effect with an empty key and no ledger row. A retry returns the recorded `Outcome` without calling `Run` again unless that outcome is uncertain, and the approval's mutex covers steps 1 to 4 only, never `Run`. A kind with no registered `SidecarEffectLookup` is refused before its Reserve. In a tainted run (I-9) each outward action needs a fresh decision: the daemon spends no further use of a decision whose request was untainted (§16.6's TS1), and harness evidence counts only if the matching `requests` rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)). MCP, control mode, the CLI, local SMTP submission and the sdk remote backend all pass it; server-visible actions carry the decision to §8.10's gate.

### 5.5 Identity (X10)

| Level | Id | Durable | Key | Admitted by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Network | `network_id` | yes | — | platform |
| Member | `user_id` (§7) | yes | recovery keys (5.9) | login; an admin's config-repo record |
| Sidecar (a device instance in one network) | `sidecar_id` | until revoked | Ed25519 identity key ([owner decision 44](#od-44)); X-Wing ReaderKey (§10.5) | `SidecarAdmit` in the config repo (5.6) |
| Client (transport) | `client_id` | until reaped | connect ClientKey | operator-signed history |
| Agent | `agent_id` in the sidecar | per registration | Ed25519 subkey, `not_after` ≤30 d (v1) | an attribution label |
| Forwarding (apps; [owner decision 197](#od-197)) | its forwarding Delegation's `delegation_id` | until revoked, superseded or its sidecar's revocation | Ed25519 forwarding key; X-Wing forwarding reader key; its forwarding clients' ClientKeys, all generated in the VPN component and never exported | its sidecar's forwarding Delegation (§7.9, §18.6) |

- **Binding.** `POST /sidecar/bind` appends each `SidecarIdentityBinding` (5.4) to a never-reaped log, which §6's `Hello` checks (D-PROTO-13). A `sidecar_id`'s first binding has generation 1 and creates its `sidecar_identity` row; each new client (5.8) binds generation n+1, the newest plus one, under the same `sidecar_id` and identity key, which that row holds, keeping admissions and grants. A client binds once, whatever the `sidecar_id`: `sidecar_identity_binding.client_id` is unique across every sidecar, so a copied token cannot bind a key of its own, and a binding must carry the key enrollment stored in `network_client_owner.client_public_key` where that column is set (§7.4, §7.7; 5.15's refusals). The binding names the client id as well as its key, so a peer resolves a client to its sidecar from signed bytes (§17.9). The `sidecar_id` names MLS leaves, ReaderKeys, statements, admissions, client names and bridge addresses; the client id stays the transport, contract and policy subject. Git committers ([owner decision 81](#od-81)) and §8's `sidecar:<id>` and `client:<id>` resolve through the log, and a sidecar reads a repo iff a subject it hosts does.
- **Agents.** A device or `--instance` is one sidecar per network. Agents are attribution labels on its client (`source = agent_asserted`) holding no credential or group key; the daemon signs, decrypts and enforces per-agent reads for them. Own reach (grants, an overlay address, an ssh key) needs the agent's own sidecar under its own OS user, container or VM ([owner decision 4](#od-4)); otherwise grants attach to the sidecar, usable by any local process ([owner decision 47](#od-47)). An in-daemon agent has a durable `agent_id`, one per (sidecar, label): a random `Id` minted at the label's first session and kept in the network's keychain.ur beside that agent's subkey record, so it is restored with keychain.ur (5.9's backup) and cannot be guessed from the label; once `AgentRevoke` tombstones it, the label's next session mints a new one, a new registration being a new `agent_id` ([owner decision 285](#od-285)). The daemon resolves a session's label to its id, which `McpSession` exposes and every MCP tool passes, into evs pushes' sealed provenance and `NewSidecarAction`'s `agentId` (§16.5; [owner decision 470](#od-470)); a session with no agent has none.
- **Signatures.** §6's typed `Signed` (a purpose and §6.11's `SignedType`), Ed25519 in v0: the identity key signs every statement the server stores or verifies, and approvals unless a presence key does (§16.6); agent subkeys only sealed provenance, ended by a local `AgentRevoke` and by `not_after` (below); the ClientKey only the binding and §7.4's DPoP proofs; an app's forwarding key only its sidecar's `WindowDelegation`s (§17.9). A compromised identity key means a `SidecarRevoke` for compromise and a new `sidecar_id`.
- **Agent subkeys (v1).** The identity key signs `AgentCert{sidecar_id, agent_id, public_key, not_after_ms}`, `not_after_ms` at most 30 days after signing, as a typed `Signed` with purpose `agent-cert` and `SIGNED_AGENT_CERT = 0x1A02` (§6.11). That `Signed` rides inside the sealed provenance it vouches for, RECORD.md section 5.3's `AgentSignedBody` and a push's sealed metadata (§11.6), never a log statement or config record. A reader checks the certificate under the identity key of the sidecar that signed the carrying entry, that the entry's time is before `not_after_ms`, and then the subkey's signature: a bad signature alarms, and an absent certificate reads `agent_asserted`. `AgentRevoke` is a local act, not a record ([owner decision 285](#od-285)): `Sidecar.AgentRevoke(agentId)` deletes the subkey from `keychain.ur`, and the daemon signs nothing more with it, since a subkey never leaves the daemon; readers bound a subkey by its certificate's `not_after_ms`. A compromised daemon is a `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}`, and provenance from its `since_n` on reads unattributed.

### 5.6 Login, enrollment, admission, refresh, revocation

| Path | Credential (used once, then erased) | Client |
|---|---|---|
| `ur login [--invite <link>]` | §7.8's `ur-cli` (PKCE; the device grant in v1) mints a single-use, user-owned auth key (≤5 min) for the daemon, then drops the OAuth token, and offers to register a platform presence key (§16.6) | top-level (§20.8); a child after pairing (5.8, M8) |
| `ur connect --token ur-authkey-…` | A §7 auth key (expiry, uses, tags, ephemeral), whose server part alone enrollment sends (§7.8); from a pre-approved key's client-only `#<bundle>` the daemon signs its own `SidecarAdmit` with the Delegation's key, carrying exactly the Delegation's tags and, unless `--ephemeral`, a `not_after` no earlier than the Delegation's (§7.9's scoped), and keeps only its reader key (§10.5); `urn_` keys are refused | top-level; tagged or user-owned |
| `ur connect --token-file <path>` | The same key read from a mode 0600 file, which `ur` unlinks after enrolling, erasing its copy: a cloud VM's setup writes it and the `--project` cloud profile's SessionStart hook passes it (§16.9); `ur` reads no key from its environment and refuses to enroll if `ur-authkey-` appears there ([owner decision 449](#od-449)) | top-level; tagged |
| sdk host | The device's token mints the child (`admin_refused: true`); the host's `TokenSource` refreshes it (§18.7), with the core's DPoP signer installed (`Api.SetDpopSigner`) | child |

- **Enrollment.** The daemon generates the ClientKey seed, identity key, ReaderKey and `sidecar_id`, calls `POST /network/enroll` (§7) or `/network/auth-client`, declaring no provider egress unless `ur proxy` or a public exit is set (§20.8), then `POST /sidecar/bind`, and persists the keychain only if the reply confirms `admin_refused`. The bind answers the generation alone, and enrollment, child enrollment and pairing keep the token they bound with: a service reads a sidecar from its service token's `ur_sidecar_id` (§7.8), sockets included, so the client token carries no `sidecar_id` claim, and the re-mint that [owner decision 286](#od-286) had the sidecar adopt, with the sdk host's `SidecarTokenSourceRemint`, is gone ([owner decision 588](#od-588)). An `--ephemeral` keychain stays in memory, but a cloud VM's sidecar, enrolled by `--token-file`, keeps its keychain in a mode 0600 file, since a paused VM loses its processes, so a restored VM rejoins until its client is reaped (§7.7, 30-36 min; §16.9); reaping revokes it (§7.10).
- **Readable credentials (D-TRUST-3; [owner decision 283](#od-283)).** `ur` refuses to enroll, and an enrolled daemon alarms at each start and at each `SyncRefetchInterval` (the `credential_store` event, 5.4), while a store on its host holds a readable network `by_jwt`, whatever §7.4's stage. The check is by state, with no signal: no reply field, config key or other spoofable input turns it off, a host the app and extension releases cleaned passes by itself, and a later `ur` release drops the check once the fleet has moved. It reports a store only if this user can read it and it holds a token, and never copies, logs or sends a value. App stores: under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\URnetwork`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/urnetwork`, `~/Documents` and the Documents of the macOS containers `network.ur` and `com.bringyour.urnetwork`, any `.by/.auth_state` whose JSON `by_jwt` is non-empty (sdk/local_state_auth.go:31-35), or a non-empty legacy `.by/.by_jwt`. Extension stores (extension/src/background/index.ts:134): a Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave profile's `Extensions/*/*/manifest.json` naming URnetwork, or a Firefox profile's `extensions.json` naming `urnetwork@bringyour.com`, at a version below D-SDK-11's first non-persisting release, which stays unset, so every version counts, until that release ships. No extension's storage is opened, and no LevelDB or IndexedDB is parsed.
- **Recovery setup.** `ur login`, once its device is admitted or has signed Genesis and base 1 and its member has no current binding, offers recovery setup on `/dev/tty` (5.9's recovery code). `ur login --recover` is a code-only recovered device's command, reading the 12 words only from `/dev/tty`, as the pass is, never argv, env or stdin. `ur login --replace` and `ur connect --token <key> --replace` run on a restored state directory whose machine-id hash differs: they keep the `sidecar_id` and identity key, bind generation n+1 on the new client and remove the old client (5.9's backup).
- **Admission (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112)-[114](#od-114), [126](#od-126)-[128](#od-128), [144](#od-144), [149](#od-149)).** Until a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` (§7.9) names it, a sidecar gets no peer, MLS group, wrap or grant. The rules:

```text
genesis  before the owner's first untagged device signs it (§7.9), tagged and ephemeral enrollments
         get no_genesis; a ur login device without an invite's or auth key's anchor shows a safety
         number over the genesis and its identity key for the admitter to compare (§2.8 EX5); a
```

- **Refresh.** `sidecarTokenManager`, a root file in both legs, runs the sdk schedule on `GET /auth/refresh` through `SidecarApi` with a DPoP proof that crypto/ed25519 signs by the ClientKey (§7.4), and on a refused credential (connect's `AuthorizationClosed`, connect/transport.go:528, or a 401), against §7's 7-day, no-grace expiry (D-TEAM-14); it installs tokens in `SidecarApi` and the keychain and, where connect links, by `api.SetByJwt` and `transport.SetAuth` (:1924). A refused refresh returns the sidecar to `Unenrolled` with its identity and admission; only a `SidecarRevoke` that verifies against the config, announced by the `core` push or a refused bind, means `Revoked`; an unverifiable claim leaves it Unenrolled and alarms (`refused`). Events of an older client generation are dropped. After a Postgres restore, a refresh whose identity, binding or registration api lacks answers `restore_required`, and the daemon re-registers its identity and newest binding (`POST /sidecar/bind`, taken once the re-published projection admits the key), then its mail host keys, TLS endpoints and push token (§19.10).
- **Revocation.** `ur logout` signs a `SidecarRevoke` (`removed`) for its own `sidecar_id`, removes its client (`POST /network/remove-client`) and wipes state. A signer allowed above revokes a lost device as `lost`, or as `compromise` with `since_n` (above): the device proposes the first entry timed at or after the loss time the person gives, or the tip where that time is past but later than the log's newest entry (plan, below; [owner decision 292](#od-292)), which the person may move earlier, and lists what P parks and voids before the person confirms on `/dev/tty` or in an app's UI; it signs none whose P holds its own sidecar. The server removes the revoked client (§7.10), closing its connections within about 90 s (server/session/AUTH.md:197). Stale revocations (§7.10's `stale` row) ride the act that carries them, under that act's confirmation and, wherever this sidecar registered a live presence key, its one presence check ([owner decision 187](#od-187)): a page Worker's admission, the member's `OwnerConfirm` of an admin-admitted page Worker (`ur approve` on `/dev/tty` included, D-CORE-13), or its answer to that admission's alarm. Every other revocation by a member of another of its own devices runs as 5.4's `PreviewDeviceRevoke` and `RevokeDevice` (D-CORE-20), §18.5's alarm answers that revoke a named device included (the admission alarm, `recovery_rebind` and `recovery_unseen`), with the `since_n` the alarm fixes; a `ur` command confirmed on `/dev/tty`, §18.5's `SidecarApprovals` in an app's UI and a remote-mode app's control calls (5.8) reach them, never MCP. `ur devices` lists 5.4's `Devices()`; `ur devices revoke <name|sidecar_id> [--compromise [--since <time|position>]] [--keep-key <key_id>]...`, which with `--compromise` and no `--since` asks on the terminal for an RFC 3339 time or a log position before it calls the daemon and fails without a terminal, prints the plan, signs once the person confirms on `/dev/tty`, under Presence after the daemon's presence prompt, and at k > 1 also signs the target's `Suspend` (sign); `ur approve <proposal_id>` prints a revocation proposal's plan and signs its `AuthorityCosign` under the same approval. The rules:

```text

          Workers and quick burners, parked, stale and admin-admitted ones included; never this

          an admin revokes (§7.10's agents row)
caller    a device approval-capable for M (§16.6: consented, untagged, not ephemeral, not
          read_only, on a host that signs decisions) that is not suspended (§8.8)
approval  the person's approval at this device, recorded with its evidence in the membership entry
          the act writes (§16.8): presence wherever M holds a live presence key whose KeyRegister
          this sidecar signed (§7.9's KeyRegister signer row), the plan's derivation setting its
```
