### 7.18 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A missed `admin_user_id` read lets a member act as owner | Medium | High | classify the 133 reads; fail closed |
| A reusable auth key leaks: its reader seed reads later generations, past reaps, until its Delegation's key drops, and its signing seed admits fresh agents, which read by their own wraps, until the Delegation ends | Medium | High | expiry, uses, `max_admits`, which rows count for the Delegation's life; `not_after` ≤ 90 d; §10.5's CI bound and key drops; `DelegationRevoke`, whose `since_n` parks a leak's admissions, or a compromise revocation of one of its agents ends the Delegation; the revoke plan names the agent, the key and the admission authority apart (7.10) |
| A `Suspend`, or a lost or removed revocation, of one CI agent drops its Delegation's shared key, so the Delegation's later agents read only once a holder wraps to them | Medium | Low | the plan lists the agents and repos the drop reaches; the console replaces the Delegation as at a CI secret rotation (§10.5) |
| An agent drives `ur-cli` through the user's browser | Medium | High | consent code, `auth_time`, DPoP |
| Strict expiry strands an offline sidecar | Medium | Medium | early refresh; re-enrollment keeps the `sidecar_id` |
| A team loses its admin keys | Medium | High | k of n; recovery keys ([owner decision 127](#od-127)) |
| n ≤ 2 forces k = 1: either admin alone can remove the other or change the AdminSet | Medium | High | the console recommends n ≥ 3; AdminSet notices (7.8) |
| An admin's leaked recovery code signs authority statements, alone at k = 1 | Low | Critical | the 72 h window from the newest recovery signature, a late cosign included, on every member device; any admin device vetoes; a `RecoveryRebind` of the code's member voids every pending proposal the code signed or cosigned; a server hiding that signature from every admin device defeats the veto, detected on first sight |
| A stolen recovery code admits a device under a non-admin member at once | Low | High | the member's devices alarm ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); `RecoveryRebind` |
| A compromised AdminSet device gossips a veto backdated before a recovery activation | Low | Medium | devices that applied the activation only alarm; those still before it fork until the log reverses it, by a compromise revocation of the recovered device, whose member then recovers again; admins revoke the vetoing device (7.9) |
| An admin admits a device as a new member's first, consented under §8.5 or JIT | Low | High | the member's real device, parked, alarms; admins re-invite the member |
| SCIM deprovisioning waits for an admin's signature | Medium | Medium | server denial at once; the console's unsigned-removal list; `scim_signer` on an admin's indexer |
| No admin device online to sign a member's revocation, or no admitting device online after a reap | Medium | Medium | server denial; own-device revocations commit at once ([owner decision 128](#od-128)); the gate refuses writes (412) |
| A designated indexer stays offline, so its services wait on their fallbacks, and a Team's mail on sender retries | Medium | Medium | per-service fallbacks (§3.6); two mail indexers (§15.6); `ur status` lists each indexer's services and newest sign of life |
| An admin designates its own device as a network-scope search indexer to collect members' queries | Low | High | no designation by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)); own indexers first, and other members' owner-bound repos never reach it ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); the app names the answering member before the first query and again when it changes; a per-device `own` or `off` mode (§18.4); designations are signed and listed in every config and `ur indexer ls`; one other member's device at a time (§11.14) |
| After a site loss, one compromised member device pre-empts log positions with a forged TICK (any time_ms), a reordered statement or one it signs, forking every longer tail, or a device's longer tail goes unuploaded | Low | High | uploads only from member devices in reseed mode, matched to the restored `network_acl_head`; api adopts an entry only once devices of two members hold its digest, and checks the newest adopted base against the re-seeded config repo; a forged activation raises `recovery_unseen`; a device whose tail passes the stop sees a FORK and keeps the evidence (7.9) |
| A compromised device spends its network's daily append limit, delaying admissions and approvals | Low | Medium | revocations, Suspend and vetoes are exempt, so admins revoke it at once; 429s carry `retry_after_ms`, and the day's budget refills within 24 h (7.9) |
| A thief holding a member's unlocked device that registered no presence key, or who knows its passcode or its security key's PIN, signs what 7.9's presence row covers on a confirmation alone | Low | High | `ur login` and the apps offer a platform presence key ([owner decision 142](#od-142)), after which every such statement needs its countersignature (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187), [189](#od-189)); every member device sees each revocation and offers to revoke its signer; disclosed (§2.10) |
| A device's only presence key, a security key, is lost, so the device signs nothing 7.9's presence row covers until that key is revoked or its `not_after` passes (§16.17's row) | Low | Medium | §16.17's row ([owner decision 189](#od-189)) |
| A member whose devices are all page Workers, which §8.5 never consents, or one that never answers its alarms after an admin's device admits its Worker (always so with `self_admit` off), keeps each Worker that no group of the admitting device seated, one admission per eviction toward `config_admissions` (7.10's `stale` row; §20.4) | Low | Medium | admins' devices revoke every Worker they saw stale-removed (D-TEAM-29); the member's next `OwnerConfirm` or alarm answer frees the rest; from 90% of the cap every admin device lists each member's page Workers but its newest for an admin to revoke (7.10's `cleanup` row), so none waits for the cap's refusal; FS-97 |

### 7.19 Phasing

- **P0, before any sidecar:** stage 1 (D-TEAM-1, with 7.4's allowlist and auth-code fix), D-TEAM-14 and its proof.
- **v0, personal networks (§23 M1-M2):** auth keys and their bundles, enrollment, token exchange, `rev/` objects, key sets, `ur-cli`'s auth-key scope, ephemeral reaping with its lease and close capability (MG1), API-key scopes, rename unification; the enforced config repo (M2; owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5)): the authorization log with its read cache, append limits, fold cadence and site-loss resumption, k-of-n verifier and proposals, the presence countersignature rule (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)), recovery window, consent rule, read-only admissions, compromise cascade, Delegation ends and their parks (7.9's delegation row) with the CLI's agent and Delegation revoke plans (7.10's agents row), committers and recovery path, and `IndexerSet` ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), tested though personal networks have n = 1; config.proto reserves `ServiceSettings.directory` (D-TEAM-28).
- **With §13's v0:** edge login.
- **v0, app hosts (§23 M8; [owner decision 197](#od-197)):** the forwarding Delegation and the `forward_only` mark with its exchange rule, the Delegation's `forward` fields reserved in config.proto at M2 with 7.9's records.
- **v1, Team (M6):** members, roles, invitations, switching, OIDC, domains, JIT, SCIM and `scim_signer`, OAuth clients, full `ur-cli` admin, audit log, multi-admin teams, and config wraps for member devices past the first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory, created with the team, its group under 7.9's leaves rule, and `ServiceSettings.directory` (owner decisions [170](#od-170), [171](#od-171), [182](#od-182)).
- **v1, every network (§23's M10, with storage format 2; [owner decision 169](#od-169)):** `VersioningRules` (§11.7), its type reserved at M2 with 7.9's records, and `IndexerSet`'s `search` service, which includes answering remote searches (§11.14; owner decisions [157](#od-157), [163](#od-163), [164](#od-164), [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)).
- **On app migration:** [stage 3](DESIGN-DEFER.md#team-stage-3-hard-gate) (7.4).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for stage 3 and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#team-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Blocking:** the `admin_user_id` audit blocks members; stage 1 and D-TEAM-14 block the first sidecar, stage 2 the first desktop sidecar; token exchange and `rev/` block evs (§11); the config repo needs §10 and §11 and blocks §8's gates, and its records and log freeze at M2 (§23.8).

## 8. Access control: policy, compilation, distribution, enforcement

### 8.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the access-control model and its evaluation; X3, the customer key authority (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5)-[8](#od-8), [110](#od-110), [126](#od-126)); policy rows in the signed projection, grant chains and repo access logs; gate caches; enforcement points; and evs readers, with data repos' leaf seats (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)). §7 owns the config repo's records, the authorization log and its read cache, the config and directory groups' `leaves` rule, members, roles, tokens and removal; §10 MLS; §11 repo kinds and drops; §16.11 the team directory; §17 bridge rules.

### 8.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-ACL-1 | Specify which clients, groups and networks reach a client, group, network or abstract socket | PLAN.md:74 |
| R-ACL-2 | Rules stored on the server; each client gets its rules in real time and decides locally | PLAN.md:119 |
| R-ACL-3 | One deny-by-default HuJSON policy with tags, groups, autogroups and tests; default `tag:recurd` → `autogroup:self` tcp:443 | team-management.html:813-929 |
| R-ACL-4 | Every reach grant names an approver and an expiry; one switch revokes an agent's forwards, addresses, names and mail | pitch5.html:680,729 |
| R-ACL-5 | With a policy, agents reach only granted ranges; public names authenticated by default, short-lived | pitch5.html:689,698; [owner decision 120](#od-120) |
| R-ACL-6 | Invite an external network to forward in; accept an invite | cli/UI.md:50-51 |
| R-ACL-7 | A breached server cannot add a reader | pitch5.html:745; team-management.html:940 |
| R-ACL-8 | No added query for networks without the feature; no PostgreSQL per packet | server/model/subscription_model.go:1727-1730; connect/CODESTYLE.md:106-107 |
| R-ACL-9 | The ACL decides evs readers, which clients verify; app devices, and untagged sidecars until a policy exists, keep today's reach | derived; owner decisions [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120) |
| R-ACL-10 | Tests, change audit, rollback, propagation target | team-management.html:907-929,1021-1029 |
| R-ACL-11 | Session contents stay with their author unless shared, while in a team network a run's who, what and where reach teammates by default; admins read actions, not transcripts | pitch5.html:579,640; owner decisions [126](#od-126), [170](#od-170) |
| R-ACL-12 | Admin keys sign policy from v0; a breached server can only deny or delay (§2.8's bound), and sees policy only as ids | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [72](#od-72) |

### 8.3 What exists today

- No group, tag or policy table exists [R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md).
- `GetProvideRelationshipDetails` returns Network iff both clients share a `network_id`, else Public, in one query (`server/model/network_client_model.go:2528-2606`). `CreateContract` resolves it at `server/controller/connect_controller.go:859`, picks the mode at `:933`, and settles companion requests as Network without an origin check (`:917-927`). A provider's reply to a Network source is not one: connect asks for it as a plain non-companion contract in the reply direction (`connect/ip.go:9393-9411`), and the subprotocol's query replies use the same helpers, so the request alone cannot tell a reply from a new dial (8.10's contract rule).
- FriendsAndFamily (`connect/protocol/transfer.proto:357`) escrows nothing (`connect_controller.go:1296`) and is never computed.
- Providers allow Network sources every destination, LAN and loopback included (`connect/ip_security.go:567`); other modes get public-only rules (`:385-390`).
- Contracts expire within 60 min (`server/model/subscription_contract_expiration.go:14`), and the contract-hole projection, a Redis pair lease, gates forwarding (`connect/CODESTYLE.md:107-110`).

### 8.4 Model

**Subjects** are sidecars (`sidecar_id`, mapped to the current client through §5's binding) and other clients (`client_id`: app devices, legacy clients); untagged children such as sdk window clients act as their nearest subject ancestor (D-ACL-3), so a sidecar's forwarding client and its window clients act as that sidecar, their tokens confined by `forward_only` (§7.4, §18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)). Before expansion each is classed as a member device (untagged, not ephemeral), an ephemeral sidecar, a tagged sidecar or another client (D-ACL-19). Autogroups follow the class ([owner decision 355](#od-355)): `autogroup:member` is the untagged sidecars, ephemeral ones included, which take reach from rules naming it while 8.6's ceiling alone limits their evs access; `autogroup:owner`, `autogroup:admin` and `autogroup:auditor` are the untagged subjects of members whose role is Owner, Owner or Admin, and Auditor, Network and IT admins being in none of them; app devices are in `autogroup:untagged` only, never `autogroup:member` (D-ACL-20's two disjoint sets); and a tagged subject takes no role autogroup. An untagged subject's atoms are its owner's user, groups and role, and its autogroups; an ephemeral subject's evs access is capped as 8.6 says; a tagged subject has no user atoms, and its §7 *sponsor* stands in: the admitting member or the one an admin's `SponsorSet` names, else `autogroup:admin` once that sponsor is removed ([owner decision 83](#od-83)). In-daemon agents share their sidecar's grants, which the daemon may narrow ([owner decision 4](#od-4), §5.5).

```text
selector (src or dst unless noted)   meaning
user:<email>, group:<name>           untagged subjects
tag:<name>                           via tagOwners
sidecar:<id>                         across client generations
client:<id>                          resolved through §5's binding
role:, principal:                    Embed networks
autogroup:member|owner|admin|auditor|sidecar|tagged|network
autogroup:untagged                   untagged non-sidecars; untagged sidecars are in autogroup:member
autogroup:ephemeral                  src: untagged ephemeral sidecars
network:<net>                        as that network permits (§8.11)
autogroup:public                     src: anonymous tlsedge clients
autogroup:internet                   dst: public destinations via an exit
autogroup:self                       dst: subjects sharing the source's owner or sponsor; approver: the requester's
autogroup:sponsor                    approver
autogroup:dst-owner                  approver: the destination subject's owner, or a tagged sidecar's sponsor; for a
                                     socket, its listeners' owner or sponsor where all are one; otherwise
                                     autogroup:admin (owner decision 180); acl.proto fixes its atom at M2, when the
                                     implicit document names it (8.5); Team documents name it from M6

resource                             actions; notes (* matches within a label or segment, a bare * all of a kind)
a subject, optional ip ports         dial; its addresses too (§17)
sock:<name>                          dial, listen; this network's sockets only (others reach a listener by IP, §8.11);
                                     rows carry application names as §9.4's token paths under K_sock
                                     (owner decision 67), tls/ and smtp/ names in clear; services authorize ur/ names
ip:<cidr>, ports, via subjects       route; 0.0.0.0/0 excludes loopback and link-local
evs:<repo>                           read, write (implies read), admin (lifecycle, drops), deposit; an id or config
                                     label, never a path (X2)
dns:<host>, sock, audience,          publish, admin (zone records); <host> is @, one label or, in a v1 Team
  app_mode, link_spki_sha256         scope, <host>.<scope> (dns:*.<scope> covers one scope; Q-TLS-3); audience:
                                     members (default), members-device, link or public (owner decision 42);
                                     app_mode: http (default), or raw only under public or link, a raw link's
                                     grant pinning its client certificate's SPKI SHA-256 (§13.7)
mail:<alias>                         send, listen; checked only by clients
* (as a dst)                         any subject, application socket, ip range (exits included) or general or
                                     record repo here; outward resources (tls/ and smtp/ sockets, dns:, mail:,
                                     other networks) and §8.5's kinds must be named
```

acl.proto numbers `AclAutogroup` and `AclAction` from 1 in the order the lists above write them, 0 being unspecified (§7.9's record bytes).

**Readings.** `ParseAclPolicy` runs on every reader, so what it accepts is a format. A last segment that is exactly `*` takes every name below its prefix, at least one segment deeper, so `sock:tls/*` reaches `tls/443/blog`; this is the one place "within a label or segment" is read against its letter, and any other `*` stays inside its segment, a `tls/` or `smtp/` name's or a dns host's glob kept as written in rows (`*-preview`; 8.8's `public_name`). A bare `*` dst, `sock:*` and a glob in the first segment reach application sockets and `share/` only, never `tls/`, `smtp/` or §9.4's other reserved first segments, or the implicit document's self-approved tagged rule would reach the `tls/` names its admin-approved rule holds. `admin` on a repo implies write and read of it, within 8.6's ceiling, a read_only sidecar still getting only read; a policy grant of `admin` therefore adds a key holder, which the preview names as a reader. As an approver, `autogroup:dst-owner` reads a socket's listeners as the subjects holding `listen` on it in the state at the statement's position, never live registrations: one owner or sponsor across them names that one, otherwise `autogroup:admin`; over an atom target it expands to every standing sidecar holding the atom. `autogroup:self` of a legacy client, or of a tagged sidecar whose sponsor is gone, resolves to `autogroup:admin`, as `autogroup:sponsor` does for an untagged requester ([owner decision 355](#od-355)). A `route` rule that names no `ip:` destination and no `autogroup:internet` reaches, through each advertiser its via subjects hold for the source that is also among the rule's subject destinations for that source, every prefix of that advertiser's subnet routes in force, whole, its exposed prefix included: under `route` a subject destination's routes in force are what such a rule reaches, through the vias that hold their advertiser, so grant 1 reaches exactly the prefixes a member's own devices' approved routes serve (8.5), a rule whose destinations name none of its vias opens nothing new, and only an internet or /0 rule gives exits (§17.7; [owner decision 575](#od-575)); a policy's own `ip:` tests judge such a rule as 8.8's saving rules say ([owner decision 615](#od-615)). A source holds at most 4 MiB, 8.8's rows bound, and nests at most 4 deep, the schema's real depth; both are format constants, and the nesting bound runs before `encoding/json`, which recurses per level.

### 8.5 Policy document and worked examples

The policy is HuJSON in the config repo, parsed in-repo: `aclStandardizeHujson` (sidecar/acl_hujson.go) turns `//` and `/* */` comments and trailing commas into spaces, keeping byte offsets, refuses invalid UTF-8 and hands the result to `encoding/json`, on every leg, with no new module and no dependencies.yml row; a change to it counts as a format change, since every reader must parse one source alike, and §22.6's compiler fuzz target covers it. Beyond the example it has `hosts`, with Tailscale's meaning: a name for an address or CIDR, used as `ip:<name>` and resolved at parse, so an unknown name is refused; grant fields `id`, `via`, `sock`, `audience`, `app_mode`, `link_spki_sha256` (8.4) and `note`; an `approvers` count on `requests`, which subjects or a team directory request (§16.11) file, a harness `reach:` block (recurd-app.html:1743-1749) filing none until [a later design](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mcp-harness-config-keys) (§16.7; [owner decision 452](#od-452)); and document-level `expiresDefault` (1 h) and `evidenceDefault` (all §16.6 channels; harness only in untainted runs unless a rule names it, [owner decision 142](#od-142), §16.6). A `requests` rule refuses `ip`, `via`, `sock`, `audience`, `app_mode`, `link_spki_sha256` and `expires`: a rule names who may ask and who answers, and the filed request names ports, audience and expiry, so a Team narrows a rule through `dst`, `src` and `evidence`.

```hujson
{
  "groups":    { "group:eng": ["dana@acme.com", "amir@acme.com"] },
  "tagOwners": { "tag:recurd": ["group:eng"], "tag:db": ["autogroup:admin"],
                 "tag:api": ["autogroup:admin"], "tag:audit": ["autogroup:admin"] },
  "grants": [
    { "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:untagged"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"],           // 1 laptop→phone
      "via": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial", "route"] },
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["evs:repo-x"], "allow": ["write"] },                     // 2
    { "src": ["group:eng"], "dst": ["sock:db"], "allow": ["dial"] },                          // 3
    { "src": ["tag:db"],    "dst": ["sock:db"], "allow": ["listen"] },
    { "src": ["network:partner-y"], "dst": ["tag:api"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"], // 4 share over §17's
      "expires": "2026-12-31T00:00:00Z" },                                                  // IP path (owner decision 86)
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"] },
  ],
  "requests": [ // 5: ur bridge public-tls app-preview:3000 publishes app-preview.<net>.<root> for up to
                //    24 h, approved from a device or presence key, never a harness prompt
    { "src": ["tag:recurd"], "dst": ["dns:*-preview", "sock:tls/443/*-preview"], "allow": ["publish", "listen"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:sponsor"], "maxExpiry": "24h", "evidence": ["device", "presence"] },
  ],
  "audit": { "reader": "tag:audit", "repos": ["kind:team_record", "kind:vault", "kind:mailbox"] }, // 6 Team
  "tests": [ { "src": "dana@acme.com", "accept": ["sock:db#dial"], "deny": ["evs:secrets#read"] } ],
}
```

**Grant 1 ([owner decision 344](#od-344)).** Grant 1, and Team's starting document (`acl_team_start.hujson`) with it, reads `{ "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:untagged"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "via": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial", "route"] }`. D-ACL-20 narrowed `autogroup:untagged` to non-sidecars, so the source names `autogroup:member` beside it, and a member's own sidecars and app devices reach each other; a rule's via subjects no longer share its targets (8.8), so `via` names `autogroup:self` and a member's devices also reach the prefixes their own devices' approved routes serve. FS-21's Team case uses peers of two members, since a member's own devices reach each other.

**Kind defaults** come ahead of every document, evaluated in the binary from `AclRepo` rows and the state and never compiled into rules, so an admission between bases reads at once ([owner decision 355](#od-355)); `*` never matches these kinds, which §11.12 fixes at creation. Rules add nothing to config, directory or secret repos or to a Team scope's own mailcfg, add only deposit to vault and mailbox, and add readers only to the last two, a mailcfg only where it is the network's, as to general and record repos:

| kind | read (and write where noted) | deposit |
|---|---|---|
| `config` (§7.9) | every admitted sidecar; heads from config writers (§8.8), each of which holds `admin` on it at evs and gkm, the Genesis's owner sidecar from base 1 being the first case ([owner decision 352](#od-352)); its evs `rw` goes to config writers and its gkm `rw` to member devices that are not read_only | — |
| `directory` (one per team network, §16.11; [owner decision 171](#od-171)) | every admitted sidecar of the team; every one that is not read_only writes only its own paths and stream, and a device KF2 parks for consent writes nothing that counts (I-EVS-14); documents neither add nor remove readers (D-ACL-24) | — |
| `vault`, `mailbox`, `secret` (owner-bound to member M; group inboxes stay general; each `secret` holds one secret, such as §13.8's ACME account key or §17.9's ShareKey, and §16.6 refuses `secret` repos to MCP's evs tools) | M's consented devices (below), which also write; their `EvsShare`s' subjects (§8.8); the `audit` reader where its block names the kind or repo | receipts from readers that do not write (§16.8); in `vault` and `mailbox` also M's other untagged subjects, the tagged subjects M sponsors, `tag:mail` mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)); in `mailbox` also any subject of the network that the projection marks `mail_send`, for §15.8's same-network mail (D-MAIL-8; [owner decision 333](#od-333)) |
| Team record | `autogroup:admin`, `:auditor`; no row 8.6's ceiling counts, so an ephemeral sidecar only deposits there | `autogroup:member`, tagged subjects |
| `mailcfg` | the network's: `tag:mail` mail indexers, and members write the records they sign (§15.8), its writers member devices; a Team scope's own, its row naming an owner (the scope's member, whose consented device created it; 8.8's RepoCreate row; owner decisions [631](#od-631), [644](#od-644)): owner-bound to that member as a mailbox is, so its member's consented devices read and write it, its receivers among them ([owner decision 58](#od-58)), and no `tag:mail` indexer, since a network mail indexer never resolves a scope's addresses; no rule, `RepoGrant` or other admin adds to it, a `RepoAdmin` add or `RepoDelete` takes effect only from its member's consented device and no `RepoRevoke` removes the member (8.8), so it is out of the network's admins' reach as the member's mail key is ([owner decision 126](#od-126)) | — |

A group inbox stays a `general` repo, marked at its creation: `RepoCreate`'s `inbox` is `group`, or `admin` for the network's admin address (8.8). Rotators set a marked repo's drop key as they do for a kind that takes deposits (§10.5, D-KEYS-17), and writers use §11.6's per-message slot rule for it. `ur id group-create` files its deposit grant beside the marker (§15.7); an untagged receiver in a network with no document already reaches its deposit ref through the implicit document's `autogroup:member` write on `evs:*` (§15.7). A member's deposit into another member's mailbox is bounded by §20's storage limits, and the recipient's readers show it as from a member by the push's signer; `vault` and `secret` take no such deposit, and 8.8's "never in an owner-bound repo" stands for `RepoGrant`.

**Owner consent ([owner decision 126](#od-126)).** One admin's signature admits a device under member M ([owner decision 110](#od-110)), but in M's owner-bound repos admins only revoke or add the audit reader; there a later `EvsShare` to the same subject from M's consented device lifts a config writer's standing `RepoRevoke`, and a `RepoRevoke` naming one of M's consented devices is refused, since `SidecarRevoke` and `Suspend` already remove a device ([owner decision 332](#od-332); 8.8). One predicate, which §5.6 and §7.9 cite, names M's consented devices (D-ACL-22):

```text
consented(d, M) = d's admission names member M, d is neither ephemeral nor parked by §7.9's compromise
  cascade, and one of these holds on a signature by neither a sidecar then in that cascade's set P nor a
  recovery key whose binding one signed:
  scoped     M's consented device or M's recovery key signed d's SidecarAdmit, alone or as one of k
             (§7.9, owner decision 112)
  invited    d's SidecarAdmit carries SIDECAR_CAPABILITY_INVITED, which the admitting device sets only after
             the join MAC of an invite addressed to M verifies (§7.5's invite block): §7.5's member invite,
             or the invite an admin device issues when it admits a JIT-pending member (§7.6), neither of
             which an ephemeral enrollment redeems; and d is the first admission under M in log order,
             revoked ones included, that is neither ephemeral nor read_only; a later device's bit counts for
             nothing, and readers ignore it on an ephemeral or read_only admission
  genesis    d signed the network's Genesis (the owner's first device)
  confirmed  M's consented device signed OwnerConfirm{d} (§8.8), as after an admin's admission, or the
             AdmissionConfirm{d} that lifted d's park (§7.9)
```

A signer counts for consent only if it was consented for the same member strictly before the position it signed at and the cascade does not void it there; M's recovery key is the binding in force at the admission's position; an `AdmissionConfirm` by M's consented device counts whether or not it lifted a park; a revoked device is not consented now, while what it signed before stands; and the invited clause also needs one admission signer outside every cascade ([owner decision 355](#od-355)). Members and grantor leaves refuse other Adds and wraps there, and KF2 parks d (§10.7, §10.9). A device whose consent rested on what P signed regains M's owner-bound repos only by an `OwnerConfirm` or `AdmissionConfirm` from M's consented device outside P; an admin's `AdmissionConfirm` restores only its other access (§7.9). M's devices alarm on any admission under M that M's keys did not sign and offer to confirm it (`approval_pending`; §5.4, §18.5). Only consented devices that are not read-only (§7.9) sign M's `EvsShare`s, `OwnerConfirm`s, `RecoveryBind`s, owner-bound `RepoAdmin` adds, and DROP pushes and their cancels in M's owner-bound repos (§11.7), so admins neither drop nor cancel drops there (owner decisions [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183)).

**Audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63); Team, v1).** Example 6's `audit` block counts only while a k-of-n `AuditOptIn` (§8.8) exists, and members see that reader in each affected reader list before it gets a key (§10.8).

The **implicit document**, versioned in the sidecar repo, serves Community and Pro networks without one; writers compile it into the projection's rules whenever `has_document` is false, so gates and clients evaluate the same rows (D-ACL-20). Team starts from grant 1, the `tag:recurd` default and the implicit document's last rule, the team directory's reach requests (D-ACL-23), which its document may narrow, give two approvers or remove ([owner decision 74](#od-74)); the implicit document carries that rule from its M2 version, so readers of every version compile the same rows.

```hujson
{ "grants": [  // owner decision 105: untagged sidecars (autogroup:member) and app devices
               // (autogroup:untagged) keep today's reach, and providers keep allow-all LAN and
               // loopback, disclosed (owner decisions 50, 120)
    { "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:untagged"], "dst": ["*"], "allow": ["*"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:member"], "dst": ["evs:*"], "allow": ["write", "admin"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["evs:*"], "allow": ["deposit"] },
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["autogroup:self"], "allow": ["dial"], "ip": ["tcp:443"] } ],
  "requests": [
    { "src": ["autogroup:network"], "dst": ["dns:*", "sock:tls/*", "sock:smtp/*"], "allow": ["publish", "listen"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:admin"], "maxExpiry": "7d" },                             // §13.9
    { "src": ["autogroup:tagged"], "dst": ["*", "sock:*", "evs:*", "mail:*"],
      "allow": ["dial", "route", "listen", "read", "write", "send"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:self"], "maxExpiry": "30d" },                             // owner decision 74
    { "src": ["network:*"], "dst": ["*"], "allow": ["dial", "route"],
      "approver": ["autogroup:admin"], "maxExpiry": "30d" },                            // shares (§8.11)
    { "src": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:tagged"],                                  // the team directory's
      "dst": ["autogroup:member", "autogroup:tagged", "sock:*"], "allow": ["dial"],     // reach requests
      "approver": ["autogroup:dst-owner"], "evidence": ["device", "presence"],          // (§16.11; owner
      "maxExpiry": "30d" } ] }                                                          // decisions 179, 180)
```

An ephemeral sidecar's evs access takes 8.6's ceiling: the config's and its team directory's read, the directory's own-path writes, kind-default deposits, and grants and EvsShares that name it. A tagged ephemeral sidecar is in `autogroup:tagged`, yet gets no deposit from the implicit document's `autogroup:tagged` rule: the ceiling counts a rule only where it names the sidecar, and that rule does not. Standing publishes need a Pro or Team document; §13.9 caps the rest, and §21.7's probation is a hard deny.

### 8.6 Evaluation semantics

```text
allowed(s, a, r, t) = not hardDeny(s, a, r, t)
                      and exists g in rows(t): s in src(g), r in dst(g), a in allow(g), ports match,
                      ceiling(s, r, g)
rows(t)          = the state's AclRows: the network's document, or the implicit document when it has none
                   (has_document = false), compiled into the same rows; kind defaults, the audit block,
                   standing grants, activated requests, access-log RepoGrants and EvsShares, unexpired at t,
                   not revoked by a GrantRevoke or RepoRevoke, and no EvsShare that §7.9's cascade voids
ceiling(s, r, g) = true unless s is ephemeral and r is an evs: resource; then g names s (sidecar:<id>,
                   client:<id>, autogroup:ephemeral, or a tag s carries), is a kind default's deposit row,
                   the config kind default's read row or the directory kind default's read and own-path
                   writes, or is an EvsShare to s; so every ephemeral sidecar that hardDeny spares, never a
                   parked one, reads the config (owner decision 6) and its team's directory, and none
                   writes a config head
ports match      = for a rule with ip CIDRs or ports, each reader's check against the policy it compiles from
                   the sealed source (AclLocalPolicy); rows carry only whether a rule limits ports
                   (ports_limited, 8.8), so api and the gates check ids, and readers check a requested grant's
                   prefix against its rule
hardDeny         = unadmitted, revoked or parked sidecar (§7.9; parked by its compromise cascade or by a
                   leaked bundle's DelegationRevoke, unlike KF2's consent park) | unapproved client (§7) |
                   suspended subject | abuse halt (§21) | quota (§20)
```

- **Base.** Grants form a union over a deny base, without precedence, as in Tailscale (https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/grants); hard denies win, and no deny grants exist.
- **Direction.** The src initiates; replies are implied. Deposit implies no read, subscription, key or place in `RepoReaders`. Publish requires listen on the bound socket. Gates use server time and clients allow ±60 s of skew (`AclEngineSettings.ClockSkew`: the engine honors a rule until 60 s past its expiry by the local clock), so a daemon reserves a server-gated use only until 60 s before its `not_after` (§16.6).
- **Requests (owner decisions [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75), [142](#od-142), [180](#od-180)).** A requested grant matches a `requests` rule and lasts its `expires`, else `expiresDefault` (1 h), up to `maxExpiry` (30 days by default; publishes follow §13.9). The rule's approvers approve, by default the requester's owner or sponsor; grants touching other members, shares or `autogroup:public` need an admin's decision as well, whatever the rule says (the admin clause), except that a touched member who approves as `autogroup:dst-owner` meets it for reach to a device that member owns or sponsors ([owner decision 180](#od-180), amending [owner decision 74](#od-74) for this case); two do where a Team rule's `approvers` asks. An Owner's or Admin's decision counts toward the rule's k only where the rule's approvers name it (`autogroup:admin`, or a group the admin is in) or where `autogroup:dst-owner` resolves to an admin because no owner or sponsor stands (D-ACL-23): under the directory's default rule an Admin's lone decision activates no reach grant to another member's worker, a rule whose approver is `autogroup:self` reaching another member's device needs the requester's owner and an admin, and an Admin who wants to grant reach alone writes it as a document rule ([owner decision 349](#od-349)). Approvals are §16.8 `ApprovalDecision`s on channels the rule's `evidence` lists, or for an action no `requests` rule governs the document's `evidenceDefault`, both of which rows carry as effective lists (8.8; [owner decision 342](#od-342)), harness evidence in a tainted run only where the rule itself names it, checked by clients, `harness_ok` and api; they activate the grant as a §7.9 delta (§8.8), whose `grant_id` the approval fixes, so a replay is refused.
- **Admission.** An admission past its `not_after` is refused at exactly that time; an untagged sidecar or app device whose member is no longer a member is unadmitted; and a hard-denied destination subject is no destination either ([owner decision 355](#od-355)).
- **One switch.** A `Suspend` (§8.8's signers) removes a subject's atoms and activations across client generations; contracts, sockets, names, aliases, bridge rules and evs (§8.12) then refuse it, and for an agent a live Delegation admitted it also drops that Delegation's shared reader key at its position, so the next generation reaches the Delegation's other agents only by their own wraps and never the suspended one, which an `Unsuspend` returns uncovered (§10.5). Suspensions, revocations and cascade parks close open contracts, whose forwarding stops within 5 s; contracts a narrowed rule no longer allows lapse within 60 min (§8.3). A §21 suspension is server state that `hardDeny` reads, never a signed `Suspend` (I-4): it refuses contracts for sidecar subjects, shares included, names, publishing and sending, as §21's halts refuse sending, and never reaches evs or gkm, so the network's data stays readable, writable, erasable and exportable (§21.7; [owner decision 531](#od-531)).

### 8.7 Policy authority (X3)

Owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5) and [6](#od-6) settle X3 (§7.9, Q-ACL-1): config writers sign the policy, every admitted sidecar evaluates it, and gates enforce its id-only projection (§8.8-§8.10). A breached server can only withhold or delay, visibly once a HeadCheck crosses the split (I-16), within §2.8's exposure bound ([owner decision 129](#od-129)). It sees the reach graph and opaque ids, never member-chosen names, rule text or tests ([owner decision 72](#od-72); §2.8 api-7).

### 8.8 The policy in the config repo: rows, grant chains, saving

**Placement.** The policy source, repo labels and `K_sock` are config repo files that only config writers' heads change ([owner decision 5](#od-5)): `policy.hujson`; the `tags` and `groups`, `rules`, `labels` and `resolve` files, which are protocol/config.proto's `ConfigAtomTable`, `ConfigRuleTable`, `ConfigLabelTable` and `ConfigResolution`, none server-visible, so none has a §2.8 row ([owner decision 339](#od-339)); and `socket/key`, a single-record file beside `policy.hujson`, `SocketKeyFile{current_key = 1, previous_key = 2, rotated_at_ms = 3}`, its keys 32 B, with `previous_key` and `rotated_at_ms` set from a rotation until the head that clears them (§9.4), which a config writer creates with the repo (§7.9's paths). Server gates know policy only as `AclRows`, §8's part of §7.9's ProjectionRows, which the writer compiles at each base from the config head and the log-derived rows at its fold, §7.9's open proposals and ring compiled beside them, and readers recompile, alarming on a mismatch (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 5):

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/acl.proto: §8's rows inside §7.9's ProjectionRows. Ids only.
message AclRows {
  bool has_document = 1;                  // owner decisions 50, 105
  repeated AclAtom atoms = 2;             // §7.9's opaque tag and group ids -> member_ids, sidecar_ids, a
                                          // tag's owners; derived atoms for selectors no table names (Atoms)
  repeated AclRule rules = 3;             // rule_id, src atoms, targets, actions, expires; a
                                          // publish's audience, app_mode and link_spki_sha256 (8.4), the
                                          // pin in full, as a requested grant's GrantActivate shows it to
                                          // api anyway (§16.6 AD4); ports (5) reserved: bool
                                          // ports_limited = 11 says the rule has an ip port list, never
                                          // which, for 8.10's legacy rule; an activated grant's
                                          // source_rule_id = 10 (Folded grants); a route rule's via subjects
                                          // in via = 12, apart from its targets, or with no via the
                                          // advertisers whose BridgeRouteRow names the rule (§17.8; owner
                                          // decision 344); CIDRs and ports stay in each reader's
                                          // AclLocalPolicy (8.6)
  repeated AclRequestRule requests = 4;
  repeated AclRepo repos = 5;             // repo_id, kind, owner_member_id and the owner's consented
                                          // sidecar_ids (§8.5), whose consenting admission, AdmissionConfirm
                                          // and OwnerConfirm signers and positions §7.9's SidecarRow keeps;
                                          // its access log folded: repo admins, RepoGrants and EvsShares
                                          // with their expires, each with its signer sidecar_id and its
                                          // carrying entry's log position (§7.9's cascade), config writers'
                                          // standing RepoRevokes, the newest RepoDelete with any RepoRestore
                                          // of its deletion_id; the newest RepoVersioning's lock (folded from
                                          // M2, enforced from format 2); holders_shrunk_at: the newest log
                                          // position that dropped a key holder (§7.9); a removed admin's
                                          // removal position, the RepoDelete's entry time and signer, and
                                          // the prefix rule sets that took effect (Repo rows); and
                                          // holders_shrunk_time_ms = 13, the time_ms of the entry at
                                          // holders_shrunk_at, or of the RepoCreate's while that is 0, §7.9's
                                          // t_s (owner decision 557)
  bytes bridge = 6;                       // §17's id-only section
  AclAudit audit = 7;                     // owner decision 63; Team only
  repeated AclSuspension suspensions = 8; // the Suspends a fold keeps (Folded grants)
  repeated AclSpentGrant spent_grants = 9; // activated and revoked grant ids (Folded grants)
  repeated uint32 evidence_default = 10;  // the document's effective evidenceDefault, compiled at each base
                                          // as each AclRequestRule's evidence is: the ApprovalDecision.channel
                                          // values accepted for an action no requests rule names; default
                                          // all three (owner decision 342)
}
message AclRequestRule {
  bytes rule_id = 1; repeated bytes src_atoms = 2; repeated AclTarget targets = 3;
  repeated uint32 actions = 4; repeated bytes approver_atoms = 5; uint32 approvers = 6;
  int64 default_expiry_seconds = 7;       // expiresDefault: 1 h unless the document overrides it
  int64 max_expiry_seconds = 8;           // maxExpiry: 30 days unless the rule overrides it
  repeated uint32 evidence = 9;           // accepted ApprovalDecision.channel values (§16.8): the effective
                                          // list, evidenceDefault where the rule names none, else its own;
                                          // whether the rule itself names harness stays in AclLocalPolicy
}
// In a *_atoms field an autogroup is 16 bytes: fifteen zero bytes, then its AclAutogroup value, 1 to 14,
// autogroup:dst-owner (ACL_AUTOGROUP_DST_OWNER) being 14; no tag or group id takes that form.
message AclAudit {                        // a reader every member sees (owner decision 63)
  repeated bytes reader_atoms = 1; repeated uint32 repo_kinds = 2; repeated bytes repo_ids = 3;
  bytes audit_opt_in = 4;                 // the k-of-n AuditOptIn record, which api and readers verify
}
message AclTarget {                       // exactly one kind set (owner decision 355)
  bytes atom = 1; bytes sidecar_id = 2; bytes network_id = 3;
  bytes repo_id = 4;                      // sixteen zero bytes: every general or record repo (evs:*, a bare *)
  repeated bytes socket_tokens = 5;       // §9.4's token path of one socket name, 16 B a segment; several
                                          // are alternative paths of that name, newest K_sock first; while
                                          // the K_sock file holds a previous key, compile writes a second
                                          // target with the path under that key (owner decision 334)
  bool socket_prefix = 6;                 // every name strictly below the path, in whole segments; with no
                                          // token, every application and share/ socket; finer globs project
                                          // to their literal prefix
  string public_name = 7;                 // a tls/ or smtp/ socket name or a dns host, its glob kept, the two
                                          // told apart by a /, which no host holds
  reserved 8;                             // an ip target's CIDR, kept in AclLocalPolicy, never in rows
  bool mail_send = 9;
  bytes client_id = 10;                   // a client no binding names, a legacy client among them: D-ACL-5's
                                          // naming it, under an unrestricted grant
}
// The rows above as Atoms, Folded grants and Repo rows below give them, and §8.4's and §11.12's named lists
message AclAtom {                         // Atoms
  bytes atom = 1;
  repeated bytes member_ids = 2;
  repeated bytes sidecar_ids = 3;
  repeated bytes tag_owner_member_ids = 4;  // a tag atom's tagOwners, expanded to member_ids at compile
  repeated bytes client_ids = 5;          // client:<id>, for a client no binding names
  repeated bytes network_ids = 6;         // network:<net>, resolved at save
  string role = 7;                        // role:<name>
  string principal = 8;                   // principal:<name>
}
message AclRule {
  reserved 5; reserved "ports";           // a rule's ports stay in AclLocalPolicy (8.6)
  bytes rule_id = 1;
  repeated bytes src_atoms = 2;
  repeated AclTarget targets = 3;
  repeated uint32 actions = 4;            // AclAction
  int64 expires = 6;                      // 0 none
  AclAudience audience = 7;               // a publish's (8.4)
  AclAppMode app_mode = 8;
  bytes link_spki_sha256 = 9;
  bytes source_rule_id = 10;              // an activated grant's (Folded grants)
  bool ports_limited = 11;
  repeated AclTarget via = 12;            // a route rule's via subjects (Via subjects; owner decision 344)
}
message AclPortRange {                    // a grant's port range on the device alone, never in rows
  uint32 protocol = 1;                    // the IP protocol number; 0 any
  uint32 first = 2;
  uint32 last = 3;
}
message AclSuspension {                   // Folded grants
  bytes subject = 1;
  bytes suspend_id = 2;
  uint32 signer_class = 3;                // 1 owner or sponsor, 2 admin, 3 k of n
  bytes signer = 4;
  uint64 at = 5;
}
message AclSpentGrant { bytes grant_id = 1; int64 retain_until_ms = 2; }   // Folded grants
message AclRepo {                         // every row keeps its signer and the position of its entry
  bytes repo_id = 1;
  RepoKind kind = 2;
  bytes owner_member_id = 3;
  repeated bytes consented_sidecar_ids = 4;
  repeated AclRepoAdminRow admins = 5;
  repeated AclRepoGrantRow grants = 6;
  repeated AclRepoShareRow shares = 7;
  repeated AclRepoRevokeRow revokes = 8;  // config writers' standing RepoRevokes
  AclRepoDeletionRow deletion = 9;        // the newest RepoDelete, with any RepoRestore of its deletion_id
  RepoVersioningLock lock = 10;           // the newest RepoVersioning's
  uint64 holders_shrunk_at = 11;
  repeated AclRepoPrefixRulesRow prefix_rules = 12;   // RepoPrefixRules (owner decision 345)
  int64 holders_shrunk_time_ms = 13;      // §7.9's t_s (owner decision 557)
}
message AclRepoAdminRow {
  bytes sidecar_id = 1;
  bytes signer = 2;
  uint64 at = 3;
  uint64 removed_at = 4;                  // a RepoAdmin{remove}'s position; 0 while the admin stands
}
message AclRepoGrantRow {
  bytes subject = 1;
  RepoGrantRole role = 2;
  int64 expires = 3;                      // 0 none
  bytes signer = 4;
  uint64 at = 5;
}
message AclRepoShareRow { bytes subject = 1; int64 expires = 2; bytes signer = 3; uint64 at = 4; }
message AclRepoRevokeRow { bytes subject = 1; bytes signer = 2; uint64 at = 3; }
message AclRepoDeletionRow {
  bytes deletion_id = 1;
  bool now = 2;
  uint64 deleted_at = 3;
  uint64 restored_at = 4;
  int64 deleted_time_ms = 5;              // the RepoDelete entry's time_ms (owner decision 343)
  bytes signer = 6;                       // the RepoDelete's signer
}
message AclRepoPrefixRulesRow { bytes signer = 1; uint64 at = 2; }   // one RepoPrefixRules that took effect
enum AclAutogroup {                       // §8.4; in a *_atoms field fifteen zero bytes, then the value
  ACL_AUTOGROUP_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ACL_AUTOGROUP_MEMBER = 1; ACL_AUTOGROUP_OWNER = 2; ACL_AUTOGROUP_ADMIN = 3;
  ACL_AUTOGROUP_AUDITOR = 4; ACL_AUTOGROUP_SIDECAR = 5; ACL_AUTOGROUP_TAGGED = 6; ACL_AUTOGROUP_NETWORK = 7;
  ACL_AUTOGROUP_UNTAGGED = 8; ACL_AUTOGROUP_EPHEMERAL = 9; ACL_AUTOGROUP_PUBLIC = 10;
  ACL_AUTOGROUP_INTERNET = 11; ACL_AUTOGROUP_SELF = 12; ACL_AUTOGROUP_SPONSOR = 13;
  ACL_AUTOGROUP_DST_OWNER = 14;
}
enum AclAction {                          // §8.4; AclRule.actions and AclRequestRule.actions
  ACL_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ACL_ACTION_DIAL = 1; ACL_ACTION_LISTEN = 2; ACL_ACTION_ROUTE = 3;
  ACL_ACTION_READ = 4; ACL_ACTION_WRITE = 5; ACL_ACTION_ADMIN = 6; ACL_ACTION_DEPOSIT = 7;
  ACL_ACTION_PUBLISH = 8; ACL_ACTION_SEND = 9;
}
enum AclAudience {                        // zero reads as members
  ACL_AUDIENCE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ACL_AUDIENCE_MEMBERS = 1; ACL_AUDIENCE_MEMBERS_DEVICE = 2;
  ACL_AUDIENCE_LINK = 3; ACL_AUDIENCE_PUBLIC = 4;
}
enum AclAppMode { ACL_APP_MODE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; ACL_APP_MODE_HTTP = 1; ACL_APP_MODE_RAW = 2; }   // zero: http
enum RepoKind {                           // §11.12's kinds, fixed at creation
  REPO_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0; REPO_KIND_GENERAL = 1; REPO_KIND_RECORD = 2; REPO_KIND_CONFIG = 3;
  REPO_KIND_DIRECTORY = 4; REPO_KIND_TEAM_RECORD = 5; REPO_KIND_MAILCFG = 6; REPO_KIND_VAULT = 7;
  REPO_KIND_MAILBOX = 8; REPO_KIND_SECRET = 9;
}
```

**Atoms (owner decisions [339](#od-339), [353](#od-353)).** A tag's or group's atom id is 16 random bytes that the config's sealed `tags` and `groups` tables hold beside its name (§7.9). compile writes an `AclAtom` for every tag the document declares in `tagOwners` and every group in `groups`, whether or not a grant or request names it, and for every derived atom the policy names: `AclAtom{atom = 1, member_ids = 2, sidecar_ids = 3, tag_owner_member_ids = 4, client_ids = 5, network_ids = 6, role = 7, principal = 8}`. A tag atom's `member_ids` stays empty, its `sidecar_ids` lists the sidecars carrying it, and `tag_owner_member_ids` is its `tagOwners` expanded to member_ids at compile, which `CanApplyTag` reads and subject evaluation never does: applying a tag needs a standing member device (untagged, not ephemeral, not read_only) of a member in that list, and no consent, so a declared tag with no rule of its own can still be applied by a Delegation or a tagged `SidecarAdmit`, its sidecars holding what `autogroup:tagged` and the kind defaults give them. A selector with no table name compiles to a derived atom, id = SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/acl-atom" || 0x00 || kind || 0x00 || value)[:16], kind one byte (1 member, 2 sidecar, 3 client, 4 network, 5 role, 6 principal), unkeyed because each value is already server-visible; `network:*` is the kind-4 atom over the one byte `*`, which names no subject until 8.11's shares. Rows name only what a writer can sign and never enumerate app clients: an app device with an owner row matches `user:`, `group:` and autogroups at the gate through `network_client_owner.member_id`, so app clients coming and going change no rows; a legacy client has no owner row and matches only `client:<id>`, `autogroup:untagged`, `autogroup:network` and `*`, D-ACL-5's "naming it" being `AclTarget.client_id` under an unrestricted grant; and `role:` and `principal:` match the identity that `getProvideRelationshipDetails`'s one query loads, never `GetClientIdentity`'s Postgres fallback, so the gate stays under §22.5's `DenyPostgresForTest`. A member that the log's rows no longer hold expands to nothing. A bare `*` dst compiles to `autogroup:network`'s atom, the socket prefix with no token and the wildcard repo, its ip ranges staying on the device. Every group the document defines has a row, and an empty group's, like a tag's with no owners or sidecars, holds only its atom id, so the prefix filer tells a group's atom from a tag's by the head's group atom ids, never by what its row holds: a group's atom names nobody, an empty group's included, and a tag's row names someone (RepoPrefixRules' subjects; [owner decision 559](#od-559)).

**Rule ids ([owner decision 339](#od-339)).** A document rule's `rule_id` is 16 random bytes held in the sealed `rules` file, keyed by the SHA-256 of the rule's canonical form: RFC 8785 JCS of one JSON object per rule, its lists sorted as strings, `id` and `note` left out and socket names in clear, a request writing its effective evidence, `expires_default` and `max_expiry`, so a change of the document's defaults is a change of meaning. An unchanged rule keeps its id across saves and `K_sock` rotations; any change of meaning makes a new id, so live grants under the old one end at that base (FS-14); identical rules compile to one; and compile refuses a rule with no row. An implicit-document rule takes the constant SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/acl-implicit-rule" || 0x00 || u32be(index))[:16], with no table, the index counting its grants and then its requests, and 8.5's `tag:mail` kind-default rules, the only kind defaults that need the head, take SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/acl-kind-rule" || 0x00 || u32be(i))[:16], i 0 the read and 1 the deposit. An activated grant's rule_id is its grant_id. 8.5's `id` never enters rows (8.7).

**Folded grants.** A fold keeps what the entries it drops still decide. `AclSuspension{subject = 1, suspend_id = 2, signer_class = 3, signer = 4, at = 5}`, class 1 owner or sponsor, 2 admin, 3 k of n: a fold keeps a `Suspend` until an `Unsuspend` of its own suspend_id lands, `signer_class` settles who may lift it (the statements below), and `hardDeny`, §7.9's leaves rule and `BridgeIdentity.suspended` read it. A `GrantActivate` folds to an `AclRule`: rule_id = grant_id (32 B), `source_rule_id` the CanonicalAction's rule_id, src the subject's derived atom, targets and actions from `grant_dst` and `grant_allow`, expires = `expires_millis`, and a publish's app_mode and link_spki_sha256; a share's grant, whose CanonicalAction names the other network in `share_network_id` beside its subject, the requesting sidecar, is matched by a request rule's `network:` source, the implicit document's `network:*` or a named network, and folds with that network's derived atom (kind 4) as its source, so the contract gate's share half finds the rule naming `network:Y` in X's rows (8.11; [owner decision 346](#od-346)). compile drops the rule once `source_rule_id` names no `AclRequestRule` in this head (FS-14), once a `GrantRevoke` names it, or once its expiry is at or before the head's newest record time. A `sock:` entry in `grant_dst` holds §9.4's token path in hex, never an application name, since GrantActivate shows api the action; that path dies at the next `K_sock` rotation's end, so such a grant ends there, the closed direction, and is requested again (§9.4). `AclSpentGrant{grant_id = 1, retain_until_ms = 2}`: every activated or revoked grant_id enters `spent_grants`, with `retain_until_ms` the latest `not_after_millis` among its decisions plus 60,000 (8.6's skew); a `GrantRevoke` of an id no activation carried has no decisions to read, so it keeps 0, meaning the network's life, and since readers can verify only an admin's such revoke, these stay few; compile drops a row once `retain_until_ms` is below the newest `ConfigRecord.time_ms` in the head, never by a clock.

**Repo rows.** Every row of a repo's folded access log keeps its signer and position. A `RepoAdmin{remove}` keeps the admin's row, stamped `removed_at = 4` with the removal's position, until the next base's compile drops a row whose removal its retention point has passed, and the deletion row carries `deleted_time_ms = 5`, the RepoDelete entry's time_ms, and `signer = 6`, the RepoDelete's signer ([owner decision 343](#od-343)). Readers, evs and taskworker then judge from rows alone, on any day: a RepoRestore within 7 days of a RepoDelete without now, taskworker's shred at 7 d 10 min after the RepoDelete's entry (§11.12), a removed admin's right at a position before its removal (`AclState.RepoAdminAt`), and evs's reconciler applying a RepoDelete after its entry left the log's retention, writing repo/'s deleted{deletion_id, time, signer} from the row. A repo whose rows' newest RepoDelete stands unrestored gives its standing admins the evs `admin` right alone: no read, write or deposit, and no rule or kind-default right; so the exchange mints only `admin` for a deleted repo, evs's guard honors it for DELETE, with and without now, while its read and write routes stay refused, gkm's guard reads the same rights and, as evs's does, honors a route's rights only whole, so from the moment the RepoDelete is in its state the token passes only gkm's admin routes, which its own repo/ recheck closes outside a re-seed (§10.6's checks row; [owner decision 563](#od-563)), and a RepoRestore's `restored_at` lifts the deletion (§11.12's refused row; [owner decision 351](#od-351)). `subject` in RepoGrant and EvsShare is 16 bytes naming a sidecar_id, an untagged sidecar's member, or any atom the sidecar holds; within 8.6's ceiling only its sidecar_id, a tag it carries or `autogroup:ephemeral` counts; and a config writer's standing RepoRevoke voids grants naming the revoked subject and every grant to a sidecar it names. The config repo's own row comes from no `RepoCreate`, one of kind config staying refused ([owner decision 341](#od-341)): where a state's rows hold no `AclRepo` for the network's config repo, ACL's state build adds `AclRepo{repo_id: Genesis.config_repo_id, kind: config}` with no admins and `holders_shrunk_at` 0, so the kind's defaults answer it alike in every reader, gate and api, all of which hold the Genesis, and base 1's compile stays empty. The rows gain it only at the first entry that shrinks the config's key holders, `AclRepo{repo_id, kind: config, holders_shrunk_at: n, holders_shrunk_time_ms: that entry's time_ms}`, sorted in with the rest and advanced there afterwards like any repo's, which §7.9's `shrunk_repo_ids` may name; until then the synthesized row's t_s is the Genesis's `time_ms` (§7.9's shrink row; [owner decision 557](#od-557)); the state keeps a config row the rows hold and synthesizes one only where they hold none. Every other repo's `holders_shrunk_time_ms` is set by ACL's fold at its RepoCreate, to that entry's time_ms, and with each `holders_shrunk_at` after, and bases carry both, so a verifier that starts at a base reads t_s from the rows.

**Via subjects and route rows ([owner decision 344](#od-344)).** A rule's via subjects ride `AclRule.via = 12`, apart from its targets, so they no longer share targets with its dial destinations, and an internet rule that names a via holds to it at every gate. A route rule that names no `via` takes as its via subjects the advertisers of the approved routes that name it: `BridgeRows.routes = 2` holds a `BridgeRouteRow{route_id = 1, advertiser = 2, route_rule_ids = 3}` for every approved route in force, written at the fold and applied by every verifier in log order after a base, as the egress mode is, and the state adds each advertiser to the via subjects of the no-via route rules its row names (§17.8). The server sees only the ids §17.8 already describes (§2.8 api-7).

**K_sock's overlap ([owner decision 334](#od-334)).** While the `socket/key` file holds a previous key, compile writes a second `AclTarget` under that key beside each `sock:` target, a pure function of the head, so gates' `MayListen` and `MayDial` do not change and readers recompile the same rows; a grant the rotating head drops is dropped on both paths. A requested grant's `sock:` entry is a literal token path (Folded grants), so it gets no second path and works through the overlap as §9.4 says. The first writer head at or after `rotated_at_ms` + 10 min clears the previous key (§9.4). Rows therefore hold both paths until that head, which links them for as long as those rows are kept, at least 30 days (§2.8 api-7).

**Grant chains.** These statements act at once as §7.9 deltas, checked by api and readers against the state at their log position until a writer folds them in, so none waits for an admin (owner decisions [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74)). Each opens with §7.9's `StatementHeader`, whose `at` pins the signer's state. Re-applying a base's tail judges nothing (§7.9's tail verdicts; [owner decision 356](#od-356)): `AclState.ReapplyStatement` takes only the parts of a verdict that the statement's body and signers give, the signer and an OwnerConfirm's target, and derives every other fold input itself from the body and the rebuilt rows it folds into, never from a check run again: a Suspend's or Unsuspend's class and whether an Unsuspend lifts, a RepoRevoke's or RepoGrant's config-writer standing, a RepoCreate's owner and consented sidecars, a GrantRevoke's retain_until_ms and a GrantActivate's grant. Each is a pure function of (body, signers, rebuilt rows), so a new device, a gate that started at the base and a long-running reader fold alike, and a head change that would make the check refuse on the rebuilt rows changes no fold:
