**Statement bytes.** The table's statements, each opening with §7.9's `StatementHeader` and its other fields in the order the table writes them, with the named lists they use (§7.9's record bytes):

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/acl.proto: the grant chains and access logs
message GrantActivate {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes grant_id = 2;
  bytes canonical_action = 3;             // §16.8's CanonicalAction, as stored
  repeated Signed decisions = 4;          // ApprovalDecisions
}
message EvsShare {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  bytes subject = 3;
  int64 expires = 4;                      // 0 none
}
message OwnerConfirm { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes sidecar_id = 2; }
message RepoCreate {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  RepoKind kind = 3;
  // inbox = 4 (RepoInbox: 0 none, 1 group, 2 admin; the table's RepoCreate row) joins this fence once acl.proto
  // declares it
}
message RepoAdmin {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  bytes sidecar_id = 3;
  RepoAdminChange change = 4;
}
message RepoGrant {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  bytes subject = 3;
  RepoGrantRole role = 4;
  int64 expires = 5;                      // 0 none
}
message RepoRevoke { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes repo_id = 2; bytes subject = 3; }
message RepoDelete { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes repo_id = 2; bytes deletion_id = 3; bool now = 4; }
message RepoRestore { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes repo_id = 2; bytes deletion_id = 3; }
message RepoVersioning {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  RepoVersioningLock lock = 3;
  bytes sealed_rules = 4;                 // optional: a VersioningRules (RepoVersioning, above)
}
message RepoPrefixRules {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes repo_id = 2;
  bytes sealed_rules = 3;                 // a PrefixRuleSet: 48 B and a multiple of 256 B (RepoPrefixRules, above)
}
message PrefixRuleSet { repeated PrefixRule rules = 1; }   // sorted, no rule twice; no server holds it
message PrefixRule {
  bytes subject = 1;                      // 16 B, one of the subjects row's
  repeated bytes path = 2;                // the prefix in whole components; none: every path
  PrefixAction action = 3;
}
message AuditOptIn { StatementHeader header = 1; repeated bytes reader_atoms = 2; int64 not_after = 3; }
message AuditOptOut { StatementHeader header = 1; }
enum RepoAdminChange {
  REPO_ADMIN_CHANGE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; REPO_ADMIN_CHANGE_ADD = 1; REPO_ADMIN_CHANGE_REMOVE = 2;
}
enum RepoGrantRole {
  REPO_GRANT_ROLE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; REPO_GRANT_ROLE_DEPOSIT = 1; REPO_GRANT_ROLE_READER = 2;
  REPO_GRANT_ROLE_WRITER = 3;
}
enum RepoVersioningLock {
  REPO_VERSIONING_LOCK_UNSPECIFIED = 0; REPO_VERSIONING_LOCK_LOCKED = 1; REPO_VERSIONING_LOCK_UNLOCKED = 2;
}
enum PrefixAction { PREFIX_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0; PREFIX_ACTION_WRITE = 1; }
// sidecar/protocol/bridge/auth.proto: the three statements sidecar/device's posture applies between states
// (§17.8)
message GrantRevoke { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes grant_id = 2; }
message Suspend {
  StatementHeader header = 1;
  bytes subject = 2;
  bytes suspend_id = 3;                   // random; only an Unsuspend naming it lifts this
}
message Unsuspend { StatementHeader header = 1; bytes subject = 2; bytes suspend_id = 3; }
```

**Access logs ([owner decision 8](#od-8)).** A repo's access log, the ordered chain of its RepoCreate, RepoAdmin, RepoGrant, RepoRevoke, RepoDelete, RepoRestore and RepoVersioning statements, rides §7.9 deltas into config heads, which keep it for the repo's life, each statement with the log position of the entry that carried it, so a reader judges a signer's repo admin right at any position, one before its retention point included (§16.11's repo file row); readers replay it, members check Adds and Removes against it (§10.9), and, as a RepoDelete or RepoRestore precedes its §11.12 route, the log never shows a deleted repo live, so a re-seed after a site loss can refuse a repo whose log ends in a RepoDelete past 7 days or with `now` (§19.10). A DROP push rides its ref, not this log, since it changes no reader, writer or key (§11.7). A team directory's decision entry cites the `RepoGrant` or `EvsShare` it approved by hash and log position, or the `ApprovalDecision` a `GrantActivate` spends, as its request's receipt; the statements are unchanged (§16.11). Config writers, who alone write config heads, are the AdminSet members' member devices (untagged, not ephemeral; 8.4) that are not read-only, and only k of n adds one (§7.5, §7.9; owner decisions [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [128](#od-128)).

**Saving.** A writer's device validates, compiles, tests, previews and signs; a failing test rejects the head (https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/syntax/policy-file). The writer's device runs `tests` before signing, and readers do not rerun them at replay. A test's `ip:<cidr>#route` check judges a route rule by its prefixes: an accept passes on a rule whose prefixes hold the whole range, and a deny fails on one whose prefixes overlap it. A route rule that names no prefix reaches its destinations' routes in force, which no save can see (8.4's readings), so a deny of any range also fails where such a rule takes the test's source and names, for that source, a sidecar among both its via subjects and its subject destinations, whose routes in force could serve any range, the failure naming that rule, while an accept of such a range still fails: under grant 1 every member's `ip:` deny test fails until the Team narrows grant 1, by an `ip:` destination or no `route`, so a deny test bounds what the head can route to ([owner decision 615](#od-615)). An `autogroup:internet` route rule reaches every public destination through its vias' routes in force, which no save sees either, so a deny of a range holding a public address (global unicast and not private) also fails where such a rule takes the test's source, the failure naming the rule, while an accept of such a range still fails: an internet rule and a `*` rule fail the same public-range deny, a deny of a private range is unaffected, and a Team keeping public-range deny tests beside an internet rule narrows the rule's source before its next save ([owner decision 653](#od-653)). The config repo's signed head history is the change audit: read-only `ur acl log` lists each head's config_version, signer and time and never runs through MCP (D-MCP-17), and a rollback is `ur acl push` of an older source, a new head at a higher version (D-ACL-9). Validation refuses unknown atoms, approver-only atoms (`autogroup:sponsor`, `autogroup:dst-owner`) outside `approver`, tags outside `tagOwners`, bad ports, overruns, `evs:` paths (X2), owner-bound readers outside the `audit` block, any grant on a Team scope's own mailcfg ([owner decision 644](#od-644)), `evs:` grants naming the config or the directory (D-ACL-13, D-ACL-24), an `audit` block without an `AuditOptIn`, publishes past §13.9's limits, `raw` outside `public` and `link`, and a raw `link` without a pin; `network:` selectors resolve from labels or aliases, never legacy names (D-DNS-2). compile is a pure function of the head, so `user:`, `network:` and `client:` selectors resolve through the config's sealed `resolve` file (§7.9's paths), one row per selector the policy names: the writer fills it at save, a server answer being only a proposal, as §7.6 treats SCIM. For an email it uses its own invite record where it has one, else `GET /network/members`, and the preview lists each new or changed row with the member's role and devices, which the person's confirmed save signs; for a network, §12's ResolveNetworkLabel, by label or alias, the id pinned until a person saves again, so a moved alias retargets nothing (§7.12); for a client, a dual-signed `SidecarIdentityBinding` the writer verifies itself, a client with no binding staying a literal client id. Validation refuses a member_id with no live MemberRow, so a stale row fails closed until the next save; 8.4's grammar and the stored source do not change. The preview names readers a repo cannot seat (§8.12).

**Code and limits.** Pure Go `acl_*.go` in the sidecar root; `ur acl test policy.hujson` runs offline. Per-tier limits ([owner decision 73](#od-73)) are §20.4's `acl_*` keys in `config/all/pro.yml` (`model.Pro()`). ProjectionRows hold at most 4,096 atoms and 4 MiB, a forwarding Delegation's row about 200 B since its reader key is a gkm object its digest names ([owner decision 202](#od-202)), and §7.9's `config_admissions` bounds subjects; validation and api's verifier refuse a head or base over a limit (`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`). An acl statement's re-application in a base's tail reads only its body and the rebuilt rows, an effect the new rows no longer allow being dropped (`ReapplyStatement`; §7.9's apply; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 5). Every tier may hold a document (owner decisions [50](#od-50), [73](#od-73)); after a downgrade new heads must fit (§20.7).

### 8.9 Distribution: local evaluation and gate caches

**Clients.** Every admitted sidecar follows the config repo and §7's `team` hints, verifies config heads and the authorization log (§7.9) and evaluates its own rules in `AclEngine`, with no always-on compiler ([owner decision 6](#od-6)). The engine swaps compiled state through an `atomic.Pointer`, checks without locks or allocation, and compares its auth pin (n, A_n) in HeadCheck (§6.4), which any admitted reader, agents included, may witness ([owner decision 129](#od-129)): it refuses a lower pin, and reconciles, alarms, relays (`proven`) and stops sealing in shared groups as §6.4's auth rules say. For a host, §17.8's compiler reads through the engine every rule and activated grant by which each subject may dial it, route through it or exit through it, and the same for what the host may reach (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 12). An app's forwarding role follows them itself in its VPN component, by its forwarding Delegation's reader key, through the same engine (§18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)), and between its compiles `sidecar/device`'s posture checks the chain and bases' signatures and applies at once, as denials, the revocations it can check by their signers' keys in the rows it holds, opening nothing (§17.8's forwarding roles).

**Gates.** api's verifier (§7.9) keeps each network's newest base and the entries after it, which api, evs and gkm read from §7.9's verified Redis cache `{acl_<networkId>}e` when it reaches `{acl_}v` and every pin they hold, else from `proj/` on the first metadata cluster ([owner decision 136](#od-136)); only api writes that cache, which decides nothing, and other gate services fetch from api, as only those three and taskworker reach the metadata tier (§2.8 evs-10). Each process caches them per (network, n), loading asynchronously outside packet locks on api's `INCR {acl_<networkId>}v` (class `$`, xops/redis-set-notify-keyspace-events.sh:23) after every entry it appends and on a 5-min poll; a network without a config repo costs one map miss (R-ACL-8). Gates check every entry's chain from their own pin wherever they read it, and refuse a lower n, or a second A_n at one n, with an alarm. A sockets process that learns a network's log moved (the `{acl_}v` event, a position in its own store above the one it holds, or after a resubscription a `{acl_}v` that differs from the one its state was loaded at) and has not verified the new entries within 5 s refuses for that network until it has (§9.8); with no such evidence the last verified state serves, an api outage included, since api is the log's only writer ([owner decision 337](#od-337); DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 13). Taskworker's gkm reconciler tells its cache of the networks §10.6's networks row names, at its runtime's start and again for one the bounded cache evicted, so a quiet network's hints, key deletions and sweeps run after a restart; gkm and the reconciler read their state through this cache ([owner decision 371](#od-371)).

**The internal gate surface ([owner decision 340](#od-340)).** Services with no database read rules, facts and quotas from one read surface on api under `/internal/gate/`, a prefix the lb refuses from outside. Each caller class holds its own bearer in `secret_files`, one vault file per gate caller class, connect's first, which api verifies by its SHA-256 in constant time (§19.4, §19.16); mxedge's platform listener holds a class of its own, `mxedge-platform`, which alone reaches the role-mail notice route, `POST /internal/gate/abuse-notice` (§21.8), and which no other route takes, so no edge block's bearer can page the rota ([owner decision 650](#od-650)). `GET /internal/gate/projection/<network_id>?after=<n>` answers the body of the Client route `GET /network/config/projection` (§7.9): `{genesis, entries, rows, tip: {n, chain}, more}`, each message verbatim in base64, paged, from the retention point when `after` is before it; `GET /internal/gate/rows/<network_id>/<rows_sha256>` answers the ProjectionRows bytes verbatim (`application/octet-stream`), which the caller holds to their hash; `GET /internal/gate/listen-facts/<network_id>` answers `network_verified`, whether a `mail_network` row exists, and each `network_tls_cert` row's name and expiry; and `GET /internal/gate/over-limit` answers §20.7's list, spent and storage-over networks apart. One encoding serves devices and gates, and gates verify entries' chain and signatures as they do from `proj/`, so api stays a carrier. A gate refreshes a network's projection on `{acl_<networkId>}v` and the 5-min poll, its facts at most every 60 s off the inline path, and the over-limit list every 5 s. A process that has never loaded them stays not ready, and a `tls/` entry with no cached facts answers `unavailable`. Other gates' reads and §20.14's quota routes join the prefix under the same rules.

**A gate behind the log ([owner decision 337](#od-337)).** On a failed refresh a gate keeps serving what nothing contradicts: with no evidence that the log moved, the last verified projection, facts and list serve without limit, so an api outage changes nothing, api being the log's only writer. A sockets process answers `unavailable` for a network once it has had evidence for 5 s, this section's target for server gates, that the network's authorization log passed what it holds and it has not verified the new entries: the `{acl_<networkId>}v` event, a store answer naming a higher position, or after a resubscription a `{acl_}v` that differs from the one its state was loaded at (§9.8).

**Targets**, revocations included: to server gates ≤5 s; applied on connected clients p50 ≤1 s, p99 ≤5 s, measured from acks (`POST /acl/ack`) kept 7 days (§2.8). An ack's body is `{version, time_ms}`, `time_ms` used only for the delay histogram, and an ack counts only above the client's last and at or below the network's head row ([owner decision 355](#od-355)). At an app host's forwarding role (§18.6) the targets bind revocations, which apply on their hint with no compile. A grant is an opening, which only a compile applies, and the role keeps its compile delays on every host class, coalescing 2 s after a hint and starting no compile within 10 s of the last, for the battery and §18.10's per-compile memory cap; so a grant is bound by the p99 alone, when no compile ran in the 10 s before it: at a quiet moment it applies 2 s after its hint, and within 10 s of the previous compile up to 10 s after it ([owner decision 558](#od-558)).

### 8.10 Enforcement points

Server gates are coarse (who talks to whom, holds a name, fetches ciphertext) and read `AclRows`; clients check direction, port, socket, alias and path where access yields plaintext or a local effect. An outward action passes a server gate only under a standing grant, a request whose §7.9 delta carries the approval and whose GrantActivate signatures verify, or a decision sent with `Idempotency-Key: <effect_key>`: the gate first answers a use committed under that key from its `approval_use` row while the row lasts, and otherwise runs §16.6's spend check and consumes a use in the effect's own transaction (one row per approval and effect key, §16 D-MCP-11), so a lifted token cannot publish (I-8) and a retry past `not_after` gets its stored result; a gate keeps the decision only in memory, and `approval_use` only the approval id, use index, effect key, state, result and the decision's expiry (§2.8 api-10). Platform and ControlId clients skip the contract gate; nothing is checked per packet (connect/CODESTYLE.md:106-107).

| resource | server point: rows read | client point |
|---|---|---|
| subject dial, `ip` route | `CreateContract` (`:859`-`:933`): subjects, dial and route rules (src → via), `has_document`; a 5 s heads snapshot; subject ids on the existing query (`server/model/network_client_model.go:2544`) | stream accept (§6); the provider hook per flow (`connect/ip.go:5676,3602`; `connect/ip_icmp.go:786`) |
| `sock` | sockets (§9.10): token paths and public names | listener verifies the dialer |
| `evs` | the token exchange's `repo:<id>:deposit\|r\|rw\|admin` scopes from `AclRows` (§7.8, [owner decision 2](#od-2)); evs and gkm honor `r`, `rw` and `admin` only for current readers and writers, and `deposit` only while its subject may deposit there (D-ACL-21), and check §11.8's gate; a deleted repo's standing admins get `admin` alone, which evs honors for §11.12's DELETE ([owner decision 351](#od-351)), and every config writer gets `admin` on the config repo ([owner decision 352](#od-352)); `admin` also covers DROP pushes and their cancels, in an owner-bound repo only from its owner's consented sidecar_ids (§11.7); in the team directory, as in every repo, only `admin` covers the erasing pushes, closure uploads and slot deletions §11.12's directory row lists, and only its consented, not-read-only admins get it (§7.8, §16.11) | heads only from writers ([owner decision 7](#od-7)); every Add, Remove and wrap (§8.12) |
| `dns` publish | dns, certs, tlsedge (SNI → name → socket): publish rules; the `tls/` `ValidateListen` refuses `raw` unless the grant's audience is `public` or `link`, and a raw `link` whose grant carries no pin (§13.9); an edge (`autogroup:public`) Find for a `tls/` name passes as §9.10's edge Finds do ([owner decision 348](#od-348)) | only the listener's front enforces `audience` and a raw `link`'s pin, both from its own evaluation (§13.7, §21.4) |
| `mail` | mxedge: `listen` on `sock:smtp/25/mx` (a scope's `smtp/25/mx.<scope>`); smtpedge: `mail_send`, From domain (§14.5) | receivers, local mail server: `mail:<alias>` (§15.10) |
| shares, egress | contract gate: share grants, `bridge` (§17.9) | provider: a verified `WindowDelegation` matching C13's sealed network (§17.9) |

**Contract rule** (networks with a head row), on the request's own `Companion` bit, replacing the origin-free normalization at `:917-927`: (1) a non-companion a→b with `reach(a,b)` passes, class data; (2) a non-companion without it but with `reach(b,a)` is a reply: the gate returns that verdict from memory, then `CreateContract` runs `model.CompanionOriginExists` once, with the companion path's bounded origin wait, and an origin passes as class data; (3) otherwise the witness exception below gives class `control`, else `ContractError_NoPermission`; (4) a companion a→b needs `reach(b,a)`. Step 2 precedes step 3, or a reply racing its origin would stick on a control contract. `reach` is an active dial or route grant, sockets expanding to listeners and `ip` grants to via subjects (8.8). connect is left as it is, asking for a same-network reply as a non-companion contract (8.3), and sidecar RPC replies ride this rule (§6.10.1). The gate's own decision reads no Postgres (§22.5); the origin read belongs to contract creation and runs only with a head row and only when `reach(a,b)` fails. While b's origin stands, a holds a data contract to b, so a legacy b, which checks nothing, is reachable from a for that time, as under any reply path. The gate also refuses Network contracts from §18's hosted devices (I-10), and Public ones from subjects in `exits` or `none` egress mode (`ContractError_NoPermission`); a device's default egress and route local traffic, and its network's requirement of default egress, change no gate (§17.11; owner decisions [606](#od-606), [607](#od-607)). In any network, with a head row or without, `CreateContract` refuses Public contracts from declared no-egress clients, from M1 (§20.8). With a document, providers refuse LAN, loopback, link-local and overlay destinations to Network sources no rule allows ([owner decision 50](#od-50), §17). Witness exception: any two admitted sidecars of one network, neither revoked, parked nor suspended, get a Network contract of class `control` without a reach grant; it carries only what §6.4 lets a control contract carry, never IP, which receivers and providers enforce and the gate does not check (D-PROTO-18, D-PROTO-21).

**Receivers** see window-client ids [R:connect-ip](design/design-research/connect-ip.md); C13 seals the source client's stored `acl_subject_client_id` (never a request field), `source_network_id`, the contract class and the subject's `WindowDelegation` into `StoredContract` (D-PROTO-19), and receivers admit a native flow only from a verified delegation (§17.9). A **legacy** client (no `acl_enforcing`, set at mint, §7.7) is reached only through an unrestricted grant, naming it (`AclTarget.client_id`, 8.8) or a selector containing it as dst with `dial` and no `ip` ports (its rule's `ports_limited` false), `sock` or `via`; otherwise it is source-only ([owner decision 106](#od-106)).

### 8.11 Cross-network sharing and invites

- **Consent.** X grants `network:Y` a resource with an admin's approval ([owner decision 74](#od-74)), the grant's CanonicalAction naming Y in `share_network_id` so that X's rows hold a rule whose source is `network:Y`'s atom (8.8; [owner decision 346](#od-346)), and Y grants its subjects `dial` on `network:X`; access is the intersection, enforced as two halves: X's provider checks X's grant against the verified source network and share (§17.9), and Y's routers and the contract gate (8.10) check Y's grant; neither sees the other's groups. X's half verifies only that a current reader of Y's config signed for the share, never Y's per-subject grant, so the unit X can check is Y's whole current reader population: a Y reader that Y's policy denies, running modified software, reaches X's granted targets only on a contract the operator mints, still within X's grant (§17.9, §2.10).
- **Invite.** `ur bridge invite` (cli/UI.md:50) files X's request with a hashed 256-bit code, `uses = --count` and a 7-day window; `accept-invite` (`:51`) files Y's, the server binds `invited_network_id`, and each activation is a delta in its network. `POST /acl/accept-invite` takes two body forms ([owner decision 350](#od-350)). A claim, with the code's hash alone, takes a use, binds the invited network to a share, the invite's own row first and then a new row of the same target table for each later claim of a multi-use code, and answers the share's id with the sharing network's sealed targets; a repeat claim answers the share the network already holds and takes no use. A completion, with the share id, the sealed accept and the status, stores them once. A claim binds before the invitee's preflight, so a refused preflight still holds its use and completes with a refusal status, and the ShareKey's sealed body rides in the sealed accept, so `network_bridge_share` holds no column for it (§17.9). Y's approving admin creates the share's ShareKey in a `secret` repo of its own (8.5); X's approving admin's device pins it as §17.9's share pins say, in the act that files the share's GrantActivate, and the ShareKey certifies a ShareSigner per generation of Y's config, so a sidecar Y removes signs only within §17.9's bound. Both networks' tables travel under §17.9's share seal, bound to its label, both networks and the table's version; a multi-use code's accepters all hold its key, so a seal proves only a code holder, and X's approving admin is what pins one ShareKey to one share. The row is deleted once its uses run out or its window closes.
- **Contracts and data plane.** Shares ride the IP path ([owner decision 86](#od-86)) as FriendsAndFamily toward marked sidecars, escrowed from the dialer's network (§6.10.1, Q-PROTO-3 (b), [owner decision 11](#od-11)); §4's C18 stops providers treating those sources as Public toward private destinations, and §17's hook admits them only under a `route` or `dial` grant.

### 8.12 ACL and evs readers

- **Readers.** `RepoReaders(repo)` is the set of sidecars that 8.6's `allowed` gives read on `evs:<repo>`, from kind defaults, the audit set, rules, EvsShares and the access log, so `RepoReaders(directory)` is every admitted sidecar of the team (8.5); writers likewise, and readers accept heads only from writers ([owner decision 7](#od-7)). The directory's `admin` needs consent and a device that is not read_only; a repo whose newest RepoDelete has no RepoRestore gives no right but its standing admins' `admin` (8.8); and the audit block counts only with a non-empty `audit_opt_in` ([owner decision 355](#od-355)). Under 8.8's prefix rules, which are [Later](DESIGN-DEFER.md#acl-prefix-write-rules) ([owner decision 586](#od-586)), `AclEngine.AllowPrefixWrite`, over a write's repo, ref and paths, is the writer's own refusal, at the state its push pins, before anything is sent (`EVS_PREFIX_RULE`, §18.5); at launch no write asks it. An expiry drops a reader at its time (§7.9's coverage); evs and gkm honor an `r`, `rw` or `admin` scope only while its subject reads or writes the repo, as the scope says, in their newest state, and a `deposit` scope only while 8.6 gives its subject deposit there, under its ceiling and hard denies, or it reads an owner-bound repo it does not write (§16.8's receipts), computed as the exchange computes the scope; gkm's drop-key route takes the same check (§7.9's tokens row).
- **Leaves, seats and wraps (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).** Member devices are MLS leaves of the repos they read, in the config and team directory groups only as §7.9's `leaves` rule entitles them; other sidecars (tagged, ephemeral, CI, cloud agents) hold §10.5's per-generation `ReaderWrap`s, the config repo's and the directory's included, and agents a live Delegation covers read its repos through the Delegation's wrap (§10.5). A group holds at most 1,000 leaves (D-KEYS-2):

```text
seats (owner decisions 144, 182; §10.9 commits)
config    §7.9's leaves rule alone decides the config leaves and their moves: the first 1,000 live member
          devices by (live_since, sidecar_id) are leaf-entitled, members accept a config Add or external join
          only of an entitled device, and the rest read by ReaderWraps, as agents do; an entitled device
          without a KeyPackage also reads by ReaderWrap, the first from its admission's signer, until it
          uploads one, no other device takes its place, and a leaf that may commit it then adds it
directory the team directory's group, the one exception to data seats, follows D-KEYS-23 (owner decision
          182): every admitted sidecar of the team reads it (8.5), none keyless
data      member devices stay leaves of the data repos they read, at most 1,000 a repo; a reader without a
          seat waits keyless, and the writer's preview and the console name the repo; committers fill a free
          seat with the earliest-admitted waiting member device that has a KeyPackage (KF2), members checking
          only that it reads and the 1,000 bound; a seated device keeps its leaf until a Remove, and an
          external commit that adds a leaf needs a free seat
wrapped   a wrapped config or directory member commits no Add or Remove in that group (§7.9): for an
          admission it signed, it writes the new device's first ReaderWrap at once, so that device reads with
          no admin online (owner decision 128); for a revocation, it rotates by wraps to every remaining
          holder, and the next leaf commit removes a leaf target; revoking a wrapped member device is, as for
          an agent, a new generation not wrapped to it, while a move shrinks nothing and needs no rotation
```

- **Committers (§10.9; owner decisions [113](#od-113), [128](#od-128)).** Signed grants, admissions and revocations carry the authority: any writer leaf commits the Add or Remove one requires, as may, in the config and directory groups, the leaf that signed it; a recovery-admitted device self-joins by external commit if leaf-entitled (§7.9), else reads by its RecoveryWrap, then by wraps. Wrapped writers rotate by re-wrapping but never commit an Add or Remove; revoking an agent is a new generation not wrapped to it.
- **Removal (no server transaction, [owner decision 5](#od-5)).** When an authorization-log entry drops a key holder, evs closes the repo's write gate (§11.8, D-EVS-18); Removes cover revoked, cascade-parked, suspended, no-longer-reading and stale sidecars and, in the config and directory groups, leaves that lost entitlement, each by its signed input (§10.9).
- **Invariant (the primary control).** A client never encrypts to an epoch or generation that a sidecar its own evaluation marks as a non-reader holds, a live Delegation's key aside, which its reaped agents and its ephemeral agents past their own `not_after` keep until it drops (§10.5's Residual; [owner decision 114](#od-114)), committing the Remove or rotation first, and checks every Add and wrap against §7.9's admissions, §8.5's consent and the access log, so a breached server can neither admit a ghost nor grant a reader (R-ACL-7).

### 8.13 Alternatives considered

| option | pros | cons | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server-compiled policy, or a Postgres authority log beside it | one compiler; Tailnet Lock's shape | the server grants reach and readers; plaintext policy | superseded (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6)) |
| Every admitted sidecar an MLS leaf | one mechanism | a commit per agent join and reap; agents share the leaf cap | superseded ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) |
| A cap of 1,000 member devices per network | config leaves only | refuses Teams past about 330 members with three devices each | rejected ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) |
| Server-only or client-only enforcement | simple | a breach grants anything, or anyone takes names | rejected: both enforce |
| Server-checked evs prefixes or aliases | finer gates | plaintext paths and aliases | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Admins add vault or mailbox readers | no owner step | silent admin reads | rejected ([owner decision 126](#od-126)) |
| Cedar or OPA Rego | expressive | hard to compile to bitsets | rejected |

### 8.14 Decisions proposed

**D-ACL-1 (proposed).** One HuJSON source in the config repo; every sidecar compiles it, and each base's writer compiles the rows. *Why:* no server compiler ([owner decision 6](#od-6)).

**D-ACL-2 (proposed).** Deny is the base; grants form a union; hard denies win; tier defaults are starting documents. *Why:* no precedence ambiguity.

**D-ACL-3 (proposed).** `network_client.acl_subject_client_id`, written once at creation, stays nullable until a backfill and validated CHECK (§19.7; connect/CODESTYLE.md:87-88); NULL means itself for a top-level client, else its source client's subject. Every insert writes a value, a top-level client its own id; a child client is its own subject when it asks for `strict_exp` itself and its parent has none, and otherwise takes its source's subject; a child of a legacy child keeps NULL; and the backfill names a sidecar's client by its `sidecar_identity_binding` row ([owner decision 355](#od-355)). *Why:* identity without recursive queries.

**D-ACL-4 (proposed).** The in-memory gate checks non-companion contracts forward, passes a non-companion with only the reverse reach as a reply once contract creation finds its origin, checks companions reversed, and skips networks without a head row (8.10). *Why:* R-ACL-8; it closes the origin-free companion path, and connect asks for a same-network reply as a non-companion contract.

**D-ACL-5 (proposed).** Legacy clients are reached only through unrestricted grants, otherwise source-only ([owner decision 106](#od-106)). *Why:* only endpoints enforce ports, and Network providers allow everything.

**D-ACL-6 (withdrawn).** Superseded by owner decisions [5](#od-5) and [6](#od-6): the config repo and local evaluation replace server compilation.

**D-ACL-7 (proposed).** Requested grants activate within `maxExpiry` only on approvals over the rule's `evidence` channels, harness evidence in a tainted run only where the rule names it (§16.6). *Why:* R-ACL-4, I-8, I-9, owner decisions [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75) and [142](#od-142).

**D-ACL-8 (proposed).** One `Suspend` per subject acts at once at gates and clients, closes its contracts and, for an agent a live Delegation admitted, drops that Delegation's shared reader key (§10.5). *Why:* pitch5.html:729; a suspended agent holding a live shared key would still open what the server delivers to that key.

**D-ACL-9 (proposed).** Failing tests block a config head, and rollbacks are new heads. *Why:* R-ACL-10, I-16.

**D-ACL-10 (proposed).** Shares need two-sided consent and resolve to FriendsAndFamily toward marked sidecars, source-pays (Q-QUOTA-5 (a)). *Why:* the only non-Network mode outside the egress index.

**D-ACL-11 (proposed).** evs grants are per repo (read, write, admin, deposit), from policy or the repo's access log ([owner decision 8](#od-8)); prefix writes follow Q-EVS-3: a repo per prefix. Prefix rules in a general repo, which every reader would enforce and no server check (§11.7), naming only subjects an admission fixes and binding the repo's admins too (8.8; [owner decision 345](#od-345)), are [Later](DESIGN-DEFER.md#acl-prefix-write-rules) ([owner decision 586](#od-586)), so at launch separate repos are the write boundary; they remain the only boundary a server enforces, and the only one that limits reads. *Why:* the repo is the cryptographic boundary, and X2 hides paths.

**D-ACL-12 (proposed).** Mail authorization follows Q-MAIL-8 (a), split as in §8.10. *Why:* under X6 and X7 no edge sees an alias.

**D-ACL-13 (proposed).** Kind defaults precede every document; owner-bound repos add readers only as §8.5 allows, and policy never widens the config repo's writers. *Why:* R-ACL-11; owner decisions [5](#od-5), [63](#od-63), [110](#od-110) and [126](#od-126).

**D-ACL-14 (proposed).** Sidecars are subjects in `autogroup:sidecar`, named by `sidecar:<id>`; `RepoReaders` returns sidecar ids. *Why:* agents multiplex onto sidecars (D-CORE-4).

**D-ACL-15 (proposed).** Policy reaches servers only as `AclRows` in §7.9's ProjectionRows, compiled at each base and recompiled by readers; §8.8's grant chains ride the authorization log as statements. *Why:* one signed store (owner decisions [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6), [8](#od-8), [74](#od-74)).

**D-ACL-16 (proposed).** Server gates evaluate only the newest verified base and the entries after it, cached per (network, n) and refreshed by `INCR {acl_<networkId>}v` and a poll. *Why:* owner decisions [5](#od-5), [6](#od-6) and [72](#od-72); R-ACL-8.

**D-ACL-17 (proposed).** Member devices hold leaves, in the config and team directory groups by §7.9's rank (their first 1,000 live member devices) and in another data repo up to 1,000, seated earliest-admitted first, each kept until a Remove; wrapped config and directory members and all other sidecars read through §10.5's per-generation ReaderWraps (§8.12). *Why:* owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144) and [182](#od-182): agents cost no commit and read with no member device online, members accept config Adds by one function of the log, and no network stops at 1,000 member devices.

**D-ACL-18 (proposed).** Clients never encrypt to a non-reader (§8.12); the evs gate is D-EVS-18. *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2) and [5](#od-5) leave no server transaction for a gate.

**D-ACL-19 (proposed).** Subjects are classed before expansion (member device, ephemeral, tagged, other client), and an ephemeral sidecar's evs access takes 8.6's ceiling: the config's and its team directory's read, the directory's own-path writes, kind-default deposits, and grants and EvsShares naming it (8.4-8.6). *Why:* inheritance gave a quick burner its owner's write and admin, while every admitted sidecar reads the config and its team's directory (owner decisions [6](#od-6), [171](#od-171)).

**D-ACL-20 (proposed).** `autogroup:untagged` is untagged non-sidecars, and writers compile the implicit document into the projection's rules whenever `has_document` is false, so gates and clients evaluate one function (8.5, 8.6). *Why:* two compilers must not publish different rows for one file.

**D-ACL-21 (proposed).** evs and gkm honor a capability (`r`, `rw`, `admin`, `deposit`) only while its subject holds that right on the repo in their newest verified state, gkm's drop-key route included (8.12; §7.9's tokens row). *Why:* a group edit or Suspend must not wait out a 15-minute token.

**D-ACL-22 (proposed).** One consent predicate, §8.5's `consented(d, M)` (scoped, invited, genesis, confirmed, each on a signature outside §7.9's parked set), which §5.6 and §7.9 cite; the invited device is M's first admission in log order that is neither ephemeral nor read-only, carrying the `invited` capability bit its admitting device set after the invite's join MAC verified, from an invite no ephemeral enrollment redeems, and a JIT member's invite comes from the admitting admin device. *Why:* three definitions left JIT members with no consented device, as an ephemeral or read-only first device would, and a stolen device's consents must stop with it.

**D-ACL-23 (proposed).** As an approver, `autogroup:dst-owner` names a request's destination's owner, a tagged sidecar's sponsor, or a socket's listeners' one owner or sponsor, else an admin. The implicit document and Team's starting document carry the directory's default rule: dial on members' devices, tagged sidecars and sockets; approver dst-owner; evidence device or presence; 30 days at most. A touched member who approves meets §8.6's admin requirement ([owner decision 180](#od-180)), and an admin's decision counts toward the rule's k only where dst-owner resolves to an admin or the rule's approvers name one ([owner decision 349](#od-349)). *Why:* owner decisions [74](#od-74), [179](#od-179) and [180](#od-180): [owner decision 74](#od-74)'s admin stood in for the touched member, who here consents directly.

**D-ACL-24 (proposed).** The `directory` kind's defaults come ahead of every document, which may neither widen nor narrow them. They give every admitted sidecar of the team read, and every one that is not read_only write of its own paths and stream. §8.6's ceiling admits ephemeral sidecars to both. *Why:* [owner decision 171](#od-171)'s "members and their agents"; one fixed audience, which policy cannot quietly shrink.

**D-ACL-25 (proposed).** A drop is a repo admin's act, in an owner-bound repo only a consented, not-read-only device of its owner's; a lock refuses and voids drops. *Why:* owner decisions [126](#od-126), [160](#od-160), [173](#od-173) and [183](#od-183).

### 8.15 Open questions

**Q-ACL-1.** [X3] Who is the policy authority? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5)-[8](#od-8), [110](#od-110)):** a customer key authority from v0, compiled on customers' devices, in the config repo (§7.9, §8.7); Q-TRUST-1, Q-TEAM-5 and Q-KEYS-5 follow. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-2.** Cross-cutting (§2). How should team-management.html:814 and :917 describe policy? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 72](#od-72)):** "signed under your key authority, stored encrypted in your network's config repo. URnetwork enforces an id-only projection: it sees which ids may reach which, never names or rule text," replacing both lines' false claims. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-3 (withdrawn).** Merged into Q-PROTO-3 and Q-QUOTA-5, decided by [owner decision 11](#od-11).

**Q-ACL-4.** What do sidecars get on Community and Pro without a document? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 105](#od-105)):** untagged sidecars act as app devices until the network writes a policy, tagged ones get §8.5's implicit tagged rules, and [owner decision 120](#od-120) keeps that allow-all, disclosed. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-5.** How do clients without the engine take part? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 106](#od-106)):** with a policy, legacy clients are reached only through unrestricted grants, otherwise source-only, and listed by `GET /network/clients` (§8.10, D-ACL-5). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-6.** May Community networks write a policy? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 73](#od-73)):** every tier may, within §20.4's limits (§8.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-7.** Who approves requested grants, and for how long? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [74](#od-74), [75](#od-75)):** §8.6's approvers, for 1 h by default and 30 days at most, a lone device's harness prompt counting unless `evidence` excludes it; [owner decision 142](#od-142) (2026-11-04) counts it in a tainted run only where the rule names it. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-8.** Which names may server-stored policy carry? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** moot; the rows carry ids, opaque atom ids (16 random bytes the config's sealed tables hold beside each name, §7.9), socket token paths ([owner decision 67](#od-67)) and public names. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-9.** Cross-cutting (§7, §10). May tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars read and write through per-generation X-Wing wraps instead of MLS leaves? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 114](#od-114)):** (a) yes, in every repo granting them access, amending [owner decision 60](#od-60) (§8.12). A leaf's Remove still waits for a leaf, and a reaped Delegation-admitted agent, or any holder of its reader seed, reads later generations until the Delegation's key drops (§10.5 lists when, `not_after` at the latest); a holder of the whole auth key also admits fresh agents, each with its own wraps, until the Delegation ends (§7.9's delegation row). [Owner decision 144](#od-144) extends config wraps to member devices past §7.9's first 1,000. *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-10.** Cross-cutting (§7, §10, §11). Does [owner decision 8](#od-8)'s "network admins can always grant or revoke" reach owner-bound kinds? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 126](#od-126)):** (a) no: there admins revoke and add only [owner decision 63](#od-63)'s visible audit reader, and other readers need the member's signed consent (§8.5), keeping pitch5.html:640's "Sessions open only when the developer shares them", for session contents ([owner decision 170](#od-170)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-ACL-11.** Who approves a member's request to reach another member's device, or a tagged sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 180](#od-180)):** (a), the destination's owner, or a tagged sidecar's sponsor, through the approver atom `autogroup:dst-owner` in the directory's `requests` rule (8.4, 8.5); §8.6's admin clause is met when the touched member approves, amending [owner decision 74](#od-74) for this case; an admin stands in when the sponsor is gone, and a Team may ask for two approvers (options (b), owner and admin, and (c), an admin alone, not taken). *Residual:* none.

### 8.16 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:119.** Met as [owner decision 5](#od-5) reads it: stored rules are signed and encrypted, and every device gets the whole config in real time through evs subscriptions ([owner decision 6](#od-6)).
- **PLAN.md:147** ("participants are leaves"): member devices are leaves, and other sidecars, like member devices past the config and directory groups' first 1,000 (§7.9), read through wraps (Q-ACL-9; owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).
- **PLAN.md:74** (networks reach an abstract socket): other networks reach a listener by IP through a share ([owner decision 86](#od-86); Q-BRIDGE-6); application sockets are dialed only within their network (§9.4).

- **Provides:** `sidecar.ParseAclPolicy`, `sidecar.CompileAcl` → `AclRows`, and `CompileAclLocal(input *AclCompileInput) (*AclLocalPolicy, error)` on the same input, which holds what rows drop on purpose (exact socket globs, aliases, per-rule harness naming and names for previews) and is never serialized off the device; read-only `ur acl log` (8.8); `AclState` over an `AclAuthView`, which has no `Suspended`, `AclState.Suspended` answering from the rows' folded Suspends, and gives `Genesis()`, `SidecarIds()`, `CascadeVoids(signer, at)` and `Sidecar(id)` → `AclSidecar{Row, MemberId, TagIds, Ephemeral}`; `AclState.ReapplyStatement` (8.8); `AclEngine.AllowPrefixWrite` (8.12); gate checks `Reach`, `MayListen`, `MayDial`, `MayPublish`, `MaySend`, `EvsAccess` and `RepoReaders` (sidecar ids), each naming its rule or delta; `AclEngine` (`AllowInbound`, `AllowRoute`, `AllowAlias`, which checks `mail:<alias>` at receivers and the local mail server, §17's `BridgeAlias` being a share's delta and no ACL resource, `VerifyRepoMember`, `VerifyHeadSigner`); §8.5's consent rule, the `directory` kind default, and the directory's default rule with `autogroup:dst-owner` (§16.11); §8.8's grant chains and access logs, each EvsShare with its expires, signer and carrying position for §7.9's cascade, and the lock's refusal and voiding of drops (§11.7, §11.13); §8.12's data-repo seats and the directory's; the contract gate's `control` class for witnesses and its remote-search exchanges (§6.4, §11.14); `CanApplyTag` (§7).
- **Consumes:** §4 C13, C18; §5 keys, bindings; §6 `Signed`, push, HeadCheck, Hello's feature bit 0; §7 the config repo, authorization log, projection and its verified read cache, the `leaves` rule, token exchange, removal; §10 MLS; §11 the gate, lifecycle routes and the DROP push and its job (§11.7, §11.13); §13.9's `tls/` `ValidateListen`; §16 `ApprovalDecision`, the spend check, `approval_use` and §16.11's directory requests; §17.9 `WindowDelegation`; §20 limits.
- **Subprotocol messages:** none; §7's `team` hints and `evs:<repo_id>` (§6.8).

No route takes policy text. Internal, by a caller class's bearer: 8.9's `GET /internal/gate/projection/<network_id>`, `/rows/<network_id>/<rows_sha256>`, `/listen-facts/<network_id>` and `/over-limit`.

§11.12's DELETE and restore require RepoDelete and RepoRestore in evs's newest projection, filed first, and take deletion_id and now from them; §7.9 designs `{acl_}e` with api its only writer, and §22.8's FS-62 loses it and serves it stale; §6.18 and §23.6 ship control contracts with M4's contract gate, and §22.8 runs FS-21's witness case then; §13.9's `ValidateListen` refuses a raw `link` whose grant carries no pin, and §2.8 api-7 lists publish rules' app modes and raw link grants' client-certificate SPKI SHA-256; §5.4 and §18.5 alarm on admissions under a member that its keys did not sign; §7.5's and §7.6's invite joins refuse an ephemeral enrollment; §7.9's SidecarRow keeps each admission's, AdmissionConfirm's and OwnerConfirm's signer and position, and its cascade lifts a park only by a signer outside P; §10.5 drops a live Delegation's key at a `Suspend` of one of its agents, and §7.9 refuses a Delegation-signed admission whose tags differ from the Delegation's; §2.10 and §22.7 cover an admin minting a device under a member, and §22.7 runs the one-definition, consent, grant-replay and seat cases, its cascade case restoring no owner-bound repo by an admin's AdmissionConfirm of a device a P member admitted; §11.7 and §11.13 check a DROP's signer against `AclRepo`'s admins and consented sidecar_ids, never refuse a cancel under a lock, and void at the job's start a drop a lock meets; §16.6 refuses DROP pushes and their cancels; §16.11 files directory requests under 8.5's directory rule, its decisions citing 8.8's receipts; §6.4's receivers accept SEARCH on a control contract only at Hello feature bit 0; FS-85 runs `autogroup:dst-owner`'s approvals, every reader refusing an admin's vault `EvsShare`, and a share's `expires` ending it with no device online; and FS-19 runs the ceiling: under an Admin in a personal network, the config read and deposits, no other repo's generation, and its config head and base refused, with no evs `rw` on the config (M2-out); Delegation-admitted, the config's next generation by its own ReaderWrap after a DelegationRevoke; tagged and in a Pro network, a read grant or vault EvsShare opening exactly its repo, its removal a shrink (M4-out); a Team network's Member and Admin runs, the team directory read with writes to its own paths only, and a member invite refusing an ephemeral enrollment (M6-out); and a quick burner's mailbox EvsShare opening exactly its repo (M8-out).

### 8.18 Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CreateContract` regression | Medium | High | one map miss without a head row; PostgreSQL tripwire test; benchmark gate |
| Gate-cache fan-out on each log entry | Medium | High | per-process caches; coalesced reloads; jitter |
| Gates run a stale or divergent projection | Medium | Medium | readers recompile rows; HeadCheck compares (n, A_n); any writer republishes |
| ACL and MLS roster drift | Medium | High | client invariant; versioned gate; drift alarms |
| A rogue or compromised admin admits a device under a member | Medium | High | §8.5's consent; KF2 parks it; the member's devices alarm |
| A data repo granted to more than 1,000 member devices seats only 1,000; the rest wait keyless | Low | Medium | the preview and console name the repo; seats fill earliest-admitted first; data-repo wraps would need the owner ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory seats past 1,000 by wraps instead ([owner decision 182](#od-182)) |
| Network sources reach LAN and loopback without a document, or through legacy providers | High | High | disclosed ([owner decision 120](#od-120)); any tier may write a document ([owner decision 73](#od-73)); unrestricted-grant rule; suspension |
| Approval fatigue | Medium | Medium | 30-day requests; standing grants; presence keys |
| A `resolve` row goes stale: a member leaves, or a network's alias moves | Medium | Low | validation refuses a member_id with no live MemberRow, so the row fails closed until the next save; a network's id stays pinned until a person saves again (§8.8's Saving) |

### 8.19 Phasing

- **v0 (§23.4):** at M2, `AclRows`, grant chains and access logs, every 8.8 statement, `GrantActivate`, `GrantRevoke`, `Suspend` and `Unsuspend` among them, being checked and folded from M2 (`RepoDelete` and `RepoRestore` included; an `EvsShare` opens an owner-bound repo only with §16.8's read receipts, D-MCP-18, and ends at its `expires`, which every reader honors from M2), acl.proto's `autogroup:dst-owner` atom, which readers evaluate from M2, as the implicit document's directory rule names it, the `directory` kind's default (8.5; D-ACL-24), compiled from the binary as every kind default is, so a device on M2-M5 code admitted to a team network computes the directory's readers, writers and erasers as M6 code does (D-PHASE-9), and `RepoVersioning`'s id-level fields and lock, folded from M2 (D-PHASE-9), local evaluation, the evs and gkm gates with current-reader scopes, member leaves by §7.9's rule and agent wraps (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144)), §8.5's consent rule, the ephemeral ceiling, whose config read FS-19 gates at M2-out, policy tests, rollback and change audit; at M4, the filing flows of requested grants and suspension, the contract gate with its `control` class for witnesses, and the closing of open contracts, which C13 seals from M4 (D-PROTO-18); other gates with their services. Blocked by X8 (§6), §5's binding, §7.9's config repo and authorization log, §10's MLS, §11's `config` kind and, for window clients, §4's C13.
- **v1 (M6):** team networks ([owner decision 55](#od-55)), with two-approver rules, scope hosts, the audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)) and config wraps for member devices past §7.9's first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory itself, created with each team, its seats under §7.9's leaves rule and Team's starting document's default rule with `autogroup:dst-owner` (owner decisions [171](#od-171), [180](#od-180), [182](#od-182)); cross-network shares (Q-PROTO-3, Q-QUOTA-5, C18); peer-list filtering (`server/connect/resident.go:4826`).

## 9. Abstract socket listeners and the scheduler

### 9.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns PLAN.md's abstract socket listener (PLAN.md:67-69): the `<net>:<name>` grammar and name blinding, registration, find-listener and accept (PLAN.md:82), the scheduler, the `sockets` service, the Go API, `ur share`, and gate, quota, overload and metrics hooks. §6 owns streams and contract modes, §7 and §8 the config repo, policy and projection (X3), §13 the TLS front, §14 and §15 mail, §17 forwards and invites. Each connection reaches one listener; group fan-out is §15's.

### 9.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-SOCK-1 | Publish that a client listens on `network:name` | PLAN.md:69 |
| R-SOCK-2 | Reach one of many listeners via a fair scheduler "similar to socket reuse on linux" | PLAN.md:69 |
| R-SOCK-3 | The TLS edge does find-listener and accept | PLAN.md:82 |
| R-SOCK-4 | Reach controlled by client, group, network | PLAN.md:74 |
| R-SOCK-5 | Renames and reclaims never move or capture registrations | `server/controller/account_controller.go:13` |
| R-SOCK-6 | Service off the data path; load-aware for uneven listeners | derived |
| R-SOCK-7 | TLS edge 1/20/200 by tier; forwards unlimited | PLAN.md:358-359 |
| R-SOCK-8 | One naming rule for §13-§15; Go adapters; CLI and MCP hooks | PLAN.md:17-20; derived |
| R-SOCK-9 | Internal names hidden from servers; gates read only the signed projection | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [67](#od-67), [72](#od-72) |
| R-SOCK-10 | `ur share add` makes a link that `ur share get` redeems at most `--count` times; file transfer counts toward the transfer balance | cli/UI.md:35-38, :97; R-CTX-31 |

### 9.3 What exists today

- No repo has a listener registry, accept handshake, scheduler or client-to-client stream ([R:connect-transport](design/design-research/connect-transport.md) §2.10); sdk listeners are "future work" (`sdk/SOCKET.md:7`).
- Substrate: ids ≥1024 and inline non-blocking handlers (`connect/subprotocol.go:46-50`, `:78`); 16 KiB frames and a 60 s ack timeout (`connect/transfer.go:1722-1724`, `:904`); receivers get the source id and `Peer{ProvideMode, Roles, Principal}` (`:608-619`); residents drop forwards not from their client (`server/connect/resident.go:4950`).
- Precedents: HMACed contracts (`connect/transfer_contract_manager.go:291-317`); Redis 8.10.2 hash-field TTLs (`xops/main/ansible/playbook-redis-clusters.yml:634`); Lua helpers (`server/redis.go:955-966`).
- Removal revokes, deletes provide keys and sets `{X}c_removed` for the client and its active descendants (`server/model/network_client_model.go:1485-1612`, `server/model/client_close_model.go:54-66`); connect consumes the flag (`server/connect/key_event_subscriber.go:129`). The 30-day idle marker skips it (`server/model/network_client_model.go:4315-4340`); idle clients hold no lease. Child tokens fail once an ancestor is inactive (`server/session/by_jwt.go:678-699`).
- warp lbs proxy to same-host blocks with `least_conn` (`warp/warpctl/config.go:1644-1665`) on every lb host (`warp/services/services.go:521-551`).

### 9.4 Addresses and namespaces

```text
address = [ net ":" ] name     ; no net: the caller's network; ur/ names: urnetwork-edge
net     = dns-label            ; a §12 label or alias (X5)
name    = seg *7( "/" seg )    ; 1-8 segments, <= 112 bytes: <net>:<name> fits §6's 128 B target (10-char label)
seg     = 1*63( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" / "_" / "." ) / "@"   ; not "." or ".."
                               ; uppercase ASCII folds to lowercase; other bytes are refused
; reserved first segments: tls, smtp, c (retired: invites use §17's IP path, owner decision 86), ur, sys,
; share (9.9's `ur share` only, blinded), single characters and "_"-prefixed segments; new namespaces
; need a §9 amendment
```

- **Canonical key `(network_id, name)`.** §12 resolves `<net>` per call (legacy names only interactively, D-DNS-2), and stored state holds the id, so renames move nothing.
- **Blinding (Q-SOCK-4, D-SOCK-13).** Edge names (`tls/`, `smtp/`, `ur/`), public anyway (SNI, DNS, MX), reach the service in plaintext; others only as the token paths below, like evs paths ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), sealed for listings; the service refuses other plaintext names. The keys derive from `K_sock`, the config repo's 32-byte socket-name key, which every admitted sidecar reads (§7.9; agents and overflow member devices by wrap, owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144)).
- **Rotation.** `K_sock` rotates on the key-holder changes that make §11.6's path epochs due, in classes of its own: a member's or member device's removal and compromise retirements at once; other key-holder shrinks and authorization expiries (§7.9's expiry identities) at most daily (a reap of an agent its live Delegation covers is none). The path epochs themselves are all batched ([owner decision 585](#od-585)), and these classes stay as they are. Only config writers change it (§8.8), so it rotates in the next writer head, republishing the projection; without a writer online it waits, and member devices alarm 24 h after the trigger. A rotating head keeps the previous key in the `socket/key` file with `rotated_at_ms` (§8.8). Listeners register both paths until `rotated_at_ms` + 10 min by their own clock, so §2.8 sock-1's 10 min holds even with no writer online, and a lister tries the previous key while the file holds it. The overlap is kept at the gates too: while the file holds a previous key, compile writes a second target under that key beside each `sock:` target, and the first writer head at or after `rotated_at_ms` + 10 min clears it; a requested grant's `sock:` entry is a literal token path with no second path, so it works while listeners register that path, through the overlap, and then its subject requests again (§8.8; [owner decision 334](#od-334)).

```text
keys   K_tok = HKDF-SHA256(K_sock, salt network_id, info "urnetwork-sidecar-v1/socket-token"), 32 B; K_seal the
       same with info "urnetwork-sidecar-v1/socket-seal"
token  t_0 = network_id (16 B); t_i = HMAC-SHA256(K_tok, t_{i-1} || seg_i)[:16], seg_i lowercased;
       name_token = t_1 || ... || t_n, as in §8's AclRows
seal   sealed_name = nonce[24] || XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_seal, nonce, pt = name || 0x00 to 112 B,
       ad = network_id || name_token): 152 B, a random nonce per seal; names hold no 0x00
open   a lister tries the newest K_sock, then within a rotation's 10 min overlap the previous one, strips the
       0x00 padding and keeps a name only if it re-derives name_token
```

| Namespace (owner) | Form, example (`acme` is an alias) | Listen; dialer | Stream protocol |
|---|---|---|---|
| TLS endpoint (§13) | `tls/<port>/<host>`, `acme:tls/443/blog` | approved `listen`, and `publish` on `dns:<host>` (§13.9); tlsedge | `tls`, passed through (X1, D-TLS-1) |
| Inbound mail (§15) | `smtp/<port>/<host>`, `acme:smtp/25/mx` | approved `listen`; mxedge | `smtp-starttls`, ending in the receiver (X6) |
| Platform (§13-§15) | `ur/<service>`, `ur/smtpedge` | `urnetwork-edge` clients; any enrolled client, authorized by the service (§14.5), not §8 | per service |
| Application | any other, `acme:db/primary` (blinded) | `listen`; `dial` within the network (other networks use IP, §6.4) | the listener's |
| Share (9.9) | `share/<token>` (blinded) | `listen` by `ur share add`, `exclusive`; `dial` by `ur share get`, within the network | 9.9's share header |

`ur/` Finds cross networks, as the names resolve to `urnetwork-edge`. `<host>` is `@` or one LDH label (`blog`, `api-dev`), as a wildcard certificate covers one label; a v1 Team scope (Q-TLS-3; owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)) adds `<label>.<scope>` hosts within one 63-byte segment (`smtp/`: `mx.<scope>`), and deeper names are refused. Custom domains (§12) alias such hosts. `<port>` has no leading zeros: `tls/` takes §13's 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 ([owner decision 121](#od-121)), `smtp/` 25. Owners register `ValidateListen` (quota, certificate, port, host depth, the scope against the projection and, in a member scope, its consented devices, §8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126); for `tls/`, a `raw` application mode only under a publish grant whose audience is `public` or `link`, §13.7) and `FirstListen`/`LastUnlisten` hooks, which stay seams with no DNS consumer: a zone's `*` and `@` address records follow its grants, never its listeners (§12.7; [owner decision 335](#od-335)).

### 9.5 Registration

A registration is a lease on `(network_id, name, listener_client_id)`, at most one per client and name, since one connect client serves a client id (§5).

```go
// POST /socket/registrations (JSON, connect/api/bringyour.yml): the client's full set, so listen,
// heartbeat, drain and unlisten are one idempotent call; a set over 1,024 entries goes as pages
type SocketRegistrationsArgs struct {
    SetVersion    uint64                `json:"set_version"`   // per client, increasing; a set's pages share
                                                                // it; older sets are refused
    KeyStart      []byte                `json:"key_start"`     // this page is the whole set within name keys
    KeyEnd        []byte                `json:"key_end"`       // [key_start, key_end); empty: unbounded
    Registrations []*SocketRegistration `json:"registrations"` // <= 1,024, sorted by name key (name, or
                                                                // name_token for blinded names)
}
type SocketRegistration struct {
    Name       string      `json:"name"`        // tls/, smtp/ and ur/ names only (9.4)
    NameToken  []byte      `json:"name_token"`  // other names: the token path, 16 B a segment
    SealedName []byte      `json:"sealed_name"` // with name_token: 9.4's 152 B seal
    ListenId   *connect.Id `json:"listen_id"`   // random per Listen; older tickets refused
    Protocol   string      `json:"protocol"`    // default "tcp"; one protocol per group
    Version    int         `json:"version"`
    Alpn       []string    `json:"alpn"`        // tls/: ALPN ids served
    AppMode    string      `json:"app_mode"`    // tls/: "http" (default; h2, http/1.1 or no ALPN reach §13.7's
                                                 // HTTP front, D-TLS-13) or "raw"; other names: ""
    Weight     int         `json:"weight"`      // default 100, 1-1000: relative share
    MaxStreams int         `json:"max_streams"` // default 256: hard cap at the listener
    Exclusive  bool        `json:"exclusive"`   // refuse later registrations
    Affinity   bool        `json:"affinity"`    // honor affinity keys (9.7)
    Serving    bool        `json:"serving"`     // default true; false keeps the lease, takes no tickets
    Draining   bool        `json:"draining"`    // no new tickets; issued ones accepted
    Inflight   int         `json:"inflight"`    // load report
    Claim      []byte      `json:"claim"`       // §6 Signed by the identity key, purpose socket-registration, over
                                                 // (network_id, name or token path, listen_id, protocol, app_mode);
                                                 // Find returns it with tickets for the dialer's check (9.6)
    CertifiedNames []string          `json:"certified_names"` // tls/: the custom hosts and aliases mapped to this
                                                 // name for which the listener has an unexpired certificate
                                                 // installed; outside the signed claim, since they only route
    AcmeNames      []*SocketAcmeName `json:"acme_names"`      // tls/: the names it holds a pending TLS-ALPN-01
                                                 // challenge for, each {name, claim_seq}: the account lock's
                                                 // claim it answers under (§13.8)
}
```

- **Pages.** A call carries at most 1,024 entries and takes one bucket token (9.10); a larger set, unlimited in size ([owner decision 66](#od-66)), goes as pages over consecutive key ranges under one `set_version`. Each page is the whole set within its range (an entry outside it refuses the page), so entries it lacks there unlisten at once, and an eager report sends only its own page.
- **Re-check.** Each call re-checks the projection (9.10) and quota per entry and recreates missing state, so Redis loss heals in one heartbeat; an entry answered `revoked` closes with its streams. The service judges a page on one verified state and stamps each lease with the listener's `sidecar_id`, the authorization log position it was admitted at and the page's `set_version`. A removal for cause leaves a tombstone in the group for 10 min, and an unlisten one for 60 s: a later write admitted below the tombstone's position, or from an older set, is refused, and the caller of a write fenced by a position its process has not reached is answered `unavailable` with `retry_after_ms`, its page's other entries applied (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 13).
- **Certified and ACME names.** A `tls/` registration may list the custom hosts and aliases it is certified for and the names it holds an ACME claim for. §13.9's `ValidateListen` holds both to rows, a certified name to the sidecar's unexpired certificate row and an ACME name to the account lock's claim that sidecar holds, drops what the rows do not bear out and never refuses the entry for them, so a listener keeps its network names; a list past its count, a setting, is malformed (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.10).
- **Lease.** Heartbeats every 15 s ± 20% carry load, and eager reports follow in-flight moves ≥ max(8, 25% of `max_streams`), at most every 2 s; leases are 45 s hash-field TTLs whose expiry stops tickets, not streams.
- **Unlisten** stops tickets at once (a racing ticket gets `retry`, the `tcp_migrate_req` analog); **drain** ends at zero in-flight or after 30 s (cloudflared's default, [R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.8), resetting the rest.

```proto
message SocketHint {             // §6 0x1001, topic `sock`: the client calls registrations at once, and the
                                 // answer is authoritative; version: a per-client sequence from the service
                                 // clock (ms), which Redis loss cannot lower
  SocketHintKind kind = 1;
  bytes listen_id = 2;
}
enum SocketHintKind {
  SOCKET_HINT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  SOCKET_HINT_REVOKED = 1;       // a grant was revoked or §21 suspended the name
  SOCKET_HINT_DRAIN = 2;         // forced drain
}
```

### 9.6 Find and accept

The service never contacts the listener; the dialer presents a Find ticket in the §6 OPEN (D-SOCK-4).

```text
dialer               sockets service               listener L1 / L2
  | POST /socket/find --> | projection: dial? pick (9.7) |
  | <-- [ticket L1, ticket L2]                         |
  | §6 OPEN{ticket L1, early data} ---------------> L1 admits
  | <------------------------------- ACCEPT | REJECT(code)
  | retry/busy/5 s timeout: OPEN{ticket L2} ------> L2
  | both fail: Find with the failed tickets (<= 3 Finds)
```

**Find** runs in order, and a refusal signs nothing (D-SOCK-15):

```text
step  check (service)                                                           refusal
1     the calling client's control-plane bound (9.10)                           unavailable, retry_after_ms
2     the newest verified projection allows the dial (9.10), checked before     denied
      the group is read, so refusals hide names
3     the paying network (§20.6: the listener's for edge Finds, else the        quota
      caller's) is not spent in §20.7's OverLimit set, re-read every 5 s
4     pick (9.7), then the listener check: the service signs only for a         no_listener; busy;
      listener its own newest state allows, judged on its lease's stored        unavailable
      sidecar_id, removing one it refuses for cause, and gives no ticket for
      one admitted at a position above its own: unavailable when none of the
      picked can be judged (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 13)
5     sign the primary and backup tickets; edge and ur/ Finds write the {svc_} pair, a tls/ or smtp/
      pair only at or above the floor a removal left
```

```proto
message SocketTicket {           // signed: <= 370 B with a 112-byte name and dialer_sidecar_id, or an 8-segment token path
  bytes ticket_id = 1;           // 16 random bytes, single use
  bytes network_id = 2;
  string name = 3;               // tls/, smtp/ and ur/ names only
  bytes listener_client_id = 4;
  bytes listen_id = 5;           // 16 B
  bytes dialer_client_id = 6;    // edges: one of the caller's K clients
  bytes dialer_network_id = 7;
  uint64 issue_time_millis = 8;
  uint64 expire_time_millis = 9; // issue + 30 s
  uint64 policy_version = 10;    // §7.9 log position n that allowed it, at or after any GrantActivate
  bytes grant_id = 11;           // projection or requested grant: receipts, revocation
  bool backup = 12;
  uint64 grant_expire_time_millis = 13; // streams end here; 0: none; ur/: issue + its service's grant
                                 // length, 60 min by default (ur/smtpedge: 125 min)
  bytes name_token = 14;         // other names: the token path (9.4)
  reserved 15;                   // withdrawn policy_delta_seq
  bytes dialer_sidecar_id = 16;  // 16 B, ur/ tickets alone: the dialer's sidecar, its listener's subject (owner
                                 // decision 560; ur/ tickets, below)
}
message SignedSocketTicket {     // in StreamOpen.ticket (<= 512 B); §6's Signed format, purpose socket-ticket
  string key_id = 1;             // a service key; fixes the algorithm (Ed25519)
  bytes ticket = 2;              // SocketTicket
  bytes signature = 3;
}
```

**Find's request.** `POST /socket/find` carries `protocol`, `min_version` and `alpn`, 9.7's filter, and, for a dial tlsedge resolved through the custom-host map or the alias table, `server_name`, the hello's server name, empty for a name under the network's own zone; §2.8's sock-2 lists them (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.10).

**`ur/` tickets ([owner decision 560](#od-560)).** A `ur/` ticket names its dialer's sidecar in `dialer_sidecar_id = 16`, 16 bytes, which the service fills at Find from the `ur_sidecar_id` of the caller's service token, which it has already authenticated (9.8's service tokens; [owner decision 588](#od-588)), and signs with the rest; `tls/`, `smtp/` and edge tickets leave it empty, edges naming no sidecar. smtpedge reads the stream's subject from the admitted ticket, with no client-to-sidecar lookup or cache, and judges §8's `mail_send` for it (§14.5), a `ur/` stream whose ticket names no dialer sidecar answering TRY_LATER, failing closed; every `ur/` listener may read its subject the same way. The field adds about 18 B, within `StreamOpen.ticket`'s 512 B.

**Edge Finds.** A `urnetwork-edge` caller sends its K client ids, and each ticket's `dialer_client_id` is `ids[h(listener_client_id) mod K]`, so a listener's edge streams share one client (§13.6). Edge and `ur/` Finds set §6.10.1's pair, field `<dialer_client_id>` of `{svc_<listener_client_id>}`, under one of two rules. A `tls/` or `smtp/` pair is written with a TTL of the lesser of the grant's remaining life and 15 min; a registration call that accepts an edge entry of the client renews its pairs, at most every 5 min a process; and a removal leaves a floor that refuses a write allowed at an older position, so a revoked, removed or dead listener's pairs end within 15 min whatever any sweep did ([owner decision 338](#od-338)). A `ur/` pair lives its service's grant length, refreshed per Find: grant length is per `ur/` service, 60 min by default, and `ur/smtpedge`'s is 125 min, `grant_expire_time_millis` = issue + 125 min with a `{svc_}` TTL of 125 min, §14.4's 2 h of DATA plus 5 min for the ticket's 30 s, the pre-TLS exchange and `SmtpOutcome`. Contracts keep §6.10.1's rule and roll at their 60-minute deadline while the pair lives, and the edge's own timers still end the connection at §14.4's 30 min, or 2 h in DATA mode, so the longer grant adds no longer session. Revocation or the last edge unlisten deletes a pair.

**Listener admission** runs in order; step 6 is [owner decision 6](#od-6)'s local evaluation:

```text
step  check                                                                         refusal (StreamRejectCode)
1     the signature verifies under a key from registration responses                invalid
2     listener_client_id is this client; listen_id is current                       invalid; retry
3     dialer_client_id is the Required session's source, always; it passed §6.4's   invalid
      Hello check unless dialer_network_id is urnetwork-edge (edges send no Hello),
      and an edge ticket names a tls/ or smtp/ name
4     unexpired by local clock plus the server_time offset; ticket_id unseen,       invalid
      kept until expiry
5     in-flight below max_streams; §20 has not stopped new streams (§20.6)          busy; quota
6     its own evaluation of the config repo, at the ticket's log position or        denied
      later (§7.9), allows the dial
7     ACCEPT, keeping the ticket as reach evidence (§16); the stream ends at
      grant_expire_time_millis or revocation
```

**Dialer.** Before OPEN, a sidecar dialer checks the ticket's claim against the listener's Hello binding and the listener's `listen` grant in its own config ([owner decision 3](#od-3)). Each attempt waits 5 s: `retry`, `busy` and timeouts try the next ticket, `denied` stops, `quota` waits `retry_after_ms`, `invalid` refetches once. These are §6.7's `StreamRejectCode`, one to one: `retry` 1, `busy` 2, `denied` 3, `invalid` 4, `quota` 5; 0, unspecified, is a protocol error, taken as `invalid` (§6.11). The next Find carries the failed tickets, which the service verifies, so only holders report. A report excludes the listener for that dialer; ejection for all needs reporters from 2 networks within 30 s, read literally: reporters whose `dialer_network_id`s differ, so ejection and `ejections_total` act on `ur/` names only, and other namespaces rely on exclusion, the backup ticket and the 45 s lease; edges report only accept timeouts. Both last 30 s per consecutive ejection, up to 300 s, for at most half a group (Envoy's defaults, https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/cluster/v3/outlier_detection.proto).

### 9.7 The scheduler

Each Find runs weighted power of two choices (P2C; [owner decision 65](#od-65)), which stays effective on stale load where least-loaded herds (Mitzenmacher, IEEE TPDS 11(1), 2000, https://www.eecs.harvard.edu/~michaelm/abstracts/tpds2000.html):
1. Filter to live, `serving` listeners not draining, ejected or excluded for this dialer, matching protocol, version and ALPN (an offered id the listener serves, or none, which §13.7 dispatches by `AppMode`), with `reported_inflight < max_streams`, the listener's own report alone, `est` staying for step 3's comparison; if none remain, ignore ejections and exclusions. A dial with a server name matches only listeners certified for it; a dial offering `acme-tls/1` matches only listeners holding a claim for the name, whatever their load, and takes the one with the newest claim, with no backup and no draw; and a listener that lists only `acme-tls/1` matches no other dial (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.10). Without affinity, groups above 64 listeners filter a random 64 (`ZRANDMEMBER`, Redis ≥6.2, https://redis.io/docs/latest/commands/zrandmember/), bounding a Find's cost.
2. Sample two distinct candidates in proportion to `weight`.
3. Pick the lower `(est + 1) / weight`; the other is the backup.
4. `est = reported_inflight + issued`, where `issued` sums, over dialers, each dialer's primary tickets since the listener's last report, each counted for at most 30 s (unredeemed tickets expire), and clamped per dialer at c = max(4, ⌊10% of `max_streams`⌋). The clamp bounds the estimate only: Find never refuses or delays a ticket for it, so a dialer's tickets are limited by step 1's `reported_inflight < max_streams`, its control-plane bucket (9.10) and the listener's admission (9.6, step 5).

- **Affinity (opt-in).** A rendezvous hash of `affinity_key` skips listeners above 1.25 × mean `est` (https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.01350); tlsedge sends a keyed hash of the visitor's /24 or /48, never stored.
- **Fairness.** Weighted sampling reaches every listener, and no dialer moves `est` by more than c. A dialer that takes tickets and opens nothing cannot make a listener look fuller than c streams to others. In turn, one dialer's burst of short connections counts at most c above the last report, so P2C can send that burst to one listener past its real load until the listener's next report: an eager one once in-flight moves by max(8, 25% of `max_streams`), at most every 2 s, else the 15 s heartbeat (9.5). The listener's `max_streams` answers the excess `busy`, and the backup ticket takes it. Find's own `busy` means the listener said it is full: step 1 never filters on `est`, which would hold a listener with many dialers to about `max_streams` new streams per report interval. Saturation returns `busy` without a server queue, and dialers back off with jitter.
- **Throughput.** One Find issues one primary ticket for one stream, so a sidecar dialer opens at most `sockets_control_qps` new streams a second per sockets process (50, burst 500; 9.10), and an edge process W2's 2,000 (§19.5), whatever c is. A listener takes at most `max_streams` over its mean stream time: a 256-stream listener with 100 ms streams takes about 2,560 a second. A lone sidecar dialer is therefore bound by its bucket, never by c: connection throughput is the lesser of the dialers' buckets and `max_streams` over the mean stream time, never concurrent-stream capacity alone (§22.5's one-dialer case).

### 9.8 The sockets service

Stateless processes keep all state in Redis Cluster, with no Postgres tables; §2.8's sock-1 to sock-5 give fields and TTLs, and `sock` hints are connect-4.

```text
{sg_<network_id>_<h16(name)>}  group HASH: per listener m: registration, r: in-flight, i: issued, e: ejection,
                               x: a removal's tombstone (9.5);
                               per dialer shares and exclusions; v: version; ZSET …ix orders the leases;
                               h16 is the first 16 hex digits of SHA-256
{svc_<listener_client_id>}     Service pairs (9.6), with the floor their last removal left
{sn_<network_id>}names         the listing index; entries leave with their leases; one field, which a listing
                               skips, holds the newest revocation sweep's claim
{sc_<client_id>}set            each client's set, ordered by name key for pages (9.5); expires 5 min after
                               the client's last call
```

Hash tags are per group (D-SOCK-7).
