A Find is one group-key script (check `v`, filter or sample, read two loads, increment one) plus a `{svc_}` write per edge ticket; counters are advisory, the listener cap authoritative. `server/cli/sockets` runs on every lb host, since each lb proxies only to its own; 100,000 listeners make about 6,700 registration calls/s. Only the service signs (vault `secret_files`, a yearly rotation with overlap; keys at `GET /socket/keys`). The ticket key file is written by `sidecarctl sockets ticket-keygen -out <file> [-in <file>]` (§19.4): it reads the existing file if `-in` names one, adds a new Ed25519 key that expires RotationInterval (365 days) plus KeyOverlap (1 day) after its creation, drops expired keys, writes the file 0600, refusing to overwrite unless `-in` names the same file, and prints no key; the operator runs it once a year in each environment and places the file in vault, and the block rereads it every minute ([owner decision 354](#od-354), whose 30 days [owner decision 590](#od-590) makes 365: a leaked key could forge tickets for up to a year, but a forged ticket alone admits nothing, since 9.6's steps 3 and 6 still check the session's source and the listener's reading of the config). Every listed key verifies until its expiry, and the newest settled key signs while it outlives `SignMargin`: a key settles `SettleTime` (10 min) after the later of its `created_millis` and the first read in which this process saw it, a per-process map keeping each key's first sight, so however long the hand placement takes it only delays the switch, and no ticket names a key a listener has not been given; a restarted process sees every key as new, so for its first `SettleTime` the oldest live key that outlives `SignMargin` signs, one every listener already holds, and blocks may sign under different keys for up to a reread interval, each of which every listener verifies; the command prints no placement deadline ([owner decision 562](#od-562)). Each process caches each network's newest base and the entries after it from api (§8.9) and acts on what narrows it. On `{X}c_removed` (`server/model/client_close_model.go:64`) every process refuses the client's leases from memory at once and removes them with its pairs; after an entry that can narrow, which every statement kind is but those that only grant or admit, one process a network and position, by a claim in `{sn_}names`, sweeps the network's leases against its state, removes for cause those it refuses, with the pairs of a listener left with no edge entry, and sends `SocketHint`; a §21 suspension is refused from the kill set in memory. A sweep that dies leaves nothing wrong: each lease it did not reach is judged at its listener's next heartbeat and at any Find that picks it, and its pair ends by its TTL (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 13). A process acts on a network's state only while it has no evidence older than 5 s that the authorization log passed it; past that it answers `unavailable` for that network until it has verified the new entries, and with no such evidence its last verified state serves without limit (§8.9; [owner decision 337](#od-337)).

**Service tokens ([owner decision 588](#od-588)).** The `/socket/*` routes take the 15-minute service tokens that evs, gkm and dns take: sockets is an audience of §7.8's exchange, which grants it to an admitted sidecar's client with no scope, and the block verifies a token offline, with no SQL, against the svc- JWKS it mounts as they do (`oauth-jwks-svc.json`), through `sidecarhost`'s Authenticator. The token names its client, the sidecar it acts for in `ur_sidecar_id`, which is the caller's §8 subject, its subject client in `ur_subject_client_id` and, in a team, its `member_id`. A removed client, a revoked sidecar and a removed member are refused through §7.8's signed `rev/` objects, which the block reads for the token's three subjects on the first metadata cluster (`sidecar.RevocationChecker`, cached at most 5 s), and through the removal and projection events above; a token's 15 minutes bound the rest. A token that does not verify, another audience's, an expired one and one a `rev/` object voids answer 401, as does a client token presented in a service token's place; a block with no cluster, or whose `rev/` read fails, answers `unavailable`. A Find still makes no Postgres call, but the exchange does, so sockets stops taking sidecars' new registrations and Finds about 15 minutes into a Postgres outage, as evs and gkm stop new sessions, where the earlier check ran about an hour; each sidecar makes one more exchange every 15 minutes (§19.10). This reverses owner decisions [347](#od-347) and [497](#od-497), under which sockets checked Client-class tokens against a verify-only by_jwt keyring and a Redis revocation record with no Postgres, and what served them: the `sidecar_id` claim `POST /sidecar/bind` re-minted into by_client_jwt (§5.6), the record's member and user fields ([owner decision 561](#od-561)), sock-5's valid-check time, `revocation_record_enabled` as a step of sockets' rollout, and `sidecarctl jwt export-jwks` with its file ([owner decision 578](#od-578)). None of them is built, and neither owner step remains.

**Edge clients' tokens ([owner decision 589](#od-589)).** `urnetwork-edge`'s platform clients, which no sidecar binds and no exchange serves, get theirs from api: `POST /internal/gate/edge-client` (§13.6) answers, beside each client's jwt and only once that jwt's mint has found the client active, a 15-minute service token of audience sockets naming the client, with `network_id` and `ur_client_id` and no sidecar, member or scope, signed under the svc- set as the exchange signs. `server.NewPlatformClientSource` keeps it beside the jwt and renews both, and the edge hosts present it to sockets: tlsedge's and mxedge's router's Finds the first client's, and smtpedge's `ur/smtpedge` registrations each client's own. A removed edge client is refused by its client `rev/` object, which its removal writes, and the route's checks of block, host, slot and index still bound what a stolen edge bearer can mint (§13.6). api's removal finds an edge client by sidecar.yml's `urnetwork_edge`, and while its process has no good read of the file, the file there but unreadable or unparsable with no earlier read to keep, by the device spec `edge`, which the mint sets: one query in the removal's own transaction, run only while that read is marked, owes the `rev/` object for each removed client on an edge device in the client's own network, so I-15 holds whatever the file reads, sockets keeping its own good read through a broken push; a user device that names itself `edge` owes a harmless extra `rev/` object when removed then ([owner decision 641](#od-641)). sockets so takes service tokens alone. Since the mint reads Postgres, an edge's token is not renewed while Postgres is lost: the source holds the last one until it ends, and the edge's Finds and registrations are then refused until api answers again (§19.10).

### 9.9 Client API

```go
// package sidecar, files socket_*.go (§4 places the engine); §18 wraps it for gomobile
type SocketAddress struct {
    NetworkId    *connect.Id // set once resolved
    NetworkLabel string      // "" is the caller's network
    Name         string
}
type SocketListenSettings struct { // defaults as in 9.5
    Protocol   string
    Version    int
    Alpn       []string
    AppMode    string         // tls/: "http" (default) or "raw" (9.5)
    Weight     int
    MaxStreams int
    Exclusive  bool
    Affinity   bool
    Decision   *bridge.Signed // ApprovalDecision for tls/ and smtp/ (§5.4's gate)
}
type SocketDialSettings struct {
    Protocol      string
    MinVersion    int
    Alpn          []string
    AffinityKey   []byte
    AcceptTimeout time.Duration // default 5 s
}
func ParseSocketAddress(text string) (*SocketAddress, error)
// Listen on tls/ and smtp/ calls §5.4's Authorize (I-8), which may return *ApprovalPendingError.
func (self *Sidecar) Listen(ctx context.Context, address string, settings *SocketListenSettings) (*SocketListener, error)
func (self *Sidecar) Dial(ctx context.Context, address string, settings *SocketDialSettings) (*SocketConn, error)
// *SocketListener implements net.Listener (Accept, Close, Addr). Close unlistens at once;
// accepted conns stay open, and a pending Accept returns net.ErrClosed.
func (self *SocketListener) AcceptSocket(ctx context.Context) (*SocketConn, error)
func (self *SocketListener) Drain(ctx context.Context) error // returns at zero in-flight or ctx end (like http.Server.Shutdown), then closes
func (self *SocketListener) SetServing(serving bool)         // e.g. false while the local target refuses
// *SocketConn implements net.Conn; Close sends FIN and stops reading (the peer reads io.EOF).
// Deadlines are local (os.ErrDeadlineExceeded, Timeout() true); the stream survives them.
// RemoteAddr is the dialer's network and client id, Network() "ur"; edge client IPs arrive in-band (§13).
func (self *SocketConn) CloseWrite() error // FIN
func (self *SocketConn) Abort() error      // reset
func (self *SocketConn) Ticket() *SocketTicket
// Errors are *net.OpError{Net: "ur"} wrapping one of these. All but ErrSocketReset are Find's errors too,
// in 9.6's step order; no_listener, busy, quota and unavailable carry retry_after_ms.
var (
    ErrSocketNoListener  error // syscall.ECONNREFUSED
    ErrSocketBusy        error // syscall.ECONNREFUSED
    ErrSocketDenied      error // syscall.EACCES
    ErrSocketReset       error // syscall.ECONNRESET
    ErrSocketUnavailable error
    ErrSocketQuota       error
)
```

CLI (added to cli/UI.md): `ur socket`; `ur socket listen <addr> [<ip>:]<port>` (to a local port; `serving=false` while it refuses; prints `ur approve <id>` for outward names); `ur socket dial <addr> [--listen=[<ip>:]<port>]` (a local forward: 0.0.0.0/:: unless `<ip>` is given, without the TLS-only rule; D-TRUST-8, owner decisions [84](#od-84), [130](#od-130); else stdin/stdout (`ssh -o ProxyCommand`); `ur socket ls [<net>]` (unseals names locally); `ur socket drain <addr>`. `ur bridge public-tls` (cli/UI.md:47) is `listen tls/443/<host>`; §16.5 maps the MCP tools.

**Share (D-SOCK-16).** `ur share add <path> [--count=n] [--expires=d]` hashes the file, writes the record below, listens `exclusive` on `share/<token>` (`<token>`: 16 random bytes, lowercase base32) and prints the link `<net>:share/<token>#<k>`, whose fragment `k` is base64url(the sharer's `sidecar_id` ‖ a 256-bit secret). An omitted `--count` means one use, `--count=n` n, and `--count=0` unlimited uses until the expiry; with `uses` 0 only a Remove or `expire_millis` ends a share, since the end row's Done for each of `uses` Reserves cannot fire. `--expires` defaults to 24 h, and `ur share add` refuses more than 30 days, the longest ordinary grant ([owner decision 74](#od-74)), so every share ends. `ur share get <link> <out>`, which also takes `-` for the link and then reads it from stdin, so that the link's reusable secret stays out of argv, `ps` and shell history ([owner decision 336](#od-336)), dials from a sidecar of the sharer's network, the only one an application name reaches (§6.4), and before OPEN refuses a listener whose verified `sidecar_id` is not `k`'s. `ur share` blocks and lists live shares with their remaining uses and expiry; `ur share rm <token>` ends one early (`--expires` and `rm` added to cli/UI.md). Records survive restarts, but a share is served only while the sharing sidecar runs (the daemon stays up while one is live, §5.8), as the CLI and `ur status` say. Both ends need §8's `listen` and `dial` on `share/`, which the implicit document gives untagged subjects; bytes count toward the network's transfer balance like any same-network stream (§20.6).

```text
record  <state>/net/<network_id>/share/<token>, local file class `share` (§5.9), append-only; each record
        is fsynced before the step it guards (§16's reserve-before-effect ledger, D-MCP-11)
  Share{token, path, size, mtime, sha256, secret, uses (0: unlimited), expire_millis}   at add, after hashing
  Reserve{get_id, use_index, getter_sidecar_id, millis}   Done{get_id, millis}   Remove{millis}
get     getter -> version[1] = 1 ‖ secret[32] ‖ get_id[16] ‖ u64be offset
        (get_id random, kept with <out>.part until a clean close)
        sharer, under the share's mutex, first match:
          the secret differs (constant time), a Remove exists,     reset; no use spent
            or the sharer's clock is at or past expire_millis
          the file's size or mtime differs from Share             status changed
          get_id is reserved by this getter                       resume at offset; spent after its Done
          count(Reserve) < uses, or uses = 0                      append Reserve, fsync: the linearization point
          otherwise                                               status spent
        sharer -> status[1] (0 ok, 1 spent, 2 changed); ok adds u64be size ‖ sha256[32], then bytes [offset, size)
        getter: SHA-256 over [0, size) equals sha256; it renames <out>.part to <out> and sends done[1] = 1,
        and the sharer appends Done
end     a Remove, a Done for each of `uses` Reserves, or expire_millis (by timer, and at start for a sharer
        offline then): reset the share's streams, unlisten and delete the record
```

Served uses never exceed `uses`, counted by Reserves, and no get starts, resumes or keeps streaming at or past `expire_millis`; a crash or a lost stream never frees a Reserve (burn on uncertainty), and only its own getter resumes it.

### 9.10 ACL, quotas, abuse, identity, metrics

- **Gates (X3, D-SOCK-14).** The service checks each registration and Find against the network's newest verified id-only projection (§7.9, §8.9; owner decisions [5](#od-5), [72](#od-72)): `listen` and `dial` rules over subjects and token paths, `tls/` publish and `smtp/` listen grants, grant ids and expiries. Requested grants count once their GrantActivate enters the authorization log (§7.9; [owner decision 74](#od-74)); edge listens need one or a standing grant (I-8). Edge Finds run as `autogroup:public` on `tls/` (§13.5), passing under any publish grant for the host, whatever its audience: the gate reports the audience and judges neither it nor a raw link's pin, which the listener's front does from its own evaluation (§8.10, §13.7; [owner decision 348](#od-348)), so a members visitor without a session reaches §7.8's edge login at the front and a link URL's token is traded for its cookie; they check the receiver's `listen` on `smtp/` (§15.4). For §13.9's system publish `tls/443/mta-sts`, each receiver's own approved `smtp/25/mx` listen grant stands in for the `tls/` listen and publish grants at registration, Find and admission, and its expiry or revocation ends that receiver's publish. Without a policy document, the implicit one gives untagged subjects `dial` and `listen` on every application name, disclosed (owner decisions [105](#od-105), [120](#od-120)). Both ends re-derive the grant (9.6), and revocation resets its streams.
- **Quotas.** `tls_endpoints` (PLAN.md:358) counts active publish grants per (host, port) at activation (§20.7); `ValidateListen` refuses a `tls/` listen without one, except the system publish, which takes no unit (§13.9).
- **Overload protection, no caps** (Q-SOCK-2, [owner decision 66](#od-66)). Established streams and forwards are unlimited; the transfer balance alone limits use. System-protection bounds, equal for every network and tier, keep a byte-free client from pinning Redis or the signing key (D-SOCK-15): a per-process token bucket per calling client over Finds and registration pages of at most 1,024 entries (`sockets_control_qps`, default 50 calls/s, burst 500; 9.5) answers `unavailable` with `retry_after_ms` before any sampling or signing, and Find's spend check (9.6) answers `quota` before signing, the listener's step 5 staying the authoritative stop. No count of names, listeners or streams is capped. Processes serve calls in per-network fair-share order, shedding the heaviest network only when saturated; 9.7 bounds group and dialer costs, and §19 sets per-address lb limits (W2) and per-edge-process Find limits, which replace the bucket for `urnetwork-edge` callers.
- **Hijack.** `listen` grants, `exclusive` and the `ur/` rule prevent group hijack (the SO_REUSEPORT same-UID analog), except under a blanket `listen` grant (9.16).
- **Removal (X10).** Besides 9.8's deletion, connect closes the client's transports (code 4005, `server/CLIENTCLOSE.md` §4), so dialers use backup tickets; a child listener is removed with its parent (9.3) and fails its next call once its parent is otherwise inactive.
- **Metrics** (`urnetwork_sockets_*`): `find_total{result}`, `find_seconds`, `registrations`, `registration_calls_total{result}`, `failure_reports_total{reason}`, `exclusions_total`, `ejections_total`; no network, name, client or IP labels.

### 9.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Service pushes to the listener first (X8) | Early refusal | A non-e2e ControlId push per connection (§6.8) | Rejected |
| Per-listener MAC ticket (contract pattern) | Cheap verify | Server holds the keys; no receipt | Rejected |
| 4-tuple hash (SO_REUSEPORT) | Stateless, sticky | Load-blind; aborts a closing socket's queue without `tcp_migrate_req` ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.10) | Opt-in affinity |
| Presence-only liveness | No heartbeats | Residents outlive disconnects ~5 min (`server/CLIENTCLOSE.md`); no load data | Rejected |
| Edge-delegated ticket keys | Edges survive a sockets outage | Keys on edge hosts; C9 still needs Redis | [Later](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-edge-delegated-ticket-keys) |
| Plaintext application names | Server-side globs | URnetwork reads every internal name | Rejected ([owner decision 67](#od-67)) |
| One HMAC per whole name | Hides depth | No server-side prefix grants | Rejected |
| `ur share` as an evs object sealed under a link-fragment key | Works while the sharer is offline | Changes format 1, which freezes at M2 | Rejected (D-SOCK-16) |

### 9.12 Decisions proposed

**D-SOCK-1 (proposed).** Key sockets on `(network_id, name)`, resolving `<net>` per call. *Why:* names are mutable and reclaimable.

**D-SOCK-2 (proposed).** Use 9.4's namespaces and host forms, refusing deeper names. *Why:* one rule for §13-§15; a wildcard covers one label, and [owner decision 40](#od-40)'s scopes add one.

**D-SOCK-3 (proposed).** Registrations are 45 s leases renewed every 15 s by the full set, in pages of at most 1,024 entries (9.5), carrying load. *Why:* one idempotent path; Redis loss heals in one interval.

**D-SOCK-4 (proposed).** Find returns single-use 30 s Ed25519 tickets (primary, backup) carrying the grant expiry; the service never contacts listeners. *Why:* push stays off the connection path; tickets are reach evidence.

**D-SOCK-5 (proposed).** Schedule by weighted P2C on `(est + 1) / weight` with listener caps, opt-in affinity, a per-dialer clamp on each dialer's share of `est`, which never refuses or delays a ticket, and 64-listener samples. *Why:* load-aware, stale-tolerant and bounded; a clamp that stopped issuance would hold a lone short-connection dialer to c tickets per report, about 25 per 15 s on a 256-stream listener, since short connections never move in-flight enough for an eager report (meta review CC-06).

**D-SOCK-6 (proposed).** Dial with a 5 s accept timeout, the backup ticket, then ≤3 Finds carrying failed tickets; ejection needs reporters from 2 networks. *Why:* bounded latency; a lying reporter harms only itself.

**D-SOCK-7 (proposed).** Keep state in Redis Cluster with per-group hash tags and field TTLs. *Why:* warp has no key routing; per-network tags create hot nodes.

**D-SOCK-8 (proposed).** Adopt 9.9's `net.Listener`/`net.Conn` API with syscall-compatible errors. *Why:* existing Go code and retry logic work unchanged.

**D-SOCK-9 (proposed).** Delete registrations on `{X}c_removed`; keep no per-dial record beyond §2.8's sock-2 fields (≤300 s) and sock-3 pairs, a `tls/` or `smtp/` pair at most 15 min past its listener's last accepted registration and a `ur/` pair its service's grant length ([owner decision 338](#od-338)). *Why:* reuses the removal signal; minimal metadata.

**D-SOCK-10 (proposed).** Host the engine as `server/cli/sockets`, its routes authorized by a 15-minute service token of audience `sockets` (§7.8, 9.8; [owner decision 588](#od-588), which reverses the Postgres-free check of Client-class tokens that owner decisions [347](#od-347) and [497](#od-497) gave them). *Why:* registration load stays off `api`, and sockets authenticates as evs, gkm and dns do.

**D-SOCK-11 (proposed).** Platform services listen as `ur/<service>` in `urnetwork-edge`, authorized by the service. *Why:* sidecars reach smtpedge through the same Find and Service path.

**D-SOCK-12 (proposed).** Edge tickets bind one of the caller's K clients, and edge Finds write the `{svc_}` pair authorizing C9 until the grant ends, a `tls/` or `smtp/` pair living at most 15 min past its listener's last accepted registration ([owner decision 338](#od-338)); source equality holds for edge tickets too, and only the Hello check is waived (9.6). *Why:* step 3 stays exact; contracts outlive the ticket, not the grant.

**D-SOCK-13 (proposed).** Send names outside `tls/`, `smtp/` and `ur/` only as 9.4's HMAC token paths, sealed for listings, under the config repo's `K_sock`, rotated on §11.6's triggers. *Why:* [owner decision 67](#od-67), built like evs paths ([owner decision 2](#od-2)); prefix grants still work.

**D-SOCK-14 (proposed).** Gate registrations and Finds on the signed id-only projection (§7.9, §8); listener and dialer each re-derive the grant from the config repo. *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [6](#od-6) and [72](#od-72): a breached server can only deny or delay, within §2.8's exposure bound.

**D-SOCK-15 (proposed).** System protection bounds registration and Find work, never the number of names or established use: a per-client token bucket charges each Find and each registration page of at most 1,024 entries, larger sets going as pages (9.5), and a spend check precedes signing (9.6, 9.10). *Why:* [owner decision 66](#od-66) allows system-protection bounds but no count caps; an authenticated byte-free client otherwise pins Redis and the signing key.

**D-SOCK-16 (proposed).** `ur share` is a live sharer: a blinded `share/<token>` socket, a fragment-borne 256-bit secret, a durable use count and an expiry (24 h by default, at most 30 days), on the transfer balance, available while the sharing sidecar runs (9.9). *Why:* R-CTX-31; no link outlives its expiry, even with unlimited uses; an evs object under a link key would change format 1, which freezes at M2.

### 9.13 Open questions

**Q-SOCK-1.** Is load-aware weighted P2C, with opt-in affinity, an acceptable reading of PLAN.md:69's "similar to socket reuse on linux"? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 65](#od-65)):** yes, as 9.7 designs, with drain and retry. *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-2.** Do abuse caps contradict "IP and port forward [unlimited]" (PLAN.md:359)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 66](#od-66)):** yes, so none apply; the transfer balance alone limits use, and 9.10 keeps overload protection. *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-3.** Which relationship carries cross-network streams (X11, §20)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** Q-PROTO-3 (b), accepted with [owner decision 11](#od-11): Service (C9) for edges, authorized by 9.6's pair; shares ride §17's IP path as FriendsAndFamily ([owner decision 86](#od-86)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-SOCK-4.** Should application names be blinded from the server? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 67](#od-67)):** yes, as 9.4's token paths under the config repo's `K_sock` (D-SOCK-13); public edge names stay plaintext, and clients resolve names locally. *Residual:* none.

### 9.14 Departures from PLAN.md

- The scheduler is load-aware, not a 4-tuple hash (Q-SOCK-1, [owner decision 65](#od-65)).
- Internal names reach the server blinded (Q-SOCK-4, [owner decision 67](#od-67)).
- PLAN.md:74: other networks reach a listener by IP through a §17 share, not a §9 dial (§8.16; Q-BRIDGE-6, [owner decision 86](#od-86)).
- PLAN.md:82's tls edge "opens a client on a network": edges are `urnetwork-edge` platform clients in Service mode (§13.14, Q-TLS-5; owner decisions [11](#od-11), [59](#od-59)).

### 9.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the grammar, namespaces and token paths; registry, scheduler, tickets, admission; the control-plane bounds; `{svc_}` pairs; hooks; `SocketHint`; the Go API, `ur socket` and `ur share`.
- **Consumes:** §6 streams, `StreamRejectCode`, `Signed`, the Hello check, topic `sock`, Required mode; §4 C9; §5 identity keys, `Authorize`, local file classes; §7.9's authorization log and projection (§8's rows and audiences, statements, revocations); the config repo's `K_sock` and policy; §12 resolution; §13-§15 edge dialers, hooks; §16's reserve-before-effect ledger (D-MCP-11); §19, §20 limits and `OverLimit`; §21 suspensions.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `SocketHint` (0x1001, ControlId→client, topic `sock`; revocation, forced drain); `SignedSocketTicket` in `StreamOpen.ticket`; `StreamRejectCode` `retry|busy|denied|invalid|quota` (1-5; 0 unspecified) in `StreamReject.code`; on `share/` streams, 9.9's fixed-width share header.
- **API routes** (Client class, authorized by a service token with aud `sockets`, 9.8; [owner decision 588](#od-588)): `POST /socket/registrations` (Client; 9.5, pages of ≤1,024 entries; statuses, `server_time`, keys); `POST /socket/find` (Client; 9.6, errors 9.9; platform callers add K client ids); `GET /socket/list` (Client, same network; token paths, edge and sealed names); `GET /socket/keys` (Public).
- **Tables:** none (9.8's Redis keys, behind `SocketStore`).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/sockets`; vault ticket keys; the svc- JWKS and the first metadata cluster's `rev/` objects, read only (9.8); pro.yml `tls_endpoints`; `sockets_control_qps` and `urnetwork_edge` (the `urnetwork-edge` network id) in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` (§6.10.1, §19.11).
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §4.5's engine stores include `SocketStore`, with field TTLs and an atomic pick-and-increment.
  - §7.9's projection lists Team scopes (9.4); §11.6's REMOVE generations are the key-holder changes 9.4 classes, authorization expiries among them, though §11.6 batches every path epoch.
  - §13.7 dispatches on `AppMode` (D-TLS-13) and defines a raw endpoint's `link` check; §20.7's `OverLimit` lists spent networks within 5 s.
  - §22.5's §9 row tests 9.5's pages, 9.4's vectors, 9.9's share and 9.7's clamp ([owner decision 551](#od-551)).

### 9.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A dead listener costs 5 s until skipped | Medium | Medium | Backup ticket; exclusion; 45 s lease |
| A leaked signing key forges tickets until rotation | Low | High | Vault; rotation; both ends' checks refuse unauthorized streams |
| Reconnect storms, uncapped groups or byte-free clients load the service | Medium | Medium | Jitter; `retry_after_ms`; sampling; the per-client bucket and pre-sign spend check (D-SOCK-15); fair queuing; shedding |
| The bucket delays a legitimate client making over 50 calls a second: opening that many streams, or renewing over about 768,000 names (750 pages per 15 s) | Low | Low | Burst 500; `retry_after_ms`; 45 s leases outlast a late page; `find_total` and `registration_calls_total{result}` show it; sidecar.yml tunes the bound |
| Edge names are public; token paths show structure; a dropped or expired reader, with server help, tests guessed names until `K_sock` rotates | High | Low | §2.8 rows; rotation and its alarm (9.4) |
| A blanket `listen` grant (§8.5's grant 1) lets any member's untagged device join an application group and take dials | Medium | Medium | `exclusive`; narrower `listen` rules |
| A sockets or Redis outage fails Finds (`unavailable`) and new edge connections; streams stay up | Low | High | Every lb host; failover; §19.10; SLO burn pages the out-of-hours rota ([owner decision 143](#od-143)) |
| Dialers inflate `est` or report falsely | Medium | Medium | 9.7's per-dialer share cap and decay; step 1 filters on the listener's own report, so `est` never refuses; two-network ejection, for `ur/` names |
| One dialer's burst of short connections reaches one listener past its real load until the listener's next report, since that dialer's tickets count at most c in `est` | Medium | Low | The listener's `max_streams` admission and the backup ticket; eager reports at most every 2 s (9.5, 9.7) |
| A leaked share link lets any sidecar of the network redeem its remaining uses until it expires | Medium | Medium | `--count` (one use when omitted; with `--count=0` only `ur share rm` or the expiry ends it); `--expires` (24 h default); `ur share rm`; each Reserve names the getter; `ur share get -` reads the link from stdin |

### 9.17 Phasing

- **v0 (§23 M5):** the `sockets` service with 9.10's bounds; blinded application names; `tls/` with §13, `AppMode` included; tickets, P2C and 9.7's per-dialer clamp on `est`; `SocketHint`; the Go API; `ur socket` and `ur share`; MCP tools. Blocked by §6 streams, §5 identity, the config repo and projection (X3, M2) and §4's C9.
- **v0, mail track:** `smtp/` with §15 (M7); `ur/` once §14 passes D-SMTP-16's gate, DATA mode included (M9; owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125)).
- **v1 (M6):** affinity, with §13; Team scope hosts (owner decisions [40](#od-40), [55](#od-55), [58](#od-58)), the `smtp/` ones with §15.
- **Later:** [region-aware selection](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-region-aware-selection) (one lb site today, [R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §5 R8), [slow start](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-slow-start), [edge-delegated ticket keys](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-edge-delegated-ticket-keys), [registration over push](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-registration-over-push).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#sock-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).

## 10. Group keys for evs: MLS and the GKM service

### 10.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns X12: the in-house MLS subset, ciphersuite, credentials and groups; GKM, stateless over metadata-cluster objects (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [145](#od-145)); the key hierarchy, generations, key holders and their wraps, the write-gate predicate, membership flows and committers, revocation, erasure, recovery, re-seeding, key domains and sizes. §5 owns the identity key and recovery code, §6 push and `HeadCheck`, §7.9 the config repo, the authorization log and the `leaves` rule of the config and team directory groups, §16.11 the directory, §8 readers and consent, §11 the object format, placement and the gate's enforcement, and §19 the file cluster.

### 10.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-KEYS-1 | MLS (RFC 9420) secures evs from v0 | PLAN.md:44; [owner decision 1](#od-1) |
| R-KEYS-2 | One directory = one git repo, under "one session key stored in GKM" | PLAN.md:53 |
| R-KEYS-3 | Lazy rewrap: a client that detects a needed rewrap sends a checkpoint | PLAN.md:47-50, :338 |
| R-KEYS-4 | Forward-only revocation: a removed or expired holder reads nothing new | PLAN.md:149, :167-168; I-15 |
| R-KEYS-5 | One accepted Commit per epoch | PLAN.md:157-161; RFC 9420 §14 |
| R-KEYS-6 | No server holds a group secret, epoch key or file key; gkm sees ciphertext and 10.6's headers | CONVENTIONS §0; PLAN.md:221; I-1; [owner decision 115](#od-115) |
| R-KEYS-7 | MLS built in house in the sidecar repo, pure Go, no cgo | owner rule 1; [owner decision 43](#od-43); sdk/js/Makefile:69 |
| R-KEYS-8 | A breached server yields only ciphertext and listed metadata and adds no reader | P5:745 |
| R-KEYS-9 | Two key domains: sessions for their author, others reading only by consent or as the audit reader; actions and approvals for admins | P5:579, :640; MK2:482-486; [owner decision 126](#od-126) |
| R-KEYS-10 | Per-entry keys for records from the first release | REC:217-223; [owner decision 61](#od-61) |
| R-KEYS-11 | MLS membership follows the signed readers, which clients verify; agents, and config and team directory readers past a network's first 1,000 member devices, hold wraps, so no member-device cap applies | owner decisions [3](#od-3), [6](#od-6), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182); §8.12 |
| R-KEYS-12 | Ciphertext resists harvest-now-decrypt-later by a passive adversary | [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.5, §2.12; [owner decision 44](#od-44) |
| R-KEYS-13 | Signed grants, admissions and revocations decide membership, waiting for no admin; members update their own leaves | owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8), [113](#od-113), [128](#od-128) |
| R-KEYS-14 | gkm's durable state is objects on its repo's metadata cluster, never Postgres or Redis, written within §11.13's NVMe write budget; acks are Redis soft state | owner decisions [2](#od-2), [136](#od-136), [140](#od-140), [145](#od-145) |

### 10.3 What exists today

- **GKM** appears only at PLAN.md:53; no repo has code for it [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md).
- **Go 1.27.4** (connect/go.mod:3). `crypto/hpke` implements X-Wing as `MLKEM768X25519()`, KEM 0x647a, from draft-ietf-hpke-pq (GOROOT/src/crypto/hpke/pq.go:21, :39-41); `crypto/mldsa` arrived in Go 1.27 (GOROOT/api/go1.27.txt:4).
- **Constraints.** The browser build is `CGO_ENABLED=0` (sdk/js/Makefile:69). server's `BlobStore` has `PutIfAbsent` but no Delete, If-Match or ranged read (server/blob.go:160-192); `ServiceHost.Blobs` adds them, per metadata cluster (§4.5, §19).
- **Test material** (2026-11-03). The mlswg's 16 vector files carry only RFC 9420's classical suites (https://github.com/mlswg/mls-implementations/tree/main/test-vectors). MIT differential peers: thomas-vilte/mls-go v1.6.0 (0x0001-0x0003; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.4); tmc/mls, whose provisional 0x004F has exactly 0x0010's algorithms (wire.go:33-50); OpenMLS, whose unregistered 0x004D pairs X-Wing with ChaCha20-Poly1305 (https://cryspen.com/post/pq-openmls/).

### 10.4 Implementation, ciphersuite, credentials

**MLS is Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)).** v0 distributes every group key RK_g through 10.5's `KeyDelivery` wraps alone: a join is a LATE delivery, a removal is the REMOVE rotation, which wraps to every remaining holder, and a resync fetches deliveries, so gkm keeps no epochs, Welcomes, KeyPackages, GroupInfo or acks and `gkm:<group_id>` is versioned by generation alone; the generation, the ladder, ReaderKeys and their bounds, DelegationWraps, RecoveryWraps, drop keys and 10.6's gate are unchanged. This subsection, and what 10.5 to 10.9 say of epochs, leaves, commits, KeyPackages, Welcomes and GroupInfo, is the design [MLS](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-mls) returns with: the drafted MLS code stays on the branch, dark, with [owner decision 99](#od-99)'s deferred audit, and the review phase reworks KF1-KF7 onto deliveries. Lost: TreeKEM's post-compromise healing of the key-encryption keys; a copied keychain heals by 10.5's bounds instead, a reader at its ReaderKey's not_after plus the next generation. Each rotation costs about 1.37 KB a holder, about 1.37 MB and 1,000 objects at 1,000 holders; no phone holds a 1,000-leaf tree, an agent's repo is keyed with no member device forming a group, and recovery above 16 leaves needs no leaf online.

**Subset (D-KEYS-12).** Only what evs uses; anything else is refused when parsed.

| RFC 9420 feature | v0 |
|---|---|
| Tree math; codec, mls10 only (§6, App. C) | yes |
| Labeled crypto, key schedule, exporter (§5, §8) | yes |
| Secret tree, PrivateMessage, transcript hashes (§6.3, §8.2, §9) | handshakes only |
| TreeKEM, parent and tree hashes, validation (§7) | yes |
| Add, Remove, GroupContextExtensions, inline (§12.1); path-only commits for self-update (§12.4) | yes |
| Welcome, `ratchet_tree`, ExternalInit (§12.4.3) | external commits only to resync or recover |
| KeyPackages, last resort; credential 0xF552 (§10, §16.8, §17.5) | yes |
| PSK, ReInit, branching, application messages, external senders, standalone and Update proposals | refused |

**Conformance.** No vectors exist for 0x0010, so every mlswg vector file covering a v0 feature runs under 0x0001, from the 16 files committed in testdata/mls/mlswg/, whose repository carries no license (§4.4; [owner decision 263](#od-263)); 0x0010 adds X-Wing known-answer tests (KATs) and [owner decision 43](#od-43)'s differential runs: mls-go under 0x0001, tmc/mls patched to 0x0010, and OpenMLS's 0x004D once an M0 KAT matches its X-Wing to Go's. The patch is literal: mlsinterop/ builds tmc/mls at v0.0.0-20260930074835-1c42a372504a with one build overlay changing its provisional 0x004F, wire.go:39's constant, to 0x0010, which no other tmc/mls suite uses, so both stacks sign and hash one number; the artifact records the patch, and that tmc/mls cites the suite's draft -06 where this section cites -07. **The 0x0010 gate (D-KEYS-10)** adds what those cannot show:

```text
specified  the MLS wire (credential 0xF552, GkmCommitHeader, GenRotate, ur_group), the delivery wire
           (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery under its ReaderWrap and DelegationWrap types, 10.6's wrap and recovery
           paths) and suite 0x0010, at M2's entry review; no field is removed after it
frozen     at M2's exit review (D-PHASE-7), on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact:
  kem      X-Wing KATs from the draft's vectors pass for Go's crypto/hpke MLKEM768X25519(), DeriveKeyPair
           included, the only independent X-Wing evidence; tmc/mls's encapsulation and decapsulation equal
           Go's on fixed seeds, a check of wiring, not of X-Wing, since tmc/mls runs that same code
           (owner decision 359)
  stacks   one scripted lifecycle in both directions between mls_* and tmc/mls (patched to 0x0010, above): at
           least 10 epochs with a Welcome, path commits, a Remove, an external commit with ExternalInit and a
           PrivateMessage decrypted per epoch, both sides computing equal epoch_authenticator and "UR evs 1.0
           kek" exporter outputs
  ladder   GenWrap's, LeafWrap's and GenLink's AAD and KeyDelivery's wrap_aad (10.5), reproduced by
           mlsinterop/'s own code
  gaps     no stacks step may be a gap: one tmc/mls lacks holds the freeze unless a second peer runs it in
           both directions (OpenMLS's 0x004D, once its M0 KAT matches); mlswg vectors under 0x0001 count toward
           no part of it
```

**Ciphersuite ([owner decision 44](#od-44); D-KEYS-12).** 0x0010, MLS_128_MLKEM768X25519_AES128GCM_SHA256_Ed25519, in groups and credentials from v0 (draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-07, Publication Requested 2026-11-01; [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.1). Each MLS AEAD key is used once, so wasm's table-based AES (GOROOT/src/crypto/internal/fips140/aes/aes_generic.go:58-74) is no practical timing target.

**Framing (D-KEYS-3).** Member commits are PrivateMessage (RFC 9420 §6.3), whose clear header shows group_id, epoch and content type; only external commits (resync, recovery self-join) are PublicMessage, as RFC 9420 §6 requires for non-members. `authenticated_data`, clear but bound into the AEAD and signature, adds only what the gate needs and no roster delta ([owner decision 59](#od-59)):

```proto
message GkmCommitHeader {   // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto, in authenticated_data of every commit
  uint64  generation = 1;   // the generation of this epoch's GenWrap: the newest gen/ the committer holds;
                            //   0 only for a recovery self-join that carries no GenWrap (10.6's epoch PUT, 10.8)
  AuthPin auth = 2;         // the state (§7.9) the new roster was checked against
}
```

**Leaves and readers (D-KEYS-2, D-KEYS-23).** Member devices that read a repo are its group's leaves, at most 1,000 (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60)); in a data repo, those past the 1,000 seats wait keyless (§8.12). Agents read by 10.5's wraps, outside that cap ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). Readers are §8's `RepoReaders`, which every device evaluates ([owner decision 6](#od-6)) and the projection carries as ids. In the config group, which every admitted sidecar reads, §7.9's `leaves` rule alone ranks member devices, whose admissions carry no not_after, and moves them between leaf and wrap, as a function of the log ([owner decision 144](#od-144)); the team directory's group, its own MLS group ([owner decision 60](#od-60)), which every admitted sidecar of a team network reads (§16.11), follows the same rule: the first 1,000 live member devices are its leaves, and a rotation costs ~1.3 KB a wrap per overflow device ([owner decision 182](#od-182)). In both, the rest, and an entitled device not yet added, read by ReaderWraps (wrapped) and stay leaves of their data repos. §10 adds:

```text
adds      in both groups members accept an Add or external join only of a leaf-entitled device (§7.9); one
          without a KeyPackage reads by ReaderWrap until it uploads one, and no other device takes its place
wrapped   a wrapped member device commits no Add or Remove in them, only first wraps and rotations (10.9)
```

**Credential.** Private-use type `ur_sidecar = 0xF552` (RFC 9420 §17.5), required through `required_capabilities`; KeyPackages are public, so it names no member, tag or client:

```proto
message UrMlsCredential {                         // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto
  bytes sidecar_id = 1;                           // durable leaf identity (§5)
  bytes identity_public_key = 2; string identity_alg = 3;  // §5; ed25519 in v0
  bytes mls_signature_public_key = 4;             // rotated by self-update
  uint32 cipher_suite = 5; int64 not_after = 6;   // 0x0010 (owner decision 44); not_after: ms since the
                                                  // epoch, the signing time plus 90 days, KeyPackages'
                                                  // life; every UpdatePath leaf and external join
                                                  // re-signs it, so the tree carries each leaf's last
                                                  // change (10.9's Remove row)
  bytes admission_sha256 = 7;                     // its §7.9 SidecarAdmit's statement id (§7.9's ids), from
                                                  // Signed.body or AuthorityProposal.statement; for the
                                                  // first device SHA-256(Signed Genesis)
  bytes identity_signature = 8;                   // §6 signing, purpose mls-credential, fields 1-7:
                                                  // over "urnetwork-sidecar-v1/mls-credential" || 0x00 ||
                                                  // u32be(0x1306, SIGNED_UR_MLS_CREDENTIAL) || the
                                                  // credential's received bytes before field 8's tag
}
// A credential encodes fields 1 to 7 in ascending order with no unknown field, then field 8 last with nothing
// after it, or it is refused; a verifier checks that prefix, never a re-marshal.
```

- **Admission (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [127](#od-127)).** Members accept a credential only if an unrevoked, unparked `SidecarAdmit`, verified through the authorization log back to the genesis and signed as §7.9 allows (one admin, the member's own device unless `self_admit` is off, or k of n for AdminSet members), names its sidecar_id and identity key. Only a network's first device is trusted on first use, against its safety number (§2.8 EX5). Clients pin that key, refuse a second and share pins through §6's `Hello` (D-PROTO-13). After a `SidecarRevoke`, GKM deletes the sidecar's KeyPackages.
- **Self-updates and forks.** A leaf that commits no path for 7 days (30 in groups above 50 leaves) commits a path-only commit (D-KEYS-14). Clients pin each push's sealed (group_id, epoch, epoch_authenticator) (§11.6) and each generation's C_g, refuse a lower or conflicting pin with an alarm and compare pins by §6's `HeadCheck`, whose generation heads serve holders that are not leaves (I-16, D-PROTO-14, D-TRUST-10; [owner decision 129](#od-129)).
- **Last resort ([owner decision 361](#od-361)).** A last-resort KeyPackage carries draft-ietf-mls-extensions' `last_resort` extension, type 0x000A with empty extension_data, in its own extensions only, and every leaf lists 0x000A and 0xF553 in its capabilities; a device that joined through it commits a path-only self-update at its first opportunity and replaces it at its next upkeep pass. D-KEYS-12's suite migration moves the number if the draft's does.

### 10.5 The key hierarchy: what "one session key stored in GKM" means

The MLS exporter changes every epoch, is not forward-secure (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11 §4.4), and gives a new member nothing earlier, so the evs keys sit above MLS. In v0 no epoch exists (10.4; [owner decision 610](#od-610)): no KEK_e, GenWrap_e, LeafWrap or GroupInfo_e is written, GenRotate's `leaf_wrap` stays in the format unset, and every holder of a generation, member devices among them, takes RK_g by a `KeyDelivery`, STAGED to each holder at its rotation or LATE when it joins, the rows below that name leaves and epochs being MLS's, Later:

```text
MLS epoch e --MLS-Exporter("UR evs 1.0 kek", repo_id, 32)--> KEK_e (key-encryption key)
RK_g: repo key generation g, 32 random bytes = PLAN's "session key"; cause_g ∈ {remove, request, schedule};
      gen/1 carries cause REQUEST, and a reader refuses REMOVE there (owner decision 360)
C_g = SHA-256("UR evs 1.0 commit" || repo_id || u64be(g) || RK_g)                 the generation's commitment
GKM stores only:
  GenRotate_g = the Signed record in gen/<g> (below): C_g, parent C_{g-1}, cause, auth pin, time, holders
                hash, the wrap count, GenLink_g, an optional LeafWrap, the drop key and its expiry
  GenLink_g   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_link_g, RK_{g-1}; aad repo_id||u64be(g)||u8(cause_g), 25 B)   the ladder
  GenWrap_e   = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||u64be(e)||u64be(g), 32 B)    in epoch object e,
                g its newest
  LeafWrap    = XChaCha20-Poly1305(KEK_e, RK_g; aad group_id||u64be(e)||u64be(g), 32 B)    in GenRotate_g,
                for every leaf of e
  GroupInfo_e = XChaCha20-Poly1305(K_groupinfo, GroupInfo incl. ratchet_tree; aad group_id||u64be(e), 24 B)
                inside each epoch object at <= 16 leaves; on demand above (10.6); these widths are as built,
                and testdata/gkm/ladder.json pins the bytes (owner decision 360)
  RecoveryWrap_{m,g}   = HPKE-XWing(recovery_pub_m, RK_g), unsigned, bare enc || ct, 1,168 B (a 1,120 B enc,
                         the 32 B RK_g, a 16 B tag), info "UR evs 1.0 recovery", aad member_id || group_id ||
                         u64be(g) || C_g || SHA-256(the binding's Ed25519 key)[0:8], the bytes b8 spells (10.8)
  ReaderWrap_{g,s,k}   = §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, a KeyDelivery (below): {group_id, g, C_g, s, k,
                         staged or late, a late one's auth pin and time, HPKE-XWing(ReaderKey_{s,k}, RK_g)}
  DelegationWrap_{g,d} = the same to the reader key of d, which d fixes, d = delegation_id = the Signed
                         Delegation's statement id, the SHA-256 of its signed bytes (§7.9's ids); k = SHA-256
                         of the X-Wing public key sealed to, its incarnation
HPKE-XWing = HPKE base mode with KEM 0x647a (X-Wing), KDF HKDF-SHA256 (0x0001) and AEAD AES-128-GCM (0x0001),
             by crypto/hpke's NewSender and Sender.Seal, since hpke.Seal takes no AAD, for ReaderWraps,
             DelegationWraps, RecoveryWraps and deposit slots, a slot's info "UR evs 1.0 deposit" and its aad
             repo_id || u64be(g) || slot_id (§11.12)
RK_g --HKDF-SHA256(salt repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 "||purpose||u64be(g) [||group_id||u64be(e)])-->
     link|fek|manifest|path|ref|drop|groupinfo|index|statement (the last: §7.9's sealed bodies)
ReaderKey_{s,k} = §6 Signed, purpose reader-key, {sidecar_id, xwing_public_key, not_after}, numbered 1 to 3 in
              that order, not_after an int64 of ms since the epoch, at most 7 days after signing; every reader
              holds one, a fresh X-Wing pair once it is 6 days old, k its incarnation (readerkey, below)
ur_group    = GroupContext extension 0xF553 (RFC 9420 §17.3's private use), listed in required_capabilities and
              fixed at creation, in TLS presentation (RFC 9420 §2.1.2): struct { opaque network_id<V>; opaque
              repo_id<V>; uint8 kind; opaque owner_member_id<V>; }; kind is acl.proto's RepoKind, one of
              §11.12's kinds, general 1 to secret 9, directory among them from M2's reservation (owner
              decision 171); owner_member_id is empty for a repo that is not owner-bound
```

- **PLAN.md:53, precisely.** One current key, RK_g, encrypts every new object, and GKM stores it only wrapped (I-1). It rotates when a key holder drops or its authorization expires (`remove`), on `ur keys rotate` (`request`) and after 30 days (`schedule`); Adds and self-updates keep it, so in-flight writes stay valid.
- **Ladder.** RK_g opens every earlier generation, so a joiner gets the whole history; to withhold history, use a new repo (§11). A removed reader gets no later KEK, RK or wrap, but keeps every generation it held and opens files untouched since its removal until they are rewritten or `ur evs rekey` re-checkpoints them. MLS updates heal the tree and its KEKs, but a copied keychain derives every KEK until the device's own next path commit (10.4) and opens every delivery to a ReaderKey it holds, to which a rotator or deliverer seals only before that key's not_after, at most 7 days after its signing, whatever advertisement gkm serves (readerkey, below); so content heals only at the first generation sealed after both. A passive copy (the keychain's bytes, used only to open what the operator serves, a stale advertisement included) therefore reads, while the device runs, what is sealed up to about 37 days after the copy, 60 above 50 leaves (the path commit within 7 days, 30 above 50 leaves, the newest copied ReaderKey's not_after within 7, then up to 30 days to the next generation), and every earlier generation through the ladder; while the device does not run, its copied leaf derives each later epoch's KEK until it commits again or a stale Remove (10.9) removes it, and a copy of a wrapped reader's keychain heals at that not_after whether or not the device runs. An active clone, one that uses the copy's identity key or ClientKey, signs fresh ReaderKeys and KeyPackages and commits as the device, so no path commit or key replacement ends it: only a `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}` from a since_n at or before the copy, whose cascade parks what the clone admitted (§7.9), and the device's enrollment anew, since `--replace` keeps its identity key (§5.5), as for a compromised backup (10.8). A Delegation's reader key in it reads as the Residual below says. X-Wing protects ciphertext against harvest-now-decrypt-later by a passive adversary ([owner decision 44](#od-44)); signatures are Ed25519, so an adversary that can forge them (a future quantum computer, say) and that the operator serves could forge admissions, or a holder's ReaderKey, to which an honest rotator or hinted holder then seals RK_g with no person acting, and, through the ladder, read all retained history; a device's daily check of the ReaderKey gkm serves under its id (readerkey, below) shows such a key only after deliveries to it, and only where the operator does not hide it from the device ([owner decision 358](#od-358)). An external commit needs RK_g, under which the GroupInfo is sealed, so a published identity key alone commits nothing; RK_g itself rests on those signatures.
- **Authentication.** The key schedule and every GroupInfo signature bind `ur_group`; clients accept RK_g only if it matches `gen/<g>`'s signed C_g; the newer, verified generation authenticates each GenLink, whose AAD covers the cause §11's rewrap rule reads; a missing key is refused, never defaulted (ePrint 2024/546).

**Generations (D-KEYS-15).** Every evs head carries the generation pin {group_id, g, C_g}, C_g as the block above defines it (§11.8). `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match, is the only place a generation is created, which a gen pack later holds verbatim (10.16): MLS commits change the tree and give joiners the newest generation's key in GenWrap_e, and the rotation a Remove requires is a separate gen/ claim, by any writer.

```proto
message GenRotate {              // sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto; §6 Signed, purpose gen-rotate, by the rotator's identity key
  bytes   group_id = 1; bytes repo_id = 2;
  uint64  generation = 3;        // g; generation 1 is written with epoch 0 (KF1) and has no parent
  bytes   parent_commitment = 4; // C_{g-1}
  bytes   commitment = 5;        // C_g
  uint32  cause = 6;             // 1 REMOVE, 2 REQUEST, 3 SCHEDULE; REMOVE iff it covers a shrink, an
                                 //   authorization expiry or a compromise retirement since the parent (10.9)
  AuthPin auth = 7;              // the state KeyHolders was computed at (§7.9); never below the previous
                                 //   base or the parent's auth
  int64   time_ms = 8;           // the evaluation time for expiries; within 10 min of gkm's clock
  bytes   holders_sha256 = 9;    // SHA-256 over the sorted KeyHolders(R, auth, time) identities (below)
  uint32  wrap_count = 10;       // staged wraps and recovery wraps, for completeness checks
  bytes   genlink = 11;          // GenLink_g
  LeafWrap leaf_wrap = 12;       // optional: one wrap for every leaf of that epoch, 72 B
  bytes   drop_public_key = 13;  // only for kinds that take deposits (D-KEYS-17)
  int64   drop_not_after_ms = 14;  // time_ms + GkmSettings.DropKeyLifetime, 90 days (owner decision 357);
                                 //   members refuse one past time_ms + DropKeyLifetime + 10 min (10.9)
}
message LeafWrap { uint64 epoch = 1; bytes ciphertext = 2; }  // RK_g under KEK_epoch,
                                                              //   aad group_id||u64be(epoch)||u64be(g)
message KeyDelivery {              // the body of a ReaderWrap or DelegationWrap, gkm's wrap/ object (10.6)
  bytes   group_id = 1;
  uint64  generation = 2;          // g
  bytes   commitment = 3;          // C_g, all 32 bytes
  bytes   recipient = 4;           // sidecar_id; a DelegationWrap's, the delegation_id
  bytes   recipient_key_sha256 = 5;  // SHA-256 of the X-Wing public key sealed to: a ReaderKey's, which a
                                     //   replacement changes, or the Delegation's reader_xwing_public_key
  uint32  delivery_kind = 6;       // 1 STAGED: by gen/<g>'s rotator before its claim; 2 LATE: after it (10.9)
  AuthPin auth = 7;                // LATE only: the signer's newest verified state when it signs
  int64   time_ms = 8;             // LATE only: the signer's clock or, if later, gen/<g>'s time_ms; within 10 min of gkm's
  bytes   ciphertext = 9;          // HPKE-XWing(that key, RK_g), info "UR evs 1.0 wrap", aad wrap_aad
}
message ReaderWrap { KeyDelivery wrap = 1; }      // §6 Signed, purpose reader-wrap, by the signer's identity key
message DelegationWrap { KeyDelivery wrap = 1; }  // the same, to a Delegation's reader key
// wrap_aad = u8(1 ReaderWrap | 2 DelegationWrap) || group_id || u64be(g) || C_g || SHA-256(recipient)
//            || recipient_key_sha256 || u8(delivery_kind), then, LATE only, u64be(auth.version) || auth.chain
//            || i64be(time_ms)
```

```text
Rotate: one algorithm for every cause and every rotator
1  S = my newest verified state (n, A_n); t = now; H = KeyHolders(R, S, t); require me in H or covered by a
   Delegation in H, and me ∈ writers(R, S) or, in the config group, me = the signer of an admission or
   revocation this rotation answers (owner decision 128) or, after api's reap of an uncovered ephemeral
   agent, of its admission (§7.10)
2  g = the newest generation (GET gen/<g+1> answers 404); RK' = 32 random bytes; persist RK' and the
   GenRotate draft in my keychain; a stored draft is reused only while its time_ms is within
   RotateDraftMaxAge (5 min, under 10.6's 10 min of claim skew) of now and its group_id is my pinned
   group, else dropped and drawn afresh, as one whose delivery set changed is (owner decision 666)
3  stage deliveries for g+1, each a STAGED KeyDelivery at wrap/<g+1>/<c8>/<recipient>/<k8> (10.6), c8 =
   hex(C_{g+1}[0:8]), in batches of at most 256, up to 4 at once, RecoveryWraps by their own batch route
   (10.14), reading the recipients' ReaderKeys, and a config rotator its forwarding Delegations' reader keys,
   in batches of up to 256 (owner decision 364):
     leaves        if I am a leaf at the current epoch e and e's tree holds no leaf outside H, one leaf_wrap
                   under KEK_e inside GenRotate; else a ReaderWrap to each leaf's ReaderKey
     wrapped       in the config and directory groups, member devices in H that e's tree lacks, wrapped or not
                   yet added: a ReaderWrap each (owner decisions 144, 182); in other groups they join by Add (KF2)
     agents        not covered by a live Delegation: a ReaderWrap each
     Delegations   live ones in H: a DelegationWrap each
     recovery      members reading R with a current RecoveryBind: a RecoveryWrap each
4  PUT gen/<g+1> If-None-Match                                          <- the linearization point
     201      done; hint (D-KEYS-19); the generation is complete, since every delivery already exists
     412      GET it and check it (10.9); if it covers every shrink and expiry I rotate for, adopt it and fetch
              my wrap; else go to 1, rotating at g+2
     unknown  GET gen/<g+1>: my commitment = done; another = 412; 404 = repeat 4 with the same bytes
5  seal content to g+1; delete my keychain draft
retry      the GenRotate bytes, named by their commitment, a restart resuming from the draft within step 2's
           bound and re-staging every delivery under a fresh RK' past it; every delivery precedes the claim,
           so a crash before 4 leaves only staged objects, which GC removes after 24 h, and one after it a
           complete generation;
           a recipient whose ReaderKey appears or changes later gets a LATE delivery to that key from any
           holder but a read_only one (10.6's late wraps, 10.9)
remove X   a writer leaf commits Remove(X) at epoch e+1 (the revoking device first, 10.9); then any writer
           rotates (in the directory group, in 10.9's order), a leaf by leaf_wrap under KEK_{e+1}, which X
           cannot derive; until a leaf commits the Remove, a wrapped writer (an agent, or in the config or
           directory group a wrapped member device, 10.4) may rotate by ReaderWraps to every remaining leaf,
           no leaf_wrap uses an epoch whose tree holds X, and the next leaf commit must remove X; wrapped
           writers never commit Removes (owner decisions 114, 144, 182), yet no repo stays gated while every
           leaf is offline
```

Every path epoch the table names is due within 24 h of its rotation, a compromise's and a member device's removal's alike, and none holds a creation ([owner decision 585](#od-585)).

**Residual ([owner decision 114](#od-114)).** Every holder of a Delegation's reader key reads every later generation of the Delegation's reach (the config, a team network's directory and its tag repos) until the key drops: each agent it admitted, reaped ones and ephemeral ones past their own `not_after` included, since such an agent can close itself, and api can reap it, before any cutoff keyed to that `not_after` (§7.7), and each copy of its auth key. The key drops, at its position, at `DelegationRevoke`, at a revocation for any reason but reaped or a `Suspend` of one of its agents, and at a compromise revocation whose closure voids the Delegation (§7.9's cascade), and at `not_after`; reaping an agent does not drop it. A copy of the whole auth-key bundle also holds the Delegation's signing seed, which no honest daemon's erasure reaches: it admits fresh agents, uncovered once the key has dropped and so reading by their own ReaderWraps, until the Delegation ends or passes `not_after` or `max_admits` (§7.9's delegation row), after which api and every reader refuse its admissions, whatever bearer or client the operator supplies. A lost or removed revocation, or a `Suspend`, thus retires the key but not the admission authority; the revoking device's plan says so and offers `DelegationRevoke`, whose `since_n`, like a compromise revocation's, parks the agents the Delegation admitted from that position on (§7.10's agents row). Bounds: `not_after` is required, at most 90 days (§7.8); `max_admits` counts every admission for the Delegation's life; the console gives CI and cloud Delegations 30 days and replaces them (a new Delegation, then `DelegationRevoke` of the old) at each CI secret rotation and after a key drop.

| Content key | Use (symmetric sealing with XChaCha20-Poly1305; ids, tokens and pads with HMAC-SHA256) |
|---|---|
| `fek` | Wraps each object's random 256-bit key (PLAN.md:148) in a sealed segment header (general repos) or a deletable slot (record-class repos, group inboxes; 10.8); a versionless path in those repos, the search index's files included, keeps one key in a slot only that path's versions name, until a REMOVE generation, a CLOSURE or `ur evs rekey` replaces it (§11.7, §11.14) |
| `manifest` | Names, entry fields, push metadata and ref names (§11) |
| `path` | Token keys per path epoch (§11.6, [owner decision 2](#od-2)) |
| `ref` | Ref ids and the search index's document keys, from RK_1 for the repo's life, since ref ids name every `head/`, `log/` and `idx/` key (§11.6) and a document's key must not change at a rotation (§11.14) |
| `drop` | An X-Wing key pair for deposits that depositors cannot read back, `hpke.MLKEM768X25519().DeriveKeyPair(K_drop)`, K_drop being this 32-byte derivation, published in its generation's GenRotate under the depositor rule below |
| `groupinfo` | Seals GroupInfo and its tree per (group_id, epoch) |
| `index` | Draws the keyed pad that hides which trigrams a search-index shard's documents share (§11.14); per generation, which the shard's header names, so a removed reader cannot predict a later shard's size |

```text
depositor (D-KEYS-17)  before sealing to generation g's drop key, a depositor, which reads the config,
           requires: GenRotate_g verifies; g is the newest generation gkm serves (10.14's drop-key route); g
           covers R's holders_shrunk_at and every holder expiry up to now in its own state (§7.9); now <
           drop_not_after_ms, and g's time_ms < drop_not_after_ms <= time_ms + DropKeyLifetime + 10 min, as
           readerkey's check is, so no signer voids the backstop with a far-future value (owner decision 357);
           g is not below its pin for R, which it then raises; else it waits for a newer rotation, which the
           gate, or for a drop key with under 7 days left 10.6's renewal, makes writers write
```

Clients cache every RK_g in the §5 keychain and, beside it from v0's first generation, each verified GenRotate's Signed bytes, since a signature cannot be rebuilt later and a re-formed group's ladder carries them (10.8); they keep MLS state, trees included, on disk under §5's AEAD, load one group's tree at a time (§18.4's budgets) and delete other epoch secrets (RFC 9420 §9.2). The engine keeps a large tree on disk and streams it rather than holding it whole: a path sealed and written a node at a time, the tree hashed and encoded from its on-disk sections, one decode for a resync, and a copy-on-write of the path in place of a whole-tree clone before a commit, so that a 1,000-leaf group's join, path commit and resync fit a phone's budget; the review phase brings the engine there, measured on §22.8's ios32 cell first, its harness reporting the peaks and failing nothing until then ([owner decision 366](#od-366)). Every derivation and unwrap calls §22's `testHookSecret`.

### 10.6 GKM: the Delivery Service and wrapped-key store

GKM is a strongly consistent Delivery Service (DS; RFC 9750 §5.2.1) with no state of its own: its records are metadata-cluster objects ordered by conditional writes (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)). It verifies 15-minute capability tokens offline (aud `gkm`; scopes `repo:<id>:r|rw|admin`, `deposit` on the drop-key route only, and an unadmitted client's `recovery:<member_id>` for that member's own recovery wraps), honors its scopes as §8.12 says, in gkm's newest verified state, the drop-key route taking the `deposit` check though the key it serves is public (§7.9's tokens row), and honors §7.8's `rev/` objects. gkm reads that state, and taskworker's reconciler each network's, through ACL's one gate cache (§8.9), whose scope check for the gkm audience both share, adding only what gkm alone answers: readers, writers, pins, Delegations, late holders and dropped holders; the cache lists the networks it holds, maps a sidecar to the network that admits it and calls back when a network's new state is installed, and until both views stand the gkm block and the reconciler fail closed ([owner decision 371](#od-371)). Each route takes the scope the scopes block below gives.

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/gkm.proto: the objects' bodies; a Signed, a KeyPackage, a Welcome and a RecoveryWrap's
// ciphertext are stored bare
message GroupForm {              // §6 Signed, purpose group-form, its signer Signed's (owner decision 368)
  bytes repo_id = 1;
  bytes group_id = 2;
  bytes previous_group_id = 3;   // the group this one re-forms, or empty
  uint64 generation = 4;
  AuthPin auth = 5;              // the signer's state when it signs, at which members judge the signer
}
message GkmGroupOwner { bytes repo_id = 1; bytes network_id = 2; }   // owner decision 201
message GkmEpochObject {         // gkm writes header, uploader and time_ms itself, from the commit, the token
                                 //   and its clock, so an upload has none to state falsely
  bytes commit = 1;              // empty at epoch 0
  GkmCommitHeader header = 2;    // at a creation's epoch 0 gen/1's generation and auth; at a re-form's the
                                 //   form's generation and no auth
  bytes uploader = 3;            // at epoch 0 gkm-1's creator
  int64 time_ms = 4;
  bytes gen_wrap = 5;
  bytes sealed_group_info = 6;
  uint64 group_info_generation = 7;
  bytes network_id = 8;          // 8 and 9 only in epoch 0
  uint32 cipher_suite = 9;
}
message GkmGroupInfoObject {     // at most 16 leaves the pointer {epoch}, that epoch's object holding the sealed
                                 //   GroupInfo; above, all three
  uint64 epoch = 1;
  uint64 generation = 2;
  bytes sealed_group_info = 3;
}
message GkmWelcomePointer { bytes group_id = 1; uint64 epoch = 2; bytes key_package_ref = 3; }   // owner decision 363
message GkmKeyPackageClaim { bytes group_id = 1; bytes claimer = 2; }   // the target is the sidecar_id in its key
```

**Write gate (D-KEYS-6; D-EVS-18).** The predicate below, over §7.9's causal identities, decides which writes a key-holder change blocks; §11.8 enforces it at each ref's head CAS. Target: p99 close-to-reopen ≤5 min with a writer online, in the directory group a hinted or pushing one (10.9); alarm at 1 h.

```text
pass      a push or deposit to R declaring generation g passes only if g covers R's holders_shrunk_at in evs's
          newest verified state and no holder of R expired in (t_g, now] (§7.9's coverage)
shrinks   SidecarRevoke, MemberRevoke and parks (§7.9's compromise cascade); api's reap of an ephemeral
          sidecar no live Delegation covers; Suspend; GrantRevoke and RepoRevoke of a grant that reads;
          DelegationRevoke and a Delegation's key drop (10.5); a compromise retirement (SidecarRevoke or
          RecoveryRebind with reason compromise, or a leaked bundle's DelegationRevoke with since_n > 0), a
          shrink by §7.9's test though a rebind keeps recovery(m)'s
          identity; an authority statement's completion that drops a holder; any base whose rows drop one
expiries  RepoGrant and requested grants' expires; an uncovered agent's SidecarAdmit and a Delegation's
          not_after (a member device's admission carries none, §7.9); a ReaderKey's lapse is none (10.5)
never     admissions, grants, OwnerConfirm, Unsuspend, routine RecoveryRebinds, reaps of covered agents and,
          where their Delegation covers, ephemeral agents' own not_after, and a member device's move between
          leaf and wrap (10.4; owner decisions 144, 182)
window    heads' auth pins never fall (§11.8); a push validated before a shrink commits ordered before it,
          within §11.8's bound: about 10 s, 5 min if api's notification is lost, plus §19.6's 10 s store
          request deadline, since §11.8 issues and reissues a head PUT only within 5 s of its validation, or,
          for one whose drive commits stalled, until §19.6's settle rule releases the head, which no read or
          commit passes meanwhile
```

**Sizes (D-KEYS-14)**, from RFC 9420's structures, which §22.8 measures at M2:

inputs: X-Wing key 1,216 B, ciphertext 1,120 B (GOROOT/src/crypto/mlkem/mlkem.go:27, :30;

  every parent full .. blank
