**What GKM sees.** §2.8 adopts these rows verbatim; [owner decision 115](#od-115) confirmed them (Q-KEYS-12).

```yaml
gkm-1:
  sees: GroupForm chain (repo_id, group_id, previous group, generation, signer, and the signer's auth pin when it signs (owner decision 368)); epoch 0 (network_id, cipher suite 0x0010 (owner decision 44), creator); each group's owner marker (repo_id, network_id), written first at a creation or re-form, through which alone gkm resolves the group (owner decision 201); and each forwarding Delegation's reader public key, by delegation_id, which gkm and every rotator check against its row's digest (owner decision 202)
  why: one accepted commit per epoch; re-forming; one repo to a group; sealing to forwarding Delegations (§10.5)
  ttl: life of the repo, epoch 0 while epoch/0 exists; an owner marker until the repo's shred, a re-seed's form writing it again; a forwarding Delegation's reader key until 24 h after the Delegation ends or is superseded
gkm-2:
  sees: epoch objects; group_id, epoch, content type, generation, auth pin, size, time, uploader sidecar_id; the commit as PrivateMessage ciphertext; GenWrap; at most 16 leaves, the sealed GroupInfo and the generation that seals it
  why: ordering; the write gate
  ttl: 30 d, then until every leaf acking in the last 30 d has applied it; never the newest epoch
gkm-3:
  withdrawn: no roster delta in the clear (owner decision 59); membership shows only as sidecar ids in gkm-4, gkm-5, gkm-7 and gkm-10, as in api-7
gkm-4:
  sees: "KeyPackages (init and leaf HPKE keys, signature key, credential: sidecar_id, identity key and its algorithm, suite, not_after, admission hash, signature); claims (group, claimer, target); ReaderKeys (owner decision 114)"
  why: asynchronous adds; wrapped readers
  ttl: KeyPackages until claimed, or 90 d; claims 90 d; ReaderKeys until replaced or past their not_after, at most 7 d
gkm-5:
  sees: Welcome objects and pointers, the pointers keyed by recipient, group and epoch and naming the KeyPackageRef the Add used (owner decision 363); recipient sidecar_ids and KeyPackageRefs in the clear; secrets and GroupInfo encrypted
  why: deliver joins
  ttl: until every recipient has acked, at most 90 d
gkm-6:
  sees: external commits, for resync and recovery only (PublicMessage); the joiner's leaf and credential, its removed old leaf, their ExternalInit and Remove proposals and their UpdatePath's public keys and encrypted path secrets
  why: offline catch-up and recovery
  ttl: as gkm-2
gkm-7:
  sees: key ladder; GenRotates (group, generation, parent and own commitments, cause, auth pin, time, holders hash, the count of its staged and recovery wraps, signer; GenLink and leaf-wrap ciphertexts; the drop public key and its expiry where the kind takes deposits); GroupInfo pointers and, above 16 leaves, sealed GroupInfo and the generation it names; staged and late wraps (group, generation, commitment, recipient sidecar_id or delegation_id and the SHA-256 of the key sealed to, staged or late, a late one's auth pin and time, ciphertext, signer; owner decisions 114, 144, 182)
  why: ladder, resync, deposits; wrapped readers
  ttl: life of the repo, a gen pack's GenRotates as gen/'s; GroupInfo until superseded; wraps until the next generation's exist, staged wraps of a lost claim 24 h, a recipient's wrap to an older key 30 d after one to a newer key exists
gkm-8:
  sees: recovery wraps (member_id, group_id, generation, the 8-byte prefix c8 of the generation's commitment, which gkm-7 shows whole, an 8-byte prefix of the binding's Ed25519 key hash, which the authorization log already shows, HPKE ciphertext); the bindings are §7.9's RecoveryBind config records, not gkm objects
  why: recovery after losing every device
  ttl: until a RecoveryRebind replaces them or the repo is deleted; staged ones of a lost claim 24 h
gkm-9:
  sees: request log; client, route, group, time, bytes (GroupInfo requests included)
  why: rate limits, abuse
  ttl: 7 d
gkm-10:
  sees: acks in Redis {gka_<group_id>}; group_id, sidecar_id, newest applied epoch, time; written at most daily
  why: retention
  ttl: overwritten by the leaf's next ack; 31 d after its last write; deleted with its group's gkm objects at a shred (§11.12); soft state outside the rdb bundles, lost with Redis, after which gkm deletes no epoch for 30 d; a hold's copy excepted (api-14)
```

### 10.7 Flows

In v0 each flow runs on deliveries (10.4; [owner decision 610](#od-610)): a creation stages its first generation's wraps, an admitted device or a new member takes a LATE delivery of the current generation, a removal rotates with cause REMOVE to every remaining holder, and a resync fetches the deliveries its generations lack; the review phase rewrites KF1-KF7 so, and their epoch, Welcome, KeyPackage and GroupInfo steps below are MLS's, Later.

**KF1. Create a repo.** A member's device C files §8.8's `RepoCreate`, creates the repo in evs as `keying` (§11.12), placing it ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), and becomes its admin ([owner decision 8](#od-8)); a config repo follows §7.9's bootstrap. `POST /gkm/groups` takes C's Signed GroupForm, epoch 0's GenWrap_0 and sealed GroupInfo (a random 16-byte group_id) and `gen/1`'s Signed GenRotate of a new RK_1, without a parent, and writes the group's owner marker ([owner decision 201](#od-201)), the GroupForm, `epoch/0` and `gen/1` in that order, each If-None-Match, equal bytes answering success, so KF1 resumes after a crash. C writes generation 1's deliveries (10.5's step 3: ReaderWraps, DelegationWraps, RecoveryWraps) while the repo is still keying, resuming from its keychain after a crash, and only then has evs activate it (`POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/activate`, which checks the GroupForm and `gen/1` and answers 409 GROUP_NOT_READY without them, §11.12), so no content predates its recovery wraps. C then adds the other leaves in one Add-only commit with its Welcome and GroupInfo. A tagged or ephemeral sidecar, which holds no leaf for an epoch 0, files the `RepoCreate`, places the repo and stays its admin, and a member device forms the group: gkm hints `pending` to the network's config writers for a keying repo with no GroupForm (10.6), and the first to act that is a key holder of the repo and holds admin on it at gkm, which §8.5's implicit document gives every member device, runs the steps above as the group's creator, epoch 0 holding its own leaf, and wraps generation 1 to the agent, which then has evs activate the repo; a repo an agent creates while no such device is online, or under an ACL document that gives no member device both, stays keying, which leaks nothing, a rule revisited at M6, when Team policies can narrow member devices' evs rights ([owner decision 365](#od-365)). A network's first device splits KF1 for its config repo at bootstrap (§7.9): before base 1 it draws the config group's id and RK_1, keeping them as KF1's draft, seals and signs the first config head's push with them, auth {0, A_0} and generation pin {group_id, 1, C_1}, and publishes base 1; after it, it signs GenRotate_1 at S(1) over that RK_1, runs the rest of KF1 and sends the push, C_g holding no pin ([owner decision 373](#od-373)).

**KF2. Add a device D.** D enrolls, its `SidecarAdmit` enters the authorization log (§5.6, §7.9), and it uploads a ReaderKey and, as a member device, KeyPackages. Once the state lists D where its subject reads, and again at D's first KeyPackage upload (10.6), GKM hints `pending` to the writers, and a committer per 10.9 claims a KeyPackage and commits the Add with other pending changes, the Welcome, the sealed GroupInfo and GenWrap; an agent, or in the config or directory group a member device that is wrapped or has no KeyPackage (10.4; owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)), gets a late ReaderWrap of the current generation instead, signed at a state that lists D (10.9's late row), and a covered agent reads at once through its Delegation's wrap. D checks RK_g against `gen/<g>`'s C_g and walks the ladder (10.5). A newly admitted device holds no generation of the config repo, so until it does it joins on states its config follower applied rows-only, which serve only to take its config Welcome or wrap and open the config repo's generation keys; once it holds the key the follower re-reads those bases in full before it stands, and D signs, seals, commits and rotates nothing before that (§7.9's no key row; [owner decision 319](#od-319)). Owner-bound repos park a D without its owner's consent (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)), whose devices raise `approval_pending` until an `OwnerConfirm`.

**KF3. Add a member N.** A repo or network admin signs N's grant into the repo's access log (§8.8; owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8)), or in an owner-bound repo the owner's device an `EvsShare` ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and KF2 runs for N's devices: the granting device at once, other writer leaves after 15 s plus jitter; while none is online, N waits and nothing leaks.

**KF4. Remove a member or device X** (§7.10). The revocation's log entry n' drops X from the key holders of every repo it read, so evs refuses writes whose generation does not cover n' (10.6, §11.8), and evs and gkm refuse X's tokens (§7.8). A committer per 10.9, the revoking device first, commits the Remove with a path; any writer then rotates (10.5), staging its wraps before it claims `gen/<g+1>`, at the latest through `EnsureWritable` before its next write, so reaps batch. A wrapped X needs only the rotation, and a wrapped revoker in the config or directory group rotates first, leaving a leaf X's Remove to the next leaf commit (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)). D-TRUST-10's witness stop never holds a Remove, rotation or revocation ([owner decision 129](#od-129)).

```text
   api (§7.10)       evs               gkm               writers
1  |--entry n'------>|                 |                 |   holders_shrunk_at = n': 412 below; receivers 451
2  |                 |                 |--hint pending-->|   per-client gkm topic, the revoking device first
3  |                 |                 |<--epoch/<e+1>---|   a writer leaf: Remove + path; header (g, (n', A'))
4  |                 |                 |<--gen/<g+1>-----|   any writer: staged wraps, then the claim at (n', A')
5  |                 |<--write at g+1, auth >= n'---------|   the gate passes it
```

**KF5. Offline catch-up.** Up to 100 epochs behind, the device replays each later commit in order (each epoch derives from the previous `init_secret`). Further behind, or if commits were pruned, processing fails or its leaf was removed as stale, it opens the current sealed GroupInfo (10.6) with the key of the generation it names, its object's group_info_generation or generation, from its wrap (a device none of whose keys opens a delivery of it, its ReaderKey lapsed or past retention, publishes a new one and asks for a late delivery to it, 10.6's late wraps), and resyncs by external commit (ExternalInit, a Remove of its old leaf, GenWrap_{e+1}); else it awaits a re-add or uses its recovery code (10.8). Nothing is lost.

**KF6. Concurrent commits.** The 409 loser, having stored no Welcome, processes the winner and retries what remains. Rotations race only on `gen/<g+1>` (10.5).

**KF7. gkm unavailable.** Cached keys serve reads and deposits; evs checks the gate itself from the authorization log, so writes continue while every shrink is covered, and a removal still stops them until gkm returns and a writer rotates. Joins, catch-up and membership changes wait. gkm never answers 502 or 504 itself, its routes buffering at the lb, so its client takes one whose body is no gkm refusal as no answer from gkm, as it takes a transport error: this fallback holds, a Welcome watch stays, and a write's outcome is unknown and resolved as after a lost answer, never judged refused ([owner decision 374](#od-374)).

### 10.8 Revocation, erasure, recovery, re-seeding, key domains

**Removed or expired holder X ([owner decision 64](#od-64)).** X keeps what it held up to generation g and loses everything after: the generation that covers its drop is cause REMOVE (10.9), so content rewraps lazily, each file's next write a full checkpoint under a fresh object key (§11.7; Q-KEYS-10), the search index's versionless files included (its heads at their writer's next push, its shards at their next merge or roll-up; §11.14), and path tokens re-key through §11.6's path epoch, at once for a member's device or a compromise, within 24 h for other drops and for expiries ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), or, while two source epochs stand, once one drops; §11.6 reconciles the two.

**Erasure ([owner decision 61](#od-61)).** An entry's key lives only in a deletable slot (§11.12), so an ERASE push deleting it, cached copies and mirrors' slot copies (§11.12) shred the entry even if ciphertext survives; §11.12's CUT first fences the index's publication of it, then its CLOSURE rewrites the search index's files holding its postings without it, under fresh keys in new slots, and the ERASE destroys their old slots' keys, one of which every older stored version of those files uses, staged bytes in a batch included (§11.14); no operator copy holds slots or wraps ([owner decision 90](#od-90)), and owner devices' mirrors hold slot copies and apply each erasure (§11.13). gkm, like evs, refuses a `deleted` repo but for a re-seed's GroupForm (below; [owner decision 82](#od-82)); its shred (§11.12) deletes the repo's gkm objects and `{gka_}` acks, and again after 10 min for writes in flight (10.6's checks), even under a preservation hold, subject to counsel ([owner decision 133](#od-133)), and members drop its keys.

**Recovery when M loses every device (owner decisions [62](#od-62), [127](#od-127), [128](#od-128), [592](#od-592)).** §5.9's recovery code derives X-Wing and Ed25519 keys that §7.9's `RecoveryBind` binds to M, each by HKDF-SHA256 from the code's 16 bytes under its own info string, with no BIP-39 PBKDF2 step (§5.9); every rotator, agents included, wraps RK_g to every reading member's current X-Wing recovery key, a public key every config reader holds, and the ladder opens older generations.
- With the code, a new device is admitted by the recovery key as §7.9's table says: at once outside the AdminSet, or at the cosign with `self_admit` off; through the 72 h window and veto for AdminSet members and k = 1 networks; meanwhile it reads only the authorization log and M's own recovery wraps (10.14). Where they apply, the window and veto bound admission, not those wraps, which the device fetches at once and opens once admitted ([owner decision 367](#od-367)): yet a code holder with M's login holds every generation wrapped to M's recovery key and, through the ladder, each earlier one, and with the operator's ciphertext and gen/ objects reads them, whatever a veto does: a rebind or a cascade void stops new wraps, and the code keeps opening what was wrapped to it and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once; revoking the device it admitted does not retire the code (§2.10). Before admission it fetches its recovery wraps under `recovery:<member_id>`, keeping the newest per group whose b8 names its code's binding (10.6); once admitted, when `gen/<g>` reaches it, it opens its config-group RecoveryWrap first and passes §7.9's `anchor` on it, raising §5.4's `head_alarm` (fork) and acting no further otherwise; only then does it open the rest and each group's sealed GroupInfo, self-join by external commit the config group and every group M writes ([owner decision 128](#od-128)), join the others through KF2, revoke M's lost devices through §5.6's calls (D-CORE-20; k of n for an AdminSet member's devices, its own signature counting as one), remove their leaves and rotate (10.5), in any order: a self-join may leave revoked leaves if it carries no GenWrap (generation 0) and its next commit removes them, so no generation reaches a thief's leaves. Above 16 leaves, a self-join waits for one leaf online to write the current GroupInfo; past the first 1,000, the device reads the config and the team directory by their RecoveryWraps, then by wraps (§7.9; owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).
- A cascade's void of M's binding in effect leaves M no binding and restores no earlier one (§7.9's cascade; [owner decision 592](#od-592)): no rotation wraps to a voided code, and none of M's codes admits a device, so until a device of M's outside P binds a fresh code by `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9), whose `RecoveryBind` takes RecoveryWraps as the next bullet says, M's new device comes in only by an admin's admission, parked for owner-bound repos ([owner decision 126](#od-126)).
- `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) signs a `RecoveryRebind` (§7.9), re-wraps each group's current generation to the new binding at that binding's own b8 path (10.6), deletes M's old binding's wraps only once every new one exists, so a crash between leaves both and its retry finishes, and requests a `request` rotation in M's groups, or, for a code retired as compromised (`RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}`), a `remove` one, which starts a path epoch, due within 24 h as every due is ([owner decision 585](#od-585)), and full checkpoints (§11.6, §11.7). No rebind or void reaches a keychain backup sealed before it, whose `keychain.wrap` the retired or voided code still opens, yielding what §5.9's backup bullet lists, so after a compromise rebind or a void each device whose backups may hold such a sealing is revoked as compromised (§7.9) and enrolled anew by §5.9's procedure ([owner decision 212](#od-212)).
- Without the code, admins revoke the lost devices and admit a new one (§7.9), moving every team repo M read to a new generation; M's owner-bound repos, which need M's consent ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), and single-member repos are lost.

**Site loss (D-KEYS-13; order in §19.10).** gkm objects have no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)), but devices keep each group's MLS state and every RK_g: a device 10.6's GroupForm rules allow, a repo admin's and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented device, re-forms each group under a GroupForm linked to the cached RK_g, re-uploads the ladder and re-adds readers and RecoveryWraps, and members check the signer and their cached C_g. A re-formed group carries the ladder by these rules:

```text
form      a re-form draws a new 16-byte group_id, and its GroupForm names previous_group_id and generation,
          the newest g the re-former holds
bytes     the new group's gen/<k>, k <= the form's generation, holds the old Signed GenRotate byte for byte,
          naming its old group_id, from the copy each client keeps beside RK_g (10.5); GenLink's AAD and C_g
          hold no group_id, so the ladder carries over
route     POST /gkm/groups/<id>/ladder, admin scope, at most 64 Signed GenRotates a call in ascending order,
          open only while the newest GroupForm names the group and before its epoch/1 exists, and in
          re-seed mode with the form: gkm checks the order, parent_commitment against gen/<k-1> and
          k <= the form's generation, writes each If-None-Match, equal bytes answering success, and skips
          the claim checks' time and signer rows
wait      the group takes no commit, wrap or claim until gen/<form's generation> exists
members   check the form's signer by 10.6's rule at the auth pin the form carries, where their retained log
          reaches it and not before (owner decision 368), and each C_k against their cached one, a mismatch being an
          alarm and no adoption, and judge each GenRotate's signature and 10.9's rotation checks only where
          their retained log reaches, as 10.9's judged row does
delivery  for g <= the form's generation, 10.9's delivery checks compare a body's group_id with the path's
          group, not gen/<g>'s
pins      generation pins compare (g, C_g); a new group_id at an equal (g, C_g), and a new epoch pin from
          epoch 0, are taken only along a verified GroupForm chain, and evs and readers resolve a statement's
          gen/<g> through the repo's newest GroupForm (§11.8)
after     later rotations run as usual; in §19.10's groups step a re-seeded live repo's first rotation and its
          Adds come in a second call, once repo/ is active, since the form, epoch 0 and the ladder are all gkm
          takes while repo/ reads keying or deleted (10.6's checks row; owner decision 618)
```

A repo re-seeded as deleted (§11.13) takes only that GroupForm, with its epoch 0 and ladder, while deleted ([owner decision 82](#od-82)), which leaves the re-former's keychain record at its finishing phase; the re-former's gkm client resumes that record by itself at its syncs once gkm takes the rotation's writes (repo/ active), at most once a `ReformResumeInterval` (15 min) while gkm refuses them, so once the repo is restored, however and on whichever device, its next sync rotates to g+1, staging each reading member's RecoveryWrap, then makes the pending Adds; a sync never drafts a re-form, and a call to re-seed or resume that finds no record answers the group the device pins ([owner decision 663](#od-663); §19.10's groups row). Devices open its files from their cached RK_g once it is restored, its readers rejoin by KF2 and late wraps, and a shred deletes the group. Slots return from owner devices' mirrors (§11.13). Repos no device holds are lost (§2.18).

**Key domains ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S4)**, each its own repo and group, take §8.5's kind defaults as readers (owner-bound kinds: [owner decision 126](#od-126)).

| Domain | Readers (agents by wrap) | Deposits by drop key |
|---|---|---|
| Author vault ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S1, S2) | the author's consented devices; `EvsShare` recipients | the author's other devices, tagged and headless sidecars |
| Team record ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) S3; X20) | admins' and auditors' devices | members' and tagged sidecars; authors keep copies |
| Shared team repos | every reading sidecar (§8) | — |
| Config (§7.9); a team network's directory (§16.11) | every admitted sidecar; member devices past the first 1,000 by wrap (owner decisions [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) | — |
| Burner vault and mailbox (§15) | the user's consented devices | `tag:mail` mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), which cannot read the archive |

**Escrow ([owner decision 63](#od-63)).** None by default, and never silent: Team's v1 opt-in `tag:audit` reader on a customer device (sidecar/design/improve.md:106-108; §8.5's `audit` block under a k-of-n `AuditOptIn`) gets ReaderWraps only once every member's config holds the block and each affected reader list shows it.

### 10.9 Authorization of MLS operations

In v0 only the wrap rules below apply, a delivery's check against its header, the holder set at its state and the access log, for STAGED and LATE deliveries alike; the commit rules are MLS's, Later with it ([MLS](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-mls); [owner decision 610](#od-610)).

GKM sees no proposal ([owner decision 59](#od-59)), so members verify each decrypted commit and each wrap against its header, the authorization state at its auth pin (§7.9) and the repo's access log (§8.8). On a mismatch a member alarms and never adopts or encrypts to the epoch or generation; a bad commit can stall a group until an admin revokes its committer and the group re-forms through the ladder. The `refused` alarm is evidence against a party: a committer whose own commit gkm refuses only because a newer generation stands takes that generation and commits again, raising none (10.6's refused row; [owner decision 375](#od-375)). GKM originates nothing; no group has external senders (I-4).

**Committers (owner decisions [113](#od-113), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).** The signed input, not the committer, carries the authority, so no membership change waits for an admin, and members reject a commit without it. Wrapped writers (agents, and the config and directory groups' wrapped member devices, 10.4) rotate by re-wrapping but never commit an Add or Remove.

```text
Add            committer  a writer leaf, the granting device first; for a first wrap (an agent's, a
                          Delegation's or a wrapped member device's), any holder but a read_only one by the
                          delivery checks' late row, gkm hinting writers first (10.6); in the config and
                          directory groups also the admission's signer, by an Add from its leaf, or by the first
                          wrap if it or the device is wrapped, and from its leaf the signer of a revocation that
                          made the device leaf-entitled (§7.9's move)
               check      a signed grant in the access log, admission or EvsShare, or owner decision 63's audit
                          assignment; in an owner-bound repo only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) and their
                          EvsShares (owner decision 126); in the config and directory groups a leaf only for a
                          leaf-entitled device (§7.9); admitted, unrevoked, unparked, outside URnetwork platform
                          networks, key pinned, KeyPackage claimed for this group
Remove         committer  a writer leaf, the revoking device first; in the config and directory groups also the
                          revocation's signer from its leaf, a wrapped signer rotating instead; never the target
                          (RFC 9420 §12.2)
               check      its signed input: a SidecarRevoke or MemberRevoke (which a server deactivation
                          follows), a park (§7.9), a Suspend, a revoked or expired grant, in the config and
                          directory groups the target's loss of leaf entitlement at the auth pin under §7.9's
                          rank (it reads on by wraps), or staleness: a stale Remove is valid iff the target's
                          credential in the prior epoch's tree has not_after - 90 days + §7.9's stale_leaf_days
                          (90), read at the commit's auth pin, <= my clock + 60 s, so a member judges it from the
                          tree alone and a day-old joiner and an old member agree; a writer leaf commits one only
                          a day past that, and only if its own record shows no later change of that leaf; the
                          value is evidence only, refusing no commit, so a leaf that inflates it delays only its
                          own stale Remove; a stale-removed device returns by resync (KF5)
Rotation       committer  any writer that holds the key, as a holder or covered by a Delegation, at a pin
  alone                   covering what it rotates for, wrapped ones included (owner decision 114); in the config
                          group also the signer of the admission or revocation (owner decision 128) or, after
                          the reap of an uncovered ephemeral agent, of its admission (§7.10), each while a holder
               check      the rotation checks below; deliveries only to key holders (10.5)
Self-update    committer  the leaf itself, by a path-only commit
               check      sidecar_id and identity key unchanged
External       committer  the sidecar itself
  commit       check      resync (same sidecar_id and key, removing at most its old leaf), or a recovery-admitted
                          device's self-join in the config group, if leaf-entitled, or in a group its member
                          writes, under the Add row's checks; it may leave revoked leaves, carrying no GenWrap
                          (generation 0), if its next commit removes them
GroupContext   committer  a repo admin's leaf (required_capabilities); rotations need none
  Extensions   check      kind and owner never change
Directory      committer  every admitted sidecar reads the team directory and all but read_only ones write it
  group                   (§16.11), so each admission makes its subject a reader there and its signer seats it
                          at once by the Add row; a revocation's signer commits by the Remove row a leaf
                          target's Remove, then the rotation, and after api's reap of an uncovered ephemeral
                          agent the device that signed its admission rotates, as in the config group; any other
                          writer leaf may commit after 15 s plus jitter (KF3; owner decisions 113, 182)
               hints      gkm hints pending there only to that signer, at once, and to the config writers, which
                          act after 15 s plus jitter; an unhinted writer rotates only for a push the gate
                          refuses, after a random wait of up to 15 s that a covering generation ends, so one
                          rotator normally stages a rotation's wraps (~1.3 KB a wrapped reader) and the gate
                          reopens within ~20 s of the first push it refuses
ReInit, PSK, external or standalone proposals: refused

rotation checks: every member, for each GenRotate
signer    in KeyHolders(R, auth, time) or covered by a Delegation in it, and a writer at auth or, in the config
          group, the signer of the statement it answers (owner decision 128) or, after the reap of an
          uncovered ephemeral agent, of its admission (§7.10)
chain     parent_commitment chains; auth is on my chain and not before my previous base
holders   holders_sha256 equals my recomputation; each staged delivery I read passes the delivery checks
          below; a leaf_wrap's epoch tree holds no non-holder leaf
cause     REMOVE iff the generation covers a shrink, an authorization expiry (10.6's expiries) or a compromise
          retirement since the parent, or its parent is poisoned (below)
time      time_ms <= my clock + 60 s and >= the parent's
drop      where R takes deposits, time_ms < drop_not_after_ms <= time_ms + DropKeyLifetime + 10 min, as
          readerkey's check is, so no signer voids the backstop with a far-future value (owner decision 357)
poisoned  a delivery the delivery checks below judge invalid: members alarm, never seal to the generation and
          rotate at once (cause REMOVE), and admins revoke the signer
roster    every commit's roster lies within the key holders at its auth pin, and in the config and directory
          groups within the leaf-entitled devices (§7.9), except a recovery self-join's revoked leaves (10.8),
          whose generation-0 epoch has no GenWrap; the next leaf commit after a leaf's drop, or its loss of
          leaf entitlement there, removes it, and no leaf wrap uses an epoch whose tree holds a non-holder
window    after a compromised leaf's commit whose tree holds a party dropped at the commit's own header, a
          wrapped writer, which reads no commit, and a leaf whose seal races that commit may seal to the
          generation it carried until the refusing member's REMOVE rotation reaches them; accepted, since the
          commit needs a compromised leaf, which already holds that generation's key and could hand the
          dropped party the same content or the key itself (owner decision 369)

delivery checks: every member, for each ReaderWrap or DelegationWrap it reads (its own when it fetches it,
others' when it answers wrap-pending), judged at the delivery's own state, never at the member's later one
body      it verifies as its SignedType under the signer's identity key; group_id, generation and commitment
          equal gen/<g>'s, or for g at or below a re-form's generation the group_id is the path's group
          (10.8's delivery row); recipient and recipient_key_sha256 match its path's recipient and k8 (10.6)
staged    STAGED: no auth or time; the signer is gen/<g>'s; the recipient is in the KeyHolders set whose hash
          gen/<g> carries, and wrap_count counts it
late      LATE, a first delivery or a replacement to a newer key alike: auth (n_d, A_d) lies on my chain with
          n_d >= gen/<g>'s auth.version; gen/<g>'s time_ms <= time_ms <= my clock + 60 s; the recipient is in
          KeyHolders(R, auth, time_ms); the signer is in it or covered by a Delegation in it, and not
          read_only (§7.9)
judged    at the delivery's auth, a STAGED one's being gen/<g>'s, only from my previous base to my tip, and
          invalid if a row above fails, an auth off my chain included; one above my tip waits until I reach
          it, one I cannot reach being withheld (§7.9's retain row); one before my previous base I do not
          judge, and it counts against no one
history   a delivery valid at its own state stays valid after its recipient's or signer's revocation, a key
          replacement or a replay, and poisons nothing later
use       the recipient opens only a delivery to itself and to a key it holds whose body verifies and whose
          RK_g matches C_g, then judges it as any member does
```

### 10.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| PublicMessage handshakes or a clear roster delta | GKM checks proposals or rosters | GKM reads credentials, proposals, the tree (RFC 9420 §16.4) or the roster | Ruled out (owner directive; [owner decision 59](#od-59)) |
| Every admitted sidecar a leaf | One key path; read is membership | A commit per CI join and reap; agents share the 1,000 leaves | Rejected ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) |
| Generations raised both by MLS commits and by wrapped writers | No separate claim object | Two paths mint g+1 and fork the ladder | Rejected (D-KEYS-15) |
| A rotation at every reap of a Delegation-covered agent | Each reap looks like a removal | Excludes nothing the Delegation's key still reads | Rejected (D-KEYS-16) |
| Suspend as a server-only control | No rotation or individual wraps when one agent pauses | A suspended agent opens what the server still delivers to its Delegation's key; the one-switch claim and §8.12's invariant would need another exception | Rejected (D-KEYS-16) |
| A time identity at each covered agent's own `not_after` | Keeps non-ephemeral admissions shorter than their Delegation | An admission landing after a rotation's pin would shorten a holder's life that the generation never saw; an ephemeral agent closes itself, or api reaps it, before any such cutoff | Rejected: §7.9 floors a non-ephemeral one at its Delegation's `not_after`, and an ephemeral one ends as a reap (D-KEYS-16) |
| 1,000 member devices per network, or a larger config tree | No member wraps | The cap refuses Teams past ~330 members; 5,000 leaves make a 7.9-14 MB tree and path commits to ~6 MB, past §18.4's budgets | Rejected ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) |
| Proxy re-encryption (PLAN.md:223, :284-327) | The server re-wraps headers blind | Semi-honest (PLAN.md:323), against D-TRUST-1; no supported Go pairings (golang.org/x/crypto/bn256 is deprecated: bn256.go:22-23) | Rejected |

### 10.11 Decisions proposed

**D-KEYS-1 (proposed).** v0 distributes every group key under 10.5's hierarchy by `KeyDelivery` wraps alone; MLS, built in house, is Later, its drafted code dark (owner decisions [43](#od-43), [610](#od-610), the latter amending [owner decision 1](#od-1)). *Why:* wraps already serve agents, member devices past 1,000, Delegations and recovery codes, and MLS cost about 42.5k lines, 23 decisions and 27-63 MB of heap at 1,000 leaves; against a passive keychain copy, content keys heal at the ReaderKey's not_after plus the next generation, and against an active clone only after a compromise revocation and a new enrollment (10.5); the ladder keeps §11's format distributor-independent.

**D-KEYS-2 (proposed).** In v0 every reader of a repo, member devices among them, holds per-generation ReaderWraps ([owner decision 610](#od-610), amending [owner decision 60](#od-60)); with MLS, Later, a repo's group gives a leaf to each reading member device up to 1,000, other readers holding ReaderWraps, and in the config and team directory groups member devices past §7.9's first 1,000 as well, which commit there only wraps and rotations. *Why:* owner decisions [1](#od-1), [7](#od-7), [60](#od-60), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144) and [182](#od-182), which [owner decision 610](#od-610) leaves as the design MLS returns with.

**D-KEYS-3 (proposed).** With MLS, Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), member commits are PrivateMessage whose clear header adds only the generation and the auth pin, and only external commits are PublicMessage; v0 has no commits. *Why:* [owner decision 59](#od-59); the gate needs both.

**D-KEYS-4 (proposed).** Credential 0xF552 binds the MLS key to `sidecar_id` and the identity key under a config-repo `SidecarAdmit`; only the genesis rests on trust on first use, and owner-bound repos add only consented readers (10.9). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110), [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126); R-KEYS-8, R-KEYS-9.

**D-KEYS-5 (proposed).** GKM keeps no state of its own and orders, claims, delivers and retains through conditional object writes on its repo's metadata cluster, with acks as Redis soft state (10.6). *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2), [136](#od-136), [145](#od-145); RFC 9420 §14.

**D-KEYS-6 (proposed).** Commit before write: an authorization-log entry that shrinks a repo's key holders, or a holder's expiry, closes evs's gate (D-EVS-18) until a generation covering it is claimed (§7.9, 10.5), which is cause REMOVE (10.9); generations also rotate on request and every 30 days. *Why:* no server transaction changes readers ([owner decision 5](#od-5)), and an expired holder must lose new content as a removed one does (R-KEYS-4).

**D-KEYS-7 (withdrawn).** Superseded by owner decisions [113](#od-113) and [128](#od-128): the signed statement, not an admin committer, authorizes each membership change (10.9).

**D-KEYS-8 (proposed).** Drop keys in each generation's signed GenRotate give write-only deposits, which depositors accept only if the generation covers every shrink they know (10.5); each lives `GkmSettings.DropKeyLifetime`, 90 days, and writers renew it once under 7 days are left ([owner decision 357](#od-357)); each key domain is its own repo. *Why:* agents deposit sessions they cannot read (R-KEYS-9).

**D-KEYS-9 (proposed).** Rotating devices wrap each generation to every reading member's current `RecoveryBind` key; Team's only escrow is a visible audit reader. *Why:* owner decisions [62](#od-62), [63](#od-63), with no server-guessable secret.

**D-KEYS-10 (proposed).** M2's entry fixes the MLS wire's fields and the delivery wire's (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery, 10.6's wrap and recovery paths); its exit freezes them and suite 0x0010 on §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact (10.4), with 10.4's conformance plan, fuzz targets run as Go tests and 10.6's sizes measured (§22.8); the security page says this MLS on draft suite 0x0010 is not independently audited. *Why:* owner decisions [99](#od-99), [101](#od-101), [119](#od-119) (§2.18).

**D-KEYS-11 (proposed).** Tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars read and write through ReaderWraps, and live Delegations get DelegationWraps that cover their agents (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114): no commits, and reads with no member online.

**D-KEYS-12 (proposed).** With MLS, Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), MLS is 10.4's subset on ciphersuite 0x0010, migrating through GroupForm and the ladder if IANA assigns this suite another value; v0 freezes no MLS wire. *Why:* [owner decision 44](#od-44).

**D-KEYS-13 (proposed).** After a site loss, repo admins' devices, and for owner-bound kinds the owner's consented devices, re-seed each group from their keychains under a GroupForm linked through the ladder (10.8): the form draws a new group_id and names the previous one and its generation, the old Signed GenRotates go up byte for byte from the copies clients keep, and pins follow (g, C_g) only along a verified GroupForm chain. *Why:* gkm has no off-site copy (owner decisions [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94)); a GenRotate's signature cannot be rebuilt, and GenLink's AAD and C_g hold no group_id.

**D-KEYS-14 (proposed).** With MLS, Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), groups scale by 10.6's sizes: 10.4's self-update interval, KF5's resync, GroupInfo on demand above 16 leaves, daily acks, trees on disk, which the engine streams rather than holding whole ([owner decision 366](#od-366)); in v0 a rotation costs a delivery a holder. *Why:* a full 1,000-leaf tree is 2.8 MB, which a per-epoch GroupInfo would rewrite about 143 times a day.

**D-KEYS-15 (proposed).** `gkm/<group_id>/gen/<g>`, created If-None-Match by the rotating writer, is the only place a generation is created, which a gen pack later holds verbatim (10.16); MLS commits never raise the generation, and a removal is a Remove commit followed by an independent rotation (10.5). *Why:* two paths minting g+1 fork the ladder; one claim object serializes every rotator (owner decisions [1](#od-1), [114](#od-114), [128](#od-128)).

**D-KEYS-16 (proposed).** KeyHolders are leaves (in the config and directory groups, member devices past their first 1,000 by wrap), uncovered agents, live Delegations over their reach (the config, a team's directory and the repos a grant names one of their tags for; a forwarding Delegation's, the config alone, its holder its sidecar's forwarding, which a newer one keeps; [owner decision 197](#od-197)) and recovery keys; live Delegations get DelegationWraps keyed by delegation_id; a covered agent's reap, or an ephemeral one's own `not_after`, is no shrink, and a Delegation's key drops at its end (§7.9's delegation row), at `not_after`, and at any other revocation but a reap, or any `Suspend`, of one of its agents, which no `Unsuspend` undoes (10.5). *Why:* [owner decision 114](#od-114)'s read-at-once, bounded, with no dropped party signing the rotation that excludes it; a suspended agent must lose what the server can still deliver to its Delegation's key, and an ephemeral agent can close itself, or api reap it, before any cutoff keyed to its own expiry.

**D-KEYS-17 (proposed).** Drop keys ride each generation's signed GenRotate, only for kinds that take deposits and for a general repo whose `RepoCreate` marks it a group or admin inbox (§8.5, §8.8), rotators setting `drop_public_key` and `drop_not_after_ms` for both; a depositor seals only to a generation that covers every shrink and expiry it knows and is not below its pin, and whose drop key is unexpired and lives at most `DropKeyLifetime` past its time ([owner decision 357](#od-357)); the deposit scope reaches only the drop-key route (10.6, 10.14). *Why:* a stale but unexpired drop key would reach a removed reader.

**D-KEYS-18 (proposed).** With MLS, Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), at most 16 leaves the epoch object carries the sealed GroupInfo and `group-info` is a pointer rewritten at each Add and by gkm with any epoch 16 or more past it, resync probing to a 404, and above 16 recovery and resync need one leaf online (10.6-10.8); in v0 and with MLS, KF1 writes the group's owner marker before its form (D-KEYS-27) and its first wraps, recovery wraps included, before evs activates the repo. *Why:* a crash between two PUTs must not break code-only recovery.

**D-KEYS-19 (proposed).** `gkm:<group_id>` is versioned epoch × 2^24 + generation, and work hints go on the per-client `gkm` topic of the sidecars that must act (10.14). *Why:* same-epoch work hints and commit-less rotations must not be dropped as stale.

**D-KEYS-20 (proposed).** Retention never deletes a group's newest epoch, moves the `group-info` pointer before deleting the epoch it names, and keeps every GenRotate for the repo's life, as a gen/ object or in a gen pack (10.6, 10.16). *Why:* the next commit needs its predecessor, and code-only recovery needs no epoch history.

**D-KEYS-21 (proposed).** gkm acks are Redis soft state, and the epoch reconciler deletes only while the ack family is 30 days old; a GroupInfo above 16 leaves is written at most once per epoch, on request. *Why:* acks are rebuildable ([owner decision 136](#od-136)), and a 1,000-leaf GroupInfo costs ~0.7 MB on each drive.

**D-KEYS-22 (proposed).** The search index's document keys derive from `ref` (RK_1), and its keyed pad from a per-generation `index` key that each shard's header names. In slot-keyed repos each versionless index file keeps one key, in a slot only that path's versions name, until a REMOVE generation, a CLOSURE or a rekey replaces it (§11.7). *Why:* document keys must survive rotations, or every rotation reindexes the repo; a removed reader must not predict new shards' sizes; and an ERASE must reach postings ([owner decision 61](#od-61)) without a slot object per index write ([owner decision 140](#od-140)).

**D-KEYS-23 (proposed).** In v0 the team directory's readers, member devices and agents alike, read it by per-generation wraps ([owner decision 610](#od-610)); with MLS, Later, its group follows §7.9's leaves rule as the config group does, the first 1,000 live member devices being leaves ([owner decision 182](#od-182)). An admission's signer seats its subject at once; gkm hints only the statement's signer and the config writers, and other writers rotate only for a push the gate refuses, after up to 15 s of jitter (10.9). *Why:* every admitted sidecar reads the directory, and §8.12's data-repo seats would leave members of a large Team keyless; every sidecar but read_only ones also writes it, so hinting every writer would race rotations that each stage a wrap per wrapped reader.

**D-KEYS-24 (proposed).** Every ReaderWrap and DelegationWrap is a typed `KeyDelivery` whose immutable identity, in its path `wrap/<g>/<c8>/<recipient>/<k8>`, its body and its wrap_aad, includes the recipient key it seals to, so a delivery to one ReaderKey never blocks, replaces or opens as one to another, and a rebind's RecoveryWraps take their binding's own path (10.6, 10.8). A STAGED delivery is its claim's and is judged against the claim's holder set; a LATE one, first or replacement, carries its signer's AuthPin and time, is judged at that state, may be signed by any holder that is not read_only, and stays valid after later revocations (10.9). *Why:* a fresh ReaderKey needs a delivery its old one's object cannot occupy, and a delivery made after its generation's claim needs its own authorization state, which neither the claim's pin nor a verifier's newer one gives.

**D-KEYS-25 (proposed).** A ReaderKey is valid at most 7 days after signing and replaced at 6 days, its private key kept 30 days past its not_after, and rotators and deliverers seal only to an unexpired one valid no longer than that; so a passive keychain copy heals at the first generation after the device's next path commit and that not_after, about 37 days after the copy (60 above 50 leaves) whatever advertisement gkm serves, and an active clone, which signs fresh keys, ends only at a compromise revocation and a new enrollment (10.5). *Why:* gkm serves one overwriteable advertisement with no authenticated retirement, so only the key's own validity bounds a stale one, and whoever holds an identity key can sign another.

**D-KEYS-26 (proposed).** gkm's routes take 10.6's scopes: a sidecar's own ReaderKey and KeyPackages under a gkm token of its own that holds an r, rw or admin scope on some repo, a token whose only repo scopes are deposit reaching the drop-key route alone; reads, acks and a member device's commits under r; GroupInfo and deliveries under r from a sidecar that is not read_only; claims, Welcomes and KeyPackage claims under rw; members, not gkm, check what a commit carries (10.9). *Why:* reader-only and read_only leaves must keep their keys and leaves current (D-TEAM-24), and gkm cannot see a PrivateMessage's proposals.

**D-KEYS-27 (proposed).** A group belongs to one repo from its first byte: `gkm/<group_id>/owner`, created If-None-Match by gkm from the token before the GroupForm at a creation or a re-form, names the repo through which alone gkm resolves the group, every group route requiring that repo among the token's scopes, and a form naming a group id another repo's marker holds answers 409 with nothing written (10.6, 10.14; [owner decision 201](#od-201); DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 6). *Why:* a form naming another repo's group would give a reader of that repo a write position in its group, and a LIST before the form leaves a race in which two newest forms name one group.

### 10.12 Open questions

**Q-KEYS-1.** [X12] Build MLS or fork it? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 43](#od-43)):** build 10.4's subset in house (~5-8k lines); its audit is [deferred](DESIGN-DEFER.md#trust-external-audit) ([owner decision 99](#od-99)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-2.** [X12] Which ciphersuite? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 44](#od-44)):** 0x0010 (X-Wing, Ed25519) from v0; groups migrate through the ladder if IANA assigns another value. *Residual:* post-quantum confidentiality against a passive adversary only; a future Ed25519 forgery is retroactive through the ladder (10.5, §2.18) until 10.16's hybrid signatures.

**Q-KEYS-3.** [X12] At what granularity are groups formed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 60](#od-60)):** per repo, grants mapping onto membership; agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-4.** [X12] What do "GKM" and "one session key stored in GKM" mean? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 59](#od-59)):** a DS plus wrapped, laddered generations (10.5) in the file cluster. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-5.** What admission evidence must a credential carry? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [3](#od-3), [5](#od-5), [110](#od-110)):** a config-repo `SidecarAdmit` chained to the genesis, subsuming DeviceAdmit; a member's own device may sign it ([owner decision 112](#od-112)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-6.** Is per-entry crypto-shredding required? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 61](#od-61)):** for record-class repos and mail, through format 1's key slots. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-7.** How does a member recover after losing every device? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 62](#od-62)):** a recovery code receiving wraps under a signed, rotatable binding, plus admin re-add of team repos (10.8); its key counts as one of k after a 72 h veto window ([owner decision 127](#od-127)); a binding the cascade restored admits only through that window, its device anchoring on a config ReaderWrap ([owner decision 149](#od-149)). *Residual:* §2.10's row for an operator colluding with a recovery-code thief: the code opens its wraps at once, whatever the window or a veto, and after a rebind or a cascade void stops new wraps keeps opening what was wrapped to it and reads the current generation until the next rotation, which `RecoveryRebind{reason: compromise}` makes a remove rotation with a path epoch at once (revoking the device it admitted does not retire it), and keychain backups sealed before a rebind stay open to the old code (10.8).

**Q-KEYS-8.** Should teams get escrow? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 63](#od-63)):** a visible audit reader on a customer-operated device, a Team opt-in in v1, never silent (10.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-9.** [X12] Does v0 ship MLS, or per-device wraps with MLS in v1? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 1](#od-1)):** MLS in v0 (PLAN.md:44); agents' wraps carry its generations ([owner decision 114](#od-114)). **Amended by owner 2026-11-17 ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), after the complexity review:** v0 distributes every group key by 10.5's `KeyDelivery` wraps alone and MLS is Later ([MLS](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-mls)), its drafted code dark on the branch; keeping MLS as planned, or keeping it with wrap-only config and directory groups, was not taken. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-10.** Is 10.8 the right reading of PLAN.md:50 and :338? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 64](#od-64)):** lazy rewrap, a full checkpoint at the first write after a `remove` generation, plus `ur evs rekey`. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-11.** How long does GKM keep epoch objects? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), 30 days, then until every leaf that acked in the last 30 days has applied them, on four conditions (10.6): the newest epoch is never deleted, and the `group-info` pointer moves before the epoch it names goes; nothing the ladder, resync or recovery needs lives in an epoch (generations are `gen/` objects, GroupInfo rides in the newest epoch at 16 leaves or fewer or in `group-info` above, and recovery wraps are their own objects), so a device past retention resyncs from GroupInfo; a preservation hold pauses the sweep ([owner decision 133](#od-133)); and §19.9 sizes the family at M2's benchmark: a 10-leaf group keeps about 42 commits of 11-17 KB plus inline GroupInfo (1.2-1.9 MB), a 1,000-leaf group about 26 MB. *Residual:* §19.9's measured size.

**Q-KEYS-12.** [X12; directive residual] Which header values does gkm see? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 115](#od-115)):** 10.6's rows: ciphertext, group id, epoch, sizes and sidecar ids (membership, as api-7 shows it; [owner decision 72](#od-72)), never, in a member commit, a proposal, credential change, tree or key; external commits show gkm-6's values. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-13.** Does [owner decision 7](#od-7)'s "only from keys allowed to grant" bind the committer or the change? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 113](#od-113)):** (b) the change (10.9), withdrawing D-KEYS-7. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-14.** Who commits the config group's membership changes, when only admins write config records (§8.8)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 128](#od-128)):** (a) also the leaf that signed the admission or revocation; recovery-admitted devices self-join by external commit (10.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-15.** How many member devices may one network hold, given the config group's 1,000-leaf cap? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)):** (b), with no member-device cap: from the start, member devices past the first 1,000 read the config group by per-generation wraps, as agents do, and stay leaves of their data repos, each still at most 1,000 leaves, amending [owner decision 114](#od-114) for the config group only; §20.4 keeps 5,000 Team admissions. §7.9's `leaves` rule ranks and promotes (10.4); wrapped devices commit no config-group Add or Remove, so a wrapped signer writes an admission's first wrap or a revocation's rotation, and the next leaf commit removes a leaf (10.9). Cost: ~1.3 KB of wrap per wrapped device per config rotation. *Residual:* none.

**Q-KEYS-16.** Cross-cutting (§7.9, §8.12). How does the team directory's group seat every admitted sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 182](#od-182)):** (a), its own MLS group under §7.9's leaves rule, extending [owner decision 144](#od-144) to one more group, at ~1.3 KB a wrap per overflow device per rotation (options (b), keys derived from the config group, and (c), data-repo seats, not taken). 10.4 and 10.9 apply it with the config group's committers, gkm hinting only a statement's signer and the config writers, since every sidecar but read_only ones writes the directory. *Residual:* none.

### 10.13 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:147** ("participants are leaves"). Member devices are leaves ([owner decision 60](#od-60)); agents hold wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114) on Q-ACL-9; D-KEYS-11), as do member devices past the first 1,000 in the config and team directory groups (owner decisions [144](#od-144) and [182](#od-182) on Q-KEYS-15 and Q-KEYS-16).
- **PLAN.md:148.** Per-object keys are wrapped under RK_g, which the epoch KEK or a holder's wrap delivers (Q-KEYS-4).
- **PLAN.md:221.** Narrowed by the owner directive: gkm holds ciphertext plus 10.6's header values (Q-KEYS-12).
- **PLAN.md:223, :284-327.** Proxy re-encryption is rejected (10.10).

### 10.14 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `GkmClient` (`CurrentRepoKey`, `RepoKey(repoId, generation)`, `EnsureWritable`, which first commits the pending changes its device may, `DropKey`); `EvsRepoKey.DeriveKey(purpose, context)`; credential validation and pins (also for §6's `Hello`); GenRotates and drop keys, ReaderWraps and DelegationWraps (`KeyDelivery`, 10.5) with 10.9's delivery checks, and recovery wraps; 10.5's KeyHolders and 10.6's gate predicate (§7.9, §11.8, §11.12); each group's owner marker, the one binding of a group to its repo (D-KEYS-27).
- **Consumes:** keys, bindings, keychain, recovery code, `SidecarEvent` (§5); topics, `Signed`, `HeadCheck` (§6); tokens, `rev/` (§7.8); the authorization log, `AuthPin`, causal identities, recovery, the `leaves` rule and removals (§7.9, §7.10); `RepoReaders`, seats, kind defaults, consent, `OwnerConfirm`, access logs, `audit`, `EvsShare`, and the gate cache with its network list, sidecar index and install callback (§8, §8.9); kinds, `repo/` state, `place/`, slots, manifests, path epochs, the head-CAS gate and the write budget (§11); `ServiceHost.Blobs` per cluster and Redis (§4.5, §19).
- **Subprotocol messages:** `GkmHint{group_id, epoch, kind, recipient}` in `PushHint` (§6.11, 0x1301), numbered 1 to 4 in that order, `epoch` a uint64, `kind` a `GkmHintKind` (COMMIT 1, PENDING 2, WELCOME 3, KEY_PACKAGES_LOW 4, WRAP_PENDING 5) and `recipient` bytes in the wrap path's `s:` or `d:` form: commit on `gkm:<group_id>` (version = epoch × 2^24 + generation); pending, welcome, key-packages-low and wrap-pending (a GenWrap, wrap or sealed GroupInfo is missing; for 10.6's late wraps, `recipient` names the ask's `s:` or `d:` recipient, and a hint lost or coalesced comes again at the next ask) on the per-client `gkm` topic (§6.8).
- **API routes:** Client class, under 10.6's tokens and scopes, specified in connect/api/bringyour.yml.

  ```text
  POST /gkm/key-packages                       bare KeyPackages, whose own extensions say which is last-resort
  POST /gkm/key-packages/claim                 a KeyPackage of the target for the group, 404 when it holds none
  POST /gkm/reader-key;  GET /gkm/reader-key/<sidecar_id>
  POST /gkm/reader-keys                        up to 256 sidecar_ids: each one's Signed ReaderKey, or an empty
                                               Signed, in order, under GET reader-key's scope
  PUT|GET /gkm/delegation-keys/<delegation_id> a forwarding Delegation's reader key (owner decision 202)
  POST /gkm/delegation-keys                    up to 256 delegation_ids: each stored key, or none, in order,
                                               under the GET's scope (owner decision 364)
  POST /gkm/groups                             creation (KF1): the Signed GroupForm, epoch 0's GenWrap_0 and
                                               sealed GroupInfo, and gen/1's Signed GenRotate, written after the
                                               owner marker in that order, each If-None-Match, equal bytes
                                               answering success; 409 on other bytes, a group id another
                                               repo's marker holds answering 409 at the marker with nothing
                                               written (D-KEYS-27)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>                        the GroupForm that names the group, and nothing else
  GET  /gkm/repos/<id>/forms                   r, rw, admin: the repo's Signed GroupForms, oldest first
  POST /gkm/repos/<id>/forms                   admin: a re-form only (10.8), writing the new group's owner
                                               marker first; 409 on other bytes, and at the marker for a group
                                               id another repo's marker holds (D-KEYS-27)
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/ladder                 admin: a re-formed group's old Signed GenRotates, at most 64 a
                                               call, before its epoch/1 (10.8)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs?after=          epoch objects, in order, with their sizes, to gkm's bound, a
                                               client asking again after its last until none comes
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/epochs/<n>             200, 409 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/gen/<g>                the claim: 201, 412 (with the winner), 403, 429
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/wraps/<g>/<c8>         a batch of 1 to 256 staged or late ReaderWraps and
                                               DelegationWraps: 200, each item's 201, 412 (with the winner),
                                               403, 409 (stale kind, generation or key), 429 or 0 (not tried)
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/recovery-wraps/<g>/<c8>  a rotator's 1 to 256 RecoveryWraps, answered as a wrap batch
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/welcome/<n>            the Welcome, naming each recipient's sidecar_id beside its ref
  HEAD /gkm/groups/<id>/welcome/<n>            rw: 200 or 404, no body, whether epoch n's Welcome stands (owner
                                               decision 372)
  POST /gkm/groups/<id>/group-info (409 when its epoch does not rise), /ack (Redis)
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/gen?since=             GenRotates, in order, to gkm's bound, as the epochs route
  GET  /gkm/welcomes                           each pointer with its Welcome, which no other route serves
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/wraps/<g>?recipient=&want=<k8>&since=   the caller's deliveries of g, the object at
                                               want first, the recipient's prefix on a miss, which hints
                                               wrap-pending (10.6's late wraps)
  GET  /gkm/repos/<id>/drop-key?since=<g>      deposit, r, rw, admin: the newest GenRotate of the repo's newest
                                               GroupForm's group, up to 64 after since; api reads it for §14.8's
                                               report intake under a deposit token it issues itself
  GET  /gkm/groups/<id>/group-info?want=<epoch>  sealed; an older one also hints wrap-pending (KF5)
  GET|POST|DELETE /gkm/recovery/<member_id>/wraps  GET also under an unadmitted client's recovery:<member_id>,
                                                   for that member's own wraps only (§7.8, §7.9); POST, a
                                                   rebind's re-wrap, 201 or 412; DELETE ?binding=<b8>
  ```

  Each body is a protocol/gkm.proto message or a bare `Signed`, as `application/octet-stream`, as §6.8's `PollResponse` is.
- **Tables:** none; gkm's durable state is 10.6's objects (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [21](#od-21), [145](#od-145)), and Redis `{gka_<group_id>}` holds acks as soft state ([owner decision 136](#od-136)). §6.8's per-client hints need a client id for each `sidecar_id`: gkm, which reads no Postgres, resolves them through api's internal `POST /sidecar/identity/clients` behind the `Push.HintSidecars` seam, with a 5-minute map in each process, and counts and passes over a failed call, the hourly resync covering a lost hint (§5.15).
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/gkm` hosts `gkmservice` from v0; root `mls_*` and `gkm_*` files and the nested `mlsinterop/` test module (D-REPO-2, D-REPO-3, D-OPS-2); the reconciler (retention, hints, staged-wrap GC) in taskworker; limits in config/all/pro.yml.
- **Assumptions about other sections:**
  - §7.9 defines the authorization log, `AuthPin`, the causal identities (a compromise retirement shrinks though a rebind keeps the holder's identity; ReaderKey lapses are no expiry, 10.5) and `holders_shrunk_at`, `RecoveryBind` and its reasons, `stale_leaf_days`, Delegations, the recovery window, `anchor` and `restored` order, the compromise cascade, the Delegations it voids and the bindings it restores, which take no wrap until re-signed, the Delegations it or a `DelegationRevoke` ends, parking their agents admitted from `since_n`, the scoped rule giving each Delegation-signed admission exactly the Delegation's tags and, unless ephemeral, a not_after no earlier than its own, with `max_admits` counted for the Delegation's life, and the `leaves` rule of the config and directory groups, refusing a not_after on a member device's admission; §7.8 gives member devices other than read_only ones gkm `rw` in the config group, every sidecar but read_only ones `rw` in the team directory, and issues the `deposit` and `recovery:<member_id>` scopes; §7.10 and §8.12 name 10.9's committers, §7.10 also the reaped agent's admission signer, §8.12 the data repos' seats, which the directory does not take, and §8.5 consent and the directory kind default (every admitted sidecar of a team network reads, every one not read_only writes; §16.11), and §8.6's ceiling passes the config kind default's read row, so ephemeral sidecars read the config as 10.5's depositor rule needs; §7.9's read_only row accepts a read_only device's own ReaderKeys, KeyPackages, path-only commits, resyncs and acks under its r scopes and refuses its wraps and GroupInfo (10.6's scopes), and §5.9 keeps ReaderKeys and their private keys as 10.5's readerkey row says; §5.4 alarms on admissions a member's devices did not sign and raises `head_alarm` (fork) on a failed recovery anchor, and §5.9 has each device re-seal `keychain.wrap` at every change to its member's current binding, a void included, with no HPKE copy while none is current.
  - §11.8 enforces 10.6's predicate at each ref's head CAS, reissuing a timed-out head PUT only within 5 s of its validation, owns `place/` and lists the first cluster's families, gkm's per-sidecar objects included; §11 owns path epochs (authorization expiries batched within 24 h), §11.7's checkpoint after a REMOVE generation, deletion (its shred deleting the group's gkm objects and `{gka_}`, again after 10 min; a re-seed's GroupForm the only gkm route it admits while deleted), mirrors, re-seeding and §11.13's write budget, whose inputs count expiry rotations and path epochs; §19.6 sets the 10 s store request deadline; §19.9 sizes gkm's objects, gen/ unpacked until 10.16's packs start, expiry rotations, the config and directory groups' rotation wraps and the first cluster's per-sidecar ones included.
  - §11.14 derives search-index document keys under `ref` and shard pads under `index` through `EvsRepoKey.DeriveKey`, keeps each index file's key in its path's own slot in slot-keyed repos (§11.7), and destroys an erased document's index files' old slot keys by its ERASE.
  - §22.7 covers 10.5-10.9's cases, the gate's 412 (a compromise rebind's at the old generation included), an expired RepoGrant's REMOVE rotation, checkpoint and path epoch (FS-18), gkm accepting a generation-0 recovery self-join, a reap's config rotation by the admission's signer, an admin-only admission never reading its member's vault or mailbox, a recovery self-join with no leaf online, FS-20 also killing KF1's creator before activation and gkm between an epoch 16 past the pointer and the pointer's rewrite, a 1,001st member device reading the config and the team directory by wrap, the directory group's hint audience and rotation wait (10.9) and FS-87's directory Removes and rotation reaching leaves and wraps, and a Team member whose only device was stolen recovering by the restored code, its device anchoring after the window on its config ReaderWrap (a forged one raising `head_alarm`), then self-joining, KF2 adding it elsewhere; FS-6 holds a gkm commit at a barrier across a --now shred and restores a repo re-seeded as deleted; FS-103 to FS-106 test delivery identity, delivery authority, copied keychains and key upkeep under r; §22.8's M2 benchmark measures 10.6's sizes and drive costs, a 1,000-leaf group on the iOS surrogate cell and 1 h requested grants on large repos included; its schedules lose the ack family and race a repo's placement, its group landing on the repo's cluster.

### 10.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The unreviewed in-house MLS misreads RFC 9420 or skips a check ([owner decision 99](#od-99)) | Medium | Critical | 10.4's subset, conformance plan and 0x0010 gate; disclosure (§2.18, [owner decision 119](#od-119)) |
| IANA assigns this suite another value, or X-Wing changes | Medium | Medium | Migration through GroupForm and the ladder ([owner decision 44](#od-44)) |
| An operator substitutes a network's first device at trust on first use | Low | High | Safety numbers; genesis in invites and auth keys |
| Every app device's forwarding Delegation adds a DelegationWrap of about 1.2 KB to each config rotation, about 6 MB at a 5,000-device team's ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) | High | Low | config rotations follow removals and the 30-day schedule, not rule edits; a newer forwarding Delegation is no shrink (10.5) |
| A copied forwarding reader key opens the config generations wrapped to it until its Delegation ends | Low | Medium | it never leaves the VPN component (§5.9); the app rotates it at every new client generation and after 90 days; `DelegationRevoke` shrinks the config at once (10.5) |
| A member stalls a group with a commit the others refuse | Low | Medium | Alarms; revocation; re-forming (10.9) |
| A rogue or compromised admin admits a device under a member | Medium | High | §8.18's row, whose consent 10.9's refusals hold ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); team repos stay readable until revocation |
| A removed leaf stays in a repo's MLS tree until a writer leaf commits its Remove (owner decisions [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)) | Medium | Low | Wrapped writers' rotations reopen the gate meanwhile, and no leaf wrap uses an epoch that holds it (10.5); hints wake writer leaves |
| A reaped Delegation-admitted agent, an ephemeral one past its own `not_after`, or a leaked reader seed reads later config, directory and tag-repo generations, and a leaked whole auth key admits fresh agents ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | Medium | High | `not_after` ≤ 90 d (30 d for CI), replaced at each CI secret rotation and after a key drop; any `Suspend` or non-reap revocation of its agents, or a cascade voiding it, drops the key; its admissions stop at its end (10.5, §7.9's delegation row) |
| Large groups strain phones (10.6's sizes); a large Team's leaves sit in two 1,000-leaf groups, the config's and the directory's | Medium | Medium | D-KEYS-14, the engine keeping trees on disk and streaming them ([owner decision 366](#od-366)); §22.8's benchmark |
| Short grants (1 h requested grants) expire often, and each covering generation is REMOVE, so files re-checkpoint at their next write and a repo's batched path epoch recurs daily, ~17 h of copying for a 1M-file ref (§11.6) | Medium | Medium | One rotation covers every expiry up to its time_ms, and writers batch them at a pending hint or their next write (KF4); 16-diff chains checkpoint anyway; at most one batched path epoch per repo a day (§11.6); §11.13's inputs and §19.9's gen/ row count these rotations and epochs, and §22.8's fixture of 1 h requested grants on large repos reports rotations, full checkpoints and path-epoch copy operations a day |
| A config or directory rotation stages a wrap per wrapped reader and a RecoveryWrap per member, up to ~6,000 objects (~7.5 MB, ~50 MiB a drive) at §20.4's 5,000 Team admissions, and a wrap per leaf more if its rotator is wrapped; the directory, whose writers push often, rotates at nearly every shrink of a Team's sidecars, and racing rotators would multiply each | Medium | Low | A leaf rotator's one LeafWrap covers every leaf; covered agents' reaps rotate nothing (10.5); the directory group hints only a statement's signer and the config writers, and unhinted writers rotate after a jitter (10.9); §11.13 runs REMOVE rotations at once as P0, never refusing them, so many large Teams shrinking at once can wear a cluster's drives past the budget ([owner decision 186](#od-186); §11.21's P0 row), and §19.9's projection counts both groups' rotations |
| With no witness, shared writes stop at `witness_bound_hours` (default 72 h), a lone cloud agent's included (§2.8's bound, which a split defeats) | Medium | Medium | Agents witness ([owner decision 129](#od-129)); 24 h alarm; up to 168 h; Removes, rotations and revocations never stop |
| After a void leaves M no binding, M loses every device before one of them binds a fresh code: no code of M's admits a device, so only an admin's admission brings one back, parked for M's owner-bound repos, and in a network where M is the only admin nothing does ([owner decision 592](#od-592)) | Low | High | M's devices raise `recovery_rebind` at the void (§5.4), and any of them can run `ur keychain recovery-rotate` (§5.9) at once to bind a fresh code that takes wraps (10.8) |
| A device offline past its ReaderKey's 7-day not_after gets no staged wrap and, back with a new key, waits for a late delivery, longer where no writer is online | Medium | Low | Lapsed private keys kept 30 days for what was staged (10.5); any holder but a read_only one delivers, gkm hinting writers, then after 15 min up to 64 other holders (10.6); a leaf also takes the next GenWrap |
| An active clone of a keychain (its identity key and ClientKey) reads and acts as the device past any path commit or ReaderKey replacement | Low | High | `SidecarRevoke{reason: compromise}` from a since_n before the copy, whose cascade parks what it admitted, and a new enrollment (10.5, 10.8); each device's daily check of the ReaderKey gkm serves under its id raises `key_changed` for one it never signed ([owner decision 358](#od-358)); the 37-day heal is a passive copy's (§2.10) |
| Site loss erases every gkm object ([owner decision 94](#od-94)) | Low | Critical | Device re-seed (D-KEYS-13); owner-device mirrors |

### 10.16 Phasing

- **v0 (M2):** all of 10.4-10.9 but v1's items and MLS, which is Later ([owner decision 610](#od-610)), every group key going by `KeyDelivery` wraps, with `directory` among `ur_group`'s kinds (§11.12), D-KEYS-10's gates, D-KEYS-14's scaling and `ur evs rekey`, a client job that re-checkpoints every file of a repo under the current generation in multi-part pushes of at most 1,024 entry writes, at most 50 files/s per repo, resumable from its last committed push. On a git-mode ref a rekey is a REKEY push (§11.7): the same job, any writer's device ([owner decision 540](#od-540)).
- **v1:** the Team audit reader ([owner decision 63](#od-63)), and with Team at M6 the config group's wraps for member devices past the first 1,000 ([owner decision 144](#od-144)) and the team directory's group under the same leaves rule ([owner decision 182](#od-182)); at M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), the `index` purpose, with storage format 2's search index ([owner decision 163](#od-163); §11.14), and format 2's one slot key per versionless path (§11.7).
- **Later:** [MLS](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-mls), its subset, groups, commits and the leaves rule, with its drafted code dark ([owner decision 610](#od-610)); [0x0020 by migration](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-suite-0x0020-hybrid-signatures), with hybrid Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 authority signatures; [SafeExportSecret](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-safe-export-secret) (draft-ietf-mls-extensions-11); [key transparency](DESIGN-DEFER.md#trust-key-transparency); moving a group with its repo once [a move tool](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-repo-move-tool) exists ([owner decision 145](#od-145)); [gen packs](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-gen-packs), once §19.9's projection from §22.8's M2 count needs them: taskworker writes `gkm/<group_id>/genpack/<k>`, holding gen/<256k+1>..<256k+256> verbatim, If-None-Match with repo/ rechecked as for every gkm write, once 64 newer generations exist, then deletes those objects, a retry that finds the pack verifying it and resuming the deletes; a read falls back from `gen/<g>`'s 404 to `genpack/<⌊(g-1)/256⌋>`, and a claim still needs `gen/<g-1>` as an object, so none lands at or below a pack; packs count as gen/ for every other rule (gkm-7's life of the repo, shreds and their 10-minute repeat, re-seeds) and hold no slot, so erasure is unchanged.
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Dependencies:** §7.9's authorization log and config repo, §8.5's consent, §11's format 1 and §19's conditional writes block v0; §22.8's M2 benchmark sets §19.9's epoch-retention size (Q-KEYS-11's residual).

## 11. Encrypted versioned storage: format, git service, head API, subscriptions

### 11.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns evs repos and kinds, `config` and `directory` included; the format and what the server sees (X2, [owner decision 2](#od-2)); the file-cluster objects, their placement and the push, commit and read protocols; refs and their modes, record streams and deposits; git compatibility and the local tier (X19, [owner decision 24](#od-24)); subscriptions; per-object versioning, the versionless purge and the drop-history action (11.7, 11.13; [owner decision 173](#od-173)); GC and evacuation, the metadata write budget and fair share, quotas, durability, deletion and export; and the encrypted search index's placement, format, upkeep, erasure and read path, with remote search, an app host's "search more" answered end to end by a designated indexer (11.14; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)), whose search tools are §16's and §18's.

Keys come from §10, identity from §5, push from §6, tokens, the projection and grants from §7 and §8, hardware from §19 (X13), quotas from §20 and layouts from §15 and §16. The metadata clusters also store, and 11.13 budgets, §7's `proj/`, `projrows/` and `rev/`, §10's `gkm/` and §21's `hold/` objects.
