| R-EVS-26 | A repo admin can drop a path's history on a file-mode ref in v1: a signed action held 7 days for any repo admin to cancel, deleting only content that the dropped versions alone name, keeping every statement, hash and the head, and deferred silently under a hold | owner decisions [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183), [184](#od-184) |

### 11.3 What exists today

- **No code** exists for evs or a git server [R:server-platform](design/design-research/server-platform.md) §5.10.
- **BlobStore** has an overwriting Put (server/blob.go:674-679), PutIfAbsent as one If-None-Match request (:683-697), whole-object Get, List and SetLifecycle, but "deliberately no Delete", no ranged read and no streamed put (:155-183).
- **MinIO.** The deployed build (§19.3) checks If-Match and If-None-Match under its namespace lock but proceeds when that read loses quorum (minio@v0.0.0-20251015172955-9e49d5e7a648 cmd/erasure-object.go:1261-1279); PR #21653, merged 2025-10-24, fixes it, and [owner decision 18](#od-18)'s clusters build from the final upstream source (§19.6). MinIO verifies `x-amz-checksum-sha256` before an object exists (cmd/object-handlers.go:1993-2006) and inlines shards of up to 128 KiB in xl.meta (internal/config/storageclass/storage-class.go:278-294). It stores an object as a directory and lists that directory as one object without descending (cmd/metacache-walk.go:239-264). Names are at most 1,024 B (cmd/object-api-utils.go:197-203). xl.meta up to 4 KiB is written O_DSYNC, and larger ones with O_DIRECT and fdatasync (cmd/xl-storage.go:2247-2285). An overwrite also writes the previous xl.meta, inline data included, as a backup until quorum (:2784-2800, :2874-2887). With several pools, a PUT picks its pool by free space even when its key lives in another pool, and checks its precondition only there (cmd/erasure-server-pool.go:637-656; cmd/erasure-object.go:1261-1285). Upstream's DELETE evaluates no precondition (cmd/object-handlers.go:2563-2671; cmd/object-api-options.go:273-318), so an If-Match sent with it is ignored; §19.6's in-house build honors one condition of its own, `x-ur-if-unmodified-ms`, under the key's lock ([owner decision 225](#od-225)). A LIST asks a set's online drives and returns a key that half of those asked hold (cmd/metacache-set.go:728-733), so with three of eight drives offline it can leave out a key that five took; the in-house build answers such a LIST 503 ([owner decision 226](#od-226)). A cancel stops a PUT on the handling host's own drives before their commit rename (cmd/xl-storage.go:2891-2893) but reaches no drive operation on another host, whose storage RPCs run under context.Background() (cmd/storage-rest-server.go:366, :708; internal/grid/handlers.go:294), and the handler's deferred unlock frees the object's lock while they run on (cmd/erasure-object.go:1269), so a cancelled write can land after a later request on its key, and holding the lock to the 30 s drive timeout would still release a commit stalled after its last check; §19.6's in-house build (D-OPS-20) closes both with its deadline and settle rules.
- **lb.** `client_max_body_size 16m` is global (warp/warpctl/config.go:1301); `streamable_paths` (warp/services/services.go:694-701) get 60 s timeouts and no request buffering (warp/warpctl/config.go:2311-2319).
- **Crypto and clients.** x/crypto v0.54.0 (connect/go.mod:30) has XChaCha20-Poly1305 (chacha20poly1305/xchacha20poly1305.go:24) and no AES-SIV. Clients are reaped after 30+30 idle days (server/model/network_client_model.go:4179, :4199), so the durable signer is §5's `sidecar_id`.

### 11.4 Architecture

```text
git, harnesses        sidecar daemon                                  evs (stateless)             file cluster (§19.6)
 push/fetch ------->  local git server (http, ssh), git-remote-ur     tokens verified offline     metadata clusters (NVMe); a
                      bare repo; sealed mirror of evs objects         head CAS: tip on git refs,  repo lives on the one its
 MCP tools -------->  sync engine --segments, signed pushes, HTTPS--> path-level on file refs --> place/ names: repo/ head/
 apps (head mode) ->  EvsClient  <--PushHint evs:<repo_id> (§6)-----  batches; lazy index folds   log/ pb/ idx/ slot/ hp/ pmap/
                      keys: §10 RK_g -> path, ref, manifest, fek      hints via §6's Redis        pidx/ drops/ gkm/; the first also
                                                                      Redis: hints, leases, push  place/ proj/ projrows/ rev/
                                                                      sequence, head cache        hold/, per-sidecar gkm/
                                                                      usage events -> §20         segment cluster (HDD):
                                                                      write budget, fair share    seg/ pack/ dropscan/
```

evs never parses git, holds no key (I-1) and keeps no Postgres or durable Redis state; Redis carries §6's hints and rebuildable soft state: leases, the push sequence, drop hints, a verified head cache (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [17](#od-17), [136](#od-136)). Its one queue, of versionless purges due a minute after their replacement, lives in each process's memory, and evacuation's sweep covers its loss (11.13).

### 11.5 X2: what the server sees

[Owner decision 2](#od-2) settles X2's residual (Q-EVS-1): the server sees exactly §2.8's evs rows, one per 11.8 family: each ref's token tree, push DAG, pins and per-file changes (token, time, uploader, Padmé-padded size), each client's reads and subscribed prefixes, and which pushes one evs process batched. It never sees names, contents, messages, authors, branch or display names, agent ids or entry sequence numbers, nor links equal content across or within repos (per-repo keys, random nonces, records reused only for renames and merges). It also sees each file version's versioning setting (11.7), which content rides staged inside a push, and when the purge deletes a replaced versionless version's content, about a minute after the replacement commits, staged content with its batch, at most 26 h (11.13); each drop's token-path lineages, listed entry hashes, window, cancel, the deletions its job makes and admins' dry runs (§2.8's evs-12, evs-28); of a git-mode push, its flags and changes, how many of its parts hold no change and the padded size of the history it carried, never its commits, its tips or the other refs it names as sources (11.7, §2.8's evs-4); and, in a team directory, when each sidecar's card and each request's notice change, never their contents (evs-27). Of the search index it sees only shape and fetch times (11.14's server rows), never a query, a match, or which trigrams documents share, and nothing of a remote search (§2.8's connect-5).

**Token leak bound.** A token alone shows only its place in the tree. With the server's help, a key holder can test guessed names created before the path epoch that drops it (11.6), which every drop of a key holder, a member's, a member device's, a compromise and an authorization expiry alike, makes due within 24 h, or, while two source epochs stand, once one drops (11.6's commit row), each landing when a mapper commits (writers alarm an hour past due, not while such an epoch waits), names created meanwhile included, since no due holds a new name ([owner decision 585](#od-585), which reversed owner decisions [229](#od-229), [414](#od-414) and [569](#od-569)); the token of a name first sent within 5 s of a cut-over, which can reach the server under the epoch just left (11.6's read row); and guessed branch names for the repo's life, since ref ids stay keyed from RK_1. A new ref starts in the newest path epoch its creator holds ([owner decision 232](#od-232)), so no new ref's first names are tokenized under a removed key. Contents stay sealed throughout. A Delegation's reader key counts as dropped only when §10.5's live(d) ends, at one of the drops §10.5 lists. Holders follow files they knew through the map.

### 11.6 Format: keys, tokens, records, segments

**Keys** are §10.5's `fek`, `manifest`, `drop`, `path` (tokens of path epoch p, from RK_p), `ref` (ref ids and the search index's document keys, from RK_1, since ref ids name every `head/` and `log/` key and a document's key must not change at a rotation) and `index` (the search index's keyed pad, per generation; 11.14).

**Tokens:**

```text
names    name_i is the path component's raw bytes as git stores them, never normalized, so NFC and NFD names are
         distinct paths, as in git
tokens   t_i = HMAC-SHA256(K_path_p, t_{i-1} || name_i)[:16], t_0 = 16 zero bytes, K_path_p = HKDF-SHA256(RK_p, salt
         repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 path" || u64be(p)); 26 base32 characters in keys; at most 32 components, keeping
         keys within MinIO's 1,024 B; the root is a directory whose token path is empty in every epoch, which a
         change names only for a directory delta and a read names in any epoch with no token (owner decision 231);
         deposit and erasure refs, in every kind, whose writers hold no path key or need none, name entries by
         random 16 B ids under no K_path
ref ids  ref_id = HMAC-SHA256(K_ref, "ref" || ref name bytes)[:16], K_ref = HKDF-SHA256(RK_1, salt repo_id, info
         "UR evs 1.0 ref" || u64be(1)), so any reader derives head/<repo>/<ref> for `main`; a ref's name bytes are
         <b> for refs/heads/<b>, the whole refs/tags/<t> for a tag, and the bare name for every other ref (main,
         ur/<sidecar_id>/…, <sidecar_id> as Id.String() there, record streams' included (owner decision 406),
         ur/index, ur/lfs, cards), as sealed_ref_name holds them, so a reader maps a listed ref
         back, the local tier refusing a branch whose short name starts with refs/; deposit refs: the first 16 B of
         SHA-256(repo_id || sidecar_id); the erasure ref: the first 16 B of SHA-256("UR evs 1.0 erasure" ||
         repo_id), so no writer squats its name, evs refusing any other ref kind at that id and an erasure ref
         kind at any other (409 REF_MODE)
leaks    K_path is per repo, so one path has one token on every ref of a repo in one epoch (overlays need this);
         ref ids stay keyed from RK_1, so a removed holder can test guessed branch names for the repo's life
         (11.5, §2.8's evs-2)
```

**Path epochs ([owner decision 2](#od-2) item 9)** are named by the generation p that derives K_path. A ref starts in the epoch its first push names ([owner decision 232](#od-232)): a ref that is no overlay in the newest generation at or below the push's that its creator holds whose GenRotate cause is REMOVE, else 1, so no new ref's first names are tokenized under a removed key; an overlay in its base ref's current epoch, so overlay and base share token paths; deposit and erasure refs in 1 for life (below). On a ref with no head, 5e accepts any p with 1 <= p <= the push's generation, which the new head takes as its current epoch with no sources and no due below p (11.8):

```text
due      the first commit whose generation pin crosses a REMOVE generation (§10.5: it covers a shrink, an
         authorization expiry or a compromise retirement, §7.9; a reap of an agent its live Delegation covers is
         none) records it in head.path_epoch.due with due_by_ms 24 h after that commit, a due already recorded
         keeping its earlier due_by_ms and taking the newer generation; every due is batched, whatever drop or
         expiry it covers, a member's or a member device's removal and a compromise retirement included (owner
         decision 585, which reversed owner decisions 229, 414 and 569): nothing classes a crossing, no due holds a
         creation or a new name, in the push that crosses it or after, a refusal records no due, and
         due_blocks_creation stays in the format unused, evs writing it false and every reader reading past it;
         until the epoch lands, a removed holder can test the names created meanwhile under the current epoch
         (11.5), so the block (below) is the only creation refusal a due brings; writers alarm 1 h past
         due_by_ms, a REMOVE generation no head has recorded falling due, for a device that holds it, 24 h after it
         first held it, but not while the commit row defers the epoch, which §19.8 reports, nor within 1 h of that
         deferral's end
random   deposit and erasure refs name entries by random ids (tokens, above): evs records no due on them, sets
         no block, refuses a PATH_EPOCH there (409 REF_MODE) and keeps them at path epoch 1 for life, so
         depositors and CONSUME pushes declare 1
map      the writer that rotates, or any writer holding every name of the ref (a full-sync device, or a mobile mirror
         of under 100,000 names), wrapped agents included (owner decision 114), uploads Signed EvsPathMap parts, each
         by POST .../path-epoch with EvsPathMapRequest {path_map_sha256 1, part 2} (owner decision 408), for
         the newest generation p_new to pmap/<repo>/<ref>/<p_new>/<path_map_sha256>/<k>/_: the root's move first, an
         empty path in each epoch and no sealed name (owner decision 231), then per live path its token path in
         p_new, in the current epoch and in each listed source at or above the epoch its standing creation
         committed in, or its row's (the server was shown its token there; a source below it never held the
         path), and its name re-sealed for the new parent and child tokens, moves ascending by new token path
         within and across parts; the map binds its source head (map_source_version, map_source_chain), any version
         at or below the head (commit, below); keys name the map, and a mapper keeps its built parts and a job
         record on disk, resuming an interrupted upload from them, so no nonce is drawn twice, and builds a fresh
         map only when its PATH_EPOCH answers 409 MAP_SOURCE or its oldest part passes 20 h, under the 24 h evs
         takes (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 9); once p or a newer epoch commits, taskworker deletes p's
         uncommitted maps, and the nightly pass deletes a map above the head's epoch once 11.13's horizon has passed
         its oldest part's LastModified + 24 h + 2 min, each part by a DELETE naming its LastModified (owner decision
         203)
tail     paths that versions after the map's source create, through the PATH_EPOCH push's base, get moves like
         the map's, removed ones included, which the mapper builds from those pushes, their sources naming the
         current epoch alone: the PATH_EPOCH push carries them in its payload under path_tail_sha256, and evs checks
         every token path the window's versions after the source create (base_entry_version 0) against them, else
         409 naming the paths; creations between an older source and the window are the mapper's to cover, which
         the copy's end LIST and replaying readers catch (owner decision 228); so a creation costs the mapper a
         longer tail, never a fresh map; a reader opens each sealed name and record of an unfolded version with the
         keys of the generation its own statement names, never the epoch's or a tail move's p_new, so a creation of
         a newer generation that a tail carried reads through its source before the copy runs, and every
         committed version stays readable across any cut-over (owner decision 381)
block    10 min past due_by_ms, a mapper may stop creation for at most 2 min, at most once each 10 min: POST
         .../path-epoch/block, an EvsPathEpochBlockRequest {ref_id 1, ms 2 <= 120,000} (owner decision 408), sets
         head.path_epoch.block_until_ms by one head CAS that raises only the fence (11.8); until it passes, a push
         creating a path gets 412 PATH_EPOCH_DUE after a fence (11.8's refuse row), which writers wait out, so the
         mapper's tail stops growing and its epoch commits on a ref with steady creation; it is the one creation
         refusal a due brings and 412 PATH_EPOCH_DUE's one use (owner decision 585); evs refuses a block while two
         sources stand, since the commit row defers the epoch
commit   a PATH_EPOCH push (file and git mode alike; it carries no git commit, and in git mode it takes TIP like
         every push, its mapper re-signing on a newer head or, on a busy ref, first taking the seal lease) commits
         if its map's parts exist, each under 24 h old, path_map_sha256 matches, its source is a version at or
         below the head whose statement and chain evs reads from the window or that version's log page (one cached
         GET of at most 70 KiB) and which declares the head's current epoch, so no PATH_EPOCH lies between (owner
         decision 228), else 409 MAP_SOURCE, its tail covers every creation the window holds after that version,
         and its own process's fold left nothing unfolded (11.7 (4)); the head then makes p_new current, lists the
         old current epoch first among the sources and clears due and the block; every due being batched, an epoch
         waits, 412 EPOCH_SOURCES_FULL, while two sources stand, with no block and no map built meanwhile, covering
         every removal and expiry due when it lands, so a head lists two sources at most, though the format holds
         three (owner decision 585); pushes declaring an older epoch get 412 PATH_EPOCH, part and seal checks
         included, and re-tokenize (read, below)
copy     one taskworker job per ref, for the newest map and its tail only, as P2 work (11.13), first hashing the
         map's parts against the head's map_sha256 and checking their order, moving nothing and alarming on a
         mismatch (owner decision 230), then running the moves in descending token-path order, so a directory moves
         after its children and the root last (owner decision 231): each move reads the entry from the
         newest source holding it, keeps its folded versions and drop mark (11.7), rewrites a directory's name table
         from its children's moves, matching each row in that row's own epoch, PUTs the new entry (If-None-Match,
         carried) and deletes
         every source copy; on 412 a file, or a removed or fresh entry (11.7), is done, its source copies deleted
         (a source marker's carried ids first put in an orphan marker, 11.7's orphan row)
         unmoved, and a carried directory's carried rows are translated and the entry PUT If-Match, read again on
         412; after each PUT it HEADs the path's prefixes in the current epoch and, finding one removed or fresh,
         turns what it put into a marker (If-Match on that PUT's ETag, 11.7; on 412 the newer entry stands); at most
         50 operations a second per repo, 150 while two or more sources stand, and 250 in all on the repo's metadata
         cluster, its taskworker processes together through {nvb_<set>} (each cluster's copies spend that cluster's
         P2 budget, 11.13), up to 1,000 while A1 left a quarter of T unspent over the last minute; jobs whose ref
         holds the most sources run first, then the one with the oldest source; each job reports the moves it has
         left, §19.8's copy liability; it rereads the head at least every 5 s (11.7's stale rule) and stops when a
         newer map supersedes its own; at the end it LISTs
         idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p_i>/ for each source, deletes the markers there unmoved, alarms on any other entry or
         carried row the map missed and keeps that source listed; when every source is empty, a fence write drops the
         sources (11.8), and 11.7 collects the current epoch's markers; one a fold left racing a move reads as absent
read     a client keeps, per path, the lowest epoch in which it holds evidence the server was shown the path's
         token (its floor): a verified version, removal or row naming it there, a request of its own that evs
         answered, or the push a verified version names as its predecessor; it sends the path's token path in the
         current epoch, in each listed source at or above the floor, and in any other epoch at or above it whose
         statements it needs proofs under, at most 8 (11.9's request row); a path with no floor is a new name: its
         token goes only under the current epoch, on a head verified within 5 s, never in a read while sources
         stand, and no due holds it (owner decision 585); such a name is looked up through its parent's table, from
         the root, which has no token; while sources stand, evs also HEADs in the same round a path's prefixes'
         current entries, whose state (11.7) rides in object metadata, each settled by 11.7's rule: under a removed
         prefix the path is absent, and under a fresh one too unless its own current entry is fresh; else evs uses
         the current entry, else the newest source's, and if every GET of the path returned 404 it GETs the current
         one again, since a fold and the copy PUT it before deleting a source copy; the reply names the epoch that
         served (entry_epoch); changes name their source paths by the floor (the payload's source paths), and a
         delta removing a child lists its token in the current epoch and each such source, so a fold drops a carried
         row too, and the server sees no source-epoch token of a name created since the cut-over but one first sent
         within 5 s of it (11.5); a push refused 412 PATH_EPOCH makes its epoch the floor of every path it named and
         is re-tokenized on the new head with every sealed byte, receipt and slot id kept (object key, below);
         readers check a carried row under its epoch's tokens and AAD, an untagged row under the serving epoch's,
         and every statement under the path's token in that statement's own epoch (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 9)
leases   the PATH_EPOCH hint reaches every lease holder of the ref, which re-creates its leases in p_new; a
         holder that missed it does so at its next resync, and a lease on every ref with no prefix names no
         token and matches in any epoch (11.10; owner decision 409)
costs    a 1M-file ref moves in about 17 h at 50 operations a second (3 per entry), about 6 h at 150, and one
         cluster's copies together move at most 7.2M entries a day at 250, so §19.9 plans each cluster's copy load as
         the live entries of its rotating refs times their epochs a day, under half of that; while sources stand, a
         read takes a HEAD per prefix and, for an unmoved path, a GET per listed source, in the same round
```

**Removal: tokens first, content later (owner decisions [2](#od-2), [64](#od-64)).** Tokens re-key server-side at the path epoch, which every removal makes due within 24 h: the server sees them, a removed key holder could keep testing them, and the copy moves no content. Until the epoch lands, new names on every ref are tokenized under the current epoch, which the removed holder can test, since no due holds a creation ([owner decision 585](#od-585)); a new ref starts in the newest epoch its creator holds ([owner decision 232](#od-232)), so no new ref's first names are tokenized under a removed key. Content rewraps lazily: the removed reader already holds every version it could decrypt, so a file's first write checkpoints it under the new generation (11.7 (4)), or `ur evs rekey` does; moved entries keep their bodies under their old generation, which the ladder opens for current readers.

**Nonces.** Every AEAD is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with random 192-bit nonces, so writers share no counter, wasm needs no lookup tables (§10.4), and nothing is encrypted deterministically.

```text
record          header sealed under manifest (160 B): record id, kind, key ref, body length, base record id, result
                git oid (32 B with its oid_kind, SHA-1 alone in v0, owner decision 249), nonce prefix. Body: 64 KiB
                STREAM frames under its object key, nonce = 19 B prefix || 32-bit counter || final flag, as in age
                (https://github.com/C2SP/C2SP/blob/main/age.md). AAD = repo_id || file_id || record id || generation
                || frame index. The header is sealed under manifest, or on a deposit ref under K_dep (Bytes,
                below). evs checks nothing.
segment         immutable, <= 8 MiB: 32 B public header {URvs, format 1, flags, repo_id, generation}, records,
                random padding to Padme(length); id = SHA-256 of all bytes. evs checks id, size, repo, generation.
                A kind-5 segment's header is format 2's, 48 B, adding the push_id that introduces it, which evs
                checks against the uploading or staging push, so no other push adopts its bytes (11.7).
object key      random 32 B, wrapped under fek_g. General repos: one per segment or inline chain, in its sealed
                header, which is owner decision 61's slot per segment, erased with the repo. Group inboxes: one
                per message, in a deletable slot/ object (§15.7). Record-class repos: one per entry or chain, in
                a deletable slot/ object; in group inboxes and record-class repos, one per versionless path, in a
                slot only that path's versions name (11.7). Deposits: one per deposit, HPKE to the drop key, in a
                slot/ object CONSUME deletes. Slot ids are 16 random bytes drawn per statement: a push rebuilt
                after a refusal draws new ones, and a retry of the same statement keeps them (11.8); a retoken,
                which sends a statement refused 412 PATH_EPOCH again in the new epoch with its sealed bytes kept
                (the PATH_EPOCH row), keeps them too, and evs gives it the object by a takeover (11.8's step 6). A
                slot object carries the statement that created it as its origin, in object metadata, and is that
                statement's for as long as it stands (owner decision 399; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 14)
statements      §6 Signed by the §5 identity key only: EvsPush (purpose evs-push; a DROP by a repo admin, in an
                owner-bound repo only by a consented, not-read-only device of its owner, 11.7), EvsPathMap
                (evs-path-epoch, by a writer), EvsImport (evs-import, by a repo admin; 11.11, owner decision 241: one
                push's imported commits, tip_oid that push's new tip, oid_list_sha256 the SHA-256 over its
                carried commit oids in carried order, count their number), EvsReseed (evs-reseed, by a repo
                admin; 11.13)
kinds           EvsLocator.kind 1 (segment) and 2 (inline) ship in format 1, which also reserves kind 5 (versionless
                segment), EvsEntryVersion.versioning (14; owner decision 167 needs no field 15), EvsLocator.staged
                (6), the kind-5 segment header (above), EvsUploadReceipt.versionless (8), batch format 2 (11.8),
                EvsPush flag 256 (DROP) and field 33 (drop_sha256; owner decision 173), flag 512 (CUT) and field 34
                (index_epoch; 11.8, 11.12), flag 1024 (COMPLETION, a completion ERASE, 11.12; owner decision 658),
                the read reply's per-path states drop_pending and dropped (11.9);
                format-1 code refuses each in use as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED {needs_format: 2} (owner decision 163), never
                as a fork, tampering or a missing segment, and ignores window bits 4 and 5, a head's index_epoch
                (EvsHead's 24, which format-1 writes carry, and EvsHeadSummary's 15; owner decision 235), and from M3
                sets and honors the push provenance's tainted bit (Records; owner decision 245); it verifies §7.9's
                VersioningRules and §8.8's RepoVersioning by signature and chain, folds the head holding the first
                and the lock of the second, and applies nothing from either, so no device stalls or forks (D-PHASE-9;
                §7.9, §8.8); repo/'s kind directory is known from M2, since the team directory runs on format-1
                streams from M6 (11.12; owner decision 171); format-1 clients refuse to write the .ur-index/
                directory on file-mode refs and the ur/index and ur/lfs refs (11.14); format 2 (v1) gives them
                meaning (11.7); kinds 3 (push-payload range) and 4 (pack range) stay reserved and refused, so either
                can ship with a format version that readers learn before writers use it
format          a repo's format is repo/'s object format: 1, or 2 from v1; PUT /evs/v1/repos/<id> always writes 1,
                the raise below is the only path to 2, a raise whose push then fails stands, since format-1 data
                is valid format 2, and nothing lowers it; evs takes format-2 values only from
                networks in §19.11's format2 gate, raising a format-1 repo at the first such push by an If-Match on
                repo/ before its step 7 (11.8), and GET .../refs returns it; format-1 data is valid format 2, so
                nothing is rewritten; a reader below format 2 says the repo needs an update and refuses its format-2
                values, reading every other file; format-1 evs, as after a rollback, which is a configuration of a
                real binary, EvsSettings.InstanceFormat 1 in evs's and taskworker's block config (default 2 from
                M10's release; §19.10; owner decision 412), serves a format-2 repo's stored bytes, refuses its
                pushes (503) and purges nothing
```

**Records** are `checkpoint`, `diff` (a git pack delta against the file's previous version, https://git-scm.com/docs/gitformat-pack) or `chunk`. Trees are not stored: directory names and each child's sealed {mode, oid} rebuild them exactly, except an imported tree that does not, which travels as its bytes beside the commit that brought it (`EvsSealedCommit.trees`), the tree builder using them once git's reading of them equals the entries it built; an imported commit travels as its bytes, and only a sidecar's new commits meet the strict codec, so [owner decision 81](#od-81)'s committer rule stays as strict as it is ([owner decision 236](#od-236)). Commits travel sealed in push records with provenance (§5.5's `agent_id`; agent-subkey signatures from v1, each with its `AgentCert`, a `Signed` of purpose `agent-cert` that rides in the push's sealed metadata and that a reader checks under the pushing sidecar's identity key before the subkey's signature, an absent certificate reading `agent_asserted`; from M3, format 1 included, the writing run's `tainted` bit, so §16.6 and the search index mark files from a tainted run: a version so marked reads `trust: untrusted` and reading it taints the run first, while a push bound to no run, a person's own `git push` included, carries none; [owner decision 245](#od-245)) and §10's `epoch_authenticator`. A file's random 16-B `file_id`, sealed in its entry, lets a rename keep its chain and stops evs swapping chains between files. From format 2 the sealed metadata also carries `index_none`, under sealed_metadata_sha256, on a push that changes no document (11.14's coverage row); nothing server-visible changes.

```proto
message EvsPush {                       // sidecar/protocol/evs.proto, inside §6 Signed, purpose evs-push; <= 1 KiB signed
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; uint32 ref_kind = 3; bytes owner_sidecar_id = 4;
  bytes push_id = 5;                    // 16 random bytes; names this statement only (11.8)
  uint64 base_version = 6; bytes base_chain = 7;        // the head it read: v and C_v
  repeated EvsChange changes = 8;       // every change, while the signed statement stays <= 1 KiB
  bytes sealed_metadata_sha256 = 9;     // commits, messages, provenance, epoch_authenticator, EvsImport
  uint64 generation = 10; uint64 path_epoch = 11;
  AuthPin auth = 12;                    // the authorization pin (n, A_n), §7.9
  bytes signer_sidecar_id = 13; bytes client_id = 14; int64 time_ms = 15;
  uint32 flags = 16;                    // 1 FORCE, 2 DELETE, 4 BASE, 8 IMMUTABLE, 16 CONSUME, 32 PATH_EPOCH,
                                        // 64 ERASE, 128 CLOSURE (an erasure's re-checkpoint, 11.12), 256 DROP
                                        // (a drop-history action or its cancel, 11.7; format 2), 512 CUT (an
                                        // erasure's index cut, 11.12; format 2), 1024 COMPLETION (with ERASE
                                        // alone: a completion ERASE, 11.12; format 2; owner decision 658),
                                        // 2048 EXACT_HEAD (file mode, formats 1 and 2, same base version and
                                        // chain at commit, 11.8)
  bytes path_map_sha256 = 17;           // PATH_EPOCH: SHA-256 over the epoch's EvsPathMap parts, in order
  uint32 part_count = 18;               // 0 for a one-part push, else 2 to 1,024
  bytes parts_sha256 = 19;              // SHA-256 over the parts' SHA-256s in part order (the list is in the payload)
  uint32 ref_mode = 20;                 // 1 git, 2 file (11.7)
  reserved 21;                          // the pin's chain lives in auth (12)
  bytes group_id = 22; bytes generation_commitment = 23;     // the generation pin with generation: {group, g, C_g}
  bytes changes_root = 24; uint32 change_count = 25;         // when changes are not inline: the root over all of them
  repeated EvsTokenPath changed_prefixes = 26;               // then: token paths, <= 512 B in all, covering every change
  bytes new_objects_sha256 = 27;        // segments (id, padded size, upload day) and slots (id) it introduces
  uint64 map_source_version = 28; bytes map_source_chain = 29;  // PATH_EPOCH: the head the map covers (11.6)
  bytes erased_sha256 = 30;             // ERASE, CLOSURE: SHA-256 of its payload's (slot id, key index) list (11.12)
  bytes path_tail_sha256 = 31;          // PATH_EPOCH: SHA-256 of the tail's moves in its payload (11.6), or empty
  bytes source_paths_sha256 = 32;       // while sources stand: SHA-256 of the payload's source paths (11.6), or empty
  bytes drop_sha256 = 33;               // DROP: SHA-256 of the payload's EvsDropHistory; else empty (format 2)
  uint64 index_epoch = 34;              // a CUT, or a push other than a CLOSURE creating or replacing an index
                                        // file: the head's index_epoch it was built at, the ref's erasure set at
                                        // that epoch applied (11.8's 5d, 11.14); else 0 (format 2)
  uint64 consumed_through = 35;         // CONSUME: the highest version of this deposit ref at or below which its
                                        // ingester's read left no unconsumed deposit; else 0 (11.12's deposits)
}
message EvsTokenPath { repeated bytes token = 1; }            // 16 B per component
message EvsChange {
  repeated bytes token_path = 1;        // 16 B per component, in the push's path epoch
  uint64 base_entry_version = 2;        // 0 creates; the path-level CAS condition (directories merge, 11.7)
  bytes entry_sha256 = 3;               // SHA-256 of the new EvsEntryVersion; empty deletes
}
message EvsPushPart {                   // unsigned; parts_sha256 binds it
  bytes push_id = 1; uint32 part = 2;
  repeated EvsChange changes = 3;       // at most 1,024 entry writes; a path appears in one part only
  repeated bytes entry_versions = 4;    // EvsEntryVersion bytes, as each change's entry_sha256 names
  repeated bytes inline_records = 5;    // empty in format 1: an inline record rides its entry version (Bytes)
  bytes sealed_metadata = 6;            // a slice; sealed_metadata_sha256 covers the slices in order
  bytes changes_root = 7;               // root over this part's changes; the statement's root is over these roots
  bytes sections = 8;                   // its slice of each payload section past fields 3-6, framed as a payload
                                        // is; joined in part order, the slices are a one-part push's (Bytes, below)
}
message EvsEntryVersion {               // what entry_sha256 hashes; in the push record, and folded into idx/
  uint64 version = 1;                   // base_entry_version + 1; a creation's max(the push's effective base
                                        // version, an overlay's chain included, a standing removal's) + 1, so it
                                        // never restarts (11.7)
  bytes push_id = 2; uint64 base_version = 3;            // the push that wrote it and the head it read
  bytes prev_push_id = 4; uint64 prev_commit_version = 5; // the version it replaces, for history walks
  int64 time_ms = 6; uint32 kind = 7; uint64 padded_size = 8;
  bytes sealed_fields = 9;              // file: {file_id, mode, git oid, size}, plus content_sha256 (the
                                        // plaintext's SHA-256) for a versionless file; directory: none
  repeated EvsLocator chain = 10;       // file: at most N+1 records
  repeated bytes slot_ids = 11;
  EvsNameTable names = 12;              // directory: a push's delta; in idx/, a fold's table (11.7)
  uint32 layout = 13;                   // directory: 0 single; other values reserved and refused
  uint32 versioning = 14;               // file: 0 every version kept, 1 versionless, 2 a versionless file of the
                                        // search index (11.7); directory: 0; format 1 refuses any value but 0
}
message EvsNameTable { repeated EvsName names = 1; repeated bytes removed_tokens = 2; }  // a fold's table removes none
message EvsName {                       // sealed as 11.7's name row
  bytes token = 1; uint32 kind = 2; bytes sealed_name = 3;
  uint64 epoch = 4;                     // 0, or the source epoch whose token and AAD a carried row keeps (11.6)
}
message EvsLocator {
  uint32 kind = 1;                      // 1 segment, 2 inline, 5 versionless segment (format 2, 11.7); 3
                                        // (push-payload range) and 4 (pack range) reserved
  bytes id = 2;                         // kinds 1 and 5: segment_id, at seg/<repo>/<id> (kind 1 also through
                                        // spidx/, 11.13)
  uint32 offset = 3; uint32 length = 4; bytes inline = 5;
  bool staged = 6;                      // kind 5: the segment rides in this version's push (11.7); format 1
                                        // refuses true
}
message EvsPathMap {                    // purpose evs-path-epoch; at most 8 MiB per part
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; uint64 path_epoch = 3; uint32 part = 4; uint32 parts = 5;
  repeated EvsPathMove moves = 6;
  uint64 source_version = 7; bytes source_chain = 8;    // the head whose paths the map covers
}
message EvsPathMove {
  repeated bytes new_token_path = 1;
  repeated EvsSourcePath sources = 2;   // the path in the current epoch and in each listed source
  bytes sealed_name = 3;                // re-sealed under AAD with the new parent and child tokens
}
message EvsSourcePath { uint64 epoch = 1; repeated bytes token_path = 2; }
message EvsImport {                     // purpose evs-import, in one push's sealed metadata, over that push's
                                        // own imported commits: tip_oid its new tip, oid_list_sha256 over
                                        // their oids in carried order, count their number (owner decision 241)
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; bytes tip_oid = 3; bytes oid_list_sha256 = 4; uint32 count = 5;
}
message EvsReseed {                     // §6 Signed, purpose evs-reseed, by a repo admin (§8.8); §19.10
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2;
  uint64 version = 3; bytes chain = 4;  // the re-seeded head: v and C_v
  bytes incident_id = 5;                // the recovery's identity (§19.10)
}
message EvsDropHistory {                // a DROP push's payload body (format 2; 11.7)
  bytes drop_id = 1;                    // 16 random bytes drawn per statement; a retry of the statement keeps it
  uint32 action = 2;                    // 1 drop, 2 cancel
  bytes cancels_drop_id = 3;            // cancel: the drop it ends, committed on this ref
  uint64 cancels_version = 4;           // cancel: that drop's ref version
  int64 not_before_ms = 5;              // drop: time_ms + 604,800,000 (7 days), or time_ms with now (owner
                                        // decision 183)
  repeated EvsDropPath paths = 6;       // drop: 1 to 1,024 lineages, sorted by their newest token path's bytes;
                                        // the body at most 256 KiB as bytes (owner decision 396)
  bytes preview_id = 7;                 // drop: the dry run its signer confirmed (11.13), or empty
}
message EvsDropPath {                   // one lineage: one path name on this ref, as far as evs can follow it
  repeated EvsSourcePath lineage = 1;   // its token path per path epoch, newest first; each older entry a source of
                                        // the next in that epoch's committed map or PATH_EPOCH tail (11.6)
  repeated uint32 map_parts = 2;        // per older entry, the map part (1 to parts) holding its move; 0 the tail
  uint64 through_version = 3;           // the path version that stays; every listed version is older
  uint32 boundary = 4;                  // 1 written: this push writes through_version, the head's content again;
                                        // 2 removed: through_version is the path's standing removal
  uint32 count = 5;                     // listed versions, 1 to 1,048,576, and at most that many over all of a
                                        // DROP's paths (owner decision 396)
  bytes listed_sha256 = 6;              // SHA-256 over the listed entry_sha256 values, ascending, which follow the
                                        // body in the payload, spread over the push's parts past one part's 1 MiB;
                                        // a check of the signer's enumeration, which the job's resolve and a
                                        // replaying reader recompute and no reader is sent (owner decision 396)
}
message EvsUploadReceipt {              // unsigned; evs MACs it (11.13), the push carries it back
  bytes repo_id = 1; bytes segment_id = 2; uint64 padded_size = 3; int64 upload_ms = 4;
  bytes uploader_sidecar_id = 5; uint32 key_id = 6; bytes mac = 7;  // HMAC-SHA256 over fields 1-6 and 8, first 16 B
  bool versionless = 8;                 // the segment's header is a kind-5 header naming the receipt's push
                                        // (11.7); format 1 issues false
}
message EvsPlace {                      // where a batch record's bytes are (11.8); assigned by evs, 20 B packed
  uint32 minute = 1; uint32 instance = 2; uint32 seq = 3; uint32 offset = 4; uint32 length = 5;
}
```

```text
size     a signed statement is at most 1 KiB, so log pages hold statements; big change lists move to the payload
         under changes_root
payload  in the push's batch record for a one-part push, else spread over its parts and its seal: entry versions,
         sealed metadata, inline records, the change list when not inline, the part hashes, the new-objects list
         (segment id, padded size and the UTC day of its upload, from its receipt, or a staged mark for a staged
         segment, whose bytes follow the payload outside every payload hash, 11.7; slot ids), new slot bodies
         (section 7, covered by no hash, which evs writes to slot/ at step 6 and empties from the record it stores,
         as idx/ elides inline records, so the slot object is the one stored copy of each key and an ERASE leaves
         an erased key nowhere a reader can fetch; a push in parts carries them whole in its seal request and in
         none of its parts, within a format setting, a part's 1 MiB by default; owner decision 400), the
         erased list, a DROP's EvsDropHistory, whole in part 1, and then its sorted lists, across the push's parts
         when large in each part's sections field, in parts that hold no change once the changes end (slices,
         below; 11.7, 11.8's parts row), a PATH_EPOCH's tail moves, the source paths (per change, an EvsSourcePath
         for each listed source that may hold it, 11.6's read rule, in change order), the reuse list of committed
         versions whose segments a new version cites ((ref, token path, entry version), 11.8) and, per entry
         version, its Merkle proof to changes_root (empty when inline)
checks   at push time evs checks that each entry version hashes to its change's entry_sha256, that the change list
         matches changes_root, is sorted (merkle, below) and changed_prefixes cover it, that the payload lists
         match new_objects_sha256, parts_sha256, erased_sha256, path_tail_sha256, source_paths_sha256 and
         drop_sha256, each drop list its listed_sha256 and count, sorted and unrepeated (409 DROP_LIST), a DROP's
         body within 256 KiB and its counts within 1,048,576 in all (owner decision 396), that each staged segment
         hashes to its id and names this push in its header, and that versionless versions keep 11.7's rules (409
         VERSIONING); a statement over 1 KiB is refused
merkle   RFC 9162 hashing: leaf SHA-256(0x00 || bytes), node SHA-256(0x01 || left || right); changes sort by
         their token paths' bytes, each part a contiguous run in part order, so inclusion proofs of two adjacent
         leaves show that no path between them changed (11.9); every proof is repeated, part level last, the leaf
         in its part and then the part in the statement's root, so a change in a push in parts proves as one in a
         one-part push (owner decision 378); the root covers only the parts that hold a change, so a changeless
         part joins no level of it and absence proofs name changed parts only, and a statement in parts may state
         no change at all, change_count 0 and changes_root RFC 9162's empty tree (SHA-256 of the empty string),
         with no changed_prefixes and every part changeless, as a git-mode push whose net change is empty but whose
         commits and history blobs pass one part does (owner decision 376)
```

```text
http      bodies are evs.proto messages, application/x-protobuf, but a segment PUT's raw bytes: EvsPushRequest
```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/evs.proto: what a push's sealed metadata opens to (sealed, above)
message EvsSealedMetadata {
  GroupHead group = 1;                  // §10's (group_id, epoch, epoch_authenticator) the writer pins
  EvsProvenance provenance = 2;
  repeated EvsSealedCommit commits = 3; // git mode: the carried commits, parents before children (11.7)
  bytes signed_import = 4;              // a Signed EvsImport over this push's own commits
  EvsGitUpdate git = 5;                 // git mode, every push but a PATH_EPOCH: the ref's update
  bytes ref_name = 6;                   // a creating push: payload section 15's signed copy
  EvsOverlay base = 7;                  // a creating push of an overlay: payload section 16's signed copy
  bytes erasure_note = 8;               // an ERASE's or a CLOSURE's note (11.12; owner decision 384)
  repeated bytes written_over = 9;      // a repair form's: the push ids of the ignored versions it writes over,
                                        //   16 B each, for ur evs log alone (owner decision 415)
}
```

### 11.7 Diffs, checkpoints, index entries, reconstruction

**Mapping to git.** Each ref has a mode: git-mode refs, which the local tier writes, commit only on their tip; file-mode refs land by path ([owner decision 141](#od-141)). One evs push carries one git ref update, in parts when large (11.8); its cleartext changes are the net change of the ref's path state, and its sealed metadata states the update (`EvsGitUpdate`: its shape, the ref's value before and after, and any annotated tags) and carries every commit and blob that the ref's readers do not already hold: each commit's object with its changes against its first parent, any tree that does not rebuild from them as its bytes ([owner decision 236](#od-236)), any annotated tag as its bytes, and each blob that no entry carries as one sealed history record (a checkpoint, chunks, or a diff against the same path's blob in the commit's first parent, which readers hold by then) in a segment the push introduces, found by `EvsSealedBlob {git_oid, size, base_oid, file_id, records}` and named by no entry version's chain ([owner decision 237](#od-237)); what readers hold is what the ref's previous tip, its overlay base and the push's named sources reach ([owner decision 238](#od-238)), so export and every syncing device rebuild every original oid and every blob (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 8).

```text
      git-remote-ur, ur evs     CAS for every push, FORCE and          non-fast-forward; the client    and oids
      import, and evs_write     PATH_EPOCH included                    fetches, merges or rebases
      through it (§16.2)                                               (new commits) and pushes again
file  evs_write on file-mode    path-level CAS: each changed file      evs lands a disjoint push at    one deterministic commit
      refs, head mode, record   path's newest committed entry version  the next version itself; a      per version: tree = the
      streams, deposits, mail,  equals its base_entry_version, and     shared path answers 409 with    state, parent = the previous
      config, mailcfg           base_version >= v - 63                 the paths                       version's, committer
                                                                                                       <client_id>@ur.invalid of the
                                                                                                       signer, time time_ms, message
                                                                                                       "ur push <push_id hex>"
exact     an authorized file-mode writer may also sign EXACT_HEAD to require the current version and chain at
          commit (11.8 step 5f). A reader replaying the chain checks that such a statement names its immediate
          predecessor's version and chain. The ordinary file-mode path rule above still admits disjoint pushes.
set       the ref's first push sets ref_mode in its statement and the head; another mode is refused (409 REF_MODE);
          only git-mode refs take overlays (below), which are git mode
replay    replaying readers of a git-mode ref check TIP; that the update's stated old tip is the ref's; that every
          carried commit hashes to its oid with its parents held or carried, and that the new tip is their top;
          descent, except on a FORCE push the refs table allows or when the ref has no tip; each tree against its
          commit and each blob against its oid; that the changes are exactly the net change to the new tip's tree;
          and that every carried commit is canonical with the committer <client_id>@ur.invalid of the push's
          client or of a client of its signer (owner decision 81), or is listed by the push's own EvsImport, so
          the forced identity is a property of the stored history, not only of the hook; a commit reached through
          a named source was judged where it was carried; PATH_EPOCH and REKEY pushes carry no commit and move no
          tip
shapes    a git-mode push is an UPDATE (commits and the net change; FORCE when it does not descend), a DELETE, a
          REKEY (no commit; file entries re-checkpointed, modes and oids unchanged; any writer's device, owner
          decision 540) or a PATH_EPOCH; a tag ref (refs/tags/…) holds no path state and its pushes carry no change
sources   a push names up to 16 committed versions of the repo's other git-mode refs (EvsGitUpdate.sources),
          chosen from tips its writer's mirror has applied, whose tips its readers replay first; a commit a source
          reaches is not carried and not judged again; a carried commit is new, and its committer is the signer's
          or it is one of the commits the push's own EvsImport lists; a version is applied only after the versions
          it names, a cycle of waits is refused, and a ref whose source cannot be replayed waits with no alarm of
          its own (owner decision 238)
history   a carried blob that is no entry's content is one sealed history record in a segment of the push: a
          checkpoint, chunks, or one diff against a blob named by oid that readers hold by then; no entry's chain
          names it (owner decision 237)
kinds     a git-mode push may write a file where a directory stands and a directory where a file stands, as a
          creation, removing what was below by its own changes; a gitlink is a file entry with no chain
head mode mobile and wasm read both modes and write only file-mode refs; the SDK's Write on a git-mode ref returns
          EVS_GIT_REF, since a head-mode client cannot build a git tree, which needs every sibling's oid
scope     tags are git-mode refs pushed IMMUTABLE that hold no path state and have no base: a tag's one push
          carries no change and names as sources the refs whose tips already reach its commit, carrying what its
          commit reaches beyond them as commits and history blobs, so a tag of what a branch reaches is one push
          with no commit, change or upload, and writers and replaying readers refuse a change on a tag ref (owner
          decision 244); git-mode refs refuse versioning off (versionless files, below);
          LFS (v1: 11.11's versionless store), replace refs, notes other than export's refs/notes/ur, partial-clone
          filters and atomic multi-ref pushes are outside v0 (11.11)
why tip   a path-disjoint landing gives a git ref a tree no git commit has, so export could not keep the original
          oids, and a server-made merge would merge shared branches automatically, which sidecar/design/market2.md:519-520
          forbids; tip CAS costs a client retry only when two merges meet (about 2% in the twenty-agent test)
```

**Checkpoints (PLAN.md:63)** are written when (1) the chain has N = 16 diffs; (2) its diffs exceed 50% of the file's size (Mercurial's revlog rule, [R:ext-storage-crypto](design/design-research/ext-storage-crypto.md) §2.10); (3) the file is new, or the delta outgrows it; or (4) a REMOVE generation (§10.5's GenRotate `cause`: it covers a shrink, an authorization expiry or a compromise retirement) is newer than the chain's key, which is PLAN.md:50's rewrap rule ([owner decision 64](#od-64)); or (5) a DROP writes the path's kept head (Dropped history, below); every checkpoint draws a fresh object key, except that a slot-keyed repo's versionless path keeps its key until (4), a CLOSURE or a rekey replaces it. A versionless file's every version is a checkpoint or a chunk set: (1)-(3) do not apply to it, and (4) makes its next write re-encrypt every chunk.

**Large files** over 8 MiB are 4 MiB `chunk` records, rewritten only where touched; fixed sizes avoid content-defined chunking, whose chunk sizes leak and whose keyed variants were broken in 2025 (ePrint 2025/558). A file is capped at 2,147,483,648 B of plaintext (512 chunks) through M10, versionless files and git-lfs objects included: writers and the git-lfs agent refuse a larger one by name (`EVS_FILE_TOO_LARGE`), so `git push` fails before the ref moves, and a later raise to about 8 GiB is a settings default and tests, with no format change ([owner decision 248](#od-248)).

**Versionless files (owner decisions [158](#od-158)-[165](#od-165)).** A file version whose `versioning` is 1 or 2 is versionless: its path keeps only its newest version's content, and the purge deletes a replaced version's content once its replacement commits (11.13). Format 2 (v1) carries it (11.6).

```text
setting   per file version: 0 keeps every version (the default); 1 versionless; 2 versionless, marking the search
          index's own files, which readers accept only under the index's roots (.ur-index/ on a file-mode ref, or
          the repo's ur/index ref; 11.14; owner decision 168); in format 2 only 11.14's mechanisms write under
          .ur-index/ and on ur/index, and readers ignore any other version there and alarm; directories carry 0;
          a path's setting is its newest version's, and a new version keeps it unless its writer sets another
choose    a writer sets a new path's setting from the rules in force at its creation (owner decision 167): the repo's
          own, from its access log's RepoVersioning (§8.8), else its network's VersioningRules (§7.9), else the
          platform rule, versionless above 64 MiB of plaintext; first match wins; a present rule set replaces the
          next source entirely, so a path none of its rules matches is created versioned (0), and the platform rule
          applies only where neither the repo nor the network has a record (owner decision 164); an owner-bound
          repo's own rules are sealed to its generation, so only that repo's readers read them (§8.8); the index
          writes 2, 11.11's git-lfs store 1 (its settings file 0) and §15.7's mail component s/model 1 (each 0 in a
          locked repo, the index excepted), and the team directory 1 on its cards ref's d/, r/ and q/ paths from its
          format 2 (format 1's notices are versioned files; §16.11), whatever the rules say; a writer changes an
          existing path's setting only explicitly (ur evs versioning, MCP's and the SDK's argument), as a new version
          that rewrites nothing stored; evs never reads rules
refused   409 VERSIONING for 1 or 2 in config and mailcfg repos, whose replaying readers verify authority from
          every version (§7.9, §15.7), on git-mode refs, and on creates-only refs (record-class streams, deposit
          and erasure refs); for 1, not 2 (owner decision 168), in a repo whose access log holds a lock §8.8's
          signer filed (a repo admin or a config writer; in an owner-bound repo only a consented device of its
          owner) in the authorization state evs validates against (5d), so a write validated before the lock
          serializes before it; readers refuse a 1 in a push whose auth pin includes the lock; the directory kind
          refuses every RepoVersioning (§8.8)
content   one checkpoint record, or 4 MiB chunk records above 8 MiB, never a diff or an inline record (readers
          check; evs sees only locator kinds): kind 5 for what its push writes and for unchanged chunks its path's
          previous version named as kind 5; kind 1 for chunks that version named as kind 1 (versioning just turned
          off; never purged); content_sha256 in its sealed fields
kind 5    a segment holding exactly one record of one versionless version, its 48 B header naming its introducing
          push (11.6), at seg/<repo>/<id> or, while staged, in that push's batch record; read and verified as kind 1
          (id, AEAD, then content_sha256 and the git oid); an upload whose header names another push than its
          ?push= gets 409 VERSIONING, and its receipt marks it versionless (11.6), so equal bytes are only ever the
          same push's retry and no push adopts another's segment as its own upload
staged    a record that pads to at most 16 KiB, but an ur/lfs object's, which is always a kind-5 upload so a touch
          always cites it, rides in its push's or part's payload as a one-record segment
          (Padmé-padded) instead of PUT .../segments: its new-objects entry carries a staged mark and its locator
          staged = true; no receipt; evacuation moves the record without the staged bytes and writes them to seg/
          only while their version is retained (11.13), so content replaced within about a day of its write never
          reaches the HDDs; packs and parcels never hold it, and pidx/ lists the staged segments a record
          introduced, as it lists uploads
cite      a kind-5 segment is named only by the version that introduced it and then, in turn, by its path's next
          version on the same ref, or, in the push that removes the path, by a version that push creates (a
          rename); never by another path, ref or repo, nor through a reuse source (a copy re-uploads); a staged
          segment only by its introducing version, a later version re-staging its <= 16 KiB
keys      general repos keep each kind-5 segment's key in its sealed header, so it goes with the segment; slot-keyed
          repos (record-class repos, group inboxes) keep a versionless path's one key in a slot that only that
          path's versions name and, in turn, the rename target of the push that removes it, reused by each next
          version until checkpoint rule (4), a CLOSURE or ur evs rekey
          draws a fresh one in a new slot, so an overwrite writes no slot
removal   a push removing a directory, and a ref's DELETE, list each versionless file below as a file removal (the
          client holds the tree), so the commit names every version it replaces and the purge deletes their content
          a minute later, at most ~26 h when its queue is lost (11.13's sweep); a versionless file below that the
          push did not list goes at its marker's collection: the removal fold alarms and carries its kind-5 segment
          and slot ids in its marker, and the collection deletes them (collect, below; §2.8's evs-4, evs-5)
off       version k+1 written versionless keeps the path's earlier versions, written on, for the repo's life unless
          a drop lists them (Dropped history, below; owner decision 173); if its content is unchanged and k's chain
          holds no diff or inline record, it cites k's records as kind 1, with no upload; else it writes one
          checkpoint as kind 5
on        version k+1 written with versioning on starts history there; k's content is purged once k+1 commits,
          unless k+1 adopts k's uploaded kind-5 segments as kind 1 (no re-upload; then kept for good); staged
          content becomes inline again
history   a removed path's earlier versions and earlier lives read by number (11.9's reply row; owner decision 380);
          a replaced versionless version keeps its statement and entry version for the repo's life: history shows
          its hashes, padded size, time and signer, and answers `collected` for its content, which nothing restores;
          a dropped version keeps its statement likewise (Dropped history, below)
reads     head reads are unchanged: every path's newest version has its content (I-EVS-1); a staged locator
          resolves by id in its push's record while that record is batch-resident, else at seg/, which evacuation
          writes before deleting the batch; a version replaced mid-read stays readable at least 60 s after its
          replacement commits, after which its reads answer `collected` and the client re-reads the head fresh and
          restarts on the newest version
writers   a racing write to a versionless path gets path-level CAS's 409 like any write; the SDK, MCP and the sync
          engine surface it and never retry by rebasing blindly, since the loser's content would replace the
          winner's with no history to recover it from (the index's heads, which hold only what their writer wrote,
          are the one exception, 11.14)
git       git-mode refs hold no versionless version: a git commit names every blob, and exact oids (owner decision
          141) and export need every blob of every commit; a repo's git-mode refs keep their search index on its one
          ur/index file-mode ref (11.14), and large git files use 11.11's git-lfs store (v1)
root      no Merkle root: a 2 GiB file's 512 chunk locators (~23 KiB) sit in one entry version, which the statement
          signs through entry_sha256; per-frame AEAD covers ranged reads
cli       ur evs versioning on|off <path|glob>... [--ref r] writes new versions with the same content; ur evs ls -l
          shows each path's setting; ur evs log marks replaced versionless versions `collected`; ur status reports
          each repo's versionless bytes, its search index's bytes apart from content (§20.7; D-QUOTA-10) and the
          versioned paths whose history holds most of its storage; ur history drop|drops|cancel (below)
```

This is Perforce's rule, applied per version: each version's own setting says whether it is kept once replaced, so no later write destroys history written under the keep-forever default.

**Dropped history (owner decisions [173](#od-173), [183](#od-183), [184](#od-184)).** A repo admin may drop a path's history on a file-mode ref: content that only its earlier versions name goes, and every statement, hash and the head stay. Format 2 (v1) carries it.

```text
action    a DROP push (flags 256) on the path's ref carries EvsDropHistory (11.6), at most 262,144 B with at most
          1,048,576 listed values in all (400 INVALID and 409 DROP_LIST past them; a larger drop goes in several DROP
          pushes cut at lineage boundaries, each previewed and confirmed once as one command, each counting in
          evs_drops_per_day, and one lineage alone past a bound is refused locally; owner decision 396): per lineage
          of the path's token paths across epochs, its versions with an entry_sha256 below through_version, by entry
          hash, a removal having none, so it is never listed or counted; not_before_ms is time_ms + 7 days, or time_ms
          with now, as RepoDelete's (owner decision 183); one repo admin signs it, in an owner-bound repo only a
          consented, not-read-only device of its owner (owner decision 126), never MCP (§16.6); any repo admin
          (owner-bound: such a device of the owner) cancels it by a DROP with action 2 committed before not_before_ms
          less 60 s by evs's clock; a lock standing when its job starts voids it (§8.8); 11.13's job deletes nothing
          before not_before_ms + 25 min, and marks only once evacuation's horizon has passed by 12 min the time evs
          saw the drop committed, which covers a citation validated on a cached head, so a now drop's deletions start
          25 h 12 min to 26 h 12 min after it (owner decisions 204, 397)
rule      once it executes: kind-1 segments and slots that only listed versions name, on any ref and path, are
          deleted, each once evacuation's horizon has passed its LastModified + 24 h + 2 min (owner decision 397);
          listed versions' statements, window entries, log pages, chain values, times, signers and entry hashes stay
          for the ref's life, so history verifies, and their entry versions stay where their chains name no inline
          record; ids a live version (11.13) names (a rename, a copy on another ref, a revert, the kept head's chunks)
          stay, kind-5 segments stay the purge's (I-EVS-9), and the pushes' sealed metadata stays; inline records in
          batches, parcels and packs, and packed segments, stay unserved until a later compaction, unscheduled (owner
          decision 247), though deleting a slot makes slot-keyed inline content unreadable at once; the DROP's index
          rewrites remove listed versions' postings (11.14); devices delete their copies
boundary  1 written: the DROP writes through_version, the path's next version, with the head's plaintext, mode and
          git oid: up to 8 MiB as one checkpoint under a fresh object key (an upload, or inline when it pads to at
          most 16 KiB; a new slot in slot-keyed repos), above that the head's chunk set cited as it stands; evs
          checks one locator naming an upload or inline record of this push, or chunk locators each an upload of
          this push or a kind-1 locator its base names, all but the last a whole 4 MiB chunk, and versioning 0;
          readers check record kinds, oid and mode; 2 removed: through_version is the path's standing removal,
          which stays, nothing is written, and a re-creation continues from it (owner decision 148); beside the
          written lineages' changes evs takes a DROP's index rewrites (11.14's drop row): changes of versioning-2

          length); ur/index is another ref and never rides the push; every other change is 409 DROP_BOUNDARY
          (owner decision 619)
why       a diff chain's checkpoint and early diffs are older versions' content, so a head still citing them would
          keep listed versions reconstructable; the fresh checkpoint leaves those records named only by listed
          versions, and chunk records hold only the head's bytes
not       no boundary below the head: a drop keeps one version's content, and nothing keeps the newest n (owner
          decision 165)
fence     from its commit, 5h refuses (409 DROPPED) as a base, deleted path or reuse source any version a DROP
          lists: a window version a DROP in the window lists (window bit 5), or one below its entry's drop mark
          (index entries, below); a reuse source's head may come from the cache, which serves a head only
          within 10 min of that head's own write (11.9's cache row; owner decision 397); a seal reruns this
          against the heads it rereads; a cancel lifts nothing, so a later copy re-uploads
states    drop_pending: a listed version before not_before_ms by the reader's clock, with no cancel seen and evs not
          reporting the drop refused: readable, shown "drop pending until <time>"; dropped: after not_before_ms or at
          any 404 of its content, unless a committed cancel names the drop or evs reports it refused: nothing fetched
          or shown, history keeping its version, time, signer, entry hash and, where served, padded size; no alarm for

          over a body of at most 256 KiB, not_before_ms equal to time_ms + 604,800,000 or time_ms, each entry of the
          path's lineage the path's token path in its epoch, the boundary where the reader reads the kept version,

          computed from its own history, equal to count and listed_sha256, which only a replaying reader can compute,
          so a DROP whose own list disagrees with its body is invalid to a replaying reader, taken by its body at a

refused   409 DROP_KIND in config and mailcfg repos; REF_MODE on git-mode refs, overlays included, and creates-only

          whose count, order or repeats are wrong, past 2^20 values in all the DROP's lists (and 400 INVALID for a
          body past 262,144 B; owner decision 396), or, written, lacking the base step 4 read; DROP_STATE
          for a drop whose not_before_ms is neither time_ms + 604,800,000 nor time_ms (a cancel carries 0), a cancel
          of no pending drop on this ref, or one within 60 s of its not_before_ms; 403 below admin scope;
          429 past evs_drops_per_day (§20.4), which counts drops (EvsDropHistory action 1) only: a cancel never
          counts and is never refused by it, so one admin's drops cannot block another's cancel (owner decision 183;
          D-QUOTA-12); QuotaRefusal at the limit when the kept checkpoint needs an upload
cli       ur history drop <repo>:<path>... [--ref r] [--follow] [--recursive] [--now] [--dry-run] [--confirm

          ur history drops [<repo>] lists drops and their states; ur history cancel <repo> <drop_id>; the command
```
