
**Index entries** cache each path's committed versions, folded from committed pushes; push records hold every one:

```text
version   an EvsEntryVersion (11.6): a file's sealed fields, its chain (at most N+1 locators, inline when it pads to
          <= 16 KiB) and slot ids; a directory's names
holds     only committed versions, written by folds: per file up to four folded EvsEntryVersions with their push id
          and commit version u, the newest with its inline records and older ones with inline records elided (evs
          restores them from the push record before serving the signed bytes); per directory one name table, as of
          the newest delta applied; per removed path its marker (removal, below); per dropped path its drop mark
          {drop_id, through_version}; beside each folded version, table and marker the place of its change in its
          own statement's list (leaf_part, leaf_index; owner decision 200), an inline list's as leaf_part 0 and
          leaf_index the change's index plus 1, 0 meaning only not recorded, so evs serves every committed version
          of an older path epoch in one round (owner decision 233); a fold never drops the newest folded version,
          and drops older ones only for newer
newest    a path's newest committed version at a head H is the newer of its entry's newest folded version, a marker's
          removal included, and the newest version after h that changes the path or a prefix holding it (the digest
          first, then the statement's change list), h being the folded_through of a head evs read before the entry: a
          fold's PUTs precede the commit that raises folded_through over them, so the entry holds every version
          through h; H's window must hold every version after h, else evs reads the entry again after H, and a folded
          version committed after H's v sends evs to a newer head; head reads, listings and 11.8's path-level CAS,
          reruns included, all use this rule
versions  a write's version is base_entry_version + 1; a creation's (base_entry_version 0, naming the path absent,
          never written or removed) is max(b, m) + 1, m the version of the newest removal its marker or the window
          holds, else b, and b its push's effective base version: its base_version, plus, on an overlay, the base
          versions along its chain of EvsOverlay bases, which evs reads at the ref's creation and caches, so a
          path's versions never fall below any it held on a base ref; a removal is one of the path's versions, one
          past its last, which its marker keeps (owner decision 148), and for a directory whose newest delta is
          already folded, which the fold finds by a LIST below a removed directory or a prefix removal with no
          delta of its own in the fold's range, names_through + 1, an upper bound that versions only ever skip past
          (owner decision 380); evs (5g, 409 for any other version) and
          replaying readers (alarming) check both rules, so no version exceeds the effective ref version it commits
          at; an honest creation's base shows the path absent, so every earlier version is at most b, and a removal
          after b is in the window (b >= v - 63): a path's versions never restart, whether its marker stands, was
          collected or was dropped by a path-epoch copy, and a push based on one from before a removal fails 5g; a
          client refused creating (409) reads the removal (11.9) and retries
fold      for a ref's window versions (f, u]: read their statements and entry versions (the process's cache, else
          batch ranges); per changed file path, its newest version or removal (its own or a prefix's) in (f, u],
          skipped when a window version after u changes that file again; per changed directory, every delta in (f, u]
          past the version its entry holds, applied in version order, since a newer delta never replaces an older
          one; GET each entry (404: create it, once a cluster read of the ref's head in this fold succeeds, 11.13's
          skip rule), merge (a file's folded versions, the newest four kept; a creation, or a DROP's written version,
          replaces what the entry held, carrying nothing, a marker's carried ids first put in an orphan marker
          (orphan, below), the DROP's setting the entry's drop mark {drop_id, through_version}, and a DROP at a
          removed boundary setting it on the path's marker entry while that entry holds folded versions, so its fence
          outlives the window, as DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 10 has it), PUT If-Match (If-None-Match to create), on
          412 read again and merge; an entry that already holds a version is not written, and a marker takes only a
          newer one (collect, below); while sources stand, once the current entry holds a path's change the fold
          deletes each listed source copy its pushes' source paths name, and under a removed directory LISTs and
          deletes everything below it in those sources, its range counting as folded only when the deletes answered,
          so a source holds only what still has to move (owner decision 227); folds are idempotent, and any evs
          process may run one
stale     each fold and copy write carries a store deadline 15 s after it issued the cluster read of the ref's head
          it relies on (§19.6's settle rule: past it the store neither takes the write nor begins a drive commit of
          it, and one it began lands before the next request on its key or never), a page-out's fold reading the
          head from the cluster when step 4's came from the cache; a fold relies only on a read whose
          folded_through is at most its f, stopping at one above it (another folded its range), and a copy only on
          one still listing its sources, so no write planned before the horizon rose or the sources dropped is
          taken past 15 s, or lands after a later request on its key
when      (1) after a commit that leaves 96 or more versions unfolded, the committing process folds the oldest 64,
          off the reply path, at most once per ref per 10 s; (2) 10 min after a ref's last commit, the process that
          made it folds the rest; (3) a commit that pages versions out of the window first folds any of them still
          unfolded (11.8 step 6); (4) a PATH_EPOCH push's process first folds every unfolded version, as step 6
          does for a page-out (on a busy git-mode ref under the seal lease), and its step-7 head sets
          folded_through = v, so an idle ref whose folded_through trails v still commits its epoch
horizon   folded_through: every file change at or below it, a removal as its marker, is in its path's entry or
          replaced by a newer window version of that file, and every directory delta at or below it is applied to its
          name table; it rises only with a commit by the process that folded, so folds add no head write, and a stale
          value costs readers only statement reads
lag       if a page-out's fold cannot finish within 11.8's 5 s rule, the commit proceeds without paging, the window
          growing to at most 255 versions; past that, pushes to the ref get 429 FOLD_BEHIND with retry_after_ms
epochs    a fold writes the current path epoch's entries, each, while the head lists sources, with its state in its
          object metadata: carried, as the copy writes, when the change's source paths (its push record) name a
          source still holding the path, keeping that source's folded versions and drop mark and tagging its
          untagged rows with its epoch, rows already carried keeping theirs until the copy translates them (11.6);
          fresh when the path is new to the current epoch, a re-creation replacing a marker and carrying nothing;
          or removed:
removal   a fold never deletes an entry (owner decision 148): a removal at r gives the path and, for a directory,
          every current-epoch entry below it (LIST) a marker {removing push id, r, the path's version (versions,
          above), and, for a versionless file the removing push did not list, its kind-5 segment and slot ids, with
          an alarm}, in version order with the versions below it, by PUT If-Match on the entry it read (If-None-Match
          on a 404) only while that entry holds a version older than r, a marker staying as it is; on 412 it reads
          again; the path's own marker precedes that LIST, so while sources stand no read or copy falls back to a
          source at or below it (11.6), and no repeated, queued or late removal fold writes over an entry a later
          fold wrote, which holds a newer version
collect   markers whose removal r the horizon has passed by a base range (folded_through >= r + 64, so no push based
          before it can commit, 11.8) are collected while the head lists no source, by taskworker's nightly pass from
          the removals the ref's statements name after head.collect.done (a removed directory's markers by LIST), in
          windows: one head CAS raising only the fence sets collect {through: the window's newest r, until_ms: 30 s
          on}, opening only 150 ms after the last window lapsed by the opener's clock; 15.3 s later, every fold and
          copy write planned on an older head having landed or never landing (stale, above: a 15 s deadline the
          store host checks by its own clock, plus up to 50 ms of slew in each of the folder's, the opener's, the
          collector's and that host's clocks, which §19.6 holds within 50 ms of UTC), it GETs each marker of a
          removal at or below through, deletes the kind-5 segments and slot it carries that no hold keeps (a 404 is
          done), and DELETEs the marker once, unconditionally (11.3), unless a hold kept part of what it carries,
          which leaves the marker for a window after the hold ends, each DELETE carrying a deadline 50 ms before
          until_ms by its own clock, or cancelled at once if that clock turns unsure, so the store takes none after
          until_ms in UTC, and once all have answered sets done to through, or below the oldest marker it left, by
          another such CAS; a fold that read a head whose until_ms is ahead writes over no such marker until 150 ms
          past it by its own clock, at least 100 ms past in UTC, nor does one on a process whose clock is unsure
          (11.8's fence row), and a 404 needs no wait, a window deleting a key once; each margin needs only those
          clocks and §19.6's deadline and settle rules, never a measured lag, and on a cluster whose build has not
          passed §22.9's settle cases (FS-114) taskworker opens no window, markers staying
orphan    carried ids never leave with their entry: before a write or delete would drop them (a fold's creation over
          a marker with carried ids, a fold's creation over an entry whose newest versionless version a prefix
          removal in the same fold range did not list, so no marker was ever written, or a copy's unmoved delete of a
          source marker with carried ids), the fold or copy first PUTs an orphan marker idx/<repo>/<ref>/_o/<r as 20
          digits>-<first 8 B of SHA-256(ids) in hex>.e (If-None-Match, equal bytes on 412 success) holding {removing
          push id, r, token path, kind-5 segment ids, slot ids}, then proceeds, so a crash only repeats the PUT; the
          collection LISTs idx/<repo>/<ref>/_o/ once per ref and collects each whose r is at or below the window's
          through exactly as a marker, by the same margins, clock and hold rules, a hold leaving it for a window
          after the hold ends, deleting only ids the path's newest version does not name; its key sits outside any
          epoch, so copies never move it, and evs-4's and evs-5's ttls hold
directory a push's directory change is a delta {names added, child tokens removed} that merges without a path-level
          CAS, since each child's own path is checked, except that a child directory D is checked both ways: a push
          removing D gets 409 with D's path if a delta to D committed after its base, and a push changing D gets
          that 409 if D's removal committed after its base; a fold applies committed deltas to the name table {child
          token, kind, sealed name}; at most 4,096 children and 448 KiB of name table (its EvsName rows: tokens,
          kinds, sealed names with nonce and tag; a carried row counted at its untagged size, so the bound holds
          through a copy, its epoch adding 3-5 B, under 466 KiB at the bound, within idx/'s 512 KiB), checked in
          step 5g against the folded table plus the deltas after h (newest, above; 409 DIRECTORY_FULL), which is
          v0's git limit; the bytes bind first, at 3,584 children whose names are under 64 B; `layout` reserves
          paging; §15 and §16 shard by sequence and size directories by these bytes
name      sealed alone: the name, then 0x80 and zeros to the next multiple of 64 B, under a random 24 B nonce with
          a 16 B tag; AAD repo_id || path epoch || parent and child tokens; with its token, kind and framing, an
          untagged row takes 128 B for a name under 64 B, 194 B under 128 B, and 64 B more per further 64 B
repair    an entry that lacks its path's newest committed version older than the window is refolded from that push's
          record; a version a newer one replaced is reached by the history walk, a dropped one as `dropped` (11.9);
          push records, log pages, packs and parcels are the record, idx/ the cache
keys      idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/<t1>/.../<tn>.e: the entry of path t1..tn sits beside the directory t1/.../tn/ that
          holds its children's keys, and the root's, its token path empty, at idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>.e beside
          idx/<repo>/<ref>/<p>/ (owner decision 231), so no key is a path prefix of another (11.3, 11.8's keys
          row), and a file entry takes one directory and one file on each drive instead of two directories and a
          file; LIST by prefix still lists a subtree
```

Readers check each name against its token, so evs folds committed directory deltas itself, and pushes adding different files to one directory never conflict on a file-mode ref.

**Overlays.** Only git-mode refs take overlays: a ref created from one (an agent branch) records its base (ref, version) and writes only the paths it changes, its first push taking its base ref's current path epoch ([owner decision 232](#od-232)), so overlay and base share token paths at its creation, each cutting over by its own PATH_EPOCH afterwards. The base is chosen at creation as the nearest version of another branch whose tip the new tip descends from, and never changes. It holds a directory whole or not at all: its first push that adds or removes a child of a directory writes that directory as a creation whose delta lists every child it has in the new tree, later pushes sending deltas, so a path reads as the overlay's own standing entry, else absent if any ancestor directory the overlay holds does not list the next name, else the base's, and a removal of an inherited path stands as long as the table does ([owner decision 243](#od-243)). A path it has not changed has the base ref's version at that base version, which its writers (the local tier) and its readers settle and check by replaying both refs; head mode reads no overlay (§18.5's `ReadHead` names no ref). So 5g checks an overlay only on paths its own entries or window hold, TIP settling the rest, a chain citing the base's segments names that base version as a `reuse` source (5h), and 11.9 answers `base` {ref, version} for any other path; §22 covers overlays by FS rows, not the model.

**Reconstruction:** check the entry version against its statement (11.9), read the chain, unwrap its keys, apply the deltas and check the blob oid. Delta bases over 1 MiB spill to the sealed local store.

### 11.8 The evs service: objects, push, commit, reads

**Placement ([owner decision 145](#od-145)).** The metadata tier grows only by whole clusters, never MinIO pools, whose PUTs can pass a precondition in a pool the key is not in (11.3):

```text
place     PUT /evs/v1/repos/<id> first creates place/<repo_id> {cluster id, creator sidecar_id} on the first
          metadata cluster (If-None-Match), naming the cluster that takes new repos (§19.9); on 412 it reads the
          object: the same creator continues on the cluster it names, and for the config kind alone, whose id the
          Genesis fixes, so does any sidecar whose config admin evs's guard honored (every config writer, owner
          decision 352), place/ keeping the cluster and creator it names, so another config writer places a config
          repo whose creator is gone with its repo/ unwritten, its create stopped between place/ and repo/ or a
          restore having brought back place/ alone (owner decision 567); any other gets 409 REPO_PLACED and picks
          another id (owner decision 411); only then does it write
          repo/<id> there (If-None-Match), so of two racing creates exactly one places the repo, and a retry never
          moves it
resolve   evs and gkm read a repo's place/ once and cache it for the process's life, since it never changes (a 404
          for 5 s); every metadata object of the repo and its gkm group, batch records included, lives on that
          cluster, so each ref keeps one commit point
first     the first cluster also holds §7's proj/, projrows/ and rev/, §10.6's per-sidecar gkm/ objects (KeyPackages
          and their claims, ReaderKeys, Welcome pointers) and §21's hold/
form      each cluster's drives and erasure set are §19.6's and §19.9's (owner decisions 116, 139); a repo's
          cluster changes only with a later move tool that keeps one commit point
```

**Authorization.** The daemon's §7 service token (aud `evs`, scope `repo:<id>:deposit|r|rw|admin`, 15 min) never leaves it (I-7). evs verifies it offline, checks §7.8's `rev/` objects for its three subjects, honors a scope only while its newest verified state agrees (D-ACL-21), read from §7.9's verified `{acl_}e` cache, which only api writes, else from `proj/`, and takes the token's (`ur_sidecar_id`, `ur_client_id`) pair as §5's binding, as the exchange bound it when it minted the token, checking in its own state only that `ur_sidecar_id` is an admitted, unrevoked sidecar of the token's network, so a rebind's old client reads for at most the token's 15 min and its writes meet the `rev/` object every write reads ([owner decision 377](#od-377)); `admin` covers FORCE, DELETE, BASE, ERASE, CUT, CLOSURE and its uploads (in the team directory too, whose `admin` §7.8 mints only to its consented, not-read-only admins; 11.12), DROP pushes, their cancels and dry runs, re-seeding, deletion and restore, and in §19.10's re-seed mode only `/reseed` (§7.8). evs-7 is evs's 7-day service log (§19.8).

**The head** (D-EVS-29) is server-internal, never a client wire format:

```proto
message EvsHead {                       // head/<repo>/<ref>; written only by If-Match (create: If-None-Match)
  uint64 version = 1; bytes chain = 2;  // v, C_v
  bytes push_id = 3;                    // the push committed at v
  uint32 ref_kind = 4; uint32 ref_mode = 5; bytes owner_sidecar_id = 6; bytes sealed_ref_name = 7;
  EvsOverlay base = 8;                  // an overlay's (ref_id, version)
  AuthPin auth = 9; reserved 10;        // authorization pin (n, A_n), §7.9: never falls (below)
  bytes group_id = 11; uint64 generation = 12; bytes generation_commitment = 13;  // generation pin: never falls
  EvsPathEpoch path_epoch = 14;         // 11.6
  bytes window = 15;                    // 64-byte EvsWindowEntry records, versions v-w+1..v, oldest first;
                                        // w in 64..127, at most 255 while folds lag (11.7)
  uint32 fence = 16;                    // raised by every write that changes no version (below, 11.13)
  EvsSealLease lease = 17;              // git mode: {push_id, until_ms}, or empty
  bool deleted = 18;                    // DELETE committed; a later push to the name continues the versions
  bytes window_base_chain = 19;         // C at version v-w, so the window's chain is computable forward
  uint64 folded_through = 20;           // 11.7's horizon: file changes folded or replaced, directory deltas applied
  int64 written_ms = 21;                // evs's clock at this head's write
  int64 fence_ms = 22;                  // its writer's clock at the newest evacuation fence (outcomes)
  EvsCollect collect = 23;              // 11.7's marker collection: done, through and a window's until_ms
  uint64 index_epoch = 24;              // on a ref holding an index: its newest CUT's version, else 0 (11.12);
                                        // never falls; a re-seed sets it from the newest CUT it replays
  bytes refused = 25;                   // 16-byte EvsRefusal records, at most 8, oldest first (outcomes)
  int64 refused_ms = 26;                // its writer's clock at the newest refusal fence
  uint64 consumed_through = 27;         // a deposit ref's newest CONSUME mark, never falling (11.12's deposits)
}
message EvsOverlay { bytes ref_id = 1; uint64 version = 2; }
message EvsSealLease { bytes push_id = 1; int64 until_ms = 2; }
message EvsPathEpoch {
  uint64 current = 1;                   // p: the generation whose RK derives K_path
  repeated EvsEpochSource sources = 2;  // at most 3 older epochs still holding entries, newest first; 2 while
                                        //   every due is batched (11.6's commit row)
  uint64 due_generation = 3;            // a generation that requires a new epoch, or 0
  bool due_blocks_creation = 4;         // unused: written false, read past (owner decision 585)
  int64 due_by_ms = 5;
  int64 block_until_ms = 6;             // a mapper's creation block (11.6), or 0
}
message EvsEpochSource { uint64 epoch = 1; bytes map_sha256 = 2; }
message EvsCollect { uint64 done = 1; uint64 through = 2; int64 until_ms = 3; }
```

```text
entry     EvsWindowEntry, 64 B, fixed layout: push_id (16) | statement_sha256[0:16] (16) | place (20) | paths_digest
          (8) | flags (4: bit 0 the push creates a path; bit 1 its change list is in the payload under changes_root;
          bit 2 PATH_EPOCH; bit 3 FORCE, DELETE, BASE or ERASE; bit 4 it replaces or removes a versionless version,
          its record listing the purge's candidates (11.13); bit 5 a DROP push (11.7); bits 16-31 its change count,
          saturating)
refusal   EvsRefusal, 16 B, fixed layout: push_id[0:8] (8) | statement_sha256[0:2] (2) | code (2: the refusal's
          status and reason, from evs's fixed code table) | until_s (4: UTC seconds, rounded up); only outcomes'
          refuse row adds one, and any head write drops each whose until_s its writer's clock has passed, but
          one by a process whose clock §19.6 finds unknown or over 50 ms off drops none
digest    a 64-bit Bloom filter, k = 2, over each changed token path and, when the change list is not inline, each
          covering prefix: indexes from SHA-256("UR evs digest" || token path)[0:4] mod 64 and [4:8] mod 64; evs
          queries a path and each of its prefixes: a match only sends it to the statement's change list, and a miss on
          all of them proves the push changed neither the path nor a prefix holding it
size      at most ~0.85 KiB of fields, 127 entries and 8 refusal records: ~8.9 KiB, typically ~7 KiB with no
          record, so its xl.meta is one 4 KiB block (or three 1 KiB blocks) on each drive; a log page holds its 64
          versions' entries and Signed EvsPush statements and C at both ends, at most ~70 KiB
fill      at step 7 evs appends P's entry from the statement it checked and the place its batch write returned;
          readers never parse the head object (they get 11.9's head summary)
etag      every head write raises the version or, for a write that commits nothing (a refusal record, a fence, a
          seal lease, a creation block, dropping drained path-epoch sources, a collection window), the fence, so an
          ETag never repeats; only evacuation's fences also set fence_ms, and a refusal fence sets refused_ms
          (the outcome rules below)
trust     a wrong place, hash or digest can only produce a missing or mismatched statement, which breaks the chain
          and alarms; the digest cannot hide a change, because readers check every returned statement's change list
```

**Batches (D-EVS-30):**

```text
key       pb/<yyyymmddhh>/<mm>/<instance>-<seq>: the UTC hour and minute the batch was opened, the evs process's
          random 32-bit id (8 hex) and its counter within that minute (8 hex)
bytes     header {"URpb", format 1, or 2 for a batch holding staged segments or purge candidates, instance, minute,
          seq, created_ms, record count} | records | index | trailer {index offset, SHA-256 of all bytes before it};
          at most 256 KiB, or one record of up to 1 MiB; an evacuator that does not know a batch's format leaves it,
          alarming
record    {type, repo_id, ref_id, push_id, signer_sidecar_id, time_ms, length, body}; push: the Signed EvsPush and its
          payload (11.6); part: the Signed EvsPush, EvsPushPart k, its receipts and the head version evs checked it
          at; seal: the Signed EvsPush, its parts' places and each part's changes_root and first token path, the root's
          empty path a 52-byte item of place and changes_root alone (owner decision 376);
          reseed: a re-seeded push or part (11.13); a push's or part's record carries its staged segments
          after its payload, and a push's or seal's record replacing versionless versions lists the purge's
          candidates, a part's never (11.13; owner decision 405)
place     an EvsPlace (11.6), 20 B: where a record's bytes are
open      each evs process holds one open batch per metadata cluster, for repos placed there; a request's record
          joins it at step 6 (a part or seal at its own step), and the request waits for that batch's write
flush     a process writes an open batch when it reaches 256 KiB, when its oldest record has waited 20 ms, or at once
          when it has no batch write in flight there and took fewer than 50 records in the last second; at most two
          batch writes in flight per process and cluster; a record over 256 KiB is a batch alone
write     PUT If-None-Match, the SHA-256 as x-amz-checksum-sha256; a 412 reads the key back: equal bytes are success,
          others a fault that alarms; an unknown outcome GETs the key: equal bytes written, 404 written again with the
          same bytes; with the store unreachable, every waiting request gets 503, retryable, since nothing it carried
          reached a head
bind      step 7 adds P's window entry with the place, so a record is committed only at the place its version's entry
          (window or log page) names; another copy of P (a retry on another process, a part posted twice) is dead
          weight that evacuation drops (11.13)
read      evs reads a record by range at its place; on 404 (evacuated) it finds the version in pidx/ (11.13) and
          caches the record, every reader of a window version's record doing so: the newest rule, fold, purge,
          collect, step 4 and the log route (owner decision 383); readers
          verify what evs returns as before: statements by signature and chain, payloads by the statement's hashes
cache     each process keeps the records it wrote or read by place; they never change
latency   under light load a push's record is written at once, in step 6's round: no added round; under load it
          waits at most 20 ms, ~10 ms on average
```

**Push ([owner decision 2](#od-2)):**

```text
client 1  choose push_id P; build the statement on the head it read (v = b, C_b)
       2  PUT each new segment (chains over 16 KiB; at most 4 at once; a versionless record padding to at most 16 KiB
          is staged in the payload instead, but an ur/lfs object, which is always an upload, 11.7) with ?push=P: evs
          streams it with If-None-Match and its id as x-amz-checksum-sha256 and answers 200 {receipt} (11.13's
          uploads); the client posts only after every 200
       3  POST .../push {Signed EvsPush, payload, receipts}
```

**Linearizability.** A ref's history is its head's sequence of successful If-Match PUTs, evaluated under MinIO's namespace lock with quorum reads (strictly since PR #21653) and read-after-write consistent (§22's suite checks both), and a PUT whose answer was lost, cancelled or timed out takes effect before the next request on its key or never (§19.6's settle rule, D-OPS-20), so the lock's order is the history even when answers are lost. Nothing a push writes before step 7 is visible: readers and writers use only versions whose push the head history names, at the place it names; unfolded versions are themselves in the head. A push linearizes at its step-7 PUT, where its checks hold: each reads an object that PUT's If-Match covers (head pins, path epoch, index epoch, tip, base window), a state evs read in step 4, at most 5 s before it, from a cache at most 5 s old (repo/ state; the authorization state, as fresh as §8.9 delivers it), or a receipt's age. `idx/` entries are read state outside the If-Match, sound by 11.7's rule: each was read after a head whose folded_through it is combined with, and every later version is in the window that PUT's If-Match covers; while sources stand, a path that no epoch's GET found is read again in the current epoch, which the copy writes before it deletes a source copy, and a removed or fresh prefix entry stops any fall-back to a source (11.6). File-mode pushes commit only if their paths are unchanged since their base, as in a serial order; git-mode pushes only on their tip. A refusal the head does not settle linearizes at the head CAS that records it (outcomes), after which no attempt of its push id commits.

**Outcomes (D-EVS-23):**

```text

          evs's client reads a 502 or 504 whose body is not an evs refusal as the lb's, no answer from evs at all,
```

Invariants (§22 model-checks them):

```text
I-EVS-1  a committed head's dependency closure (statements, payloads, entry versions, segments, slots) stays

         drop job)

         that push's statement is the slot's origin (owner decision 399), and a batch record only once Resolve
         finds its push dead or committed at another place

         answered a refusal, no attempt of it commits, however late it reaches evs, save one validated before
         its repo's shred began, which the shred destroys (11.12): the head settles the refusal for good, or
         records it until the statement can pass 5b nowhere
I-EVS-4  pending state never evicts the newest committed version of a path, and a reader finds that version in its
         entry or its push payload
I-EVS-5  no segment becomes reachable after GC decided to delete it: a push, or a seal for its parts, adopts only

         segments and a pending one by a fence on its ref, a ref with no head by a placeholder head; and GC
         deletes a segment only once no batch is left from before its LastModified + 24 h + 2 min, no pidx/
         entry read after that names it, and by a DELETE that names its LastModified (owner decision 203)
```

**Refs.** evs (step 5) and replaying readers check:

| `owned`, record-class: a per-writer stream, `ur/<sidecar_id>/record`, `<sidecar_id>` as Id.String() as in every `ur/` name, ids in paths inside a repo staying 32 lowercase hex (so a requester derives a decider's ref_id from `decider_sidecar_id`; [owner decision 406](#od-406)) | file | its sidecar, creates only, a directory taking add-only deltas, with no removed token, on its entry's newest version, the entry staying a directory ([owner decision 406](#od-406)) | refused; BASE (`admin`, flag 4, the directory's included): only removals, each naming its path's newest version, with no entry version, segment, slot or inline record, changes_root and parts allowed past 1 KiB, else 409 with the paths; it commits at the next version with window bit 3, its statement kept, leaving the live set, and readers take a removal on a creates-only stream only from a BASE a repo admin signed at its auth pin, reading the gap in that writer's seq chain as expired, not withheld; keys go by ERASE first, and BASE deletes nothing itself; erasure by ERASE pushes |

**Gate (D-EVS-18):**

```text
pins      every statement declares the authorization pin auth = (n, A_n) (§7.9's AuthPin) and the generation pin
          {group_id, generation, C_g}; the head records the newest committed ones; generation pins compare
          (g, C_g), a new group_id at an equal (g, C_g) being taken only along a verified GroupForm chain, and
          evs and readers resolve a statement's gen/<g> through the repo's newest GroupForm (§10.8's re-form)
fence     step 7 commits only if (1) the push's pins pass §10.6's gate predicate against the newest authorization
          state evs holds, and (2) neither pin is below the head's (equal versions need equal chains and
          commitments); the head If-Match makes (2) atomic with the commit, so once any commit carries a newer
          state, no commit under an older one follows on that ref, retries included
timing    evs issues step 7 within 5 s of reading the authorization state it validated against, and reissues a
          timed-out PUT only within that window (outcomes, below); api's notification brings a new projection to evs
          within 5 s (§8.9), at worst at its 5-min poll
contract  a removal takes effect, per ref, at the first commit validated against a state that includes it; a write
          validated before then serializes before the removal; so no write sealed to an excluded generation commits
          more than about 10 s (worst case 5 min) after api stores the dropping projection, plus one store request
          deadline for a PUT already sent (§19.6's 10 s, under the lb's 30 s read timeout), or, for a PUT whose
          drive commits began within that deadline and stalled, until §19.6's settle rule releases the head,
          which no read or commit passes meanwhile (§22's suite checks both); the writers' own rule never to seal
          to a generation a non-reader holds (§8.12) stays the primary control; expiries close the gate too,
          through the predicate's time identity (§7.9)
refusals  412 GATE_CLOSED to pushes and deposits below the requirement; receivers answer 451 (§15); new refs are
          fenced by the same check on their creating push; the clause that also held a push creating or
          re-creating a ref in a repo with prefix rules to an auth pin at or above the log position of the
          repo's newest rule set (owner decision 416) is Later with the rules and out of the gate (owner
          decision 586)
```

No gate object exists, and no gate write precedes a commit.

**Readers verify** against a malicious server (I-4, I-16). The signed head of owner decisions [2](#od-2) and [7](#od-7) is C_v over Signed `EvsPush` statements: a head is accepted only if a writer signed every push since the reader's pin, each covering its parts through `parts_sha256` and its segments through `entry_sha256` and segment ids, wherever evs read them:

```text
replay    syncing devices replay pushes from their pin, checking signers against their config's writer set, ref
          rules, the 64-version bound, path-level CAS, C_v, pins, generations, path epochs and tails (no reader
          downloads a map: the copy checks it whole, 11.6; owner decision 230) and,
          decrypted, git oids, descent, TIP and the forced committer on git-mode refs (owner decision 81), imports,
          stream chains (§16.8) and epoch_authenticator; they pin (ref, version, C_v) and alarm on any head not
          extending it
head      head readers verify every statement after their pin and the statement behind each entry they read (11.9)
witness   §6's HeadCheck, which any admitted reader may witness (owner decision 129; D-TRUST-10), compares
          authorization, generation, epoch and ref pins (§6.4-§6.5's RefHead); a lower side reads the ref's
          statements from its version up (11.9) and recomputes C forward
```

### 11.9 Head-read API

```text
request   POST /evs/v1/repos/<repo_id>/read (r): {ref_id, pin_version (0 if none), fresh (no cached head), up to 64

          read, the root's empty in every epoch (owner decision 231), ranges (64, <= 32 MiB), wanted slots, maps, log
          pages, push records and parts by push id, and the DROP pushes whose body the reader already holds and has
          checked, by ref version, at most 64 (held_drops)}; this, the refs and log routes and 11.10's subscription
          routes answer a deleted repo 409 REPO_DELETED and a shredding or shredded one 409 SHREDDING, from the 5 s
          repo/ cache the upload route uses (11.12's refused row; owner decision 379)
exact     An authenticated fresh single-ref read of a file-mode or uncreated ref reports whether this host enforces
          EXACT_HEAD in 11.8 (EvsHeadSummary.supports_exact_head, bool field 18). Listings, streams and cached
          reads omit it. Missing or false leaves the native ACL client at its preview (§7.9). Older hosts reject
          the signed flag. Older readers of either format need an upgrade to replay past a flagged version.
streams   POST .../read {refs: up to 64 (ref_id, pin_version)} (r) reads a record-class repo's owned streams: per

reply     one framed stream of u32 length | EvsReadFrame, each frame one of these parts by its set fields, with no

          present for the path itself or a removal; owner decision 378), a removed path staying removed through a

          which it shows as a loss
collected from T, the end of the UTC minute in the replacing record's EvsPlace plus 60 s, every read of a replaced

dropped   a reader shows a listed version by 11.7's states, which the DROP's signed body, window and cancels decide:

serve     from not_before_ms, unless the drop is cancelled or refused (its void record, 11.13's table row; a drop

trusts    for a path it has never read or no longer remembers (its record evicted, or its record's pin past the
          budget), which writer-signed version is current at its first pin, and, after a
          re-pin past the budget, for every path, is evs's word (it could serve an older version or a refused
          push's entry); every later change is verified; its next HeadCheck with a replaying peer confirms the pin
          (v, C_v), not those versions (§2.8)
states    a path entry's state is EvsReadPathState {0 unspecified, 1 collected, 2 drop_pending, 3 dropped}, with the
          states' payloads (drop_id, not_before_ms, version) as ordinary fields of that entry; format-1 code
          refuses each as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED {needs_format: 2}, and the enum joins D-PHASE-9's reservation lint
budget    a mobile catch-up fetches at most 4 MiB of statements and proofs (4,000-8,000 versions); further behind,
          the reader re-pins at the head and marks the gap, shown as "verified since <time>": the pin record
          holds the time of the newest re-pin past the budget, each such re-pin raises §5.4's evs_gap, and
          EvsRepo.VerifiedSince(refId) answers that time, zero when nothing was skipped (§18.5 mirrors it); a

```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/evs.proto: the read reply's frames (reply, above)
message EvsReadFrame {                  // u32be(length) then this, one part by its set fields, the last with end set
  EvsHeadSummary head = 1;              // first, and in a streams read first for each ref
  EvsReadStatement statement = 2;       // each version after the pin, in order
  uint64 behind = 3;                    // the pin is older than the window: the first missing version
  uint64 more = 4;                      // a streams read stopped at its 4 MiB: this ref's next version
  EvsReadPathReply path = 5;            // a path's, then each of a listing's deltas past the first in its own frame
  EvsReadObject object = 6;
  bool end = 7;
  EvsRefusalReply error = 8;            // the reply could not be finished: the last frame, in end's place
                                        //   (owner decision 378)
}
message EvsReadPathReply {              // one path: its version, its listing, or what stands for them
  repeated bytes token_path = 1;
  EvsIndexVersion version = 2;
  bytes statement = 3;                  // the one that wrote it, when not among those this reply returned
  repeated EvsMerkleProof proof = 4;    // to that statement's changes_root, part level last; empty when inline
  repeated EvsAbsenceProof absences = 5;  // later statements that left this path and its prefixes alone
  EvsRemovalMarker removal = 6;         // a removed path's
  EvsOverlay base = 7;                  // an overlay's path it holds no version of
  EvsNameTable names = 8;               // a directory's folded table
  uint64 names_through = 9;
  repeated EvsIndexVersion deltas = 10; // the directory's deltas after names_through, in version order
  EvsReadPathState state = 11;          // format 2 (states, above), with the five fields after it
  bytes drop_id = 12;
  int64 not_before_ms = 13;             // drop_pending
  uint64 drop_version = 14;             // dropped: the DROP's ref version
  bytes drop_statement = 15;            // the DROP's Signed EvsPush, when this reply returns it nowhere else
  bytes drop_body = 16;                 // its body, which its drop_sha256 covers, on the first path naming the drop
  uint64 entry_epoch = 17;              // the epoch whose copy served it; 0 the head's current one
  bool stale_epoch = 18;                // the request named no token path in the head's current epoch
  repeated EvsDeltaProof delta_proofs = 19;  // one per entry of deltas, in order (owner decision 378)
  bool continues = 20;                  // the next of the path's deltas after the frame before, with its proof alone
}
message EvsDeltaProof {                 // a delta's proof to its own statement's changes_root, part level last
  repeated EvsMerkleProof proof = 1;    // empty for an inline statement
}
message EvsAbsenceProof {               // two adjacent leaves with a path between them (11.6's merkle row)
  uint64 version = 1;                   // the statement this speaks for
  repeated bytes token_path = 2;        // the path or the prefix shown absent
  repeated EvsMerkleProof below = 3;    // the leaf sorting just below it; empty when none does
  repeated EvsMerkleProof above = 4;    // the leaf sorting just above it; empty when none does
  repeated EvsMerkleProof present = 5;  // in their place, for a strict prefix the statement changes by a delta:
                                        //   that change's inclusion proof (owner decision 378)
}
```

### 11.10 Subscriptions

The sidecar reads the statements after its pin (11.9), fetching payloads only for what it syncs, and raises a change event (ref, version, matching paths, signer) to MCP sessions and §18's `SidecarRepoChangeListener`; §18 wakes phones a hint cannot reach ([owner decision 88](#od-88)).

```text
lease    POST /evs/v1/subscriptions, an EvsSubscriptionRequest {repo_id 1, ref_id 2 (empty for *), path_epoch 3, <= 16
         token prefixes 4} (r), and GET ?repo_id= answering EvsSubscriptionsReply {subscriptions 1} of EvsSubscription
         {ref_id 1, path_epoch 2, prefix 3, expires_ms 4} (owner decision 408), writes one lease per
         prefix into Redis {evsl_<repo_id>} (holder, ref, path epoch, prefix -> expiry; an empty prefix is the
         whole ref) and raises {evsl_<repo_id>}v in the same script, then answers 200; DELETE removes them; the
         sidecar retries until 200, keeping the subscription in its sealed store across restarts, and rereads the
         head fresh (11.9) 5 s after the 200; the sidecar API subscribes by dir and subpath (PLAN.md:55) and
         computes the prefixes
renew    the sidecar renews each lease once it is over 24 h old, at a random time within the next hour, never
         because it reconnected; a lease expires 7 d after its last renewal, and a daily sweep drops expired ones
match    after each commit, the statement's changes, or its covering prefixes, are matched against the repo's
         leases from a copy each evs process keeps until a GET of {evsl_<repo_id>}v after the commit shows a new
         value; a lease matches if its prefix and a changed path are on one branch of the tree; holders a rev/
         object names, or the newest projection no longer lists as readers, are skipped; a commit whose GET
         preceded a lease's write precedes its 200, so the holder's fresh reread covers it, whatever the head cache
         holds
epochs   leases name their path epoch and match only in the ref's current one, since their tokens are that epoch's,
         but for a lease on every ref (*) with no prefix, which names no token, so evs matches it for a commit on
         any ref of the repo whatever that ref's epoch while its holder still reads the repo, a device leasing a
         whole repo keeping one such lease, created with main's current epoch, and hinted on every ref at once
         (owner decision 409); a PATH_EPOCH commit is hinted to every lease holder of the ref, whatever its
         epoch, which re-creates its leases in the new epoch (11.6)
sequence after a commit, evs raises the push sequence {evsq_<repo_id>} in Redis by one script: if absent, SET it to
         the master's TIME, read inside the script as server/model/subscription_redis_admission.go:225 reads it,
         in µs x 1,000: the reply's seconds, its microseconds zero-padded to six digits and "000", joined as
         strings, so no arithmetic touches it; then INCR, PEXPIRE 30 d, and a reply of GET's bulk string, never
         INCR's integer, which Lua holds as a double (near 1.8 x 10^18, a multiple of 256); evs parses it with
         strconv.ParseUint and hints with the new value: one past a client's names the only commit between, and a
         skip sends it to the window; GET .../refs returns it; a crash before the raise leaves that commit to the
         hourly resync; the hint's delta also lets a client compare the ref's version with its pin
hint     §6.8's PushHint{topic "evs:<repo_id>", version: the push sequence, delta} per matching client, delta
         EvsHeadChanged{ref_id, version, chain, push_id}, numbered 1 to 4 in that order, version the ref's while
         PushHint.version is the repo's push sequence, coalesced to 10 per second per repo
gap      hints are lossy (§6): a client catches up at once on repos whose versions moved in §6.8's PushReset,
         reading the window or GET .../log?ref=&since= (<= 1,000 versions a page); its full resync of every
         subscribed ref, fresh, runs hourly at a random offset, and after an incomplete reset a background daemon
         first waits a random 0-10 min
loss     leases and the sequence are soft state outside the rdb bundles (owner decision 136); after a loss or
         expiry the sequence restarts above every earlier value, which clients see as a gap, provided the new
         master's clock trails the old one's by less than the lost family's age less 1 µs per 1,000 raises
         (§19.6's chrony on the Redis hosts); holders re-create their leases at their next hourly resync, which
         reads every subscribed head
slots    every script touches one hash tag ({evsl_<repo_id>}, {evsq_<repo_id>}, {evsh_<repo_id>} or
         {evsc_<client_id>}, whose script runs before the lease script), and hints use §6.8's per-client script,
         so no command crosses Redis Cluster slots
caps     pro.yml's sidecar_abuse: evs_subscribers_per_repo, 1,000 subscribed clients per repo, the distinct holders
         of {evsl_<repo_id>} the lease script counts, except the team directory, up to the network's
         config_admissions, whose readers poll the cards ref (§16.11) and lease only notice prefixes q/<h>/<tgt>/;
         evs_repos_per_client, 500 repos per client, counted in {evsc_<client_id>}, a sorted set of repo ids scored
         by last subscribe or renewal ms: one script drops members older than 7 d, refuses if the repo is absent and
         the set holds evs_repos_per_client, else adds it, and sets EXPIRE 8 d; a DELETE removes the repo once the
         client's last lease on it goes; a loss fails open, and renewals rebuild the set within a day; evs writes the
         family that evs-8 names, its cap script before the lease script (owner decision 409); past either cap the
         route answers a QuotaRefusal whose limit_key names the key (§20.7)
```

### 11.11 The local tier

**Git access ([owner decision 24](#od-24)).** `ur mount add <dir>` (cli/UI.md:31-34) resolves or creates the repo and serves it over http and ssh; only the sidecar talks to evs. The server is the system git on a plain bare repository: `git http-backend` (https://git-scm.com/docs/git-http-backend) behind the daemon's authenticating HTTP front, `git-upload-pack` and `git-receive-pack` behind x/crypto/ssh; the bare repository is plaintext like the working tree ([owner decision 47](#od-47)), while evs mirrors stay sealed. `git-remote-ur` serves `ur://<net>/<repo>` wherever a sidecar runs. Repos use git's SHA-1 object format only in v0, the oid's width reserved (11.6): the daemon creates its bare repository with `--object-format=sha1`, and `ur mount add`, `ur evs import` and `git-remote-ur` refuse a sha256 repository, naming it, before any evs write, head mode's codec and export staying SHA-1 only ([owner decision 249](#od-249)), sha256 being [Later](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-sha256-object-format). The pre-receive hook enforces [owner decision 81](#od-81):

```text
helper      git-remote-ur (§4.10) answers capabilities with connect (gitremote-helpers(7)) and pipes its
            stdio to §5.8's git hello; the daemon runs the system git-upload-pack or git-receive-pack on
            the bare repository behind the same hook
names       <net>: a label or alias (§12's ResolveNetworkLabel); <repo>: a display name from the config
            repo, or id:<repo_id>; the first use creates an implicit mount under <state>, with no listener
new commit  one that no ref of this repo's local mirror reaches
committer   a new commit's email is <client_id>@ur.invalid, where §5's binding log maps client_id to this
            sidecar_id (any generation); the name is the agent label, free-form; author fields stay free
set by      ur mount add, ur mount share and git-remote-ur write committer.name and committer.email into
            the clone's config (git >= 2.22, within §22.9's matrix); a refusal prints both
import      ur evs import <dir> [<ref>]: a repo admin's daemon fetches <dir>'s history into the bare
            repository and publishes it itself, not through the hook, as ordinary updates cut at commits of its
            tip's first-parent line (11.8), each with an EvsImport a repo admin's device signs over that push's
            carried commits (owner decision 241), into a ref that has no tip or an owned ref of this sidecar;
            imported commits are held to no committer rule and travel as their bytes, trees that do not
            rebuild from names, modes and oids included (11.6; owner decision 236), so history stock git holds
            imports with its oids; a tree entry name with a slash, a tree naming one entry twice, a tag of a
            tree or blob and a sha256 repository are refused before any evs write; where one first-parent step
            would pass a push's bounds, the import brings the largest merged side into a helper ref,
            ur/<sidecar_id>/import/<id>/<n>, an owned ref of the importing sidecar filled by the same cut
            pushes, and repeats until the step fits, the step's push then carrying its merge commit alone and
            naming the helpers as sources (owner decision 242); a side with such a step of its own gets a
            helper inside its helper, to 8 levels and 64 helpers an import; when the import ends it deletes
            its helpers, whose history evs keeps, so the pushes that name them stay replayable; one commit that
            changes more than 1,048,576 entries and a step that needs more than 16 sources are refused, naming
            the commit; a rerun resumes from each ref's tip and the import's record of its helpers, and ur evs
            import --abandon deletes the helpers of an import that will not be finished; a large merge into a
            busy shared ref takes the seal lease (11.8); from v1 it
            first uploads, through the agent, each git-lfs object the imported tips require (R, below)
            that <dir>'s own git-lfs store holds, so the tip check refuses only what neither store holds
```

**Binding (owner decisions [84](#od-84), [130](#od-130); D-TRUST-8).** Listeners bind all interfaces unless `--listen` narrows them (cli/UI.md:11). Plain http with Basic auth, which git needs before 2.46 (https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.46.0/Documentation/RelNotes/2.46.0.txt), answers only on 127.0.0.1 and ::1; beyond loopback the mount serves only ssh, whose host key `ur mount` prints, or https with the device's §13 certificate, else a self-signed one whose fingerprint it prints (§15.10). HTTP checks Host; an ssh key maps to the sidecar or an isolated agent (§5.5). The http front, on loopback and off, takes Basic with username `ur` and a per-mount secret, 32 random bytes `ur mount add` draws and keeps in the sealed store (§5.9), compared in constant time, else 401; `git-credential-ur` (§4.10, §7.17), which `ur mount add` and `ur mount share` set as the clone's `credential.<url>.helper`, dials the daemon's control socket, whose peer-uid check (§5.8) is the real authentication, and prints the username and secret for a host and port the daemon serves, nothing for any other. The secret never enters a remote URL, an environment variable, MCP output or a log, and grants only what the daemon grants its OS user, as §15.10's credential does ([owner decision 47](#od-47)); no service token is involved, so I-7 takes no exception.

**Refs (D-EVS-28):**

```text
receive   the daemon sets receive.procReceiveRefs to refs/heads and refs/tags and receive.advertiseAtomic to false
          (git >= 2.29; §22.9's matrix starts at 2.34), so `git push --atomic` fails before any write and each ref
          update reports its own status; the pre-receive hook keeps owner decision 81's committer check for all;
          before any evs write the local tier refuses a branch named erasure, ur/index or ur/lfs, one under ur/
          whose second component is not this sidecar's id, and one whose short name starts with refs/ (11.6)
journal   per ref update, before any evs write, the daemon records {old, new} in a sealed journal, and before each
          attempt's first POST its {push id, statement hash, base version, time}; from v1 it runs the git-lfs tip
          check on a git-mode tip (below), whose refusal drops the update (an owned ref's waits); the proc-receive
          hook answers `ok` only after the push is in the ref's history and the local ref has moved; `ng <ref>
          non-fast-forward` only when the ref's tip moved and no attempt of the update is in the history; the
          daemon itself signs again when only commitless versions (PATH_EPOCH, a rekey) moved the head,
          re-tokenizing on 412 PATH_EPOCH (11.6), re-uploads on SEGMENT_GONE, re-posts on PARTS_MISSING, builds
          again under a new push id on GATE_CLOSED, and waits on 429 and a mapper's block's PATH_EPOCH_DUE for up
          to 3 min; unknown -> `ng <ref> remote outcome pending`; any other refusal, a gate still closed after its
          rebuilds among them -> `ng <ref> <code>` (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 8)
restart   the daemon never sends a statement again: an attempt in the ref's history committed, one whose base
          the head has passed never will (TIP), and one that is neither is pending, as `ur status` says, until
          its time bound; settle then runs for every ref whose local ref is not at the tip applied, raising §5.4's
          evs_conflict, an ordinary event naming the repo, the path and the local conflict ref, where it makes one
apply     a device's refs move only by applying evs's versions in order, its own pushes included: the mirror's
          record of the ref first, then, under the ref's apply lock, the local ref, by settle
settle    whenever evs's tip for a ref changes, the local ref follows it when it is the tip last applied or an
          ancestor of evs's, and stays when it is ahead by an owned ref's queue; otherwise its commits go, in the
          git ref transaction that moves it, to a conflict branch ur/<sidecar_id>/conflicts/<ref's name>/<time>,
          <time> UTC yyyymmddThhmmssZ at the next free second, an owned ref of this sidecar that the queue
          publishes as an overlay of the conflicted ref, EvsConflict names both, and the local ref follows evs;
          only settle makes one, the daemon never merges, moves or deletes one, its owner does with stock git, ur
          status lists each until it is deleted, and a ref with 64 stops settling, its local ref left alone, until
          one goes (owner decision 240)
owned     ur/<sidecar_id>/… refs are accepted at once (the journal, the local ref, `ok`; the queue pushing within
          250 ms, then at most once per 2 s, one push for everything queued; sidecar/design/market2.md:518);
          offline pushes queue, and on reconnect the engine seals to the generation then current; a final refusal
          holds the queue and is shown until the local ref moves or ur evs retry; ur/<sidecar_id>/import/… is an
          import's: the daemon takes no client update of a ref there but its deletion
locks     a publish lock per ref serializes one device's pushes to it and is held across the network; the apply
          lock covers only local state and is never held across a request; the sync engine takes only the apply
          lock, so receive-pack and sync never race on a ref and neither waits on evs for the other
Later     the two rows below, prefix and new refs, are Later with §8.8's prefix rules (owner decision 586;
          DESIGN-DEFER.md's acl-prefix-write-rules entry): at launch no device judges a push against rules,
          repairs or pin-pushes, evs's gate holds no clause for them, and the rows give the design the rules
          return with, built and dark behind AclPrefixSettings.Enabled
prefix    under §8.8's prefix rules (owner decision 345) a device checks each push it applies: on a git-mode ref one
          that breaks them fails the mount's check like any refused push, every mount stopping at it with
          evs_alarm prefix_rule naming the signer, the recovery an admin's delete of the ref and push of it again,
          and no mount skipping it, git mode keeping one tip rule; a re-creating push states nothing at a tainted
          token path the stopped span left removed and its new tree lacks, the reader keeping beside each tainted
          path whether the span's last change there was a removal, which clears the taint; in file mode, after a
          device ignores a write, a desktop or the daemon that mirrors the ref and may write the path writes the
          accepted state back unasked, the names 5 min plus jitter after it ignored the event, a removed file
          re-created and a versionless one rewritten from its own copy, a versioned file left alone until 8
          ignored versions lie over it, at most RepairPushCount (60) pushes an hour and RepairByteCount (1 GiB) a
          day per repo and device, `ur evs repair` doing the rest by hand; a repair form's sealed metadata names
          the push ids of the ignored versions it writes over (written_over, 16 B each, in ref-version order, for
          `ur evs log`'s marks only, its absence reading as no list); the lasting answer to a writer that keeps
          breaching is its revocation, which the alarm names (owner decision 415)
new refs  under prefix rules a push that creates a shared ref is judged from a shared branch's tree: a new shared
          branch from its base when that is a shared branch, else from the empty tree, and a tag passes only when
          it tags a commit that is or was a shared branch's tip, which its push names, so a held writer may branch
          off a shared branch with changes under its prefix or tag a commit a shared branch held, but publishes no
          unchecked tree under a new shared name; a filer's no-change pin push goes only to shared branches with a
          tip, never a tag, a deleted ref or a ref stopped at a refused version on the filer's device, a deleted
          branch bound from the push that re-creates it and listed unbound by `ur evs rules show` until then; and
          evs's gate refuses a push creating or re-creating a ref at an auth pin below the log position of the
          repo's newest prefix rule set (11.8's gate; owner decision 416)
index     after each git push commits, the daemon journals the index entries of its changed text files and pushes
          them to its head on ur/index at most once a minute on 1 KiB XFS blocks, else once every 5 minutes (owner
          decision 172; 11.14); a ref DELETE journals a ref tombstone
```

The bare repository hides `refs/ur/` (`transfer.hideRefs`), where the daemon keeps each ref's tip as evs holds it, and runs no automatic gc: the daemon runs `git gc` itself, at most daily (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 8).

**Git and versionless content (owner decisions [141](#od-141), [162](#od-162)).** Git-mode refs hold no versionless version (11.7). A repo's git-mode refs keep their search index on its `ur/index` file-mode ref, written by companion pushes after git pushes commit (11.14). Export skips `ur/index` and `ur/lfs`, so git history stays exact. From v1, git-lfs carries large files:

```text
store     one per repo: the shared file-mode ref ur/lfs, each object at <oid[0:2]>/<oid[2:4]>/<oid> (names sealed and
          tokenized), versioning 1, or 0 in a locked repo (§8.8); its content is uploaded once, and later versions
          (touch, below) only cite it; pointers stay ordinary git blobs, so oids stay exact
agent     ur mount and git-remote-ur configure a standalone custom transfer agent (lfs.standalonetransferagent,
          lfs.customtransfer.<name>.path; git-lfs-config(5), https://www.mankier.com/5/git-lfs-config), so git-lfs
          moves objects through the daemon with no LFS server; uploads run in git-lfs's pre-push hook, before the
          ref update
touch     for each object git-lfs asks it to upload, the agent writes the object's path: a creation, or a new
          version citing the stored content (no re-upload); a creation's 409 means another writer stored it
requires  R(c), the objects a commit or tag c requires: each blob of c's tree (a tag peeled to it) at a path whose
          filter attribute, under that tree's own .gitattributes files (gitattributes(5)), is lfs and whose bytes are
          a git-lfs v1 pointer (under 1024 bytes; https://github.com/git-lfs/git-lfs/blob/main/docs/spec.md)
tip check git-lfs uploads only objects of commits the remote's old tip does not reach, so a force push to an
          ancestor, a new ref or tag at old history, an import, or a push that skips the pre-push hook (--no-verify,
          GIT_LFS_SKIP_PUSH) uploads nothing; so for every git-mode update from old to new, through any listener or
          git-remote-ur, the daemon takes R(new) less R(old), old being the tip the push's TIP CAS names (none for a
          new ref or the first push after a DELETE), by git's tree diff unless a .gitattributes file differs, and
          reads each object's newest ur/lfs version, by a head read (11.9) wherever its cache does not show one:
  fresh   a creation or touch signed under 5 days ago: nothing to write
  stale   older: a protecting touch, all in one ur/lfs push (parts as needed) retried as the journal's pushes are,
          whose 200 precedes the git push's POST, each naming the version read, so a prune that read it fails
          path-level CAS; a 409 rereads the path, a newer version counting as fresh
  missing absent or removed: `ng <ref> lfs objects missing`, nothing published, the hook printing
          `git lfs push --object-id <remote> <oid>...`, which uploads them through the agent, and up to 20 oids, each
          with a path that needs it and when its prune committed, if one did
  again   before a push id's first POST when the check is over 1 h old; an owned ref, accepted at once, is checked at
          receive when online, else before its first POST, where a missing object holds its entry, `ur status` naming
          the objects and the command, until an upload or a later tip that does not need them
  why     an object R(old) also names is safe, since the push commits only while old is the tip, so a prune's start
          read finds old or new (or a later tip, checked in turn); a fresh one is under N days old (N >= 7) at any
          prune start up to 2 days after the check, by when the tip has committed and a start reads it; ordinary
          pushes write nothing more, their objects just uploaded, and an object takes at most one protecting touch in
          5 days
smudge    checkout reads objects through the agent; ur mount sets lfs.skipdownloaderrors, so a commit whose objects
          were pruned checks out with pointer files in their place, and ur names each such object and when its prune
          committed; the tip check keeps every current tip's objects present, so only history checks out pointers
prune     daily, any device holding every ref that may write ur/lfs, whatever its service list, an unretired and
          unparked IndexerSet subject (§7.9) starting at 00:00 UTC plus its offset and any other at 12:00 UTC plus
          it, the offset u64be(SHA-256(sidecar_id || repo_id)[0:8]) mod 43,200 s, a device asleep then running at
          its next wake that UTC day; it reads every ref's head from evs at its start s (syncing a tip it lacks,
          else refusing) and removes, in one push (parts as needed), each object that no tip of that read and no
          commit of the last N days requires (R), a commit counting when its committer date or the time_ms of the
          first push that introduced it falls in [s - N days, s], and whose newest version, its last upload or
          touch, is older than N days at s; N comes from the settings file (below); each removal names the
          object's version, so a
          concurrent touch wins at path-level CAS and the prune reruns; the purge deletes the content a minute after
          the prune commits (11.13)
settings  a versioned file `settings` at ur/lfs's root, one path component of those 8 bytes, which no object's
          2-character first directory can collide with, at versioning 0 though the store's objects are 1, an inline
          record whose body is EvsLfsSettings {uint32 window_days = 1}, marshaled deterministically and sealed as
          any file, so it needs no §2.8 row; N is 30 when it is absent or window_days is 0, 1 to 6 read as 7, and 7
          or more as written; a version counts only if its push's signer held repo admin (§8.8) at its auth pin,
          else devices alarm and use the newest version such a signer wrote; a prune reads it at its start s, and
          `ur evs lfs window <days>` writes it, 7 to 365
```

**Mobile and wasm** run head mode: the evs core with its own git codec and delta code (about 1k lines) reads and writes single files on file-mode refs (git-mode refs are read-only in head mode) and commits only changed entries; mobile never diffs files over 1 MiB, runs at most 2 transfers, and fetches versionless content only on an explicit open, except the search index's, which follows the index's fetch policy. They write their own index entries in the push that changes a document, keep the latest buckets of the repos they sync, fetch the all partition under §18.4's policy, and merge only when out of slots or on Wi-Fi while charging (11.14).

**Drops.** Every mirror and cache applies an executed drop (11.7: `not_before_ms` passed, no cancel, evs not reporting it refused): it deletes from its sealed store the segments, inline records and slot copies that only listed versions name, and every decrypted copy of a listed version it manages (index caches, local stores; §5.9, D-CORE-19), keeping statements and served entry versions; one offline at the drop keeps its copy until it syncs, as with an ERASE (§2.18). `ur history` (11.7) sits beside `ur evs`.

### 11.12 Repos: kinds, naming, grants, deposits, lifecycle, export

**Kinds** are fixed at creation and bound into §10's `ur_group`; §8's `*` matches only `general` and `record`:

```text
kind         one per                            class          read and written by
general      any: git repos, group inboxes      general        grantees
record       any: ledgers                       record-class   grantees
config       network (§7.9)                     general        every admitted sidecar reads; config writers write
directory    team network (§16.11): the team    record-class   every admitted sidecar of the team reads; each one
             directory, also its coordination                  that is not read_only writes only its own paths and
             log                                               stream
team_record  network (§16.8)                    record-class   grantees
mailcfg      network and Team scope (§15.7)     record-class   grantees
vault        member, owner-bound                record-class   the owner's consented devices (below)
mailbox      member, owner-bound                record-class   the owner's consented devices (below)
secret       any number a member, owner-bound:  record-class   the owner's consented devices (below)
             one secret, such as a custom
             domain's ACME account key (§13.8)
```

**Owner-bound** repos carry `owner_member_id` (D-EVS-11). The first consented, not read_only device of member M with an entry to write files RepoCreate{kind vault} (§10's KF1), and M's vault is M's live vault repo whose RepoCreate has the lowest log position, live as RECORD.md section 4.2 reads it, by which writers, depositors and readers all judge at their pin; once its RepoCreate lands, and before its first write, a device reads the log, and if another repo is the vault it ingests any deposit into that one and files RepoDelete{now} for its own empty repo. Only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) read and write them, so one admin signature never makes a reader; others read through a consented device's `EvsShare` or as a Team's visible audit reader, the only reader admins may add, though they may revoke (owner decisions [63](#od-63), [126](#od-126)); the owner's other sidecars deposit into its vault and mailbox, and a `secret` takes only read receipts; MCP's evs tools reach no `secret` repo and never read the config's contents (§16.6). Members refuse, and no writer commits, any other Add or wrap; KF2 parks such a device with `approval_pending`, and the owner's devices alarm on admissions under the owner they did not sign (§10.7, §5.4).

**Naming and creation.** `repo_id` is random, URLs carry only ids (I-13), display names are sealed, and labels exist only in the config repo ([owner decision 59](#od-59)). A sidecar files §8.8's `RepoCreate`, becoming repo admin; `PUT /evs/v1/repos/<id>` then places the repo (11.8) and writes `repo/<id>` (If-None-Match) with kind and owner from the projection and network_id from the token's network, checked against the projection's AclRepo, never changed and kept in the shredded tombstone, `keying` until §10's KF1, or, while §19.10's reseed gate is on, `deleted{deletion_id, its entry's time, signer}` at creation for a repo whose projection ends in an unrestored, dated `RepoDelete` without `now` whose 7 d restore window holds the time, one past restoring answering 409 SHREDDING, so a re-seed's segment uploads and calls meet it deleted from its first object ([owner decision 602](#od-602)); taskworker matches `hold/` and reports stored bytes by that network, a re-seed writes it from the projection, and a reader that finds it absent treats the repo as held and keeps everything. A config repo's `repo/<id>` follows its network's first projection base, whose sidecar alone holds the first `admin` token (§7.9). A team network's one `directory` repo and its `team_record` repo are filed as §7.5 says (D-TEAM-28; [owner decision 303](#od-303)), refused and given admins as §8.8's directory and team_record rows say, api alone seeing the tier (§20.5's `NetworkTierOf`). `RepoKind` numbers the kinds from 1 in the order written, 0 being unspecified (§7.9's record bytes).

**Grants (owner decisions [7](#od-7), [8](#od-8), [60](#od-60), [114](#od-114), [144](#od-144), [182](#od-182)).** Member devices are leaves of the repo's MLS group, except readers of the config and of the team directory past §7.9's first 1,000, which read by wraps; the directory's readers are fixed by kind, which refuses `RepoAdmin` adds, `RepoGrant` and `RepoRevoke` (§8.5, D-ACL-24); tagged, ephemeral, CI and cloud sidecars hold per-generation `ReaderWrap`s or a covering Delegation's wrap (§10.5), and RecoveryWraps hold recovery copies ([owner decision 62](#od-62)). Writers are sidecars whose pushes readers accept. Repo admins and config writers sign the access log (§8.8), which clients verify from the config repo and the token exchange mirrors as scopes. `ur mount share` files a grant, or an `EvsShare` for owner-bound kinds; `ur share` is §9's (D-SOCK-16).

**Deposits.** `Deposit(name, reader)` checks the drop key against §10's `GenRotate_g` and §10.5's depositor rule, then appends entries under random ids, each body under a random key that a slot holds HPKE-wrapped to the drop key (below), to the depositor's `deposit` ref (11.6); entries may span segments, so 50 MiB messages pass the lb (§15). Receivers and tagged or headless sidecars deposit; a reader with `rw` ingests in version order, then commits a CONSUME deleting the entries and their slots. A depositor learns its own ref's version and chain, so it can infer that and when a reader consumed, and nothing else of the head: EvsDepositHead {version, chain, consumed_through} rides a push's 200 on the caller's own deposit ref (the version committed, or for a 5a retry the current head) and 5f's 409 BASE_STALE there, read from the cluster head and final, so nothing is recorded; every read route stays closed to it (FS-23). It keeps the newest in its sealed store and builds each push on it, rebuilding after BASE_STALE under a new push id and new slot ids and keeping receipts under 24 h old; a new ref's first push uses version 0 and C_0, which it computes. The ingester's CONSUME declares consumed_through, the highest version of the deposit ref at or below which no unconsumed deposit remains by its own read, which evs copies to the head, never falling, so a depositor, receipt-only readers included, learns when its deposits were ingested: it prunes its spooled deposits at or below the mark and keeps the rest within §16.7's 1 GiB, oldest dropped first and coverage naming spool_drop, with no age bound, since ingest lets no outcome hold a ref back. A reader of an owner-bound repo that is not its writer deposits only `read` receipts (§16.8): at most `evs_read_receipt_bytes` (4 KiB) each and `evs_read_receipts_per_repo_day` (256) a day per repo, which evs counts through `Quota.CountRate` on the repo's network under a key naming the repo and no day, the push id its debit id, so a retry counts nothing twice, else 429 with `retry_after_ms` to the next 00:00 UTC (§20.4; [owner decision 519](#od-519)); evs sees only sealed bytes, so the owner's ingest enforces the kind, taking from such a depositor only entries of kind `read` with source `observed` and consuming any other without ingesting it, with an alarm.
