**Deletion ([owner decision 82](#od-82))** is a state of `repo/<id>` (D-EVS-19):

```text
state      keying -> active (KF1) -> deleted{deletion_id, time, signer} -> shredding{deletion_id, time}
           -> shredded{deletion_id, time}; every transition is If-Match on repo/<repo>
activate   POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/activate (admin), no body: evs reads repo/ from the cluster; keying: it lists
           gkm/repo/<id>/, reads the newest GroupForm, HEADs gkm/<group_id>/gen/1 and CASes repo/ to active by
           If-Match, no GroupForm or no gen/1 answering 409 GROUP_NOT_READY; active: 200, so a retry is harmless;
           any later state: that state's refusal; the write is P1 for the creating network; evs cannot see
           whether wraps are complete, so KF1's order on the creator stays the guarantee (§10.7)
log first  the device files §8.8's RepoDelete{repo_id, deletion_id, now} or RepoRestore{repo_id, deletion_id} into
           the access log, then calls the route, which requires that statement in evs's newest projection
           (AclRepo) and takes deletion_id, now and time from its entry, else 409 STATEMENT_MISSING; taskworker's
           reconciler applies a projected statement repo/ lacks, so a device killed between the two leaves a
           state the log records, and a re-seed after a site loss can trust the log (§19.10)
delete     DELETE /evs/v1/repos/<id> (admin; ur evs delete): active -> deleted; members get a hint and stop syncing,
           and stored bytes count until the shred (§20.7); with now (?now=1, --now): active, or deleted under a
           newer RepoDelete{now}, -> shredding at once, never restorable
refused    evs and gkm refuse every route but restore and DELETE with now while deleted, reads and subscriptions
           included (11.9; owner decision 379), except /reseed, its segment uploads and gkm's
           GroupForm in §19.10's re-seed mode for a repo re-seeded as deleted (the re-seed exception, below; 11.13),
           and all while shredding or shredded; the token exchange mints only admin for a deleted repo, whose
           standing admins keep that right alone, which evs's guard honors for DELETE with and without now (§8.8;
           owner decision 351), each guard honoring a route's rights only whole, so that admin passes only the
           routes that take admin alone (§8.8's Repo rows, §10.6's checks row) and evs's one marked pass below
re-seed    PUT .../segments, the one route of the exception that takes more than admin, says so in its route entry;
           on it, when the
           state refuses the whole right set evs's guard asks, the host's reseed gate is on and the state honors the
           bare admin right, the guard passes the request holding admin alone, marked as admitted by the exception,
           and the upload takes a marked request only while reseed is on and repo/ shows deleted under the
           unrestored RepoDelete the projection ends in, inside the 7 d restore window, the request holding admin,
           else 403 SCOPE, as the guard would, a keying or active repo/ before repo/ shows deleted included; every
           other route keeps the whole-set rule, so that admin reads, writes and deposits nothing, and a repo
           re-seeded as deleted takes its segments back in a recovery (11.13; owner decision 565)
restore    POST /evs/v1/repos/<id>/restore (admin; ur evs restore): deleted -> active by If-Match on the deleted
           object read; a repo past deleted answers 409 SHREDDING; §19.10's groups step sends it, the route alone,
           for a repo its state shows restored, so a repo/ a recovery's place created deleted while evs's
           projection trailed the RepoRestore returns without waiting for the reconciler's daily walk (owner
           decision 618)
start      taskworker, 7 d 10 min after the RepoDelete's entry, once the newest projection holds no RepoRestore of its
           deletion_id, which api takes only within 7 d (§8.8): deleted -> shredding by If-Match; exactly one of
           restore and start wins, as the log says; members get a hint, drop RK_g and caches, and mirrors drop the
           repo (11.13)
phases     each step rereads repo/ and runs only while it shows shredding with the job's deletion_id, so a stale
           job of an earlier incarnation deletes nothing; steps are idempotent and resume after a crash:
           1 wait 20 s, two of 11.8's 5 s validation windows plus §19.6's 10 s request deadline, so a push
             validated before the CAS has landed or never will, or holds its keys until §19.6's settle rule
             decides it, which the later phases' requests on those keys wait for
           2 delete slot/<repo>/* (keys first)
           3 delete the repo's gkm objects, its group's {gka_<group_id>} acks and recovery wraps (§10.8)
           4 under a preservation hold, stop: the ciphertext a shred leaves stays until the hold ends, evacuation
             still moving its batched records into packs and parcels (11.13; owner decision 133)
           5 delete every other family: idx/ head/ log/ pmap/ pidx/ spidx/ hp/ drops/ and the repo's Redis families
             ({evsq_}, {evsl_}, {evsh_}, {evsd_}), and seg/, pack/ and dropscan/ on the HDDs; its records in shared
             batches go with them, at most 26 h after each batch was written (11.13)
           6 after 10 min, longer than the issue-time recheck of repo/ (cached at most 5 s) that 11.13's P2 writes
             and every gkm write make (§10.6), plus the store's request deadline, so no fold, evacuation or gkm
             write lands later, repeat 2, 3 and 5 once for stragglers; a DELETE's settle copy (§19.6's settle row,
             evs-10) is gone by then, since §19.6 keeps the settle sweep's interval inside this pass
           7 rewrite repo/<repo> as shredded{deletion_id, time}, a tombstone kept with its place/ for the
             network's life
drops      a drop's job pauses while repo/ shows deleted, resumes at a restore and ends at shredding, the shred
           deleting everything (11.13)
```

**Export** (`ur evs export`) rebuilds plain git: git-mode refs with their original oids, rebuilt from each push's sealed commits, raw trees, tags and history blobs, replaying a push's sources first, a version a replaying reader refuses reported and skipped to the ref's next DELETE, and, from the first commit holding a blob a committed ERASE destroyed, with new oids: that blob is the retention row's erased stub, named by the first entry version in the replay that carried it, and the trees, commits and tags holding it, and every later commit of the ref, are written with every other byte their own, the replay going on in the original oids, each rewritten commit's note naming its original (`rewritten <oid hex>`) and the note of the push that wrote a stub naming the stub's token path and entry hash (`erased <token path hex> <entry hash hex>`), while the local tier's replay still meets such a blob as erased, since a mount pushes on its tip's original oid, and a history blob so erased still ends the export ([owner decision 671](#od-671)), file-mode refs with one deterministic commit per version (11.7), leaving out the search index's `.ur-index/` files (its roots and erasure set) and the `ur/index` ref, which are derived (11.14), and the `ur/lfs` store (11.11), checked by `git fsck`, with signed provenance in `refs/notes/ur`; every replaced versionless version exports as the git-lfs pointer to its content_sha256 and size, noted there, whether or not its bytes survive in a store, batch or cache, and only a path's newest version exports its content, and a dropped version as the stub blob `ur-dropped <drop id hex> <entry hash hex>\n`, its mode from its entry version where served, else the next kept version's, the drop noted there; a pending drop's versions export with their content.

### 11.13 Backend, IOPS, GC, quotas, durability

**Store needs (X13):**

```text
needs     ServiceHost.Blobs declares, on every cluster, quorum-evaluated conditional PUT, consistent reads, a LIST
          answered only when it is whole, else 503, as §19.6's list row has it while a set has three or more drives
          offline, or one while another heals (owner decision 226), and whole too for a key whose overwrite is in
          flight, a key an asked drive holds whose xl.meta read failed other than not-found being read again under
          the key's lock, else 503 (owner decision 382), so evacuation's horizon, the nightly pass and
          uncached pidx/ lookups wait in that state, streamed and ranged I/O, object metadata on PUT and HEAD (11.7's
          entry states), a Delete, unconditional or naming its object's LastModified (11.3, §19.6; owner decision
          225), and §19.6's deadline and settle rules: a request refused once its x-ur-deadline-ms has passed, and a
          PUT or DELETE that takes effect before any later request on its key or never (D-OPS-20; 11.7's stale and
          collect rows), each metadata cluster in one pool (11.8) and no lifecycle rule on any bucket, which §22's
          suite checks;
          segment PUTs ride streamable_paths: ["/evs/v1/repos/[^/]+/segments/[^/]+"]; pack/ PUTs stream too,
          with no deadline header, settled 40 s after their last byte, taskworker cancelling one whose last
          byte has not gone 8 min after issue (§19.6's deadline row)
address   a segment is addressed only by segment_id = SHA-256 of its bytes, never by cluster, bucket, pack or
          offset; locators are signed (inside entry versions), so packing never rewrites them; readers GET
          seg/<repo>/<id>, and on 404 look the id up in spidx/<repo>/ (LIST-cached, packs never change); records
          authenticate by AEAD, so a range read from a pack needs no segment hash
```

[Owner decision 140](#od-140)'s binding limits are the drive budget: at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS at the design load, met at ~27-43 KiB a push before [owner decision 148](#od-148)'s markers, which add ~12.5-14 KiB a removed entry (§22.8's fold row counts them); the head's If-Match overwrite alone (~14 KiB, [owner decision 2](#od-2)) sets the floor (Q-EVS-9). §22.8's M2 exit runs this mix at 2× year one with the write budget on, refilled at 0.8 DWPD for the run, a restart included: p99 ≤ 25 ms per operation, at most 43 KiB per push per drive ([owner decision 140](#od-140)), no push refused by the budget, no ref at FOLD_BEHIND and no batch past 26 h, after FS-116's exact-cost run, with P0's bytes by kind measured against the refill to set §19.8's P0 warn line (D-TEST-11); that sizing bounds the drives' wear at the admitted mix only, since P0 work past the refill writes past it ([owner decision 186](#od-186)). Batches are per process and cluster (11.8), so a set near its capacity sustains the pushes §19.9's sets row gives, not the ~490-650 [owner decision 145](#od-145) records, which assumed batches shared across the whole load; §19.9 sizes year two's sets from §22.8's records per batch per cluster. Each next cluster starts at §19.9's triggers, the second at about 1.25× year one (about 1.2× with v1's index on 4 KiB blocks, at [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s cadence; §19.9), and takes new repos ([owner decision 145](#od-145)). v1's search index (11.14) adds to this mix at [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s cadence: on 1 KiB blocks one companion push a minute per writer, about 4 KiB a push, ~34-37 KiB a push at 2× year one, inside D-TEST-11's 43; on 4 KiB blocks one every 5 minutes, about 2 KiB, ~42-45 KiB; year one stays under the ~0.45 DWPD that one a minute would cost on 4 KiB blocks, and §19.9 gives the indexed set's pushes and year two's sets.

**Fair share and the write budget (owner decisions [140](#od-140), [186](#od-186)).** No network can wear or take a metadata cluster, or the segment cluster's drives, from the others by P1 or P2 work, and no count cap applies ([owner decision 66](#od-66)); P0 safety work runs at once whatever its volume, so P0 work past the refill, from one network or many, wears a cluster's drives past the budget and holds its other classes while it lasts (gates, below):

```text
budget   every metadata write spends its cluster's one budget: 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS on the busiest
         drive not under heal (§19.6), a bucket B that every measured drive byte drains, P0's included (§19.6's
         counters), refilled at r = 0.768 DWPD (0.8 x 24/25) with a depth D of 1 h of r and floored at zero: P0's
         bytes past what B holds are P0's excess, forgiven, counted and reported by kind and never repaid (owner
         decision 190); every class but P0 issues only while B holds it (gates, below), so no 24 h window passes
         0.8 DWPD but by P0's forgiven excess, and P0, which never waits, passes the budget whenever it alone outruns
         r (owner decision 186); the other classes' IOs are bounded, not metered: each drive write moves at least one
         512 B sector, so the refill caps their sustained writes at ~33,000 a second, 39% of 85,000, while P0's follow
         its bytes
price    each write is priced before it is issued in drive bytes: the cost row above (§22.8's measurement) times k,
         the measured over the priced bytes of the last 10 min; each nvme run's measured table lands as a code
         change, replacing the default 1 KiB and 4 KiB price tables, PriceBlockByteCount's default taking the block
         size D-TEST-11 chooses, reviewed at M2's exit and before M3's pilot, k absorbing a constant error, and a
         live config value comes only if production's measured over priced bytes drifts past D-TEST-13's 10%
         (owner decision 413)
classes  P0, never queued, refused or paced, bounded only by its classes' own rate limits (§10.6's 60 commits an hour
         per uploader and group, which each gkm process counts for itself; §7.9's per-network append limits; 11.12's
         ERASE rate), never by the budget: rev/, proj/ and projrows/ (kinds revocation and log), hold/ (kind
         lifecycle), repo/ lifecycle (deletion, restore), shred steps, ERASE, CUT and CLOSURE pushes within that rate
         and every slot rewrite, gkm Removes and REMOVE rotations, a staged delivery or claim of generation g+1 being
         P0 only while gkm's newest verified state shows a shrink, an authorization expiry or a compromise retirement
         since gen/<g>'s auth pin and time (the causes of §10.9's REMOVE that gkm can see), and an MLS commit, which
         gkm cannot read, counting as a Remove only while that state shows a holder dropped since the previous
         epoch's auth pin and time (§10.6), else P1; P1, queued per network by evs: place/, a repo's creation writes
         (repo/, its first head) and activate's CAS, per-sidecar gkm/, pushes, parts, gkm commits, Adds, Welcomes,
         KeyPackages, ReaderKeys, LATE key deliveries (§10.6), GroupInfo, path maps; P2: folds, evacuation, packing,
         GC, copies, retention, fences, drop jobs and dry runs
accounts every 5 s §19.6's loop publishes in {nvb_<set>} B and the allowance T: 5 s of r, times 1 while B is at least
         D / 2 and falling linearly to 0.2 as B falls to zero, less P0's measured writes of the last 5 s, and never
         more than B holds less the priced bytes in flight, so T is zero while P0 takes the refill or B is at
         zero; T is the only account P1 and unfunded P2 debit, split as A_U, what unfunded P2 can issue in the next
         5 s within its own rates, at most 40% of T while its backlog lasts, and A1, the rest, T - A_U; a P1 admission
         debits A1 at full price, its own writes plus the P2 work it causes (fold share, batch delete, evacuation,
         parcel and pidx/ writes, its purge), and moves that deferred part into W, so shedding a push sheds its P2
         work; funded P2 spends W alone, through A2 = min(W, B - T - the priced bytes in flight), none while that is
         not positive, and never T, so a push's P2 work is paid once; conservation: the priced bytes issued in any
         window are P0's, A_U's, the immediate part of what A1 admitted, and A2's, A2 spending only what P1 moved into
         W, and the drives write k times them, so at a steady load P1 admits all of T at full price and the drives
         write T and P0's bytes, r while P0 stays under it
wallet   W, per metadata cluster in {nvb_<set>}, funds the P2 work a P1 admission caused (funded P2); P2 with no payer
         (copies, GC, nightly passes, dry runs, a lapsed credit) is unfunded; each process adds in its 5 s report the
         deferred part it admitted and subtracts the funded P2 it issued; the loop clamps W to the priced cost of the
         funded backlog the processes report, so the credit of a push that aborts, of a deduplicated retry or of a
         record evacuation drops lapses; a retry is priced again only for the writes it repeats; a process killed
         before its report loses at most 5 s of credit, whose work then runs as unfunded P2, paid once from A_U; a
         lost {nvb_<set>} restarts W at zero, the backlog unfunded until admissions refill it; priced and measured
         bytes differ only through k, and B, which measured bytes drain, carries any difference into its level and so
         into T's factor, never into W
gates    P0 issues at once, never queued, refused or paced (owner decision 186); its bytes drain B as any class's do,
         down to its floor, and come off the next T; every other class issues only within its account, and no account
         passes what B holds less the priced bytes in flight, so only P0 empties B (one interval's issue times the
         pricing error aside); while P0 takes the refill T is zero and pushes are shed, and funded P2 spends only what
         B still holds, so folds and evacuation stop once P0 empties B, within an hour from a full bucket at the
         stress below; when the storm ends, P0 back at its ordinary rate, B refills by the difference, P0's excess
         forgiven (owner decision 190), and the other classes restart within one interval: funded P2 at once on what B
         holds beyond T, evacuation's oldest minute directories first, up to four-fifths of r while its backlog lasts,
         and pushes at a fifth of r less P0's own, T rising with its factor once that backlog is spent and B refills;
         with pushes then taking all of T, T reaches half of r ~18 minutes later and 90% after ~78, the ramp holding
         back D / 2, 30 minutes of r, in all; P0 is bounded only by its classes' rates, per uploader, group and
         network, never per cluster: 100 large Teams on one cluster, each shrinking every 5 minutes within every rate,
         ask ~57,600 config and directory rotations a day, ~2.9 TiB a day a drive, about twice r, which the drives
         write past 0.8 DWPD and their 1 DWPD rating while it lasts (11.21; §19.8's P0 page)
reports  every evs, gkm, api and taskworker process reports in {nvb_<set>} every 5 s its queued P1 priced bytes, its
         unfunded P2 demand and backlog, its funded backlog by P2 rank (evacuation, page-out folds, other folds,
         copies, packing, retention, GC, drops), its priced bytes issued by class (P1, unfunded P2, funded P2) and
         in flight, the credit it moved into W and spent from it, and its P0 priced bytes by kind (revocation, log,
         lifecycle, shred, erasure, remove, rotation); k is measured bytes over all priced bytes issued in the last
         10 min, P0's included, so P0's measured writes are its bytes times k; T and A2 subtract what is in flight,
         and A2 is handed out rank by rank; {nvb_<set>} also carries a per-cluster at_limit flag, which the budget
         loop sets from FileClusterAdminInfo at 80% summed raw use or 70% inodes (§19.9) and evs reads with its
         allowance, keeping the last value while the key is absent; §19.6's loop splits A1, A_U and A2 across
         processes by the reports, with no network or repo id
order    P2 runs by deadline: evacuation, oldest minute directory first; the folds a page-out needs; other folds,
         path-epoch copies, packing, retention, GC and drops; a fence goes with the work that raises it, a refusal's
         record with its request
queue    each evs, gkm and taskworker process queues P1 work per network (the token's) and serves the queues by
         weighted fair queuing on priced bytes, with tier weights in pro.yml (<tier>.sidecar: store_weight; 1, 4 and
         16), within its A1 share; admission is fair over time too: a write admitted at once, the queue empty,
         advances its network's virtual finish tag as a queued one does, and a network past its weighted share of
         the interval's P1 queues behind the others even while the queue is empty, so a flood cannot spend the
         share before the lighter networks' pushes arrive (owner decision 617)
shed     past 100 ms of queueing delay it refuses, 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with retry_after_ms (§6.5's codes), one
         network at a time, three ways: first the heaviest flood, a waiting network past its weighted share of
         the share window, while a served network of that window, waiting or not, has less queued priced bytes per
         weight; while no flood waits, a network only while it is strictly heavier than the lightest one waiting,
         so equal light loads are kept; and while floods wait with none lighter served and every waiting network
         equally loaded, a flood by id, the larger first, keeping the last network waiting, so a uniform overload
         still sheds; only floods are refused by id, a network alone in the share window is never refused, a
         light network is never refused while a flood holds more than its weighted share, and its pushes are
         served within the interval, while a burst past a network's weighted share, other networks of the window
         holding theirs, gets 429s with retry_after_ms of one interval even when those shares go unused, so a
         burst spreads over intervals (owner decisions 617, 668)
fallback a process without a fresh allowance for 60 s runs P1 and unfunded P2 at half its last shares and funded P2 at
         most at its last minute's rate, and one that never had an allowance, at start, runs them within the refill
         over twice the process count unless the loop's saved state shows B at zero; P0 runs at once throughout;
         §19.6's loop resumes B and W from their saved state, else W at zero and B at zero, its floor, which is
         conservative
backlog  §19.8 exports per metadata cluster, with no network or repo label, P0's bytes by kind and their share of the
         last hour's refill, B and P0's forgiven excess by kind, the busiest drive's wear against its rating, and the
         outstanding work by class: queued P1 priced bytes, W and the funded backlog, the unfunded backlog and the
         path-epoch copy moves left (11.6), each with its drain time at the last hour's rate
bound    no request does more than a part's ~2,060 operations, so an import interleaves with other networks
outside  §19.5's W2 zones still count per address
hdd      per-network fair queues admit segment PUTs on each segment cluster against its drive operations a second
         (its HDDs' reads and writes completed) and its measured capacity, both read from {nvb_<cluster>}, which
         §19.6's hdd row publishes every 5 s with a 15 s ttl, the figures Q-OPS-2's trigger and the drop job's pause
         read; past 50% of that capacity evs refuses the heaviest network's uploads first (503, Retry-After), never
         authorization, deletion, shredding, erasure or closure uploads within their own bounds; §19.8 counts
         refusals by cluster, with no network label
```

**GC and evacuation ([owner decision 136](#od-136))**, all P2 work under the write budget:

```text
gc        folds keep up to four folded versions a path, and markers go in 11.7's collection windows; history stays
          forever by default, except replaced versionless content (purge, below) and executed drops (Drop history,
          below), and record-class repos follow §16's retention through an admin BASE that re-lists the live set and
          keeps every push statement (11.8's refs table), their expired ciphertext staying, keyless, until a later
          GC, which would delete, 7 d after a BASE, only segments that no entry of its live set and no later version
          names, by a mark and verify like the drop job's, under holds (owner decision 246); a deposit's version is
          retained until a committed CONSUME removes it, and its segments go 7 d after that once no other version
          names them; no GC takes a segment a retained push introduced, history records included (11.7; owner
          decision 237); taskworker works from the log, the hourly
          evacuation and one LIST of each repo's prefixes a night, and skips held networks' in-scope objects (§21.9)
when      hourly (so each day everything older than 24 h leaves the batches; owner decision 136), taskworker
          evacuates each minute directory pb/<h>/<m>/ of each metadata cluster once that minute is over 25 h old:
          batches leave NVMe within 26 h, and a small repo's history leaves its parcels within 7 d (move, below),
          except while P0 holds the write budget's bucket empty, when evacuation waits with every class but P0 and
          batches pass 26 h within the hour; it restarts as the P0 storm ends, oldest minute first, while the bucket
          refills (owner decisions 186, 190; 11.21)
resolve   per batch, GET it whole; per record, Resolve its push id on its ref (11.8): committed at this place ->
          keep; committed at another place -> drop; dead -> drop, deleting of the slots its record lists only
          those whose origin, read by a HEAD after the repo recheck, is that record's statement and whose
          LastModified is SlotSettleAge (2 s) old by the run's checked clock, each by a DELETE naming that
          LastModified (a 412: changed since the HEAD, kept), the only cleanup (11.8), a slot of another origin,
          of none or of an unparseable one, an unsettled one and a held one staying, and only once
          EvacuatorSettings.DeleteDeadSlots is on, off in the release that brings origins until one release after
          every process writes them, a dead record's slots staying meanwhile, at most 8 KiB each (owner decision
          399); pending -> raise the ref's fence (one head CAS, or for a ref with no head one placeholder head
          created with its fence raised, 11.8's first row), then Resolve again; parts follow their seal; a reseed
          record, a one-part push's, a re-seeded part's or a reseed seal's (re-seed, below), resolves by its
          statement as a push record does, the fence in place of the time clause: committed at this place -> keep,
          at another -> drop as a duplicate, else pending, the ref's fence raised, and dead -> drop if the push is
          still not committed on the fenced head, a head whose fence_ms is at or past the time this run held the
          record, never because the statement's time_ms + 35 min has passed, a reseed record listing no slot
          (owner decisions 404, 564); Resolve tells a reseed seal from a pushed one by its parts' record type, or
          takes the fence rule for every seal, which only moves a pushed seal's drop from its time clause to a
          fence, and FI-6's oracle takes the same rule
move      per repo, the kept records, one pack or parcel per repo a run across all the minute directories it
          evacuates: once its aged material (these, its parcels, and its log pages older than 24 h, which wait at
          log/ until a pack takes them) reaches 256 KiB, one pack/<repo>/<pack_id> on the segment cluster
          (If-None-Match, its SHA-256 as checksum) holds all of it, then a pidx/ entry per ref, then its parcels
          and those log pages are deleted; below 256 KiB, one parcel hp/<repo>/<parcel_id> (If-None-Match) of the
          records alone and its pidx/ entries, the log pages staying at log/; a repo's aged material
          also packs once its oldest (parcel content or unpacked log page) is 7 d old: in the run that evacuates
          the repo, or, for an idle repo, in the nightly pass, which packs any whose oldest would pass 7 d before
          the next pass
delete    once every repo of a minute directory is moved, DELETE each of its batches, whole (I-EVS-7)
skip      every P2 write for a repo (folds, moves, packing, copies) rereads repo/ when issued, not when queued (cached
          at most 5 s), and proceeds only while it shows active or deleted, or, for moves and packing, shredding
          while a hold/ has the repo in scope (§21.9); so an unheld repo in shredding or shredded loses its batched
          records here, and no write re-creates its objects after its shred; a deleted, restorable repo keeps them;
          a held network's records, a shredding repo's included, are moved as usual and nothing deletes them while
          the hold stands; phases 5-6 remove a shredding repo's once it ends (11.12)
index     pidx/<repo>/<ref>/<v_first>-<id> (v_first zero-padded to 20 digits, <id> the container's pack_id or
          parcel_id, the first 16 B of SHA-256 over its bytes; nothing extends it, and containers never share a
          key): {container kind, versions v_first..v_last with each record's kind, offset and length and the 20 B
          place it had in the batch it left (11.8's EvsPlace), by which a seal, naming its parts by place, finds
          a part once evacuation has deleted the batch (evs-17; owner decision 256), the log pages a pack holds
          (a parcel's entry lists none), the segment ids its records introduce}; a push whose parts
          and seal evacuate in different runs has an entry in each container; a parcel is replaced by its pack's
          entries first, then the parcel and its entries are deleted
readers   a record whose batch is gone is found by LIST pidx/<repo>/<ref>/ (cached; entries never change), a pack's
          entry taken over a parcel's for a record both name, and a range read
negative  a reader whose cached pidx/ or spidx/ lookup misses or names a deleted container, and so gets a 404, drops
          the cache and lists again; a container precedes its index entries, and both precede the deletion of what
          they replace, so one retry finds the object
resume    a run first lists the repo's pidx/ entries and moves only what no container holds (from a parcel, what no
          pack holds); a container with equal bytes on 412 is reused, entries are create-only, and a batch is
          deleted only after its minute's moves finished, so a killed run restarts the minute; the nightly pass
          deletes a pack or parcel with its entries once newer containers' entries name its every record, and one
          no entry names after 25 h
cost      at year two ~6 HDD PUTs a second (busy repos' packs); on the metadata cluster ~3 parcel and pidx/ writes a
          second in year one and ~30 in year two at 10 records a parcel (§22.8 measures records per parcel), and one
          DELETE per batch; NVMe residency 25-26 h for batches, and for a small repo's history at most 7 d after its
          commit plus an hour
purge     a versionless version V of path X is replaced at the first committed version u of X's ref that writes X
          or removes it (directly, as a listed file below a removed directory, or by the ref's DELETE); u's
          candidates are V's kind-5 segments less every segment a version of u's push names, and, in slot-keyed
          repos, V's slot when no version of u's push names it; evs computes them in step 5 from the versions step
          4 read, and for a push in parts at the seal, from what each part's record carries of the versions it
          replaced, whole, in a list marked replaced that no purger or sweep deletes from, less every segment and
          slot any part's versions name (owner decision 405), and lists them in the record of the push, or of a
          push in parts' seal, no part's record listing any (at most 2,048 ids and within the record's 1 MiB,
          which counts its staged tail too, else a mark from which the sweep recomputes them, whatever the id
          count) and sets window bit 4 (11.8)
who       the evs process that commits u: once its step-7 PUT answers 200, or a reread shows u committed, it
          queues u's candidates in memory; 60 s later, the readers' allowance, it rereads X's newest version and
          the network's hold/ objects (cached at most 5 s, a bound held at the DELETE itself: a cover read older
          than it is read again once, and one that comes back past it answers unknown and deletes nothing; owner
          decision 629), and DELETEs each candidate that the newest version
          does not name and no hold keeps: kind-5 segments on the segment cluster, slots on the repo's metadata
          cluster (204: done, MinIO answering 204 for a missing object, cmd/object-handlers.go:2678-2691); a staged
          candidate whose version's time_ms is under 23 h old is left to its batch's evacuation, an older one
          deleted at seg/; at most 200 deletes a second and 1M queued a process (§22.8 tunes both); a stopping
          process drains its queue for up to 70 s; what it cannot delete within 10 min, or while its clock is unsure
          (§19.6), is left to the sweep; it reports as stored-byte deltas in its usage batches (§20.6) each kind-5
          segment at seg/ that it deletes or that only a hold now keeps, at its stored size, a staged one only once
          its batch was evacuated, leaving batch-resident ones to evacuation's report; slots, outside §20.7's stored
          count, report nothing
holds     a hold whose scope covers the repo keeps each candidate that existed at its placement: a staged one whose
          push's batch predates it, an uploaded one whose LastModified (a HEAD, only then) does; content created
          after placement is purged as usual, since a hold collects nothing new (owner decision 133, §21.9); an
          ERASE still destroys keys at once
staged    evacuation decides each staged segment of a committed record as it evacuates the batch: written to
          seg/<repo>/<id> (If-None-Match, its id as checksum; equal bytes on 412 are success) before the batch's
          DELETE when its version is still its path's newest committed version, was replaced under 60 s earlier, or a
          hold keeps it, and, while §19.11's purge is observe, when it was replaced, logged as a candidate for the
          turn-on pass to delete, reads still answering `collected`; dropped otherwise; a dead or duplicate record's
          staged segments go with it; taskworker reports the staged content it drops, or writes only for a hold, as
          negative stored-byte deltas in its usage batches (producer taskworker, §20.6)
sweep     evacuation, resolving each committed push or seal record that lists candidates, never a part's, HEADs each
          candidate that its path's newest version does not name and no hold keeps, staged ones at seg/, and DELETEs
          only a present one (most are already gone, the committing process or an earlier evacuation having removed
          them, and MinIO answers a DELETE 204 either way, cmd/object-handlers.go:2678-2691), counting each as
          deleted or absent for §19.8's urnetwork_evs_versionless_sweep_deletes_total and
          purged_bytes_total{by="sweep"}, recomputing a marked list from the replaced versions, before the minute's
          batches are deleted, so a lost queue or a failed delete leaves content at most ~26 h; it reports nothing,
          the nightly pass counting what it frees; when a hold ends, one pass rereads the repo's versions flagged
          from 26 h before its placement to its end (log pages, then their records) and deletes what the hold kept;
          when §19.11's purge turns on from observe, one pass per admitted repo rereads its versions flagged with
          window bit 4 since its migration and deletes what observe mode kept, as at a hold's end; the side that
          ends each condition queues its pass, both idempotent: AbuseHoldPass schedules EvsSweepHoldEndTaskRequest
          for each hold it ends, before it deletes the hold/ object, and `sidecarctl evs purge-turn-on`, run in the
          runbook step that sets format2.purge to on, schedules EvsSweepTurnOnTaskRequest, a monitor row watching

budget    the purge is P2 work that u pays for at admission (accounts, above); HDD DELETEs spend no NVMe budget,
```

```text
          below) takes the same mark with no extra read
existing  if the segment exists (412), evs HEADs it (one HDD operation, only on re-uploads) and answers a receipt

          the chain under a new key and nonce, so a new segment id
push      the push request (step 3) and each part carry one receipt per new segment, unsigned and outside the
          statement; check h: each receipt's mac is valid, for this repo, its uploader is the push's signer, and
          upload_ms is under 24 h old by evs's clock; parts are checked at part time, and their records keep their
          receipts, whose age the seal checks again
keys      receipt keys are evs configuration, rotated monthly with the previous key kept 48 h (§19.4); losing a key

orphans   the nightly pass first takes each metadata cluster's horizon, from one LIST of pb/: the start of the
          minute its oldest batch names, or 25 h before the LIST if that is earlier or none is left; it then LISTs

          segment whose LastModified + 24 h + 2 min is at or before its repo's cluster's horizon and that no pidx/
          entry lists as introduced is an orphan, which taskworker deletes by a DELETE that names its LastModified
          (§19.6; owner decision 225), at most 10 a second a segment cluster, on clusters whose build passed §19.6's settle cases; it
          raises no fence and reads no batch, so an orphan goes 49 to 75 h after its upload (owner decision 203);

why       a push, or a seal for its parts, adopts a segment only with a receipt under 24 h old at its last check,
```

```text
          and frees their bytes a minute after it commits; other erased or deleted ciphertext stays until a later
          compaction, unscheduled (11.12; owner decision 247)
freed     a drop's listed content counts as stored until its job deletes it or moves it to held: each seg/ object's

          nightly pass corrects drift; inline records and packed segments count for the repo's life, until a later

wait      an eraser's allowance (§20.4's evs_closure_bytes_per_day: 64 MiB a UTC day, never under
```

**Durability (owner decisions [89](#od-89), [90](#od-90), [94](#od-94), [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[139](#od-139), [150](#od-150)).** Erasure coding survives two of four hosts for objects whose every shard exists (§19.6), on 8 × PM9A3 1.92 TB at EC:4 (~7.7 TB usable); with two down, writes get 503 until the cold spare returns one. A site loss loses server-held data (§19.10), so owner devices keep full mirrors of every record-class repo and the config, slots included, as the customer's own copies (no operator copy holds slots or wraps; [owner decision 90](#od-90)): first the indexers designated for `mirror` (§3.6), the owner's for vaults and mailboxes and an admin's for team records and the config. A phone-only user, on iOS or Android, has no indexer (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [197](#od-197)), so the app mirrors `mailcfg` and the mailbox's `vault/` and `i/` and head-reads `m/` bodies, which a site loss erases (§2.18, §15.16). Unconsumed deposits and unmirrored repos are lost.

```text

          packs' contents), the repo's slot objects as their wrapped bytes (fek-wrapped or drop-HPKE), the RK ladder

          re-seed window; for a versionless path, only its newest version's content, a replaced version's dropped
          when the mirror applies the replacing push; for an executed drop's listed versions, only their statements
          and served entry versions (11.11)

          indexer is listed with its services and the newest sign of it this device holds (§3.6)
erasure   immediate on the server; on each mirror, which applies each ERASE push before its next sync (11.12)

          ref re-seeds as far as its mirror holds statements; 5a keeps a version from committing twice, and the

          strips from it every key an ERASE it holds covers, as an ERASE's rewrite does, key indexes unchanged,
```
