### 11.14 The encrypted search index

Each indexed repo keeps an encrypted, versionless trigram index that devices download whole and search locally or, on an app host whose network designates a search indexer, ask it (remote search, below), so evs never sees a query (owner decisions [151](#od-151)-[156](#od-156), [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178)). Every committer updates it. An indexer serving the repo for search is one whose `IndexerSet` names `search` at a scope covering the repo (network scope: repos other than members' owner-bound ones; member scope, or a personal network's network scope: that member's own; §7.9); it runs roll-ups, backfills and verification first (owner decisions [150](#od-150), [157](#od-157)), but a network has none by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)), so each row's fallback below (the next capable writer, a desktop or the daemon, the first writer after expiry) is the default path, and a roll-up still needs a writer of the ref. This subsection owns its placement, format, upkeep, erasure and read path, remote search included; §5.9 holds the local cache (D-CORE-16), §18.4 each device's fetch policy, remote mode and targets, §16.10 and §18.5 the tools, and §15.7, §16.8 and §16.11 their documents' fields.

**Placement and settings.**

```text
in-ref    a file-mode ref whose documents change in place (a mailbox's or group inbox's ref, a general repo's or
          vault's file-mode refs) holds its own index under <root> = .ur-index/i1; a push that changes a document
          changes the index in the same statement, so one head CAS commits both (11.8)
companion git-mode refs hold no versionless file (11.7) and record-class streams take creates only (11.8), so each
          repo's are indexed on one shared file-mode ref, ur/index (<root> = i1), by companion pushes (commit path,
          below); a document's key names its ref, so one root serves every branch and stream of the repo
settings  <root>/settings, a versioned IndexSettings (files and format, below); a version counts only if one of
          the repo's admins (§8.8) signed it, else devices alarm and use the newest version an admin signed; absent,
          the index is on, with 30-day windows; `ur evs index on|off|window <days>` writes every root's settings in
          a repo, and `ur evs index status|rebuild` reports coverage and sizes or rebuilds under the lock
files     every other index file is versionless, versioning 2 (11.7), whatever the repo's versioning rules say
          (owner decision 159), and a repo lock does not refuse 2 (owner decision 168)
never     config, mailcfg and secret repos; .ur-index/ paths and index files; binaries; a mailbox's i/, r/, vault/,
          o/, forward, ra/, f/ and s/model (only m/ messages are mail documents); deposits before their ingest; an
          index covers only documents every reader of its ref can open, so a mailbox's never covers vault/
head      no single index head exists: the listing of <root> at a ref version is the index's state, each file's
          plaintext SHA-256 in its entry version (11.7's content_sha256), its buckets' and all's manifests naming
          their shards; one head file written by every committer would turn disjoint pushes into 409s
```

**Documents.**

```text
document  a text file; a mail message (§15.7's m/ files); a record entry, or a document §16.8 derives from entries
          (a run card); text past 1 MiB is one document per 1 MiB of the file, each with the next 256 B, so a
          query of up to 256 B across a boundary is found and an append to a large file re-indexes its last chunk;
          a term reaching further past a boundary, or terms ANDed across two chunks, are in no document, and
          SearchOracle evaluates each query per document, not per file
key       doc_key = HMAC-SHA256(K_ref, "UR evs 1.0 doc" || ref_id || u16be(len(name)) || name || u32be(chunk))[:16];
          name = the path's bytes, or a derived document's registered name (a run card run/ || run_id, a directory
          announcement a/ || announcement_id); K_ref from RK_1 (§10.5), so keys survive rotations and path epochs;
          a rename is a removal and a creation
version   the path's entry version (11.7's versions: known before the commit, never restarting, overlays included);
          a run card's, the index_epoch its push names times 2^32 plus the stream version of its run's newest
          source entry (§16.10; owner decision 459), and a directory announcement's, the Announcement's; everywhere
          the newest version of a key wins, and a removal is a tombstone at its version, as is a version that drops
          a chunk, for that chunk's key; a ref DELETE is a ref tombstone at the ref version it commits at, above
          every version of the ref's documents before it and below every re-creation's (11.7's versions); no
          version of a path's key exceeds the effective ref version it commits at, which hosts with the text hold
          every entry to (the reads' coverage row; owner decision 669)
sniff     a file is text when its first 8,000 bytes hold no NUL and are valid UTF-8 but for a cut final sequence
          (git's rule), or it opens with a UTF-16 byte-order mark and is decoded; a chunk whose key set would encode
          past 512 KiB, which nearly every query would match, or that alone would not fit a shard by
          protocol/INDEX-FORMAT.md's D6, is skipped (caps, below); a version that turns binary or skipped is a
          tombstone at its version
fields    1 subject, 2 from, 3 to (to and cc), 4 title, 5 body; 6-15 registered per document class, each
          class's numbers and its uses of 4 and 5 where the class is written: §16.8's record entries and run
          cards and §16.11's directory documents; started, expires, private and tainted are the row's
          attributes, not fields; one posting set covers every field, and a field-scoped query is confirmed
          against the doc table row (at most 2 KiB, 256 B a field), which costs nothing for header fields
          (12.6-17.3% less index than per-field postings)
directory the team directory's derived documents (§16.11): one per announcement, from the card or repo file holding
          it, its version the Announcement's, and one per stream entry; a renewal keeps the version and writes no
          index entry, and an item dropped from its card after its end writes no tombstone, only a withdrawal
          or a revocation does (owner decision 181); the kind's window is 7 days by default (7-90; a window_days
          of 0, or no settings, means 7 there), and it refuses IndexSettings.off (owner decision 171, over owner
          decision 156's general rule, for this repo)
extract   extractor 1, every byte of which protocol/INDEX-FORMAT.md fixes and testdata/index/conformance/ pins; it
          calls no library parser, reads damaged input by rule and refuses none; mail: the message's own Subject,
          From, To and Cc values with RFC 2047 words decoded (fields 1, 2 and 3, To before Cc), and in field 5, in
          the message's order and joined by one space, each part's name and each text/plain and text/html part's
          text, MIME-decoded (RFC 2045, 2231), HTML with its tags, scripts and styles removed and its character
          references decoded; every alternative is read, an attachment gives its name alone, a message/rfc822 part
          is one, and multiparts are read 16 deep; never transport headers, attachment bytes or base64; files: the
          title is the first line holding a letter or a number, without its heading marks, at most 80 B; field 4 is
          the title, a space and the path, and field 5 the text; records: §16.8's mapping of an entry's sealed body;
          every chunk of a document carries its fields 1-4; the extractor's id is in every file header
          (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 11)
own       extractor 1 defines its own base64, quoted-printable, HTML character-reference, header and whitespace
          rules, each a rule of the index format that protocol/INDEX-FORMAT.md writes out, with HTML's reference
          table in the repository (testdata/index/conformance/entities.json) and conformance vectors holding the
          index's extractor and SearchOracle to it, so no standard-library parser's behavior is part of the
          format and no Go release changes an index; a logical header line, and the joined values of one header
          name, are cut at HeaderMax (16,384 B), and a multipart delimiter line or a quoted-printable soft line
          break whose trailing blank run passes LineWindow (1,024 B) reads as text, so extraction runs in one
          pass in at most 150 KiB beyond the normalizer, whatever the message (11.15; owner decision 389)
charsets  extractor 1 decodes a MIME part, RFC 2047 word or RFC 2231 value through
          golang.org/x/text/encoding/htmlindex from the pinned module, a charset label read as bytes and the
          replacement encoding's labels passing as bytes (owner decision 389); no charset or an unknown label is
          read as UTF-8, and invalid bytes go to U+FFFD at normalization
html      extractor 1's own scanner on the decoded text, no parser library: <script> and <style> go with their
          content, up to the matching end tag, case-insensitive; comments, <!...> and <?...> go; a tag is <, then a
          letter or /, to the next > outside quotes; a tag in the block list (address, article, aside, blockquote,
          br, center, dd, details, dialog, dir, div, dl, dt, fieldset, figcaption, figure, footer, form, h1-h6,
          header, hgroup, hr, li, main, menu, nav, ol, p, pre, section, summary, table, tbody, td, tfoot, th,
          thead, tr, ul) becomes one space and any other tag nothing; then character references decode by the
          format's own rule and that table of names, so &lt; stays text (owner decision 389)
readings  (owner decision 389, each pinned by a vector in testdata/index/conformance/) a file's UTF-8 byte-order
          mark is dropped; names compare by ASCII case, and only ASCII whitespace is trimmed; an unterminated
          multipart's last part keeps its last line break; of two RFC 2231 pieces of one name, kind and section
          the first counts, and sections that join to nothing fall through to the extended piece, then the plain
          one; a section number is 1 to 9 digits; base64 decodes a last partial group, and inside an encoded word
          skips nothing; quoted-printable passes control bytes, has no line limit and keeps a line's trailing
          blanks, and a soft line break may hold blanks before its line end; a numeric character reference needs
          one digit, &#x; is text, a number past U+10FFFF is U+FFFD, and all 2,231 of HTML's names decode;
          SearchHit.correction is at most 256 B and SearchCoverage.chain at most 32 B; extractor 1 keeps its
          number; a part directly inside a multipart/digest with no Content-Type is message/rfc822 and not
          entered; the block list stays the 44 names above; format=flowed is not read
```

**Normalization (normalizer 1).**

```text
text      invalid UTF-8 -> U+FFFD; NFKC; full case folding, cases.Fold() followed by a fixed map, U+AB70-U+ABBF to
          U+13A0-U+13EF and U+13F8-U+13FD to U+13F0-U+13F5, which x/text's fold swaps, published with the tables so
          SearchOracle applies it too and a no-op on a correct fold; accents: NFD, nonspacing marks after a Latin,
          Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic or Hebrew letter dropped, NFC (so が and กิน keep their marks and Hangul stays one
          syllable); each run of code points that are not letters, marks or numbers -> one space (so Indic vowel
          signs stay); subject, from, to and title cut at 1 KiB on a code point; each field padded with one space
          each side, fields joined in field order
tables    golang.org/x/text links Unicode 15.0.0 tables under Go < 1.27 and 17.0.0 under Go 1.27
          (.gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.43.0/unicode/norm/tables15.0.0.go:3, tables17.0.0.go:3; cases/ alike),
          and connect and sdk declare go 1.27.4 (connect/go.mod:3, sdk/go.mod:3): normalizer 1 is Unicode 17.0.0
          from one x/text module version, at least v0.43.0, linked by every leg with one toolchain, since one
          norm.Version does not fix NFC: v0.40.0 and v0.41.0 compose U+05D2 U+0307 to U+105C9 and U+05DA U+0307 to
          U+105E4 (U+FB32 and U+FB3A alike), where v0.42.0 and v0.43.0 keep them, all reporting 17.0.0, examples
          of a defect covering 19,960 two-rune strings, supplementary letters included (U+10044 U+0307 to U+1E0A;
          §4.7), which is why every module of connect, sdk, server and sn requires v0.43.0 (connect/go.mod:33);
          headers record norm.Version, cases.UnicodeVersion and the module version; another table or module
          version is another normalizer, and a rebuild; testdata/index/ pins the fold map: U+13A0 and U+AB70 both
          give U+13A0, U+13F0 and U+13F8 both give U+13F0
trigrams  every 3-byte window of the normalized UTF-8; a document's set of distinct 24-bit keys; an aligned CJK
          character is one trigram, so one- and two-character queries resolve
```

**Files and format.** protocol/INDEX-FORMAT.md writes these bytes out in full, pinned by testdata/index/ vectors, for M10's entry review.

```text
paths     <root>/settings, <root>/lock, <root>/a/m and <root>/a/<n> (the all partition); per bucket <root>/b/<S>/m,
          <root>/b/<S>/s/<n> (bucket shards) and <root>/b/<S>/w/<h>/<writer>/<k> (slots: <writer> the sidecar_id in
          hex, <h> hex of SHA-256(<writer>)[0], k 0-15) and .../<writer>/L<seq> (large entries); per ref, beside its
          roots, its erasure set x (.ur-index/x on a file-mode ref, x on ur/index), an IndexErasureSet only a CUT
          writes (11.12); names are sealed and tokenized like any path; ASCII throughout: <S> the bucket's start
          day as unpadded decimal, <n> an unpadded decimal shard number from 0, a new shard taking the manifest's
          highest n plus 1 and joined shards keeping the lower n, <k> in w/ unpadded decimal 0-15, L<seq> L and
          the unpadded decimal seq, <writer> the sidecar_id in lowercase hex and <h> its first two digits
slot      one writer's entries, at most 16,208 B, so its record (11.6's 160 B header and one 16 B frame tag) is 16
          KiB and is staged in its push's batch (11.7); a writer's head is its slot with the highest seq, and keeps
          one entry per doc_key, a newer one replacing the writer's older one there; a slot's entries sort ascending
          by their 16 B key (doc_key, or ref_id for a ref tombstone), then by kind, one entry a key, a replacing
          entry taking its predecessor's sorted place, so a head is a function of its entry set, and decoders
          refuse out-of-order or repeated keys
entry     kind (1 full, 3 tombstone, 4 ref tombstone; 2, a diff's, is reserved and a decoder refuses it, since every
          entry is full or a tombstone: owner decision 584) | doc_key (a ref tombstone: ref_id) | VByte version |
          VByte time (s) | full: row | key set; encoded from its own document only
row       doc kind (file, mail, record, derived) | VByte flags (bit 0 tainted, from the push's provenance; bit 1
          outside: mail from outside the network, or an EvsImport's content; bit 2 private, a directory document's;
          bits 3-17 a field cut at its cap) | VByte size | VByte chunk | VByte trigram count | VByte started and
          expires (s; a derived document's, else 0) | ref_id (in ur/index only) | locator (the path or derived name,
          at most 512 B), subject, from, to, title (each at most 160 B) and §16.8's and §16.11's registered display
          fields (each at most 256 B), each a VByte length and UTF-8 cut on a code point, file and mail rows
          stopping after title and record and derived rows then holding fields 6-15 in number order, each with its
          length, 0 when empty; at most 2 KiB: each field is first cut to its own cap, setting flag bit 2+n for
          field n, and a row still past 2,048 B walks locator, then fields 1-4, then 6-15, each keeping what the
          2,048 B leave after the fixed part and the fields before it, cut on a code point, its flag bit set; flag
          bit 18 says the locator is cut, or held a non-UTF-8 path mapped to U+FFFD, so it is not the exact path
key set   VByte count, then VByte gaps between ascending keys, the first gap key + 1
large     one full entry over 8 KiB, alone, at most 1 MiB, a segment upload; its writer removes it once it is
          absorbed (commit path's dependency row)
shard     at most 1,032,192 B before its pad and 1 MiB with it (the Padmé step there is 16 KiB), so every index
          file is one ?closure=1 upload (11.12): "URix" | header | doc table | tombstones | dictionary | postings |
          pad
doc table live documents ascending by doc_key, a document's docid its rank: doc_key, VByte version, VByte time,
          row; no row refers to another
tombstones the deletions a bucket keeps for older partitions until its roll-up (merges, roll-up): header field
          15's count of entries ascending by kind, then key: kind (3 tombstone, 4 ref tombstone) | doc_key or
          ref_id | VByte version | VByte time (s), with no postings; a key at most once in a shard and never in
          both its tables, a ref tombstone only on ur/index, and none in an all shard
dictionary VByte block count; per block of 64 keys (1 to 64 in a rewrite that keeps a replaced partition, shrink
          below; decoders refuse an empty or larger block and re-encode from the file's own partition), its first key
          (3 B) and the VByte offsets of its entries and of its first list, both absolute, the entries' from the
          first byte after the block index and the list's from the first byte of the postings; per key, ascending: a
          byte {bits 0-1 prefix shared with the previous key of its block, 0 for a block's first; bit 2 bitset}, the
          key's other bytes, VByte document count, VByte list bytes; a 1 MiB shard's block index is typically ~10-16
          KiB (more for CJK-heavy text), so a phone finds a key's list by frame
postings  per key, VByte gaps between ascending docids (the first, docid + 1) or a bitset of ⌈N/8⌉ bytes, whichever
          is shorter, VByte on a tie; document-level, with no positions; in a bitset docid d is bit d & 7 (least
          significant first) of byte d >> 3, unused high bits of the last byte zero, and N is the shard's live
          document count, IndexFileHeader.count
pad       slots and large entries: none of their own, since their sizes add per document; a shard: zero bytes,
          u32be(HMAC-SHA256(K_index_g, "pad" || SHA-256(the shard before its pad))[0:4]) mod the Padmé step at its
          length (§10.5's index key at the writer's newest generation g, which the header names: K_index_g =
          HKDF-SHA256(RK_g, salt repo_id, info "UR evs 1.0 index" || u64be(g)), with no further context, g the
          header's pad_generation, the HMAC's input the 3 ASCII bytes "pad" then the 32-byte SHA-256), so a shard's
          size does not show which trigrams a probe document shares with others, even at a padding boundary; a
          CLOSURE pads to the replaced version's exact length instead (erasure, below); every index file carries
          IndexFileHeader.body_length, and everything past those bytes is pad, all zero bytes, else index_malformed,
          so a decoder takes any such pad on any file type within the file's size bound and re-encoding keeps the
          file's pad length; a writer's next head rewrite writes no pad
codes     VByte, bitsets and front coding only; VByte is unsigned LEB128, as encoding/binary.AppendUvarint writes
          it: 7 bits a byte, least significant group first, the high bit set on every byte but the last, minimal, at
          most 10 bytes; an entry's kind, a row's doc kind and a tombstone's kind are one byte each (entry 1, 3 or
          4, 2 being reserved; doc kind 1 file, 2 mail, 3 record, 4 derived, SearchHit.doc_kind's values; tombstone
          3-4), any other value non-canonical; doc_key and ref_id are 16 raw bytes; nothing is compressed across
          documents, since inbound mail and collaborators' commits can inject probes (a compression oracle); a
          shard's dictionary and lists, the only structures shared across documents, sit under the keyed pad
determinism a file is a function of its inputs: pinned tables and ids, docids by doc_key, ascending keys, minimal
          VByte, the shorter-list rule, blocks of 64 (or the replaced partition, shrink below; merges and roll-ups
          always re-block by 64, and both outcomes are functions of the inputs, so reproduction holds), no clock,
          randomness or library-version input; headers and
          manifests are proto3 marshaled deterministically, repeated fields sorted; devices that build one file
          from the same inputs write the same plaintext, whose SHA-256 its entry version carries (11.7); a check
          by rebuild of the team directory's cards ref compares an announcement's row less its expires, which a
          renewal leaves at the content-changing version's (§16.11's versions row; owner decision 605)
shrink    any rewrite padded to a replaced length (a CLOSURE or a DROP's rewrite; a roll-up rewrites nothing in
          place, owner decision 385) first
          builds the shard canonically, in blocks of 64, and pads if that fits the replaced length; if not, it
          rebuilds keeping the replaced shard's block partition, each block keeping its surviving keys, prefix
          sharing resetting at each block's first key, and an emptied block going: a removed key saves at least 4 B
          and costs the next key at most 2, so this always fits; the rewrite keeps the replaced header's
          pad_generation
caps      a writer holds at most 16 slots in a bucket; a bucket's shards and a/ at most 3,500 files each (11.7's
          name table): shards below n = 3,499 at a/<n>, and from there at a/<k>/<n> with k = 3,499 + (n - 3,499) /
          1,000 rounded down, so shard 3,499 is a/3499/3499 and shard 4,499 a/3500/4499, no file moving at the split
          and a/ inside 11.7's 3,584 names until some 84,000 shards; a document whose key set would encode past
          KeySetMax, or which alone would not fit a shard, a test every device computes from its key set and row
          at extraction, is skipped (no entry, a tombstone where it was indexed before) and not searchable, so no
          merge, push past 256 KiB or roll-up meets a document it cannot place (owner decision 394)
```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/evsindex.proto: plaintext inside index files, which evs seals as any file; index format 1
message IndexSettings {                 // <root>/settings, versioned; only a repo admin's version counts
  bool off = 1;                         // false (the default): the index is on
  uint32 window_days = 2;               // 0 means 30; else 7-365
}
message IndexLock {                     // <root>/lock, versionless; an empty holder is free
  bytes holder_sidecar_id = 1; uint32 bucket_start_day = 2; int64 until_ms = 3;
}
message IndexErasureSet {               // x beside a ref's roots (paths, above): versionless, staged, at most
                                        // 16,208 B; only a CUT writes it (11.12)
  uint64 listed_since = 1;              // every erasure whose CUT named an index_epoch at or above it is listed,
                                        // and every pending one
  repeated IndexErasure erasures = 2;   // sorted by erasure_id
}
message IndexErasure {
  bytes erasure_id = 1;                 // 16 random bytes an erasure draws; its CLOSUREs' and ERASEs' notes name it
  bytes eraser_sidecar_id = 2;
  uint64 epoch = 3;                     // the index_epoch the CUT that added it named
  int64 cut_ms = 4;                     // that CUT's signed time_ms
  repeated IndexErased docs = 5;        // sorted by doc_key
}
message IndexErased { bytes doc_key = 1; uint64 version = 2; }  // every indexed version up to it is erased
message IndexFileHeader {               // after "URix", VByte-length-prefixed, leading each slot, large entry and shard
  uint32 format = 1;                    // 1
  uint32 type = 2;                      // 1 slot, 2 large entry, 3 bucket shard, 4 all shard
  uint32 normalizer = 3; uint32 extractor = 4; string unicode_version = 5;  // norm.Version, as linked
  uint32 bucket_start_day = 6; uint32 bucket_days = 7;   // slots, large entries and bucket shards
  bytes writer_sidecar_id = 8; uint32 seq = 9;           // slots and large entries
  repeated IndexCoverage coverage = 10; // companion heads and backfillers': per content ref, sorted by ref_id
  uint64 pad_generation = 11;           // shards: the generation whose index key drew the pad
  uint32 body_length = 12; uint32 count = 13;            // bytes before the pad; entries or documents
  string text_module_version = 14;      // golang.org/x/text's module version, as linked (runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo)
  uint32 tombstones = 15;               // shards: the tombstone table's entries; 0 in an all shard
}
message IndexCoverage {                 // horizon: every writer's, set by a backfiller (commit path's coverage)
  bytes ref_id = 1; uint64 version = 2; bool horizon = 3;
}
message IndexManifest {                 // <root>/b/<S>/m and <root>/a/m, versionless
  uint32 start_day = 1; uint32 days = 2;          // a bucket's window
  repeated IndexShard shards = 3;                 // in document order
  repeated IndexWatermark absorbed = 4;           // a bucket's: per writer, the highest slot seq its shards hold
  uint32 rolled_through_day = 5;                  // a/m: the first day of the newest bucket rolled up
}
message IndexShard { uint32 n = 1; uint32 docs = 2; uint32 first_day = 3; uint32 last_day = 4; }  // a/: bucket days held
message IndexWatermark { bytes writer_sidecar_id = 1; uint32 seq = 2; }
```

**Buckets.**

```text
window    bucket S holds UTC days [S, S+W), S counted from 1970-01-01, its W fixed when it is created and kept in
          its files; the first starts at ⌊day/W⌋·W, each next where the newest ends, whole empty windows skipped; a
          changed W applies from the next bucket
entry     an entry goes to the bucket of its push's signed time_ms (11.6), which evs keeps within 10 min of its
          clock, or to the newest bucket already holding an entry of its document where that is newer, so clock
          skew at a boundary never leaves a newer version in an older bucket; the first writer into a window
          creates its bucket
latest    the window holding today and the one before it: 30 to 60 days at the default (owner decision 152); a
          bucket older than both is expired, and stays searched until its roll-up lands
```

**Commit path.**

```text
in-ref    the sidecar building a push extracts each changed document and appends an entry to its head: a full set,
          or a tombstone for a removal (dependency, below); the head's new version, staged, joins the push's
          statement, so the index commits with the content (owner decision 153); from format 2 a push that changes
          no document carries index_none (coverage, below), so it counts as indexed with no entry
dependency every entry is full or a tombstone, encoded from its own document alone, so no entry rests on another and
          a reader, a merge or a roll-up takes each as it stands (owner decision 584, which ended the diffs owner
          decision 385 had rested on their writer's own files); every push that writes a writer's file in a bucket
          replaces that writer's head there at the version its base showed, a head sealed as it stood written again
          with its own bytes, so a writer's pushes commit one at a time, and a merge reads no head and writes or
          removes no writer's file (owner decision 385): a writer reuses its absorbed slots and removes its absorbed
          large entries at its next push in the bucket, the bucket's roll-up removing what a writer that never
          returns left; a DROP's rewrite of a writer's file replaces that writer's head too (drop, below), and an
          erasure removes a document's entries together (erase, below)
seal      when the head cannot take an entry within 16,208 B, the next slot becomes the head: the lowest k whose
          seq the bucket's manifest shows absorbed, else a new k up to 8; with none free the writer merges first
          (merges, below) or, unable to, takes up to 16 slots and alarms; an entry over 8 KiB is a large entry; a
          push's entries past 256 KiB go straight into the bucket's shards, a merge inside that push
companion for git-mode refs and streams, the committer journals the entries in its sealed store once the content
          push commits, and pushes its head on ur/index at most once a minute on 1 KiB XFS blocks, else once every 5
          minutes, while it holds any (owner decision 172), at once when its head fills, and before it sleeps or
          exits; the head's coverage names, per content ref, the newest version whose changes it holds; its own
          device searches the journal meanwhile; a git FORCE indexes the trees' difference, and a ref DELETE
          journals a ref tombstone; a companion push is built in one order: its signed time taken, the head of
          ur/index read, then each content ref's head read from evs, the pin; it carries, per document of the
          committer's journaled versions at or below the pin, the newest, and drops one whose path the content ref
          holds at the pin at a higher version or removed, or whose ref was deleted since, leaving the newer version
          to its own committer or a backfill, and one whose push a horizon row already reaches; its coverage names
          the pin; it is sent within 5 min of its signed time (25 min in parts) and otherwise built again, and never
          sent again as built after a 429 TIME_AHEAD, so no entry trailing its content lands below a tombstone a
          roll-up dropped; hosts with the text check each live entry against its path and backfill a missing
          tombstone (the reads' coverage row), the accepted residual being a device whose clock ran about a week
          fast and that stalls that long before sending its stored bytes, which such a host repairs, naming the
          signer, and an evs counter a roll-up moves the fallback the review phase may take (owner decision 386); at
          an ERASE or CUT hint the committer drops an erased or listed document's journaled entries, and every
          companion push and 409 re-apply first applies the ref's erasure set (epoch, below), so a lost hint
          publishes nothing
conflict  only an eraser's CLOSURE, a DROP's rewrite or the writer's own other push rewrites a writer's file (owner
          decision 385); on 409 for it the writer rereads it and re-applies its pending entries, less the erasure
          set's documents: the one versionless path a client rebases (11.7), since it holds what it wrote; a 409 on
          content rebuilds the entries with the push
epoch     every push but a CLOSURE that creates or replaces an index file version (a head, slot, large entry,
          shard, manifest, lock or the erasure set), a CUT, merge, roll-up, build, backfill or DROP rewrite
          included, names the head's index_epoch (11.8's 5d) and writes no entry, posting or field of a document
          the ref's erasure set at that epoch lists, at or below its version; on 409 INDEX_EPOCH its builder
          rereads the head and the set, drops the listed documents from its pending entries, journal and inputs,
          and rebuilds (a merge, roll-up, build or backfill reruns on the new state, a multi-part push under a new
          push id); work begun at an epoch below the set's listed_since is rebuilt from content at the head, which
          an erased document's destroyed keys no longer open, or dropped and left to backfill (coverage, below); a
          replaying reader alarms on an index push that names another epoch than the version of the ref's newest
          CUT before it; hints only speed this, and no indexer takes part
coverage  a push is indexed when it changes its writer's head (in-ref), a coverage reaches its version, it touches
          only .ur-index/ or ur/index, or it carries format 2's index_none mark in its sealed metadata, which an
          index-aware writer sets when its push changes no document (every changed path under the never row, or
          binary or skipped with no prior indexed version; a version that turns binary is already a tombstone);
          hosts with the text check a marked push as an omitted document (D-EVS-56), raise index_mismatch naming the
          signer and re-enter it as a backfill, an old client's push having no mark and staying unindexed until
          backfilled, and a reader may classify a mailbox's non-m/ token prefixes with no fetch; readers derive
          indexed_through, the newest version up to which every push is indexed, and show later ones as not yet
          searchable; an indexer serving the repo for search (above), else the next capable writer, backfills a push
          still unindexed 10 min after its commit into its own head and raises its horizon, from the content at a
          pin read as a companion push reads it, each path at its state there, a path changed again after the
          horizon left to that change's own entry, skipping the erasure set's documents and any whose content an
          ERASE left unopenable
devices   desktops, the daemon and indexers index every push they make; phones and wasm index what they write and
          merge only when out of slots or on Wi-Fi while charging
```

**Merges.**

```text
when      a bucket's sealed slots (all but each writer's head) and unabsorbed large entries reach 128 KiB, or a
          writer is out of slots; an indexer serving the repo for search first, else a desktop or the daemon; never
          on an expired bucket, judged at the push's signed time, as a roll-up names only an expired one (owner
          decision 386)
input     the bucket's manifest and shards, and its sealed slots and unabsorbed large entries, at the merge's base
          version, and no writer's head (owner decision 385); the new manifest's absorbed seqs and the files the
          push replaces name them, so a reproducer learns its inputs from the push
output    each document's newest version among the inputs, the erasure set's documents left out (commit path's epoch
          row); at one version a tombstone, then the shards' own entry, then the copy from the lowest writer id and
          seq; a live version as a doc-table row with its postings, a tombstone in the tombstone table, dropping the
          bucket's older rows of its key, and a ref tombstone those of its ref below its version, each kept for
          older partitions until the roll-up; appended in doc_key order to the youngest shard, which takes the
          longest run that fits by INDEX-FORMAT.md's search, a next one opening at the cap and taking at least one,
          since extraction skips a document that alone would not fit a shard (sniff row), its older version dropped
          from the shard holding it, a shard that this leaves past the cap giving its highest entries to the
          appended ones, so a bucket's shards hold one version per document, a row or a tombstone, and an eraser
          finds a document in one shard of each partition, the lazy alternative (superseded rows masked by version,
          a shard rewritten under half current) to be measured on FS-76's corpus before M10's exit freezes the bytes
          (owner decision 387); adjacent shards under 512 KiB together are joined only where the joined shard
          encodes within the shard bound, so a layout is a function of its inputs that always writes (owner decision
          394); a merge writes and removes no file of any writer's: absorbed slots stay for their writers to reuse
          and large entries for their writers to remove (dependency, above), their tombstones in the shards
commit    one push: the shards (uploads with receipts) and the manifest, which every merge replaces or creates; a
          409 means another merge or an erasure landed first, and the merge reruns on the new state; merges take no
          lock
```

**Roll-up.**

```text
trigger   an expired bucket, oldest first (owner decision 153), judged at the push's signed time, as is the lock
runner    an indexer serving the repo for search that writes it (owner decision 150); where one exists, any writer
          committing a day past the expiry with no roll-up landed; with none, the first desktop, daemon, or phone
          on Wi-Fi while charging, that commits to the ref after the expiry, in the background (owner decision
          157); the runner must hold every bucket and the all partition at the ref's head
lock      <root>/lock: the runner takes it by a push changing it from a free version, or one whose until_ms is 10
          min past (the time check's bound), to {itself, S, now + 30 min}, renewing by the same CAS while it works;
          a 409 shows another holder, left alone until its until_ms; one roller at a time per ref
steps     1 read the bucket, the newer buckets and all at the head; 2 compute the bucket's documents as a merge
          does, writers' heads included: each key's newest version or tombstone and each ref's newest ref tombstone;
          3 per key, the newer of that and all's row stays and the other goes, all's rows of a ref below its ref
          tombstone go, and so does every version the erasure set lists; 4 append the live ones that stay in doc_key
          order to all's youngest shard, a next opening at the cap, and join adjacent shards as a merge does; a
          version or tombstone it carries that a newer bucket holds only older entries of, which racing index pushes
          near a boundary can leave, goes instead into the shards of the newest bucket holding an entry of its
          document, in the roll-up's push, which replaces or creates that bucket's manifest, nothing being removed
          from the newer bucket: reads mask its older entries by version, its merges drop them and its own roll-up
          carries the promoted entry on, a promoted tombstone still taking all's row and a ref tombstone above a
          newer bucket's older entry of its ref promoted likewise, and no file is rewritten in place and no writer's
          file touched, a merge of that bucket conflicting on its manifest's CAS (owner decision 385); every other
          tombstone then goes, nothing older remaining; 5 upload the changed shards; 6 one push, in parts if large
          (11.8): the shards, each promotion's shards and manifest, the runner's own head in the newest bucket where
          it carries forward, as a horizon row at indexed_through, the coverage that the removed bucket's slots
          held, a/m with rolled_through_day = S, the removal of b/<S>/ listing each of its files (11.7), and the
          lock set free from the version the runner holds
fence     step 6's change to the lock is the fencing token: a runner whose lock lapsed and was taken gets 409 on
          it and stops, its uploads left to 11.13's orphan rule
crash     nothing shows before step 6's head CAS (11.8): a crash leaves the bucket and all as they were and the
          lock lapses within 30 min; an unknown outcome resolves by push id (11.8's outcomes)
idempotent outputs are functions of the inputs, so a rerun writes the same plaintext; a runner that finds b/<S>/
          gone and rolled_through_day >= S stops; any other 409 (an erasure, a late merge) reruns from step 1
one       all holds one version per document: a roll-up drops the older version it supersedes, so all needs no
          dead-document bitmap, and an eraser finds a document in one shard; with step 4, no all row is newer than
          the newest bucket entry of its key or a bucket's ref tombstone of its ref (owner decision 385), so all
          holds no tombstone
cost      once per bucket length: one merge of the bucket, the changed shards' uploads, ~25 removals and, rarely, a
          newer bucket's shards and manifest taking a promoted entry; the purge then deletes the bucket's and the
          replaced shards' content (owner decision 161)
readings  (owner decision 388) a slot other than the head, or a large entry, at or below its writer's absorbed seq
          holds nothing for search, merges and roll-ups; a manifest may exist with no shard, and absorbed holds a
          row only for a watermark above 0; IndexFileHeader.coverage sorts by ref_id, then horizon false before
          true, at most one row of each kind a ref; an entry's time is its content push's signed time, and its
          bucket follows the index push's; a merge's tie at one version takes a tombstone, then the shards' own
          entry, then the full entry of the lowest writer id and the lowest seq; the youngest shard fills by a fixed
          binary search over its rows; a merge with nothing to add still commits its manifest; a push past 256 KiB
          of entries also writes its writer's head; the lock renews at half its term; a companion push that only
          raises coverage is sent; a writer replacing a multi-chunk text file without its text writes no index
          entry, and the push is backfilled; a roll-up's runner writes horizon rows at indexed_through into its own
          head in the newest bucket for each content ref the removed slots named; and a journaled unit at or below
          its ref's horizon at the companion push's base is dropped
```

**Reads.** Devices sync index files by position and search only their cache:

```text
pin       per (repo, ref): the reader's 11.9 pin (v, C_v) and a search manifest of the index files it holds (path,
          version, content_sha256, padded size, partition, a state of held or bad, and the oldest and newest time of
          its rows), which records the version of the index ref its bucket files are whole at, all's own pin and the
          roll-ups between the two, with a round's plan beside it (its target, the files wanted and those staged;
          DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.7)
trigger   a hint (11.10) or wake (§18.7), the app coming to the foreground, the hourly resync, "search more", or a
          background window (§18.4); a search reads only the cache and triggers no fetch, except "search more" for
          the all files the device lacks in repos no designated search indexer answers (remote search, below); one
          round runs at a time a ref, a trigger that arrives during it running another after it; the first hint or
          wake for a repo in a quiet Search.HintCoalesce (1 min) starts a round at once and later ones in that
          interval start one at its end (owner decision 450); a round that fails on a read keeps its plan and staged
          files and is tried again after Search.SyncRetryInterval (30 s, doubling to the hourly resync) or at the
          next trigger (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.7)
replay    POST .../read from the pin returns the statements after it; a change under the index's token prefix marks
          that file; past the 4 MiB catch-up budget the reader re-pins and lists the index directories instead (one
          read per partition directory)
fetch     whole files by sync position, never a range or file a query chose: each marked file the device keeps, up
          to 64 paths and 32 MiB of ranges a read (11.9), buckets first, then all's shards youngest first, the most
          recently searched repos first; settings, the erasure set and a/m belong to the latest set every device
          keeps, and a round fetches them before the buckets; every device keeps the buckets of the repos it syncs
          (phones too, the exception to 11.11's versionless fetch rule, but the team directory's only desktops keep,
          §16.11), and each index ref's erasure set wherever it keeps or writes that ref's index, and desktops, the
          daemon and indexers keep all in the background, others at "search more" where no designated search indexer
          answers, or on Wi-Fi while charging (owner decisions 154, 178; §18.4)
verify    11.9's checks (signed statement, entry hash), then content_sha256 after decryption; a file that breaks the
          format (past 1 MiB, a dictionary out of order, a docid out of range, a tombstone table out of order or
          naming a key its doc table holds, a tombstone in an all shard, an entry of the reserved kind 2, a
          non-canonical encoding) is dropped and raises SidecarEvent index_malformed {repo, ref, path, signer}
          (§5.4); nothing is compressed, so no decoder needs a memory bound; after a CLOSURE a manifest's
          IndexShard.docs is an upper bound and its first_day to last_day a covering range, which no step compares
          with the shard's header and the next merge or roll-up recomputes, an eraser still finding a document by
          a/m's days and the shard's doc table
swap      the manifest of a new pin replaces the old one, atomically, only when every bucket file that pin lists is
          held at the listed version and the version table (§5.9) covers it, so a snapshot is one version of the
          ref; all is swapped separately and only at the snapshot's pin, so it is never ahead; a file that fails its
          checks is listed bad, holds nothing for search and does not hold the swap, or one writer could keep every
          reader's index at an old version, and a host with the text serves that repo from the index, not from text,
          until its local layer covers what the file held; running searches keep their snapshot; files no manifest,
          plan or open snapshot names are deleted (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.7; details/IndexSync.tla, §22.8)
reproduce a device holding every input of a merge, roll-up or CLOSURE at its push's base version (the new manifest's
          absorbed seqs and the files the push replaces name them) builds the result and compares content_sha256
          with each new file's entry version: equal, it caches its own output and fetches nothing; unequal, it
          fetches the file and raises SidecarEvent index_mismatch {repo, ref, path, signer: the push's} (§5.4); a
          device lacking an input downloads, raising nothing; after a CLOSURE it deletes the replaced files (§5.9);
          a team directory reader (§16.11) holding a writer's previous head and that push's bucket at its base,
          which the head's encoding follows (dependency, above), derives the new head from the card version the push
          wrote, fetching the head only if content_sha256 differs and then alarming; any writer's head is rebuilt
          alike from that writer's files in the bucket at the push's base and the documents the push carries: an
          in-ref push's content changes, a companion push's or a backfill's paths at the pins its coverage rows
          name, and on a record stream the cards of the runs those versions touched (DESIGN-DETAILS.md sections 1
          and 15); merges run at 7.0-9.7 ns a posting natively, 2.5-5x that in wasm, so a bucket merge is
          sub-second; phones reproduce only in the foreground or a background window, else download
retained  readers search every bucket present, expired ones included, so search stays complete while a roll-up is
          pending; a device keeping all applies the roll-up by reproduction or download, then drops the bucket; one
          keeping only latest drops it, its instant coverage the last W to 2W days; a device searches its cached all
          only while it is usable, its pin the snapshot's, or every roll-up between the two pins bridged by the
          rolled bucket held as the roll-up read it, which it knows from the statements it replayed; with a bridge
          lost or not vouched for (an ERASE or an executed drop in the repo, two windows passed, a roll-up slept
          through, or a bucket copy older than the roll-up's input) it searches its buckets only, reports its
          coverage from the oldest bucket and fetches all's changed files (a/m and the youngest shards, usually a
          few MiB) at its next window or at "search more", which fetches before it answers, so no deleted document
          is found again (owner decision 393)
collected a fetch of a replaced index file that answers `collected` (11.9) restarts the round on the new head, which
          brings every file to it, so no snapshot mixes two versions of the ref (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7,
          7.2.7); only writers' heads change often, each one read, and all's shards change only at roll-ups and
          erasures
subscribe file-mode refs need no new lease, since index files change in the same push as content; a repo whose
          git-mode refs or record streams are indexed adds one whole-ref lease on its ur/index ref (11.10)
traffic   at 100 messages a day a phone's heads and sealed slots cost ~4-6 MB a month at about ten syncs a day, and
          merges nothing by reproduction (~10-25 MB a month downloaded without it); a first five-year all is
          ~110-165 MB (~27-41 at 25 a day, ~330-495 at 300); every download debits the transfer balance (owner
          decision 10), and a device that reproduces shows the server nothing
```

```text
query     normalized by normalizer 1 under the tables the index records; space-separated terms are ANDed; "a
          quoted phrase" is one term; -term drops a hit only where this host confirms the term; a term of 1-2 bytes
          matches as a whole word through its space-padded trigrams (" a "; " go" and "go "), since fields are padded
          and punctuation folds to spaces; a CJK run is one substring term; from:, subject: and date ranges filter
          doc-table fields before any posting is read (§16.10 adds agent, run, kind and path prefix), a date range
          inside the buckets never needing all; a query with no trigram matches nothing
plan      per (repo, ref), newest first: the current bucket, the previous one, any expired and retained buckets,
          then all's shards youngest first (scope latest stops before all); per shard the query's trigrams are
          looked up rarest first, one absent ending that shard, and absent from every shard of a partition, that
          partition; only the query's lists are decoded, in their 64 KiB frames, and intersected rarest first,
          galloping into VByte runs and ANDing bitsets; heads, sealed slots and unabsorbed large entries are scanned
          per document, whose key set must hold every query trigram; a median query touches 374-73,000 postings (p90
          under 120,000), about a millisecond in wasm, frame decryption dominating, within 11.15's 4 MiB working set
newest    per doc key, the entry with the highest version over every partition the device holds, tombstones
          included, is current; a hit from partition X counts only if X holds that entry, it is not a tombstone, no
          ref tombstone of its ref (its row's ref_id) is above its version, and no erasure mask (below) covers it;
          equal versions in two partitions (during a roll-up) are the same content; no all row being newer than the
          newest bucket entry of its key (roll-up's one row), a device keeping only the buckets masks exactly too;
          each candidate is answered from the device's version table (§5.9), built as it caches the files, never by
          collecting the partitions' keys at search time: lazily in rank order, as confirmation is, one probe
          reading a page of each run through a 256 KiB cache a process, so a search's mask state is its pending
          candidates (at most 20,000 a partition, too_broad past that) whatever the partitions hold; each document
          the ref's erasure set lists is masked at or below its listed version from the CUT on, whether or not an
          ERASE names it, and a key an ERASE names that no set version the device holds lists is masked whole in
          every partition until a set version lists it or the rewritten files are cached, the version table holding
          both as erased (owner decision 461); a branch's search adds its base ref's documents for paths it has not
          changed (11.7's overlays), probing the table for the branch's own key of each such path; hits stream as
          each partition finishes
confirm   hosts with the document's text (a desktop or indexer mirroring the ref, a mounted working tree, an indexer
          answering a remote search, whose verified hits the phone labels "verified by <device>") verify each
          candidate, decrypted, normalized and checked for every term and phrase, lazily in rank order until a
          page (50) is full, the count reading "about n" until all are checked, with a snippet around the first
          match; other hosts confirm a hit whose display fields contain the query, or, for mail, whose i/ address or
          200 B snippet does (§15.7), or whose body they already cache, and show the rest as possible matches from
          subject, from and date, fetching no body to check them, opening one confirming or rejecting it (owner
          decision 155); a desktop without a document's text shows it as possible; on 20 Newsgroups, headers alone
          confirmed 11% of true rare-word matches, headers and the snippet 26%
rank      1 matches (verified and confirmed), newest first, or by term density on hosts with the text; 2 possible
          matches by trigram overlap J = |T(q)| / n_d (n_d the row's trigram count), fewest distinct trigrams first,
          ties newest first, the app able to switch to newest first; 3 near hits (typos, below) by J against the
          corrected query; on 20 Newsgroups overlap raised P@5 for rare words from recency's 0.19 to 0.45 (0.54 with
          confirmations first), the true hit first from 21% to 68%, and for common words and two-word phrases from
          0.48 and 0.17 to 0.93 and 0.60 with confirmations first; a long document assembles a query's trigrams by
          chance far more often than a short one
typos     when a term has fewer than 3 exact hits, or on request, never for CJK: desktops expand it against a local
          vocabulary (the text's words with document counts) by trigram similarity (words padded with two spaces
          before and one after, shared over union trigrams, threshold 0.3, ties by count), the intended word first
          76% of the time and in the top five 92%; phones test each one-edit variant over the term's script whose
          padded trigrams all exist and share a document, display-vocabulary words first (the subjects, senders and
          i/ snippets they hold), 66% and 83%, at a median ~0.2M posting probes a term (0.4-2 ms natively); a hit
          says "showing results for <word>", one correction a term; documents missing up to 3 of a typo's trigrams
          gave 324-3,564 candidates for 8-13 true ones, so that rule is not used
cjk       UTF-8 lead and continuation bytes are disjoint (RFC 3629), so a trigram starting with a 3-byte
          character's lead byte is that character: a one-character CJK, kana or Hangul query is one exact list, a
          two-character one four lists, a 4-byte character two trigrams; two or more characters give candidates,
          verified on desktops and possible on phones; §22 measures a Japanese and a Chinese corpus; NFKC and case
          folding are stable for assigned characters, so a reader on other tables misses only characters assigned
          between them, says so, and the next writer on the newer tables rebuilds
coverage  a content version newer than the index's coverage is not yet searchable: hosts with the text index it into
          a local overlay at once, an indexer answering a remote search covering it from that overlay and reporting
          the rest as uncovered, and phones show "n recent changes not yet searchable" until the backfill lands;
          hosts with the text re-extract each document version a delta adds, check each tombstone against its path's
          history and each live entry against its path, one whose content ref holds the path removed or at a higher
          version, with nothing above it in the index, being a mismatch they backfill, and reproduce merges and
          roll-ups, on a mismatch using their own result and raising SidecarEvent index_mismatch {repo, ref, path,
          signer} (§5.4), indexers for every repo they read (owner decision 150); for an in-ref push that changed
          its signer's head they also re-extract every document the content push at that version changed, as the
          writer extracts it (a binary version, a path under the never row and a chunk D6 skips yield no doc_key),
          skipping what the erasure set at the push's epoch lists, and hold that the index at that version holds
          each resulting doc_key at that version or above, in any of the signer's files or the bucket's shards; a
          missing one is a mismatch, the host's own entry standing for it, the path queued for a backfill and
          index_mismatch naming the signer and the head file the push wrote, so a writer cannot hide a document
          it commits behind a changed head (owner decision 621); both checks are bounded by the effective ref
          version at the pin, the ref's version plus the base versions along its overlay bases, which no path
          version exceeds (11.7's versions), so an entry of a path's chunk above it is never honest: a live one is
          planted, as a never-held entry is, and a tombstone is a mismatch whatever the path holds at the pin,
          since readers take it over every version the path reaches below it: where the text keeps the chunk
          live at the pin it hides a document, the host's own entry standing for it, and where the path is
          removed or binary there, or the chunk past its text, index_mismatch names its signer and file with
          nothing to repair; the omitted-document check counts an entry only at or below the bound, and an entry
          at or below it that the device cannot place passes as before (owner decision 669); phones compare an
          opened document with its row; every writer of a ref writes its index, so an agent could otherwise hide a
          document or plant hits
off       a ref with no index: hosts with the text scan it (exact, linear), phones and browsers match names and,
          for mail, i/'s fields, and the result says "index off"; an index in a newer format turns search off for
          that ref, status "update"; no search reaches a secret, config or mailcfg repo; an owner-bound repo's
          reader that is not one of its owner's consented devices (an EvsShare subject, the audit reader) deposits
          §16.8's read receipt naming the index files before it decrypts them
```

**Remote search (owner decisions [175](#od-175)-[178](#od-178)).** With no designated search indexer, which is the default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)), every repo follows [owner decision 155](#od-155)'s download. Where one is designated, an app host's "search more", never a keystroke, sends its query end to end over §6.6's RPC on the pair's Network contract (`SEARCH` 0x1404, `SEARCH_RESULT` 0x1405; D-PROTO-21) to an indexer that may answer, which searches what it holds and returns verified hits. §18.4 owns the requester's mode (`on`, `own`, `off`), the notice it shows before another member's device is first asked, and the UI states; the engine is root `search_remote_*.go`.

```text
who       per repo, first an own search indexer (a device of the requester's member) that reads it; an owner-bound
          repo only on a consented device of its owner (owner decision 126), so the requester's own vault and
          mailbox never reach another member, and a repo another member shared by EvsShare only on that owner's
          search indexer; a team repo (general, record, team_record, the directory) otherwise on one network-scope
          search indexer that reads it, a tagged one answering only team repos, its sponsor named; in a personal
          network every indexer is own; never secret, config, mailcfg or deposit-only repos
eligible  eligible(d, R, p), which each side evaluates in its own newest verified state at every send and every
          page, never from a list made earlier, so a stale or forged view reaches nothing the other refuses: d's
          newest IndexerSet at some scope names search, unretired, and d is not revoked, parked or suspended; d is
          a ur daemon host advertising Hello feature bit 0; p is an admitted member device, untagged and not
          ephemeral, revoked, parked or suspended (in v1 an app host); d and p are in RepoReaders(R) (§8.12); for R
          owner-bound to M, consented(d, M) (§8.5), d's designation at member scope, or at network scope where the
          config state holds one member, and p reads R as M's consented device or by an EvsShare; for a team R, d
          is a device of p's member or its designation is network scope; d holds a whole snapshot of R's index
          under its background policy (§18.4), its all usable (retained, above) where the request's scope is all,
          with R's index on in a format and normalizer d reads; the indexer's verdict for a repo is the first that
          holds of REFUSED_NOT_READER, REFUSED_NOT_CONSENTED, REFUSED_SCOPE, REFUSED_INDEX_OFF, REFUSED_FORMAT,
          REFUSED_ALL_ABSENT, SERVED_INDEX (no text of the ref, or a bad file its local layer does not cover) and
          SERVED_TEXT (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.2)
auth      the phone checks d's IndexerSet, admission and consent evidence in its own config (owner decision 6) and,
          before the first request, §6.4's identity binding with HelloResult's bit 0, a failure alarming and
          dropping d until its admission changes; each reply's coverage carries the (v, C_v) its cursor pinned,
          matched at the phone's own version (else §6.4's FORK alarm) or at its next sync, never prompting a read
order     the first two own search indexers asked at once, for the repos each may answer (first the one that
          answered last within 10 min, then by rendezvous hash of the two sidecar_ids, the first 8 bytes of
          SHA-256 over a label and the two ids, ascending), the first page 0 to serve a repo wins it and the
          other reply is dropped, with no hedge delay, at two exchanges and two indexers' CPU a search (owner
          decision 391), no pair kept warm (owner decision 609); a further own indexer is asked alone, and only
          when neither of those two can be; then, where `who` allows, other members', the one that served this
          member's repos within 24 h first, else by rendezvous hash of (member_id, indexer sidecar_id), one at a
          time and sticky until it fails, so a member's queries reach at most one other device for a set of
          repos; repos sharing a first choice go in one request of at most 64, and the phone remembers for 24 h
          which repos each indexer served (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.3; details/RemoteAsk.tla, §22.8)
failover  no first page within Search.RemoteTimeout (3 s, 5 s metered), RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, UNIMPLEMENTED or a
          repo refused in coverage sends those repos to the next eligible indexer, read from the config state
          then; a later page with no reply by its deadline is asked once more, the same search_id and page,
          before its leg fails, and page 0 is never sent twice under one search_id, so no late copy of it opens a
          cursor again; CURSOR_EXPIRED reopens the search once, under a new search_id; an open leg is judged
          again whenever the config state moves, and one whose indexer may no longer be asked ends with no skip,
          its reply in flight dropped (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.4); liveness comes from the Hello a
          search sends where it finds no session (online 10 min after a HelloResult within 3 s, a failed indexer
          skipped for 2 min; D-SDK-27), with no keepalive (owner decision 609); a repo no indexer answers, in off
          mode or behind an unanswered notice follows owner decision 155's download; an indexer seen again while
          the search screen is open is asked once more for the repos that fell back
```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/search.proto (11.14): remote search over §6.6's RPC, MessageType SEARCH 0x1404 and
// SEARCH_RESULT 0x1405 (§6.11). No oneof (§6.11's rule); nothing compressed; every body padded (sizes, below).
message SearchRequest {
  uint32 search_version = 1;          // 1
  fixed64 search_id = 2;              // random per search, chosen by the requester; names the cursor
  uint32 page = 3;                    // 0 opens the search; n asks page n once page n-1 arrived; a repeat
                                      //   of n returns page n again
  fixed64 supersedes = 4;             // an earlier search_id of this requester, whose work and cursor end; 0 none
  uint32 steps = 5;                   // the reply's size in 16 KiB steps, 1-4; v1 requesters send 1
  uint32 scope = 6;                   // page 0 only: 1 latest (buckets), 2 all (buckets, then all)
  string query = 7;                   // page 0 only: §16.10's grammar, <= 512 B and 16 terms, NFC as typed;
                                      //   the indexer normalizes it with each index's normalizer
  repeated SearchRepo repos = 8;      // page 0 only: <= 64 repos the requester reads and asks of this indexer
  int64 since_ms = 9;                 // page 0 only; 0 unbounded
  int64 until_ms = 10;                // inclusive, as since_ms; a reopened search narrows it to resume
  SearchFilters filters = 11;         // page 0 only: §16.10's filters
  bool fuzzy = 12;                    // page 0 only: near hits even with 3 or more exact hits
  reserved 13, 14;                    // group_by and withhold_untrusted, for later requesters
  bytes pad = 15;                     // zeros, sizing the body to exactly 4,016 B
}
message SearchRepo { bytes repo_id = 1; bytes ref_id = 2; }   // ref_id empty: the repo's default ref
message SearchFilters {               // <= 768 B as encoded in a SearchRequest
  repeated string agents = 1;         // agent labels, or agent ids in hex
  repeated bytes sidecar_ids = 2;
  repeated bytes member_ids = 3;
  repeated bytes run_ids = 4;
  repeated string session_ids = 5;
  repeated uint32 kinds = 6;          // RECORD.md's kinds
  string path_prefix = 7;
  repeated SearchField fields = 8;    // field:text terms
}
message SearchField { uint32 field = 1; string text = 2; }    // 11.14's field numbers (1 subject, 2 from, ...)
message SearchReply {
  uint32 search_version = 1;          // the version answered
  uint32 min_version = 2;             // this indexer's supported range
  uint32 max_version = 3;
  fixed64 search_id = 4;
  uint32 page = 5;
  uint32 status = 6;                  // SearchStatus
  uint32 phase = 7;                   // 1 latest, 2 all, 3 done
  bool complete = 8;                  // no later page holds a hit
  int64 checked_through_ms = 9;       // SERVED_TEXT repos: the time of the newest candidate not yet accounted
                                      //   for, so every newer one was checked and returned on this or an
                                      //   earlier page if it matched; 0: none is left
  repeated SearchCoverage coverage = 10;   // page 0: one per repo named; later pages: none
  repeated SearchHit hits = 11;       // as many as fit the steps, at most 20
  SearchCounts counts = 12;
  bytes pad = 15;                     // zeros, sizing the body to exactly steps x 16,384 B
}
enum SearchStatus {
  SEARCH_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SEARCH_OK = 1; SEARCH_PARTIAL = 2; SEARCH_TOO_BROAD = 3;
  SEARCH_CURSOR_EXPIRED = 4; SEARCH_INVALID = 5; SEARCH_UNSUPPORTED_VERSION = 6;
}
message SearchCoverage {
  bytes repo_id = 1;
  bytes ref_id = 2;
  uint32 served = 3;                  // SearchServed
  uint64 ref_version = 4;             // the (v, C_v) the cursor pinned (11.9): the text pin when SERVED_TEXT;
                                      //   the index pin when SERVED_INDEX and the index is in the ref; else 0
  bytes chain = 5;                    // <= 32 B
  int64 ref_time_ms = 6;              // that version's signed time
  int64 latest_from_ms = 7;           // the oldest bucket day searched
  uint32 uncovered = 8;               // pushes past indexed_through that this indexer's text does not cover
}
enum SearchServed {
  SEARCH_SERVED_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SERVED_TEXT = 1; SERVED_INDEX = 2; REFUSED_NOT_READER = 3;
  REFUSED_NOT_CONSENTED = 4; REFUSED_SCOPE = 5; REFUSED_INDEX_OFF = 6; REFUSED_ALL_ABSENT = 7;
  REFUSED_FORMAT = 8;
}
message SearchHit {
  bytes repo_id = 1;
  bytes ref_id = 2;
  bytes doc_key = 3;                  // 11.14's doc_key, the same on every reader, so merges match
  uint64 version = 4;
  int64 time_ms = 5;
  uint32 doc_kind = 6;                // 1 file, 2 mail, 3 record, 4 derived (a run card)
  string locator = 7;                 // the path or derived name, <= 512 B, which the requester opens
  uint32 state = 8;                   // 1 verified, 2 confirmed, 3 possible, 4 near
  string correction = 9;              // near: the corrected term, <= 256 B
  uint32 partition = 10;              // 1 current, 2 previous, 3 older or retained, 4 all
  uint32 trust = 11;                  // 1 own, 2 member, 3 untrusted, relative to the requester (§16.10)
  bytes signer = 12;                  // the version's writer sidecar_id
  repeated SearchField fields = 13;   // display fields from the row, at most 8, each <= 256 B
  string snippet = 14;                // verified hits: <= 200 B around the first match
  uint32 line = 15;                   // files: the first matching line
}
message SearchCounts { uint32 checked = 1; uint32 verified = 2; uint32 possible = 3; uint32 near = 4; uint32 masked = 5; }
```

```text
exchange  page 0 carries the query, scope (v1 phones send 2), repos, since, until, filters and fuzzy; the indexer
          authorizes, pins a snapshot per repo and answers with coverage for every repo named and the first hits;
          later pages carry only search_version, search_id, page, supersedes, steps and pad; one page in flight a
          search, page n only after n-1 arrived, a repeat of n returning the cursor's last reply unchanged
ranking   across SERVED_TEXT repos candidates go in one order, newest first by (time, the repo's place in the
          request, doc_key), over every partition; a page reads all's shards only when the order reaches the newest
          row all holds, by the oldest and newest times the manifest keeps for each file; each is verified against
          the text before it is returned, and one whose text the indexer does not hold at that version is returned
          as a phone would judge it; checked_through_ms is the time of the newest candidate not yet accounted for, a
          hit held back for size included, so every candidate above it was examined and returned if it matched, ties
          at that time not claimed; phase 1 while that candidate is newer than every all row, 2 after, 3 with none
          left; SERVED_INDEX repos' confirmed and possible hits follow, ranked as a phone ranks them, and near hits
          come last, when a term has fewer than 3 exact hits or fuzzy is set, and these claim nothing; TOO_BROAD
          moves no span (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.5; details/RemoteCursor.tla, §22.8)
sizes     every request body exactly 4,016 B, one envelope, timeout_ms always 10,000; every reply body exactly steps
          x 16,384 B (steps 1-4, 1 in v1), failures after parsing included; nothing compressed, no Cancel, no early
          or short reply; errors decided before parsing are small envelope Errors that depend on the requester's
          identity, rate or build, never on a query; a builder rule fills the size with no wire change: a body is
          the one deterministic encoding of its message, pad last; every other field stops at the body's size less
          131 B, so pad is at least 131 B and its length takes two bytes or three, removing the 1, 2 and 130 B
          holes, and a reply whose other fields would leave exactly 16,387 B returns the most hits, at most 20, that
          leave another gap, holding the rest for the next page (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 11); SearchFilters is at
          most 768 B encoded in a SearchRequest, so page 0 holds at most 2,987 + 3 + 768 = 3,758 B against its 3,885
          B budget and every request fits, a search whose filters pass 768 B staying on the device with
          FallbackReason none, local search keeping no such cap; a body that cannot be sized is never sent short:
          UNAUTHENTICATED (§6.4's identity check), PERMISSION_DENIED (not an admitted, untagged, non-ephemeral
          member device, or no search designation or Search.RemoteServe off), RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (retry_after_ms),
          UNIMPLEMENTED
status    OK; PARTIAL (2 s of CPU or 1,000 verifications ended the page, more to come); TOO_BROAD (a partition over
          20,000 candidates: header-confirmed hits and counts, complete); CURSOR_EXPIRED (search_id unknown, idle 10
          min, superseded, a third search of the requester, or an ERASE, CUT or lost read in its scope; the phone
          reopens once); INVALID (a wrong size, a non-zero pad, a query over 512 B or 16 terms, over 64 repos, an id
          of the wrong length, steps outside 1 to 4, a malformed filter or SearchFilters past 768 B, a field the
          receiver does not know at any depth, or a body that is not the one deterministic marshaling of the message
          it parses to, checked before its pad's zeros, while a reply failing those is no reply);
          UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, judged first, so a later version's request is never INVALID, a requester raising
          search_version to send a new field, SearchRequest's reserved 13 and 14 included, and falling back to
          version 1's fields for an indexer answering a lower range (owner decision 390); a request for a page other
          than the cursor's or the next is INVALID and leaves the cursor, and a lost read, the requester's or the
          indexer's, ends it (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 7, 7.2.5); per repo in coverage, SERVED_TEXT, SERVED_INDEX
          or a refusal, which sends that repo on (failover, above)
limits    requester: at most 2 open searches an indexer, a third's page 0 superseding the oldest, 30 requests a
          minute (burst 10), 64 repos a request, a larger scope split by indexer, then by 64; indexer: per requester
          the same, else RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED before parsing; Search.RemoteSearchCount (4) computing beside §16.10's 4
          local searches, RemoteQueueCount (16) waiting at most 1 s, RemoteCpuPerMinute (30 s of CPU a minute; this
          and the page's 2 s charge a compute slot's busy wall time on the injected clock, summed across slots for
          RemoteCpuPerMinute, which over-counts under contention, so a page ends PARTIAL early and never late),
          RemoteCursorCount (64) cursors idle at most 10 min, each at most 16 KiB of resume state plus its last
          reply; a lost reply is retried by page and answered from the cursor, not §6.6's idempotency cache, which
          holds only mutating methods' responses, and SEARCH mutates nothing (§6.6)
serve     the indexer authorizes in its own state, naming a refused repo in coverage, never as an error; its checks
          run in one order, none before the third reading the body, so nothing a relay sees before then depends on a

phones    never serve: readers ignore search on a read_only or ephemeral subject, ur indexer add refuses it on an

merge     per (repo, ref, doc_key) over the remote pages and the phone's own hits, the strongest claim by class
          first, a verified or confirmed claim before a possible one before a near one, then the higher version,
          then verified before confirmed, then an indexer's claim before the phone's, then the leg whose first page
          arrived first, a leg's claim taken only for a repo that leg serves, so no indexer demotes what another
```
