### 11.22 Phasing

- **v0a** (§23 M2): format 1 with 11.8's objects and protocols (parts, ref modes, the seal lease, batches, receipts, lazy folds with removal markers and their collection, placement); streams, deposits, slots and ERASE, and the owner-bound read-receipt budget, which an `EvsShare` reader needs before it reads (§16.8, D-MCP-18); subscriptions, Redis soft state, the verified head cache and reads of §7.9's `{acl_}e`; head mode; path epochs; the gate and HeadCheck's ref pins (§6.4); usage events, fair share and the write budget, with its classes, accounts and wallet (11.13); GC and hourly evacuation; mirrors and re-seeding; soft deletion; export; format 1's reservations for format 2 (11.6), refused as FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED (EvsPush flags 256 and 512, fields 33 and 34 and the read states `drop_pending` and `dropped` among them; window bits 4 and 5 and a head's index_epoch ignored, [owner decision 235](#od-235)), and its reserved names, the `.ur-index/` directory on file-mode refs and the `ur/index` and `ur/lfs` refs, which format-1 clients refuse to write (11.14); the `directory` kind, known from M2 (11.12); the slot rule (11.8's 5h and step 6), which format 2 requires, checked by format 1 from M2 too, since it costs one NVMe HEAD on a rare slot 412 and hardens erasure, though M10 suffices for drops; `ur evs rekey`, re-checkpointing every file of a repo under the current generation (§10.16). Format 1's specification freezes at M2's entry review, after peer review of 11.5-11.8 and RECORD.md, and its bytes at M2's exit (D-PHASE-7), after §22.8's drive-write gate (owner decisions [25](#od-25), [99](#od-99), [140](#od-140)).
- **v0b** (§23 M2, with v0a; no format change): the local git server, `git-remote-ur`, the identity hook, the proc-receive journal and imports, the desktop sync engine, overlays and conflict branches, which M2's twenty-agent test uses (§3.15).
- **v1:** retention as expiry, ERASE and BASE ([owner decision 246](#od-246)); agent-subkey provenance; the `directory` kind at M6 on format 1's streams (11.12), with 11.9's streams read and moved listing; format 2 at §23's M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)): versionless files with staging, the purge and its sweep, rules and the repo lock, migration and the git-lfs store with its tip check (11.7, 11.11, 11.13), the search index (11.14) with its erasure cut and erasure sets, each repo's index built at its migration, the directory's versionless cards and its index, the drop-history action behind §19.11's `format2.drop` gate, observe first (D-TEST-18), and remote search, its app-host cases at the later of M10's and M8's exits and its team-indexer cases at the later of M10's and M6's. Cross-network shares are §17.9's IP path at M6 ([owner decision 86](#od-86)), for which evs builds nothing.
- **Later:** [compaction](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-compaction) and [the reclaim of expired ciphertext](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-expired-ciphertext-reclaim) (owner decisions [246](#od-246), [247](#od-247)); [working-tree sync](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-working-tree-sync), a git user updating a working tree with stock git meanwhile, and [derived shares](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-derived-shares) ([owner decision 250](#od-250)); [Q-EVS-3's prefix rules](DESIGN-DEFER.md#acl-prefix-write-rules) (§8.8; [owner decision 586](#od-586)); [full sync on mobile](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-mobile-full-sync); [a state commitment](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-state-commitment) if measurements show head readers need pre-pin freshness; [directory-resident children](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-directory-resident-children) for append-only record directories (the reserved `layout`), if §22.8 shows stream entries' index objects binding; [a tool moving placed repos between clusters](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-repo-move-tool) with one commit point ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), built to land before the earliest cohort exhaustion §19.9's cohorts row projects; [a per-cluster batcher](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-per-cluster-batcher), two evs processes batching each cluster's records near ~5 a batch, if §22.8 shows it saves a set; [a segment placement](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-segment-placement) that keeps the receipt check and moves upload load, not only new repos, before any added HDD set, ordered by §19.9's hdd trigger, a tracked item (§23.7) whose design is Q-OPS-11's residual ([owner decision 550](#od-550)); [a reverse citation index in `pidx/`](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-reverse-citation-index), if §22.8's `drop` row shows scans binding; for the index, [a word complement or semantic layer](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-index-semantic-layer) in the same buckets, [Elias-Fano key sets](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-index-elias-fano-key-sets), and [per-field postings](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-index-per-field-postings) if §22.8 shows field-scoped queries common.
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-v1), for [git's sha256 object format](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-sha256-object-format) (11.11) and for [the later pass over `slot/`](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-slot-orphan-pass) that 11.8's step 6 names ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Blocking:** §7's token exchange, `rev/`, authorization log and bootstrap, §8's projection, consent rule and access logs, and §10's objects block v0a; counsel's confirmation of [owner decision 133](#od-133)'s condition precedes holds (M5, §21); X13's clusters passing §22's suite and 11.13's benchmark block production storage.

## 12. DNS: the ur.network zone and per-network zones

### 12.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns public naming: the user root (X4), the network label (X5) and X17; the `dns` engine and dns edge; DNSSEC; zone content and reverse zones; the record API; DNS-01; custom domains; private names (with §17); takedown hooks (§21). §13 owns certificates and CAA, §14 and §15 mail record content, §19 the dns edge hosts, §20 quotas. Notation follows D-ARCH-1.

### 12.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-DNS-1 | `<root>` is its own zone; `*.<root>` reaches tlsedge; `mx.<net>.<root>` reaches the local mail server | PLAN.md:80-81,104; [owner decision 32](#od-32) |
| R-DNS-2 | A network owns the zone `<net>.<root>` and its entries | PLAN.md:25 |
| R-DNS-3 | DNS entries 5/200/2000; custom domains Team only | PLAN.md:357,364 |
| R-DNS-4 | DNS reveals as little as possible | CONVENTIONS §0 |
| R-DNS-5 | A released name routes nothing to a new owner | §2 I-14 |
| R-DNS-6 | Labels are issuable LDH labels; platform names are unclaimable | [R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md) §2.2 |
| R-DNS-7 | Challenge TXT served within 60 s (p99); negative TTL ≤ 60 s | [R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §3; §19 |
| R-DNS-8 | Nothing collides with WhoDis on public UDP 53 | vault/main/services.yml:345-347 |
| R-DNS-9 | Mail policy records per network; the sending addresses' PTRs under bringyour.com | RFC 8461 §3.4; [owner decision 124](#od-124) |
| R-DNS-10 | Self-hosted DNS, signed online from the first deploy, on two NS at the one site | owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [109](#od-109), [123](#od-123) |

### 12.3 What exists today

- ur.network: Route 53, expires 2027-07-02; signed by a KMS key shared with bringyour.com, no DS (RDAP 2026-11-03; mmm/lag.dev/ops/dnssec.md:25-27); MX at Google Workspace, `_dmarc` `p=none`, no SPF or CAA (dig 2026-11-03).
- The platform left ur.network on 2026-10-01: `api`, `connect` and `mcp` are NXDOMAIN, though warp and vault list them (apple/app/network/Shared/Config/NetworkConfig.swift:19-23; warp/services/services.go:396-438; vault/main/services.yml:3-35,641-739; config/main/tls.yml:2-6).
- Public UDP 53 on the lb interfaces is connect's WhoDis transport; no TCP 53 (vault/main/services.yml:345-347; server/connect/transport.go:2321).
- network_name: 5-50 of `[a-z0-9-]`, edge hyphens and `xn--` allowed, nothing reserved; one rename path holds the old name 24 h; deletion frees it (server/model/network_model.go:178-206; server/controller/account_controller.go:13,161-166; server/model/account_model.go:379).

### 12.4 Roots: the registrable domain (X4, X17)

A **root** is a user-content zone that `dns` signs and serves (`config/<env>/dns.yml`). v0's one root, `<root>` = ur.network, carries user content only (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [16](#od-16)): burners live in network zones ([owner decision 32](#od-32)), and recurd.dev only redirects to ur.io/recurd (§19; [owner decision 15](#od-15)). Platform names, the report, lb and HELO hosts included ([owner decision 124](#od-124)), live on bringyour.com; `<root>` keeps only `ns1`, `ns2` (glue), `_psl` (the PSL's proof), `canary` (12.6), `<acme_token>.acme` (certs' delegated challenge targets, one a verified custom domain, 12.8) and §14.6's `_spf`, keeping SPF checks in the signed zone.

Until `<root>` is on the Public Suffix List (PSL), its networks share one site (cookies, saved logins), one reputation (§21.6), one Let's Encrypt budget and one DMARC organization ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.5; mmm/lag.dev/ops/psl.md:51-56). Steps (D-DNS-1):
1. M0: renew to 2036 under registrar lock; the PSL wants over 2 years of term at listing.
2. Move platform names and company mail off ur.network, warp and tls.yml; the lb sends `*.<root>` to tlsedge (§13.4), and only the apex redirects to ur.io.
3. Serve the zone from the dns edge, switch NS (no DS exists) and delete the Route 53 zone.
4. Set `_dmarc.<root>` to `p=reject` once company mail has left.
5. Once eligible (~3,000 active users, `_psl`, an abuse contact), apply to the PSL and request recategorization (connect/EXTENDERUPDATE.md §10.1).

Until listed: no URnetwork cookies on the root, HSTS preload with `includeSubDomains`, exact-host autofill (§15, §18), and §13.7's rule for session cookies on same-site requests from other networks' pages.

### 12.5 The network label (X5)

**Label ([owner decision 14](#od-14)).** 10 characters `[a-z][a-z0-9]{9}` from crypto/rand (~51 bits), allocated on first need, immutable, never reassigned, and not derived from network_id, whose ULID exposes creation time ([R:server-identity](design/design-research/server-identity.md) §2.11). A draw that hits an existing row or fails `ScreenName`'s reserved or brand rules is redrawn ([owner decision 97](#od-97)). A sidecar reads its network's label and alias from api's `GET /sidecar/label` (Client, sidecar-classified, under §7.4's `/sidecar/*`), which answers `{network_id, label, alias}` for its token's own network alone, allocating the label on first need, `alias` empty while there is none, and from M5 from 12.8's `GET /dns/zone` as well ([owner decision 421](#od-421)). `dns_label` alone lands in MG2 (§19.7), with `model.EnsureNetworkLabelInTx` and `model.ResolveNetworkLabel`, pending until M2's Gn-out, so `<net>` in `.ur`, git-remote-ur, §9.4's addresses and `network:<net>` hold a real label from M2; draws before M5 run `ValidateDnsName`'s reserved and brand rules, which hold this section's list, curated brands included, and `ScreenName` joins at M5; the rest of `dns_*`, all DNS serving and aliases stay at M5 and M6.

**Alias** (opt-in, "public forever (CT)"): the network_name, one per network: a copy of the label's records except challenges, live once §13's certificates name it. Labels and aliases share `dns_label`'s primary key (root, label) across kinds and states, so alias claims and `RenameNetwork` (§7.12) refuse any name a row holds, live, retiring or tombstoned.

**Validation** (aliases and new names, §7.12; every new name through `ScreenName`, §21.6): `ValidateNetworkName`; no edge `-` (Boulder refuses it); no `--` at positions 3-4 (no `xn--` or IDNA homographs); not reserved; not brand-confusable after mapping 0→o, 1→l, 3→e, 5→s and rn→m per `-` token ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §5). Team scope labels (v1; owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)), from the signed projection (§8), also avoid reserved owners, hosts, client names (§7.7) and word-number labels. The reserved block guards only the names directly below `<root>`, labels, aliases and scope labels, where such a word would pass for a platform name: inside a network's own zone a record owner or published host (§13), `<host>.<net>.<root>`, takes §21.6's brand rules and 12.7's owner table instead, so `www` and `api` there are the network's own, and `ScreenName` screens a host apart from a label ([owner decision 419](#od-419)). Reserved, versioned in the sidecar repo:

```text
www mail mx smtp imap pop dns ns ns1-ns9 edge acme canary rpt out mta-sts autoconfig autodiscover
  wpad isatap localhost
api app web connect mcp gossip grafana taskworker proxy alt monitor mmm lb auth login account admin
  status abuse postmaster security support billing evs gkm sockets tlsedge smtpedge mxedge certs
fuji cosmic fireside crisp gala snow jazz honey, plus every services.yml host label (a release check)
*-lb *-v4 *-v6 main-* beta-* canary-* community-* local-* by-*
ur urnetwork bringyour recurd burner, plus a curated list of the most-phished brands
```

**Census** (a read-only query in M0):

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name !~ '^[a-z0-9-]{5,50}$') AS pre_rule,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name ~ '(^-|-$)') AS edge_hyphen,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE substr(network_name, 3, 2) = '--') AS dash34,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE network_name = ANY($1) OR network_name ~ $2) AS reserved
FROM network;
```

**Renames, deletion and restore (D-DNS-10).** Renaming network_name changes nothing. A changed or released alias serves 90 days as `retiring` (outlasting 5-day sender retries) under CAA `issue ";"`, its certificates revoked (§13), then is tombstoned forever; deleting a network withdraws its records at once and tombstones label and alias, whose certificates are revoked or expire within 45 days. After a Postgres restore and 12.6's restore step (§19.10), taskworker re-reads CT for `<root>` names logged since the restored dump's time minus 7 d and inserts each name `dns_label` lacks as `retiring` with no network; `label-reclaim` (12.8) re-binds it to its network, and the rest tombstone after the 90 days, so I-14 holds across the gap.

### 12.6 Hosting: the self-hosted dns edge

```text
write (api or dns route), one transaction: under a decision, §16.6's gate first (12.8): a stored result
  for the request's effect_key answers it with no write, else the spend check, then the approval_use claim;
  lock the dns_root row (503 while restoring), serial+1, records + dns_zone_journal diff (+ the use's
  result), commit; then raise {dns}serial:<root> to that serial (a script that never lowers it), which
  wakes the feed (PgBouncer's transaction pooling bars LISTEN/NOTIFY)
dns API blocks (dns.bringyour.com), every internal route under /dns/internal/ and taking one caller class's
  bearer (12.8): GET /dns/internal/journal?root=&after=<applied> (long-poll <= 25 s);
  /dns/internal/snapshot (the rows at one serial); a poll the journal cannot continue (after < serial, no
  row after+1: a 7-day gap, a restore) answers reload, with restore_serial; every answer also names each
  lb interface's reported custom-host version, with its probe name and the hosts it added, and the
  map-stale interfaces (§13.4)
  rows and snapshots stay readable across releases N and N+1: N ignores fields N+1 adds, and writes
  N cannot read wait until N+1 serves 100% (§19.11)
dnsedge on ns1, ns2 (host-pinned; UDP and TCP 53; no proxy in front, so RRL sees resolver addresses):
  apply each diff atomically, in serial order --> zone in memory + local snapshot; a reload swaps in
    /dns/internal/snapshot's; a replaced snapshot older than restore_serial is kept only until POST
    /dns/internal/reload-diff takes its diff, at most 24 h, and any other is deleted at once
  serve a zone build or key set only once its self-check passes, else keep the previous one
  answer from memory, sign online, rate-limit; SOA serial = root serial
  probe each lb interface every 10 s (owner decision 34; server/services_lb_inventory.go:11-17,35):
    tlsedge's alert on 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 (§13.4; owner decision 121);
    on 443 also the route probe of the custom-host version the interface reported (§13.4), posted
      to POST /dns/internal/route-probes;
    the 25 banner on §19.5's router interfaces
    drop one after 3 failures, or while the journal names it map-stale (§13.4), never all, and the one
    §19.5's W1 drains
      --> answered from the healthy set at answer time, with no journal write: the A, AAAA at *, @,
          each copy of *'s records and each mx host on router interfaces (12.7)
certs: GET /dns/internal/ready?serial=s, checked in this order --> stale while restoring or for
  s <= restore_serial (certs writes again at a new serial, §13.8); else API blocks read each running NS's
  SOA over TCP and hold while any is below s, a running NS that does not answer included; then
  canary_failing while the canary is not clean (monitor, below), which holds an order with no rewrite and
  no new serial; else ready
running NS: dns_ns(root, ns, state running or stopped, stopped_time, reason), seeded from dns.yml; an NS
  is running whether or not it answers now; the restore step or `sidecarctl dns ns stop|start` writes
  stopped, and it leaves stopped only once it serves at or above restore_serial (owner decision 418)
restore (§19.10, after the dumps load and the abuse step, before api's replay; Postgres comes back at dump
  age with an empty journal, while ns1 and ns2 serve newer zones until they reload):
  §19.10 sets dns_root.restoring as the dumps load, before api or the dns blocks serve: every dns write
    gets 503, so the CT replay (12.5) and api's replay of revocations (§7.10), their DKIM and TLSA
    deletions (I-15) included, commit after this step; until the transaction below, 12.9's SuspendZone,
    SuspendHost and Restore set only their rows, taking no serial, so the suspensions and lifts
    §19.10's abuse step re-places (§21.10) are in its snapshot
  read each running NS's SOA over TCP; an NS that does not answer is written stopped, and serves again
    only from a reload, its local snapshot taken as the replaced one
  one transaction: serial := restore_serial := max(restored serial, the SOAs read, {dns}serial:<root>)
    + 2^24, above every serial the lost primary issued, since the key lacks only raises that failed or
    that a Redis failover lost (RFC 1982 allows a jump below 2^31); raise the key
  each edge reloads at restore_serial and posts its diff (POST /dns/internal/reload-diff); once every
    running NS answers that SOA, restoring := false; the step lists, by network_id, owner and type, each
    RRset but challenges' and canaries' in a posted diff, and raises the custom-host map's version,
    dns_root.custom_host_map_version, 2^24 above max(every network_dns_custom_host.map_version, every
    version in dns_custom_host_map_applied, 0), both tables being in the dump, every host's map_version
    with it, so W1 loads the map from the restored rows (§19.5) and each host stays pending until every
    interface is current for the new version (§13.4), listing the hosts that adds or drops, in the
    incident and in each network's admin events (§7.11), both kept 400 d, flagging networks with an open
    §21 case
monitor, at the site and on 1 outside host: the site's copy rewrites canary.<root> TXT each minute
  through POST /dns/internal/canary {root, value}: value <= 64 printable ASCII bytes, starting with its
  unix ms; TTL 60; one serial and journal row (model.DnsWriteInTx); answered {serial}, 503 while restoring;
  each copy validates it through each NS against the KSK as a configured trust anchor (Unbound
  trust-anchor), the outside copy also checking the value is under 180 s old, and posts POST
  /dns/internal/canary-report {root, source: site or outside, serial, ok}, ok only if the TXT validated
  through every running NS; only the site's copy writes, so no write credential leaves the site;
  dns_canary_verdict(root, source, serial, ok, report_time), primary key (root, source), overwritten in
  place; clean: the site row ok with report_time under 180 s old, and no outside row not ok under 180 s
  old; a missing site row reads as failing; a stale outside row alone holds no order and raises a
  visibility alert;
  2 public resolvers check propagation only until the DS, then validate as well;
  DNSKEY window > 7 d; equal SOA serials
  --> incident alert (server/monitor/alert_classes.go:3-8); from M5, both NS failing or a canary
      signature failing pages §19.8's rota at any hour, 30 min to acknowledge (owner decision 143), and
      one running NS failing SOA reads for 1 h pages it in business hours, since orders then wait (owner
      decision 418)
```

```yaml
# config/<env>/dns.yml (sketch)
roots: [ur.network]
reverse: from smtpedge.yml's sending addresses   # M9; HE's classless delegation; unsigned
delegated: Team customers' _domainkey.<domain> zones   # v1 (§14.6); not roots
ns: [ns1, ns2]                  # two hosts at the site; IPv4 and IPv6 from different gateway blocks
ttl: {challenge: 60, edge: 60, mx: 300, mx_host: 300, tlsa: 300, mail_policy: 3600, caa: 3600,
      user: 300, user_range: [60, 3600], soa_minimum: 60, ns: 86400, ptr: 3600}   # edge: A, AAAA at *, @
rrl: {ipv4_prefix: 24, ipv6_prefix: 56, slip: 2, classes: [answer, denial, error]}
signatures_per_second: <cap per host>   # cached answers first
edns_udp_size: 1232
any: minimal                    # RFC 8482
client_subnet: ignore           # RFC 7871; never echoed or stored
tcp: {connections_per_source: <cap>, idle_timeout_s: 10}
```

**Placement (D-DNS-3; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)).** The `dns` engine (`sidecar/dnsservice`, miekg/dns) runs as server/cli/dns: API blocks serve §12.8's routes and the feed; the edge role, `dnsedge`, runs only on §19's dns edge hosts, whose own addresses leave the lb's UDP 53 to WhoDis (R-DNS-8), and deploys one host at a time (§19.11). Edges never query Postgres (I-12), so with the core down they keep serving and signing while writes and ACME wait. Both NS sit at the one site (12.15).

**Signing (D-DNS-5; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [109](#od-109))**, online from the first deploy:
- **Denial.** ECDSA P-256. Compact denial (RFC 9824; NXDOMAIN kept without DNSSEC) and wildcard answers signed as the queried name reveal neither which names exist nor which a wildcard covers.
- **Keys.** The KSK stays on an offline HSM, backed up in a second safe; a two-person quarterly ceremony pre-signs DNSKEY RRsets (current, next and standby ZSK) in 14-day windows, released one at a time. The current ZSK is a `secret_files` entry (warp/warpctl/run.go:172-204) mounted only on dns edges, rolled quarterly by pre-publication; the standby stays in vault.
- **DS.** Without one, validators treat the zone as insecure, so a fault harms no one and only the anchored monitors prove signing; the DS follows 30 clean canary days, before M7's TLSA, which §15.5's "validated" label checks ([owner decision 135](#od-135)).

**Runbook (§19.10).** NS down or flooded: resolvers retry the other; HE null-routes a flooded address. ZSK leak: mount the standby and hold a ceremony; forgery ends with the old windows (≤ 14 days). Both KSK HSMs lost: a new KSK's DS before the last window expires.

### 12.7 Zone content

System records (TTLs per 12.6; writer dns unless noted; last column, the owning section):

**Edge address records ([owner decision 335](#od-335)).** `*` and `@` A and AAAA are grant-driven. An edge grant is an active publish on `dns:<host>` in that zone, or the system publish: a network with a `mail_network` row and an approved `smtp/25/mx` listen grant, since `mta-sts.<net>.<root>` has no row of its own and resolves only through `*`. `*` has A and AAAA while the zone's set holds any host but `@`, or the system publish; `@` has them while the set holds `@`. After each accepted `POST /network/config/delta` or `POST /network/config/projection`, once the object PUT has committed, api recomputes the set from the state at that position and calls `model.DnsSyncEdgeRecords`, which makes one journal write per transition and none otherwise, in a transaction of its own, since §7.9 commits by conditional PUT and has no transaction to join. An hourly taskworker pass over §21.6's list reconciles both ways: it removes what expired and adds what a crash between the PUT and the write missed. §9.4's `FirstListen` and `LastUnlisten` have no DNS consumer, so whether a listener is up never shows in DNS.

User records:

| Type | Owners | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| A, AAAA | `@`, hosts | Public unicast only: no RFC 1918, 100.64/10, loopback, link-local, 0/8, 198.18/15, documentation, multicast, ULA or DNS stand-ins (connect/net_http_doh.go:329,337); ≤ 8 per RRset |
| CNAME | hosts, alone at the owner | FQDNs outside tombstoned labels |
| TXT | not system owners; no SPF at `@` | printable ASCII, ≤ 1024 bytes |
| MX | hosts, never `@` or `*` | FQDN targets; ≤ 4 per RRset |
| SRV (proposed) | `_svc._proto.<host>` | FQDN targets |
| Wildcard (proposed) | `*.<host>` for A, AAAA, never CNAME | `*` itself is system-owned |
| Refused | NS, DS, DNAME, PTR, CAA, HTTPS/SVCB (no ECH or h3, §13) | |

- **Refused owners** (network and alias zones): `b`, `mx`, `mail`, `mta-sts`, system `_` owners, scope labels and word-number labels (`^[a-z]+-[0-9]{4}$`, kept for burners; [owner decision 32](#od-32)).
- **Lint.** No journal row commits a CNAME beside other data at one owner, system records included (RFC 2181 §10.1).
- **Entries.** One user RRset is one `dns_entries` unit (§20.4); system, DKIM, challenge, alias and edge records are free; `tls_endpoints` bounds edge names.
- **Abuse caps** (pro.yml `sidecar_abuse:`; §21 tightens them): `dns_changes_per_hour` 60, `dns_challenges_per_name_hour` 10, `dns_dkim_selectors` 64 device selectors under `_domainkey.<net>.<root>`, burners' excluded (§14.6).

### 12.8 Record API, DNS-01, custom domains

| Route | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /network/dns` | Network, read roles | label, alias, records, quota; each custom host's state, CAA mode and readiness, a pending one naming the lb interfaces not yet current for it (§13.4); each custom domain's owed DKIM CNAMEs, name and target, by api's own lookup at each read of whether the domain answers each published selector, never stored (§14.6; [owner decision 656](#od-656)) |
| `POST /network/dns/records` | Network, DNS permission (§7.5) | `{expect_version, upserts, deletes}`, compare-and-swap |
| `POST /dns/records` | service token, aud `dns` (§7.8); §8.10's gate for §8 `admin` on `dns:<host>` (I-8) | the same, for sidecars and §16's tools; under a decision rather than a grant, the gate first answers a retry with the stored result of a use committed under its `Idempotency-Key: <effect_key>` while that `approval_use` row lasts, even past `not_after` or with a stale `expect_version`; otherwise it runs §16.6's spend check (D-MCP-12), which needs the request's upserts and deletes to equal its `CanonicalAction`'s `dns_*` fields, and consumes a use in the write's own transaction (§16 D-MCP-11; §2.8 api-10) |
| `POST /network/dns/alias-claim`, `/alias-release`, `/custom-host-add`, `/custom-host-remove` | Network, DNS permission; custom hosts Team only | alias; map `<host>.<domain>`, or an apex `<domain>`, to a host owner of the network, never a network's, alias's or scope's `@`, a strong-mode host staying `pending` until step 3's checks pass; each change to the active rows raises the custom-host map's version, which §19.5's W1 loads on every lb interface on §13.4's schedule, and a host is ready for TLS-ALPN-01 once every interface that 12.6's probe passes is current for its version (§13.4) |
| `POST /network/dns/label-reclaim` | Network, DNS permission | after a Postgres restore only: re-binds an ownerless `retiring` name (12.5) to the caller's network, given `("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/label-reclaim", name, network_id, nonce)` signed by the key of a CT-logged certificate naming it, the nonce being the restore's incident id (§19.10) |
| `GET /dns/zone` | service token, aud `dns` (§7.8); any admitted sidecar of the network | the label, allocated on first need, the alias, the zone version, and the caller's own view: the RRsets and custom-host states (state, CAA mode, readiness, pending interfaces) of the owners on whose `dns:<host>` it holds publish or admin, by §8's gate; never `GET /network/dns`'s whole body, which stays with the read roles §7.5 gives no Member |
| `POST /dns/label-reclaim` | service token, aud `dns` | `POST /network/dns/label-reclaim`'s tuple and signature for a sidecar, the token's network equal to the tuple's `network_id` |
| `POST /dns/internal/acme-challenge`, `/dns/internal/caa-canary`; `GET /dns/internal/ready?serial=` | internal: certs | challenges at most 2 values a name, TTL 60, ≤ 10 per name per hour, gone after 1 h, at `_acme-challenge` owners and a custom domain's `<acme_token>.acme.<root>` (step 3); canaries per the probe (below); ready long-polls ≤ 25 s and answers `stale`, `ready` or `canary_failing` (12.6) |
| `GET /dns/internal/custom-host-map?applied=`; `POST /dns/internal/custom-host-map/applied` | internal: each lb interface's `lbmap` (§19.5 W1), naming its interface, which the API holds to the lb inventory | the newest custom-host map (version, digest, hosts), long-polled ≤ 25 s until it differs from `applied`; then the version the caller's interface loaded, with its nginx master, or a failed render, test or reload (§13.4) |
| `POST /dns/internal/route-probes` | internal: dns edges | each lb interface's route-probe result for the custom-host version it reported (12.6, §13.4) |
| `GET /dns/internal/journal`, `/dns/internal/snapshot`; `POST /dns/internal/reload-diff` | internal: dns edges | the feed (12.6); after a reload across a restore, `{root, replaced_serial, serial, rrsets: [(owner, type)]}`, the RRsets that differ between the replaced snapshot and the new one, which 12.6's restore step maps to networks through `dns_label` |
| `POST /dns/internal/canary`; `POST /dns/internal/canary-report` | internal: the site's monitor, both; the outside monitor, the report alone | 12.6's canary and its verdicts |
| `POST /dns/key-record` | service token; §8 `listen` on `sock:smtp/25/mx` or `smtp/25/mx.<scope>`; a member scope takes only its member's consented devices (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)) | TLSA at `_25._tcp.mx` (or `_25._tcp.mx.<scope>`) for the caller's attested key; the body's repeated `retire_spki_sha256` retires, in the same transaction, the caller's own published keys of that host it names, which a receiver sends with a repeat of its new key once that key serves (§15.5; [owner decision 443](#od-443)); owners notified |

DKIM comes only through §14's `POST /smtp/dkim-keys`, TLSA only through `/dns/key-record`; user and key writes add a `network_admin_event` (§7.11). Sidecars read their zone through `GET /dns/zone`, for §13.4's and §13.8's readiness, §16.5's `dns_records` and §6.8's `dns` refetch, and file a reclaim through `POST /dns/label-reclaim` (§19.10); `/network/dns*` stay the console's and network credentials'.

**Internal routes ([owner decision 417](#od-417)).** Every internal route sits under `/dns/internal/`, where the lb answers 403 to any source off dns's allow list (§19.5 W8). Each caller class holds its own bearer, 256 random bits in one vault file per caller, current and previous values so a rotation needs no downtime, read once at start from `secret_files`: `internal-dnsedge-1.yml` and `internal-dnsedge-2.yml` on the dns edges, `internal-monitor.yml` and `internal-monitor-outside.yml` on the two monitors, `internal-certs.yml` in taskworker's and `internal-lbmap.yml` in the lb's (§19.4). The API block holds only their SHA-256, in `internal-verify.yml`, compares in constant time, and lets each route take only its class: the edges the feed, reload-diff and route-probes; the site's monitor canary and canary-report, the outside monitor canary-report alone; certs acme-challenge, caa-canary and ready; lbmap the custom-host map and its applied route. No secret is per interface, since playbook-edges.yml copies the whole vault to every edge host, and §13.4 counts an interface's report only once a dns edge's route probe of that version passes. An edge needs neither the issuer nor Postgres to keep serving (D-DNS-3).

**Gates.** Upserts creating a public name (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX or SRV owners) and alias claims need §21.7's `network_verified`, else `QuotaRefusal{limit_key: verification}` ([owner decision 96](#od-96)). A name `ScreenName` sends to review is refused with `QuotaRefusal{limit_key: screen_review}` and the case's id, nothing stored in §12's tables and nothing reserved; once a reviewer's `screen_allow` action names the network and the name, the caller's retry passes, and on probation such a name is refused with no case (§21.6; [owner decision 534](#od-534)).

**Direct MX (owner decisions [33](#od-33), [639](#od-639); Team).** Once mxedge has verified each mail indexer of §15.4's `POST /mail/direct-mx` against 12.7's A rules and its `mail_host_key` and posted the result to api, which repoints the zone itself, `mx.<net>.<root>`'s A and AAAA name their addresses and the TLSA set stays; `DELETE` restores the router interfaces. Its MX, A and TLSA stay in URnetwork's zone, so a direct MX does not exclude URnetwork (§2.8 EX2).

Custom domains, Team only (D-DNS-9):
1. Verify TXT `_urnetwork-challenge.<domain>` (§7.6 `network_domain`).
2. **Strong mode** (the default, and every apex): `<host>.<domain>` answers A and AAAA itself, statically with the lb addresses (§19.5; these miss 12.6's health drops) or through a customer-side ALIAS (flattening) of the host owner it maps to, `<host>.<net>.<root>` (an apex host's too; never `@`, whose CAA would govern the zone's device certificates, RFC 8659 §3), that keeps the queried name, synthesizes only A and AAAA, and answers every other type, CAA included, from the customer's zone. **Weak mode:** a CNAME into `<root>`, active at once, accepted only with §2.8 EX1's exception disclosed at setup: CAA discovery follows the CNAME and stops at the first non-empty set (RFC 8659 §3), so URnetwork could publish a CAA at the target admitting its own account.
3. The customer's CAA pins its own ACME account (`accounturi`, RFC 8657; [owner decision 39](#od-39); custody per §13.8); devices pass DNS-01 through a one-time CNAME at `_acme-challenge.<custom host>`, one for each custom host, since a custom certificate names its one host (§13.8), → `<acme_token>.acme.<root>`, where certs writes their challenges, or TLS-ALPN-01, which needs the ordering desktop to hold a publish grant on port 443 of the host's owner ([owner decision 426](#od-426); DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17). `network_domain.acme_token` is 16 bytes from crypto/rand, lowercase base32 with no padding, minted by api when the domain first verifies (§7.6), fixed for the row's life and shown to admins in `GET /network/dns` as the CNAME's target. An ordering desktop posts the 43-character base64url DNS-01 digest to `POST /tls/custom-challenge` (§13.15), and certs, still the only writer, writes it there through `POST /dns/internal/acme-challenge`; `GET /tls/custom-challenge/<id>` passes on `ready`'s answers, `stale` and `canary_failing` included, so the desktop asks the CA only on `ready` and posts the value again on `stale`. DNS-01 orders never wait on map readiness (§13.4). A strong-mode host commits `pending`, unmapped with `effective_caa_chain_ok` false, while a certs taskworker chain walks its CAA discovery and runs the probe below: both passing make it active, and a walk meeting a name in a URnetwork zone, or a failed probe, refuses it (`custom_host_caa_operator_alias`), each as an admin event. certs repeats both on §13.8's schedule; a failure there clears `effective_caa_chain_ok` until a check passes and records §2.8 EX1's exception in an admin event that alarms the network's admins, the host staying mapped, exposed as a weak-mode one is. The ordering desktops repeat the walk before each order (§13.8).
4. §13.4's split sends each active custom host's SNI to tlsedge, which maps it via `network_dns_custom_host`; mail uses MX `mx.<net>.<root>`, §14.6's selectors (CNAMEd or delegated to `dns`) and the customer's `_dmarc` with `adkim=s`. In strict mode (§15.4; [owner decision 98](#od-98)) the MX is the customer's `<mx>.<domain>` in its own signed zone, with TLSA at `_25._tcp.<mx>.<domain>` and A and AAAA to the router interfaces, mapped in `network_dns_custom_host` for mxedge (§2.8 mx-3). Only this path, with every MX host the recipient domain lists and its TLSA customer-signed, carries strict mode's exclusion of URnetwork; an MX host or TLSA in a URnetwork zone stays under §2.8 EX2. An active strict-mode MX host at or under a verified domain also makes the domain strict for outbound mail, so mapping or unmapping one moves its envelope between `b.<domain>` and `b.<net>.<root>`, whether or not `mail.strict` is signed yet, which an admin orders accordingly (§14.6; [owner decision 655](#od-655)).
5. A downgrade's withholding (§20.7) sets each active TLS web host of a custom domain `withheld`, which takes it out of the custom-host map, raising its version, and out of tlsedge's routing, while its row, verification and CAA mode stay (D-QUOTA-6); a release after a renewal sets it `active` with `map_version` 0, so it re-enters the map at the next version and is pending until every interface is current, as a new host is, with no re-verification and no new CAA walk. certs' result never turns a withheld host active, and a strict-mode MX host is never withheld, mail hosts keeping MX, TLSA and routing; §14's From-domain gate withholds the domain's mail From beside it ([owner decision 420](#od-420)).

```text
CAA probe (certs, for a strong-mode host once its walk passes; one probe per target at a time):
  publish  POST /dns/internal/caa-canary: <host>.<net>.<root> CAA = the walk's effective set (the
           customer's pin) + 0 urcanary "<128-bit nonce>", TTL 60 (12.7), at serial s; then
           /dns/internal/ready?serial=s
  query    repeat the walk's CAA queries at the authoritative servers of each zone it visits, RD=0,
           every 30 s for 10 min (ten times our 60 s negative TTL)
  verdict  the nonce in any answer (the ALIAS flattens CAA), or a canary the lint refuses (a CNAME
           at <host>) --> fail; else pass, once /dns/internal/ready?serial=s answers ready again
           after the last query
  canary   canary_failing counts as ready at both ready checks: §13.8 ties 12.6's canary to orders
           only, and these RD=0 queries validate no DNSSEC
  stale    at either ready (a restore, 12.6, whose edges may lack the canary) --> publish again
           under a new nonce and restart the window
  delete   the canary and its copy in one write, whatever the verdict; taskworker expires one older
           than 1 h, as it does challenges
```

CAs ignore unknown non-critical tags (RFC 8659 §3, §4.1), so the canary admits only the customer's pin, even flattened or cached.

### 12.9 Private names, visibility, capabilities, abuse hooks

**Private names ([owner decision 85](#od-85)).** `<client-name>.<net>.<root>` maps §7.7's client names to §17's overlay addresses (X18), which lie in 100.64/10 or RFC 1918 ([owner decision 132](#od-132)), so 12.7 refuses them in public records. C14's `UpgradeMux.SetLocalZone` answers them on app paths, fed in each app's VPN component by the names its forwarding role compiles into §17.8's `BridgeState` (§18.6; [owner decision 197](#od-197)); §17's per-link resolver answers them under `ur tun`. A name in the table gets an answer for every qtype, A or NODATA (the overlay has no IPv6; browsers also ask HTTPS), so no query for it leaves the device; other names pass through. The table omits a client name equal to a live published host or record owner, which §7.7's signers also refuse.

```go
type LocalZone interface { // nil keeps today's behavior
	// owned with no addrs answers NODATA; !owned passes the query through
	Answer(host string, qtype uint16) (addrs []netip.Addr, ttl uint32, owned bool)
}
func (self *UpgradeMux) SetLocalZone(localZone LocalZone)
```

**Enumeration.** CT shows labels, aliases and scope labels, never hosts (§13.8); under compact denial, hosts and replying burners' labels ([owner decision 79](#od-79)) can only be guessed, which RRL slows.

**Visibility and capabilities:** §2.8's dns-1, dns-2, EX1 and EX2. No third party serves the zone, edges log no query (I-13), and the zone and CT watches detect forgery (D-TRUST-9, D-TLS-8).

**Abuse (§21).** `SuspendZone(networkId, reason, until)`, `SuspendHost(networkId, host)` withhold records, MX included, and `Restore` returns them, within one write plus the TTL (≤ 3600 s), or, before 12.6's restore transaction, through rows its snapshot carries; tlsedge and mxedge read the same rows. A zone's suspension is its `network_dns_zone` row's reason and until. A host's is no flag on its records but a `network_dns_host_suspension(network_id, host, create_time)` row, carried in the journal and every snapshot as a withheld owner that dnsedge answers NODATA for every qtype, so `*` no longer covers the host. A suspension withholds a record by its `withheld_time`, keeping the row for `Restore`; each record also keeps its `create_time` and, for a challenge or canary, its `expire_time`.

### 12.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Route 53, or a hidden primary with anycast secondaries | anycast; flood absorption | third parties see every query | ruled out ([owner decision 69](#od-69)) |
| An offline-signed zone with NSEC3 | no ZSK on public hosts | dictionary attacks on names; health answers need re-signing | rejected ([owner decision 69](#od-69)) |
| A ZSK in a KMS or HSM | no key in host memory | a round trip per random-name query, which a flood exhausts | rejected |
| `*` CNAME to a shared edge name | one record | excludes the wildcard MX (RFC 2181 §10.1) | rejected |
| A CNAME from each custom host into `<root>` | one record; follows 12.6's health drops | CAA discovery follows it to a target URnetwork writes (RFC 8659 §3) | weak mode only, disclosed (D-DNS-9) |

### 12.11 Decisions proposed

**D-DNS-1 (proposed).** Roots are config; v0's only root is ur.network, for user content (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [32](#od-32)). *Why:* changing the root later breaks every address.

**D-DNS-2 (proposed).** Labels are random, lazy, immutable and never reused; aliases are copies. `<net>` (§8, §9) resolves label, then alias; legacy network_name resolves only for interactive input. *Why:* a network_name another network later takes captures no grant.

**D-DNS-3 (proposed).** Only 12.6's self-hosted dns edge serves `<root>`, from two NS at the site (owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123)). *Why:* no third party sees queries, and names resolve through core outages.

**D-DNS-4 (proposed).** TTLs follow 12.6. *Why:* ACME, failover and takedown need short caching.

**D-DNS-5 (proposed).** Online signing from the first deploy: compact denial, an offline KSK, 14-day DNSKEY windows, the DS after 30 clean days (12.6; owner decisions [69](#od-69), [109](#od-109)). *Why:* nothing can be walked, and a leaked ZSK dies with its windows.

**D-DNS-6 (proposed).** System records follow 12.7, with no wildcard CNAME; an entry is one user RRset; a replying burner's label carries the wildcard's records (D-DNS-11). *Why:* strict DMARC keeps networks from passing as one another, and a wildcard CNAME would drop the burner MX.

**D-DNS-7 (proposed).** 12.7 refuses non-public addresses and the listed types and owners, and caps RRsets; SRV and `*.<host>` extend [owner decision 70](#od-70)'s own records. *Why:* it blocks rebinding and overlay leaks, protects §13-§15 and keeps burner labels under the wildcard.

**D-DNS-8 (proposed).** certs is the only DNS-01 writer, after checking the caller's §8 grant; writes are rate-limited, ready-checked and expire after 1 h. *Why:* least privilege, one issuance queue (D-TLS-7) and Let's Encrypt's failed-authorization limit.

**D-DNS-9 (proposed).** Custom domains use 12.8's verified TXT, one-time `_acme-challenge` CNAME and the customer's CAA `accounturi` pin ([owner decision 39](#od-39)). A strong-mode host keeps its effective CAA under customer authority, through customer A/AAAA or an ALIAS that synthesizes only A and AAAA, never a CNAME into `<root>`, which certs checks by the walk and the canary probe before the host goes live and on §13.8's schedule; a CNAME host is weak mode, under §2.8 EX1. *Why:* devices pass DNS-01 without per-order edits, and CAA discovery follows a CNAME, or an ALIAS that also flattens CAA, to a target URnetwork writes (RFC 8659 §3), so only a customer-held chain keeps URnetwork from issuing.

**D-DNS-10 (proposed).** Labels and aliases are tombstoned forever; a changed alias retires over 90 days. *Why:* old certificates and mail retries cannot enable a takeover.

**D-DNS-11 (proposed).** A `<blabel>` with any child owner carries an explicit copy of the wildcard's MX, A and AAAA, written and removed atomically with its selectors; dnsedge answers the copy from `*`'s current records, health drops included (12.6, 12.7). *Why:* an empty non-terminal blocks the wildcard (RFC 4592 §2.2), so a replying burner's first selector would otherwise end its inbound mail, and copied addresses would keep serving a dropped interface.

### 12.12 Open questions

**Q-DNS-1.** [X4] Which registrable domain carries user names? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 13](#od-13)):** (b1), ur.network for user content only, signed, strict-DMARC and PSL-listed when eligible (§12.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-2.** [X5] What is a network's label? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 14](#od-14)):** (a), opaque, random and immutable, with an opt-in alias equal to network_name (§12.5). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-3.** [X17] Which roots and keys does recURd use? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [15](#od-15), [108](#od-108)):** ur.io/recurd on the main bringyour.com services, with no dedicated keys; recurd.dev redirects there (§12.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-4.** Which providers serve `<root>`? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71)):** none: a self-hosted dns edge, signed online, with two NS on separate hosts at the site (§12.6; [owner decision 123](#od-123)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-5.** Cross-cutting (§15, X6): when is the root signed? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 109](#od-109)):** from the dns edge's first deploy (M5, main-dark), soaked before inbound mail relies on DANE (D-DNS-5). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-6.** Does "owns all entries" (PLAN.md:25) let a network override system records or publish non-public addresses? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 70](#od-70)):** (a): own A/AAAA, CNAME, TXT and extra MX records under quota; system records, NS/DNAME and private or loopback addresses refused (D-DNS-7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-DNS-7.** Cross-cutting (§19). Should one NS run outside the site before M7? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 123](#od-123)):** (b), two NS at the one site only, though RFC 2182 §3.1 and §5 want one well removed. Every gateway block reaches the internet through Hurricane Electric (vault/main/services.yml:82-104), so a site or HE outage stops every `<root>` name and, from M7, inbound mail until restored, bouncing mail whose senders' retries (14 h to 5 d, §15.3) end first (12.15). *Residual:* none.

### 12.13 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:25 "`<me>.ur.network`".** The default label is opaque; the name becomes an opt-in alias ([owner decision 14](#od-14); Q-DNS-2).
- **PLAN.md:25 "owns all entries".** System records are fixed; some types, owners and addresses are refused ([owner decision 70](#od-70); Q-DNS-6).
- **PLAN.md:104 "`mail.<me>.ur.network`".** The mail host is `mx.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 32](#od-32); Q-MAIL-3).
- **Not in PLAN.md.** A self-hosted dns edge replaces Route 53 for ur.network (owner decisions [13](#od-13), [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71)), consistent with PLAN.md:80.

### 12.15 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| A site or Hurricane Electric outage, or a flood, stops both NS: every `<root>` name, ACME DNS-01, DANE and, from M7, inbound mail fail until restored; paged out of hours, 30 min to acknowledge, it can still outlast senders' retries (14 h to 5 d, §15.3), bouncing their mail | Medium | Critical | Accepted (owner decisions [123](#od-123), [143](#od-143)); separate hosts and blocks; RRL |
| A signing fault or lost KSK breaks validation; CAs refuse issuance | Low | Critical | self-check, canary (paged from M5), soak, standby ZSK, backup HSM |
| A leaked ZSK, URnetwork or a registrar hijacker forges records | Low | High | zone watch (D-TRUST-9), CT watch, 14-day windows, registrar lock (12.4) |
| A weak-mode custom host, or an ALIAS that also flattens CAA, lets URnetwork publish the CAA that governs it; the canary probe is URnetwork's own, so a compelled operator can pass such an ALIAS at setup or renewal, leaving it as exposed as weak mode (§2.8 EX1) | Low | High | strong mode by default and for every apex; the probe refuses CAA flattening unless the operator is compelled (12.8); setup discloses §2.8 EX1; zone watches (D-TRUST-9) and the CT watch (D-TLS-8), the only control against a compelled operator |
| Safe Browsing flags, or a registrar holds, the whole root | Medium | Critical | takedown hooks; §19.8's pager carries registrar and registry notices from M5 (owner decisions [134](#od-134), [143](#od-143)); PSL; nothing critical on the apex |
| The PSL declines or lags; Talos keeps "Personal VPN" | High | Medium | §12.4's interim rules; recategorization; custom domains |

### 12.16 Phasing

Milestones and the v0 and v1 sets are §23.4's.
- **v0:** renewal and census (M0); labels, `dns_label` and api's `GET /sidecar/label` (M2); `ur tun`'s resolver (M4) and C14's seam, dark on app paths until §18's app hosts (M8; [owner decision 85](#od-85)); the moved root signed without a DS, labels, edge, challenge, SPF, DMARC, null MX and user records, routes, gates, quotas, suspension, label reclaim and the restore step, the canary and its pages (M5); mail records, `b`, `mx`, TLSA and the DS (M7); replying burners' selectors and label copies, the reverse zones' PTRs (M9).
- **v1:** aliases, custom domains in both CAA modes, Team scopes (M6); direct MX and strict-mode MX hosts (M7); scope mail hosts with §15 (M8).
- **Later:** [the PSL application](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-psl-listing) once eligible, then §14.6's cut-over; [bring-your-own NS](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-bring-your-own-ns); [HTTPS/SVCB](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-https-svcb-records).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Blocking:** §19's dns edge hosts block M5; the soak blocks the DS and M7's DANE; §13.4's generated split map blocks M6's custom hosts; HE's reverse delegation blocks M9's PTRs.

## 13. The TLS edge and certificates

### 13.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns the public path to published names: the lb's SNI split and ports, `tlsedge` and its connect identity, the sidecar's TLS front, certificates and the CT watch, endpoint counting, abuse hooks and `ur bridge public-tls`.

Under X1 (decided, §0), TLS ends only in the listening sidecar; `tlsedge` routes by SNI without a user key. §9 owns Find, §6 streams and contracts, §8 grants and owner consent, §12 records and the dns edge, §19 lb rendering, §20 payment and §21 abuse policy.

### 13.2 Requirements

| Id | Requirement | Source |
|---|---|---|
| R-TLS-1 | lbs forward network names (`*.<root>`) to tlsedge, unterminated | PLAN.md:81, :84 |
| R-TLS-2 | tlsedge opens a client on a network, finds a listener and accepts over the subprotocol | PLAN.md:82 |
| R-TLS-3 | Certificates are automatic for each listened endpoint | PLAN.md:84 |
| R-TLS-4 | Edge sees only encrypted bytes and small headers (SNI); key stays in the sidecar | owner directive 2026-11-03; sidecar/design/pitch5.html:699 |
| R-TLS-5 | Explicit, authenticated by default, short-lived; no agent control panels | sidecar/design/pitch5.html:698 |
| R-TLS-6 | TLS edge 1/20/200; usage counts toward transfer balance; custom domains Team only | PLAN.md:353, :358, :364 |
| R-TLS-7 | `ur bridge public-tls hostname:[local ip]:local port`; TLS only; Let's Encrypt | cli/UI.md:47, :106, :120 |
| R-TLS-8 | No client IP logged; removal revokes the device's certificate; CT watched | §2 I-13, I-15, D-TRUST-6 |
| R-TLS-9 | Shared lb addresses; TCP 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 | owner decisions [34](#od-34), [68](#od-68), [121](#od-121) |

### 13.3 What exists today

**lb.** Each interface runs its own nginx (vault/main/services.yml:338-475): http servers bind `443 ssl` (warp/warpctl/config.go:1857-1863) and key their limits on `$binary_remote_addr` (:1496-1545); stream servers send PROXY v1 (:2508-2510), idle out at 15 min (:1383) and take `tcp_stream_port_services` (warp/services/services.go:558). `ssl_preread` is compiled in, unused (warp/lb/Dockerfile:58). Host networking rewrites IP `listen`s, not `unix:` ones (warp/nginx.go:354), behind per-interface DNAT (warp/warpctl/run.go:3126-3136).

**ACME.** The extender chain orders by DNS-01 with the client's CSR, revokes, caps weekly orders with Retry-After holds and renews at two thirds of the lifetime, lacking ARI (server/taskworker/work/extender_measurement_acme.go:34-36, :232-335; extender_measurement_work.go:384-392).

**Missing:** the split, tlsedge, certs, the front, a CT watch, ARI, the Service mode (§4 C9) and an in-place lb reload (warp/nginx.go:51-79 only drains nginx, on SIGQUIT or SIGTERM).

### 13.4 Ingress: the SNI split, ports, PROXY, port 80

```text
visitor --TCP 443--> any lb interface (shared, owner decision 34): nginx stream server, ssl_preread
    SNI under <root>, or an active custom host --PROXY v1--> tlsedge --POST /socket/find--> sockets (§9)
    other SNI, or none --PROXY v1--> unix socket --> http servers (platform names, as today)
tlsedge ==§6 stream, Required, Service mode==> listening sidecar (TLS ends here) --> [local ip]:local port
```

**The split (Q-TLS-1, [owner decision 34](#od-34)).** A stream server takes TCP 443 on every interface, ahead of the http servers (§19 W1):

```nginx
# stream {}. Exact names win, then the longest wildcard, so platform names left under <root> keep
# working until §12.4's move. warpctl refuses to render a <root> name absent from §12.5's reserved
# list; W1's generator refuses a custom host under <root> or a platform domain.
map $ssl_preread_server_name $tls_split_upstream {
    hostnames;
    ur.network        lb-https;  # the apex, which redirects to ur.io (§12.4)
    <platform-name>   lb-https;  # generated: each name the http servers serve under <root>; none after
                                 #   §12.4's move. www is reserved (§12.5): tlsedge answers it
                                 #   unrecognized_name.
    *.ur.network      stream-service-block-tlsedge-443;
    include /run/warp-lb/tls-custom-hosts.map;  # generated: one "<host>.<domain>
                                 #   stream-service-block-tlsedge-443;" per active custom host (§12.8),
                                 #   and one for the map version's probe name (custom hosts, below)
    default           lb-https;  # platform names, unknown SNI, hellos without SNI
}
upstream lb-https { server unix:/run/warp-lb/https.sock; }
server {
    listen 443 reuseport backlog=65535;
    listen [::]:443 reuseport backlog=65535;
    ssl_preread on;
    preread_timeout 10s;         # tlsedge's ClientHello deadline (13.5)
    proxy_protocol on;           # PROXY v1 to both branches
    proxy_pass $tls_split_upstream;
    # proxy_buffer_size: 16k by default, two buffers per session; the gate sizes it. connect's H1
    # transport, which carries pushes and relayed sidecar traffic, passes here; H3 keeps UDP 443.
}

# http {}. Every 443 listen moves to the socket (options on the first server only, as today): host
# networking rewrites IP listens (warp/nginx.go:338-431), and `pass` cannot carry preread bytes
# ([R:ext-edge] §2.7). realip restores $remote_addr and $remote_port from PROXY
# (src/http/modules/ngx_http_realip_module.c:238-239 at the lb's pinned nginx commit), so the
# interface's 450/min zone, net_connections cap and exclude_subnets keep their per-visitor key and
# X-UR-Forwarded-For is unchanged; without it, every visitor would share one key.
listen unix:/run/warp-lb/https.sock ssl proxy_protocol backlog=65535;
set_real_ip_from unix:;          # only the stream server reaches the socket
real_ip_header proxy_protocol;
```

**Custom hosts (D-TLS-12; Team, v1).** `network_dns_custom_host`'s active rows (§12.8, a strong-mode host entering only once certs' walk and probe pass, 13.8) say what the lb should route; whether each lb interface does is a separate, reported state.
- **Versions.** Each change to the active rows, §12.6's restore step included, raises the custom-host map's version in its transaction, its digest being the SHA-256 of the version's sorted host list, and an entering host keeps that version as its `map_version`.
- **Loading.** Beside each lb interface's nginx, §19 W1's `lbmap` loads the newest version: before nginx serves 443 at start, and otherwise 5 s after the first unapplied version, at most once per 15 min, since each reload keeps the old workers, with their connections, for up to `worker_shutdown_timeout` (60 min; warp/warpctl/config.go:1181). It renders `tls-custom-hosts.map` and the port-80 redirect's custom names from that version's rows, plus one line sending the version's probe name, `<digest[0:12]>.map.probe.invalid` (RFC 6761 §6.4), to tlsedge, runs `nginx -t`, reloads, and reports the version loaded with its nginx master's pid and start time (`POST /dns/internal/custom-host-map/applied`, §12.8); a failed render, test or reload keeps the prior map and is reported. Its long-polls repeat the report, and an interface whose `lbmap` has not polled for 2 min, or whose nginx master has changed since its report, has loaded no version.
- **Route probes.** Every 10 s each dns edge sends each interface, on 443 as a visitor would, ClientHellos offering ALPN `ur-route-probe` then `http/1.1` for the probe name of the version that interface reported, and, once per reported version, for up to 16 hosts it added (§12.6). tlsedge answers each `unrecognized_name` with no Find (13.5), while the http branch would select `http/1.1` and present a platform certificate (warp/warpctl/config.go:1851-1887). An interface is current for a version once it reported that version or a later one loaded, an edge's probe of the reported version's probe name passed within the last 2 min, and the latest probe of each added host probed for the reported version passed, a failing host probe repeating every 10 s until one passes.
- **Ready.** A host is ready once every lb interface that §12.6's probe passes is current for its `map_version`. `GET /network/dns` shows a host that is not as pending, naming those interfaces, and `GET /dns/zone` shows a sidecar the hosts it publishes or administers the same way (§12.8), and devices start a TLS-ALPN-01 order, a renewal's included, only while it is ready (13.8); DNS-01 orders never wait. Readiness is an operational target, about 15 min and paged past 20 min (§19.8), not a timer.
- **Map-stale.** An interface that is not current for every version older than 20 min is map-stale: the dns edges drop it from user-name answers as they drop a failed one, never all (§12.6), and it pages until it is current again. A strong-mode host with static addresses misses that drop, as it misses every health drop (§12.8), and a host added meanwhile stays pending, naming the interface.

Until the reload, tlsedge answers a host that left the active rows `unrecognized_name` from §12's map (13.5). *Invariant:* a ready custom host's ClientHello reaches tlsedge on every interface that §12.6's probe passes, and platform, user, unknown and absent SNI route as before (§22.8 FS-35, FS-122).

**Gate.** Before any interface flips, §22 benches split against unsplit nginx on one test interface at the observed peak and at `concurrent_clients` (786,432; vault/main/services.yml:357): ≤5% less throughput on connect's H1 transport, ≤1 ms more p99 for connect and api, head-to-hint p99 ≤2 s, ≤15% more CPU per Gbit/s, memory within headroom. Nothing flips until it passes.

**Rollout** (§19 W1). `warpctl deploy main lb <version> <block>` (warp/warpctl/main.go:66-68) flips interfaces to the split one at a time. Each first runs it drained, out of DNS answers by sidecar.yml's `drained`, the one list `warpctl dns` and the dns edges both read, `warpctl dns` leaving the interface out of the `<env>-lb` sets while keeping its health checks, so only probes and the gate's bench reach it; it then rejoins and is held 24 h against unsplit ones on the gate's metrics. Until launch, only internal and design-partner networks publish ([owner decision 91](#od-91)).

**Probes.** An interface that does not answer a hello for the reserved `probe.edge.<root>` with tlsedge's `unrecognized_name` leaves user-name answers (§12.6); monitor's verified handshake and §19 W7's HTTPS checks with SNI drop a broken one from platform answers. From M5 a failing probe pages at any hour ([owner decision 143](#od-143)). The `probe.edge.<root>` hello cannot test the custom-host map, since the `*.<root>` wildcard routes it whatever the map holds; the dns edges' route probes (custom hosts, above) do, and from M6 a map-stale interface leaves user-name answers and pages too.

**Ports.** 8443, 8883 and 5671 ([owner decision 121](#od-121)) go unsplit to tlsedge as permanent stream ports (§19 W7), since no platform name uses them (vault/main/services.yml:339-341); tlsedge takes the port from its accepting listener, as DNAT rewrites PROXY's destination.

**PROXY.** tlsedge's listener (§4.5) takes PROXY v1 or v2 only from the lb, dropping connections without it: `tlsedgeservice.NewProxyHeaderListener` holds pires/go-proxyproto on the engine leg, server/cli/tlsedge applies it, and server/cli/mxedge may call it, since server may import both engines. The visitor address feeds caps, §9's affinity key (a keyed /24 or /48 hash) and `TlsEdgeOpen.client_ip`; logs drop IP literals (server/scrub.go:112; §19.4).

**Port 80** stays with the http servers: a generated server for `*.<root>` and the active custom hosts redirects to `https://` and logs nothing (I-13), so no plaintext reaches tlsedge and HTTP-01 is never served.

### 13.5 tlsedge: the connection path

1. Read the PROXY header and TLS records until the ClientHello completes; a bounds-checked parser (`tlsedgeservice/clienthello.go`, after connect/ip_sni.go:331-462) extracts SNI, ALPN and ECH presence; a hello that does not parse gets `decode_error` and a close. `ReadClientHello`, `ParseClientHello`, `NormalizeSni` and `WriteTlsAlert` export from `tlsedgeservice`, and server/mxedgehost passes them into `MxEdgeDeps` as functions, so no engine imports another (§15.4). A hello whose ALPN list includes `ur-route-probe` gets `unrecognized_name` at once, whatever its SNI, with no lookup, Find or record: it is 13.4's route probe.
2. Normalize the SNI (lowercase, no trailing dot, LDH) and map it with the listener's port to `(network_id, tls/<port>/<host>)` through §12's label map, held in memory by `TlsEdgeStore`: a full snapshot at start, then `model.DnsLabelMapSince` every 5 s, so a withdrawn name stops mapping within 10 s, read through tlsedge's restricted Postgres role off the path (§19.4), a process that cannot load its first snapshot staying not ready and a running one keeping its last through a Postgres outage, so no connection path touches Postgres (I-12; [owner decision 495](#od-495)); (`<host>.<x>.<root>`, or `<x>.<root>` as `@`, `<x>` a label or live alias) or custom-host map; deeper names match only v1 scope hosts, `<label>.<scope>` (Q-TLS-3).
3. Check, in memory, the kill switch, the caps (13.9) and a 30 s negative cache of `no_listener` and `denied`, which absorbs scans, keyed on (name, port, sorted offered ALPN set), so one scanner's bogus ALPN cannot refuse every visitor to a name. A network's limits load in the background through `ServiceHost.Quota.Limits`, cached per network; until they arrive it gets Community's caps, never a refusal, and the kill switch waits on none of it.
4. Call Find (§9.6) as `autogroup:public` with the offered ALPN ids in hello order, as many as keep the encoded `TlsEdgeOpen` within 512 B, the list `TlsEdgeOpen` carries, an affinity key and the process's K client ids; Find applies §8 `MayPublish` (for 13.9's system publish, the receiver's `smtp/25/mx` listen grant, §9.10) and `MayDial` and returns primary and backup tickets, each naming the tlsedge client that opens it.
5. From that client, send `StreamOpen{target, metadata: TlsEdgeOpen, ticket, early_data}` with the hello's first 2,048 B (§6.7), the rest of a longer (PQ) hello following at once in StreamData within the initial window, not after the accept. §9's retries finish before the visitor's first byte, showing only as delay; tlsedge blames a listener only for an accept timeout, never for a visitor's reset.
6. Splice under §6 credit; FIN maps to StreamClose, RST to StreamReset.
7. On failure, send a plaintext alert before any ServerHello and close: `unrecognized_name` for unknown, unpublished, denied or killed names, which are indistinguishable; `decode_error` for a hello that does not parse; `internal_error` for no listener, busy, quota, a cap, the gate off, an unready map or overload. A Find that finds no listener for the offered ALPN keeps `internal_error`, since no application byte moves and FS-34 holds; 13.7's `no_application_protocol` covers hellos that reach the front. tlsedge never presents a certificate.

```proto
message TlsEdgeOpen {              // StreamOpen.metadata, edge -> listener (§6 0x1501), <= 512 B
  bytes client_ip = 1;             // 4 or 16 B, from PROXY; edge memory only
  uint32 client_port = 2;
  string server_name = 3;          // normalized SNI
  repeated string alpn = 4;        // offered by the visitor, in hello order, cut to keep this message <= 512 B;
                                   // informational: the listener decides from the real hello, so a hello whose
                                   // only matching id was cut finds no listener
  uint32 client_hello_byte_count = 5;
  bytes connection_id = 6;         // 16 random B; joins abuse reports for 24 h
  uint64 expire_time_millis = 7;   // the ticket's grant_expire_time_millis; streams end here
}
```

A listener trusts `TlsEdgeOpen` only when admission step 3 passes and the ticket's `dialer_network_id` is `urnetwork-edge` (§9.6).

```yaml
# config/<env>/tlsedge.yml (sketch; endpoint and visitor caps are pro.yml's, 13.9)
clients: 4                                          # K (13.6)
max_connections: 50000                              # per process (13.9)
blocks: 4                                           # required, >= 1: the lb hosts running tlsedge, each host's
                                                    #   g1 block once and its beta block not at all; caps divide
                                                    #   by it (13.9); it has no default, and tlsedge refuses to
                                                    #   start without it
proxy_header: {timeout_s: 2, max_bytes: 2048}
client_hello: {timeout_s: 10, max_bytes: 16384}
find: {timeout_s: 2, max_finds: 3}                  # D-SOCK-6
accept: {ticket_timeout_s: 5, setup_timeout_s: 15}
idle_timeout_s: 900                                 # the lb's proxy_timeout
drain_s: 600                                        # a deploy's old process drains, then resets, on its own slot's
                                                    #   clients (13.6); streams end at grant expiry
```

§22 targets (p95): setup adds ≤300 ms warm and ≤1.5 s cold, contract round trip and e2e handshake included.

### 13.6 tlsedge as a connect client

Each tlsedge process runs K connect clients in the platform network `urnetwork-edge` (§4's `ServiceClientSource`), Required and relay-only toward sidecars (D-PROTO-6), so `TlsEdgeOpen` rides only sealed streams; Find's tickets pin each listener's edge streams to one of them, spreading load across K inline readers (§9.6; [R:connect-transport](design/design-research/connect-transport.md) §2.4).

**Edge clients (owner decisions [428](#od-428), [577](#od-577)).** An edge block, tlsedge, mxedge's router or smtpedge, mounts no vault and no network-level token: it holds the `edge` class's bearer for api's internal gate surface (§8.9), 256 random bits with current and previous values in its `secret_files`, read once at start, api holding only its SHA-256, the block's file and api's line both written by a `sidecarctl` command the owner runs (§19.4; [owner decision 638](#od-638)). `POST /internal/gate/edge-client`, which takes only that class, answers a short-lived client jwt, beside it the 15-minute sockets token the edge's Finds and registrations present (§9.8; [owner decision 589](#od-589)), and the url the pool needs for one client of `urnetwork-edge`, whose id api derives from (environment, host, block, slot, index) by a fixed, documented derivation and creates on first use; it refuses a host the environment's config does not name, an index at or past the block's K and a slot at or past the slot count, 4. `server.NewPlatformClientSource` asks for each of its K indexes at start and refreshes each jwt before it lapses, the jwt's life and the refresh point being settings, so a restart reuses its ids and the edge keeps no state. Every process of an edge service on a host holds its own slot: the beta and g1 blocks of tlsedge, and of mxedge's router, run side by side on every lb host (§19.4) and pass the same environment, host and block, so warp gives each new process (`WARP_SLOT`, beside `WARP_BLOCK`) a slot that no running process of that service on the host holds, listing them by the `warp.env` and `warp.service` labels, not the name prefix, which mxedge-platform's containers share, and server's `EdgeClientKeySettings` and warp's `DeploySlotSettings` both count 4 slots ([owner decision 577](#od-577)). The beta and g1 processes, and a deploy's old and new process of each, so hold different clients: the new process connects its own K while the old one drains its streams for `drain_s` (13.5), each counting only its own toward readiness; `urnetwork-edge` holds at most four times K clients a block and host, and a stolen edge bearer mints only its environment's fixed edge clients. taskworker's reap of idle top-level clients (`RemoveDisconnectedNetworkClients`) leaves the clients of sidecar.yml's `urnetwork_edge` out of its idle marking, so an edge slot unused for 30 days can still be deployed into and the mint finds its derived clients active; the set stays bounded by the config, an operator's removal still ends a client, and a host dropped from the config keeps its clients until an operator removes them ([owner decision 591](#od-591)). The marking holds off while taskworker's process has no good read of sidecar.yml: a config that came from a failed first read, the file there but unreadable or unparsable with no earlier read to keep, marks nothing in that run, the reap's other passes running as before, while an absent file still lets the marker run, since the environment then has no `urnetwork_edge` to protect. The marker so fails in the direction that loses nothing, as the reader's gates do, sidecar.yml stays the only source for the edge network, and ordinary idle clients wait for the first good read, minutes against a 30-day threshold ([owner decision 622](#od-622)).

Contracts in both directions use §6.10.1's Service mode (C9; [owner decision 11](#od-11)), issued only while §9's Find-recorded pair lives.

A sidecar provides Service only while it holds a `tls/` or §15 `smtp/` registration, or while it holds a `ur/` stream, from a `ur/` ticket's open until its last `ur/` stream ends (§6.10.1 item 2; [owner decision 298](#od-298)), within §6.7's edge-peer budget; above half of GOMEMLIMIT, new streams open at 64 KiB windows. Sidecars get `TlsHint` (orders, issuance, revocation) on topic `tls`, and suspensions through `sock` (§9.5).

**Accounting (X11, [owner decision 10](#od-10)).** tlsedge spends §20.6 leases (meter `tls`) for the listening network (PLAN.md:353); bytes per host exist only in 13.9's 24 h records. An empty balance refuses new connections (Find `quota`) and resets open streams with QUOTA.

### 13.7 The sidecar's TLS front

The `tls` component (§5; files `tls_*.go`) accepts streams for its `tls/` registrations and runs `crypto/tls` over the `SocketConn` (§9). It alone enforces §8's `audience`, which a modified sidecar skips (§21.4).

| Concern | Rule |
|---|---|
| Versions | TLS 1.2 and 1.3; X25519MLKEM768 first |
| Slow visitors | Handshake within 10 s; first HTTP request within 30 s; one visitor /64 or /32 holds at most 1/8 of the endpoint's concurrency |
| Dispatch (D-TLS-13) | By the signed registration's `AppMode` (§9.5), never by ALPN's absence. `http` (default): `h2`, `http/1.1` or no ALPN reach the HTTP front; any other id fails the handshake with `no_application_protocol` (RFC 7301 §3.2). `raw`: a decrypted TCP forward for the declared ids or none, registered only under `public`, where the local service authenticates, or `link`, where the front requires a client certificate whose SPKI SHA-256 equals the publish grant's `link_spki_sha256` (§8.4), over TLS 1.3 so the edge never sees it. `acme-tls/1` reaches only the TLS-ALPN-01 responder. Whatever the ALPN, no application byte reaches the local service before its audience check (§22.8 FS-34) |
| 421 | Host and `:authority` must equal the SNI (RFC 9113 §9.1.1), since browsers coalesce a network's hosts on one wildcard and address set |
| HTTP/3 | None; upstream `Alt-Svc` h3 entries are stripped |
| Visitor address | To the local service only on request (PROXY v2 or `Forwarded`) |
| Audience ([owner decision 42](#od-42)) | `members` (default): §7.8's edge login, checked against the front's config (§7.9; issuer trust: §2.8 EX8). `members-device` adds a §6 `Signed` (purpose `edge-login`) over origin and nonce by a member's consented device (§8.5), via the app or extension (§18). `link`: a signed link, reusable until its grant ends, traded for a cookie (below; `raw`: the pinned client certificate). `public`: explicit, e.g. webhooks. Members on URnetwork may also reach a service over the overlay by §17's own rules, its private name or overlay address (§12.9) with a §17.6 map or route grant to the local port, which adds no listener, audience or authentication path and passes no front, tlsedge or edge login (v1, with M6's `ur tun` on macOS and Windows) |
| Other origins (§12.4) | Session cookies (`__Host-ur-session`, a `link` cookie) count only on `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` or `none`, or top-level GET or HEAD navigations (`Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`); without Fetch Metadata, only with no `Origin` or the host's. Other requests, from the network's other hosts too, arrive anonymous (edge login under `members`). Browsers without Fetch Metadata (before March 2023: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Sec-Fetch-Site) still send them on other origins' GETs (§2.10) |
| Reach receipts ([owner decision 25](#od-25)) | §16.8's `ReachReceipt` per publish grant, visitor, server name and 5 min: the SNI, in `server_name` ([owner decision 465](#od-465)), and a keyed `client_ip` hash (v1), HMAC-SHA256(k, family ‖ the /32 or /64 prefix's address bytes)[:16], k = HKDF-SHA256 of the front's session root, salt the network_id, info `urnetwork-sidecar-v1/tls-front-reach`, stable across windows and restarts, since it names a visitor only inside the author's sealed record ([owner decision 431](#od-431)) |
| Control panels | Refused and recorded for the daemon's API or MCP port and for targets that answer like agent UIs (§16's list) |
| Interstitial | A one-time browser notice on Community `public` endpoints ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.8), never on 13.9's system publish |

**Link tokens ([owner decision 422](#od-422)).** A link is a `TlsLinkToken` (below) in a §6 `Signed` (`SIGNED_TLS_LINK` 0x1503, purpose `tls-link`) by the publishing device's identity key, `expire_time_millis` at most the grant's expires, at `https://<host>/.well-known/ur/link?t=<base64url(Signed)>`. The front verifies the signature against the projection, that the signer is the sidecar the grant names, that `grant_id` is active and that `host` equals the SNI, then sets `__Host-ur-link` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, 12 h, capped by the token's expiry) holding the same token and answers 302 to `/` with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Any listener of the grant honors it with no shared state, and a GrantRevoke or the grant's expiry ends every link of the grant.

**Members-device logins ([owner decision 431](#od-431)).** The statement is a `TlsEdgeLogin` (below; `SIGNED_TLS_EDGE_LOGIN` 0x1502, purpose `edge-login`), `origin` as the front writes it, `https://<sni>` with `:<port>` only where the port is not 443, and `nonce` 32 random bytes the front draws, with no network_id. After the ID token checks out, the callback seals `{nonce, member_id, expiry, return path}` into `__Host-ur-device-pre` (`DeviceLoginLifetime`, 10 min) and answers 302 to `/.well-known/ur/device`, whose GET answers `{origin, nonce}` and whose same-origin POST of field `s`, the base64url `Signed`, completes the login with 303 to where the visitor began; the nonce leaves the pending set only once a statement verifies, so a login completes once. The signer is `AclState.ConsentedFor(signer, member)`, and not read_only, suspended or revoked. `__Host-ur-session` gains the device's sidecar_id: a device session counts on a `members` endpoint, a `members` session never on a `members-device` one, and consent and membership are checked on every request. `Sidecar.SignTlsEdgeLogin(origin, nonce)` answers the encoded `Signed` under the sidecar's consented untagged admission, and §18's `SignEdgeLogin` decodes base64url and passes the asking page's own origin, never one the page names; a remote-mode app reaches it through §5.8's Confirm method `tls.edge_login.sign`, which TLS owns and the daemon answers only for a confirmed call ([owner decision 489](#od-489)). Members reach a service over the overlay by §17's rules alone, as the audience row says.

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/tls.proto: the front's two statements, each the body of a §6 Signed by a device's identity key;
// neither reaches a server, each traveling between the visitor and the front inside TLS
message TlsLinkToken {           // SIGNED_TLS_LINK 0x1503, purpose tls-link, by the publishing device (link tokens)
  bytes grant_id = 1;            // the publish grant's rule_id
  string host = 2;               // the link's host, which the front holds to the SNI
  uint64 expire_time_millis = 3; // at most the grant's expires
  bytes nonce = 4;               // random, so two links of one grant differ
}
message TlsEdgeLogin {           // SIGNED_TLS_EDGE_LOGIN 0x1502, purpose edge-login, by a member's consented device
```
