```proto
  string origin = 1;             // https://<sni>, with :<port> only where the port is not 443, as the front writes it
  bytes nonce = 2;               // 32 random B the front draws, taken once
}
```

### 13.8 Certificates

| Property | Choice |
|---|---|
| Identifier set | `{*.<net>.<root>, <net>.<root>}`: every one-label host, `mx.<net>` included (§15); CT shows only the opaque `<net>` (X5). Network-level devices add each live alias's pair, which §12 answers once a device holds it. A Team scope's devices (member or tag, Q-TLS-3; its mail receivers too) hold only `{*.<scope>.<net>.<root>, <scope>.<net>.<root>}` (owner decisions [40](#od-40), [58](#od-58)); a member scope's set goes only to its member's consented devices (§8.5; [owner decision 126](#od-126)) |
| Key | P-256 per listening device, sealed in its keychain (§5): never exported, in evs or on a server. One certificate per device, so I-15 is one revocation. Rotated every 180 days, on suspicion, or on request |
| Ordering (Q-TLS-2) | `POST /tls/cert-order`: the CSR plus a `Signed` attestation (purpose `tls-key`, `SIGNED_TLS_KEY_ATTESTATION` 0x1501, §6.9) by the device's identity key, of `TlsKeyAttestation {network_id, sidecar_id, spki_sha256, identifier_set_sha256, issue_time_millis}`, `identifier_set_sha256` the SHA-256 over the set's lowercase ASCII names, a wildcard written `*.x`, sorted bytewise, each followed by one 0x00 byte. certs checks the caller's §8 grant (13.15), orders under URnetwork's ACME accounts, deactivated on compromise, and alone writes DNS-01 records (§12). Every account key is in vault before any CA knows it, and certs never writes a key: it reads one YAML file per CA from taskworker's `secret_files` (`ca`, `private_key`, an optional `next_private_key`, `key_create_time`, `eab_key_id`, `eab_mac_key`, `contact`), and once `key_create_time` is a year old, the rollover age a setting, and the file holds a `next_private_key`, it signs RFC 8555 §7.3.5's key change with both keys and orders with the next from then on. Restarted with both keys in the file, it finds the account under whichever key the CA holds, so the operator promotes `next_private_key` to `private_key`, with a new `key_create_time`, at leisure, and the account's URI, which the CAA row pins, never changes; without a next key nothing rolls over, and certs reports the account due but not ready (`rollover_due_cas`; §19.10; [owner decision 432](#od-432)) |
| Challenge | DNS-01 in URnetwork zones, the only wildcard method; never HTTP-01. Orders wait for `GET /dns/internal/ready`, which answers `stale`, `ready` or `canary_failing` (§12.6), and `CertsDns.CanaryClean` reads that answer: `stale` as below, and `canary_failing`, a §12.6 canary that is not clean, keeps an order waiting with no rewrite and no new serial, since CAs validate DNSSEC once the DS exists (CA/B SC-085v2, from 2026-03-15) and LE allows 5 failed authorizations per identifier per hour; a strong-mode probe counts `canary_failing` as ready, and the delegated challenge route passes all three answers on (§12.8) |
| Custom domains (Team, v1; [owner decision 39](#od-39)) | One ACME account per domain, pinned by the customer's CAA `issue "letsencrypt.org; accounturi=<uri>"`. CAA discovery follows a CNAME and stops at the first non-empty RRset (RFC 8659 §3), so the pin excludes URnetwork only in strong mode, where the host has customer A/AAAA or a customer-side ALIAS that synthesizes only A and AAAA (§12.8). certs walks the whole discovery chain and publishes §12.8's canary CAA, with a per-check nonce, at the ALIAS target, a host owner `<host>.<net>.<root>` and never `@`, an apex host's too: at setup, the host pending until walk and probe pass (§12.8), and again at half the lifetime of the host's newest registered chain, before the desktops renew at two thirds. Only a CAA-flattening ALIAS returns the nonce at the host. The ordering desktops repeat the walk, not the canary, before each order: the walk does not rest on certs, but the canary does, so a compelled operator can pass a CAA-flattening ALIAS (§2.8 EX1; 13.16). A strong-mode host whose walk reaches an operator-controlled name (`custom_host_caa_operator_alias`) or returns the nonce is refused at setup and takes §12.8's failure effect at renewal. A host CNAMEd into an operator zone is weak mode, its setup disclosing §2.8 EX1's operator-issuance exception. An admin's desktop makes the account key in a `secret` repo of its own, one per domain (§11.12's owner-bound kind; never the config repo, [owner decision 6](#od-6), nor the admin's vault, since an `EvsShare` opens a whole repo), and shares it by `EvsShare` with the desktops holding the domain's publish grants ([owner decision 126](#od-126)); every MCP evs tool and `ur://evs` resource refuses the kind (§16.6). They order with acmez (TLS-ALPN-01, only while `GET /dns/zone` shows the host ready (13.4), or §12.8's delegated DNS-01), for mobile devices too, registering chains at `POST /tls/cert-register`; one must be online by two thirds of the lifetime. When the key repo's holders shrink, or its owner leaves, a network admin's ordering desktop changes the account key (RFC 8555 §7.3.5) under the account's lock: the new key is committed to a secret repo the remaining holders read before the CA is asked to require it, and the row's key sequence moves last; the pin is kept. Until that request a removed holder still signs as the account (below) |
| CAA | At `<root>`: `issue` and `issuewild` for `letsencrypt.org`, `pki.goog` (GTS, Google Trust Services; https://developers.google.com/public-key-infrastructure/faq/configure-caa) and `sectigo.com` (ZeroSSL; https://help.zerossl.com/hc/en-us/articles/360060119753), each with every URnetwork account URI and `validationmethods=dns-01`. No per-label URnetwork `accounturi` |
| CA, profile | LE `tlsserver`: 45 days, 25 names, 7 h authorization reuse (https://letsencrypt.org/docs/profiles/, 2026-10-04). GTS (100 new orders per hour per project), then ZeroSSL (unlimited 90-day certificates; [R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.4), when LE refuses on a limit, and first for ephemeral sidecars (CI, cloud agents) |
| Renewal | ARI (RFC 9773) via acmez v3 in the engine (Apache-2.0; https://github.com/mholt/acmez), using the stored CSR so devices may be offline; else at two thirds of the lifetime |
| Revocation | A device's certificate on removal (§5); a network's on takedown or deletion; an alias's when §12.5 retires it (I-14); `keyCompromise` on compromise. LE ended OCSP ([R:server-platform](design/design-research/server-platform.md) §5), so the kill switch and 45-day lifetimes carry the load |
| Lost rows | After a restore the certificate manager compares `GET /tls/certs` with its local chain and re-orders a live chain with no row: `POST /tls/cert-order` with a fresh attestation and `replaces` naming the old leaf's ARI id, so the limits skip it; `replaces` rides the request and no row stores it, and `ValidateListen` refuses until the new row exists (§19.10). An old certificate with no row may raise a peer's CT alarm, the safe direction |
| Code | The CAA walk is pure code in the root behind `TlsCaaResolver`; for desktops acmez and its resolver sit in `cli/`, injected as provers are, so neither reaches an sdk leg, and certs keeps acmez on the engine leg; dependencies.yml lists acmez for engine and cli only |

```text
certs' DNS writes: an order's _acme-challenge TXT, or a strong-mode probe's CAA canary (§12.8)
  write    POST /dns/internal/acme-challenge or /dns/internal/caa-canary, committed at serial s; 503
           while a restore runs --> retry with backoff
  wait     GET /dns/internal/ready?serial=s: ready --> the order asks the CA to validate, or the probe
           starts its 10-min window; canary_failing --> an order keeps waiting, with no rewrite and no
           new serial, and a probe takes it as ready; stale (a restore, §12.6; final for s) --> write
           again, the same TXT or the canary under a new nonce, and wait on the new serial
  verdict  a probe's pass counts only if /dns/internal/ready?serial=s still answers ready after its
           last query; stale --> write again and restart the window, since the restored edges may lack
           the canary
```

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/tls.proto: the ordering row's attestation, and certs' hint (13.15)
message TlsKeyAttestation {      // the body of a Signed, SIGNED_TLS_KEY_ATTESTATION 0x1501, purpose tls-key, by the
                                 //   device's identity key: this key, for these names
  bytes network_id = 1;
  bytes sidecar_id = 2;
  bytes spki_sha256 = 3;         // of the DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo
  bytes identifier_set_sha256 = 4;  // the ordering row's hash of the identifier set
  uint64 issue_time_millis = 5;
}
message TlsHint {                // §6 0x1502, topic tls: the client refetches GET /tls/certs, so a hint is never
                                 //   authoritative
  TlsHintKind kind = 1;
  bytes cert_id = 2;             // the 16-byte row id
}
enum TlsHintKind { TLS_HINT_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0; TLS_HINT_ORDER = 1; TLS_HINT_ISSUED = 2; TLS_HINT_REVOKED = 3; }
```

**CT watch (D-TLS-8).** Each listening sidecar queries Cert Spotter (`issuances?domain=<net>.<root>&include_subdomains=true&match_wildcards=true`, https://sslmate.com/help/reference/ct_search_api_v1) and crt.sh for its zone and custom domains every ~6 h (jittered; optional Team key), alarming on a certificate no device attested in `GET /tls/certs` or one an identity pinned under 24 h before issuance attested. Failures show "CT watch degraded"; keyless queries are best effort and never ride a URnetwork proxy (§2.8 ext-1).

**Budget.** LE allows 50 new certificates per registered domain per 7 days across accounts (https://letsencrypt.org/docs/rate-limits/, 2026-08-05): each network's or scope's first certificate spends a unit of `<root>`'s shared budget, a repeated set gets 5 per 7 days (refill 1 per 34 h, no overrides), and ARI renewals skip all limits. certs (`certsservice`, taskworker chains) reimplements the extender pattern, which sidecar cannot import: a `network_tls_cert` queue, a weekly new-set cap below the CA's, counted in Redis `{tcb_}` (13.15), Retry-After holds, the row written before the order; a row keeps its issued chain, which `GET /tls/cert-order/<id>` answers after a restart or to a device that was offline, a requested revocation's reason (`keyCompromise` from `POST /tls/cert-revoke`, `cessationOfOperation` for §21.6's takedowns) until the sweep's revocation reaches the CA, and `state_time`, the time of its latest state; rows stay 30 days, a setting, past expiry, read from `not_after`, or past revocation or failure, read from `state_time`, from which the rebuild of a lost `{tcb_}` key may read an order's admission (cert-1; [owner decision 254](#od-254)); budget entries 7 days. certs backs a URnetwork-zone name whose authorizations keep failing at a CA off, doubling from a start to a day, both settings, so it fails at most about once a day there, which Let's Encrypt's daily refill of the 1,152 consecutive failures after which it pauses a name for an account hands back, and one broken name no longer holds LE's new orders for every other network; the backoff survives a restart in `network_tls_name_backoff` (cert-1), and a success at that CA resets it ([owner decision 430](#od-430)).

**Custom-domain orders (Team, v1; owner decisions [424](#od-424)-[427](#od-427)).** A custom-domain certificate names exactly one custom host and carries one device's key, so a host's devices share the CA's exact-set limit: its first 4 devices are certified at once, one certificate kept back for a compromised key, and each further device 34 h after the one before, both settings, and a device without a certificate for a custom host is not routed that host's visitors. URnetwork's orders for a customer's registered domain are held at the server to a bucket of 25 new certificates, one back each 6 h 43 min (`CertsCustomSettings`' `DomainCap` and `DomainRefill`), half the CA's assumed 50 in 7 days, counted before any request reaches the CA, ARI renewals outside it; a value the customer's admin sets per domain is a later product setting. The CA's numbers (a 45-day lifetime, 7 h authorization reuse, 50 certificates a registered domain in 7 days, 5 an exact set in 7 days with one back each 34 h, 300 new orders an account in 3 h, 5 failed authorizations an hour, an ARI renewal counting against no limit) stay assumptions held as `CertsCustomSettings` defaults, which the owner corrects from the CA's rate-limits and profiles pages; if the ARI exemption fails in any part, a host's ceiling of about 21 certified devices becomes the product's stated limit. Budgets are rows of spends replayed as buckets, never counters: a bucket's replay starts full at its key's latest quiet window, the newest instant t at or before now with no spend of the key in (t − cap × refill, t], where the CA's bucket is full whatever came before, and replays the spends after it, or, where no such instant lies within the retained spends, starts empty at the retention's start; spends are kept 16 d (`SpendRetention`), and a grant reads all of its key's, at most a few dozen rows for the set and domain buckets. So the level never reads above the truth, and it is exact for any number of a host's devices while the host's busy stretch is shorter than the retention less one window, 214 h: after a burst of four each device comes 34 h after the one before, the 10th at 8.5 d and the 11th after a window's pause, and a refused claim's wait, (need − level) × refill, is answered by a grant ([owner decision 571](#od-571)). Every custom certificate is a `network_tls_cert` row first, in states of its own (`custom_queued`, `custom_ordering`, `custom_issued`, `custom_revoking`) that no other certs pass takes: `POST /tls/cert-register` takes a chain only for a queued row whose account lock the caller holds, so a desktop's own CSR is queued by `POST /tls/cert-order` like a phone's and claimed like any row. The lock is one an account, since the CA may hand two newOrders for one host the same order and the key change needs the same exclusion. An ordering desktop touches the CA for an account only while it holds that lock, `network_tls_account`'s sequence, holder and lease on the database's clock and no other, one order in flight an account, and every server write it makes names the sequence its claim returned, a write under an older one refused. It sends one newOrder a grant and finalizes only an order whose URL the server recorded under that sequence; a takeover resumes the recorded order and starts another only when the CA itself calls it invalid or gone, never on a timeout or a 5xx, so a row yields at most one certificate, and a holder that must give a live order up kills it by deactivating its authorizations, since an order left recorded keeps its row first in line. The server grants each newOrder in the claim's transaction, after checking and spending the account's budgets (the exact-set, registered-domain, new-order and failed-authorization limits, each a setting, one certificate of the exact set kept back), and records a CA's 429 as a hold on the account row that every desktop honors (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.6 to 17.2.8; `details/CertOrder.tla`, §22.8). An ordering desktop answers TLS-ALPN-01 for a custom host only where it holds an approved port 443 publish grant on the host's owner, 13.9's gate taking no exception; without one it uses the customer's DNS-01 CNAME for that host or leaves the row to a desktop that holds the grant, and a row no online desktop can serve waits and raises `tls_custom_queue_stalled` after 24 h, a setting. Before asking the CA to validate, a desktop probes its own challenge through public DNS and the edge, twice, and a failed probe asks the CA nothing. A 429 on an ordinary order holds ordinary orders and lets ARI renewals through, and one on an ARI renewal holds everything. The plan orders revocations, the row in flight, replacements of revoked certificates, renewals by expiry, then first certificates, the least-served host first. A device presents the newest installed certificate whose row is `custom_issued`, falling back to its predecessor, and for a custom name with none it fails the handshake, never presenting another certificate. A renewal is a successor row the server queues with the stored CSR, so a phone need not wake for it, at a uniform point of the certificate's ARI window, or at two thirds of its life where the CA gave none, and its order carries `replaces`; ordering desktops keep the windows fresh from the CA's renewalInfo. A revocation is marked by the server, which from that commit certifies the name for that listener no longer, and sent by an ordering desktop under the account key, spending no budget and waiting on no hold (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.11, 17.2.12). A row that ends while an order is recorded for it goes to `custom_revoking`, and the account orders nothing until that order is killed at the CA or its certificate revoked. The account key is held by an admin's devices and the ordering desktops it is shared with, each keeping the key file's last good bytes in its local secret store; any holder orders, but only a network admin's ordering desktop changes the key or writes the account row. The change is due the moment the key repo's holders shrink or its owner leaves, and the first admin desktop online makes it within one poll, under the account's lock, committing the new key where the remaining holders read it before the CA is asked to require it, the account row's key sequence moving last, so at every instant some holder reads whichever key the CA accepts and an order in flight resumes under the new key (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.13); a desktop that sees it due and may not make it raises `tls_account_rollover_due`, and fewer than two admins' desktops seen in 7 days is a warning. Until the CA takes the change, a removed holder still signs as the account (13.16).

### 13.9 Endpoints, caps, metering, abuse

**Endpoint (PLAN.md:358).** An endpoint is an active publish grant per (host, port); custom-domain aliases count, listeners and certificates do not, and §20.7 counts `tls_endpoints` at grant activation. Each `tls/` registration passes `ValidateListen` (§9.4's owner hook):

```text
ValidateListen(tls/<port>/<host>) refuses
  host     unmappable (13.5); mta-sts, except the system publish below; a member-scope host from a
           device its member did not consent to (§8.5); a host ScreenName refuses, or sends to review
           with no reviewer's allow on its case (§21.6), screened at each registration through a short
           per-process cache of the verdict, so a refusal needs no change to the signed GrantActivate
  port     other than 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671
  client   URnetwork-run (D-TLS-1)
  network  no network_verified (§21.7)
  grant    no active approved publish grant for (host, port) (§8.10, I-8); an AppMode other than its
           app_mode; raw under an audience other than public or link; a raw link grant without
           link_spki_sha256 (13.7)
  time box a grant with no expires, or more remaining life than its cap, in a network at Community
           (7 d) or in probation or restricted state (24 h); Pro and Team may hold standing names, and
           a network whose tier fell keeps a standing grant until §20.7's 14-day clock ends
  cert     no unexpired certificate row, except an acme-tls/1-only registration before its first order;
           a custom host or alias is listed for a listener only while its sidecar holds an unexpired
           certificate row for it: a certified or ACME name the rows do not bear out is dropped, and
           the registration stands
  facts    an unknown fact, of the ones above that TlsListenFactsSource brings (§8.9)
system publish tls/443/mta-sts (§15.5): AppMode http, audience public, no tls/ grant of its own
  only     a receiver (an approved smtp/25/mx listen grant, §15.4) holding an unexpired certificate row
           for the network's pair, in a network with network_verified (§21.7) and a mail_network row
           (§15.15)
  grant    that listen grant stands in for the tls/ listen and publish grants as §9.10's gates say
  serving  the receiver's mail component answers; no interstitial, tls_endpoints unit or expiry of its own
```

Caps protect the devices, which do the handshakes: endpoint caps are tier quotas, visitor caps `sidecar_abuse:` limits equal on every tier (§20.4, D-QUOTA-7); §21 tightens either per network.

| Cap | Community / Pro / Team | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent per endpoint | 256 / 2,048 / 8,192 | ⌈cap ÷ blocks⌉, at least 1, per process, no shared counter, blocks being tlsedge.yml's count of lb hosts running it (13.5) |
| New per endpoint | 50 / 200 / 1,000 per s | token bucket per process |
| Bandwidth per endpoint | 20 / 200 / 1,000 Mbit/s | token bucket in the splice, ⌈cap ÷ blocks⌉ |
| Per visitor /64 (IPv6) or /32 (IPv4), per process | 64 concurrent (`tls_visitor_concurrent`), 20 per s (`tls_visitor_new_per_s`); `tls_visitor_aggregate_multiple` (4) times those per /48 or /24 | HMAC under a per-process key rotated daily |

**Visitor hashes.** Cap keys stay per process (§2.8 tls-2). tls-3's visitor hash and Find's affinity key use a fleet-shared daily key: 32 random bytes in Redis `{vhk}tls:<yyyymmdd>` (UTC), created by the first process with `SET NX EX 90000` and read by every process each minute and at the date change. `k_record` and `k_affinity` derive from it by HKDF-SHA256 with infos `urnetwork-sidecar-v1/tls-visitor-record` and `urnetwork-sidecar-v1/tls-visitor-affinity`, and the hash is HMAC-SHA256(k, family byte ‖ the /24 or /48 prefix)[:16], so one visitor links across processes for a day. A process that cannot reach Redis uses a random key of its own for that day, the closed direction. mxedge's daily key has the same shape under `{vhk}mx:<yyyymmdd>` (§15.4), so tls-3's rows and `{mxc_}` keys never join.
| Per process | 50,000 connections | tlsedge.yml; §19 derives §9's platform Find limit from it |

**Abuse hooks** ([owner decision 41](#od-41); §21 sets policy), none inspecting content:
- **Kill switch.** `POST /tls/suspend` writes `network_tls_suspension` (§19.7), then one MULTI sets `{tes_<network_id>}` (`<host or *>` → reason, until) and INCRs its trigger (D-PROTO-12). tlsedge, on the shared key-event subscriber (§4.5), refuses new connections and resets open ones within 5 s, reloading from Postgres every 60 s; Find refuses too, and §8 suspension and revocation follow (§21.6). Row and keys go only when the case lifts it or `until` passes; a reload drops a kill only once neither its row nor its key holds it, so a Postgres restore lifts none, and §19.10's abuse step re-applies the kills and lifts mailed after the dump (§21.10).
- **Time box, verification.** Publishes follow §8's `expires`: 24 h by default, at most 7 days on Community, 24 h on probation (§21.7); standing names only in Pro and Team documents (§8.5). They need §21.7's `network_verified`, so anonymous-only networks publish nothing (owner decisions [41](#od-41), [96](#od-96)).
- **Published names, CT.** Active publish grants (host, port, label, expiry) form the list §21.6 checks hourly against Web Risk: taskworker reads ACL's `AclState.PublishedNames(now)`, every rule allowing publish grouped by host and port, `PublishGrant`'s agreement rule deciding audience and expiry and disagreeing rules listed as the closed audience, through a gate cache of its own, installed as `model.SetTlsPublishedNamesSource`'s source, a name's label and aliases coming from `network_edge_label` and the verified domains, so the check reports what the gates enforce; a process with no source answers unavailable, which the hourly check takes as a failed pass ([owner decision 423](#od-423)); reviewers open reported URLs as visitors, a case keeping a URL's path and query until its first review ends (§21.8; [owner decision 207](#od-207)), joining connections by `connection_id` for 24 h; §21's worker screens CT under `<root>` (§21.8), and D-TLS-8 covers mis-issuance.

Server-visible fields are §2.8's tls-1 to tls-4, cert-1, cert-2, api-11 and api-7's publish rules (audience, `app_mode`, a raw link's `link_spki_sha256`); tls-3's records leave tlsedge in 10 s batches.

### 13.10 `ur bridge public-tls`

`ur bridge public-tls <host>:[<local ip>:]<local port>` (cli/UI.md:47; local ip 127.0.0.1 by default):

1. Check `<host>` against §9.4's grammar, §7.7's client names and 13.9's system host.
2. Pass §5's `Authorize` (I-8). Without an active approved grant, file §8's request `{dst: [dns:<host>, sock:tls/<port>/<host>], allow: [publish, listen], audience, app_mode, link_spki_sha256, expires}` (§8.5 example 5; the pin only for a raw `link`), print `ur approve <id>` and its approval channels (§16.6; in a tainted run, harness evidence only where the rule names it, [owner decision 142](#od-142)), and wait.
3. Get the device certificate if missing, probe the target (13.7), then `Listen("tls/<port>/<host>", alpn, app mode)`.
4. Print the URL (raw `link`: the client-certificate file), expiry, audience and "passthrough: key on this device".

Flags: `--port` (443, or a listed port), `--expires`, `--audience`, `--alpn`, `--tcp` (`AppMode` raw, with `--audience public`, or `link`, which writes a client key and certificate whose `link_spki_sha256` the request carries), `--proxy-protocol`. The MCP tool `tls_publish` passes the same gate (§16.5).

### 13.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edge termination, in a TEE or not, and edge interstitials (PLAN.md:84) | WAF, edge auth, warnings | Plaintext and keys on servers | Ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| One network key shared through evs | One certificate per network | Keys leave devices; reissue per removal | Rejected (D-TLS-6; [owner decision 40](#od-40)) |
| Per-host certificates, or TLS-ALPN-01 in our zones | Isolation | Every host in CT and the budget | Custom domains only |
| Unknown SNI to tlsedge, platform names listed | No lb reload per custom host | Every scan and foreign name loads tlsedge; an unlisted platform name breaks | Rejected (D-TLS-12) |

### 13.12 Decisions proposed

**D-TLS-1 (proposed).** Passthrough only: tlsedge holds no user key or user-name certificate and mounts no vault, and no URnetwork-run client (platform, proxy, hosted DeviceLocal) listens on `tls/`. *Why:* the owner directive; a URnetwork `*.<root>` key would cover every network.

**D-TLS-2 (proposed).** Ingress is 13.4's gated, probed SNI split on the shared lb addresses; port 80 only redirects; active custom hosts route to tlsedge through the split's generated map (D-TLS-12). *Why:* [owner decision 34](#od-34) leaves no other addresses; the gate and probes catch split faults.

**D-TLS-3 (proposed).** tlsedge is 13.5's layer-4 router. *Why:* it sees only SNI, ALPN and bytes (R-TLS-4), and retries stay invisible.

**D-TLS-4 (proposed).** tlsedge runs K platform clients per process on Service contracts (13.6). *Why:* clients do not grow with networks, and the edge holds no Network privilege.

**D-TLS-5 (proposed).** The front enforces 13.7; dispatch keys on the registration's application mode, never on ALPN's absence (D-TLS-13). *Why:* under passthrough only the sidecar can; coalescing and the shared site (§12.4) make the 421 and origin rules mandatory.

**D-TLS-6 (proposed).** Every device holds its own P-256 key and a certificate for its network's or scope's set, a member scope's only on that member's consented devices (13.8). *Why:* no shared key, minimal CT exposure, and member isolation one admin cannot break (owner decisions [40](#od-40), [126](#od-126)).

**D-TLS-7 (proposed).** certs proxies CSRs, queues orders, puts ephemeral sidecars on GTS or ZeroSSL first and alone writes DNS-01 in URnetwork zones (13.8); overrides are requested at least 6 weeks ahead. *Why:* a shared budget needs one queue, CI runs would exhaust a set's 5 per 7 days, and mobile builds need no ACME client.

**D-TLS-8 (proposed).** Sidecars watch CT through two sources and check attestations against pinned identity keys (13.8). *Why:* URnetwork can always pass DNS-01 in its zones (§2.8 EX1), so detection is the remaining control.

**D-TLS-9 (proposed).** Endpoint counting, caps, the kill switch, the time box and 24 h records follow 13.9. *Why:* PLAN.md:358 needs a unit, and these controls work without inspection.

**D-TLS-10 (proposed).** TCP 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671 (owner decisions [68](#od-68), [121](#od-121)), with no h3 or published ECH configs; tlsedge routes on SNI and ignores GREASE ECH. *Why:* QUIC SNI cannot be preread while connect owns UDP 443 ([R:server-platform](design/design-research/server-platform.md) §2.4), and ECH routing needs split mode, which Go's server lacks ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §2.7).

**D-TLS-11 (proposed).** A Team custom domain's one customer ACME account is shared by its ordering desktops, which order for every device (13.8); its CAA pin excludes URnetwork only in strong mode, and a strong-mode host is refused at setup, and takes §12.8's failure effect at renewal, when its CAA walk passes through an operator-controlled name (certs and the desktops check) or it returns certs' canary. *Why:* the customer's pin excludes URnetwork ([owner decision 39](#od-39)) only while CAA discovery stays under customer authority (RFC 8659 §3), and one account needs no CAA edit per device.

**D-TLS-12 (proposed).** Active custom hosts route to tlsedge through the split's generated map, reloaded at most once per 15 min (13.4); unknown SNI keeps the platform default. Each map has a version; each lb interface reports the version it loaded, which the dns edges route-probe as a visitor would; a host is ready for TLS-ALPN-01 only once every interface that §12.6's probe passes is current for its version; and an interface more than 20 min behind leaves user-name answers and pages. *Why:* a downstream map cannot correct an upstream dispatch, and each reload holds old workers for up to an hour; a wait is not readiness, since an lb that missed or failed a reload, or restarted with an old map, kept sending a host to the platform branch while probes of `<root>` names passed (meta review K02).

**D-TLS-13 (proposed).** Dispatch binds the signed registration's application mode (13.7): `http` takes `h2`, `http/1.1` and no ALPN through the HTTP front, and `raw` registers only under `public` or a certificate-pinned `link`; ALPN omission never selects a less-restrictive path. *Why:* ALPN negotiates a protocol, not an audience (RFC 7301).

### 13.13 Open questions

**Q-TLS-1.** [X1] Where does TLS end, and how does TCP 443 split? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 34](#od-34)):** in the listening sidecar (§0), via (a), 13.4's `ssl_preread` split on the shared lb addresses. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-2.** [X1] Who orders certificates for device-held keys? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 39](#od-39)):** (c), certs' CSR proxy in URnetwork zones; on Team custom domains, the customer's own CAA-pinned account (D-TLS-11), which excludes URnetwork only in strong mode (13.8). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-3.** [X1] How do a team's devices share the wildcard? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 40](#od-40)):** (a), per-device keys and certificates, plus scope sublabels `*.<scope>.<net>.<root>` past the 1-per-34 h refill or for isolation, with hosts `<label>.<scope>` (13.8); no shared key. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-4.** [X1] Is abuse handling without inspection enough? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 41](#od-41)):** (c), 13.9's hooks plus a verified account before any Community publish. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-5.** Cross-cutting (X11): a tlsedge client per served network (PLAN.md:82), or platform clients? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by owner decisions [11](#od-11) and [59](#od-59)):** platform clients on Service contracts (13.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-6 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): `tls/` and `smtp/` hosts are `@` or one LDH label, as a wildcard covers one, plus Team scope hosts (Q-TLS-3); applied in 13.10 and §9.4.

**Q-TLS-7.** Cross-cutting (§8, §7.8): what does "authenticated by default" (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:698) mean? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 42](#od-42)):** `members` by default, else `members-device`, `link` or explicit `public`, plus members' overlay access (13.7); `raw` endpoints take only `public` or `link` (D-TLS-13). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TLS-8.** Cross-cutting (cli/UI.md:121): may names publish ports other than 443? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 68](#od-68)):** (b), a short fixed list of permanent ports on the shared addresses. **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 121](#od-121)):** 8443 (a second HTTPS service per host), 8883 (MQTT over TLS) and 5671 (AMQP over TLS), permanent lb ports to tlsedge (§19 W7); mail ports, plaintext-before-TLS protocols and control-plane defaults (2376, 6443) stay excluded. *Residual:* none.

### 13.14 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:84** ("so that the tls edge can do its own certificate termination"): superseded by owner directive 2026-11-03. Certificates stay automatic but go to the listening sidecar (D-TLS-1, D-TLS-6).
- **PLAN.md:82** ("opens a client on a network"), read as one client per served network: D-TLS-4 departs, as owner decisions [11](#od-11) and [59](#od-59) approve (Q-TLS-5).
- **Outside PLAN.md:** cli/UI.md:105's `<sub>.<you>` depth (Q-TLS-6, Q-TLS-3) and :121's any-port `hostname:port`, narrowed to a fixed list (Q-TLS-8).

### 13.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** tlsedge; the split, its custom-host map with versions, interface reports and readiness, gate, probe and route probes (§12, §19); certs (13.8, D-TLS-7); `TlsEdgeOpen`, `TlsHint`; the `tls` component, its `AppMode` dispatch and publish receipts (13.7, §16); `tls/` hooks with the MTA-STS system publish (13.9; §9, §15); mail-host and off-loopback listener certificates (§15; D-TRUST-8, [owner decision 130](#od-130)); the kill switch, published-names list and CT hook (§21); lease spends (§20).
- **Consumes:** §4 C9, `ServiceHost`, acmez v3; §5 keychain, `Signed`, `Authorize`; §6 streams, Service, topic `tls`; §7 membership, edge login, client names; §8 grants (`audience`, `app_mode`, `link_spki_sha256`), approvals, consent, `EvsShare`; §9 Find, hooks, the signed `AppMode`; §11 owner-bound repos; §12 label and custom-host maps (with CAA mode), records, probe, pending custom hosts, DNS-01 and canary-CAA writes, ready and its `stale` answer across a restore, `canary.<root>`; §15 `mail_network`, receivers' `smtp/25/mx` grants; §16 `ReachReceipt`, approval channels; §19 W1 (drained rollout, map and port-80 reloads), W7, monitor, §19.8's pager, §19.10's abuse step; §20 leases, caps; §21 `network_abuse_state`, `network_verified`, `ScreenName`, holds.
- **Subprotocol messages:** `TlsEdgeOpen` (0x1501; StreamOpen metadata, edge→listener); `TlsHint` (0x1502; push `tls`, whose version is the writer's clock in ms, per client, with no durable sequence; §6.8): `{TlsHintKind kind = 1; bytes cert_id = 2}`, kinds 1 order, 2 issued, 3 revoked, `cert_id` the 16-byte row id; the client refetches `GET /tls/certs`, so a hint is never authoritative.
- **API routes** (api; bringyour.yml, route_authz.go):
  - `POST /tls/cert-order` (service token, aud `certs`; caller holds a §8 `tls/` or `smtp/` grant, which api's subject asks the gate in one call, `AclGateView.HoldsPublicGrant(networkId, subject, now)`, true when a rule in force gives the subject publish with listen on any `tls/` name or listen on `smtp/25/mx`; until that call lands, api grants a caller the view allows listen on `smtp/25/mx`, or one `PublishGrant` grants, in http or raw mode, a host and port `AclState.PublishedNames` lists for the network, each `*` asked as the letter `x` and a dotted Team scope host skipped until M6, every answer the gate's own, the closed direction ([owner decision 429](#od-429)); CSR, attestation); `GET /tls/cert-order/<id>` (state, retry_after, chain, ARI window).
  - `POST /tls/cert-register` (service token, aud `certs`, as every custom-domain route here; a custom domain's chains, v1, each only for a queued row whose account lock the caller holds, under that claim's sequence, its leaf carrying the row's key and exactly its one name); `GET /tls/certs` (Client; certificates, attestations and queued custom-domain CSRs; `?work=1`, which an ordering desktop asks with its `certs` service token, only accounts and waiting rows, so a desktop's poll carries no chains).
  - `POST /tls/custom-claim` (service token, aud `certs`; an ordering desktop, a sidecar holding an active approved publish grant on a `tls/` name of the owner of an active custom host of the domain, takes or renews the account's lock for one row, purpose `order` or `revoke`, or, a network admin's desktop only, for a key change, `rollover`; the answer carries the claim's sequence, its lease, the row, the recorded order's URL to resume or the grant of one newOrder, its budgets checked and spent in that transaction, and the predecessor's leaf where the order names it in `replaces`; refused 403 `orderer`, 404 `no_account`, 409 `key_seq`, `locked`, `in_flight` or `state`, and 429 `budget` or `hold` with `retry_after_ms`, never waiting on the lock); `POST /tls/custom-progress` (service token, aud `certs`; what the holder learned at the CA, applied only while the lock's sequence is its claim's, else 409 `claim`: `order_recorded`, `order_invalid`, `authz_failed`, `rate_limited`, `not_exempt`, `release`, `failed` and `revoked`, and with no claim `ari`, the certificates' renewal windows, and `rollover_due`); `POST /tls/custom-account` (service token, aud `certs`; a network admin's desktop creates the account row or begins, ends, aborts or repairs a key change: `create`, `roll_begin`, `roll_end`, `roll_abort`, `repair`). Durations on these routes are milliseconds from the answer, never a time of day, so no desktop clock is compared with the server's (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 17, 17.2.5; v1).
  - Bodies are JSON from 13.8 and §2.8's cert-1: a stored field cert-1 lacks needs its row first (I-18), and a request-only value, such as `replaces`, is stored nowhere.
  - `POST /tls/custom-challenge` (service token, aud `certs`; the caller holds an active §8 publish grant on a host mapped under the domain; `{domain, value}`, the value the 43-character base64url DNS-01 digest) and `GET /tls/custom-challenge/<id>` (§12.8's ready answers, `stale` and `canary_failing` included): a custom domain's delegated DNS-01 at its `<acme_token>.acme.<root>`, which certs alone writes (§12.8 step 3; v1).
  - `POST /tls/cert-revoke` (OwnClient: a client token revokes its own client's certificates; Network admin for any of its network's, meaning a personal network's owner's token, a team member's token whose role holds `devices`, a role that cannot be read holding nothing, or an API key whose scopes reach `devices`, since revoking a device's certificate is part of removing the device; an OAuth identity or admin token revokes nothing there; [owner decision 429](#od-429)); `POST /tls/suspend` (§21), a model call inside api and taskworker, its route built only once a caller outside them exists ([owner decision 417](#od-417)).
- **Tables** (migrations ≥926): `network_tls_cert` (certs; orders and certificates, with §2.8 cert-1's fields, among them the issued chain, a requested revocation's reason and `state_time timestamp NOT NULL`, set with every state change, in MG5's CREATE; [owner decision 254](#od-254)); `network_tls_suspension(network_id, host, reason, until)`; `tls_connection_record` (hourly partitions, dropped at 24 h once a §21.9 hold has copied out its network's rows, [owner decision 133](#od-133)); `tls_connection_day` (13 months). Redis: `{tes_<network_id>}` and trigger `{tes_<network_id>}n`; certs' budget `{tcb_<ca>_<registered_domain>}`, a sorted set of the last 7 days' new-set orders, checked against the cap and added to in one script (server/ip_ratelimit.go:105's sliding window), expiring 7 days after its newest order and rebuilt from `network_tls_cert` on loss.
- **Services and config:** `server/cli/tlsedge` blocks behind the split and the port list (TCP 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671; nothing on 80); the lb's generated `/run/warp-lb/tls-custom-hosts.map` and port-80 names, and `lbmap`, which generates and loads them beside each interface's nginx (13.4); certs as taskworker chains, routes in api, each install left out unless sidecar.yml's `certs` switch is on (§19.11), so certs fails closed through M5's Gn-out and the first real CA order is the owner's act: api's with the engine, the Postgres store, the `certs` authenticator and a reader of a caller's identifier set, identity key and grant from its network's verified projection through `AclGateView`, once ACL's gate cache runs in api, and taskworker's with the engine, its DNS client, its ACME client on the account files and its hint writer, reading `certs.yml`, the account files its `account_file` names and `internal-certs.yml` from `secret_files` ([owner decision 429](#od-429)); `config/<env>/tlsedge.yml` (13.5; caps in pro.yml); certs' account and EAB keys in vault (13.8).
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §11.12's `secret` kind holds a custom domain's account key, and §16.6 refuses every MCP evs tool and `ur://evs` resource on it, which §22.7's actions suite tests (13.8); gates read §8.5's consent from the projection, as §15.5 assumes; §21.9's holds name tls-3 rows; §22.7's scope-certificate check covers unconsented devices; §22.5's §13 row tests 13.9's refusals and system publish; §9.10's gates let a receiver's `smtp/25/mx` listen grant stand in for `tls/443/mta-sts`'s grants at registration, Find and admission (13.9); §12.8 keeps a strong-mode custom host pending and unmapped until certs' walk and probe pass, refuses it at setup when its walk reaches an operator name or its answers return certs' canary, and defines that failure's effect at renewal; the canary admits at most the customer's account, carries its nonce in a non-critical property (RFC 8659 §4.1), sits beside a copy of `*`'s records (RFC 4592 §2.2) at a host owner, an apex host's included, never a network's, alias's or scope's `@`, whose CAA would govern that zone's device set (RFC 8659 §3), is checked after the 60 s negative TTL and takes 13.8's `stale` handling, the re-check before a pass included; FS-32 runs the CAA-flattening and the address-only ALIAS again at an apex host whose pin sits at `<domain>`; §19 W1's `lbmap` renders the custom-host map and the port-80 names from one version's rows, before nginx serves at start and otherwise at most once per 15 min, and reports the version each interface loaded (13.4); §12.6's edges route-probe each interface's reported version and drop map-stale interfaces; §19.10's abuse step re-applies, from §21.10's off-site record, the kills and lifts mailed after a restored dump; §19.7 and §2.8 cert-1 name `{tcb_}`.

### 13.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| The shared budget runs out before the override, a team adds devices faster than 1 per 34 h, or CI runs drain a set's 5 per 7 days | High | High | X4, early override, queue, fallback CAs (ephemeral sidecars first), Team scopes (Q-TLS-3) |
| Phishing on a user name flags `<root>` or gets a shared lb address listed, also stopping smtpedge's mail from it ([owner decision 124](#od-124)) | Medium | Critical | X4, kill switch, verified publishers, Web Risk (§21.6), M5's registrar and registry pager (owner decisions [134](#od-134), [143](#od-143)) |
| The split slows connect's H1 transport or fails fleet-wide | Low | High | 13.4's gate, drained rollout, probes paging at any hour ([owner decision 143](#od-143)), rollback |
| Custom-host reloads pile up old lb workers, each holding its connections up to 60 min and then cutting them (warp/warpctl/config.go:1181) | Low | Medium | Team-only provisioning changes, coalesced to at most one reload per 15 min (13.4) |
| An lb interface misses or fails a custom-host reload, or restarts with an old map, so a host's SNI reaches the platform branch there while `<root>` probes pass | Low | Medium | 13.4's versions and route probes: a host is ready, and TLS-ALPN-01 starts, only once every interface is current for its version; a map-stale interface leaves user-name answers and pages; a static-address host stays pending, naming it (§12.8) |
| A flood at user names saturates the shared interfaces, platform included ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §5) | Medium | High | 13.9's caps, kill switch, router ACLs, upstream help (§19) |
| A dns-edge signing fault after the DS, or a site or Hurricane Electric outage that also stops the lbs ([R:ext-edge](design/design-research/ext-edge.md) §5; accepted, [owner decision 123](#od-123)), fails DNS-01 and CAA | Medium | High | Orders pause on §12.6's canary, which pages at any hour ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); renewal at day 30 of 45 leaves 15 days |
| Compelled mis-issuance enables MITM of a name, of a weak-mode custom host, or of a strong-mode one behind a CAA-flattening ALIAS, which only URnetwork's own canary checks (13.8) | Low | High | Two-source CT watch (D-TLS-8), the remaining control for those hosts; customer CAA in strong mode (13.8) |
| Same-user agents read the device key and impersonate names | High | High | Accepted ([owner decision 47](#od-47)); removal revokes (I-15) |
| A custom domain's certificates lapse with no ordering desktop online | Medium | Medium | Two ordering desktops; warnings from half-life name the host and device; fewer than two ordering desktops seen in 7 days is itself a warning, as fewer than two admins' desktops is ([owner decision 425](#od-425)) |
| A removed holder of a custom domain's account key signs as the account, revoking its certificates or deactivating or taking the account, until the CA takes the key change (accepted, [owner decision 425](#od-425)) | Low | High | The change is due at once and made by the first admin desktop online within one poll; `tls_account_rollover_due` where a desktop may not make it; only the CA's key change ends the exposure |
| The CA's limits differ from `CertsCustomSettings`' assumed defaults; if an ARI renewal counts against a limit, a host keeps at most about 21 certified devices ([owner decision 424](#od-424)) | Medium | Medium | The owner corrects the defaults from the CA's pages; a wrong number costs waits and refused requests, never a certificate too many, since a 429 becomes a hold |
| Raw clients lack TLS 1.3 or client certificates for a `link` endpoint | Medium | Low | `public` with the service's own authentication; members' overlay access (§17) |

### 13.17 Phasing

**v0** (§23 M5): the split after its gate and drained rollout, its custom-host map empty; tlsedge and Service contracts; certs with LE, GTS, ZeroSSL, ARI and per-device keys; the front with `members` login and `AppMode` dispatch (FS-34); desktop `ur bridge public-tls`; the CT watch; ports 443, 8443, 8883 and 5671; app listeners with §18 and the MTA-STS system publish with §15 (both M8). It waits on §9's `tls/` and Find, §6 streams, C9, §12's dns edge, §19's W1, §7.8's edge login, §21's kill-switch policy and the LE override's lead time.

**v1** (§23 M6): Team custom domains (with §12's custom-host-add, the split's custom-host map with its versions, interface reports and readiness, and strong-mode CAA checks; FS-32, FS-35, FS-122), Team scopes, affinity, `members-device`, overlay access for members by §17's maps and grants alone, with M6's `ur tun` on macOS and Windows (§17), and publish reach receipts (§16).

**Later:** [ECH split mode](DESIGN-DEFER.md#tls-ech-split-mode), [h3 on edge UDP 443](DESIGN-DEFER.md#tls-h3-edge), [the PSL listing](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-psl-listing) (§12), [anycast](DESIGN-DEFER.md#tls-anycast). DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#tls-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).

## 14. The SMTP edge: outbound mail and abuse attribution

### 14.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns outbound mail: the path through `smtpedge`, the preamble and its proofs (X7), TLS policy, sending identity, quotas, abuse attribution, halts and report intake. §15 owns the local mail server, inbound mail and burners; §12 publishes DNS; §20 sets prices and numbers; §21 owns abuse policy.

X7 is decided (CONVENTIONS §0; owner decisions [35](#od-35), [36](#od-36), [38](#od-38), [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125)): TLS runs end to end from the sidecar to the destination MX, so `smtpedge` sees ciphertext plus proven header values.

### 14.2 Requirements

| id | requirement | source |
|---|---|---|
| R-SMTP-1 | "N outgoing connects per day for free", more for Pro; N small | PLAN.md:89 |
| R-SMTP-2 | Send emails/day 5 / 200 / 20000 | PLAN.md:356 |
| R-SMTP-3 | A PROXY-like plaintext header (routing path, Message-ID), ZK-verified against the first N buffered bytes | PLAN.md:90, :94 |
| R-SMTP-4 | Abuse reports against the Message-ID halt the network's sending for a day | PLAN.md:91 |
| R-SMTP-5 | The header holds every field reports need to join back | PLAN.md:97 |
| R-SMTP-6 | The local mail server sends through the edge | PLAN.md:104 |
| R-SMTP-7 | Mail infrastructure sees only encrypted bytes and small header values, except D-SMTP-19's report and role-mail intake (§2.8 mx-4; D-TRUST-4) | owner directive 2026-11-03 |
| R-SMTP-8 | Usage counts toward the transfer balance | PLAN.md:353; [owner decision 10](#od-10) |
| R-SMTP-9 | TCP/25 never crosses providers | connect/ip_smtp_policy.go:16-19 |
| R-SMTP-10 | URnetwork holds no DKIM key; logs hold no recipients or client IPs | §2.6, §2.8 EX2, I-13 |
| R-SMTP-11 | Gmail, Yahoo and Outlook.com sender and bulk rules | [R:ext-email-zk](design/design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §2.8 |
| R-SMTP-12 | Team mail on custom domains | PLAN.md:364 |
| R-SMTP-13 | No outbound mail before sound, fast, interop-tested BDAT and DATA proofs | owner decisions [35](#od-35), [99](#od-99), [125](#od-125) |
| R-SMTP-14 | Send from the shared lb addresses, with bringyour.com PTRs and HELO = PTR; no IP pools | [owner decision 124](#od-124) |

### 14.3 What exists today

- **connect.** TCP/25 stays local in both clients, "so an SMTP relay attempt can never reach a provider" (connect/ip.go:10694-10699; connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:6705-6713), and providers check again (connect/ip.go:7869-7872). `DohCache.Forward` is exported (connect/net_http_doh.go:1111).
- **warp.** The lb carries ingress only, PROXY v1 on TCP streams (warp/warpctl/config.go:2477-2513), with no public TCP 25; hosts egress from their own addresses (warp/services/services.go:216-220) and can source-route by `--fwmark` (warp/warpctl/config.go:2686-2689).
- **Addresses (2026-11-03).** The 12 lb addresses are HE's (vault/main/services.yml:82-106, :338-461; §19.5), and none has a PTR. HE delegates classless reverse zones (https://faq.he.net/index.php/Reverse_DNS); its colocation port-25 policy is unknown.
- **Go; missing.** Go's `KeyLogWriter` exports TLS 1.2's master secret (Go 1.27.3 src/crypto/tls/handshake_client.go:785) but never TLS 1.3's HS (common.go:1605-1609; handshake_client_tls13.go:491). Missing: port-25 egress, PTRs, `smtpedge`, a prover, DKIM publishing, report ingestion, mail quotas.

### 14.4 Connection model

```text
MUA / agent --(submission or mail_send, §15)--> local mail server --> SmtpSender (sidecar)
  (a phone writes its mailbox outbox instead; a prover host sends it, D-SMTP-18)
 1 §9 Find ur/smtpedge (resolves in urnetwork-edge) --> ticket
 2 §6 stream (Required, Service mode) --> smtpedge (platform client, sending IP)
     SmtpPreamble -->        gate, halt, quota, §8 send, From domain (14.5); MX (validating);
                               TCP/25 from the sending IP, banner, EHLO <PTR name>, STARTTLS, 220
     <-- SmtpPreambleResult  send_id, X-UR-Ref, Feedback-ID, MX host, DNSSEC chain, EHLO keywords
 3 sidecar applies §15.10's header rules (BURNER), adds headers, DKIM-signs,
   sends ClientHello (SNI = MX host)
 4 sidecar <====== TLS 1.2/1.3, spliced by the edge ======> destination MX
     TL4, or below the domain's pin on the host: no data; retry on the schedule below, then DSN
     SmtpHandshake (1.3), then SmtpProof parts (RPC): the key part, one an envelope group, one a header
       or DATA body record --> each verified before the records it releases (14.5)
     inside: EHLO, MAIL FROM:<..@b.<net>.<root>>, RCPT x R, BDAT n LAST or DATA .. CRLF.CRLF, QUIT
 5 SmtpOutcome --> (self-report, untrusted; a NO_REPLY envelope to the ticket's listener, 14.14)
```

- **Transport.** The sidecar's Required client Finds `ur/smtpedge` in `urnetwork-edge` (§9.4); the Find-recorded pair authorizes the Service-mode stream (§6.10.1; [owner decision 11](#od-11)).
- **MX.** The edge resolves MX with a DNSSEC-validating resolver, honors null MX (RFC 7505), and dials only public unicast IPv4 addresses ([owner decision 34](#od-34)). With no MX RRset and no null MX, RFC 5321 §5.1's fallback to the domain's address applies: `mx_host` is the domain, DANE uses that host, and NO_MX answers only when no address exists either. The sidecar never names an IP, so the edge is no port-25 proxy and the proofs keep ORIGO's no-MITM assumption. An MX on mxedge's router interfaces (§19.5) is spliced to mxedge over the host LAN, with a PROXY header naming the dialed address (D-SMTP-13).
- **Pre-TLS.** The edge runs the banner, `EHLO <PTR name>` and `STARTTLS` itself, in MX preference order, and answers NO_TLS or TRY_LATER before any sidecar byte if no MX offers STARTTLS. The sidecar's first bytes must be a ClientHello with SNI = MX host and no early data; inside TLS it re-sends EHLO, and only that reply's keywords count (RFC 3207 §4.2; Z8, Z9).
- **Shape.** One transaction to one recipient domain per connection, in BDAT mode if the MX offers CHUNKING after TLS, else DATA (14.5). The sidecar sends the envelope's commands in groups, MAIL and 12 RCPT, then 13 RCPT a group, under AES-128-GCM (18, then 19, under ChaCha20), settings with these defaults, and waits for each group's replies before the next, so each group's replies are proven with the group that follows (14.5); within a group it pipelines (RFC 2920 §3.1) only if the post-TLS EHLO reply offers PIPELINING, and otherwise each command, QUIT included, waits for the previous reply, still under the part that covers it. A send costs one unit and is one transaction at the MX whatever its recipients, each further 12 to 19 adding one proof part; `smtp_recipients_per_message` caps the connection, and the sender never splits a domain's recipients over connections ([owner decision 434](#od-434)).
- **Retries.** A send that fails retries first at 30 min, doubling to 4 h, then every 4 h, with a DSN at 5 days; HALTED, QUOTA and TRY_LATER honor `retry_after_ms` and still end at 5 days. A message's retries that reach MAIL spend at most `SmtpSenderSettings.RetryUnitsPerMessagePerDay` connection units a UTC day, 2 by default, and past that it waits for the next UTC day. Idle limits are 10 min after a client record (RFC 5321 §4.5.3.2.6) and 5 min after a server record (§4.5.3.2.7), 30 min in all, 2 h in DATA mode; a 421 banner backs the destination off.

**TLS policy (D-SMTP-2; [owner decision 38](#od-38)).** STARTTLS is mandatory: stripping it fails the send. The sidecar, as TLS client, authenticates the server and records each message's level (I-11).

| Level | Authenticated by |
|---|---|
| TL1 DANE | TLSA under DNSSEC (RFC 7672): the edge returns the MX and TLSA chain (`dnssec_chain`), which the sidecar validates to the root |
| TL2 MTA-STS | The HTTPS policy (RFC 8461), which the sidecar fetches and caches, plus PKIX for a listed MX |
| TL3 independent MX | The sidecar's own DoH MX lookup agrees with the edge, and PKIX is valid for that host |
| TL4 unauthenticated | Nothing |

TL1-TL3 exclude a malicious or compelled edge (D-TRUST-1), TL4 only a passive one, so the sidecar refuses TL4 with a DSN giving the reason unless the user allowed the recipient domain; such mail is labeled "readable by an active URnetwork edge" (§2.8 EX4). The allowance is an outward action of its own (I-8), `SidecarActionKind` 18, `mail_tls_unauthenticated`, whose action's `host` (5) holds the recipient domain, lowercase with no trailing dot, and whose `expires_millis` (8) ends an allowance that ends; approvers render it from daemon-built fields as `Send mail to <domain> through a mail server that cannot be authenticated: an active URnetwork edge could read it`, and no ordinary `mail_send` approval counts as TL4 consent ([owner decision 436](#od-436)). It is kept per recipient domain: a desktop keeps a granted allowance in its `SidecarStore`, and a phone's message carries the approval's id with its approved domains on its signed `o/` entry (`tl4_domains`, §15.7), which a prover host honors only if that entry's signature verifies and its signer is a consented device (§8.5) of the mailbox's owner, for that message only, never copying them to its own store. Each MX host's best level for each recipient domain is pinned for 90 days, and nothing goes below a pin. TL2 and TL1 are properties of the recipient domain, its own MTA-STS policy and its MX RRset validating under DNSSEC before the host's TLSA counts, so a shared MX host that reached TL2 or TL1 for one domain refuses no other domain that publishes less, while a send to a domain through a host below the level it reached there is refused as a downgrade, a malicious edge stripping TLSA for a domain that reached TL1 included; a domain never sent to carries no pin, even where its host holds one from another domain, and a TL4 allowance lifts no pin ([owner decision 438](#od-438)). Until §13 issues a receiver's certificate (§15.5), mail to it authenticates only at TL1.

### 14.5 The preamble and what makes it trustworthy (X7)

PLAN's byte header becomes protobuf frames ahead of the raw TLS bytes (D-SMTP-3), and nothing ships before the proofs below make every value proven ([owner decision 35](#od-35)).

```proto
message SmtpPreamble {           // 0x1601, sidecar -> edge
  uint32 version = 1;
  string recipient_domain = 2;    // enforced: the edge resolves and dials it; every RCPT is at it (Z4)
  uint32 recipient_count = 3;     // proven (Z4); capped per message and per day (14.7)
  string message_id = 4;          // proven (Z5)
  string header_from_domain = 5;  // proven (Z5); in the network's zone (§15.9) or a verified Team domain (§7.6)
  string dkim_selector = 6;       // proven with d= (Z5)
  uint64 message_byte_count = 7;  // proven: BDAT's n, or DATA's octets before the end mark (Z4, Z6); declared
                                  //   for the expected mode (below)
  bytes retry_of_send_id = 8;
  uint32 flags = 9;               // 1 BULK, 2 REQUIRETLS, 4 BURNER
  bytes proof_key_set = 10;       // SHA-256 of the keyset.json every part of this connection is proven under
                                  //   (14.9)
}
message SmtpPreambleResult {     // 0x1602, edge -> sidecar
  uint32 code = 1;  // §6.11: 1 OK, 2 HALTED, 3 QUOTA, 4 DENIED, 5 NO_MX, 6 NO_TLS, 7 TRY_LATER,
                    //   8 KEYS (the edge does not accept proof_key_set: no MX is dialed, nothing is debited);
                    //   0 UNSPECIFIED, a protocol error
  uint32 retry_after_ms = 2;
  bytes send_id = 3;
  string x_ur_ref = 4;            // issued; proven present (Z5)
  string feedback_id = 5;         // issued; proven present (Z5)
  string helo_name = 6;           // the sending address's PTR name (14.6)
  string mx_host = 7;
  bytes dnssec_chain = 8;         // every cut's DS and DNSKEY, then the MX and TLSA RRsets, with RRSIGs, in
                                  //   RFC 9102's order (TL1)
  repeated string ehlo_keywords = 9;  // pre-TLS hints only; Z8 proves the post-TLS reply
  string envelope_domain = 10;    // OK only: the envelope the edge derived from the ticket's network, which Z4
                                  //   holds MAIL FROM to; the sidecar resets before any record where its own
                                  //   differs and never sends at this one (14.6; owner decision 655)
}
message SmtpProof {              // 0x1605, RPC sidecar -> edge (M9)
  bytes send_id = 1;
  uint32 index = 2;               // the part's ordinal, from 1; part 1 is the key part
  uint32 mode = 3;                // 0 in part 1; 1 BDAT or 2 DATA from part 2 on, which fixes it (Z9)
  uint64 first_record = 4;        // client application records covered, by TLS sequence number;
  uint64 last_record = 5;         //   a part that opens none has last_record = first_record - 1
  bytes proof = 6;                // 164 octets
  bool last = 7;                  // covers octet n, the end mark (DATA) and QUIT
  uint64 server_record_count = 8; // server records after Finished that this and earlier parts cover (0 in
                                  //   part 1); this part covers those past the previous part's count (Z7)
  repeated bytes records = 9;     // ciphertext of each client record the part opens, in sequence order
                                  //   (BDAT's last part: its header record from first_record, then QUIT at
                                  //   last_record)
  bytes key_commitment = 10;      // part 1 only: C, 64 octets (owner decision 433)
  uint32 reply_count = 11;        // the replies the server records it covers hold (Z8)
  uint32 header_record_count = 12;  // on the part that opens the header block's first record, and no other:
                                    //   how many client records hold the header block
  bytes carry = 13;               // on a part that opens a header or body record: the scan state after it,
                                  //   64 octets
}
message SmtpProofResult {        // 0x1606, edge -> sidecar
  uint32 code = 1;                // §6.11: 1 OK; 2 INVALID, and the edge cuts the connection (14.7);
                                  //   0 UNSPECIFIED, a protocol error
}
message SmtpOutcome {            // 0x1603, a NO_REPLY envelope to the ticket's listener (14.14), self-reported:
                                 //   it only tightens (14.8) and never feeds attribution
  bytes send_id = 1;              // the edge takes it from the connection's dialer once, from the connection's start
                                  //   until 15 min after its end (owner decision 640)
  uint32 tls_level = 2;           // 1-4 for TL1-TL4, 0 if none was reached
  uint32 mode = 3;                // as SmtpProof.mode, 0 if the send ended before the mode was known
  repeated uint32 reply_codes = 4;  // the MX's reply codes, as the sidecar read them inside TLS
  uint32 dsn_count = 5;           // DSNs made or received since the last accepted outcome, so a late bounce
  uint32 hard_bounce_count = 6;   //   rides the next send
  bool downgrade_refused = 7;     // the send refused an MX below its pin, or TL4 without an allowance (14.4)
}
message SmtpStatus {             // 0x1604, in PushHint.hint on topic mail (14.14)
  uint32 kind = 1;                // SmtpStatusKind
  uint32 retry_after_ms = 2;      // when the queue may try again; GET /smtp/status gives a halt's scope
}
message SmtpHandshake {          // 0x1607, RPC sidecar -> edge, TLS 1.3 only (the disclosed SHTS, below)
  bytes send_id = 1;
  bytes shts = 2;                 // the server handshake traffic secret, which the edge forgets after E2
}
message SmtpHandshakeResult {    // 0x1608, edge -> sidecar
  uint32 code = 1;                // SmtpHandshakeCode
}
// §6.11's edge codes, each 0 a protocol error that the receiver answers by resetting the stream or dropping the hint
enum SmtpPreambleCode {          // SmtpPreambleResult.code
  SMTP_PREAMBLE_CODE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SMTP_PREAMBLE_OK = 1; SMTP_PREAMBLE_HALTED = 2; SMTP_PREAMBLE_QUOTA = 3;
  SMTP_PREAMBLE_DENIED = 4; SMTP_PREAMBLE_NO_MX = 5; SMTP_PREAMBLE_NO_TLS = 6; SMTP_PREAMBLE_TRY_LATER = 7;
  SMTP_PREAMBLE_KEYS = 8;
}
enum SmtpProofCode { SMTP_PROOF_CODE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SMTP_PROOF_OK = 1; SMTP_PROOF_INVALID = 2; }
enum SmtpStatusKind {
  SMTP_STATUS_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SMTP_STATUS_HALTED = 1; SMTP_STATUS_QUOTA = 2; SMTP_STATUS_CLEAR = 3;
}
enum SmtpHandshakeCode { SMTP_HANDSHAKE_CODE_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SMTP_HANDSHAKE_OK = 1; SMTP_HANDSHAKE_INVALID = 2; }
```

Recipient addresses, subjects, bodies and the MX's replies inside TLS stay private witnesses; §2.8 smtp-1 to smtp-6 list what the edge sees.

**Frames.** Only `SmtpPreamble` and `SmtpPreambleResult` travel as frames ahead of the raw TLS: u32be body length ‖ u16be `MessageType` ‖ body, the body at most 65,536 B. Raw TLS follows an OK result, any other result ends the stream after its frame, and a bad length or type resets it with PROTOCOL. A `dnssec_chain` that would pass the bound is sent empty, so TL1 is not available on that connection; the sidecar validates the chain to the keys of IANA's current root-anchors file, which it embeds, updated by release. `SmtpProof` and `SmtpHandshake` are RPCs to the edge, and `SmtpOutcome` a NO_REPLY envelope to the ticket's listener (14.14).

**The disclosed SHTS.** In TLS 1.3 the sidecar sends `SmtpHandshake` (`SMTP_HANDSHAKE` 0x1607, above) as soon as the handshake ends, and the edge answers `SmtpHandshakeResult` (0x1608): 1 OK, 2 INVALID, on which the edge ends the connection, 0 a protocol error. TLS 1.2 sends none. The edge forgets the SHTS after E2 (D-SMTP-10).

**Declared bytes.** The preamble declares `message_byte_count` for the expected mode, the pin's (14.4), else BDAT's unstuffed form, and every issued header has a fixed length (14.6), so each length is known first. If the mode the post-TLS EHLO selects cannot meet the declared count, the sidecar ends the connection before MAIL and reconnects once with the other count and `retry_of_send_id` set, costing a burst token and no unit (14.7); a second mismatch is `deferred` on 14.4's retry schedule, so an MX that offers CHUNKING always gets BDAT.

**Authorization.** A Find for `ur/smtpedge` needs no §8 grant (§9.4); preambles failing the gate, quota or halts (14.7, 14.8), `mail_send` or the From-domain check (§8.10, `ScreenName` §21.6) get DENIED, HALTED or QUOTA before any byte reaches the MX. `SmtpGate` answers from memory only, fed by §8.9's internal gate surface; a miss answers TRY_LATER and starts a refresh. The sidecar `mail_send` is judged for is the one the stream's admitted `ur/` ticket names in `dialer_sidecar_id`, which sockets filled at Find from the `ur_sidecar_id` of the caller's authenticated service token and signed (§9.6's `ur/` tickets; [owner decision 588](#od-588)), so the edge needs no client-to-sidecar lookup or cache, and a ticket naming none answers TRY_LATER, failing closed ([owner decision 560](#od-560)). A preamble naming a key set the edge does not hold gets KEYS, before any MX is dialed or anything debited.

**Soundness.** PLAN's "first N bytes" proof is unsound: the client authors the ciphertext, and AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 do not commit to keys, so the bytes can open to benign headers under one key and the real transaction under another (https://eprint.iacr.org/2024/733 Theorem 4; https://eprint.iacr.org/2019/016). Nor is a malicious sidecar's control flow evidence of the MX's state: STARTTLS voids the pre-TLS keywords (RFC 3207 §4.2), and an MX without CHUNKING, or one that refused the envelope, parses an alleged message body as commands (RFC 3030 §2). So the proofs bind the keys to the observed handshake, cover the whole client flow and prove the MX replies that interpret it; E1-E3 run at the edge, Z1-Z9 in the circuit.

| # | Check |
|---|---|
| E1 | No PSK or resumption, early data or renegotiation (1.2: each client record it forwards is application_data by its clear type); SHA-256 suites (1.3: AES-128-GCM, CHACHA20-POLY1305; 1.2: ECDHE AES-128-GCM) |
| E2 | The edge dialed the MX it resolved and checks the server's signature: 1.3's CertificateVerify and Finished with the disclosed SHTS, 1.2's ServerKeyExchange in clear |
| E3 | Client records go in sequence order, each once a verified part covers it: an opened one only if it equals the ciphertext the part proved, BDAT's unopened body only up to octet n by the edge's count; no message record (BDAT's command and chunk, DATA's octets) goes before verified parts cover every server record relayed before it and every reply the envelope's commands are owed, proving each MX reply (Z8); PLAN's "first N bytes buffer" |
| Z1 | Under the edge's handshake inputs (below), in the connection's first part: 1.3: a private HS yields the disclosed SHTS, then MS and both directions' application keys and IVs (ORIGO); 1.2: a private master secret yields the key block, under which the relayed server Finished record decrypts to the verify_data that secret gives the relayed handshake (D-SMTP-21); and the public commitment C commits to those keys and IVs. In every later part: the keys and IVs it uses open C |
| Z2 | Each proven plaintext, client or server, is its ciphertext XOR the keystream at its sequence number (1.2: explicit nonce) |
| Z3 | Each client record the circuit opens is unpadded application_data, with no KeyUpdate, so lengths fix offsets; BDAT's unopened body rests on the relation's count bound |
| Z4 | `EHLO <helo_name>`, `MAIL FROM:<x@b.<net>.<root>>`, exactly R × `RCPT TO` at the recipient domain, then `BDAT n LAST` or `DATA`: one transaction |
| Z5 | Over the header block's records in order, the single fields and the fixed signature's line in the first, the header block holds, once each, a From in the declared domain, the declared Message-ID, the issued X-UR-Ref and Feedback-ID, and a DKIM-Signature with the declared d= and s= covering them; no bare CR or LF; List-Unsubscribe-Post if BULK |
| Z6 | BDAT: the chunk's n octets end at a record boundary, counted exactly over the opened head and by E3 over the unopened body, and the last client record, opened, is exactly `QUIT` CRLF. DATA: octets 1 to n, over the header and body records in order, end in CRLF, hold no bare CR or LF and no CRLF.CRLF, and exactly `.` CRLF `QUIT` CRLF follow |
| Z7 | The private server application key decrypts every server record the part covers (NewSessionTicket skipped; a KeyUpdate fails it); no key leaves the circuit |
| Z8 | Those replies are a valid SMTP exchange for the proven flow, part by part: the server records a part covers hold exactly its `reply_count` whole replies; the post-TLS EHLO reply advertises CHUNKING before a proven BDAT, MAIL and each RCPT get 2xx, DATA gets 354 before any message octet, and no message record is covered before all of them are proven |
| Z9 | `mode` is fixed from part 2 and matches Z8's post-TLS capabilities: BDAT to an MX whose EHLO reply lacks CHUNKING is unsatisfiable |

```text
Z1's handshake inputs (public; the edge computes each over the handshake it relayed, and uses the one prover
value, the disclosed SHTS, only once E2 has checked it)
1.3  H_shts = SHA-256(SHTS)
     H_sh   = Transcript-Hash(ClientHello .. ServerHello)       RFC 8446 §4.4.1, a HelloRetryRequest included
     H_sf   = Transcript-Hash(ClientHello .. server Finished)   the server's flight as E2 opened it
     Z1: SHA-256(HKDF-Expand-Label(HS, "s hs traffic", H_sh, 32)) = H_shts; MS from HS (RFC 8446 §7.1);
         each direction's key and IV (§7.3) from HKDF-Expand-Label(MS, "c ap traffic" | "s ap traffic", H_sf, 32)
1.2  r_c, r_s = the ClientHello and ServerHello randoms
     S_ckx  = the SHA-256 state (chaining value, unhashed tail, length) after ClientHello .. ClientKeyExchange,
              every handshake message before the client's Finished; the sidecar's client offers no SessionTicket,
              so the server's Finished is the next message after the client's; any other shape fails Z1
     SF     = the server Finished record as relayed: explicit nonce and ciphertext
     Z1: key_block = PRF(master_secret, "key expansion", r_s ‖ r_c), both directions' keys and IVs;
         cf = 14 00 00 0c ‖ PRF(master_secret, "client finished", SHA-256 finished from S_ckx)[0:12];
         SF opened under key_block's server key and IV = 14 00 00 0c ‖
           PRF(master_secret, "server finished", SHA-256 resumed from S_ckx over cf)[0:12]   RFC 5246 §6.3, §7.4.9
```

**Relation (D-SMTP-22; [owner decision 433](#od-433)).** Public inputs are values the edge holds anyway: Z1's handshake inputs (above), the client ciphertexts a part opens (`records`, which the stream must repeat, E3), the server records it covers, the preamble and issued values, the part's ranges and counts, and the commitments the sidecar publishes: C, in the connection's first part, and a carry on each part that opens a header or DATA body record. Both directions' keys, IVs and plaintext are private witnesses. The first part, the key part, proves Z1 once and that C commits to both directions' keys and IVs; every later part proves that the keys it uses open C, and holds no key schedule. C and each carry are Pedersen commitments, over the curve embedded in BN254's scalar field, under a fresh uniform 251-bit blind drawn from the source of the TLS keys: each is a uniformly random group element whatever it commits to, so no public value depends on a key or on an octet of plaintext, even to an edge with unbounded computation or the setup's trapdoor, and binding, on discrete logs on that curve (about 2^125), ties every part to the keys the first fixed. A part covers the client records `first_record` to `last_record`, or none, and the server records from the previous part's `server_record_count` up to its own, which hold exactly its `reply_count` replies, so prover and edge check the same records, and it can verify before its records are sent, so the sidecar paces them (14.4). The envelope takes one part a group of commands, the header block one part a record, and DATA's body one part a record; the state a scan carries from one record to the next is the carry, which the edge hands from each part to the next. An MX awaiting a command sends no reply, so a server record relayed past a part's count, such as a late NewSessionTicket, only holds message records (E3) until the next part, which may open no client record, covers it; once the MX closes, a 421 included, outstanding parts are moot. DATA opens every octet. BDAT's parts open the records through the header block and the final `QUIT`; the body between streams unopened once the last part verifies, and the edge counts each of its records as its length minus 17 octets, the most a 1.3 record carries (RFC 8446 §5.2; a 1.2 record, typed in clear by E1, carries exactly its length minus 24). So the MX never counts more chunk octets than the edge: it reaches octet n and the proven `QUIT` only if every body record is unpadded application data, and otherwise ends the chunk inside the `QUIT` record, or never. No client record reaches the MX after it (14.7), and 6 octets hold no transaction, so a malformed body alters only its own unproven content or fails the send. A part that cannot be proven, as after a refused MAIL or RCPT, ends the connection before any message octet, and the sidecar retries or returns a DSN per recipient; a part resent under its `send_id` and `index`, byte for byte, is idempotent, and a verified part is never replaced.

```text
sidecar                                   smtpedge                              MX
 |--SmtpPreamble, naming its key set-------->|--banner, EHLO, STARTTLS----------->|
 |==ClientHello .. Finished (spliced; 1.3 discloses SHTS, E2)====================>|
 |--part 1 (key): Z1 once, C, the EHLO record-->| verify: C is the connection's from here
 |==EHLO=========================================================================>|
 |<=EHLO reply====================================================================|
 |--part 2 (env): opens C; that reply: 1 reply, all 250, CHUNKING; MAIL, RCPT x g1-->| verify
 |==MAIL, RCPT x g1==============================================================>|
 |<=their replies=================================================================|
 |--part 3.. (env): opens C; 1 + g1 replies, each 2xx; RCPT x g2-->|   one part a group, while recipients remain
 |--part m (msg): opens C; the last group's replies; BDAT n LAST, header record 1; carry S1-->| verify
 |==BDAT n LAST, header record 1=================================================>|
 |--part m+1.. (hdr): opens C and S1; header record 2; carry S2-->|   one part a record
 |--the last part: the header block's last record and QUIT; last-->| verify
 |==that record, the body unopened to octet n, QUIT==============================>|
 DATA: the last env part opens DATA; msg proves the 354 and opens header record 1; a body part opens each
 body record, opening and publishing a carry; the last also opens ". CRLF" and "QUIT CRLF". Without
 PIPELINING each command, QUIT included, goes only after the previous reply.
```

**DATA mode (D-SMTP-20; [owner decision 125](#od-125)).** An MX without CHUNKING after TLS gets DATA, which ends at the first CRLF.CRLF, or on some receivers at bare-LF forms (SMTP smuggling, CVE-2023-51764), so Z6 checks every message octet, at minutes per 100 KiB on desktops. Each part opens one record and carries the scan state to the next in a hiding commitment (D-SMTP-22); a part is one fixed circuit, and a host whose part takes over 2 min, against the MX's 5-minute timeout (RFC 5321 §4.5.3.2.7), sends no DATA. A 2 h connection therefore proves at most `smtp_data_proof_bytes`, measured on each host and recorded (about 3 MiB on the M1 reference and 360 to 460 KiB on an m5.large, by projection until D-SMTP-16's runs): a larger message to an MX without CHUNKING gets a DSN before MAIL, as does a body still unproven at 2 h, while other recipient domains and every CHUNKING MX are unaffected.

**Send capability and results ([owner decision 125](#od-125)).** The cap stays; what a user needs is which recipient it stops, how large the message is and whether waiting helps, at composition when known and before MAIL otherwise.
- **Check.** `SmtpSender.Check(message)` reports, per recipient domain:
  - the mode: `bdat` or `data` from the post-TLS EHLO reply of this device's last session with that domain's MX, kept 90 days as its TLS pin is (14.4), or from a send outcome (`or/`, §15.7); else `unknown`;
  - the message's encoded bytes, headers, DKIM signatures and dot-stuffing included;
  - the cap: the `smtp_data_proof_bytes` of the host that will prove it, or for a phone's outbox the largest its member's prover hosts record (`p/`, §15.7);
  - the expected delay: BDAT's parts at that host's measured time a part (six parts for D-SMTP-16's send, ≤ 30 s on an M1), or a DATA send's parts at that host's measured rate (up to 2 h at the cap), plus, through an outbox, the wait for a prover host;
  - a prediction: `ok`, `too_large` (mode `data` and bytes over the cap) or `unknown` (mode `unknown` and bytes over the cap).
- **Outcomes.** Each send records, per recipient domain, one of: `sent`; `queued` (in the outbox for a prover host); `deferred` (TRY_LATER, QUOTA or HALTED, with `retry_after_ms`); `too_large` (bytes and cap); `refused` (the MX's reply code); `tls_refused` (TL4, below a pin, or a REQUIRETLS message without TL1 or TL2 and the post-TLS REQUIRETLS keyword, TL3 not qualifying, its DSN `5.7.30` for the missing keyword and `5.7.10` for missing TLS authentication); or `failed`.
