**Readers** are the owner's consented devices (§8.5), as MLS leaves, their `EvsShare` subjects (agents by ReaderWrap, [owner decision 114](#od-114)) and [owner decision 63](#od-63)'s visible audit reader ([owner decision 126](#od-126); D-ACL-13). A device an admin admitted under the owner stays parked until a consented device signs `OwnerConfirm`; it, the tagged sidecars the owner sponsors and `tag:mail` mail indexers only deposit. **Admins.** ERASE and CLOSURE pushes take `repo:<id>:admin` (§11.8, §11.12), so each consented device that is not read-only files `RepoAdmin{add}` for itself once seated (§8.8), and any of them erases, shreds trash or deletes a vault entry, whether or not the mailbox's creating device survives; `EvsShare` subjects, the audit reader and deposit-only sidecars never erase.

A group repo is a `general` repo whose `RepoCreate` marks it an inbox: `group`, or `admin` for the network's admin address, which only a config writer creates, once a network. Rotators give a marked repo a drop key and writers use §11.6's per-message slot rule for it (§8.5, §8.8, D-KEYS-17), and `ur id group-create` files, beside the marker, `RepoGrant{role: deposit}` to `tag:mail` in a team network. **Group mail** is deposited once, into the group repo, and members' devices add `r/` references to their own mailboxes, so storage counts once (§20); a group has at most 100 members (§20.4). Only the group repo's admins (§8.8: its creating device and those a repo admin or config writer adds) erase its messages and shred its trash; members' devices then drop their `r/` references.

**Deposit** (§11.12): a body under a random key, HPKE-wrapped (X-Wing) in a slot to the drop key of the repo's newest signed GenRotate, which the receiver accepts only under D-KEYS-17's depositor rule. The body is the message's bytes, then `MailDeposit{version, ingress, evidence, mail_from, require_tls, recipients, tls_version, tls_suite, receiver_sidecar_id}`, then u32be of its length (15.5's session): a trailer under the deposit's object key, whose slot CONSUME and ERASE destroy, so it needs no K_dep (§11.6), STREAM's final flag authenticating the tail, and a reader takes it by a ranged read before the body. `ingress` and `evidence` are 15.5's, `mail_from` MAIL's reverse path as received (bytes, empty for `<>`), `require_tls` its REQUIRETLS flag, `recipients` this repo's alone, at most 100, `tls_version` and `tls_suite` the session's IANA numbers, and `receiver_sidecar_id` the depositing receiver, which ingest holds to the deposit push's signer; a same-network deposit sets `version`, `mail_from` and `recipients` only, its signature being the deposit's EvsPush signer (15.8). evs sees the repo id, size, time, depositor and slot.

**Ingest.** On a §11 hint, any reader takes the deposits in order; checks that `MailAuthEvidence` names the message's hash and the signing receiver; scores and labels the message from it (15.5), never from later DNS, showing any re-check apart (D-MAIL-14); adds `Authentication-Results` and `Received`; writes `m/`, `i/` and, where the search index is on, the message's index delta in one push on the repo's file-mode ref, which lands by path ([owner decision 141](#od-141)); records §16.8's reach receipt ([owner decision 25](#od-25)); and consumes the deposit ref. The deposit id is the message id, so racing readers converge; slot ids are 16 random bytes drawn per statement, never derived from a deposit, message or entry id (§11.6): a deposit rebuilt for a newer drop key after 412 GATE_CLOSED, or an ingest re-sealed under a newer generation, draws new ones, and only a retry of the same statement keeps them. An admin's erasure, of one message or a batch such as the trash shred, first commits, in a format-2 mailbox, a CUT on the mailbox's ref that lists them in its erasure set, so no index push built before it publishes them and searches mask them at once (§11.12, §11.14), and an ERASE of their bodies' keys and any unconsumed deposit's slot, which re-key nothing and so go at once even at the storage limit; it then re-checkpoints each `i/` segment holding them once, without them, into one record under a fresh key, and, where the search index is on, rewrites in place each index file holding their postings (§11.14), by a CLOSURE push bound to its ERASE, one pair per part (Limits), which evs takes even at the storage limit (§11.13), since §11.12's closure bound admits a merged record that padding rounds up a step past the replaced records' sum; each such ERASE destroys the old chains' keys and the rewritten index files' old slot keys (§11.12), and a device whose `i/` write meets such a CLOSURE's 409 re-applies its change without the erased messages; on its hint, every reader and mirror deletes its cached keys, slot copies and every decrypted copy (local store, index and search caches) and refuses those keys, and a daemon serving IMAP expunges the messages; copies an IMAP client or agent already took stay beyond recall (§2.18). Attachments stay inside messages, as content-addressed extraction would leak equality.

**Limits** (`config/all/pro.yml`, §20.4): `mail_inbound_message_bytes` 25 MiB on Community, else 50 MiB; 100 recipients; all mail counts as evs storage (PLAN.md:355); erasing it frees no stored bytes in v0, and from v1 frees at once only its versionless content, while the search index's rewritten files keep their lengths (§11.14, §20.7), so at the storage limit RCPT gets `452 4.2.2`. Admins shred trash after 30 days, a per-entry erasure that preservation holds never block ([owner decision 133](#od-133)) and the storage limit only paces: there, and while spent, §20.7 counts each erasing sidecar's closure uploads against its own 60 a minute and its closure bytes against its own `evs_closure_bytes_per_day` a UTC day, which §21 may tighten but never below `evs_closure_bytes_floor` (§11.12, §20.4; [owner decision 146](#od-146)), and paces the network's closure uploads in equal turns, k erasers asking at once each getting one every k/4 s, at most 4 a second a network, a refused eraser counting in k until its turn, so no other admin's closures spend an eraser's rate, turns or allowance; ERASE and CLOSURE pushes past the network's 60 a minute queue as P1 and commit. An erasure therefore runs in parts, each one CLOSURE and its ERASE for the messages of whole `i/` segments, sized to what remains of the allowance, since a CLOSURE adopts only uploads under 24 h old (§11.13); a part refused 429 past its eraser's rate, turn or allowance resumes at its `retry_after_ms`. An allowance re-keys 60 full segments a day by default and 3 at the floor, each an `i/` segment or a search-index file of at most 1,088 KiB; a message's erasure re-keys its `i/` segment and every index file version holding any of its documents, which are one per 1 MiB chunk of its text and may have copies (§11.14's bound), so its wait follows from those bytes: at the floor its last part commits after at most the ⌈B / 3,008 KiB⌉-th 00:00 UTC after its allowance first refuses it, B its closure bytes left then, plus a turn per upload of that day, a one-document message with no copy after the next 00:00 UTC within two turns, and a backlog of n full re-keys after the ⌈n/3⌉-th (§11.13, §20.7); the eraser's device shows each erasure's progress and estimate (§5.4's erasure event); the waiting messages' bodies are gone from the first ERASE, and their IndexEntries and postings stay openable to key holders, masked in search, until their part's ERASE commits.

**Reads.** Apps head-read `i/` and messages through §11 (PLAN.md:63), learning of mail by hints or §18 pushes. **Search** (v1; D-MAIL-16), from M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), runs on the search index under §18.4's policy: the two buckets answer at once, and older mail follows from all, kept in the background on desktops and indexers, and on phones fetched at "search more" or on Wi-Fi while charging. Phones confirm a hit against `i/`'s subject, address and snippet, which they mirror, and show the rest as possible matches confirmed when opened; desktops verify against the mail they mirror. Once a search indexer is designated (§7.9), a phone's "search more" asks it end to end by default instead (§11.14, §18.4; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)), its hits verified where it mirrors the mail: the member's mailbox goes only to their consented search indexers ([owner decision 126](#od-126)), a group inbox to their own search indexer that reads it, else to one network-scope search indexer that reads it, after the app names that device's member or sponsor. With none designated (the default, [owner decision 177](#od-177)) or none answering, the phone fetches all and shows possible matches as above. A member's search covers their mailbox and the group repos they read, and leaves out spam and trash unless asked: §5.4's `SearchRequest` takes them only with `IncludeSpam` and `IncludeTrash`, which the MCP `search` tool's `include: [spam, trash]` and `ur search --include spam,trash` set and IMAP SEARCH sets from the selected folder, so a search inside Trash or Spam finds its messages, and the engine passes them to the device-side join ([owner decision 444](#od-444)). The daemon serves §16's `mail_list`, `mail_read` and `ur://mail/{alias}`, and IMAP (emersion/go-imap v2, whose tags are all pre-releases: v2.0.0-beta.8 or a newer v2 tag, its `dependencies.yml` row saying so; M8) under D-MAIL-11 and 15.10's credential; IMAP SEARCH (RFC 9051 §6.4.4) runs on the same engine, verified. Outside mail is `untrusted` and taints the run (I-9), whose outward actions, sends included, then each need a fresh second-device or presence-key decision; harness evidence counts only where the matching `requests` rule names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)).

### 15.8 Addresses, groups, vault entries

| Address | Form | Mailbox |
|---|---|---|
| Admin (`@` in the CLI) | `admin@<net>.<root>`, aliased by `postmaster@` and `abuse@` (RFC 5321 §4.5.1, RFC 2142) | the owner's; on Team, an `autogroup:admin` group repo |
| Id | `ur id create <name>` gives `<name>@<net>.<root>` | the creator's |
| Group | `ur id group-create [--private]`, `group-add` (the only way in, §16.11) | the group repo |
| Agent | `<agent>@<net>.<root>`, at registration ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) §2.2 N2) | the sponsor's |
| Scoped (Team) | `<name>@<scope>.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 58](#od-58)) | the scope member's |
| Bounce | `bounces+<token>@b.<net>.<root>` (§14.6) | the sender's |
| Burner | `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` (15.9) | the owner's |

- **Local parts** match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}`; `admin`, `postmaster`, `abuse`, `mailer-daemon`, `bounces` and `r-*` are reserved. No device can terminate cli/UI.md:21's shared `you@ur.network`, so cli/UI.md:68's form holds.
- **Address directory.** A receiver honors a creator-signed `mailcfg` record only if §8's policy grants the creator `mail:<alias>#listen` (D-ACL-12). `creator` is the sidecar_id whose signed push wrote the record's first version, which a reader checks against that push's signer, and the grant is evaluated at the reader's current state for the creator's subject, an untagged sidecar's member or a tagged one's tags, read from its `SidecarRow`, which outlives the device: removing a device leaves its addresses standing, and revoking the grant ends them. A later version of `addr/` or `burner/` (burn, pause, resume, members) counts only if a consented device (§8.5) of the member who owns the record's mailbox signed it, or for a group a repo admin of the group repo; readers ignore another signer's version and raise `mail_receiver_alarm`. Created only if absent bars a second first version, not a state change, and after a compromise revocation the owner's devices list the addresses that device created. Policy and `mailcfg` are encrypted, and the projection carries only `mail_send` (§8.8), so alias names never reach the server. Creating an alias or a burner is an I-8 outward action: the `mail` component writes the record only once `Authorize` passes (§5.4), for `ur id`, the apps and §16's `mail_alias_*` alike. The record is created only if absent and, under a decision, carries the use's `effect_key`, which also seeds the DRBG a burner draws its candidate labels from, so a retry or a restart's `Lookup` finds its own record (§16 D-MCP-11). MCP's evs tools never write `mailcfg` (D-MCP-17).
- **Same-network mail** is deposited to the recipient's drop key and signed with the sender's identity key (§6.9), without smtpedge, send quota or DKIM; that signature replaces the TLS label (D-MAIL-8). The sender's device learns the mailbox from `mailcfg` and asks the exchange for `repo:<id>:deposit`, which §8.5's mailbox row gives any subject of the network that the projection marks `mail_send` ([owner decision 333](#od-333)); §20's storage limits bound it, and the recipient's readers show the message as from a member by the push's signer, labeled member-signed (`MailTlsLabel` 3) only if that signer may send as its From address.
- **Network mail key:** the drop key of a personal network's owner's `mailbox`, of a team's general repo whose signed `RepoCreate.inbox` is 2 (§8.8), or, for a scope, of its member's mailbox, carried in each of that repo's GenRotates (D-KEYS-17); §14.8 seals to it the reports that reach the network's own token, burners' once the PSL listing sends theirs there, and finds it through api's rows alone, so `POST /mail/enable` takes no field.
- **Vault entries** (MM:594-605) each have their own slot, so deleting one shreds every version of it ([owner decision 61](#od-61)); only the owner's consented devices (§8.5) read them or write "Used at". That narrower readership is a rule, not a key ([owner decision 440](#od-440)): a mailbox's `EvsShare` subjects and a Team's audit reader hold the keys that open its vault entries, so clients enforce it, `MailVault` refusing every device but the owner's consented ones, and §16.6's refusals leave an agent holding an `EvsShare` of the mailbox no path to its `vault/` family (§2.18). A second seal to an owner-only vault key stays the option should the readership have to hold against a holder of the mailbox's keys.

```text
VaultEntry{entry_id, address, title, username, password, password_history,
           totp{secret, algorithm, digits, period} (RFC 6238), urls, notes,
           used_at[{registrable_domain, first, last}], created, updated, state}
```

### 15.9 Burner email

**Format.** Burners sit in the network's own zone ([owner decision 32](#od-32)): `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, with `<blabel>` a generated word-number label such as `otter-4821` (`^[a-z]+-[0-9]{4}$`) and `<name>` any local part (D-MAIL-7). They are linkable through `<net>`, and an alias, which shared receiver keys in TLSA and CT tie to the label, names the network (Q-MAIL-10). The sidecar picks unused labels, and §12.7 and §7.7 refuse word-number DNS owners and client names, so nothing shadows the wildcard; labels live only in `mailcfg`.

**Records** are §12.7's rows marked §15, outside the user's quota: the wildcard MX `*.<net>.<root>` → `mx.<net>.<root>` covers every burner label, with 15.5's TLSA, and alias zones and Team scopes repeat both with their own `mx` host. Until the PSL listing, a replying burner's selector (§14's `POST /smtp/dkim-keys`) gives its label its own records, guessable but not walkable under §12.6's compact denial ([owner decision 79](#od-79); §2.8 dns-1). Since a child name makes `<blabel>` an empty non-terminal the wildcard no longer answers (RFC 4592 §2.2.1), dns writes `<blabel>` MX and A/AAAA equal to the wildcard's in the journal write of its first `_domainkey` child and deletes them with its last selector, at §14.6's cut-over or a burn (D-DNS-11).

**Replies** come with sending (M9, [owner decision 35](#od-35)), through §14 with `header_from_domain = <blabel>.<net>.<root>` and flag BURNER. They pass strict DMARC under the burner's own selector ([owner decision 79](#od-79)), send from the shared lb addresses, sharing the domain's reputation (owner decisions [32](#od-32), [124](#od-124)), and count against the daily connection quota ([owner decision 30](#od-30)).

**Spam.** The edge applies only IP listings and rate limits (15.4); readers apply the sealed SPF, DKIM and DMARC results (a DMARC reject files it as spam), rules, a per-mailbox naive Bayes filter of the mail component's own, kept in the one `s/model` file (mox's `junk` does not fit it), and user verdicts, never greylisting, since one-time codes cannot wait.

**Burn** is local ([owner decision 32](#od-32)): receivers answer `550 5.1.1` for the label from then on, the label is never reissued, and devices mark the vault entry burned and may shred its mail; pause answers the same, reversibly. DNS and the server change only when a replying burner's selector retires (§14.6).

**App seams (§18).** `SidecarMail` gains `CreateBurner(site)`, `Burn(id)`, `GetVaultEntries`, `GetUsedAt(entry)`, `GetOneTimeCodes(since)` (from vault TOTP and mail) and `GetReceiverCoverage()` (§18.5). Its coverage copies are §18.5's, `foreground-only`'s saying that a phone alone cannot reliably receive mail (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [197](#od-197)), and none speaks of sending, whose limits `CheckSend` gives (§14.5). Before the first burner, `CreateBurner` shows the `foreground-only` copy whenever coverage is `foreground-only` or `none`, and it never refuses for coverage ([owner decision 12](#od-12)). Autofill is app work (§18.15). With no server burner state, the sidecar applies `mail_burners_active` and `mail_burner_creates_per_day` locally (§20.4).

### 15.10 Sending

The local server is the MTA (PLAN.md:104), on §5.8's submission port under D-MAIL-11 and D-TRUST-8's certificate rule (owner decisions [84](#od-84), [130](#od-130)). AUTH and IMAP's LOGIN take one local credential per network, kept in that network's keychain.ur under the mail component's names, the user name `ur` for every network: the daemon compares the presented pair in constant time with every network's verifier, and the match names the mailbox the session serves, so no name says which networks exist. `ur mail credential [--network]` draws the secret in ur's own process, asks on `/dev/tty`, sends the daemon only SHA-256 over the user and the secret through a Confirm method and shows the secret once on the terminal, never stdout, so the daemon holds no secret to give out (I-7), and a lost credential is replaced by making a new one; it grants only what the daemon grants its OS user (owner decisions [47](#od-47), [442](#od-442)). [Later](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mail-named-credentials) a network may hold several named verifiers, made and revoked on their own as app passwords are (`ur mail credential ls` and `rm`). Agents use §16's `mail_send`; both paths pass §5.4's outward-action gate (I-8). For each message the server:
1. checks From against `mail:<alias>#send` (D-ACL-12) and holds mail to unapproved recipients, non-members with no approval record (below), until an I-8 channel approves it (`ur approve <id>`, §16.6);
2. stores a copy in `sent`, an ordinary `m/` and `i/` entry with label `sent` in `f/`, pushed by the sending device, and deposits same-network mail directly;
3. for BURNER sends, applies the header rules: removes every Received header and adds none, rewrites Date to UTC at minute precision, strips User-Agent, X-Mailer and client `X-*` headers, and regenerates the MIME boundaries and the Message-ID under `<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, so replies reveal no device, client or timezone (§14.4 step 3);
4. queues the rest at `o/<h>/<effect_key>`, created only if absent (§16 D-MCP-11), for §14's `SmtpSender.Send`, which holds it on HALTED, QUOTA or TRY_LATER (§14.7-14.8); probation and anonymous-only networks deliver only same-network deposits (§21.7, D-SMTP-14). The sending device writes each recipient domain's outcome to `or/<h>/<effect_key>` (§14.5), with the send's send_id from the entry's Message-ID, and the composing device raises `mail_send {send_id}` (§18.5) for each `or/` record of its member whose outcomes changed since it last read them. `MailClient.CheckSend` checks the message Send would make with the bound sender, or on a host with none through the member's `p/` (`SmtpSender.Check` over the mailbox), and `MailClient.SendResult` reads `or/`'s outcomes by send_id, so every device of the member answers alike, a desktop app's daemon following its phone's sends included ([owner decision 651](#od-651)).

**Approved recipients ([owner decision 280](#od-280)).** An approved recipient is a (sending alias, recipient address) pair with an approval record in the repo that holds that alias's mail, `mailbox:<member>` or the `group:<group>` repo, at `rcpt/<h>/<name>` (15.7), never in mailcfg, `<name>` hashing the pair ([owner decision 632](#od-632)). Its body, `MailRecipientApproval{alias, recipient, decision, action}`, holds the stored bytes of one `ApprovalDecision` on channel device or presence, `decision` being that decision's stored `Signed`, and of the `CanonicalAction` of kind `mail_send` listing that recipient, `action`. The daemon writes one record per recipient a done use names, after that use's Outcome is done, created only if absent; a decision on channel harness sends its one message and creates no record. Every device re-verifies the embedded decision at each use under its current pin (its signer eligible, its channel in the governing list), so a file an agent wrote, or one whose approver was revoked, approves nothing. A record lasts until a person removes it with `ur mail recipients rm` on `/dev/tty` or in an app, and MCP's evs tools refuse `rcpt/` in a mailbox and in a group inbox (§16.6's refused row; [owner decision 635](#od-635)), so an agent cannot read a standing record and write its bytes back after a person removed it. `mail_send` is W only when every non-member recipient has a record and the run is untainted, else O; in a tainted run records are ignored (§16.6's TS1).

Internet sending waits for smtpedge's BDAT and DATA proofs (M9, owner decisions [35](#od-35), [125](#od-125)), which only desktop-class hosts run, so the owner's consented `ur daemon` sidecars, indexers among them ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), send what a phone queues (D-SMTP-18). Each such prover host records its measured cap and DATA rate at `p/<sidecar_id>`, so a phone's composer can show them (§14.5).

**Forwarding ([owner decision 53](#od-53); M9).** (1) One external address per mailbox, confirmed by a 6-digit code sent through §14, is kept with the opted-in burners in the mailbox's signed `forward` entry. (2) Readers forward opted-in burner mail only if it scores below the spam threshold with no DMARC fail as received. (3) The forward is a new message From `r-<token>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>`, `<token>` being a MAC of the original sender under the mailbox's reverse-alias key, one key a mailbox, sealed in its `vault/` family where only the owner's consented devices read it (15.7), so every device of the member gives one sender one reverse alias, which `ra/` records ([owner decision 633](#od-633)), with step 3's header rules and `X-UR-Forwarded`, DKIM-signed like a reply (15.9) and queued in `o/` for a prover host. (4) Mail to `r-<token>` from the verified address, passing DMARC as received, is relayed From the burner to the original sender. (5) Each code, forward or relay costs one connection ([owner decision 30](#od-30)). (6) Forwards never go to `<root>` addresses or repeat a message carrying `X-UR-Forwarded`, which stops loops.

DSNs arrive at `b.<net>.<root>`, and receivers deposit them to the sending mailbox.

### 15.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| SNI splice with DANE | end to end for senders that send SNI | senders without SNI defer | chosen (owner decisions [31](#od-31), [34](#od-34)) |
| Encrypt-on-receipt (Proton, Tuta) or plaintext SMTP at the edge | every sender; filtering; a queue | plaintext at URnetwork | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03) |
| Hosted or TEE receiver, delegated credentials (RFC 9345), or a receiver in an app's VPN component | always on; phone-only users | keys on our hardware, or in a component that runs only forwarding (§18.4) | ruled out (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [197](#od-197)) |
| Per-network IPv6 or IPv4 | senders without SNI reach receivers | no dedicated addresses (§19.5, D-OPS-15) | not now ([owner decision 34](#od-34)) |
| Shared burner domain (mock), or labels on a burner root | short; or unlinkable | routable only on RCPT; a new domain and per-burner DNS | ruled out ([owner decision 32](#od-32)) |
| Verify SPF, DKIM and DMARC at ingest | one verifier, on the reader | judges DNS days after reception, past selector rotation (RFC 6376 §3.1) | rejected (D-MAIL-14) |
| An MTA-STS policy per burner | MTA-STS-only senders enforce for burners | a policy host, certificate and CT entry per burner | rejected ([owner decision 32](#od-32)) |

### 15.12 Decisions proposed

**D-MAIL-1 (proposed).** Inbound TLS ends only at customer receivers, except at D-MAIL-10's platform listener for URnetwork's own report and role addresses (§2.8's statement, mx-4); mxedge's router routes by SNI alone, and every unroutable or offline case gets a temporary failure. *Why:* the directive, with D-TRUST-4's one exception; senders retry.

**D-MAIL-2 (proposed).** mxedge's router speaks only 15.4's pre-TLS dialog, refuses plaintext transactions and splices from the ClientHello on. *Why:* RFC 3207, CVE-2011-0411 and Postfix's retry with TLS.

**D-MAIL-3 (proposed).** Receivers run emersion/go-smtp, forked in-tree with 15.5's two upstreamable changes, `ServeConn` and the bare `<Postmaster>` path ([owner decision 446](#od-446)), and verify with mox over DoH as mail arrives, ARC with their own code. *Why:* pure Go everywhere.

**D-MAIL-4 (proposed).** Each receiver presents its own §13 certificate and TLSA record for `mx.<net>.<root>`, which serves every burner, and serves MTA-STS as a system publish (15.5). *Why:* URnetwork holds no key, removal deletes one record (I-15), and user-publish rules would break policy fetches.

**D-MAIL-5 (proposed).** Receivers deposit each message under its own key, slotted to the drop key in the repo's newest GenRotate (D-KEYS-17), and answer 250 only once it is durable; readers ingest with per-message slots, and an erasure also takes the deposit slot, the index copies and every reader's decrypted copies. *Why:* receivers never read archives, no stale drop key reaches a removed reader, and erasure covers every copy (§11.12).

**D-MAIL-6 (proposed).** Each member has one owner-bound `mailbox` repo, which each of the member's consented devices that is not read-only joins as a repo admin, each group one general repo storing its mail once, which only its repo admins erase, and each network one signed `mailcfg`. *Why:* few MLS groups; one upload per message, not ~5 GB per 50 MiB message to 100 members; and erasure, which takes `admin` (§11.12), never waits on the device that created a mailbox, nor lets every group member destroy the group's mail.

**D-MAIL-7 (proposed).** Burners are `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the wildcard MX; receive-only burners have no records, keys or server state of their own, and burning is local (owner decisions [32](#od-32), [79](#od-79)). *Why:* nothing can be enumerated, and URnetwork stores nothing.

**D-MAIL-8 (proposed).** Same-network mail is delivered by deposit and never crosses the internet. *Why:* "end to end between members" (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:708).

**D-MAIL-9 (proposed).** Burners launch once the owner accepts the SNI loss the M7 census measures ([owner decision 34](#od-34)). The census is scripted ([owner decision 439](#od-439)): a dark test network in main ([owner decision 91](#od-91)) takes mail one sender at a time, from provider test accounts, ESPs and real sign-ups at the top-100 list, and `sidecartest/mailcensus` joins each sender's window with the router's existing `urnetwork_mxedge_*` result counters and the test receiver's own view, one row a sender: sender, ASN, SNI, DANE, TLS version and plaintext fallback, the ASN from the census's own sender list, never from `sender_ip` at the router, so mx-1, mx-2 and ops-1 stay as written; §14's destination-MX probe joins it. Report senders are listed but left out of the bar, since `rpt.bringyour.com` terminates every session, SNI or not (D-SMTP-19). Proposed bar: the share of sign-up senders without SNI, each weighted 1/rank in the sign-up list, under 5%, shown beside the unweighted share, since a census of senders cannot measure volume. *Why:* SES and Yahoo coverage is unknown ([R:ext-email-zk](design/design-research/ext-email-zk.md) §5 item 3).

**D-MAIL-10 (proposed).** Reports and role mail reach `rpt.bringyour.com`'s platform listener, which terminates every session and accepts only platform recipients (D-SMTP-19), for §14.8's intake, which parses headers and aggregate report data only (D-SMTP-23) and persists no plaintext. *Why:* reporters without SNI must deliver, the router holds no key, and no third party stores reports.

**D-MAIL-11 (proposed).** Submission and IMAP bind every interface unless `--listen` narrows them ([owner decision 84](#od-84)); off loopback they speak implicit TLS (RFC 8314 §3), chosen per connection by local address, and plaintext stays on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 ([owner decision 130](#od-130); D-TRUST-8, I-17). *Why:* no credential or mail crosses a LAN in cleartext, and one port serves both.

**D-MAIL-12 (proposed).** A Team direct MX names at most two of its mail indexers, verified before §12 publishes them; strict mode refuses spliced URnetwork-zone hosts and accepts direct-MX sessions, and only an MX selection and TLSA both in customer-signed zones carry the claim that URnetwork cannot redirect mail, surfaced only as `tls_basis.strict_custom_mx`, so a URnetwork-zone direct MX keeps EX2's residual; a member scope's receivers are that member's consented devices (15.4, 15.5). *Why:* owner decisions [33](#od-33), [58](#od-58) and [98](#od-98), trusting neither URnetwork's zone, which a DANE sender follows wherever it points (RFC 7672 §2.2), nor a lone admin.

**D-MAIL-13 (proposed).** [Owner decision 135](#od-135)'s operator list is `mail_operators.yml` in the public sidecar repo ([owner decision 118](#od-118)), embedded in each release with a list version as `mail_operators_gen.go`, which `go generate` writes from it, since the root has no YAML parser, and `make check`'s stale-code rule keeps equal to it; each entry names an operator's PTR suffixes, DKIM domains and published DANE or MTA-STS enforcement, which a label's basis cites, never MTA-STS for burner mail (15.5). *Why:* anyone can recheck a label against it, with no new server or key; the list is an operator-reputation check, and REQUIRETLS records only the final hop's requirement (15.5).

**D-MAIL-14 (proposed).** Receivers capture 15.5's reception-time authentication evidence within its per-message and per-receiver bounds (8 DKIM signatures, aligned ones first; 8 ARC sets; RFC 7208's SPF limits; 64 queries; 30 s; 4 messages at once) and seal it in the deposit, bound to the message hash, time and receiver (`MailAuthEvidence`, at most 8,192 B, its `limits` naming what a bound skipped); readers label, score, receipt and forward from it, count an incomplete check as no result, and never rewrite a label from later DNS. *Why:* DKIM selectors have a lifecycle (RFC 6376 §3.1), and SPF, DMARC and PTR records change, so a later check would judge other DNS; a sender sets how many signatures it adds and how slowly its selectors answer, which RFC 6376 §6.1 lets a verifier limit, while authentication never decides whether mail is accepted (meta review F17).

**D-MAIL-15 (proposed).** Reliable reception rests on mail indexers (§3.6), the receivers an `IndexerSet` designates for mail (§7.9): a personal network's own always-on devices, a Team's `tag:mail` devices under `team_mail: indexers`, or a member scope's own devices; under `team_mail: indexers` an undesignated `tag:mail` device registers no listener and readers alarm on internet mail another receiver took; with none designated, any online receiver still takes mail. *Why:* owner decisions [12](#od-12), [58](#od-58) and [150](#od-150); the designations are the list [owner decision 58](#od-58) discloses to members, and they never gate the receive path.

**D-MAIL-16 (proposed).** `i/` stays the mailbox's message list. Full-text search uses the repo's search index, which covers only `m/`, is keyed by message id, and holds subject, from, to and date in its own doc table. Phones confirm hits against `i/`, or take a designated indexer's verified hits (owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)), and labels, trash and spam join on the device. *Why:* mail ships in v0, before the index (v1), and must list with the index off. An index that every mailbox reader can read must not hold vault entries, which only the owner's consented devices read. Display fields in the index spare every device a query-dependent fetch, at about 0.15 KB a message, uncompressed. On 20 Newsgroups, `i/`'s address and 200 B snippet confirmed 26% of true rare-word matches, against 11% for headers alone.

### 15.13 Open questions

**Q-MAIL-1.** [X6] How does mxedge route without terminating TLS? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [31](#od-31), [34](#od-34)):** by SNI alone, with DANE TLSA; senders without SNI defer (15.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-2.** [X6 residual] Which devices receive mail? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 12](#od-12)):** always-on receivers, which [owner decision 150](#od-150) names mail indexers, and the iOS app in the foreground, which listens only while open and so is no reliable receiver (15.6). **Amended by owner 2026-11-09 ([owner decision 197](#od-197)):** Android with the VPN on is no longer an always-on receiver: the Android app, like the iOS app, receives only while it is open, so the always-on receivers are a desktop `ur daemon`, a NAS or a VPS. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-3.** [X6 residual] What are the burner format and domain? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 32](#od-32), superseding [owner decision 29](#od-29)):** `<name>@<blabel>.<net>.<root>` under the wildcard MX (15.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-4.** Should burners forward to external inboxes (MM:583)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 53](#od-53)):** opt-in, to one verified address, with sending (15.10). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-5.** Who receives a Team network's mail? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 58](#od-58), superseding [owner decision 54](#od-54)):** disclosed mail indexers the team designates ([owner decision 150](#od-150)), or member scopes with their own `mx` host (15.5, 15.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-6.** Should mxedge reject at the banner on IP reputation? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 111](#od-111)):** only on botnet and exploit listings, never greylisting (15.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-7 (withdrawn).** Withdrawn with Q-ARCH-4; §2.8 lists mx-1 to mx-4.

**Q-MAIL-8 (closed 2026-11-03).** (a): clients check `mail:<alias>`, and mxedge only `listen`; applied as D-ACL-12 (§8.10).

**Q-MAIL-9.** [X6 residual] Should mxedge refuse senders without STARTTLS, against RFC 3207 §4? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 33](#od-33)):** yes, with 530 and a published deviation, plus a Team direct MX (15.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-10.** Cross-cutting (§2.8, §21.9). Can burners be linked? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 32](#od-32)):** yes, through `<net>`, and an alias names the network; product copy says so (15.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-11.** Cross-cutting (§16.6). Does a DKIM-verified email reply count as an approval? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 80](#od-80)):** no; email approval is dropped. *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-12.** Cross-cutting (§14.6). How do burner replies pass strict DMARC? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 79](#od-79)):** a replying burner's own selector and records until the PSL listing, then §14.6's cut-over (15.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-MAIL-13.** Cross-cutting (§2.8 EX3, §21.9). What makes received mail "validated" ([owner decision 98](#od-98)), given that few senders set REQUIRETLS? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 135](#od-135)):** (b): REQUIRETLS, or TLSA for the SNI host in our signed zone plus a sender on a versioned list of DANE- or MTA-STS-enforcing operators, identified by forward-confirmed PTR or aligned DKIM `d=`; else "opportunistic" (15.5, D-MAIL-13). Ingest records the basis, from the receiver's sealed evidence (D-MAIL-14), in `tls_basis`. *Residual:* none.

### 15.14 Departures from PLAN.md

PLAN.md:104's `mail.<me>.ur.network` becomes `mx.<net>.<root>` ([owner decision 32](#od-32); Q-MAIL-3); the receiver is still the local server, and mxedge is the ingress a public mail host implies. Not PLAN.md: refusing plaintext SMTP departs from RFC 3207 §4 ([owner decision 33](#od-33)); burners in the network zone replace the mock's `burner.ur` (MM:918) and are linkable, which [R:product](design/design-research/product.md) §2.3 asked to avoid ([owner decision 32](#od-32)); and approval by email reply is dropped ([owner decision 80](#od-80); P5:899).

### 15.15 Interfaces

- **Provides:** the `mail` component (15.5-15.10, with mail, burner, vault, coverage and one-time-code APIs for §16 and §18); the `mxedgeservice` engine (15.4); `MailIngress`, `MailAuthEvidence`, `MailDeposit`, the network mail key (15.8) and the operator list (D-MAIL-13).
- **Consumes:** §5 (the outward-action gate, tainted runs); §6 (`mail` topic, 0x17); §7.9 (`IndexerSet`, `team_mail`); §8 (grants, consent, data-repo seats, `RepoAdmin`); §9; §10 (GenRotate drop keys and the depositor rule, D-KEYS-17; ReaderWraps); §11 (deposit slots, ERASE and CLOSURE's bound, file-mode refs, the write gate and budget); §12 (D-DNS-11's burner copies); §13 (certificates, the MTA-STS publish); §14 (`SmtpSender`, D-SMTP-13's LAN splice); §16 (D-MCP-11's effect keys); §18 (receiver hosting, forced wakes); §19 (lb ports, feed credential); §20; §11.14's search engine and remote search, and §18.4's device policy, notice and setting (D-MAIL-16).
- **Subprotocol messages:** `MailIngress` (0x1701; mxedge to receiver; StreamOpen metadata on a Required stream); `MailHint{kind, host}` (0x1702; `mail` push in `PushHint.hint`, at most 256 B; server to client), on a topic whose version is the writer's clock in ms, per client, so mxedge, smtpedge and api may all write it (§6.8): `kind` is `MailHintKind` RECEIVER_NEEDED (2), `host` `mx` or `mx.<scope>`; DEPOSIT (1) stays reserved and is never sent, a new deposit reaching readers by evs's `evs:<repo_id>` hint and §18.7's wake, which covers topic `evs`; 0 is a protocol error (§6.11).
- **API routes:** `POST /mail/enable` (Client class; an empty body, returning `{enabled_time}`) turns on §12's mail records and the MTA-STS publish; `GET /mail/status`, returning `{enabled, storage_full, spent, direct_mx, strict_domains}`, which receivers read at most every 30 s (15.5), and whose `strict_domains`, the network's verified custom domains in strict mode, a sending sidecar reads at each send of a custom domain's mail, the set smtpedge's gate derives the envelope from (§14.6; [owner decision 655](#od-655)); `POST` and `DELETE /mail/direct-mx` (Network class, Admin role, Team only, an I-8 outward action; 15.4).
- **Tables** (mxedge; migrations ≥926) and Redis keys:

```sql
mail_network(network_id PK, create_time)
mail_host_key(network_id, host, receiver_sidecar_id, spki_sha256, state, publish_time, retire_time) -- host: mx or mx.<scope>
mail_direct_mx(network_id, receiver_sidecar_id, address, state, verify_time)
mail_connection_record(network_id, start_time, byte_count, result) -- router sessions, 10 s batches; no sender
--   address or burner label (§2.8 mx-2)
-- rows: mail_network until mail is turned off or the network is deleted; mail_host_key 30 days after
--   retire_time; mail_direct_mx until DELETE or its receiver's removal; mail_connection_record in hourly
--   partitions, dropped at 24 h after any §21.9 hold has copied out its network's rows; a hold's copy
--   excepted (api-14; owner decision 133)
-- Redis {mxr_<net>}: the route projection of mail-enabled labels, aliases, scopes and custom MX hosts, behind an
--   in-process cache, so connections never query Postgres: <net> the SNI's routable part (a label, an alias or a
--   custom MX host's full name), its value network_id, the host (mx or mx.<scope>), flags and
--   receiver_sidecar_ids (15.6); a suspended network has no entry, so its SNI closes in the handshake, nor has a
--   direct-MX network; {mxc_<hash>}: the fleet's closed-handshake memory, one key per sender /24 or /48
```

- **Services and config:** two warp services on TCP 25 of different lb interfaces (§19.5's W4), `mxedge`, the router, and `mxedge-platform`, the platform listener, each a thin `server/cli/<dir>` over a shared `server/mxedgehost`, `server/cli/mxedge-platform/` holding only a Makefile that builds the shared main and a Dockerfile that picks the role, as `server/cli/dnsedge/` does, so one binary serves both; `config/<env>/mxedge.yml`, with `MxEdgeSettings`' caps and `PlatformMessageByteCount` (15.4); the platform-mail key and feed credential in vault `secret_files`; `pro.yml`'s `mail_inbound_message_bytes`, `mail_group_members` and `mail_inbound_repos_per_message` (§20.4); the embedded `mail_operators.yml` and its generated `mail_operators_gen.go` (D-MAIL-13).
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §9.10's gates and §13.9's `ValidateListen` admit only a mail-enabled network's receivers' `tls/443/mta-sts` system publish without `tls/` grants, on each receiver's `smtp/25/mx` listen grant (15.5); §8.8 lets a consented device that is not read-only file `RepoAdmin{add}` for itself in its owner's mailbox, §11.12's closure bound admits a merged `i/` record padded a step past the replaced records' sum, §11.12 and §20.7 give each erasing sidecar its own closure-upload rate, an equal turn of the network's paced closure uploads and its own UTC-day closure allowance, never under the re-keys of one message's erasure, the network's erasure rate only queueing pushes as P1 ([owner decision 146](#od-146)), and §11.6 draws slot ids per statement (15.7); §21.11 publishes the RFC 3207 deviation from M5 (15.4); §2.8's mx-1 keys the closed-handshake memory per sender /24 or /48, and mx-2 names `mail_connection_record`, which §19.7's MG7 creates, with a ttl excepting a hold's copy, and §2.8's header, api-14's sees, §21.9's holds and §21.16 list its rows in `copied_rows` (15.4); §22 tests the labels, reception-time evidence and its bounds (FS-121), strict mode's sessions and its `strict_custom_mx` claim (15.4), erased deposit, index and decrypted copies, at the exact storage limit too, 429 past an eraser's own closure rate, turn or allowance, and with an `i/` re-checkpoint that crosses a padding step, and burners' records and missing MTA-STS, an MTA-STS-only listed operator's burner mail labeled "validated" on a basis citing no MTA-STS (FS-13, FS-33, FS-39, FS-47), FS-39's report intake and S7's SNI-less abuse@`<root>` gating M5; §23.4 states M8's mail-indexer criterion as release readiness (15.17), never a per-user gate.

### 15.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senders without SNI (Yahoo, AOL, Proton by anecdote; SES unknown) lose sign-up codes | High | High | DANE, D-MAIL-9's gate, direct MX, copy |
| A phone alone cannot reliably receive (the iOS and Android apps listen only while open), so phone-only users miss codes (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [197](#od-197)) | High | High | indexer prompt, wake hold, copy |
| A site loss erases a phone-only user's message bodies, on iOS or Android ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); logins, burners and `i/` survive on the phone (§11.13) | Low | High | the owner's indexer mirrors the mailbox (§11.13); copy |
| Sites block `<root>` sign-ups as disposable, and network mail shares that reputation ([owner decision 32](#od-32)) | High | High | abuse caps and burns (§21); no full mitigation |
| [Owner decision 135](#od-135)'s operator match trusts mxedge's sender address and the author's DKIM domain, not the delivering hop, so an intercepting mxedge can win "validated" for some opportunistic mail, and needs no fake for an operator listed only for MTA-STS enforcement, whose burner mail is "validated" though burner domains publish no policy; REQUIRETLS is exact only as the final hop's requirement, which an operator that read the first hop can add | Low | High | disclosed (§2.8 EX3, §2.18); no UI or API asserts path confidentiality, or MTA-STS for burner mail; `tls_basis` |
| Spam loads devices; the edge filters no content | Medium | Medium | banner rejects, prefix caps, `max_streams`, burn |
| A sender's many signatures, long identifiers or slow selectors tie up a receiver's authentication or overflow its evidence | Medium | Medium | 15.5's bounds: 8 DKIM signatures, 8 ARC sets, 64 queries, 30 s, 4 messages at once, 8,192 B of evidence; a cut check is no result, so it refuses no mail and strengthens no label (D-MAIL-14) |
| A compromised receiver exposes mail in transit | Low | High | per-device keys, I-15, Team scopes, listed mail indexers and the undesignated-receiver alarm (D-MAIL-15) |
| A compromised admitted receiver seals passing verdicts for forged mail, which ingest, checking only the hash and the signer, labels validated | Low | High | per-device keys, I-15, Team scopes, listed mail indexers and the undesignated-receiver alarm (D-MAIL-15); the label states its basis, and any re-check shows apart (D-MAIL-14) |
| A reader that starts fresh on a `mailcfg` ref whose epoch holds more than `EvsSettings.ReadVersionScanCount` (16,384) versions below a record's creation cannot learn its earlier lives and does not honor the record, and a member who can write `mailcfg` can push that many versions to make older records unknown to fresh readers ([owner decision 568](#od-568)) | Low | Medium | the record stays unknown to Resolve, failing closed, so its mail goes to nobody else (§11.9's reply row); from the review phase mailcfg's readers replay the ref from genesis, judging each life from its statements |
| A fresh reader judges an address or burner re-created across a path-epoch cut-over, which follows every REMOVE generation, on its new life alone, since evs's read below a creation ends at the newest cut-over, so under a policy granting every member `mail:*` a member who removes another's address before a cut-over and creates it after one takes it on readers that restart ([owner decision 568](#od-568)) | Low | High | readers that held the record count a new life only where its creator may change it; from the review phase mailcfg's readers replay the ref from genesis, which closes it (§11.9's reply row) |
| IMAP's and submission's secret is shown once, so a person with two mail clients saves it then, or makes a new one and enters it in each; a client keying saved passwords by host and user sees two networks' accounts at one host and user ([owner decision 442](#od-442)) | Medium | Low | several named verifiers a network, made and revoked on their own, as the later fix |
| A site or Hurricane Electric outage stops both nameservers and with them every ur.network name, ACME, DANE and, from M7, inbound mail; a weekend outage can outlast senders' shorter retries ([owner decision 123](#od-123)) | Medium | Critical | accepted; paged at all hours ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); senders retry 14 h to 5 d (15.3) |
| A direct MX publishes a mail indexer's address and depends on its uptime | Medium | Medium | two mail indexers, probes, `receiver_needed` |
| A LAN host attacks submission or IMAP ([owner decision 84](#od-84)) | Medium | Medium | TLS only off loopback (D-MAIL-11); `--listen` |
| Phone search over older mail shows possible matches that lack the query: on 20 Newsgroups, about half of the top five for rare words | High | Medium | labeled possible; ranked by trigram overlap; confirmed against `i/`, a cached body or on open; desktops and indexers verify; a designated indexer's verified answer where one is online ([owner decision 178](#od-178)) |

### 15.17 Phasing

- **v0, M5:** the platform listener (D-MAIL-10), for §21's intake before any public name; its 530 links §21.11's RFC 3207 deviation, published from M5, and M5-out runs FS-39's intake cases and S7's SNI-less abuse@`<root>` case (§22, §23.6).
- **v0, M7 (network mail):** the router, IP listings and DANE TLSA; desktop, NAS and VPS mail indexers ([owner decision 150](#od-150)); deposits with reception-time evidence inside 15.5's bounds, ingest, layout and labels; admin, id, group and agent addresses; same-network delivery; the census. Blocked by C9 (M5), §9 `smtp/`, §10's GenRotate drop keys, §11's deposit refs and slots, §12's signed root and mail records, and §19's TCP 25 ports.
- **v0, M8 (BS1, the receive-only burner launch on personal networks):** burners, vault entries and local burn; app seams and wakes ([owner decision 88](#od-88)); IMAP; MTA-STS and TLS-RPT. BS1 ships once the owner accepts D-MAIL-9's census loss and, as release readiness, the mail indexer paths (desktop daemon, NAS or VPS; no app, [owner decision 197](#od-197)) and the apps' indexer prompt pass §22 (§23.4); a user needs no indexer to create a burner, only 15.9's copy ([owner decision 12](#od-12)).
- **v0, M9 (sending):** submission through §14, burner replies with their own records and MX copies (D-DNS-11), the BURNER header rules and forwarding, behind D-SMTP-16's gate with DATA coverage (owner decisions [35](#od-35), [53](#od-53), [79](#od-79), [125](#od-125)).
- **v1 (Team; owner decisions [33](#od-33), [58](#od-58), [98](#od-98), [150](#od-150)):** network-scope mail indexers, direct MX and strict mode from M7; scopes from M8.
- **v1, M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)):** mail search (D-MAIL-16) at the later of M10's and M7's exits, and IMAP SEARCH on the engine and phones' remote search over mail (15.7) at the later of M10's and M8's, in team networks group inboxes' through network-scope search indexers once M6's has passed too; mailboxes and group repos created earlier are indexed by one full build on a device that holds their mail (§11.14).
- **Later:** [destination routing](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mail-destination-routing) if a routed IPv6 block is obtained ([owner decision 34](#od-34)), [Team burners](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mail-team-burners), §14.6's [PSL cut-over](DESIGN-DEFER.md#dns-psl-listing), [edge reputation from receiver verdicts](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mail-edge-reputation).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mail-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Ordering:** team B builds mail and burner after M2 ([owner decision 9](#od-9), X15); their lead times (port 25, PTR, the census) start in M0 (§23.7).

## 16. The local MCP server, harness integration, and record primitives

### 16.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sidecar/mcp`, the stdio MCP server in the §5 daemon: its catalog; the approval channels, spend check and use ledger behind §5.4's outward-action gate (I-8); taint, prompt injection and attribution; harness integration, ingest and restore; search over readable repos' indexes for `ur search`, `ur agents` and MCP, agent finding included (16.10); the team directory (16.11), which in a team network is also its coordination log; recURd's record primitives (X20); and the relation to `server/mcp`. §5 owns the daemon, identity and gate; §7 the config repo, §8 grants and consent, §10 keys, §11 storage and its search index; §9 and §12-§17 the components; RECORD.md record semantics ([owner decision 25](#od-25)).

### 16.3 What exists today

- **server/mcp:** stateless streamable HTTP, an OAuth 2.1 resource server for `https://mcp.bringyour.com` (scopes `mcp:read`, `mcp:fetch`) with two annotated tools (server/mcp/server.go:3-13; auth.go:15-16, :42; tools.go:29-72). It imports server, so the sidecar cannot reuse it.
- **go-sdk v1.7.0** (server/go.mod:30; Apache-2.0 plus MIT, LICENSE:1-5) serves protocol 2026-07-28, which drops `initialize` and sessions (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog), down to 2024-11-05 (mcp/shared.go:50-64), and has `IOTransport` (mcp/transport.go:130). Its typed handler fills `StructuredContent` and, with `Content` nil, one `TextContent` of the same JSON, and never rewrites a `resource_link` for an older session (mcp/server.go:398-442).
- **Missing:** everything below; connect proxies only via SOCKS5 (connect/net.go:333-363), so cloud sandboxes' HTTP CONNECT proxies need §4's C8.

### 16.4 The MCP server in the daemon

- **Entry.** `ur mcp [--agent <name>] [--instance <i>]` always speaks MCP, as does bare `ur` when stdin is not a terminal ([owner decision 57](#od-57)). Both send §5.8's hello (mode `mcp`) and relay newline-delimited JSON-RPC to one go-sdk `ServerSession` over `IOTransport`. The daemon hosts a `Sidecar` per network, so tools take an optional `network`, resolved by §5.8's `.ur` rules ([owner decision 23](#od-23)).
- **Sessions.** Each holds its agent, run bindings and subscriptions; its run's taint lives in the run's file (D-MCP-16). A session runs at most 8 in-flight calls, 20 W calls/s (`Mcp.SessionWriteRate`, burst 20, a second's worth), and `Search.SessionSearchCount` searches at once (§5.4; 2 by default) and 5 a second (16.10); results over 256 KiB become a `resource_link` from 2025-06-18, else a text naming the `ur://` resource (D-MCP-13). Calls time out at 30 s, under Codex's 60 s `tool_timeout_sec` default (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli); one awaiting a person returns `pending` at once. Restarts fail in-flight calls retryably; the relay replays `initialize` and subscriptions for pre-2026-07-28 peers.
- **Locked or Unenrolled.** Tools return FAILED_PRECONDITION naming `ur unlock` or `ur login` for the person's own terminal; MCP never asks for the pass and has no admin path (§5.7).

### 16.5 Tool, resource, and notification catalog

Tiers (16.6): **R** read, with `readOnlyHint`; **W** in-network write; **O** outward (§5.4's `SidecarAction` kinds), with `openWorldHint` (server/mcp/tools.go), calling `Sidecar.Authorize`. Only O tools, and `run_restore` in a tainted run or for shell paths, create requests, whose `CanonicalAction` the daemon builds (16.8).

| Tool | Tier | Side effects (owner) |
|---|---|---|
| `evs_repos`, `evs_list`, `evs_history`, `evs_read`, `evs_drop_preview` | R | §11; untrusted content taints, a version's trust read from its push's sealed provenance (16.6's taint row); never a `secret` repo, nor the config repo, the team directory, a mailbox's `vault/` family or the search index's contents, `evs_repos` alone naming the config repo and `evs_list` omitting the `vault/` family (16.6); `evs_history` and `evs_read` report `drop_pending` and `dropped` with the drop's id and signer (§11.9); `evs_drop_preview` on admin-scoped sidecars only, within the repo's daily dry runs, reports what a drop would free and never drops (D-MCP-32) |
| `evs_write`, `evs_delete` | W; O for agent-config files in shared repos (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, `.mcp.json`, hooks; sidecar/design/pitch5.html:737) | a signed push on either ref mode (below), this sidecar as committer ([owner decision 81](#od-81)), its sealed provenance carrying the writing run's `tainted` bit ([owner decision 245](#od-245)) and, where the session has an agent, its `agent_id` ([owner decision 470](#od-470)); a conflict → FAILED_PRECONDITION; refuses repos of kind `config`, `mailcfg`, `secret` and `directory`, the search index's files (§11.14) and the vault's `harness/` path (16.7); versioning off where §11.7 or a repo's lock refuses it → FAILED_PRECONDITION |

| `mail_send` | W only when every non-member recipient has an approval record (§15.10's `rcpt/`; [owner decision 280](#od-280)) and the run is untainted; else O | an entry listing every recipient, BCC included; quota (§14, §20) |
| `mail_aliases`; `mail_alias_create`, `mail_alias_delete` | R; O | a signed `mailcfg` record, written only after the decision (§15.8); public address (§8 `mail:`) |
| `socket_list`, `socket_status`; `socket_listen`; `socket_unlisten` | R; O, or W under a covering grant; W | §9.9 |

| `bridge_list`; `bridge_forward`, `bridge_expose`; `bridge_close` | R; O; W | §17: `bridge_expose` files its `BridgeRoute` or `BridgeMap` (a host's first map also its `BridgeAddress`), `bridge_close` a `GrantRevoke` or `BridgeWithdraw` (16.6) |
| `dns_records`; `dns_set`, `dns_delete` | R; O | `GET /dns/zone`; `POST /dns/records` (§12.8) |
| `team_members`, `team_agents`, `acl_grants`, `acl_check`, `record_query`, `run_coverage`, `approval_status` | R | §7, §8, 16.8 |
| `record_append` | W | source `agent` (16.8); in a team network, the directory (16.11) |
| `directory_list`, `directory_requests`; `directory_request` | R; O | 16.11: announcements and requests as stubs; an access request through §5.4's gate (owner decisions [74](#od-74), [179](#od-179), [180](#od-180)) |

- **Resources** (above): the daemon maps §6 topics and §11's token-prefix subscriptions ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) to them.
- **Notifications:** `resources/updated` and `progress`, which also reports a search's phase 2 (16.10); a static tool list, no prompts or sampling.

### 16.6 Local security

**Tiers (D-MCP-17).** Every tool needs an allow for the session's subject from §8's local evaluation ([owner decision 6](#od-6)); W is also recorded and rate-limited, and O passes §5.4's gate, `directory_request` among them, whose access request the member endorses before anything is filed (16.11). No tool changes policy, members, enrollment or consent (§8.5), returns keys or tokens, or approves anything:

                   §17.9), its views coming from team_members, team_agents, acl_grants and acl_check; every evs

**Approval channels (I-8).** Decisions are §6.9 `Signed` statements (purpose `approval`) labeled with their evidence. No decision needs an SSHSIG, in v0 and every milestone until a customer asks ([SSH-signed approvals](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mcp-sshsig-approvals); [owner decision 279](#od-279)): every action's risk stays normal, no policy field or classifier raises it, and `ApprovalDecision.sshsig` stays reserved, ignored wherever it is presented and never trusted. A network accepts only the channels that the matching `requests` rule's `evidence`, else `evidenceDefault`, lists (§8.5, §8.6; [owner decision 75](#od-75)), harness in a tainted run only where the rule's own list names it ([owner decision 142](#od-142)). Rows carry both as effective lists, a rule's in its `AclRequestRule` and the document's default in `AclRows.evidence_default`, so every verifier, the daemon, every server gate and every reader, checks a ruleless action's channel against the default in the spend check: `dns_set` and `dns_delete` at `POST /dns/records` (§12.8) and `bridge_expose` approvals; a document that narrows `evidenceDefault`, to device alone say, holds at the gates (§8.8; [owner decision 342](#od-342)). Email replies, MCP elicitation and the pass never count (owner decisions [75](#od-75), [80](#od-80); §5.9).

| Evidence | Channel; signer |
|---|---|
| `device` | an approval-capable device of the approver other than the requester (below): the app's `SidecarApprovals` (§18.5), or `ur approve <id>` confirmed on that host's /dev/tty; its identity key, after recomputing the action |
| `presence` | `ur approve <id>`, the daemon's presence prompt or the app, with a registered presence key of a profile below |
| `harness` | the harness's prompt for the call, or `ur`'s `/dev/tty` confirmation of a typed command; the requesting sidecar, under `harness_ok` |

                                                                      its confirmation (§5.6)

**Spend check (D-MCP-12)**, run before any effect: by the executing daemon (spend step 1, below) and by every server gate after its stored-result lookup:

```text
spendable(d, a, s, P)   decision d, canonical action a, spender s, the spender's current AuthPin P (§7.9)
  d verifies (§6.9, SIGNED_APPROVAL_DECISION) and d.decision = approve
  and d's signer fits d.channel: an approval-capable device of d.approver_member_id other than s (device), a
      presence key registered to that member (presence), or s itself under harness_ok (harness; its
      conditions, taint included, are the signing daemon's own, which no gate sees)
  and d.requester_sidecar_id = s                (a gate: the bearer token's ur_sidecar_id)
  and d.payload_sha256 = SHA-256(a as stored)   (a gate also checks that the fields it sees, parsed from a,
                                                 equal its request's: host, port, audience, expiry, name, rdata)
  and now <= d.not_after_millis                 (daemon clock; gate server time; ±60 s skew, §8.6)
  and d.auth_pin.version <= P.version and, where s retains the chain digest at that version (every position
      since its previous base, §7.9), the digests are equal
  and under P the approver is still eligible, d.channel is in the governing evidence list (the matching
      requests rule's, else evidenceDefault), and a still falls inside the matching rule where one governs
  and, on the daemon, d.request_sha256 = SHA-256(its stored ApprovalRequest), whose daemon-built
      local_port, weight, alpn and socket_name it applies (16.8)
k approvers  a rule asking for k needs k decisions with one request_sha256 from distinct approvers the rule
             names (autogroup:admin, a group the member is in, or autogroup:dst-owner resolving to an admin
             where no owner or sponsor stands, D-ACL-23), as the authorization log's quorum counts them
             (owner decision 349); an Owner's or Admin's decision the rule does not name only meets §8.6's
             admin clause where that applies, never one of the k (owner decision 471); the budget is the
             smallest uses, the expiry the earliest not_after
multi-use    a decision with uses > 1 binds a template, a CanonicalAction with scope = true whose non-empty
             fields every use equals, recipients a subset, and the fields its kind binds too, set or empty: an
             egress_change's require_default_egress, so a template that leaves it empty covers only uses that
             leave it unset and one under exits covers one distinct action (owner decision 614); each use's full
             action is what D-MCP-11 hashes; the request names the uses its agent asks for a template, 1 for any
             other action, daemon-built, under request_sha256 and rendered beside the action's other
             daemon-built fields, and the approver signs that count as uses: an app's Decide (§18.5) approves
             the request as shown, and ur approve --uses defaults to it, another count refused or narrowed as
             before, above 1 only for a template and never above the request's; the field is
             ApprovalRequest.uses = 18 at the request's version 2, which every request is filed at, an approver
             that knows only version 1 refusing version 2 whole, and a version-1 template names no count, so an
             app lists deny alone for it (owner decision 574); an agent asks for a template only through
             mail_send's uses, 2 or more, for which the daemon builds one of the call's from_alias and
             recipients, to, cc and bcc the allowed set, with no body hash or preview, and every other O tool
             files one use (16.5; owner decision 613)
grants       an approval activates one grant, by §8.8's GrantActivate under the grant_id the approval fixes,
             or, for bridge_expose, at most uses BridgeRoute or BridgeMap rules, each under the rule id §17.8
             derives from its use's effect_key; a replay adds none, and a revoked grant_id or withdrawn rule id
             is refused (§7.9)
AD1  a decision is spendable only by its requester_sidecar_id
AD2  one approval activates at most one grant or uses bridge rules, and a revoked grant or withdrawn rule
     never returns
AD3  a decision evaluated on a projection the spender knows to be forked is refused
AD4  a gate learns no field it lacked: requester_sidecar_id is the bearer's own, auth_pin holds public ids
```

**Harness evidence (D-MCP-9).** `ur install-harness` makes the harness ask before every O tool (16.7). Claude Code, Codex and Cursor run hooks and the agent's shell as children of one harness process and uid, so nothing a same-uid process sees (peer uid, pid ancestry, executable hash, session id) tells a genuine hook from a `ur hook` call by a prompt-injected agent, and no harness offers an authenticated hook channel, which the design adopts once one ships ([owner decision 47](#od-47)). The daemon signs a `harness` decision, citing the hook event's hash, only when:

```text
harness_ok(call) = the requester is an untagged sidecar of member M, consented (§8.5), M is the approver §8
                   requires, M has no approval-capable device other than the requester and no presence key,
                   and §8.5's governing evidence list (the rule's evidence, else evidenceDefault) includes harness
               and the request is untainted (ApprovalRequest.tainted = false), unless the matching requests
                   rule's own evidence names harness, never through evidenceDefault (owner decision 142)
               and either a hook event asked about this call: same session, tool and SHA-256 of the arguments
                   (Claude Code and Codex: PermissionRequest; Cursor: beforeMCPExecution answered ask), unused,
                   under 10 min old, in a session reporting no prompt-skipping mode (auto, dontAsk,
                   bypassPermissions)
                   or a person typed the command and confirmed it on ur's controlling terminal (/dev/tty)
never            a harness decision authorizes no KeyRegister (but a member's first presence key), KeyRevoke,
                 RecoveryBind, RecoveryRebind, OwnerConfirm, admission or authority statement, revocation of
                 another of the member's devices (§5.6), nor an acl or bridge statement beyond an O tool's own
                 filings (above; §8.6); those are signed directly, for a /dev/tty-confirmed command or in an
                 app's UI (D-CORE-13)
presence prompt  where the daemon's host holds M's presence key, it answers a matching PermissionRequest (Cursor:
                 beforeMCPExecution), waiting up to Ingest.PresencePromptTimeout (16.7's how), with a
                 presence prompt over the decision's signed bytes (Secure Enclave with LocalAuthentication
                 through the ur bundle on macOS, Windows Hello, or a FIDO key): channel presence, and harness_ok
                 is never needed
first run        ur login offers to register a platform presence key where the host has one, so most
                 single-device members never depend on harness evidence
residual         harness evidence shows only that the harness, or any process of the user, reported a
                 permission prompt for that exact call, which a prompt-injected agent with a shell tool can
                 forge (owner decisions 47, 75); records mark hook events source = hook, and approver screens
                 and the record label harness decisions
```

```text
device or presence evidence
agent    --O tool-------> daemon: Sidecar.Authorize (§5.4) builds CanonicalAction and risk; pending
daemon   --ApprovalRequest entry--> approver's log (16.8) --evs hint, else §18.7 wake--> approver device
         (a phone leasing each approval log it reads whole, 16.8's approvals; owner decision 573)
approver device: recompute payload_sha256; render the daemon-built fields; show summary and preview as
         untrusted; sign
approver --ApprovalDecision--> requester's log --hint--> daemon (agent watches ur://approval/{id}); a
         requester that reads no vault gets it as an ApprovalDelivery sealed to it (16.8)
agent    --same arguments--> daemon: rebuild the action; spendable; request_sha256 binds run and agent
harness evidence
harness  --PermissionRequest hook--> daemon: note (session, tool, SHA-256 of the arguments), or, on a host
         holding M's presence key, answer with the presence prompt
person   --allows in the harness prompt--> harness --O tool--> daemon: harness_ok; sign, channel harness
both
daemon   --Reserve, fsynced--> approval ledger --execute with effect_key--> component; a server-gated action,
         whose CanonicalAction holds only fields its gate already sees, carries the decision, that action and
         Idempotency-Key: <effect_key> to §8.10's gate, which consumes the use in the effect's own
         transaction and learns no field it lacks: run and agent ids, recipients, previews stay sealed
daemon   --Outcome, then an approval entry per use--> record
```

**Consumption (D-MCP-11)** reserves each use durably before its effect:

```text
ledger      <state>/net/<network_id>/approvals/<approval_id>, file class approval (§5.9), append-only, each
            record fsynced before the step it guards:
            Reserve{action_id, use_index, payload_sha256, effect_key, reserved_millis}
            Outcome{action_id, state: done | not_done | uncertain, effect_ref, millis}
            Cancel{millis, signer_sidecar_id}
action_id   SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/action" || approval_id || this use's CanonicalAction bytes); for
            uses = 1 it is ApprovalRequest.action_id, computed at proposal (R-MCP-6)
effect_key  SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/effect" || approval_id || action_id)
server      approval_use(network_id, approval_id, use_index, effect_key, state, result, create_time,
            not_after, PRIMARY KEY (approval_id, use_index), UNIQUE (approval_id, effect_key), CHECK (state =
            'cancelled' OR effect_key IS NOT NULL)), with the index approval_use_not_after, in api's Postgres,
            written in the transaction of each server-gated effect: in v0 only §12.8's POST /dns/records, since
            grant activations, §13's publishes included, use grant_id (§8.8); not_after is the expiry the gate
            checked, the decision's not_after_millis or the earliest under k approvers, on every row, done and
            cancelled alike
spend       Sidecar.Authorize with a decision (§5.4):
  1  take the approval's in-process mutex; spendable, without its expiry test when a Reserve for this
     action_id exists (a retry, which expiry below bounds)
  2  a Reserve for this action_id exists: go to 5 (the retry path)
  3  refuse: spent if uses Reserves exist, cancelled if a Cancel does, stale if the request's run is now
     tainted but its ApprovalRequest.tainted = false (TS1; Authorize then files a tainted request),
     expired past not_after, or, for a server-gated use, past not_after - 60 s (§8.6's skew), so a prompt
     presentation meets the gate's clock
  4  append Reserve{use_index = the count}, fsync               <- linearization point, local effects
  5  run the component with effect_key; each is idempotent per key, and Lookup(effect_key) finds its effect:
       outbox   o/<h>/<effect_key>, created only if absent (§15.10)
       gate     the request carries Idempotency-Key (§12.8); Lookup replays it for the stored result; a
                refusal proves no effect only at the first presentation, as an earlier one may still commit
       grant    GrantActivate under grant_id (§8.8); Lookup: grant_id in the authorization log
       bridge   bridge_expose's BridgeRoute or BridgeMap under the rule id §17.8 derives from effect_key,
                a map first filing its host's BridgeAddress when the log holds none for it (§17.4); Lookup:
                that id in the authorization log; a re-signed retry keeps the id, counted once (§7.9)
       evs      O-tier evs_write and evs_delete, and mail_alias_delete's record removal: Lookup finds the
                path's first version after base_version if it is this sidecar's, with content_sha256 (for a
                delete, a deletion); mail_alias_create's mailcfg addr/ record carries effect_key and is created
                only if absent (§15.8), and Lookup finds it; each pushes only while Lookup finds nothing, and
                looks again after a refusal
       restore  converges on target hashes (16.7); Lookup: the current hashes
  6  append Outcome: done with the effect's reference; not_done only when the component proves no effect
     happened; else uncertain
gate        one transaction per request:
  1  SELECT result FROM approval_use WHERE approval_id = $1 AND effect_key = $2; found: answer it, past
     not_after too, while the row lasts; else the spend check at server time, only the rule's named
     approvers counting toward k (owner decision 471), refused: answer, writing nothing
  2  for n in 0 .. uses-1: INSERT approval_use(n, effect_key, 'done', ...) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; the first
     success wins use n; none left: the row a racing request committed for this effect_key answers, else
     409 SPENT (the keys serialize racing gates without session locks, which PgBouncer's transaction
     pooling forbids)
  3  apply the effect and store its result in the same row
  4  COMMIT                                                     <- linearization point, server-gated effects
restart     each Reserve without an Outcome reconciles by step 5's Lookup(effect_key); a Reserve is never
            undone
retry       the same action, through a fresh MCP session too, returns the recorded outcome or completes an
            uncertain one under its effect_key; a different action never takes a reserved use; an uncertain
            use stays consumed
cancel      an approver signs ApprovalCancel{approval_id}, delivered like a decision; the daemon appends
            Cancel; for a server-gated decision, POST /approval/cancel {the cancel, the decision} inserts each
            use_index in 0 .. uses-1 that no row holds, state cancelled, effect_key and result NULL and the
            decision's not_after, each ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a racing gate's insert conflicts on the
            primary key, finds no use left and answers 409 SPENT by step 2, and many cancelled rows fit
            UNIQUE (approval_id, effect_key), since Postgres takes NULLs as distinct; a local reservation
            made before the cancel still completes, a server-gated one only if its gate committed first
expiry      a local use is reserved until not_after and completes until not_after + 10 min; a server-gated
            use is reserved until not_after - 60 s, a first presentation past not_after (server time) is
            refused, and a replay gets its stored result while the row lasts; past these, a retry only reconciles
retention   approval files 30 d after not_after; approval_use rows 1 d after their not_after, which
            taskworker's hourly sweep deletes, never reading create_time (§2.8 api-10)
AU1  for every approval, effects <= uses, counted at each step 5 component (outbox objects, approval_use
     rows, grant_ids, bridge rule ids, evs versions, alias records, restores)
AU2  every effect has a durable Reserve or approval_use row, committed before it or in its transaction
AU3  no crash or lost response frees a use; an uncertain use is completed or reported, never spent by
     another action
AU4  a retry of the same action returns the original outcome
```

**Prompt injection.**
- **Content is data.** Mail, files, other writers' entries, search hits and outside tool output return only as tagged structured output, which go-sdk also renders as one `TextContent` (Content left nil), in fields tagged `trust` (`own`, `member`, `untrusted`) and `source`, between fixed `BEGIN/END UNTRUSTED DATA` markers inside the strings; instructions and tool descriptions are constants. Search hits carry `trust` and `source` per hit, and an untrusted hit's text returns only on request (16.10).
- **Taint (I-9).** Taint, triggered as below, lasts the run, persisted before untrusted data reaches the agent and across restarts (D-MCP-16); each O action, and mail to approved outside recipients, whose records a tainted run ignores (§15.10), then needs a fresh decision, one on a request the run filed tainted (TS1). Harness-native egress stays outside the gate but in the record.
- **Secrets (I-7).** Results matching the daemon's credentials are refused; errors never echo input matching a secret rule.

```text
taint       once the run reads untrusted data through ur (outside mail, files from outside or a tainted run, a
            version's trust read from its push's sealed provenance, its tainted bit, signer and import label, and
            every version untrusted where that provenance cannot be read (owner decisions 245, 470), flagged
            entries, untrusted search hits' text, 16.10, the team directory's announcement, request and decision
            prose, 16.11), by MCP or by a ur command whose process ancestry binds it to the run (16.7), or a hook
            reports a web tool (WebFetch, WebSearch, curl), and while hook coverage lapses: no hook event bound
            it, none came within 60 s of a tool call, or a harness config hash changed (checked at SessionStart
            and every 5 min)
run file    <state>/net/<network_id>/runs/<run_id>, file class run (§5.9): {run_id, harness,
            harness_process (pid and start time; local, never shown), session_ids[], worktree, tainted,
            taint_reasons[], gaps[], first_seq, last_seq}
write-ahead tainted = true is fsynced before the daemon returns untrusted data to the agent or acks a hook
            reporting a web tool; if that write fails, the call fails
rejoin      after a daemon or relay restart a session rejoins its run by (harness, session_id) at the next
            hook event; until one binds it, it is unbound and so tainted; a missing or unreadable run file
            means tainted; every session or event under a harness process binds to the union of that
            process's runs, ended ones included, so a new run there starts with their taint, fsynced, until
            the process exits; only a SessionStart reporting a fresh start opens a new run, a session with no
            live harness ancestor binds nothing and reads tainted, and SessionEnd clears nothing (owner
            decision 448)
monotone    tainted never returns to false within a run; a new run starts untainted unless a run of its
            harness process is tainted
retention   until the run's Coverage entry is sealed, then 30 days, for restore (16.7)
TS1         once a run is tainted, no outward action in it passes the gate on a standing grant, an approved
            recipient or a decision whose request was untainted, across any restart; a use reserved before
            the taint only completes (spend step 2)
```

**Identity (X10)** follows §5.5 and §5.8: in-daemon agents are `agent_asserted` labels behind the uid-checked socket, inside the trust boundary ([owner decision 47](#od-47); D-CORE-4).

### 16.7 Harness integration, ingest and restore
