`ur install-harness <claude-code|codex|cursor> [--agent <n>] [--instance <i>] [--project]` shows a diff, then writes the MCP entry, the O-tool ask rule and the hooks (absolute path, §4.10), sealing a hash of `ur`'s entries in each file for 16.6's check (below); `--project` writes the committed files cloud sessions load, and §5.8's `.ur`. While a Team's `ServiceSettings.record_required` is set (§7.9; [owner decision 305](#od-305)), `ur install-harness` writes `onFailure: block` (Claude Code) and `failClosed: true` (Cursor) on every `ur hook` entry, adds `--required` to the hook command and seals that form; `ur hook --required` exits 2 when the daemon cannot take the event, because the hook otherwise exits 0 and neither setting would ever fire. The config-hash check counts a fail-open form as a changed config, so such a run taints, and `ur status` names each fail-closed harness. Codex documents no fail-closed setting, so there `--required`'s exit 2 blocks a PreToolUse only while the hook runs, and `ur status` says so. Enforcement stops at a member's own daemon: a same-uid edit taints but cannot be prevented.

**The config hash.** The adapter extracts only what `ur` wrote: Claude Code's `mcpServers.ur` in `~/.claude.json` (`.mcp.json` with `--project`) and, in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/settings.json` with `--project`), each `permissions.ask` rule and each hook entry whose command is this `ur`'s absolute path; Codex's `[mcp_servers.ur]` with its per-tool `approval_mode` in `~/.codex/config.toml`, and `ur`'s entries in `~/.codex/hooks.json`; Cursor's `mcpServers.ur` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and `ur`'s entries in `~/.cursor/hooks.json`. Each set is rendered as RFC 8785 canonical JSON (TOML parsed to the same form) and hashed with SHA-256, and the harness config hash, RECORD.md's `config_sha256`, is SHA-256 over the per-file hashes in that order, one rule for every file. The sealed value comes from `ur`'s own template at install, never from the file as found, so re-running `ur install-harness` restores entries and cannot bless a widened rule. The check at SessionStart and every 5 min compares a fresh extract, and also counts as changed any other entry that can answer for a `ur` tool: a hook on PermissionRequest, PreToolUse or `beforeMCPExecution` whose matcher covers the `ur` server, or a `permissions.allow` rule naming it, in those files and, at SessionStart, in the project settings files of the session's working directory. An edit elsewhere in a file changes nothing.

**The harness config** (sidecar/design/mocks/recurd-app.html:986-1009), with per-agent overrides, is one file, `harness/config.json`, on the `main` file-mode ref of the member's vault in each network: UTF-8 JSON, one object, `"version": 1`, at most 64 KiB, unknown keys kept verbatim on rewrite and ignored with a warning in `ur status`. A missing file means defaults, an unparsable file or an unknown version means defaults and a `config_unreadable` coverage gap, and a sidecar that cannot read the vault (tagged, cloud) uses defaults. It holds no hook, ask rule or MCP entry: those come only from `ur install-harness`'s own template, and no synced change rewrites a harness file or re-seals a hash. Two keys act ([owner decision 452](#od-452)): `record.redact.pii`, `off` or `hash`, default `hash`, from M3 (Redact before seal, below), and `claims`, `{"default": auto|prompt|off, "projects": {<project key>: value}}`, from M6, which `ur directory runs` and `SetRuns` write per member and project and CORE-M6-02 reads at a session's start under D-CORE-18's rule (16.11), a tagged sidecar, which reads no vault, taking the team default and `.ur`; `agents.<label>` overrides those two keys only. `record.capture` is kept and ignored, capture staying this section's fixed set, since a narrowing control weakens R-MCP-4 and needs a person-only surface first; `reach`, `models` and `identity` are kept, ignored and warned about, so a `reach:` block files no request until [a later design](DESIGN-DEFER.md#mcp-harness-config-keys) (§8.5). A value applies at each run's next SessionStart and is fixed for that session: a narrower one at once, a wider one (`pii` from `hash` to `off`, a wider `claims`) only after the member confirms on `/dev/tty` or in an app, never through MCP, and the next run's Coverage names the change.

**Model calls** ([owner decision 463](#od-463)). A Codex run's come from its PostModelRequest hook alone, one `model_call` entry a call with its request id and token counts, and `ur install-harness` writes no `[otel]` table for Codex, removing one an earlier install wrote. A Claude Code run's come from its OpenTelemetry export: `ur install-harness` draws 32 random bytes per install and seals them under `<state>/harness/` beside the template's seal, writes them into Claude Code's `env` block as `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` with an endpoint naming the loopback port it chose and sealed with them, and a re-install restores both; the daemon's receiver (`mcp.IngestTelemetry`) accepts that token, compared in constant time, for `model_call` entries alone, labeled source hook, refuses anything else 401 with nothing recorded, and passes over any record whose resource names Codex. Cursor documents no exporter. The token only adds the harness's own reports, which any same-uid process can already add through `ur hook` (owner decisions [47](#od-47), [75](#od-75)), so I-7, which keeps out credentials that administer, read or sign, admits it (§2.9).

| Harness | MCP entry; O-tool ask rule | Hooks (`ur hook <harness>`) | Transcript |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --scope user ur` (`.mcp.json` with `--project`); `permissions.ask` | SessionStart to SessionEnd (1.5 s there), PermissionRequest; fail open unless `onFailure: block` (v2.1.295+), which a Team's `record_required` writes; its OpenTelemetry exporter to the daemon's loopback receiver (model calls, above) | `transcript_path` JSONL |
| Codex | `[mcp_servers.ur]` in `~/.codex/config.toml`; per-tool `approval_mode` | `~/.codex/hooks.json`, trusted by hash; PermissionRequest; PreToolUse and PostToolUse for shell, `apply_patch` and MCP; PostModelRequest (model calls, above); SessionEnd 1 s; no fail-closed setting, so under `record_required` only `--required`'s exit 2 blocks | `transcript_path` |
| Cursor | `mcpServers.ur` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`; `beforeMCPExecution` answers `ask` | `~/.cursor/hooks.json` v1: that hook, afterShellExecution, afterMCPExecution, afterFileEdit; `failClosed: true` under `record_required` | `transcript_path`, null if disabled |

Sources (2026-11-03; edit payloads and `session_title` re-read 2026-11-05): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks.md, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli, https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks, https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp.

| Ingested | Captured from | Stored (§10 domain) |
|---|---|---|
| Transcript | `transcript_path`, tailed at Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, SessionEnd and every 30 s | author vault, per run |
| Tool calls | the PostToolUse family; the daemon's own MCP calls | vault |
| Model calls | Codex's PostModelRequest hook; Claude Code's OpenTelemetry export (above) | vault, one `model_call` entry a call |
| Diffs, restore point | the restore point and ledger of D-MCP-15 (HEAD plus dirty-file copies, per-path before and after hashes), rescanned at each hook; file events in v1 | vault, one evs push per tree, multi-part when large (§11.8); a `change` entry with hashes in the team record |
| Context | SessionStart, InstructionsLoaded, model, harness version, `permission_mode`; the run's redacted user prompts (UserPromptSubmit) as they arrive | `context` entries, the prompts in a stage-2 entry's `ContextBody.prompts` ([owner decision 467](#od-467)), so a run card reads them from the record; instruction files by hash |
| Run title, run card | Claude Code's `session_title` at SessionStart or UserPromptSubmit when set (`--name`, `/rename`), else the run's first user prompt; tool names, touched paths and times from the rows above | the run card in the vault's index, and in the team record's from its own entries (16.10) |
| Run announcement | SessionStart's title, project and branch (team networks, `claims` auto; 16.11) | the team directory (an `announce` entry at M6, the card from M10); nothing else from the session (I-20) |
| Approvals | PermissionRequest events, permission modes, I-8 decisions | team record (single-member networks: vault) |

- **How.** `ur hook` passes its stdin to the daemon (hello mode `hook`) and exits 0 within 300 ms, with two exceptions: a PreToolUse waits until the daemon holds the paths it names (else their before is unknown, below), and, on a host holding M's presence key, a PermissionRequest (Cursor: `beforeMCPExecution`) for an O tool waits until the presence prompt ends, at most `Ingest.PresencePromptTimeout` (60 s): the key signed, allow (`decision.behavior: allow`; Cursor `permission: allow`); the person refused, deny; the bound reached or no prompt available, no decision (Claude Code and Codex exit 0 with no output, the normal flow; Cursor `permission: ask`), the O call then returning pending for `ur approve`; nothing is signed on a refusal or a timeout. `ur install-harness` writes `timeout: 75` on those hook entries, since Claude Code and Codex default to 600 s and Cursor states only a platform default, and EXT-1 checks that an allow suppresses the harness's own prompt under `permissions.ask`, which Claude Code still evaluates: should a prompt still show, the person sees two and the key alone counts. Events bind to a run by (harness, `session_id`), and an MCP session joins it through the peer pids' ancestry.
- **Spool.** Capture spools locally, encrypted (1 GiB cap); a locked daemon seals to a spool public key (`crypto/hpke`, rotated at each unlock), so capture continues while locked.
- **Redact before seal.** A vendored gitleaks rule subset (MIT), PEM blocks, JWTs, the `urn_`, `ur-authkey-` (with any `#` bundle) and `ur_sk_` formats, and high-entropy assignments become `[REDACTED:<rule>:<8 hex of HMAC(local key, value)>]`; under the harness config's `record.redact.pii`, `hash` by default from M3, email addresses and E.164 phone numbers become that marker with rule `pii-email` or `pii-phone`, each a redaction in the run's Coverage; shared writes refuse on a match.
- **Limits** (settings): 1 MiB per hook payload or tool body; a control line at most `LocalSettings.RequestByteCount` (4 MiB, a 1 MiB body at up to 4x escaping), a longer one closing its session; files over 8 MiB by hash and size; 256 MiB per run-hour; vault bytes count toward storage (§20). Every cut, missed event, changed config or event lost with a closed session is a coverage gap.

**Restore (D-MCP-8, D-MCP-15).** `run_restore` runs on the worktree's device from its local restore point, never the vault's redacted copy, so it needs no network:

```text
point       <state>/net/<network_id>/restore/<run_id>/, file class restore (§5.9), at most 256 MiB a run
  base      HEAD's commit id, plus an exact sealed copy of every file differing from HEAD at run start
            (modified, staged or untracked; .gitignore honored), found through git's stat cache; clean files
            restore from HEAD's blobs; files over the cap are hash-only
  start_ns  the baseline walk's start; a file whose ctime (Windows: ChangeTime) is later than start_ns when
            the walk reaches it has an unknown base (not exact)
  ledger    per path, a chain of observations: edit{run, hook event hash, before_sha256, after_sha256},
            hashed at the file-edit hook at once; scan{interval, before_sha256, after_sha256, attribution}
  before    an edit's before_sha256, known only from bytes the edit is checked against: Claude Code and
            Codex hold, sealed in the point, each path a call names from its PreToolUse to the PostToolUse
            with its tool_use_id (at most 10 min and 8 MiB a file), keeping their hash only if the call's
            input re-applied to them gives the after bytes (Edit's old_string, new_string and replace_all,
            matched exactly; Write's content; apply_patch's patch in tool_input.command; NotebookEdit's
            cell, the parsed cells equal outside it); Cursor, needing no pre-edit event, reverses
            afterFileEdit's edits on the after bytes, last first, each new_string found exactly once;
            otherwise unknown
attribution of a change a scan finds in interval i
  edit      file-edit hooks of this run in i name the path (Claude Code Edit, Write, NotebookEdit; Codex
            apply_patch's paths; Cursor afterFileEdit), their before and after hashes chain from the scan's
            before_sha256 to its after_sha256, and no other run on this worktree named the path in i; an
            edit whose before is unknown counts as a non-path tool
  shell     this run ran a shell or other non-path tool in i, and no other run on this worktree had any tool
            activity in i
  foreign   anything else: another run active in i, no activity of this run in i, a coverage gap (the
            interval spanning a daemon restart included)
restorable(R, p) = every change of p since base is edit-attributed to R, the chain is unbroken (each before
            equals the previous after, the first the base), base(p) is exact (not redacted from local data,
            not hash-only, not changed during the walk), and the current bytes equal R's last after_sha256
dry_run     the restorable paths, and every other changed path with its reason (foreign, shell, chain-broken,
            changed-since, not-exact, dropped), plus a preview_id binding the (path, current kind and hash,
            target kind, mode and hash) set, a kind being absent, file or symlink
apply       requires that preview_id; the worktree's apply lock orders only restores, since editors, shells and
            other harnesses never take it, so apply checks the bytes it displaces, never an earlier read; per
            path, in preview order, journaling each step in the point before taking it:
  resolve   p through Go's os.Root on the worktree (https://pkg.go.dev/os#Root; Go 1.24, its Rename and Link
            from 1.25), so no symlink or .. leads outside it, creating missing parents
  stage     the target (bytes and executable bit; a symlink as a link, or, where core.symlinks is false, its
            text, as git writes it) under a fresh hidden name in p's directory, fsynced, its hash equal to the
            target's, else not-exact; a volume taking neither a no-replace rename nor a hard link of it is
            unsupported before anything moves
  aside     when the preview found p: p renamed to a fresh hidden name beside it, which moves whatever p holds
            at that instant, and those bytes hashed against the preview's current kind and hash; p is then
            absent until install or back
  install   on a match, or when the preview found p absent: the staged name renamed to p only while no p exists,
            by renameat2's RENAME_NOREPLACE (Linux), renameatx_np's RENAME_EXCL (macOS) or MoveFileExW without
            MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING (Windows), else Go's Root.Link and the staged name's removal; a target of
            absent installs nothing, and a p reappearing before end makes it recreated
  back      on a mismatch: the moved bytes renamed back to p the same way, keeping their inode, so a writer
            holding p open still writes to p; where only a hard link serves, a moved directory goes back by a
            plain rename, which replaces no file and no non-empty directory
  end       after the last path: moved-aside bytes hashed again, deleted if still the preview's current ones,
            else kept, the path then written
  copies    a conflict keeps the staged target beside p as <name>.ur-restored-<h> and any kept moved bytes as
            <name>.ur-conflict-<h>, h being run_id's first 8 hex, -2 and on when taken: each renamed with its
            inode, never over an existing name; unsupported and error remove the staged name instead
  conflict  changed (put back); recreated (p reappeared before install or back: p kept, and moved bytes other
            than the preview's current ones kept); deleted (p gone, the preview having found it); exists (p
            present, the preview having found none); in-use (Windows: p open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE); kind (p
            or a parent is now a directory, symlink, mount point or other kind, or p's on-disk name differs in
            case); unsupported; written (moved-aside bytes changed before end, through a handle opened earlier:
            kept); error (an I/O or permission error, p as it was); run_restore names each copy
  restart   a path journaled aside but neither installed nor back goes back the same way, or, p having
            reappeared, becomes recreated; a finished path's moved-aside bytes take end's rule; other staged
            names are removed
worktrees   one nothing else writes during apply (an agent's under its own OS user, container or VM, §5.5, its
            run ended) never conflicts; in a shared live one a concurrent write makes a conflict, never an
            overwrite, except a write through a handle opened before apply that lands after its end, which
            reaches the deleted moved-aside file, as under git checkout
shell paths restored only when named in paths after a dry run, as an O action (a decision in any run)
never       foreign paths; a path whose bytes changed since the preview; a redaction marker; a path whose
            needed version is dropped (§11.7; its local copies deleted with it, D-CORE-19), a conflict dropped,
            never partly restored (FI-8)
RV1  restore writes only paths whose every change since base is this run's attributed edit, verified at apply on
     the bytes it moves aside, and, on a conflict, copies beside them under new names
RV2  restore writes exact original bytes or nothing
RV3  a preview never authorizes bytes that changed after it
RV4  restore discards no bytes but the preview's current ones: other bytes it moves aside go back to their path
     or stay beside it as a conflict copy, and the path reports a conflict
```

A tainted run's restore also needs a decision, and it appends a `restore` entry.

### 16.8 Record primitives (X20)

Readers and depositors follow §8.5's kind defaults and `audit` block, ahead of any policy.

| Log (§11.12 kind) | Readers | Writers | Mirror |
|---|---|---|---|
| Author vault (`vault`, owner-bound; one per member: the first consented, not read_only device with an entry to write files RepoCreate, and the member's live vault with the lowest log position is the vault, a device whose own empty repo lost filing RepoDelete{now} for it, §11.12) | the author's consented devices (§8.5); `EvsShare` recipients (§8.8) | those devices; the author's other untagged sidecars and sponsored tagged ones deposit | the author's consented indexer (§3.6) |
| Coordination log: in a team network the team directory (`directory`, 16.11); a personal network uses the vault for every kind | every admitted sidecar of the team ([owner decision 171](#od-171)) | every admitted sidecar that is not read_only, its own paths and stream | a directory admin's indexer |
| Other ledgers (`record`) | members per §8, and the agents a grant names, through wraps ([owner decision 114](#od-114)) | members' sidecars and agents granted write; other tagged sidecars deposit; where a log admin's `ledger_scope` entry (RECORD.md's kind 43) names the repos and projects a ledger covers, each sidecar with write on it copies there each of those runs' entries bound for the team record, its projection, never a vault body, with no tool change and no agent choosing a log, and `ur status` names each `record` log a daemon copies to ([owner decision 454](#od-454)) | an admin's indexer |
| Team record (`team_record`) | admins' and auditors' devices | members' and tagged sidecars deposit; authors keep copies | an admin's or auditor's indexer |

A mirror exists once such an indexer is designated; a network has none by default, and `ur status` names each unmirrored log ([owner decision 177](#od-177)).

```proto
// sidecar/protocol/record.proto; frozen at M3's entry review (D-MCP-6). Frozen means wire-stable: numbers and
// meanings never change, versions add fields; every hash and signature covers stored bytes. Every field of an
// entry is sealed: each RecordEntry is a file in its writer's stream (§11.8), and evs sees only §2.8's evs rows; a
// CanonicalAction bound for a GrantActivate or a gate sets only what the freeze block's server row lists. The leaf
// hash SHA-256(0x00 || Signed.body) (RFC 9162) admits M6's verifiable log (16.18). §6.11 SignedType: 0x1801
// SIGNED_RECORD_HEADER, 0x1802 SIGNED_APPROVAL_DECISION, 0x1803 SIGNED_APPROVAL_CANCEL, 0x1804
// SIGNED_RETENTION_POLICY.
message RecordHeader {
  bytes entry_id = 1; bytes log_id = 2;     // random; repo id
  bytes writer_sidecar_id = 3; uint64 seq = 4; bytes prev_sha256 = 5;  // per-writer chain
  bytes agent_id = 6; bytes run_id = 7; bytes action_id = 8;
  uint32 kind = 9;   // RECORD.md's v1 registry; unknown kinds are kept and shown generically: coordination
                     // log: claim, handoff, ask, answer, check, note, and, in the team directory, announce,
                     // request, decision and erasure_request (claims and handoffs there are state of a run's
                     // announcement, 16.11). Team record: context, change, approval, route, publish, reach,
                     // membership, key, coverage, cost (while ServiceSettings.record_cost is on; owner
                     // decision 302), read, erasure, restore, inventory. Vault: raw content and read
                     // receipts, plus every kind in a personal network.
                     // membership and key entries mirror §5's SidecarEvents, admission alarms included,
                     // into each affected log; a member's own device revocation's names its approval
                     // evidence, presence with its assertion or a confirmation (§5.6).
  int64 time_millis = 10;
  uint32 source = 11;      // observed (the daemon did or saw it), hook (any same-user process can fake it),
                           // agent, approver
  bool tainted = 12;
  bytes body_commitment = 13;               // SHA-256("urnetwork-sidecar-v1/record-body" || salt || body)
  repeated ContentRef content = 14;
  uint64 policy_version = 15; bytes grant_id = 16;
  uint32 agent_source = 17;                 // agent_asserted, or isolated (own OS user, container or VM; §5.5)
}
message ContentRef { bytes repo_id = 1; bytes object_id = 2; bytes commitment = 3; }  // salt in the object's slot
message RecordEntry {                       // header: §6 Signed, purpose record-entry
  Signed header = 1; bytes sealed_body = 2;
  bytes key_slot_id = 3;                    // with key_index, the body key's slot object and index (Erasure)
  uint32 version = 4;                       // 1
  uint32 key_index = 5;
}
// The writer's identity key signs the header; from v1 an agent subkey may sign inside the body (§5.5).

message CanonicalAction {                   // built by the daemon; hashed as stored; approvers render only these
  uint32 kind = 1;                          // §5.4 SidecarActionKind, or restore (16.7)
  repeated string recipients = 2;           // to, cc and bcc
  bytes body_sha256 = 3; string preview = 4;  // preview <= 2 KiB, rendered as untrusted text
  string host = 5; uint32 port = 6; uint32 audience = 7; int64 expires_millis = 8;
  repeated string cidrs = 9; repeated string grant_dst = 10; repeated string grant_allow = 11;
                                            // a sock: entry in grant_dst is §9.4's token path in hex, never an
                                            // application name, since GrantActivate shows api the action (§8.8);
                                            // in versions 3 and 4 the clear grant_dst names destinations with no
                                            // port or prefix text, sealed_detail's holding that: a worker
                                            // target's is one sidecar:<32 lowercase hex id>:tcp:<port> a port,
                                            // ascending, no duplicates, grant_allow ["dial"], target_port that
                                            // port when there is one, else 0, and any other refused (16.11)
  uint32 version = 12;                      // 1; 2 with field 37; 3 for kind access_request (16.11), in fields 8,
                                            // 10, 11, 14, 26, 29 and 38; 4 for a dial or route grant, in fields 8,
                                            // 10, 11, 28, 29 and 38, a share's also 40 (owner decisions 220,
                                            // 457); approvers that do not know a version refuse it
  bool scope = 13;                          // a multi-use template (16.6), which an agent asks for only through
                                            // mail_send's uses (owner decision 613)
  bytes repo_id = 14; string path = 15; bytes content_sha256 = 16; uint64 base_version = 17;  // O-tier evs_write,
                                                        // evs_delete; mail_alias_delete's mailcfg record (16.6)
  string dns_name = 18; string dns_type = 19; string dns_value = 20; uint32 dns_ttl = 21;     // dns_set, dns_delete
  string alias = 22;                                                     // mail_alias_*; mail_send's from_alias
  reserved 23, 24, 25, 34;                  // socket_name, local_port, weight, alpn: ApprovalRequest's 17 and 14
                                            // to 16, daemon-built (owner decision 457)
  bytes target_sidecar_id = 26; uint32 target_port = 27;                                     // bridge_expose
  bytes rule_id = 28; bytes subject = 29;                // a grant (§8.8), with 8, 10 and 11; a publish's also 33, 35
  bytes restore_run_id = 30; repeated string restore_paths = 31; bytes restore_preview_id = 32; // run_restore
  uint32 app_mode = 33; bytes link_spki_sha256 = 35;                                         // tls_publish (§13.7)
  string alias_group = 36;                                                   // mail_alias_create's group (§15.8)
  uint32 versioning = 37;                   // O-tier evs_write: its version's setting, 0 on, 1 off (§11.7); set
                                            // only in version 2, which approvers that do not know it refuse
  bytes sealed_detail = 38;                 // versions 3 and 4: a CanonicalActionDetail{cidrs, target_port,
                                            // grant_dst} in §7.9's sealed-body format, the prefixes and ports,
                                            // which approvers and readers open and no server does; its aad's
                                            // SignedType is SIGNED_GRANT_ACTIVATE and network the action's, and
                                            // in a header nonce's place the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 over this
                                            // action as stored with field 38 left out, so it opens only beside
                                            // the clear fields it was sealed with (owner decisions 220, 457)
  uint32 egress_mode = 39;                  // egress_change: BridgeEgressMode, beside its subject (29) and,
                                            // under exits, its exits in grant_dst (sidecar:<id> entries or one
                                            // tag entry); version 1, on no server path (owner decision 462)
  bytes share_network_id = 40;              // a share's grant (§8.11): the other network, 16 bytes, on a dial or
                                            // route grant alone, beside its subject, the requesting sidecar; an
                                            // admin's approval covers it as it covers every field (§8.8; owner
                                            // decision 346)
  bool require_default_egress = 41;         // egress_change under exits alone: the subject's devices keep default
                                            // egress on, as its BridgeEgressBody seals (§17.11), optional in kind
                                            // 5 and required by no template, rendered as its own clause, "and
                                            // require its devices to keep default egress on"; refused under auto
                                            // or none and on any other kind, version 1, on no server path; an
                                            // approver that cannot name it refuses the action (owner decision 607);
                                            // a template binds it set or empty, so one that leaves it empty covers
                                            // only uses that leave it unset (16.6; owner decision 614)
}
// Rendering (D-MCP-17): approver devices render only these daemon-built fields as the action, with the
// request's daemon-built 14 to 17 and an opened sealed_detail, and ApprovalRequest.summary and preview as
// untrusted text, so an agent cannot carry trusted rdata, an alias or a path in prose.
message ApprovalRequest {                   // body of an approval entry
  bytes approval_id = 1; bytes action_id = 2; bytes run_id = 3; bytes agent_id = 4;
  bytes canonical_action = 5; bytes payload_sha256 = 6;  // SHA-256(canonical_action as stored)
  string summary = 7;                       // agent text, shown as untrusted
  uint32 risk = 8;                          // SidecarRisk: 1 normal for every action (owner decision 279)
  bytes requester_sidecar_id = 9; bool tainted = 10; repeated bytes approvers = 11; int64 not_after_millis = 12;
  uint32 version = 13;                      // 1, or 2, which adds uses (18) and always sets it; an approver
                                            // that does not know a version refuses it (owner decision 574)
  uint32 local_port = 14; int32 weight = 15; repeated string alpn = 16;  // daemon-built and rendered by
                                            // approvers, under request_sha256: the local port a socket_listen,
                                            // tls_publish, bridge_forward or bridge_expose binds, a listen's
                                            // weight and a publish's ALPNs (owner decision 457)
  string socket_name = 17;                  // a socket_listen's name, which agrees with its action's one sock:
                                            // entry in grant_dst; no server sees it (owner decision 457)
  uint32 uses = 18;                         // version 2's: how many distinct actions the agent asks the
                                            // approval to cover, daemon-built and rendered, 2 or more for a
                                            // template (scope = true), 1 for any other action, never 0; signed
                                            // as ApprovalDecision.uses, or for a template a smaller count of 2
                                            // or more, never a larger one; a version-1 request sets none
                                            // (16.6's multi-use row; owner decision 574)
}
message ApprovalDecision {                  // inside §6 Signed, purpose approval; holds no run or agent id
  bytes approval_id = 1;
  bytes request_sha256 = 2;                 // SHA-256(ApprovalRequest as stored): binds run_id, agent_id,
                                            // approvers, expiry
  bytes payload_sha256 = 3;                 // SHA-256(CanonicalAction as stored), never a re-encoding
  uint32 decision = 4; uint32 uses = 5; int64 not_after_millis = 6;  // at most uses distinct actions, each
                                                                     // once (D-MCP-11); uses > 1 only with a
                                                                     // scope = true template (16.6)
  bytes approver_member_id = 7;
  uint32 channel = 8;                       // evidence: device, presence or harness (owner decision 75)
  bytes sshsig = 9;                         // reserved: ignored, never trusted (owner decision 279)
  bytes evidence_sha256 = 10;               // harness: the matched hook event, which stays in the record;
                                            // device and presence: empty, a presence decision's assertion
                                            // riding in Signed.webauthn
  bytes requester_sidecar_id = 11;          // the only sidecar that may spend it (16.6)
  AuthPin auth_pin = 12;                    // §7.9's pin the approver evaluated the request under
  uint32 version = 13;                      // 1
}
message ApprovalCancel { bytes approval_id = 1; }  // inside §6 Signed, purpose approval (16.6's ledger)
message ReachReceipt {                      // coalesced per (grant, peer) per 5 min, and a TLS front's publish
                                            // receipts per server name too
  bytes grant_id = 1; uint64 policy_version = 2; uint32 kind = 3; bytes owner = 4; bytes approver = 5;
  int64 window_start_millis = 6; repeated bytes peers = 7; uint64 stream_count = 8; uint64 byte_count = 9;
  repeated string relays = 10;              // host, IP and operator of each relay or edge in the path
  string server_name = 11;                  // the name the visitor asked for, the TLS SNI, which only the TLS
                                            // front's publish receipts set; never a relay (owner decision 465)
}
message Coverage {                          // at run end, or after 10 min idle without SessionEnd
  bytes run_id = 1; string harness = 2; string version = 3; repeated string sources = 4;
  repeated string gaps = 5;  // hook failures, missed events, changed configs, downtime, truncation,
                             // oversize, bypass modes, redactions
  uint64 first_seq = 6; uint64 last_seq = 7;
}
message RetentionPolicy {                   // Signed (purpose record-entry) by the log's admin
  bytes log_id = 1; uint32 class = 2;       // a kind class, announce among them (keep_days 30, 16.11, its
                                            // entries' expiry only, owner decision 660)
  uint32 keep_days = 3; uint32 searchable_days = 4; bool archive = 5;
}
// The values row's four enums (what freezes, below), whose values CanonicalAction.kind, ApprovalRequest.risk and
// ApprovalDecision.decision and channel carry as uint32
enum SidecarActionKind {                    // §5.4's order, new kinds appending
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_PUBLISH = 1; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_LISTEN = 2; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_FORWARD = 3;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_EXPOSE = 4; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_EGRESS_CHANGE = 5; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_INVITE = 6;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_SHARE = 7; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_ALIAS_CREATE = 8; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_ALIAS_DELETE = 9;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_AGENT_CONFIG_WRITE = 10; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_AGENT_CONFIG_DELETE = 11;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_DNS_SET = 12; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_DNS_DELETE = 13; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_MAIL_SEND = 14;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_ACCESS_REQUEST = 15; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_PAYMENT = 16; SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_RESTORE = 17;
  SIDECAR_ACTION_KIND_MAIL_TLS_UNAUTHENTICATED = 18;   // §14.4's TL4 allowance (owner decision 436)
}
enum SidecarRisk { SIDECAR_RISK_UNSPECIFIED = 0; SIDECAR_RISK_NORMAL = 1; SIDECAR_RISK_HIGH = 2; }
enum ApprovalVerdict { APPROVAL_VERDICT_UNSPECIFIED = 0; APPROVAL_VERDICT_APPROVE = 1; APPROVAL_VERDICT_DENY = 2; }
enum ApprovalChannel {                      // ApprovalDecision.channel and AclRequestRule.evidence
  APPROVAL_CHANNEL_UNSPECIFIED = 0; APPROVAL_CHANNEL_DEVICE = 1; APPROVAL_CHANNEL_PRESENCE = 2;
  APPROVAL_CHANNEL_HARNESS = 3;
}
```

```text
what freezes (D-MCP-6)
bytes      the leaf hash covers Signed.body, the header's bytes exactly as stored; every hash and signature
           covers stored bytes, never a re-encoding, so readers keep unknown fields by keeping the bytes
kinds      RECORD.md's v1 registry; an unknown kind is kept, verified and shown generically, never refused
values     CanonicalAction.kind, ApprovalRequest.risk and ApprovalDecision.decision and channel stay uint32, and
           record.proto declares their four enums, each 0 UNSPECIFIED, written by no one: SidecarActionKind 1
           to 18 in §5.4's order, new kinds appending, 18 being §14.4's TL4 allowance (owner decision
           436); SidecarRisk 1 normal, 2 high; ApprovalVerdict
           (decision) 1 approve, 2 deny; ApprovalChannel (channel, and AclRequestRule.evidence) 1 device,
           2 presence, 3 harness, as RECORD.md section 6.2; audience and app_mode hold acl.proto's
           AclAudience and AclAppMode, a publish's action always writing the resolved non-zero value
           (members 1, http 1) and a gate mapping a request's 0 to 1 before it compares; an approver,
           spender or gate refuses 0 or an unknown value of any of these, the kinds row's "kept" covering
           RecordHeader.kind only; kinds 6, 7 and 16 have no O tool and no row in the kind table, so
           NewCanonicalAction refuses each until its owner names its fields; kind 5, egress_change, has its row,
           its subject, egress_mode 39, exits in grant_dst and require_default_egress 41, and a builder, but no O
           tool, since only a person's confirmed ur bridge egress files it (§17.11; owner decisions 462, 607, 614)
server     a CanonicalAction bound for a GrantActivate or a gate sets only kind, version, scope and the fields
           that path's gate sees: a grant 8, 10, 11, 28 and 29, version 4's also 38, sealed, and a share's
           40, a publish's also 5, 6, 7, 33 and 35; a version-3 access_request 8, 10, 11, 14, 26, 29 and 38;
           a dns_* action 8 and 18 to 21; api, every reader's GrantActivate check and each gate parse the
           stored bytes and refuse any other set field, so a socket_listen's grant carries only its grant_dst's
           sock: entry and an egress_change goes to no server; AD4 stands (16.6)
order      within one stream, (evs push version, position in the push), each push's entries sorted by
           (writer, seq); across a log's streams RECORD.md's verifiable log (M6) appends in batches, batch by
           batch and, within one, streams by ref_id bytes, each checkpoint entry listing its frontier and
           leaves: no log-wide sequence and no format change, fixed with the envelope at M3's entry review
           (D-MCP-6)
disclosure body_commitment opens with (salt, body), which only key holders have until erasure; a client
           disclosure packet (RECORD.md, M6) carries both; erasure makes later disclosure impossible, by design;
           an Opening{header, salt, body, version} names in version the RecordEntry.version it was made from,
           absent reading 1, so its reader parses body as the kind's own message (1) or the AgentSignedBody
           holding it (2), never inferring it from how bytes parse, the version being the opener's unsigned
           word (owner decision 466); ur record open writes, and ur record disclose --content reads, a
           DisclosureOpenings{version, log_id, openings, keys, purpose} file, which no reader can take for a
           DisclosurePacket, the vault's disclosure entry of act 2 recording its SHA-256 as packet_sha256
           (owner decision 456)
semantics  DESIGN.md's, which RECORD.md may not change: the logs' reader and writer matrix (§8.5's
           kind defaults), per-entry key slots, the source and tainted labels, and approvals bound by
           request_sha256 and payload_sha256
```

- **Storage (Q-ARCH-9 (a); [owner decision 2](#od-2)).** Entries are named by a stream's own counter n from 1, at `e/<n div 4,194,304>/<(n div 2,048) mod 2,048>/<n>`, each part decimal (RECORD.md section 5.2), 2,048 to a leaf directory and about 15 billion to a stream, n equal to seq in a stream that holds no ingested entry; a directory's name table (about 128 B a row: child token, kind, and a sealed name with its nonce and tag; up to 140 B while a path-epoch copy carries it with its `EvsName.epoch`) stays within 256 KiB, 280 KiB carried, inside §11.7's 4,096 children and 448 KiB of name table; per entry evs sees only a token path, padded size, key slot and push time, never record kinds, agents, runs or bodies. A push carries up to 64 entries or 1 s of them into the append-only stream, in one part, their keys 64 to a slot object (owner decisions [137](#od-137), [140](#od-140)), spilling inline bodies to segments (§11.8). Slot ids are random per push statement (§11.6): a retry of the same statement keeps them, and a push rebuilt after a refusal, such as a deposit re-wrapped to a newer drop key after 412 GATE_CLOSED, draws new ones; `key_slot_id` and `key_index` lie outside the signed header, so re-slotting re-signs no entry.
- **Chain.** `seq` and `prev_sha256` chain each writer's entries, so writers never contend and work offline. Readers verify chains after decrypting and pin each writer's head (I-16): a withheld or rewritten entry shows as a gap or a fork. Ingested deposits keep their writer's chain.
- **Erasure.** The body (paths, commands, recipients, text) is sealed under a per-entry key kept with its 256-bit salt in its own key slot ([owner decision 61](#od-61)), apart from the entry file's key; `key_slot_id` and `key_index` name it. An ERASE push naming that key (§11.12), which no backup holds ([owner decision 90](#od-90)), erases the body at once, under a preservation hold too ([owner decision 133](#od-133)), and needs no CLOSURE, so it goes first even at the storage limit; the eraser then reads the stream heads again and ERASEs any copy found now, and in a format-2 repo a CUT on the repo's `ur/index` then lists the entry and, through its epoch, the run card of each stream holding it, so every projection made before the CUT is listed, and none made after it can hold the entry, since a builder that reads a new epoch reads the log's erasure ref first and applies every ERASE on it before it folds (§11.12; [owner decision 460](#od-460)); the eraser folds each of those cards again in its own index head, and CLOSUREs rewrite in place the search-index files holding the entry's postings and the cards' listed versions (§11.14, 16.10), each followed by its ERASE of the old keys; where the rewrite finds no file holding a listed version (the index never indexed the entry's documents, the index is off, a listed card was never built, or the eraser's own re-entry push rewrote the only file in place under the same key), no ERASE with a key is left to say complete, and the eraser ends the erasure with a completion ERASE (§11.12's push row; [owner decision 658](#od-658)). Mail keeps its CUT first (§15.7). Should the eraser die between the ERASE and the CUT, another device resumes with the CUT (§11.12's reconcile row), and between the two a builder that holds the ERASE builds no card or entry document of that run. A log admin's daemon that ERASEs, under the same erasure, a copy ingested after it calls the CUT again for that copy, listing its documents and its stream's card ([owner decision 461](#od-461)). An erasure of a context entry lists that entry and its run's card; the run's other entry documents written before it keep the agent label and session ids it gave them (fields 9 and 11), and from its CUT on a builder takes them from the first context entry of the run its stream holds that no erasure names, which `ur record erase` says when it lists what it will destroy ([owner decision 460](#od-460)). On its hint, readers and mirrors delete the key, its slot copies and every decrypted copy of the body they hold (entry, search and `ur://record` caches), and refuse the key; copies an agent already took stay beyond recall (§11.12's residual). An `erasure` entry follows in the eraser's stream, retried while §11.13's limit refuses it (at the storage limit, or while spent); until it lands, the committed ERASE on the `erasure` ref records the erasure. Headers and chains still verify, since every eraser of the record names only body rows and deposit slots; an ERASE of an entry file's own key, which no record client sends, takes the header with the body, so the binding leaves that entry out, and its version once nothing else in it stands, and readers read the hole as a gap in its writer's chain, alarmed as any gap is and read past (RECORD.md 5.5; [owner decision 672](#od-672)).
- **Mirrors and site loss (D-MCP-10).** After a site loss, the table's designated mirrors (slot copies included; `ur status` reports one partial past 1 h behind, §11.13) and depositors' spools, each deposit kept until a CONSUME's consumed_through mark passes it (§11.12), re-upload signed entries verbatim (§19.10), so chains and pins verify; entries in neither are lost.
- **Approvals.** A request goes to a log its approver reads, copied to any team record: the member's vault; for a tagged sidecar, its sponsor's by deposit, or the team record while it has none (§7.10); for an admin, the team record. A phone learns of requests by a lease on each such log whole (§11.10), every push to it hinting the phone or, with the app closed, waking it (§18.7); should §22.8's wake counts on T4's surrogates show capture pushes spending the phones' wake budget, the review phase gives the vault a notice per pending request, as the directory has (D-SDK-28, 16.11's `q/` notices): the requester writes `a/<approval_id>` beside its request entry, a decision or cancel removes or rewrites it, phones lease that prefix alone, and a repair rule like the directory's covers a crash between the entry and the notice ([owner decision 573](#od-573)). A directory access request takes this route for its endorsement, then the directory's (16.11). A member's decision returns through that vault; admin approvals, and all for deposit-only requesters, activate requested grants once, as §8.8 `GrantActivate` deltas (D-ACL-7, D-MCP-12), which every admitted sidecar reads. A decision on any other action, or a cancel, for a requester that reads no vault (a tagged or ephemeral sidecar), and an admin's decision on a member's, return as an `ApprovalDelivery{header, requester_sidecar_id, sealed}`, a §7.9 delta with SignedType 0x1110 that the approver's device files after it signs, `sealed` being the Signed `ApprovalDecision` or `ApprovalCancel` HPKE-XWing to the requester's current ReaderKey (`gkm/rk/<sidecar_id>`, §10.5), so only the requester opens it; it counts against `config_statements_per_day`, shows api its signer, requester and size (§2.8's api-7) and authorizes nothing, since the requester still runs the spend check, and it serves 16.11's endorsement too, `filed_by` 3 keeping its meaning ([owner decision 447](#od-447)). Verifiers run 16.6's spend check against §7.9's admissions, §8.5's consent, `KeyRegister` records and pins (I-16). A person's statement about a change is no approval: an `attestation` entry (RECORD.md's kind 29), which `ur record attest` files on `/dev/tty` or in an app's UI, says one reviewed, tested or approved named commits, with an SSHSIG where the member holds a key; it sits outside the I-8 gate and is never called an approval ([owner decision 453](#od-453)).
- **Reach receipts** ([owner decision 25](#od-25)) come from the endpoint enforcing the grant: the listener for listens and publishes (§9 tickets, §13.7's front), the provider for forwards and routes (§17.9; sealed source subject, grant), §14.9's `SmtpSender` for sends and §15.7's ingest for received mail. The TLS front's receipt names the publishing sidecar as `owner`, leaves `approver` empty, carries in `server_name` the name the visitor asked for, the TLS SNI, publish receipts coalescing per (grant, peer, server name, window), so a visitor who reaches two aliases in a window gets two receipts and `relays` keeps R-MCP-7's meaning ([owner decision 465](#od-465)), takes as `grant_id` the lowest agreeing rule_id bytewise, the header's grant_id set only for a 32-byte activated grant's id, and as `policy_version` the config version the grant was read at; a stream counts when its first target connection opens and its TLS bytes, both ways, when it ends, in windows aligned to `ReachReceiptCoalesce` from the epoch (§13.7; [owner decision 431](#od-431)).
- **Retention.** Defaults: 400 days (90 searchable) for the team record, owner-set for the vault. Expiry erases entries as above, from the log admin's device; an admin BASE then re-lists the live set, removing only entries whose erasure is complete ([owner decision 461](#od-461)), keeping every push statement (§11.8's refs table), and the expired ciphertext stays, keyless, until a later GC, unscheduled (§11.13; [owner decision 246](#od-246)), which a preservation hold would pause as it pauses every server-side GC (§21.9; [owner decision 133](#od-133)). A team's own legal hold (Later) suspends expiry.
- **Search (16.10).** Each log's index holds only documents built from that log's own entries, for its own readers: its coordination entries and, in the vault and the team record, one run card per run and stream, registered as `run/` || run_id under its stream's ref_id (16.10; [owner decision 459](#od-459)); the directory's documents and fields are 16.11's. Each entry's header fields come from the verified entry, as §11.14's fields 6-15 for this class: 6 kind, 7 writer sidecar_id, 8 agent_id, 9 agent label, 10 run_id, 11 session ids, 12 tools, 13 claim expires, 14 claim state, 15 reserved; the title is field 4 and the text field 5. `searchable_days` masks older entries at query time; the team directory's index takes one, its cards ref and its ur/index alike: the coordination class's governing RetentionPolicy, which `ur admin directory --searchable` sets (16.11's settings row; [owner decision 660](#od-660)).
- **Reads by others (R-TRUST-7; owner decisions [63](#od-63), [126](#od-126)).** Beyond the author's consented devices, only `EvsShare` recipients and a Team's `audit` reader, which every member sees, read the vault, each first depositing a `read` entry to the repo's drop key under D-MCP-18's budget, before it decrypts any object the entry names, which the author's devices ingest and evs's request log (§2.8 evs-7) attests again; receipts are cooperative. A device admitted under the author without the author's consent, as by one admin alone, stays parked: it only deposits, and the author's devices alarm, until a consented device signs its `OwnerConfirm` as D-CORE-13 says, never through MCP.

```text
read receipt  from every reader of an owner-bound repo that is not its writer (EvsShare subjects, the Team
              audit reader), whose token carries repo:<id>:deposit for it (§7.8)
  entry       RecordHeader kind read, source observed, body {object ids (<= 64), purpose}, deposited to the
              repo's drop key (§10.5); the author's devices ingest it, keeping the depositor's chain, and
              refuse, consuming it unrecorded with an alarm, any other entry from a depositor §8.5 admits
              only for receipts (§11.12)
  order       deposit, await evs's 200, then decrypt the objects it names; the GETs run in parallel; re-reads
              of cached plaintext deposit nothing
  budget      4 KiB a deposit and 256 a day per repo, else 429 (§11.12)
  offline     a first read that cannot deposit is refused; an offline author costs nothing
```

### 16.9 server/mcp, remote MCP, and cloud agents

- **server/mcp stays separate (D-MCP-7).** URnetwork sees its inputs, so it serves public-web lookups only.
- **Cloud agents ([owner decision 49](#od-49)).** Claude Code cloud loads a repository's committed `.mcp.json` and hooks and proxies egress to allow-listed domains (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments). `ur` runs in the VM as a tagged, ephemeral sidecar holding its keys (§3.6), which its sandbox operator can also reach: the operator is inside the device boundary (§2.4). It is admitted by its auth key's Delegation, which it takes from a key file, never an environment variable ([owner decision 449](#od-449)): the environment's setup step writes the whole key string to a mode 0600 file, which the platform's snapshot keeps, and the `--project` cloud profile's committed SessionStart hook runs `ur connect --token-file <path> --ephemeral` before any other `ur` step, `ur` reading the file, enrolling, unlinking it and erasing its copy, so the key is gone from the running VM before the agent's first turn, and `ur` takes none from its environment (§5.6). The key is a Delegation key with `max_admits` above 1 and §10.5's 30-day cloud `not_after`, since every session starts from the same snapshot, a single-use key serving and preferred where a platform runs setup per session; and a cloud sidecar's keychain file (§5.6) lets a restored VM rejoin until its client is reaped, after which `ur` stays Unenrolled, capture spools and a new session enrolls. The residual: anyone who uses the environment can read the key in its setup text, every snapshot holds it, and a copy of the whole key admits fresh agents until the Delegation ends (§7.9's delegation row). It reaches the bringyour.com hosts §18.9 publishes over HTTP CONNECT (§4 C8). It reads the config, a team network's directory and its tags' repos at once by the Delegation's reader key, with no member device online ([owner decision 114](#od-114)), and deposits capture; its reap, or its own `not_after`, ends only what its own grants gave it, while the Delegation's reader key it holds reads on until that key drops (§10.5, which lists when). Other admitted readers, agents included, witness its pins; unwitnessed, it alarms at 24 h, and from `witness_bound_hours` (72 h by default) its shared-group writes stop and capture spools ([owner decision 129](#od-129); D-TRUST-10). Codex blocks agent-phase internet by default ([R:product](design/design-research/product.md) §5 item 9), so its daemon spools. Chat connectors run no process and get no sidecar tools.

### 16.10 Search

The daemon searches readable repos' encrypted indexes (§11.14; [owner decision 151](#od-151)) on the device for `ur search`, `ur agents` and three R tools, in one root-package engine (`search_*.go`, every leg, §5.4) that the sdk shares (§18.5). On daemon hosts, queries, hits and cursors never leave the device; an app host may ask a designated indexer (§11.14), whose daemon serves it from this engine outside every session. A search writes nothing to evs but the read receipts below, and index objects arrive by sync position, never by query (I-19; D-MCP-20).

```text
query       <= 512 B and 16 terms: the indexer checks the query as sent, NFC as typed, answering INVALID past
            them, and each engine applies them to the query after the index's own normalization (§11.14's
            normalizer 1), a wire-valid query that normalizes past them answering INVALID in the padded reply, so
            the phone falls back; each word or "quoted phrase" is a required substring term; a OR b; -term
            excludes only where this device confirms the term; field:text confines a term to one doc-table field
            (below); a term of 1-2 normalized bytes matches as a whole word through its space-padded trigrams;
            fuzzy asks for §11.14's near hits even where 3 or more exact hits exist (a desktop's local
            vocabulary, a phone's one-edit variants checked in the index); an empty query with filters lists; no
            regex in v1
scope       the breadth, §5.4's SearchBreadth (SearchBreadthRepo, SearchBreadthNetwork, SearchBreadthAll), apart
            from its SearchScope, which names partitions
            repo: the repos named (config display names, or id:<repo_id>), on the default ref or a named ref
            that has an index; network, the default: every repo of one network this sidecar reads by §8.6's
            local evaluation (D-ACL-14's RepoReaders), the team directory included (16.11), narrowed per agent
            (§5.5, §8.4), the network taken from the argument, .ur or the only one (§5.8); all: network scope in
            every network the daemon hosts (owner decision 23), each hit naming its network
excluded    secret repos, which search_status omits (16.6); config and mailcfg repos, which hold no index;
            repos this sidecar only deposits to; owner-bound repos of its own member where it is parked, listed
            as consent pending (owner decision 126); outside repo scope, refs whose index is off or unbuilt
            (owner decision 156), which a repo scope searches as §11.14 does without an index (this device's
            text scanned, else names and mail's i/ fields), coverage saying so; search_status gives every
            other exclusion's reason, and a repo this sidecar cannot read is never listed
owner-bound searched only by its readers: the owner's consented devices, EvsShare subjects and the audit reader
            (owner decisions 63, 126); a reader that is not a writer deposits a read receipt (purpose search,
            <= 64 index object ids) before it first decrypts those objects, and one before each hit it opens,
            under D-MCP-18's budget, and syncs such an index at most every Search.NonWriterSyncInterval (15
            min), so its receipts stay near 100 a day; a receipt that cannot land skips the repo, which coverage
            names
```

```text
sync        latest of every repo in scope is kept current from hints, coalesced on the leading edge: the first
            hint for a repo in a quiet Search.HintCoalesce interval (1 min) fetches at once, and later ones in it
            wait for its end; a search reads only the cache, never fetching for itself, and a version hinted but
            not yet fetched when a search starts counts as uncovered, so coverage reports it (FI-18; owner
            decision 450); all follows §18.4's device policy through §5.9's Search.AllPolicy (owner decision
            154); a repo followed only for search holds a lease on its index root (§11.10): the .ur-index/ token
            prefix of a file-mode ref, or its whole ur/index ref; a desktop syncs in the background, so a
            search's timing shows nothing, while an ephemeral sidecar's first sync of a repo shows when it first
            searched
phase 1     both latest buckets (owner decision 152), an expired one until its roll-up lands (owner decision
            157), a dropped one this device keeps until its cached all covers it (§5.9), and the local layer,
            the commits past indexed_through (§11.14's coverage) that this device indexed from its own
            plaintext (§5.9): answered at once
phase 2     all, at once where this device holds it current, a search of the cache reading all only while it is
            usable (§11.14's retained row; owner decision 393); with more, the owner's "search more", the daemon
            first fetches every all shard it lacks, whole, youngest first in a/m's fixed order, whatever the
            query matches, and searches each as it lands, under the cold contract (Targets, below; owner
            decisions 152, 154)
merge       §11.14's newest-wins rule over every partition searched and the local layer: per document key the
            highest version counts, tombstones and ref tombstones included, each candidate probed in §5.9's
            version table, and an ERASE masks its keys at once; entries past their log's searchable_days are
            masked (16.8); a since after all's newest time skips all
match       §11.14's states: confirmed by field (a doc-table field, or mail's i/ address or snippet, holds the
            query) or by text (this device's plaintext of the newest version does, §11.14's verified: its
            file-mode mirrors, §11.11's bare repository for git refs); possible, a trigram candidate this
            device cannot check; near, found through a corrected term, labeled with the correction; no body is
            fetched to verify (owner decision 155) but by the CLI's --verify fetch, which opens candidates as
            reads and says so; opening a possible hit checks it, dropping a false one from the cursor
rank        phase, then §11.14's tiers within it: confirmed hits newest first (or by path in file repos, header
            ahead of body), then possible hits by trigram overlap, fewest distinct trigrams first, then near
            hits; all's unmasked documents last changed before the oldest bucket phase 1 holds began, so every
            phase-2 hit is older than every phase-1 hit and a returned page is never revised; active agent
            groups lead phase 1
coverage    per repo: indexed_through against the ref's head, unindexed commits and whether the local layer
            covers them, latest's start, all's state (current, stale, absent, fetching n of m), index off or
            unbuilt: a gap is reported, never hidden
```

**Doc tables** are the index's display fields ([owner decision 155](#od-155)). Filters, header matches and possible hits use them without a body:

```text
mailbox     time, from, to (to and cc, §11.14's field 3), subject, outside; a snippet only from i/, where the
            device mirrors it (§15.7), never from the index
files       path, time, size, title (the first heading or line, 80 B), outside, tainted; the writer from the
            version's signed statement (§11.9)
records     entry_id or run_id, time, tainted, and §11.14's fields as 16.8 registers them, the title (4) at
            most 120 B, session ids (11) at most 4 and a run card's tools (12) at most 32 names; each field
            within §11.14's 256 B cap and a row within its 2 KiB
directory   16.11's fields
```

**Records and agents (R-MCP-13).** RECORD.md's kind registry gives each kind's text:

```text
documents   coordination log: in a team network the directory's announcements and entries (16.11); vault: one run
            card per run and stream, and every claim, handoff, ask, answer, check and note entry in a personal
            network; team record: one run card per run and stream built only from its own entries (context,
            change, approval, publish, route, reach, coverage), so it never holds a title, prompt or path that
            only the vault holds; a record repo: its own entries
run card    one per run and stream (owner decision 459), the fold of the run's source entries that stream holds,
            in (seq in their writer's chain, entry_id bytes) order, a run whose every source entry is erased
            having none (owner decision 461): title: the harness's custom session title (Claude Code's
            session_title, set by --name or /rename, reported at SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit), else the
            run's first user prompt's first line, 120 B after redaction; agent label, harness, model, project
            (repo display name and branch), tool names with counts, up to 256 touched paths, the first 2 KiB of
            user prompts, read from its context entries' prompts (16.7), started, last activity, ended; a vault
            card's sources add coverage and, in a personal network, claim and handoff, its claim state being the
            claim's own or handed_off as of the fold, never expired, which a reader computes, its claim expiry
            the newest claim's, and its row's expires the newest coverage's time once the run has ended; a team
            card counts each action kind asked for approval (owner decision 467); at most 16 KiB of text;
            re-indexed in its stream writer's companion push (§11.14), which a record log makes every
            RecordSettings.CardInterval (5 min) while the run moves, at once at the run's first source entry and
            at the coverage entry that ends it (owner decision 461); its version is E * 2^32 + c, E the
            index_epoch its push names and c the stream version at which the run last gained a source entry
            there, a stream version or epoch at or past 2^32 writing no card
            (IndexFormatSettings.CardVersionBitCount; owner decision 459); derived, a function of its stream at
            that version and of the erasures whose CUT precedes that epoch, so a rebuild reproduces it, and an
            erasure lists it through its CUT's epoch and folds it again without the erased entry (16.8)
rule        a log's index holds only what that log's own entries and files hold, for that log's readers; nothing
            crosses from a vault into another log's index, and a run reaches the directory only as its
            announcement (16.11; I-20)
group       by agent: key (network, sidecar_id, agent label, else agent_id), showing the label, the sidecar's
            config name, its member or sponsor, last_activity (its newest hit), active (an unexpired claim not
            handed off, an unexpired run announcement in state active, or a run card whose row carries no
            expires, its run having no Coverage entry, and that moved within 10 min, vault and team cards alike),
            a run's cards joined by run_id, started the earliest, last activity the latest, title and fields the
            card's whose row time is newer (owner decisions 459, 467), runs (run_id, title, harness, started,
            last activity, ended), claims (entry_id or claim_id, text, targets, expires, state), hit_count and
            its top 3 hits; active groups first, then the newest; by run: key run_id; by repo: key repo_id
agents      search_agents(task) is search(task, kind [claim, handoff, ask, note, run], group_by agent), since 30 d
            unless set; without a task it lists the agents active in the window; in a team network it groups the
            directory's run announcements, adding the caller's own vault run cards and, for admins and auditors,
            the team record's; members see other members' runs unless those members opted out (owner decision
            170), and a run's contents reach others only when its member shares them (owner decision 126)
claims      the harness config's claims setting (16.11), per member and per project: auto, the default in team
            networks, announces each run in the directory; prompt has the instructions ask the agent to claim,
            and the claim announces the run; off, the default in personal networks, announces nothing; a
            committed .ur narrows it at once and widens it only after the member confirms once; the value is
            fixed for each session, but off still withdraws a running announcement (16.11; owner decision 170)
```

**Trust and taint (R-MCP-14; I-9).**

```text
trust       per hit, from the doc table's outside and tainted bits and its writer: own (a device of the reader's
            member, an untainted run), member (another member's sidecar, an untainted run), untrusted (received
            from outside the network, brought in by a signed import, written in a tainted run, or flagged), and
            the team directory's prose whoever wrote it (16.11); group labels and device and member names come
            through 16.6's team views (member)
withhold    the default: an untrusted hit returns as a stub {hit_id, repo, doc type, opaque key, version, time,
            kind, match, partition, trust} with no field, path, snippet or name, a directory stub also keeping
            its attested and identifier fields (16.11), counted as untrusted_withheld, and the run stays
            untainted
include     untrusted: include returns their text between 16.6's markers, the run's taint fsynced first
            (D-MCP-16); each later outward action in the run then needs a fresh decision on a tainted request
            (TS1), by device or presence evidence, harness evidence counting only where the matching requests
            rule names it (owner decision 142)
approvals   the search tools are R: they file no request, sign no decision and are never evidence
remote      an indexer serves an app host's search (§11.14) in this engine outside every session and run, so
            serving taints no run; remote hits carry trust relative to the requester; a later agent requester
            withholds untrusted hits and taints its run before taking their text, as for local hits
secrets     a field or snippet matching the daemon's credentials is refused (I-7); queries, hits and snippets are
            never logged (I-13) and live only in a cursor, in memory
cli         ur search withholds untrusted text unless stdout is a terminal or --untrusted include is given;
            whenever it prints such text, a terminal included, it first taints each run whose harness process
            is an ancestor of the ur process (16.7's pid ancestry), so a shell tool or an editor's integrated
            terminal cannot read around I-9; terminal output drops C0 and C1 controls and bidi overrides
```

**CLI ([owner decision 166](#od-166)).**

```text
ur search <query> [--scope repo|network|all] [--repo r]... [--network n] [--ref ref] [--agent a] [--sidecar s]
          [--member m] [--run id] [--session id] [--kind k,...] [--since t] [--until t] [--path prefix]
          [--field name=text]... [--latest | --more] [--group agent|run|repo] [--sort time|path] [--limit n]
          [--cursor c] [--untrusted withhold|include] [--verify local|none|fetch] [--fuzzy] [--wait d]
          [--include spam,trash] [--explain] [--format text|json|jsonl|ids]
ur agents [<task>] [scope, time, --more and --format flags]     search_agents
ur search status [--scope s] [--repo r]... [--network n]        search_status, remote counters included
ur search sync [--repo r] [--more] [--evict] [--policy m]       sync latest (and all) now, drop the cache, or
                                                                set this device's all policy (§18.4's modes)
explain     --explain also prints the resolved scope with each exclusion's reason, the trigrams and fields each
            term uses, and each phase's timing; never the hits of a repo outside the scope
include     --include spam,trash asks for mail the device's join marks spam or trash, which every search leaves
            out otherwise; IMAP SEARCH asks the same from its selected folder (§15.7; owner decision 444)
format      text, on a terminal: a line a hit (time, network and repo, = confirmed, ~ possible or ? near, kind,
            display fields, path:line once verified), group headers, then a coverage line; json: the MCP
            result; jsonl: a line a hit as each phase lands, then a summary line; ids: a hit reference a line
exit        0 a hit, 1 none, 2 an error (as grep), 3 partial: the wait elapsed, too broad, or a coverage gap
wire        the daemon's control-mode search method (§5.8), with the MCP tool's arguments, streaming
            search.progress notifications through phase 2 and more's download; --wait defaults to 10 s on a
            terminal, else to the MCP default
```

**MCP tools.**

```text
describe      each search tool's description says that results are data, that untrusted text is withheld
              unless asked for, and that asking taints the run; the server's instructions (go-sdk's
              ServerOptions.Instructions, mcp/server.go:71, sent by server/discover and initialize, :906, :1987)
              are 16.11's texts, one per claims value, fixed per session
search in     query (required unless filters are set), scope, network, repos, ref, filters {agent, sidecar,
              member, run, session, kind[], since, until, path_prefix, fields{name: text}}, include ([spam,
              trash]: mail the default leaves out, §15.7; owner decision 444), at most 768 B encoded for a remote
              search, which an indexer answers INVALID past it and the device then runs locally with
              FallbackReason none (§11.14's sizes row), group_by (none | agent | run | repo), sort (time | path),
              latest, more, verify (local | none), untrusted (withhold | include), fuzzy, limit (hits 1-100,
              default 20; groups 1-50, default 10), wait_ms (0-25,000, default 2,000), cursor
search out    structuredContent under a declared outputSchema (D-MCP-13):
  hits        hit_id, repo_id, repo, network, ref, doc {type: file | message | entry | run | announcement, key},
              version, time, kind, match (confirmed | possible | near), by (field | text), correction,
              partition (local | current | previous | older | all), trust, source (content | index), fields,
              snippet (<= 200 B), line, open {tool, arguments}
  groups      key, agent_label, agent_id, device, member, trust, stub, active, last_activity, runs, claims,
              hit_count, top
  coverage    per repo, as above; counts {confirmed, possible, near, untrusted_withheld, masked, repos, excluded}
  status      complete, too_broad, next_cursor, tainted, trust, metered_bytes
open          evs_read(repo, path or hit), mail_read(id or hit), record_query by entry_id, run_id or hit, and a
              directory hit by directory_list or record_query, its prose only under include (16.11); a stub
              opens only by its hit_id, which lasts as long as its cursor
pages         next_cursor is opaque and session-bound, pins the ref versions read at the search's start, lasts 10
              min, and yields phase 1's ranked hits, then phase 2's (MCP's cursor model,
              https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/utilities/pagination); an erasure
              in scope or a lost read ends it with cursor_expired, so no page returns what the index no longer
              holds
async         a call returns by wait_ms, inside 16.4's 30 s, with what has landed, complete false and next_cursor;
              given a progressToken it reports phase 2 by progress notifications until it returns, and none after
              (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/utilities/progress); the next call
              returns what landed meanwhile
search_status per repo in scope: index state, coverage, cache bytes, last sync and each exclusion's reason; on
              an indexer, also remote serving counters (pages, refusals by code, CPU), never a requester or query
```
