```text
share signers (D-BRIDGE-17)
ShareKey     an owner-bound `secret` of Y's approving admin (§11.12), as §13.8 keeps an account key, never in
             the config, so it reaches only §8.5's readers of that secret; it signs only ShareCerts
ShareSigner  at accept, and whenever a ShareKey holder that writes the config sees a newer generation g of
             Y's config (§10.5), the holder replaces the share's BridgeShareSigner {share_id, g, a fresh seed,
             its ShareCert} in a config head at g, unless it already names g, and replaces it again, with a
             fresh seed and cert at g, when the cert has under 3 days left, unprompted as §7.9's folds are:
             every cert certifies a seed of its own, so one seed rides one file, in a head sealed at the
             generation its cert names, and a renewal that §10.6's gate refuses is dropped and made again at
             the new generation (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 12); §10.6's write gate takes a write at g only
             while g covers the config's holders_shrunk_at, so a sidecar that has stopped reading Y's config
             gets no later signer or cert; a ShareSigner signs only share-link WindowDelegations
file         a BridgeShareSigner is a config file, not a statement, with no Signed or SignedType of its own:
             only config writers' heads change it, as with K_sock (§8.8), and their signatures cover it; a writer
             without the ShareKey cannot certify, so X refuses its signer; a Y sidecar signs with one only
             while its share_id, g and seed's public key match its cert
keys         the ShareKey and ShareSigners, Ed25519, sign §6.9 Signeds in the sidecar role's bridge_*.go,
             beside §5.4's identity-key Sign: signer_id = share_id, key_id = SHA-256 of the signing public key;
             verifiers require signer_id = the body's share_id and resolve key_id, a ShareCert's to the
             share's pinned BridgeShareKey and a share delegation's to its ShareCert's signer_public_key
sign         a Y subject signs with the share's current BridgeShareSigner while its cert is unexpired; when
             that file changes, the compiler that reads it, a daemon's sidecar role or an app's forwarding role
             (§18.6), has BridgeHost re-sign each share link's delegations, which their next contracts carry
admit        X's host requires the ShareCert to verify under the pinned ShareKey with the delegation's
             share_id, not_after_ms ahead and at most 7 days away (§8.6's 60 s skew), and g at least the
             share's newest verified generation, which it raises and keeps in 17.8's persisted state, then the
             delegation under signer_public_key; the principal's not_after is the earlier not_after_ms; a g
             above the share's newest is committed to the persisted posture store before the contract that
             carried it is admitted: one commit per share per rotation of Y, a few milliseconds in that
             contract's VerifyPrincipal sequence before the dial, never a packet's, a flow's or a later
             contract's (R-BRIDGE-9), so a removed sidecar stays refused after a host restart (owner decision
             476)
bound        a sidecar Y removed is admitted on new contracts until a later generation's ShareCert reaches the
             host in any Y delegation, at most 7 days after its removal reaches evs, and those it opened run
             to their end (at most 60 min, server/model/subscription_contract_expiration.go:14); with no
             renewal for 7 days the share lapses for everyone; a reaped Delegation-admitted agent signs while
             it reads Y's config (§10.5); a removed holder device, or a holder member leaving the AdminSet, can
             certify until X revokes the share, so Y's devices raise a SidecarEvent naming it, and X re-invites
```

- **Isolation.** Only sidecar-owned Required hosts holding a share grant turn `FriendsAndFamilyEgress()` on; sdk providers never do. The principal's verified share and network, never an address, select the aliases, which resolve only to that share's targets through maps, dialable hosted addresses and served prefixes: never rule 4, rule 0's listeners, unmapped loopback, another host's address or an exit ([owner decision 11](#od-11)). NAT state is per source path and 5-tuple (connect/ip.go:2072-2098), so foreign flows share no entry with local ones; replies carry the alias back unrewritten. Foreign flows are shed first under NAT pressure. Reach events name the source network (§16).

### 17.10 Placement, sdk seams, apps, hosts

| Repo | Change |
|---|---|
| connect (X9) | §4.6's C5, C6a, C13 and C14 (M4), C15's key (M1), C16 before app devices host, C18 for shares (M6); not C6b, since providers terminate flows without a tun; and, default off, an egress mark on Linux for `ur tun`'s exits (17.11): egress_linux.go's `SetEgressMark` sets SO_MARK at every dial site connect's egress machinery covers, which egress_dial_sites_test.go audits, and the extender carrier's socket (`openExtenderPacketConn`, which the alt api path and the QUIC and DNS carriers share) and the provider's ICMP egress off Windows join that machinery, so the mark, and on Windows the interface pin, reach them ([owner decision 479](#od-479)) |
| sidecar | Root `bridge_*.go`: statements, the compiler that builds `BridgeState`, forwards, and forwarding's setup and signer, the compiler and signer also linked into apps' VPN components among the root's forwarding files (§18.10). `device/` (`device.Bridge`, D-SDK-20): table, pins, links, `BridgeEgressPolicy`, principals, aliases, routes, the per-link resolver and zone, and 17.8's states, importing connect and `protocol/bridge` only. `cli/` wires `device.Bridge` to the root's state producer for `ur tun` and `ur bridge` and holds `ur tun`'s OS tun (`golang.zx2c4.com/wireguard/tun`, MIT) and the userspace stack, out of every sdk binding (Q-SDK-5); on Windows `ur tun` neither bundles nor fetches wintun.dll: it loads one beside `ur.exe` or at the installed app's path only once its SHA-256 and Authenticode signer match windows/app/tools/fetch-deps.ps1's pins (0.14.1), since it runs elevated, and otherwise prints where to get it, so the release zip holds no DLL ([owner decision 222](#od-222)); the SHA-256 is the DLL's, exact per architecture, which the owner records beside the zip's pin from a Windows run of that script (`$WintunDllSha256Amd64`, `$WintunDllSha256Arm64`) and `ur tun` carries, beside WinVerifyTrust and the script's signer thumbprint, refusing every DLL until they are recorded ([owner decision 481](#od-481)) |
| sdk | Both insertion points and the exit-NAT hook through §18.6's `deviceBridge`; `DeviceLocal` implements `BridgeHost`; route export (§18); in every app's VPN component, forwarding's following, compile and signing on its forwarding client ([owner decision 197](#od-197); §18.6) |
| server | No rule tables; `network_bridge_share`; gates read `BridgeRows`; the forwarding client's `forward_only` mark (§7.4) |
| apps | Out of scope (owner rule 6): running forwarding in every VPN component, always on, and applying exported routes, a chosen block included, are §18's app work |

```go
// device (sidecar/device); implemented by sdk DeviceLocal and the CLI host, which own the client generators
type BridgeHost interface {
	// one link per target (Q-BRIDGE-2); shareAliases is nil for a same-network link (ProvideMode_Network),
	// and for a share link (FriendsAndFamily) lists the aliases C18's source half may carry; sign returns
	// the Signed WindowDelegation for each window client the link builds, not_after_ms at most notAfter, the
	// client's strict_exp (§7.4), and on a share link the host calls it again for each live one when its
	// compile finds a new BridgeShareSigner, for its later contracts (17.9)
	NewBridgeLink(ctx context.Context, target connect.Id, subject connect.Id, shareAliases []netip.Prefix,
		sign func(windowClientId connect.Id, windowClientPublicKey []byte, notAfter time.Time) ([]byte, error),
	) (connect.UserNatClient, error)
}
```

**Device abstractions (PLAN.md:31).** `device.Bridge` satisfies §18.6's `deviceBridge`, `BridgeEgressPolicy` being its hook. In every app it runs in the VPN component as the forwarding role, with the root's compiler and its own forwarding key, whenever that component runs, with no setting that turns it off and no wait on the app ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); under `ur tun` the daemon runs it, through `cli/`. On apps, sending, that is routes to other devices' addresses and subnets, forwards out and exits, needs no C16, since its links are Required window clients to sidecar-owned hosts or C16 ones; hosting, that is the device's own address, maps into it and its advertised subnet, waits for C16 on the device client's sdk provider, in that client's network only (D-BRIDGE-5, §18.6's host row).

### 17.11 cli/UI.md mapping

| Command or UI note | Meaning (v0 unless noted) |
|---|---|
| `ur tun` | OS tun `ur-<instance>` with the block and granted prefixes; the default routes, IPv6's too, only with default egress on and an egress destination, `--default-egress` and `--route-local` setting the person's two choices (below; [owner decision 606](#od-606)); yields to an app bridge |
| `ur tun ip [<ip>\|auto]`; "client assign local ip" | Show or claim the address |
| `ur bridge`; "show all ips", "show all hostname:port" | Run the bridge; list addresses, private names, rules, forwards |
| `ur bridge expose <ranges>`; "client forward ip subnet" | Advertise subnets (a route) |
| `ur bridge expose :<port>[=<ip>:<port>]` (added); "client:port → ip:port" | Map this client's port |
| `ur bridge forward client:port[:local ip]:local port`; "client:port → client:port" | Listen on all interfaces unless `--listen` narrows it ([owner decision 84](#od-84)); dial over the userspace stack under a §8 grant |
| `ur bridge egress auto\|<exit>\|tag:<t>\|none [--require-default-egress]` (added); "client egress spec" | The default route; under exits alone, `--require-default-egress` has the subject's devices keep default egress on (below; [owner decision 607](#od-607)) |
| `ur bridge block [cycle\|<cidr>]` (added; admins) | Re-roll or choose the block (17.4; owner decisions [28](#od-28), [132](#od-132)) |
| `ur bridge invite`, `accept-invite` | Cross-network port and subnet shares (17.9), v1 |
| `ur bridge activate <share_id>` (added; the sharing network's approving admin) | Show an accepted share and activate it (17.9's share pins; [owner decision 475](#od-475)), v1 |

Without an active grant, these commands print the approval prompt and wait (§16.6); `forward` warns that it serves every host reaching the listener. `ur bridge public-tls` is §13's.

```text
ur tun's default routes (owner decisions 479, 480, 482, 606, 607)
choice   (owner decision 606) two per-network settings of the device that ur tun sets and shows: default
         egress, on unless the person turns it off, whether the host's default traffic goes to the egress
         destination through the tun; and route local traffic, on by default as the sdk's DefaultRouteLocal is,
         its counterpart of the sdk's routeLocal; with default egress on, ur tun takes the default routes, both
         families, by the rows below when the client has an egress destination: under exits an exit of the
         network it can use, under auto the connect client's destination; with no destination and route local
         traffic on, default traffic stays on the host's own default routes and the tun carries only the block,
         the granted prefixes and private names, and with route local traffic off the tun still takes them and
         refuses that traffic, failing closed; with default egress off, default traffic stays on the host's
         routes in every mode; a change of either setting, or a destination that comes or goes, re-applies the
         routes without restarting the tun; the egress mode stays the admin's policy for traffic that enters
         URnetwork (§8.10)
lock     (owner decision 607) under exits, a network's admin, owner or sponsor may require default egress on,
         in the BridgeEgress statement's exits body, sealed with it (require_default_egress, 17.8), so servers
         learn nothing new; a device whose network requires it keeps default egress on for that network, and
         ur tun shows the lock and refuses --default-egress=off, naming the requirement; with no exit, route
         local traffic still decides; ur bridge egress files it through an egress_change action whose
         require_default_egress = 41 its approval shows and binds (§16.8)
linux    the daemon's own transport stays off the tun by fwmark policy routing: its sockets carry connect's
         egress mark M (17.10), and ur tun puts the default route in its own table T with wg-quick's rules,
         not fwmark M lookup T and lookup main suppress_prefixlength 0, carving nothing by the platform's
         addresses; SO_MARK needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, which ur tun already requires; until connect's mark lands,
         ur tun installs no default route under exits and says so
strict   where rp_filter is strict (1) on all or on the interface of the main table's default route, ur tun
         holds the exits, putting nothing on, and says so with the fix (rp_filter 2, systemd's default),
         trying again at each sync; ur changes no host security setting, firewall rule or global sysctl a
         person did not choose, and wg-quick's src_valid_mark and connmark recipe is a later task of its own
carve    each carved address (17.4) the host reaches only by its default route keeps the host's own route:
         a throw route in T on Linux; on macOS and Windows, where the exits ride IPv4's halves (0.0.0.0/1,
         128.0.0.0/1), a host route through the default route's gateway and interface, as wg-quick on macOS
         and WireGuard for Windows route an endpoint's /32, an address an on-link or local route reaches
         taking none; the routes follow the carve and the default route at each sync and leave with the
         exits, adding nothing by the platform's addresses, so the host's own DNS to an off-link resolver
         leaves outside the exits, as the carve already accepts for apps
ipv6     ::/0 goes through the tun too, with IPv6 copies of the two rules on Linux and the platforms'
         equivalents beside the IPv4 halves on macOS and Windows, and the bridge rejects IPv6 there (17.5);
         the carve's off-link IPv6 addresses take IPv6 throws, or IPv6 host routes through the IPv6 default
         route's gateway, as IPv4's do; the daemon's own IPv6 sockets keep the mark, so its traffic leaves
         by the host's route
```

### 17.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routing inside the multi client (a `RouteOverride`) | One place | After the mux; per-packet evaluation; reaches the IpAssoc cluster (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:7384-7395) | Rejected |
| Per-packet rewrite: in `clientReceiveAdmitted`, or of aliases at the sender | Any protocol; no alias table at hosts | Port-aware rewrite both ways, a copy per packet (connect/ip.go:10316-10335) | Rejected: the hook maps once per flow |
| Cross-network forwards over §9 streams | No foreign packets in provider NATs | No subnet invites; a second data plane | Not chosen ([owner decision 86](#od-86)) |
| App devices as targets now (Opportunistic) | Phones and app desktops host at once | Replies can cross relays in plaintext (connect/transfer_encrypt.go:477-483) | Ruled out by the owner directive until C16 |
| Trust C13's sealed subject at hosts | No signature per contract | The platform holds the HMAC key: a breached server mints any subject | Rejected (D-BRIDGE-17) |
| One ShareKey every Y reader holds, rotated on removals and re-pinned at X from Y's update | No admin key or renewal | A removed sidecar holds the old key, so it signs a successor of its own, which the operator can deliver first | Rejected: an admin's ShareKey certifies per-generation signers (17.9) |
| X verifies Y's per-subject grant: a ShareKey-signed list of Y's granted subjects with their identity keys at each change to Y's grants, each delegation signed by its subject's own key | The intersection holds against a modified Y reader and a colluding operator together | The ShareKey holder re-certifies at every change to Y's grants; X pins a list per change and learns who in Y may reach it; delegations lose the per-generation signer that spares X Y's identity log | Not chosen: Y's current config readers, with Y's routers and the contract gate, are the unit for Y's half, disclosed (17.9, §8.11; meta review CC-05) |
| Bootstrap from the unverified projection's `has_document` | Opens at once after a restart | A forged `has_document = false` reopens a LAN | Rejected (D-BRIDGE-18) |
| A pin per 5-tuple flow, a full table refusing; or the pre-edit table for TCP non-SYN segments through a drain | Exact per flow; no pair state | 1,024 slots holding UDP 5 min cap a phone near 3.4 new flows/s; a new connection's SYN and later segments split across links, and a provider drops a non-SYN segment it has no flow for (connect/ip.go:4659-4687) | Rejected: pair pins where an entry offers a choice (17.5) |

### 17.13 Decisions proposed

**D-BRIDGE-1 (proposed).** The bridge reuses connect's client-to-provider NAT path: sender routing, a per-flow provider decision, one hop. *Why:* PLAN.md:115-117; targets need no tun or root.

**D-BRIDGE-2 (proposed).** The router sits before the mux behind `deviceBridge` (17.5); the CLI shares it. *Why:* all device egress passes there.

**D-BRIDGE-3 (proposed).** Fail closed: the block is a deny backstop; providers serve only sealed flows, never dial another host's address and, with an ACL document, open private destinations only by rule. *Why:* R-BRIDGE-10, R-BRIDGE-12.

**D-BRIDGE-4 (proposed).** The C5 hook applies 17.6's order, relying on C6a, C13, C15 and, for shares, C18 (17.10). *Why:* once per flow; a nil hook changes nothing.

**D-BRIDGE-5 (proposed).** Links run Required to a fixed target with one window client, relay-only until C3, never count-capped; targets are sidecar-owned until C16, after which an app device hosts on its device client's sdk provider, in that client's network only. *Why:* D-PROTO-6, D-PROTO-10; owner decisions [66](#od-66), [197](#od-197).

**D-BRIDGE-6 (proposed).** Bridge rules are signed config-repo statements, sidecars' own as sealed deltas in the authorization log; gates see only reach rules and `BridgeRows`, applying an egress statement's clear mode in log order, and a requested grant's prefixes and ports ride sealed in its CanonicalAction ([owner decision 220](#od-220)). A fold freezes each statement's body-level verdict, judged on the state its entry lands on, into the config head's bridge ledger, which every full reader standing there checks, and a body sealed above every formed generation is frozen void after `UnformedVoidWait` (17.8; owner decisions [473](#od-473), [478](#od-478)). *Why:* [owner decision 5](#od-5); no prefixes, addresses or ports reach the server (I-4); every reader at one pin must hold one ledger, and a compile must not grow with the log.

**D-BRIDGE-7 (proposed).** Revocations reset both ends at once. Edits move no live pair off a link that still serves it while the pin table has room, and drain a removed advertiser or address for max(`drain_seconds`, 600 s) for TCP and max(`drain_seconds`, 5 min) otherwise. New pairs take the new rule, as do new TCP connections of pairs pinned to a draining link, but for 5 min after an entry first offers a choice new UDP and ICMP pairs, which cannot be told from live ones, follow the pre-change link. Pins key on the rendezvous pair, exist only where an entry offers a choice, and a full table leaves a pair unpinned, refusing nothing (17.5). *Why:* revocation is a security event; an edit should not break live TCP; [owner decision 66](#od-66) allows overload protection, not count caps.

**D-BRIDGE-8 (proposed).** An identical advertisement is an approved HA replica or remap; nesting is allowed; other overlaps are refused. *Why:* LAN prefixes repeat across sites.

**D-BRIDGE-9 (proposed).** HA is active-active by weighted rendezvous over healthy advertisers; a down mark removes a link from the hash only while another advertiser is up, and moves no pin. *Why:* NAT keeps flows symmetric; nothing waits on the server; one timed-out connect must not cut a route's live flows.

**D-BRIDGE-10 (proposed).** A forward listens on 0.0.0.0/:: unless `--listen` narrows it, under a requested grant, disclosed as LAN-exposed. *Why:* [owner decision 84](#od-84); D-TRUST-8.

**D-BRIDGE-11 (proposed).** Hosted devices (sdk/device_local.go:893-910), URnetwork-run WireGuard proxy clients, the extension worker and isolated clients (server/connect/resident.go:4790-4793) never route, host or serve. *Why:* I-10; js has no raw sockets.

**D-BRIDGE-12 (proposed).** The sdk exports hosted addresses, granted prefixes, aliases and an RFC 1918 block, minus every local /32 the physical path needs (interfaces, gateways, system resolvers), and per-peer /32s instead of the block while those are unknown, for apps to capture. *Why:* apps exclude RFC 1918, Apple's overlap semantics are undocumented ([R:connect-ip](design/design-research/connect-ip.md) §2.6), and a captured carrier resolver black-holes DNS.

**D-BRIDGE-13 (proposed).** 17.9's egress spec sets a subject's default route, enforced at §8.10's gate. *Why:* R-BRIDGE-7 must survive a compromised agent sidecar.

**D-BRIDGE-14 (proposed).** C18 reaches the hook only on sidecar-owned Required hosts holding a share grant, which map foreign flows by the principal's verified share and network to that share's targets only (17.9). *Why:* [owner decision 86](#od-86); isolation must not rest on addresses.

**D-BRIDGE-15 (proposed).** The accepting network aliases shared hosts and prefixes in its own block; both tables travel sealed under the invite code's key. *Why:* blocks and LANs repeat across networks; the server learns no addresses.

**D-BRIDGE-16 (proposed).** `ur bridge block` refuses a block outside 100.64/10 and RFC 1918, readers keep the previous block and alarm on a head carrying one, and renumbering keeps host bits; an overlap no carve resolves (17.4) is fixed by cycling, readers keeping the previous block until a head carries a valid one. *Why:* [owner decision 132](#od-132); a CLI check binds no other signing tool.

**D-BRIDGE-17 (proposed).** A host admits a native IP flow only from a window client whose customer-signed `WindowDelegation` it verified against the subject's pinned identity key, the key of the subject's live forwarding Delegation ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) or, on a share link, a ShareSigner of the source network's newest certified config generation, which the share's pinned ShareKey, kept in the approving admin's `secret`, certifies for at most 7 days, each cert certifying a fresh seed, the host committing a raised generation before it admits ([owner decision 476](#od-476)); C13's seal serves only as a consistency check (17.9). *Why:* C13's seal is the operator's statement, and a sidecar its network removes must stop signing within a bound, which no key every reader keeps allows.

**D-BRIDGE-18 (proposed).** Only a verified state opens a private destination: the engine and the forwarding role run 17.8's legacy, pending and enforcing states, persisted, never lowered by unsigned input (§18.6), and a daemon's start replays every judged denial before its provider is built ([owner decision 474](#od-474)). *Why:* a restart plus a forged `has_document = false` must not reopen a LAN, nor a restart drop a denial only a judge could decide.

**D-BRIDGE-19 (proposed).** A provider never dials its own daemon listeners, document or not (17.6's rule 0). *Why:* [owner decision 120](#od-120) opens LAN and loopback destinations, not the sidecar's own control and content plane.

**D-BRIDGE-20 (proposed).** Hosts draw from the lower /17 and aliases fill the upper /17 first-fit (17.4), so a share is refused, before any flow and with its reason in `accept_status`, only when it is wider than /17 or the upper /17 has no aligned room for it (17.9). *Why:* a /16 cannot alias a /8 or itself, and random host /32s across the whole block leave few free aligned blocks (about 5 free /24s among 1,000 hosts).

**D-BRIDGE-21 (proposed).** A revocation swaps the provider's policy before `CloseFlows`, and a flow registers its rule and policy generation before its dial and re-checks it before its first byte (17.6); the engine's order is commit, publish, close, with every denial held at its own log position (17.8's engine). *Why:* a dial can outlast the reset that should have ended it.

### 17.14 Open questions

**Q-BRIDGE-1.** [X18] Which range carries overlay addresses? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 28](#od-28)):** IPv4 only, a random /16 per network from 100.64.0.0/10 after C6a, which admins may cycle or replace (17.4). *Residual:* none; Q-BRIDGE-7 bounds the choice.

**Q-BRIDGE-2.** How do links reach targets? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (c). One `BridgeHost` link per target, as a fixed `ProviderSpec{ClientId}` multi client with window size 1 (`FixedWindowSize: 1`), `PostQuantumEncryption` Required, `OverrideAllowDirect=false` until C3, and `EnableIcmp`; not `DefaultMultiClientSettings`, whose six-client quality window (connect/ip_remote_multi_client.go:217-234) is the wrong default and six times the memory. Each window client carries the subject's customer-signed `WindowDelegation` into C13's seal, which the provider verifies (D-BRIDGE-17). Option (b), a link on the subject's own client, is adopted only where §22.9 measures per-target memory over §18.4's iOS budget and the new framing passes fragment, reply-filter and lifecycle tests; the iOS tunnel is the first candidate and runs no link until measured ([owner decision 100](#od-100)). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-3.** Should upgraded providers refuse private destinations to Network sources unless a rule allows them? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 50](#od-50)):** only with an ACL document; without one, untagged sidecars keep today's reach (17.6 rules 3-4; [owner decision 105](#od-105)), which [owner decision 120](#od-120) keeps and discloses (Q-TRUST-7). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-4.** Do overlay addresses get private names? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 85](#od-85)):** yes, in v0: `<client-name>.<net>.<root>` from the config repo, answered on the device by C14 or `ur tun`'s resolver, never forwarded or published (§12.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-5.** Which bind do forwards and local listeners use? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 84](#od-84)):** 0.0.0.0/:: unless `--listen` narrows it (cli/UI.md:11), forwards disclosed as LAN-exposed (D-TRUST-8). **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 130](#od-130)):** off loopback, git over http, IMAP and SMTP submission serve only TLS, git also ssh, and plaintext stays on 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (I-17); port forwards, which carry the user's own protocol, are unaffected. *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-6.** Cross-cutting (§8, §9). Which data plane carries forwards and invites? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 86](#od-86)):** the IP path for all, cross-network included, with C18 (17.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-7.** Cross-cutting (§18). May a chosen block lie outside 100.64/10 and RFC 1918? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 132](#od-132)):** (b), no: only 100.64.0.0/10, 10/8, 172.16/12 or 192.168/16, narrowing [owner decision 28](#od-28)'s "any /16" (D-BRIDGE-16). Public exits refuse RFC 1918 today (connect/ip_security.go:897) and 100.64/10 after C6a, so overlay traffic never reaches the internet; any /16, or adding 198.18.0.0/15, was not chosen. *Residual:* none.

**Q-BRIDGE-8.** Cross-cutting (§18). Does an app device claim its overlay address when its forwarding is set up? [Owner decision 197](#od-197) makes the device's overlay address part of its always-on forwarding, while 17.4 assigns one on demand. **Decided by owner 2026-11-15 ([owner decision 484](#od-484)):** (a), on demand, as 17.4 says: in the app's UI, by the host's first map, or by an admin. Forwarding's setup files no `BridgeAddress` of its own, and the address it names among the VPN component's forwarding is the one the device holds once it has claimed it, so no app device's loopback opens to the network's untagged sidecars (17.6's rule 3 with no ACL document; [owner decision 120](#od-120)) because its forwarding was set up; (b), filing at setup, can follow later with one statement at the next setup, and hosting waits for C16 either way. *Residual:* none.

### 17.15 Departures from PLAN.md

- **PLAN.md:117** ("from same network"): [owner decision 86](#od-86) extends maps to cross-network shares (Q-BRIDGE-6).
- **PLAN.md:353 with :359.** Relayed bridge bytes count ([owner decision 10](#od-10)); P2P bytes after C3 do not (§20, Q-QUOTA-6).
- **PLAN.md:31.** `device.Bridge`, not the whole `Sidecar`, implements the device abstractions (17.10; Q-SDK-2).
- **cli/UI.md, not PLAN.md:** the added `expose :<port>`, `egress` and `block` forms (17.11).

### 17.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** `device.Bridge`, `device.BridgeEgressPolicy`, `device.BridgeHost`, `BridgeStatus`; the compiler and forwarding's signer, which apps' VPN components link (§18.6, §18.10); `protocol/bridge/bridge.proto`'s `BridgeState`, `BridgeIdentity`, `BridgeShareKey`, `Pending`, `BridgeRows`, `WindowDelegation`, `ShareCert`, `BridgeShareSigner`, share pins' `BridgeShareGrant`, the share seal's `BridgeShareTargets`, `BridgeShareAliases` and `BridgeShareAccept`, the config head's bridge ledger (`BridgeLedgerManifest`, `BridgeLedgerAddresses`, `BridgeLedgerRules`, `BridgeLedgerEgressSpecs` and `BridgeLedgerAliases` under `bridge/ledger/`), and 17.8's statements; 17.8's states, route export, reach events (§16), the `ur tun` resolver (§12.9), `ur bridge activate` and `ur tun`'s exits routes (17.11).
- **Consumes:** §7.9's config repo, authorization log (`AuthPin`, entries, `StatementHeader`), deltas and `team` hints, and its forwarding Delegations ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); §7.4's `strict_exp`; §8 grant chains, `AclEngine`, approvals, suspension, contract gate, shares; §10's generations; §11.12's `secret` kind; §6 `Signed` and §6.11's `SignedType`, Required, §6.10.1; §5 identities, the binding log, `GET /sidecar/identity/<sidecar_id>`, `Sidecar.Authorize`, `SidecarEvent`; §16.6's decisions and `effect_key`; §12.9; §18 `deviceBridge`, forwarding's setup and the device RPC's status mirror; §20.6 debits; §4 C5, C6a, C13, C14, C15, C16, C18.
- **Subprotocol messages:** none; rules ride the config repo (§6.11 leaves MessageType 0x19 unused). `Signed` types 0x1901-0x1909 are 17.8's statements, `WindowDelegation` and `ShareCert`; `BridgeShareSigner`, a config file, takes none (17.9).
- **API routes:** statements through §7's `POST /network/config/delta`; shares through §8's `POST /acl/invite` and `POST /acl/accept-invite`, which carry the sealed tables, the accept status included, the accept in §8.11's two forms, a claim that answers the share's id with the sealed targets and a completion that stores the sealed accept and the status once ([owner decision 350](#od-350)); `GET|PUT /network/bridge/share/<share_id>` (Client, a sidecar of either network: read both tables, or replace its own at a higher version).
- **Tables:** `network_bridge_share` (api): share_id, both network ids, sealed target and alias tables, versions, `accept_status enum{active, refused_too_large, refused_no_space}`; kept until revoked.
- **Services and config:** no new service and no `sidecar_abuse:` caps; sdk flag `EnableBridge` and §19's `bridge` gate, which keep the bridge dark until its release (§19.11) and are no setting: released, an app's forwarding runs whenever its VPN component runs ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); `ur tun` needs CAP_NET_ADMIN or root.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §7.9 carries 17.8's statements as log entries, its type rule bounding a decision's bridge rules by 17.8's rule ids; §7.9's config head holds `bridge/ledger/` and `bridge/share-grant/`, its writer folds the ledger at each base that folds a bridge statement and through its tip while one is unfolded, and its head check compares the ledger ([owner decision 473](#od-473)); the daemon's `ConfigClient` stores an entry before any entry callback runs ([owner decision 474](#od-474)); §8 enumerates for the compiler the rules by which one subject reaches another (§8.9); a §5.8 Confirm method, `bridge.activate`, runs 17.9's activation ([owner decision 475](#od-475)); §16.6's step 5 has a bridge component whose Lookup finds that id in the authorization log, AU1 counts those rules, `bridge_expose` returns the id, and `bridge_close` takes it or a forward's grant_id (§16.5); `sidecar/device` parses only `protocol/bridge`'s auth.proto (§7.9: `AuthPin`, `AuthEntry`, `ProjectionHeader`, `StatementHeader`, `Genesis`, `SidecarRevoke`, `MemberRevoke`, `ForwardScope`, and §8.8's `Suspend`, `Unsuspend` and `GrantRevoke`) and signed.proto (§6.9: `Signed`, `WebAuthnEvidence`, `SignedType`), which `config.proto` and `acl.proto` import (§4.4), reading the fields of config.proto's `Delegation` and `DelegationRevoke` its overlay needs by their numbers (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4); §5.8 and §16.6 sign 17.9's own-resource filings, a host's own `BridgeAddress` among them, from any mode, and other bridge statements only for a /dev/tty-confirmed `ur` command or in an app's UI; §18.6's setup gives an app's VPN component its forwarding Delegation, forwarding clients and `Pending`, after which its forwarding role compiles 17.8's states itself, persists them as its posture and signs its links' delegations with its forwarding key or a share's ShareSigner, and `DeviceLocal` takes the physical path's /32s; §7.9 defines the forwarding Delegation, its signer, what its key signs and its ends, §6.9 that key's `signer_id`, and §7.4 the forwarding client's `forward_only` mark; §2.8 lists `network_bridge_share` with its accept status and C13's delegation with a share's ShareCert, §2.10 17.9's share-signer bound, and §2.6 and §7.9 the ShareKey's custody and the `BridgeShareSigner` seeds every Y config reader, agents included, holds; §6.9's Signers and §5.5's identity-key rule (D-CORE-6) admit 17.9's two share keys; §22 tests D-BRIDGE-16 to D-BRIDGE-21: §22.5's §17 row; §22.7's S8, its actions suite and its assert block's bridge clauses (17.5's pins, aliases, private names, the no-document rules, MCP's own-resource bridge filings); FS-38, with its share signers in the M6-out run with C18; FS-56's dial fence, no byte reaching a target after its flow's revocation (D-BRIDGE-21); and §22.9's Browsers row (the CGNAT carve) and Memory row (mobile churn past a full table, the link cell's NAT at C5's per-flow idles) ([owner decision 551](#od-551)).

### 17.17 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without an ACL document, untagged sidecars reach every provider's LAN and loopback (owner decisions [50](#od-50), [105](#od-105)) | High | High | Accepted and disclosed ([owner decision 120](#od-120); §2.18); never the provider's own daemon listeners (D-BRIDGE-19); every tier may write a document ([owner decision 73](#od-73)) |
| Providers not yet on C5 let Network sources reach everything | High | High | D-ACL-5's legacy rule; only enforcing clients advertise or host |
| Before C16, sdk providers apply rules 4 and 7 to C13's operator-asserted subject | Low | Medium | With a document, private destinations stay denied whatever the subject; D-BRIDGE-17 there from C16 |
| Foreign flows probe or exhaust a host's NAT (C18) | Medium | High | 17.9's isolation; per-source NAT state; foreign-first shedding; §22 tests |
| A sidecar the source network removed keeps signing share delegations that operator-made contracts carry: a ShareSigner until a later ShareCert reaches the host (at most 7 days), a reaped Delegation-admitted agent while it reads that config, a removed ShareKey holder until the share is revoked | Low | Medium | 17.9's per-generation ShareSigners under 7-day ShareCerts; the ShareKey only in the approving admin's `secret`; a `SidecarEvent` on a holder's removal, then a new invite |
| A current reader of the source network's config that its policy denies, running modified software, reaches a share's targets on a contract the operator mints, since X's host checks the network, the share and the signer, never Y's per-subject grant | Low | Medium | It needs a modified Y device and a colluding or compelled operator; X's grant still bounds targets, ports and expiry; the honest gate refuses the contract; Y removes the reader (17.9, 17.12; §8.11) |
| A forward on all interfaces serves the LAN and every local user ([owner decision 84](#od-84)) | High | Medium | Disclosure; `--listen`; grant expiry; the Host check |
| The block clashes with Tailscale, CGNAT or, if chosen in RFC 1918, a LAN | Medium | Medium | Cycling or choosing the block; /32 peer routes and carved interface, gateway and resolver /32s, or per-peer /32s while those are unknown (17.4); the local LAN wins (17.7); §22.9's CGNAT fixture |
| A full pin table leaves pairs unpinned, so an edit can move their live flows | Low | Medium | One pin per pair, only where an entry offers a choice; nothing refused ([owner decision 66](#od-66)); `ur bridge` counts unpinned pairs; §22.9's mobile churn case |
| After an uncovered agent's reap, new bridge deltas wait for a config rotation (§8.12) by a config writer or the agent's admitting device, a wrapped one by rotation alone (§7.10; owner decisions [128](#od-128), [144](#od-144)) | Medium | Medium | No admin needed ([owner decision 128](#od-128)); covered agents' reaps need none (§10.5); withdrawals never wait; `ur bridge` shows the wait |
| A tun's overlay address leaks in WebRTC (libwebrtc's 100.64/10 handling is unverified) | Unknown | Low | `ur tun ip auto` refuses behind `BridgeComponentSettings.AutoAddressEnabled`, false, until §22.9's Browsers check shows no ICE candidate in the overlay block; an explicit address and an admin's assignment work |
| Links, or forwarding's compile, do not fit the iOS tunnel | High | Medium | No iOS links until §22 measures; Q-BRIDGE-2's own-client links; the compile cap of [owner decision 216](#od-216), measured to admit about 4,300 devices' rows at the tunnel's connected baseline and 770 to 1,440 under provider load, a network past it keeping its last verified state on that device and alarming; links fail closed meanwhile |
| A revocation the posture cannot check does not apply on a device that cannot compile | Low | High | Accepted by the owner ([owner decision 216](#od-216)): forwarding never drops for it; `bridge_alarm` on the schedule 17.8's forwarding roles give, the condition in the status throughout ([owner decision 487](#od-487)); denials the posture can check apply at once; the review phase's storage-backed compile removes the memory cap as a cause ([owner decision 366](#od-366); DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4) |
| Between the app's runs an app's forwarding role follows the log unwitnessed, so an operator that withholds a revocation from it keeps a revoked subject reaching that device | Low | Medium | the sidecar role's witnessed pin at each run (§18.6); daemon hosts witness by HeadCheck (§6.4); it needs a malicious operator, and the subject's own revocation still ends it at every other device |
| A base that leaves a bridge filing unfolded and changes the policy its approval was judged by turns that filing's verdict at every reader | Low | Low | writers fold through their tip whenever a bridge statement is unfolded, so only a filing in the seconds between a head's writing and its base's acceptance is exposed; it fails closed alike at every reader, and the requester files again (17.8; [owner decision 473](#od-473)) |
| A standing member device keeps filing bridge bodies sealed to generations that never form, holding the config fold | Low | Medium | each is void at the fold `UnformedVoidWait` (24 h) after its entry; while they keep coming, bases past the tail cap wait up to that long at a time; the writer's `config_key_waiting` line names the filer on every plan, and revoking it, which needs no base, ends the hold one wait after its last filing (17.8; [owner decision 478](#od-478)) |
| Under `exits`, a Linux host with a strict reverse path filter keeps its own route instead of the exits until a person loosens the filter | Low | Low | `ur tun` holds the exits, putting nothing on, and says how (rp_filter 2); `ur` changes no host security setting a person did not choose (17.11; [owner decision 479](#od-479)) |

### 17.18 Phasing

- **v0, M4 (same network; Linux and WSL2 first):** C5 with its dial fence, C6a, C13 with `WindowDelegation`s, C14; statements in the config repo and 17.8's states, the rule table and the compile of `BridgeRows` landing at M2 with §7.9's records, though nothing files a bridge statement until M4; router, hook (rule 0 included), userspace stack; `ur tun` on Linux, its default route under `exits` once connect's egress mark lands ([owner decision 479](#od-479)); private names via `ur tun`'s resolver and C14's seam, dark on app paths; forwards, expose and egress under I-8 approvals; HA, pins, dispositions, block changes and the CGNAT carve; sidecar-owned hosts; the sdk insertion behind `EnableBridge`. Blocked by §7.9's config repo and authorization log (M2), §8's grant chains and gates, and C13.
- **v0, M8** (with §18's app hosts): forwarding in every app's VPN component, with its own keys, compile and signing ([owner decision 197](#od-197)): sending from M8, hosting after C16 in the device client's network, once M8's entry has measured the plaintext an Opportunistic peer has in flight at C16's latch ([owner decision 224](#od-224)), iOS links after §22.9's measurement, private names on app paths.
- **v1:** cross-network shares through C18, with ShareKeys, per-generation ShareSigners and the preflight, and `ur tun` on macOS and Windows (M6); P2P after C3, built at M6 behind §6.6's `EnablePeerP2p` and off until [a later owner call](DESIGN-DEFER.md#proto-peer-p2p) ([owner decision 296](#od-296)).
- **Later:** [L3 delivery](DESIGN-DEFER.md#bridge-l3-delivery), [multi-hop maps](DESIGN-DEFER.md#bridge-multi-hop-maps), [IPv6 subnet routes](DESIGN-DEFER.md#bridge-ipv6-subnet-routes).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#bridge-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).

## 18. SDK, apps, and extension integration

### 18.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns `sdk/sidecar.go` and its binding gates, host services, wakes, search on devices (policy, conditions, background windows and `SidecarSearch`), remote search's requester side on app hosts (its modes, notice and states, and how apps see failover and merge), the team directory's app surface (`SidecarDirectory`, access-request approvals), the drop-history calls, the forwarding role that every app's VPN component runs ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) with its setup, keys and seam `deviceBridge` and its posture, per-platform placement (with §5, X10), the browser sidecar and its key origin (X14), cloud hosts and their allow-list, and size budgets. §17 owns the bridge engine, §7.9 and §8 admissions and the projection, §5 the gate, pairing and alarms, §11.14 the search index, its read path and remote search's wire, eligibility, failover and merge, §16.11 the directory, §11.7 and §11.13 the drop, §16 approvals, §19 the push sender; app UI is out of scope (owner rule 6).

### 18.3 What exists today

- **Bindings.** gomobile binds only `github.com/urnetwork/sdk` (sdk/build/Makefile:101, :150, :160), plus an `ios_extension` binding (:155); Android output passes `mobileexports` (:118; sdk/build/cmd/mobileexports/main.go:128-137). The signed extension had 4,690,096 B of headroom on 2026-11-02 (sdk/build/APPLE_EXTENSION_MEMORY_BUDGET.md); sdk.wasm is 74,965,628 B (2026-10-31).
- **Auth.** The Api owns the token, its refresh (sdk/device_token_manager.go:20-27; sdk/api.go:364, :3672) and the network credential (:203-207), which `.auth_state` keeps beside the device client token in a 0600 file (sdk/local_state_auth.go:31-35; sdk/local_state.go:22). A confirmed 401 reaches `AddAuthLogoutEventListener` with its generation, which `IsAuthLogoutCurrent` checks (sdk/api_auth_logout_event.go:11-39), and cause `session_revoked` only for a session the server confirms revoked (sdk/api_auth_logout_cause.go:31).
- **Extension.** Its background script (extension/manifest.config.ts:35-43) keeps a network `by_jwt` in `chrome.storage.local`, written on SSO login, an external `SET_JWT` and the ur.io bridge's `SETUP` and `REFRESH_JWT` (src/background/index.ts:134, :201-206; src/bridge/background.ts:502-508, :560-565); its sdk.wasm serves only the popup (src/utils/sdk-wasm.ts:1-10).
- **connect.** In-band auth exists (connect/transport.go:2556-2600; server/connect/transport.go:1507-1552), but without `CheckOrigin` (:1597-1601) cross-origin browser upgrades fail (gorilla/websocket@v1.5.3/server.go:89-99). Proxies are SOCKS5 only (connect/net.go:333-363). `Client.Send` takes a per-frame ack callback (connect/transfer.go:4228-4235).
- **Apps, hosted devices.** The iOS app has `aps-environment` (apple/app/network/network.entitlements:5-6); no server code sends APNs or FCM. ur.io's hosted DeviceLocal (server/proxy/proxy_device.go:1302) sets `HostedIncompatible` (:1483; sdk/device_local.go:893-910); the server knows it by its `proxy_device_config` row (server/db_migrations.go:2777) or as that client's child (server/model/network_client_retired_hosted.go:2-6).

### 18.4 Roles, placement, identity

Two roles (owner decisions [87](#od-87), [197](#od-197)). The forwarding role is all of sidecar that runs in an app's VPN component (Apple's network extension on iOS and macOS, Android's VPN service, the Windows and Linux app services): the device's IP and port forwarding, that is §17's overlay address, port forwards into the device, routes to other devices' subnets and its own advertised subnet, with no sidecar-subprotocol peer. It is `sidecar/device` with the root's forwarding files (D-SDK-20, 18.10), and it is self-contained (18.6): its own forwarding keys, its sidecar's forwarding Delegation in the authorization log (§7.9), forwarding clients it refreshes itself, and its own reading of the config repo, from which it compiles its rules, so it never waits on the app. It runs whenever the VPN component runs, and no setting turns it off. The sidecar role is the full `sidecar.Sidecar` (§5) on its own Required client: a child in the device client's network (server/model/network_client_model.go:374-394), top-level in any other ([owner decision 23](#od-23)); on app hosts it runs only while the app is open, as iOS suspends it, OS-granted windows and wakes aside (18.7), on Android too ([owner decision 197](#od-197)). A CLI host has no forwarding role: its daemon runs §17's bridge in process under its own identity key (§17.10).

| Host | Forwarding role | Sidecar role | Client (X10) | Secrets | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| iOS | network extension; 18.10's budget (owner decisions [215](#od-215), [216](#od-216), [491](#od-491)) | app, while open | child | keychain group `network.ur.sidecar`; forwarding's keys in the extension's own (§5.9) | 32 MiB |
| Android | VPN service | app, while open ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) | child | AndroidKeyStore; `noBackupFilesDir`; forwarding's under its own alias and files (§5.9) | 16 MiB, added |
| Desktop apps | network extension (macOS), `urnetworkd` (Linux), app service (Windows) | `ur daemon`; app in remote mode, the macOS app's included (18.10's tags; [owner decision 493](#od-493)) | child after §5.8's pairing | §5.9 | 128 MiB; 192 MiB designated for search (§5.4) |
| CLI, cloud VM | none | `ur daemon` | top-level, §20.8 (cloud: tagged, ephemeral, by ReaderWraps) | §5.9 | 128 MiB; 192 MiB designated for search (§5.4) |
| Extension, ur.io pages | none | Worker (18.8) | top-level, declared no-egress (§20.8) | non-extractable WebCrypto key and IndexedDB, in 18.8's key origin (quick burner: memory) | 64 MiB heap above wasm data |

Phones mirror `mailcfg`, `vault/` and `i/` in full and head-read `m/` (§11.13), and keep MLS trees on disk, one loaded at a time (≤2.83 MB at 1,000 leaves; D-KEYS-14). Of §7.9's authorization log, every sidecar, phones, page Workers and agents included, keeps what §7.9's `retain` row says, every entry from api's retention point included on member devices running `ur daemon` (desktop and CLI hosts), which a site loss resumes from (§19.10). A config writer folds once the unfolded tail spans 1,024 entries or 24 h, at its next start if it was offline (§7.9's fold), so while one runs, kept tails stay within about 2,048 entries and a new device, a page Worker included, re-applies at most about 1,024. Marks: fg, foreground; VPN, whenever the app's VPN component runs ([owner decision 197](#od-197)); awake, Firefox event page alive; outbox, D-SMTP-18; C4, §4's browser carrier.

| Feature | iOS app | Android | Desktop daemon | Extension: Chrome / Firefox |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evs, mail read, burner logins | fg | fg | yes | yes / awake |
| Search: buckets; all | fg; Wi-Fi while charging; "search more" asks a designated indexer (fg), else downloads | fg; the same | yes; background | yes / awake; "search more" |
| Mail send | fg, outbox | fg, outbox | yes (§14) | outbox |
| Socket dial | fg | fg | yes | C4 |
| Listen: mail, sockets, TLS | fg | fg | yes | no |
| Approvals, admissions, alarms (18.5) | fg | fg | app or `ur approve` (for other sidecars); presence key | alarms only |
| Forwarding (§17): routes and forwards out / hosting | VPN, links after §22.9 / VPN, after C16 | VPN / VPN, after C16 | the app's VPN component, else `ur tun` / likewise, after C16 on an app's; `ur bridge` | no |

iOS suspends backgrounded apps (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/backgroundtasks), and Android's sidecar role now runs only while the app is open, whether or not the VPN runs, OS-granted windows and wakes aside, as on iOS ([owner decision 197](#od-197)), so Android 15's 6 h daily cap on `dataSync` without a VPN [R:sdk-clients](design/design-research/sdk-clients.md) no longer bears on it; forwarding alone runs in the background, in the VPN component.

**Search (R-SDK-13, R-SDK-14; D-SDK-21, D-SDK-25 to D-SDK-28).** §11.14's read path, and on app hosts its remote search, run on each host by this policy:

```text

defaults    desktop ur daemon and indexers    background: all at each roll-up and rewrite (§11.14)

                                              designated indexer answers (remote, below)
            ur.io page Worker                 wifi_charging while a tab is open (browsers, below), plus on_demand
                                              at "search more"
            quick burner                      buckets in memory, at its first search; never all
            extension Worker (Later)          on_demand
override    per device, for one repo or every repo: SetPolicy (18.5), the key origin's search policy request

            sealed in §5.9's non-derived search state, which cache eviction keeps, never in the config repo;
            app hosts and the page Worker's main set Search.AllPolicy and Search.MemoryByteCount over

conditions  hosts report unmetered, charging and low power (18.7); a condition not yet reported, or one the

browsers    the key-origin frame reports what its browser exposes: unmetered when navigator.connection.type is

            and Firefox expose neither and desktop browsers no network type

metered     a "search more" whose missing all exceeds 25 MiB on a metered link waits, reporting

caps        phones keep all only below 256 MiB per network and 10% of free space, else on_demand, and evict

targets     warm, from the cache: phone app: buckets p50 <= 50 ms and p95 <= 150 ms, a cached five-year all
            p50 <= 150 ms and p95 <= 500 ms, working set <= 4 MiB a search; desktop: <= 10 ms and <= 50 ms, a

            and <= 300 ms (p95 1 s), <= 8 MiB, yielding every 50 ms; each working set holds the search's

            shard's hits reaching the caller within 300 ms of its landing on phones and page Workers (owner
            decision 572); §22 measures them on surrogate phones (owner decision 100) and in Safari's wasm
            engine
remote      tap to the first remote page, pre-warmed, on an indexer's warm cache of five years of mail at 100

            <= 500 ms and p95 <= 1.5 s, later pages <= 400 ms and <= 1.2 s; cold (no contract or Hello in

            surrogates from the later of M10's and M8's exits
```

### 18.5 `sdk/sidecar.go`

```go
// sdk/sidecar*.go: bound types only; no sidecar-package value crosses.
type SidecarKeyStore interface { // app-implemented, gobind-safe: a host never throws across it (D-SDK-15)
	PutSecret(name string, valueBase64 string) int32 // SidecarKeyStoreOk | SidecarKeyStoreLocked | SidecarKeyStoreFailed
	GetSecret(name string) *SidecarSecret            // never nil
	DeleteSecret(name string) int32                  // Ok (deleted or absent) | Locked | Failed
}
type SidecarSecret struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Status      int32  // SidecarSecretPresent | SidecarSecretAbsent | SidecarSecretLocked | SidecarSecretFailed
	ValueBase64 string // set only when Present
}
type SidecarPresenceSigner interface { // app-implemented: a Secure Enclave or platform FIDO key, per §16.6's profiles; nil: another device approves
	GetAttestation() string                       // the public key, registered per §16.6, its attestation none
	SignWithPresence(messageBase64 string) string // after a presence check with UV over the message (webauthn-es256: its
	                                              // SHA-256 as the challenge), base64 of §6.9's WebAuthnEvidence: key_id
	                                              // and DER signature, with authenticator_data and client_data_json for
	                                              // webauthn-es256; "" if refused
}
type SidecarSettings struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Instance, StateDir    string      // StateDir "" on js: IndexedDB
	Components            *StringList // "evs", "mail", "sockets", "bridge", "tls" (§5.4); an app lists no "bridge",
	                                  // since forwarding is its VPN component's, always on (18.4)
	MemoryBudgetByteCount int64
}
type Sidecar struct{ /* stateLock; local *sidecar.Sidecar or remote §5.8 client; the extension's Worker and native host serve it too */ }
func NewSidecarLocal(networkSpace *NetworkSpace, keyStore SidecarKeyStore, presenceSigner SidecarPresenceSigner, settings *SidecarSettings) (*Sidecar, error)
func NewSidecarRemote(presenceSigner SidecarPresenceSigner, settings *SidecarSettings) (*Sidecar, error) // `ur daemon` control mode (§5.8);
                                                                                                        // the macOS app's slices too (18.10's tags;
                                                                                                        // owner decision 493)
func (self *Sidecar) EnrollWithDevice(device Device, callback SidecarResultCallback) // child, admin_refused and strict_exp (§7.4);
                                                                                  // remote: §5.8's pairing; then runs forwarding's setup for its VPN component (18.6)
func (self *Sidecar) SetForwardingDevice(device Device) // at each start, once the app has its Device (a DeviceLocal in process on Android, a
	// DeviceRemote over the device RPC to the Apple extensions): hands the sidecar role its VPN component's Device with no
	// re-pairing, and the role runs forwarding's setup when it is due, then and at each interval after (18.6; owner decision 490)
func (self *Sidecar) Unlock(passphrase string, callback SidecarResultCallback)       // local only; "": key-store wrap, called once the store unlocks;
                                                                                  // remote: refused, the daemon unlocks (§5.9)
func (self *Sidecar) GetState() string       // locked|unenrolled|offline|online|revoked (State, below)
func (self *Sidecar) GetStateReason() string // unenrolled: expired|refused|parent_lost|session_ended|keystore_lost; revoked: signed;
	// offline: subprotocol_store_failed, valid on offline alone: a generation whose start failed on a damaged sealed
	// file in the network's subprotocol store, which raises one refused event as it enters that state (§5.9's Failed;
	// owner decision 616)
func (self *Sidecar) AddEventListener(listener SidecarEventListener) Sub // §5.4's SidecarEvent kinds: state,
	// approval_pending, member_added, member_removed, key_changed, refused, admission_alarm, recovery_rebind,
	// recovery_window, recovery_unseen, head_alarm (§6.4: fork, withheld, unverified or unwitnessed, with both
	// pins; rollback, with the held and offered TopicVersions, owner decision 300), access_request, access_decided {request_id, outcome} and directory_erasure {repo_id, outcome} (§16.11),
	// history_drop {repo_id, drop_id, state, not_before_ms}, admissions_near_cap (admin devices, §7.10's cleanup
	// list), mail_send {send_id} (§14.5),
	// search_alarm {mismatch or omission, indexer, repo}, index_mismatch and index_malformed (§11.14), erasure
	// {repo_id, SidecarErasure: fenced|rewriting|waiting|done|stalled, objects and bytes left, next try, finish}
	// (§5.4, §11.12, §11.13's wait), evs_conflict {repo_id, ref_id, path}, evs_alarm {repo_id, ref_id, path,
	// signer, reason}, evs_gap {repo_id, ref_id, verified_since_ms}, record_alarm {repo_id, sidecar_id, reason},
	// credential_store (no path or value), ct_alarm, mail_receiver_alarm {sidecar_id, repo_id} and bridge_alarm
	// {reason}, each as §5.4 lists it; each carries the repo, ref and path its kind names. A remote-mode Sidecar
	// feeds this listener from one long-poll of §5.8's events method on a second control session, so every kind
	// reaches a remote-mode app, and a gap answer sends it to GetState (owner decision 287)
func (self *Sidecar) SetPushToken(platform string, token string, callback SidecarResultCallback) // "apns"|"fcm"; "" deletes
func (self *Sidecar) SignEdgeLogin(origin string, nonceBase64 string, callback SidecarResultCallback) // §13.7 members-device; v1 (M6)
	// remote: §5.8's Confirm method tls.edge_login.sign, sent with confirmed set, the bound call being the person's act in
	// the app's UI; an unconfirmed call signs nothing (owner decision 489)
func (self *Sidecar) GetSidecarId() *Id
func (self *Sidecar) GetEvs() *SidecarEvs   // nil unless registered
func (self *Sidecar) GetMail() *SidecarMail // plus §15.9's burner, vault and one-time-code methods
func (self *Sidecar) GetSockets() *SidecarSockets
func (self *Sidecar) GetApprovals() *SidecarApprovals
func (self *Sidecar) GetSearch() *SidecarSearch // nil unless evs is registered; 18.4's search policy
func (self *Sidecar) GetDirectory() *SidecarDirectory // nil outside a team network (§16.11)
func (self *Sidecar) Close()
func (self *SidecarEvs) CreateRepo(kind string, displayName string, private bool, callback SidecarResultCallback) // §11.12;
	// the result names its repo_id; in a team network a general or record repo is announced at creation unless
	// private, which writes the private marker instead (owner decision 181)
func (self *SidecarEvs) ReadHead(repoId *Id, path string, callback SidecarBytesCallback) // §11; tokens derived and decrypted here;
	// a versionless file replaced mid-read is read again from the new head (§11.7)
func (self *SidecarEvs) ReadVersion(repoId *Id, path string, version int64, callback SidecarBytesCallback) // an older
	// version: EVS_DROPPED from its drop's not_before unless the drop is cancelled or refused, readable with that
	// time while drop_pending (§11.9); a drop never takes the head
func (self *SidecarEvs) History(repoId *Id, path string, callback SidecarHistoryCallback) // each version's time, signer,
	// versioning and state: kept | collected | drop_pending | dropped (§11.7, §11.9)
func (self *SidecarEvs) Write(repoId *Id, path string, data []byte, versioning string, callback SidecarResultCallback) // ≤1 MiB;
	// file-mode refs only; versioning "", "on" or "off" ("" keeps the path's, a new path's from its rules: §11.7;
	// owner decision 167); a versionless path's 409 is surfaced, never retried by rebasing (§11.7);
	// EVS_GIT_REF on a git-mode ref (§11.7)
func (self *SidecarEvs) AddRepoChangeListener(repoId *Id, listener SidecarRepoChangeListener) Sub
func (self *SidecarEvs) VerifiedSince(repoId *Id, refId *Id) int64 // ms: §5.4's evs_gap time for the ref, the newest
	// re-pin past §11.9's budget; 0 when nothing was skipped; a seam for a later view, no UI (owner rule 6)
// Drop history (§11.7, §11.13; owner decisions 173, 183): a preview, drop or cancel only by a repo admin, in an
// owner-bound repo only its owner's consented devices that are not read_only (owner decision 126), each a person's
// act in the app's UI; the Drops listing by any reader (§11.20)
func (self *SidecarEvs) DropHistoryPreview(repoId *Id, path string, follow bool, callback SidecarDropPreviewCallback)
	// the server's mandatory dry run: versions, bytes freed, shared and kept inline, dates, list_match, preview_id;
	// a head-mode device walks the path's versions itself, within 4 MiB of statements, and a longer history
	// answers EVS_DROP_TOO_LARGE, for a device that mirrors the repo (§11.7's cli row; owner decision 396)
func (self *SidecarEvs) DropHistory(repoId *Id, previewId *Id, confirmPath string, now bool, callback SidecarResultCallback)
	// confirmPath: the name the person typed, refused unless it is the previewed path; now skips the 7-day window
	// behind a second confirmation; repo admins' devices then raise history_drop with its cancel
func (self *SidecarEvs) CancelDrop(repoId *Id, dropId *Id, callback SidecarResultCallback) // any repo admin (owner-bound:
	// the owner's consented device) until 60 s before not_before
func (self *SidecarEvs) Drops(repoId *Id, callback SidecarDropsCallback) // each drop's state, not_before and listed
	// paths, up to 1,024 lineages, named as this device names them (I-13); a drop a hold defers reads done, as
	// everywhere (owner decision 184)
func (self *SidecarEvs) Erasures(repoId *Id, callback SidecarErasuresCallback) // each erasure the repo's erasure
	// sets list or this device runs, as a SidecarErasure (§5.4): any reader sees fenced, done or stalled, and the
	// eraser's device, or one that may finish it (§11.12's reconcile row), also its rekey objects and bytes left,
	// its next try and its finish by §11.13's wait row, so an app shows one message's erasure across a UTC day
	// and a restart
func (self *SidecarMail) GetAliases() *SidecarAliasList

	// the result names its send_id, whose outcomes GetSendResult reads and the mail_send event announces; a
	// remote-mode Sidecar calls §5.8's mail.send, mail.check_send and mail.send_result for Send, CheckSend and
	// GetSendResult, so desktop apps on `ur daemon` get all three (owner decision 288); the core's
	// MailClient.CheckSend and SendResult serve them, SendResult reading or/'s outcomes by the send_id the record
	// carries, so every device of the member answers alike, a daemon following its phone's sends (owner decision 651)
func (self *SidecarMail) CheckSend(draft *SidecarDraft, callback SidecarSendCheckCallback) // for the composer, per recipient
	// domain: mode (bdat|data|unknown), encoded bytes, the DATA cap, expected delay and ok|too_large|unknown (§14.5)

	// sent|queued|deferred|too_large|refused|tls_refused|failed, with bytes and cap, retry_after_ms or the MX's code

	// always-on receiver; in a personal network or a member scope, enabling files that device's IndexerSet for mail and
	// disabling retires it (§15.6, §7.9); local mode answers refused, as app hosts receive only while open (owner decision 197)
func (self *SidecarMail) GetReceiverCoverage() string // indexer|foreground-only|none, with Coverage's copy (below; §15.9)

                                                                 // admission alarms, parked devices included; recovery_rebind
                                                                 // alarms; on AdminSet devices, recovery windows: §7.9's
                                                                 // recovery-signed authority statements (owner decision 127);
                                                                 // recovery_unseen, where this device may revoke the
                                                                 // recovered device; access_request: §16.11's requests
                                                                 // this member approves (owner decisions 179, 180); on
                                                                 // AdminSet devices, another AdminSet member's device
                                                                 // revocation proposal this device may cosign (§5.6);
                                                                 // on admin devices, admissions_near_cap's cleanup list
                                                                 // (§7.10's cleanup row)
func (self *SidecarApprovals) AddPendingListener(listener SidecarApprovalListener) Sub
func (self *SidecarApprovals) CreateRecoveryCode(callback SidecarResultCallback) // §5.9's recovery setup for apps: runs
	// in process, draws the code, signs RecoveryBind or RecoveryRebind through the sidecar and hands the 12 words
	// to the host's UI once, never over control mode
func (self *SidecarApprovals) Decide(approvalId *Id, decision string, callback SidecarResultCallback) // as shown (§16.8):
	// request: approve|deny, an ApprovalDecision (§16.6) for the uses the request names, a template's count as the
	// agent asked it and rendered, 1 for any other action, and deny alone for a version-1 template request, which
	// names no count (owner decision 574); admission: approve signs the SidecarAdmit (§5.6), with one
	// presence check over the act where §7.9's presence row asks (owner decisions 187, 189), and for
	// a page Worker, in the same act, SidecarRevoke{removed} of each of its member's page Workers §7.10's stale row
	// lets this device revoke, an admin's included (D-TEAM-29), on the member's own device listing its other page
	// Workers to revoke through RevokeDevice, and for an AdminSet member's admission proposal its AuthorityCosign
	// and one for each stale-revocation proposal filed with it that passes that row's check; admission alarm:
	// approve signs OwnerConfirm{sidecar_id} for a parked device, revoke revokes that device (below), deny dismisses
	// it, a parked device staying parked (§2.10), and each answer for a page Worker an admin admitted also signs
	// §7.10's stale revocations this device sees and lists the member's other page Workers to revoke through
	// RevokeDevice; revocation proposal (AdminSet devices): approve signs §7.9's AuthorityCosign once the person
	// reviews §5.6's plan, which this device derives, with §5.6's approval, deny dismisses it; recovery window
	// (AdminSet devices, either kind): deny signs §7.9's RecoveryVeto naming it, countersigned as §7.9's presence
	// row asks (owner decision 187); recovery_rebind: not me signs a SidecarRevoke for compromise of the rebind's
	// signer from a since_n at or before the rebind, and I did this runs §5.9's compromise procedure, which clamps
	// since_n past the rebind for the rebind's signer, revoked last (owner decision 212);
	// recovery_unseen: revoke signs a SidecarRevoke for compromise of the recovered device from a since_n at or
	// before its activation; each once the person confirms §7.9's cascade list (what P parks and voids, what
	// stands, and each device that sealed to a binding it voids, to revoke for compromise and enroll anew if its
	// backups may hold that sealing, §5.9); deny dismisses it; a revoke answer naming a device of this member runs
	// through RevokeDevice's rules (§5.6's plan, approval, Suspend and codes), for compromise from the since_n its
	// alarm fixes, an admission alarm's at that admission; access_request: approve signs §16.11's grant (a
	// RepoGrant, an owner's EvsShare, or for reach an ApprovalDecision on channel device or presence), the decision
	// entry and the notice's rewrite, deny its decision entry and the notice's rewrite to denied, both by §16.11's
	// resumable protocol, finished after a crash from the device's ledger; admissions_near_cap (admin devices,
	// §7.10's cleanup row): revoke signs SidecarRevoke{removed} of each listed page Worker, an AdminSet member's
	// at k > 1 as proposals, under §7.9's presence row, deny dismisses it until the count rises. The signer of an
	// admission or revocation then commits what it requires in the config group and a team's directory group: an
	// Add or the new device's first wrap, a Remove and its rotation; a wrapped signer, not among §7.9's 1,000
	// leaf-entitled devices, only wraps and rotations (§7.9's commit; owner decisions 128, 144, 182)
// Revoking another of this member's devices (§5.6; D-SDK-30): a person's act in the app's UI, never MCP; a
// remote-mode Sidecar forwards each call to its daemon over §5.8's control channel, where, under Presence,
// RevokeDevice first returns the act's countersigned bytes (§7.9's presence row), which the app signs by
// SignWithPresence and sends back in a second call before the daemon signs anything
func (self *SidecarApprovals) GetDevices() *SidecarDeviceList // this member's admitted devices, this one first
func (self *SidecarApprovals) PreviewRevokeDevice(sidecarId *Id, reason string, lostAtMillis int64, sinceN int64,
	callback SidecarRevokePlanCallback) // §5.6's plan; reason lost | compromise; sinceN 0: the proposed position
func (self *SidecarApprovals) RevokeDevice(planId *Id, revokeKeys *SidecarRevokeItemList, callback SidecarResultCallback)
	// after the plan's copy (below) and the person's confirmation: SignWithPresence over the act's bytes where
	// Presence, then §5.6's statements, each with its countersignature (owner decisions 185, 187); revokeKeys:
	// the plan's key items the person left selected; the result names
	// the entry, or authority_pending:<proposal_id> while other AdminSet devices' cosigns are due; refusals carry
	// §5.6's REVOKE_ codes
type SidecarDevice struct { // json in the C ABI and js; §5.4's MemberDevice
	SidecarId        *Id
	Name             string // its config device name
	This             bool   // this device: Sign out, never Revoke
	ReadOnly         bool   // a page Worker
	Ephemeral        bool   // a quick burner
	State            string // live | pending | parked | stale | revoked (§5.4)
	AdmittedMillis   int64
	LastChangeMillis int64 // 0: none seen
}
type SidecarRevokePlan struct { // json in the C ABI and js; §5.4's DeviceRevokePlan
	PlanId      *Id
	SidecarId   *Id
	Name        string
	Reason      string                 // lost | compromise
	SinceN      int64                  // compromise: where P starts
	SinceMillis int64                  // its entry's time
	Items       *SidecarRevokeItemList // §5.4's DeviceRevokeItem rows: park | void | stands | reseal | key
	Signatures  int32                  // 1, or k for an AdminSet member's device
	Presence    bool                   // RevokeDevice runs SignWithPresence
}
type SidecarRevokeItem struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Effect, Kind, Name string
	Id                 []byte // §5.4's: 16 bytes, a recovery_binding's 32-byte key hash or a key's key_id
	Position           int64
}
type SidecarRevokePlanCallback connect.ApiCallback[*SidecarRevokePlan]
type SidecarSearchQuery struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Text         string  // §11.14's query: terms AND; "quoted" phrases; -term drops only confirmed containment
	RepoIds      *IdList // empty: every repo this sidecar reads with its index on
	Scope        string  // "cached" (default: buckets and any cached all) | "latest" | "all" ("search more")
	SinceMillis  int64   // 0: unbounded; a range inside the buckets never needs all
	UntilMillis  int64
	Fuzzy        bool   // near hits even when 3 or more exact hits exist
	AllowMetered bool   // "all" may download past 25 MiB on a metered link
	Remote       string // "" (the network's mode, 18.4) | "off": this search stays on the device
	PageSize     int32  // default 50
}
type SidecarSearchHit struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	RepoId     *Id
	Path       string
	Version    int64
	TimeMillis int64
	Title      string // subject or title
	From       string // sender, or the writer's label
	Snippet    string // verified hits: around the match; mail: i/'s snippet; else ""
	State      string // verified | confirmed | possible | near | unmatched (a local possible or near hit an
	                  // indexer's checked span disproved, which apps fold into one "not matched by" row, §11.14)
	Partition  string // latest | all
	Correction string // near: the corrected term
	By         string // "": this device | the answering indexer's config device name ("verified by")
}
type SidecarSearchProgress struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Searched, Total                  int32 // partitions
	FetchByteCount, FetchedByteCount int64
	Uncovered                        int32           // recent changes not yet searchable
	Waiting                          string          // "" | metered | offline | update
	CoveredFromMillis                int64           // the oldest time this search covered
	Remote                           string          // "" | notice | asking | answered | partial | fallback | off
	RemoteBy                         *SidecarIndexer // the indexer asked, or the one a notice names
	FallbackReason                   string          // "" | none | offline | busy | refused | unreachable | off | notice
}
type SidecarSearchStatus struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	IndexOn, FormatSupported                 bool
	Policy                                   string // background | wifi_charging | on_demand | never
	Remote                                   string // this network's mode: on | own | off
	LatestFromMillis, AllCachedThroughMillis int64  // 0: all not cached
	AllCachedByteCount, AllMissingByteCount  int64
	Uncovered                                int32
}
type SidecarIndexer struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	SidecarId     *Id
	Name          string  // its config device name
	MemberId      *Id     // its member, or a tagged device's sponsor
	Member        string
	Own           bool    // a device of this member
	State         string  // online | unreachable | busy | unknown
	Acknowledged  bool    // another member's: the person answered its notice
	ServedRepoIds *IdList // repos it answered in the last 24 h
}
type SidecarSearchListener interface { // app-implemented; called on a Go thread
	SearchPage(hits *SidecarSearchHitList, progress *SidecarSearchProgress, done bool) // replaces the last page
}

func (self *SidecarSearch) SetForeground(foreground bool) // the app at start and on each lifecycle change, a page
	// Worker's frame on tab visibility; daemon hosts never call it, and an unreported state counts as background

func (self *SidecarSearch) SetRemote(mode string, callback SidecarResultCallback) // on | own | off, this network's
func (self *SidecarSearch) AcknowledgeIndexer(memberId *Id, allow bool, callback SidecarResultCallback) // a notice's
	// answer: allow false sets own; a nil memberId clears every answer ("reset notices")

	// open the view is open, the only time a phone fetches announcements (18.4); past the metered cap its listener

	// continues from where it stopped

	// untrusted text for people

	// directory view scopes its "search more" to the directory alone by naming it in SidecarSearchQuery.RepoIds
	// with Scope "all"; on the remote backend it is nil until the daemon's directory status carries it, the
	// view's "search more" covering every repo meanwhile (owner decision 628)

	// worker's announced services (owner decision 179) or a socket, with role, expiry and reason; filed by this person

	// a repo admin; an owner-bound repo only on its owner's consented device; writes or replaces its item

	// marker over the announcement at once, and an erasure_request that the directory's erasure runner completes;
	// the result reads hidden, and SidecarEvent directory_erasure names a request still pending past 24 h (owner
	// decision 181)
type SidecarResult struct { // json in the C ABI and js
	Ok      bool
	Value   string // a repo_id, send_id, approval_pending:<id> or authority_pending:<proposal_id>

}
type SidecarResultCallback connect.ApiCallback[*SidecarResult] // one terminal result (sdk/api.go:950)
// Go only; gobind skips, mobileexports names each.
func (self *Sidecar) Core() *sidecar.Sidecar
func (self *SidecarSockets) ListenContext(ctx context.Context, address string) (net.Listener, error)
```

Rules: `*Id`, `*Time` or `int64` milliseconds, `[]byte` for byte strings that are not 16-byte ids, as `ProviderIdentity.PublicKey` binds (sdk/post_quantum_identity.go:29), `int32`/`int64` counts, `exportedList[T]` lists (sdk/gomobile.go:10-71), no NSObject names (`Description`, `Hash`) or basic-type aliases (golang/go#71827), every export under `trace` (sdk/trace.go:12, :54), since a crossing panic exits the app.

- **Gate.** Outward calls (§5.4's list) pass `Sidecar.Authorize` on both backends and return `pending` with an approval id (synchronously, `approval_pending:<id>`) until a grant or decision exists.
- **Search (D-SDK-22, D-SDK-26).** Apps only render: the core assembles partitions, masks, confirms and ranks, and chooses indexers, asks, merges and labels (§11.14); hits carry their state and possible matches are labeled; apps render the notice, the remote states and "verified by `<device>`" (18.4); a remote-mode `Sidecar` forwards these calls to the daemon (18.7) and never asks an indexer.
- **Approvals** (owner decisions [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126)-[128](#od-128), [149](#od-149), [179](#od-179), [180](#od-180)). `Decide` signs what each kind requires; admissions and `OwnerConfirm`s follow a safety-number check, never through MCP (D-CORE-13), and only the member's consented devices that are not `read_only` (§7.9, §8.5) sign its scoped admissions, `OwnerConfirm`s and owner-bound `EvsShare`s; an access request reaches the approver §16.11 names for its target. The host's own requests need the `SidecarPresenceSigner`, as does every act §7.9's presence row covers wherever this device registered a live presence key, its evidence becoming the countersignature each of the act's statements carries (§5.6; owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)); a remote-mode or `ur approve` decision signs `device` evidence only for another sidecar's request (§16.6).
