- **Device revocation (D-SDK-30).** `GetDevices` lists the member's devices from the config and the groups this device holds; `PreviewRevokeDevice` returns §5.6's plan; `RevokeDevice` signs it only on a host approval-capable for the member (§16.6) and not suspended (§5.6's caller), after `SignWithPresence` over the act's countersigned bytes wherever the plan's `Presence` is set, its evidence the countersignature that api and every member device check on each statement (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187)), an empty signature answering `REVOKE_CANCELLED`. The revoked device keeps only what it could already decrypt, and its leaves and keys go as §5.6's `effects` row says. Apps show this copy:

```text
devices     GetDevices' rows: this device first as "This device", with Sign out in place of Revoke,
            then each other device by name with "Last active <LastChangeMillis>", marked "Paused"
            (parked), "Inactive" (stale) or "Being revoked: waiting for another admin" (pending)
ask         "Revoke <name>? Last active <time>."  [It's lost]  [Someone may have used it]  [Cancel]
lost        "<name> will get nothing new from this network and can't act for you. It keeps what it had
            already downloaded. Choose this if it was wiped or broken, or is locked and nobody used
            it."
compromise  "When did you last have <name>?" [date and time]; then the plan: "Devices <name> added
            since then are paused until you confirm them: <devices>. Keys, auth keys, shares and
            recovery codes it set up since then stop working: <items>. Access and approvals it granted
            stay until you revoke them: <items>." Each reseal row: "<device> may hold a backup <name>
            could open: revoke it too and set it up again."
keys        with Presence: "Also remove these keys <name> registered:", each checked, "Uncheck a
            security key you still have"; without it: "Keys <name> registered stay until you remove
            them on a device that asks for your fingerprint, face or security key."
confirm     with Presence, the platform's prompt, "Revoke <name>"; else the app's own confirmation
pending     Signatures > 1: "Another admin must approve. Until then <name> is paused and gets
            nothing new."
cosign      Decide's revocation proposal: "<member> asks from <device> to revoke their <name>.", the
            plan, then "Approve" with the platform's prompt where Presence; while another pending
            proposal of <member>'s names <device>: "<member>'s devices asked to revoke each other.
            Check with <member> before you approve either."
done        "<name> is revoked. Your other devices are changing the keys to everything it could read;
            what it already downloaded stays on it."; with items that joined after the preview:
            "Also paused or stopped since you checked: <items>."
refusals    REVOKE_PARKS_SELF: "<name> added or confirmed this device after <time>, so revoking it
            from here would pause this device too. Pick a later time if you still had <name> then,
            choose It's lost, or revoke it from another device."; REVOKE_STALE: "Something changed.
            Check the list again.", with the new plan; REVOKE_REFUSED: "The network didn't accept
            this, so nothing changed."; UNAVAILABLE: "Can't reach URnetwork, so nothing changed."
```
- **Key store (D-SDK-15).** Statuses follow §5.9's store states (D-CORE-15): only Absent, for a network with no recorded `sidecar_id`, creates a root key.
- **Coverage (owner decisions [12](#od-12), [125](#od-125), [150](#od-150)).** `GetReceiverCoverage`'s values and copy:

```text
indexer          an IndexerSet designates a mail indexer for this user's mail (§7.9, §15.6)
foreground-only  receivers, but no mail indexer: "A phone alone cannot reliably receive mail: an indexer, an
                 always-on device (a desktop ur daemon, a NAS or VPS), is needed; time-sensitive codes may
                 not arrive" (owner decisions 12, 197)
none             no receiver; CreateBurner shows foreground-only's copy (§15.9)
every value      says nothing of sending: outbound size limits are CheckSend's and GetSendResult's
```

- **Send capability (D-SDK-31; [owner decision 125](#od-125)).** `CheckSend` runs as the person composes, and `GetSendResult` and `mail_send` follow the send, from the outbox too (§14.5). Their copy:

```text
compose     too_large: "<domain> accepts messages only up to <cap> from your devices, and this one
            is <size>. Send <domain> a smaller message; your other recipients aren't affected.";
            unknown, over the cap: "If <domain>'s mail server is an older kind, it accepts only up
            to <cap>, and this message is <size>."; data mode under the cap: "Sending to <domain>
            takes about <delay>."
results     sent; queued: "Waiting for one of your computers to send it."; deferred: "Sending
            again at <time>."; too_large: compose's copy; refused: "<domain> refused it (<code>).";
            tls_refused: §14.4's TL4 refusal; failed: "Couldn't send to <domain>."
never       an indexer, receiver or coverage setting: those are inbound (GetReceiverCoverage)
```

| Gate | Change |
|---|---|
| mobileexports | A `mobileSidecarGoOnlyIds` map; names avoid `Proxy`, an `Rpc` suffix and a `DeviceRemote` prefix, whose broad rules hide lost methods |
| C ABI | Nine handle types, `SidecarSearch`, `SidecarSearchHandle` and `SidecarDirectory` included, join `behavioralTypes` (sdk/cgo/gen/gen.go:48), Go-only members `skipMethods` (:182), `SidecarSettings` `jsonParamDefaults` (:158); `SidecarSecret`, `SidecarIndexer`, `SidecarDevice`, `SidecarRevokePlan`, `SidecarRevokeItem`, `SidecarSendCheck` and `SidecarSendResult` cross as JSON, as data structs do (:15), and `SidecarIndexerList`, `SidecarDeviceList`, `SidecarRevokeItemList` and `SidecarSendDomainList` as JSON arrays, as lists do (:178); listeners and app interfaces cross as function pointers; `NewDeviceLocalWithForwardKeyStore`, with `NewDeviceLocal`'s parameters and a final `SidecarForwardKeyStore`, which gomobile exports too, takes the VPN component's forwarding key store as function pointers, so the Windows and Linux app services give their VPN component its key store as [owner decision 197](#od-197) has every VPN component forward, `DeviceLocalSettings.SetForwardKeyStore` staying for gomobile callers and the json settings staying data ([owner decision 490](#od-490)) |
| js | The local backend carries `!js`, so sdk.wasm links no sidecar root and stays under its gate: on js `NewSidecarRemote` runs over a host-supplied `ur native-host` port, and `NewSidecarLocal` answers unsupported until the extension's own Worker (Later). The extension Worker's main (18.8) and `gen_types.go` types, the device revocation's among them, where `PreviewRevokeDevice` and `RevokeDevice` answer `REVOKE_NOT_CAPABLE` while the extension is alarms-only (18.4); the page Worker links no sdk (18.10), and its key origin offers no revocation, since it is read_only (18.8); `ur native-host` relays no call that §5.8 signs only on confirmation, §5.6's revocation included, answering `REVOKE_NOT_CAPABLE` itself |

**State (D-SDK-14).** Both backends, by client generation (§5.6):

```text
reasons     unenrolled: expired | refused | parent_lost | session_ended | keystore_lost; revoked: signed
confirmed 401 for generation g    -> unenrolled(session_ended if its cause is session_revoked, else
                                     parent_lost for a child, which sidecar.json records at pairing or sdk
                                     enrollment, and refused for a top-level client), only if
                                     IsAuthLogoutCurrent(g) at the transition; identity, keys, admission and
                                     pins kept
strict_exp passed unrefreshed     -> unenrolled(expired)
parent client removed or reaped   -> the child's confirmed 401 above, unenrolled(parent_lost): no server signal
                                     tells it from a refusal, and the remedy is the same
a core revocation hint, or a bind -> fetch the config: revoked(signed) only if a SidecarRevoke{sidecar_id}
  refused with sidecar_revoked       verifies against it, else unenrolled(refused) and an alarm
re-enrollment (EnrollWithDevice,  -> offline, binding generation n+1 under the same sidecar_id
  ur login)
generations every event names its generation; one of an older generation is dropped
```

### 18.6 Device abstractions and the DeviceRemote mirror

```go
// sdk/device_sidecar.go: unexported, so connect and netip types reach no binding.
// device.Bridge (sidecar/device) satisfies it; nil keeps today's behavior.
type deviceBridge interface {
	Route(packet []byte) connect.UserNatClient // a link, a reject client, or nil for the default route; lock- and allocation-free
	EgressHook() connect.EgressHook            // §4 C5, §17.6: pass, map or deny per flow
	Routes() []netip.Prefix                    // the block if chosen in RFC 1918 (owner decision 132), hosted addresses,
	                                           // granted prefixes and aliases, minus every local /32 the physical path
	                                           // needs (interfaces, gateways, resolvers), never the whole block; with
	                                           // those unknown, per-peer /32s instead of the block (§17.4, D-BRIDGE-12)
	LocalZone() connect.LocalZone              // §12.9's private names from the state's Names and NameZones; nil before a state
	SetPending(pending *bridge.Pending) error  // legacy -> pending, at forwarding's setup (Setup, below)
	SetState(state *bridge.BridgeState, log *device.PostureLog) error // §17.8, from the forwarding role's own compile
	                                           // (Following), with the log run that vouches for the state, from the
	                                           // component's own store; versions only rise
	ApplyDeltas(log *device.PostureLog) error  // projection deltas, verified offline against the state's anchor (§8.9)
	Status() device.BridgeStatus
	AddChangeCallback(callback func()) func()
}
// bridge is sidecar/protocol/bridge (D-SDK-20). BridgeState (§17.8) carries compiled rules, names, identities and
// share keys (§17.9), its AuthPin and the anchor; in an app the forwarding role produces Pending and states in the
// VPN component's own process (Following, below), and none crosses the device RPC. DeviceLocal also implements
// §17.10's BridgeHost (NewBridgeLink), in sidecar/device, minting each link's window clients under its forwarding
// client and signing their delegations with its forwarding key (Signing, below).
func (self *DeviceLocal) GetBridgeRoutes() *BridgeRouteList // bound, for the tun owner in its process (18.15), with its listener
func (self *DeviceLocal) SetBridgeLocalAddresses(addresses *StringList) // bound: the tun owner's interface, gateway and
	// resolver addresses from the platform's routes and DNS settings, on each path change, since
	// connect.LocalIpv4Networks sees only interface subnets, or nil where enumeration is restricted
	// (connect/tun.go:490-495); until set, Routes() exports per-peer /32s
// Device, so DeviceLocal and DeviceRemote: GetBridgeStatus() *BridgeStatus, AddBridgeStatusChangeListener(listener) Sub
```

- **Lifecycle.** Past legacy, `DeviceLocal` builds `device.Bridge` on its provider client and rebuilds it with the client, like subprotocols (sdk/device_local_subprotocol.go:95-110), at §17.5-§17.6's call sites (sdk/device_local.go:5766, :5859, :6421). On each change it re-reads hook and routes and passes `LocalZone()` to C14's `UpgradeMux.SetLocalZone` beside `SetBlocker` (:5385; [owner decision 85](#od-85)).
- **Setup (D-SDK-32; [owner decision 197](#od-197)).** The sidecar role's one act for its VPN component, in each network it has joined: in process on Android, over the device RPC to the iOS extension, and from `ur daemon` through the desktop app paired per §5.8 to the macOS extension or the Windows or Linux app service; never through MCP. After it the forwarding role holds everything it needs, and the app's absence stops nothing:

```text
when        each new client generation of the sidecar S (enrollment, re-enrollment, pairing; 18.5's State), and
            any run of the app 90 days or more after the last setup; after a DelegationRevoke of S's forwarding
            Delegation by any signer but S (§7.9), only when S's person confirms in the app's UI; the app hands
            the sidecar role its VPN component's Device at each start (18.5's SetForwardingDevice), and the role
            checks what is due then and at every interval after: the 90-day rotation, no live forwarding
            Delegation, a new client generation the core finds (owner decision 490)
steps       S is the sidecar role and C the VPN component; each step is idempotent (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4)
C0 keys     C generates, and never exports, a key set under a fresh 16-byte key_set_id in its key store's slot
            next: a forwarding key (Ed25519), a forwarding reader key (X-Wing) and its forwarding client's
            ClientKey; it replies ForwardingKeys, their public halves, a repeat while next is unpromoted
            returning the same set
S1 sign     S records forward/<network>/setup {key_set_id, the public halves, its step} and signs its
            forwarding Delegation {pubkey, reader_xwing_public_key, forward: S, and in its device client D's
            network D as host_client_id and host_client_public_key} (§7.9's forwarding row), which supersedes
            S's earlier one; delegation_id is the SHA-256 of the Signed, whose bytes it records
S2 file     POST /network/config/delta, then wait for its position n; a 409 at the tip re-signs at the new
            pin and records again
S3 key      PUT /gkm/delegation-keys/<delegation_id>, the reader key's object, which gkm answers 409 until its
            state holds the row (§10.6)
S4 wrap     the late DelegationWrap of the config's current generation to that key (§10.5's dwraps)
S5 mint     S mints its forwarding client F: POST /network/auth-client {source_client_id: S's client,
            admin_refused, strict_exp, forward_only, the VPN component's client public key} with S's DPoP proof,
            a repeat for the same key reusing F; F and its window clients act as S (D-ACL-3), and forward_only
            confines their tokens (§7.4, §7.8)
S6 hand off S returns ForwardingHandOff: Pending {network_id, genesis_sha256, sidecar_id, identity public key,
            forward_delegation_id}, the key_set_id, F's id and token with its strict_exp, the config repo's
            and group's ids, the Signed Delegation as filed and the AuthPin that carried it; no key of S
C7 check    C requires the Delegation's pubkey, reader key and, where set, host client to equal slot next's
            and this device's, its forward to name Pending's sidecar_id and its signature to verify under
            Pending's identity key, else refuses and keeps current; then it stores the token and the hand-off,
            sets Pending if legacy, and follows
C8 promote  once a state at or past that AuthPin shows the Delegation live for S, C promotes next to
            current, re-signs every live window client and deletes the old set
kill        around S2 a repeat posts the recorded bytes again and finds a copy already in the log by its id,
            since the replay row refuses a second, so one Delegation is filed; after S2 the record's step
            resumes; between C7 and C8 C keeps signing with current, which hosts admit until they apply the
            newer Delegation's entry, and with next after C8: at most one compile at each host, links failing
            closed across it and rebuilding
after       the VPN component refreshes F by its own DPoP proofs (§7.4), follows and compiles (Following) and
            signs (Signing); a forwarding client left unrefreshed 7 days, its VPN component off that long, lapses
            with no grace (D-TEAM-14), and forwarding stays pending until the app's next run mints another
```

- **Following ([owner decision 197](#od-197)).** The forwarding role takes rule changes directly, with one compiler and follower shared with the daemon (18.10):

```text
pushes      team hints reach the VPN component on its device client D in D's network (21842 registered for
            pushes only, D-PROTO-8; D minted acl_enforcing, Rules below), and in any other network by §6.8's
            long-poll on F
follow      it fetches the authorization log (GET /network/config/projection?after=) with F's config-read
            token (§7.8) and hands each page to its posture, which applies denials at once (§17.8's forwarding
            roles); when an entry is not a denial it runs a compile off the packet path, CompileDelay (2 s)
            after it and at most one each CompileMinInterval (10 s): a rows-only ConfigLog restored from its
            store judges the entries, as api's does (§7.9); DelegationWraps open the config generations
            (§10.5); the head the base names is read with the replaying head reader every leg runs, the Apple
            extensions' included (owner decisions 317, 318, 491), and checked against the base, never
            compiled into rows again; and AclEngine and §17.8's compiler produce S's state, the compile
            streaming the head's bridge ledger from the component's store and reading no fold (owner decision
            473), all released afterwards; a compile is admitted by an estimate of about five times its rows'
            bytes against the host's cap and heap ceiling (18.10's memory), and one refused or deferred leaves
            the last state in force, never pending, and raises bridge_alarm; so while the app sleeps a
            revocation applies within §8.9's targets, and a new rule, grant or block at a quiet moment within
            its p99 (owner decision 558; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4)
witness     while the sidecar role runs, it sends its witnessed AuthPin (§6.4) as a hint: the forwarding role
            fetches and verifies up to it, and a pin off its chain raises head_alarm through the status mirror;
            a fork the sidecar role finds, a full reader that re-compiles each base's rows, forces the
            forwarding role pending until a later witness clears it; between the app's runs its view is
            unwitnessed (§17.17)
```

Its posture is one state machine with §17.8's engine (D-SDK-13, D-BRIDGE-18):

```text
posture      per network, persisted in the VPN component's own store, sealed under forwarding's root key (§5.9):
             iOS and macOS, the extension's container, never the app group; Android, the VPN service's files;
             Windows and Linux, the app service's state directory
legacy       no sidecar has set up forwarding here: nil deviceBridge, today's behavior
pending      setup handed it Pending{network_id, anchor, sidecar_id, identity key}: every Network source is denied
             loopback, LAN, link-local, overlay and served-prefix destinations and every exit; the block deny
             stands; maps and hosted addresses refuse
enforcing    a state its own compile verified, and the anchored deltas after it, re-verified offline against the
             anchor and restored before the first packet on every start; {doc}: §17.6's rules; {nodoc}: owner
             decisions 50, 105 and 120's allow-all, entered only on a verified base above the persisted
             document_seen_at latch (the newest pin at which has_document was true)
stored       the anchor, the newest verified AuthPin, the signed base header and rows, the statements since,
             document_seen_at, the config generations and compiled state its last compile used, the entries
             waiting for a compile with the time each was first seen, which times the alarm and nothing else
             (owner decision 487), and a fork its sidecar role reported, every record sealed under
             forwarding's root key and the highest pin committed kept in the key store as its floor (§5.9;
             DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4)
overlay      the denials it checked by signature and applies between compiles (§17.8's forwarding roles) move to
             the component's sealed store in the review phase, streamed and indexed with only an index and a
             cache in RAM (owner decision 366), so storage alone bounds them and the per-flow check reads the
             index; until then PostureSettings.OverlayMaxCount (4,096) bounds them, and past it a denial the
             posture verified and cannot hold makes its decision pending until a state at or past that denial
             (PostureDecision.OverlayFullThroughN), the posture following the chain and alarming malformed once
             a call: it denies rather than silently stops applying denials (owner decision 485)
transitions  legacy -> pending -> enforcing{doc|nodoc}; back to legacy only on this sidecar's own sign-out,
             a Signed SidecarRevoke whose sidecar_id and signer_id both equal Pending's sidecar_id, whose
             network is Pending's and whose signature verifies under Pending's identity key (§17.8's
             any -> legacy), which wipes the stored state and forwarding's keys; another sidecar's sign-out or
             an admin's revocation of this one lowers nothing, and a later Pending for the same network and
             anchor replaces the stored id and key and changes no state
never        an unverified projection, one that does not chain, a lower version, a state below the one in
             force or an unsigned has_document changes the posture; one that fails to verify leaves it
             unchanged and alarms; a store below the key store's floor, or at it on another chain, is a
             rolled-back copy, pending with store_rolled_back until a follow brings the pin back to the floor
             on the floor's chain
DP1          after a device's first verified state, no restart, delay or unsigned response lowers enforcement
so           an unverified projection is never read; a verified no-document state keeps owner decisions 50,
             105 and 120's allow-all
```

- **Signing (D-SDK-13, D-SDK-32).** The forwarding role signs its own links' delegations, so no link waits on the app:

```text
sign     per window client a link builds (§17.9's sign), the VPN component signs its WindowDelegation with the
         forwarding key: subject S, signer_id the forwarding Delegation's delegation_id (§6.9), not_after_ms at
         most the window client's strict_exp, which F's children inherit; on a share link, with the share's
         current BridgeShareSigner, read from the config, while its ShareCert is unexpired (§17.9); the window
         clients are F's children, so C13 seals S's client as their subject
only     the forwarding key signs nothing but S's WindowDelegations (§7.9's forwarding row); targets check
         every flow against their own state (§17.9's use), so it gains no reach S lacks
host     in D's network, the device's hosted address, maps and served prefixes run on D's sdk provider once
         C16 lands (D-SDK-3), which S's forwarding Delegation names, so senders link to D and check its key
         (§17.9's target); in any other network an app device hosts nothing
```

- **Rules.** An sdk mints its device client `acl_enforcing` (§7.7) only after its forwarding role leaves legacy, so its resident publishes `team` hints to it (§6.8); earlier or older-sdk clients stay legacy until the app re-mints them ([owner decision 106](#od-106)), its sidecar re-enrolling (18.5's State). `checkDeviceSubprotocolId` (sdk/device_local_subprotocol.go:85-93) also refuses 21842-21851 to apps.
- **Mirror.** Bridge status and forwarding's setup calls (the keys' public halves out, the hand-off in, the witness hint) are additive, like network peers (sdk/device_rpc.go:6202-6232, :12100-12135, :14388), each listed in its method table (sdk/device_rpc_methods.go:18, :234): an older peer answers unlisted methods as unknown (:9-18), so `DeviceRpcVersion` stays 3 (:7677). No other sidecar-role API crosses the device RPC, and no key: forwarding's keys never leave the VPN component, and S's never enter it.

### 18.7 Host services the sdk injects

| Service | sdk host | Into §5.4's `SidecarHost` |
|---|---|---|
| JWT, refresh | an Api session holding only the child token (sdk/api.go:182-192), `strict_exp` for 7 days ([owner decision 131](#od-131)); `StartJwtRefresh` at 40-50% of lifetime; refresh carries a DPoP proof from a signer sdk/sidecar.go installs (`Api.SetDpopSigner`, Go only, from the core's ClientKey), and none is sent without one | `TokenSource()`; D-CORE-8's refresher off once the signer is installed; the host's session adopts no re-minted token, since `POST /sidecar/bind` answers the generation alone and sockets reads the sidecar from a service token (§5.6, §9.8; [owner decision 588](#od-588), reversing [owner decision 286](#od-286)'s adoption) |
| Logout | `AddAuthLogoutEventListener` (confirmed 401, with its generation; `IsAuthLogoutCurrent` at the transition) | `Unenrolled` with a reason; `Revoked` only on a verified `SidecarRevoke` (D-SDK-14) |
| State, secrets | `StateDir` or IndexedDB; the app's `SidecarKeyStore` | `Store()`, re-sealing tokens on refresh; `KeyStore()` |
| Conditions, foreground, background windows | the app's `SetConditions` and `SetForeground` on each change, `SetForeground` at start too, a page Worker's frame reporting tab visibility, and the app's OS window calling `RunBackgroundSync` (below); daemon hosts report no foreground, and an unreported state counts as background | the search engine's sync windows and the foreground row below (D-SDK-23) |

**Network credential (I-6; [owner decision 45](#od-45)).** Same-user agents read `.auth_state` and the extension's `chrome.storage.local` (18.3), so two releases precede §7.4's stage 2 (M3): the desktop app's stops persisting `by_jwt` once the device client exists, re-authenticates for admin actions, seals `.auth_state` in an app-only OS keystore where one exists, and mints device clients `admin_refused`; the extension's stops persisting `by_jwt` in `chrome.storage.local` at each of 18.3's four writes, re-authenticating where it needs one.

**Search windows (D-SDK-23, D-SDK-27).**

```text
window      iOS: a BGProcessingTaskRequest with requiresExternalPower and requiresNetworkConnectivity
            (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/backgroundtasks/bgprocessingtaskrequest), which cannot
            require an unmetered path, under the processing background mode and a permitted identifier the app
            adds (its Info.plist lists only fetch and network.ur.update-tunnel:
            apple/app/URnetwork-Info.plist:17-20, :96-99); Android: WorkManager periodic work with
            setRequiresCharging(true) and NetworkType.UNMETERED
            (https://developer.android.com/reference/androidx/work/Constraints.Builder); each calls
            RunBackgroundSync(budget), which does 18.4's window work while the reported conditions allow it,
            asking again before each read of all (owner decision 583), stops at the budget and resumes next
            time
conditions  SetConditions(unmetered, charging, lowPower) on each change: iOS NWPathMonitor (unmetered =
            neither isExpensive nor isConstrained), UIDevice batteryState, ProcessInfo
            isLowPowerModeEnabled; Android NET_CAPABILITY_NOT_METERED, BatteryManager.isCharging,
            PowerManager.isPowerSaveMode
foreground  an app host with remote search on opens or reuses the Network contract with an own search
            indexer when a search needs it, sending §6.4's Hello with feature bit 1 (§6.11) where it finds
            no session there, and keeps no pair warm and sends no keepalive Ping (owner decision 609), its
            hourly HeadCheck round counting its own indexers among its own-device picks; a HelloResult
            within 3 s marks an indexer online for 10 min; another member's indexer is asked only once its
            notice is answered
control     a remote-mode Sidecar forwards Search, GetStatus and SetPolicy over §5.8's control channel to
            the daemon as a stream, asking for untrusted hits' text, since a person reads them (§5.8), so the
            desktop app and the extension's native host use the daemon's cache and policy; it never asks an
            indexer, its daemon holding all: GetIndexers lists none, and SetRemote and AcknowledgeIndexer
            answer refused
```

**Wake pushes (owner decisions [17](#od-17), [88](#od-88); D-SDK-16).** Apps call `SetPushToken` at every launch, posting `{platform, token}` to `POST /sidecar/push-token`; the server keeps one per client in `sidecar_push_token`, with a revision that each change raises, projected as `tok` below in revision order (step 0, WK5). The queue and the sentinels aside, every key below sits in the client's slot `{scp_<C>}`, and no command spans two slots:

```text
{scp_<C>}live    EX 90; its publisher (§6.8) refreshes it every 30 s
{scp_<C>}tok     api's projection of sidecar_push_token's {platform, token} at the revision tokrev holds, as
                 <platform>\n<token>, which only the sender parses; absent while the row is a tombstone (no
                 token); written only by step 0's apply script
{scp_<C>}tokrev  the newest revision of C's row applied to tok, a decimal string; no TTL
{scp_<C>}ack     the highest hint stream id C's connect stack acked; EX 3600; written only while tok exists
{wakeq_<shard>}  16 streams in their own slots: {c, t, v, h, hint_millis, due_millis}, MAXLEN ~10000; the
                 writer's hash of C picks the stream, since the sender reads all 16
{tokgen_<n>}     16,384 sentinels, one per hash slot (n the least integer whose tag hashes to it), each holding
                 the run_id of the master that served the slot at its last reconcile (step 5); like tok and
                 tokrev, no TTL, so volatile-ttl never evicts them
                 (xops/main/ansible/templates/redis/redis.conf.j2:1184)
0 token    a change to C's sidecar_push_token row (a POST, an empty POST, a vendor rejection, C's removal)
           raises its rev by one in the statement that makes it, a removal leaving a tombstone (no
           platform or token) and a new row's rev starting at its insert's time in milliseconds, above any
           rev a lost row of C reached before a Postgres restore (§19.10), as rows change far less than
           once a millisecond; its writer reads t0, the TIME of the master serving {scp_<C>}, before the
           transaction, commits, then runs the apply script on {scp_<C>}: EXPIRED when that master's TIME
           is over 60 s past t0; STALE when tokrev > rev; nothing written when tokrev = rev; else SET
           tokrev and SET tok, or DEL tok for a tombstone; an EXPIRED or failed apply rereads t0 and the
           row and applies again, at most 3 times; a POST equal to the row commits nothing and applies the
           row as it stands; revisions stay far below 2^53, so the script compares them exactly
1 hint     §6.8's one EVALSHA on {scp_<C>}: HSET ver if higher; INCR n -> seq; XADD hint with seq -> h;
           return {h, tok, live}
2 enqueue  after the script, the owning service, only if tok and the topic is mail, team, evs or core, XADDs
           to {wakeq_<hash(C) mod 16>}: due now if forced or live is absent, else now + 15 s (a deferred
           check); forced: §15.6's router on a receiver miss, and POST /sidecar/wake (§6), which writes a core
           hint; an XADD error is retried 3 times within 1 s, then counted
           (urnetwork_wake_enqueue_dropped_total) and dropped, the hint state untouched
3 ack      the publisher sends each coalesced PushHint batch with connect's frame ack (18.3) and, on the ack,
           raises {scp_<C>}ack to its h
4 send     §19.4's push sender reads each stream through one consumer group, holds entries in a heap by
           due_millis and at due MGETs ack, tok and tokrev: ack >= h or no tok drops the entry; otherwise
           it wakes under §19.4's per-client coalescing (one wake per 10 s) and vendor caps, then XACKs; a
           crash before XACK redelivers through XAUTOCLAIM after 30 s idle; entries over 60 s old are dropped;
           a vendor 410 or UNREGISTERED tombstones the row only while its rev equals the tokrev read with
           that token, so it never removes a newer registration (step 0)
5 loss     taskworker's pass, every 60 s, compares each sentinel with the run_id (INFO; random per process
           start, https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/8.10.0/src/server.c initServerConfig) of the master
           CLUSTER SHARDS shows serving its slot; with no replicas, a master that comes back empty or from
           its last RDB dump, its only persistence (xops/main/ansible/templates/redis/redis.conf.j2:453,
           :1420; xops/main/ansible/REDIS.md:140-141), or that newly serves a slot leaves the sentinel
           absent or naming another run_id; each such slot is reconciled at the first pass at least 90 s
           after the pass that found it, if the same master still serves it: read t0; list the slot's tok
           and tokrev keys (CLUSTER GETKEYSINSLOT); then read its rows by sidecar_push_token.slot and apply
           each (step 0); DEL tok and tokrev of each listed client that has no row, a row being committed
           before any key of its client exists; then SET the sentinel; every apply begun before that
           master took the slot has expired by then, §19.6's chrony holding masters' clocks within 50 ms,
           and later ones are ordered by its tokrev; one master's slots take about 2 s per million tokens,
           all 16,384 about 50 s, at 20,000 writes/s, after the 90 s (FS-36: one master killed, one
           restarted from an older dump)
6 sweep    the same pass applies every row changed since 2 min before the last completed pass began, so an
           apply lost with a killed api lands within about 2 min with no app launch, and deletes each row
           24 h after its client's removal, after DELing its tok and tokrev (FS-120)
WK1  no script or MULTI spans two hash slots: a CROSSSLOT lint, and a 3-master cluster in T3
WK2  a wake-class hint to a token holder yields a vendor submission by due plus the sender's lag, unless
     the client's stack acked a stream id >= h, coalescing folds it into a later wake, a vendor cap
     applies, or the wake is lost: its enqueue dropped after step 2's retries (counted by
     urnetwork_wake_enqueue_dropped_total) or with a service killed after the script (uncounted), its
     entry older than 60 s or lost with its master, or its tok absent until step 5 reconciles the slot
WK3  losing a wake-queue entry never changes hint state
WK4  wake payloads carry a topic class and a version only (owner decision 88)
WK5  while the slot's sentinel names its serving master, tok moves only up its row's revisions: an
     apply lands only above tokrev and within 60 s of its t0, so once a change commits, tok equals the
     newest row (absent for a tombstone) as soon as that change's apply, a retry or step 6 lands, or
     step 5 reconciles a slot whose master changed, and no older token or removed one returns; until
     that reconcile, at least 90 s after the pass that found the new master, tok may hold an older or
     removed token, from an older dump or an apply begun before that master took the slot
```

- **Resync.** The app resyncs over HTTPS (§6.8); no wake event outlives §6's hourly key (§2.8 api-6, ext-8).
- **Best effort.** Apple asks for at most two or three background pushes an hour (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/pushing-background-updates-to-your-app); FCM may demote silent ones (https://firebase.google.com/docs/cloud-messaging/android/message-priority).

```text
APNs  apns-push-type background, apns-priority 5   {"aps":{"content-available":1},"t":"mail","v":42}
FCM   data message, priority high                  {"data":{"t":"mail","v":"42"}}
      t: mail | team | evs | core (§6.8's topic with any id stripped); v: that topic's version; never an id;
      APNs's v is the stored decimal string's digits as a JSON integer, never through a float and with no
      exponent, within uint64, and FCM's stays a string
```

- **Directory notices (D-SDK-28).** From M8 a phone leases the team directory's `q/<h>/<tgt>/` prefixes for the targets its member approves, and the notice path of each of its own pending requests (§16.11, §11.10), so a decision, a denial's included, rewrites a notice the phone leases. Their hints are `evs:<repo_id>` hints like any lease's (§6.8), so they are wake-class: a request or its decision wakes the phone under topic class `evs`, naming no directory, target or request.

### 18.8 The browser sidecar (X14): the extension and ur.io pages

```text
ur.io:     page, labeled as served code (§2.8 EX7) -> iframe https://sidecar.ur.io/v1/ (key origin)
             -> Worker: sidecar.wasm; the quick burner memory-only
Chrome:    extension page -port urnetwork-sidecar-v1-> service worker (relay; mints client; alarms)
             -> offscreen document (reason WORKERS; alarms re-create it) -> Worker: sidecar.wasm (IndexedDB, WebCrypto)
Firefox:   event page -> Worker: sidecar.wasm; both unload when idle (MDN)
meanwhile: connectNative -> `ur native-host` (stdio) -> `ur daemon` control mode (§5.8)
carrier:   first HTTPS-only: §6 long-poll, §10, §11 (config repo too) | later wss H1 + in-band protocol.Auth (§4 C4)
```

- **Phasing (owner decisions [15](#od-15), [26](#od-26), [76](#od-76)).** HTTPS-only needs neither C4 nor C17, so the page Worker, on 18.10's `sidecar_http` leg, serves ur.io/recurd from RS1 (M4) and the team console from RS2 (M6).
- **Carrier.** C4's `GOOS=js` WebSocket carrier, templated on sdk/device_rpc_platform_js.go, needs the server to admit `chrome-extension://` ids, the `moz-extension:` scheme (per-install UUID origins, https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1372288) and the key origin `https://sidecar.ur.io`, safe since auth is a bearer frame.
- **Identity (owner decisions [112](#od-112), [114](#od-114), [126](#od-126), [144](#od-144)).** Each Worker but the quick burner is an untagged member device, admitted per §5.6 with the member's consent (§8.5) and counted in `config_admissions` (§20.4). The page Worker reads records, receipts and the config's names, tags, groups and policy (owner decisions [46](#od-46), [67](#od-67)); it is admitted `read_only` (§7.9), so every verifier refuses what it signs but its sign-out `SidecarRevoke`, its own ReaderKeys, KeyPackages and leaf's MLS maintenance under its r scopes (§10.6), read receipts and, from §4.6's C4 (Later), HeadCheck replies, and it is never approval-capable (§16.6) or a key deliverer; until C4 it runs no HeadCheck, so a page's view is unwitnessed and shows no `witnessed_at` (§7.9's read_only row). The extension's service worker, or on ur.io the key origin by its sign-in hand-off ([owner decision 219](#od-219)), mints one `admin_refused`, `strict_exp` top-level client declaring no egress (§20.8), re-minted under its `sidecar_id` after expiry (§5.5); the Worker gets only its token, never listens, and serves only its own pages. `nativeMessaging`, which warns of "cooperating native applications", stays optional (Firefox 87+, https://bugzil.la/1630415).
- **Key origin (D-SDK-18).** ur.io pages frame it and message it by exact origin:

```text
pages       https://ur.io/recurd, the console and the quick tools render views and hold no sidecar key, sidecar
            token or wrapped secret, though ur.io's account panel keeps a network byJwt in localStorage while a
            member is signed in on that browser, with which a page calls /auth/code-create for the key
            origin's sign-in and hands it the one-time code (owner decision 219); the team console shows the
            directory, and the drops of the repos it reads with their states and the device command; it files
            no request or decision and never dry-runs, signs or cancels a drop (read_only, admin_refused;
            D-SDK-29)
key origin  https://sidecar.ur.io/v1/, served direct from the lb, never through Cloudflare, which terminates
            https://ur.io (§2.8 EX7, §19.5's W10; owner decision 211), serves only a promoted build's loader
            and sidecar.wasm, both listed in the release's signed SHA256SUMS (§4.10), the loader pinning
            sidecar.wasm's SHA-256 and checking it before instantiating: signed means listed in those sums,
            so anyone can compare the served bytes, and no browser verifies them on load, so EX7 stands
            (owner decision 221); its CSP is exactly default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'
            'wasm-unsafe-eval'; connect-src 'self' <18.9's hosts>; frame-ancestors https://ur.io, worker-src
            falling back to script-src, and its framing rests on that frame-ancestors alone: the lb sends it
            no X-Frame-Options, warp's services.yml listing it among the exact hosts the lb sends none for,
            checked as no_access_log's are, while every other host keeps SAMEORIGIN (owner decision 486); its
            Worker holds IndexedDB, the non-extractable WebCrypto root key and its token
sign-in     the hand-off from the ur.io session (owner decision 219): the page calls /auth/code-create and
            posts the one-time code; the key origin runs /auth/code-login, mints the page Worker's client with
            POST /network/auth-client and drops the network token, and re-mints the same way under its
            sidecar_id after a lapse
messages    postMessage, accepted only when event.origin is exactly https://ur.io in production (per-env
            lists; never localhost or http:); requests name an operation (sign-in, list, read view, record
            view, directory view, drop states, search, search more, search cancel, search status, search
            policy, sign-out); replies carry plaintext views only, search hits as display fields and states;
            GetSecret's strings never leave the Worker
storage     one IndexedDB database per network, urnetwork-sidecar-v1-<network_id>, each its own sidecar
            instance with its own instance document and WebCrypto root key, so two networks' page Workers
            share nothing and the instance row's Web Lock covers everything a Worker writes (owner decision
            217); same-site with ur.io, so not partitioned in first-party use (§22.9's reload test checks it);
            the search cache is its own IndexedDB store, written only by the lock holder (D-SDK-24); a browser
            clears an origin's storage bucket in its entirety (https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/, §7), every
            network's keychain, MLS state and token with the cache: under storage pressure unless the bucket is
            persistent, and in Safari after seven days of Safari use without user interaction on the site,
            Home Screen web apps keeping their own count
            (https://webkit.org/blog/10218/full-third-party-cookie-blocking-and-more/); so the frame calls
            navigator.storage.persist(), which Safari grants by heuristics such as a Home Screen web app
            (https://webkit.org/blog/14403/updates-to-storage-policy/, 2023-08-10), and the page tells the
            person what an eviction costs: the next Worker enrolls anew (admission, below)
instance    one Worker per network (§22.9's two-tab case), as §5.8's flock keeps one daemon: a Worker opens
            a network's state only while it holds the Web Lock urnetwork-sidecar-<network_id> (exclusive,
            scoped like IndexedDB to the storage bucket: https://w3c.github.io/web-locks/), so only the
            holder loads the keychain, MLS state and token, refreshes, commits and writes; every other Worker
            loads no state and relays its page's requests, and the views back, over a BroadcastChannel of
            that name; the lock frees with the holder's Worker (its tab closed, reloaded, crashed or
            discarded), and the next waiter reloads from IndexedDB, relayed requests retrying; Chrome 133+
            does not freeze a tab whose lock blocks another
            (https://developer.chrome.com/blog/freezing-on-energy-saver, 2025-01-20); the frame refuses to
            start without locks (before Chrome 69, Firefox 96, Safari 15.4), while a SharedWorker would need
            Chrome 148 on Android (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data, 2026-11-05); quick burners,
            memory-only, take none
extension   (Later) its Worker accepts only its own extension pages' ports, never a content-script relay,
            and takes the same lock
admission   a page Worker or quick burner needs a consented device of its member online to admit it (§5.6),
            and the quick burner also to sign its EvsShare; with self_admit off, an admin admits a page
            Worker, which stays parked in owner-bound repos until OwnerConfirm; a Worker enrolling after an
            eviction is a new sidecar_id, adding a config_admissions entry (§20.4); the device admitting it,
            an admin's included, and the member's consented device revoke the member's stale page Workers as
            §7.10's stale row says (D-TEAM-29), so evictions pile up only as that row bounds, and from 90%
            of the cap admins' devices list the rest to revoke (§7.10's cleanup)
leaves      each page Worker is a read_only MLS leaf of each group it reads, within D-KEYS-2's 1,000 per
            group; in the config and directory groups, unless §7.9's rank makes it one of the 1,000
            leaf-entitled, it reads by wraps (owner decisions 144, 182); sign-out removes it, and an unused
            or evicted one goes by §10.9's stale-leaf Removes, 90 days after its leaf last changed
disclosed   script running in https://ur.io (served code, Cloudflare's altered page script, an XSS, an
            extension with page access) can request views while it runs, never the Worker's key or token, so
            that access ends with it; it can also take the account panel's network byJwt from localStorage
            while a member is signed in on that browser, and the sign-in hand-off's one-time code as it
            crosses the page, which reaches network-credential routes, but a client
            minted with it gets no admission, key or plaintext without a consented device (§5.6, §7.9; §2.4,
            §2.10); until §4.6's C4 a page's view is unwitnessed, since its Worker runs no HeadCheck
```

- **Quick burner (Q-SDK-4).** An ephemeral sidecar: a memory-only keychain (§5.6) on an `ephemeral` client (§7.7), never a genesis signer, reading the member's mailbox by ReaderWraps through an `EvsShare` (§8.8, §15.7) that the consented device admitting it signs, and reaped 30-36 min after its last poll (the lease below, §7.10); with no consented device of its member online, the page waits. It searches the mailbox's two buckets in memory only and never fetches all.
- **Lease (D-SDK-17).** No resident measures an HTTPS-only host's disconnect, so its polls carry its liveness, in a narrow table rather than `network_client.auth_time`, whose every write updates that table's ~10 indexes, so `ConnectNetworkClient` refreshes it at most hourly (server/model/network_client_model.go:3625-3634):

```text
lease        network_client_lease(client_id PK, seen_time, close_sha256 unique): one row per ephemeral
             client, inserted at its mint (§7.7); a GET /sidecar/sync/poll whose SET {scp_<C>}hb 1 NX EX
             300 sets, or errs, writes seen_time = now, so at most once per 300 s while Redis answers
reap         taskworker's ephemeral job, every 60 s, reaps (§7.10) each ephemeral client with no open
             connection whose seen_time and newest connection disconnect_time, if any, are both over 35
             min old, probing each lease row past 35 min by network_client_connection's (client_id,
             connect_time) index (server/db_migrations.go:3149-3152; closed rows live 8 h,
             server/taskworker/work/network_client_work.go:93): 30-36 min after the last poll, 35-36 min
             after the last disconnect, so an agent connected for hours survives any disconnect under 35 min
close        §7.8's enroll and auth-client responses return an ephemeral client's 128-bit close capability
             once, api keeping only its SHA-256 (§7.7); the key-origin document, not the Worker, holds it
             and on pagehide sends navigator.sendBeacon(POST /sidecar/close) with it as a text/plain body,
             since sendBeacon sets no Authorization header and Workers lack it; the Public route (§6.16)
             reaps the client whose close_sha256 matches at once; best effort, the lease bounding the rest
generations  each poll authenticates its own client_id; a reaped or revoked client's polls get 401 and
             write nothing, so no old generation keeps a replacement alive
suspended    a tab suspended over 36 min is reaped; on resume its polls get 401 and the page offers
             re-enrollment, since a memory-only keychain cannot rejoin
cost         one narrow-row write per ephemeral page per 5 min (about 33/s for 10,000 pages) and one
             index probe per lease row past 35 min per run; auth_time refreshes on a connect and on a
             strict_exp refresh, GET /auth/refresh taking refreshClientAuthTimesInTx's one-hour gate
             (server/model/network_client_model.go:3882), a child's source client included, so an HTTPS-only
             client refreshing at 40-50% of 7 days writes it about once per 3 days and the 30-day idle sweep
             never takes it in use; no poll writes network_client (§6.16)
```

### 18.9 Headless and cloud agents

| Rung | Carrier | Needs | Gives |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | H1 wss direct | egress to the platform host | everything |
| 2 | H1 via HTTP CONNECT (`HTTPS_PROXY`) | §4 C8 (M4), including API dials | everything |
| 3 | HTTPS-only | the required hosts below | evs, records, long-poll; no streams, sockets or mail send |

[Owner decision 49](#od-49) runs `ur` in the VM on rung 2, as a desktop daemon without mail receipt. `ur` embeds its allow-list and the issuer SPKIs of its hosts, `ur status` probes each entry, and mmm publishes the list at `https://ur.io/recurd/hosts/v1.json`, versioned by path, as `{"version":1,"hosts":[{"host":"...","tcp":443,"need":"..."}]}` generated from the one table `ur` embeds, which is also the one copy of the service urls: `DefaultSidecarSettings` leaves them empty, `NewSidecar` refuses until a host sets them, and cli and sdk hosts fill them from this table (§5.4; [owner decision 282](#od-282)), tests staying on `.example` names:

```text
host                          tcp  need
api.bringyour.com             443  required: enrollment, /sidecar, /acl, /tls, /mail, long-poll (§6)
auth.bringyour.com            443  required: login, token exchange (§7.8; server/IDP.md:18)
evs.bringyour.com             443  required: storage (§11)
gkm.bringyour.com             443  required: MLS (§10)
connect.bringyour.com         443  rungs 1-2: RPC, streams, sockets, mail, bridge; UDP 443 (H3) optional
sockets.bringyour.com         443  with sockets (§9)
dns.bringyour.com             443  with records or TLSA (§12.8)
api.certspotter.com, crt.sh   443  with tls: the CT watch (§13)
ur.io                         443  optional: install.sh, the release key, this list
```

Claude Code cloud adds secrets at its proxy (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cloud-environments), so the proxy may see bearer tokens, never Required-mode traffic or repo content; `ur status` reports interception (§2.4), a chain ending outside those SPKIs, without blocking it. Offline agent phases spool (§16.9).

### 18.10 Build and size

- **Imports.** sdk imports the sidecar root and `protocol` in sidecar-role files, and in forwarding files `sidecar/device`, `protocol/bridge` and the root's forwarding files, by a new rule on sdk/dependency_boundary_test.go's legs (:80-92); §4.7's `make check` fails the `ios_extension` leg if its root files leave the forwarding list below or it registers a `protocol` descriptor outside it (D-SDK-20).
- **Forwarding leg ([owner decision 197](#od-197); D-SDK-20).** Every VPN component runs forwarding and no other sidecar code: Apple's extensions link only forwarding, as the `ios_extension` leg, and the Windows and Linux app services the same file list, while Android's VPN service runs in the app's own binding, where the sidecar role's code is present but runs only while the app is open (18.4):

```text
links       sidecar/device and sidecar/protocol/bridge whole; of the root, built with ios_extension, only the
            files on the leg's list, check/testdata/ios_extension_leg.txt, which check/ regenerates as the
            closure of the Forwarder's files and §17.8's compiler (owner decision 275): 269 of 428 root files
            when first computed on 2026-11-10 and 395 of 906 on 2026-11-17, many there for one type or
            constant, since the root's files are not layered, and the linker keeps only what an entry point
            reaches; through them the every-leg types and SidecarApi, the forwarding client's DPoP refresh
            (§7.4), the rows-only follower and config verification (§7.9), DelegationWrap unwrap, X-Wing and
            the key ladder (§10.5), evs head reads of the config repo, a base's head by the replaying config
            head reader every leg runs, with the push records' readers and the seal part record's parser it
            needs (§11; owner decisions 317, 318, 491), AclEngine (§8), §17.8's statements and compiler and
            forwarding's signer; of protocol, every generated file but mail.pb.go and socket.pb.go, which
            protocol/Makefile tags; operator-core, whose Id the root's aliases (owner decision 251); and sdk's
            device_sidecar*.go, which name the root only through the Forwarder (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4)
leaves      every other root file, by its !ios_extension tag, as connect-facing ones carry !sidecar_http:
            every mail_, search_, host_, daemon_ and indexer_ file, most smtp_, socket_, tls_, dns_ and evs_
            files and some record_ files; and by module, mail's servers and verifiers, DNS, ACME and its test
            server, the MCP sdk, brotli and yaml.v3, with x/text's legacy encodings and x/net's HTML parser,
            whose tables a package-level variable roots past any dead-code pass: no listed file imports them,
            and make check refuses each in the leg's go list -deps beyond what connect links there itself
            (§4.7's legs); without the tags the same entry points measured 1,885,888 B more, stripped
            (2026-11-10)
never       cli/, mcp/, smtpproof, sidecarctl and every <svc>service: other modules or packages
make size   from M4 the leg adds at most 7.5 MiB (7,864,320 B) of executable over today's binding, measured
            stripped as the shipped binding is (owner decision 491, amending 215's 6 MiB), and the signed iOS
            extension's ceiling rises from 50 MiB to 54 MiB (56,623,104 B) (owner decision 215); owner
            decision 491 is the revisit with measurements that owner decision 251 foresaw: on 2026-11-15,
            with go1.27.4 and the replaying head reader on the leg, the leg added 7,009,216 B, 1,000,736 B of
            it the reader and the evs client it links, with no new package, leaving 855,104 B of room; a
            read-only evs core for the leg's reader is review-phase work, beside owner decision 366's
            storage-backed replay
memory      forwarding's Go heap at most 4 MiB steady, inside the iOS tunnel's 28 MiB target and 32 MiB soft
            limit (sdk/build/APPLE_EXTENSION_MEMORY_BUDGET.md); a compile is transient, and in the iOS and
            macOS extensions it is admitted only when 5 x rows + 2 x head + 1 MiB fits a 10 MiB per-compile
            cap and the room under a 30 MiB process ceiling, about 4,300 devices at the tunnel's connected
            baseline, waiting for room under provider load, the head reader's replay holding the head's files
            in memory up to that cap as the compile does (owner decision 491); a larger network keeps its
            last verified state on that device, applies at once every revocation it can check by signature,
            holding each in the posture's overlay (18.6), which past its bound makes the decision pending
            rather than stop applying them (owner decision 485), and raises bridge_alarm narrowing_overdue,
            with the oldest waiting statement's position and age, once a statement that could narrow reach
            and that it cannot check by signature has waited NarrowingOverdueTimeout (10 minutes) for a
            compile, again at doubling intervals (20 min, 40 min and so on) up to once a day while that
            lasts, and at once for each further statement that becomes overdue, the condition staying in the
            posture's status until the first compile clears it (owner decision 487); no VPN component goes
            pending for that wait, so forwarding never drops for it, the next compile judging every waiting
            statement, at the accepted cost that such a revocation may not apply on a device that cannot
            compile; it compiles on Android, Windows and Linux (owner decision 216); bulk state stays on
            storage and RAM is a working set, so the review phase's path past the cap is a storage-backed
            compile that reads its rows from the sealed store under the same cap, with an index the follow
            writes as the rows stream in (owner decision 366; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4); measured on
            surrogates only (owner decision 100)
```
- **Pruning.** No `net/rpc`, templates or dynamic reflect lookups (sdk/build/mobile_method_pruning_test.go:27); the worker needs protobuf v1.36.12, the first that keeps pruning (sdk/build/go.mod:98; sdk/js/go.mod:97 has v1.36.11), and sidecar generates with v1.36.11 (§6).
- **Tags.** sdk's sidecar-role files carry `!ios_extension`, and §5.10's Keychain tag keeps gomobile's darwin slices (sdk/dependency_boundary_test.go:91) on the app's `SidecarKeyStore`. The golang.org/x/mobile sdk pins runs each macOS slice in two configurations and fails the bind if either fails: its binding step, gobind's type-check of the bound package and its dependencies, uses GOOS=ios with the bind's tags plus `macos` (its cmd/gomobile/env.go's platformOS; https://go.dev/issue/52299), and the compile of the c-archive the slice links uses GOOS=darwin with the bind's tags alone, since a command-line `-tags` replaces the `-tags=macos` gomobile sets in GOFLAGS. So desktop behavior selects on gomobile's `macos` tag as well as on GOOS: sdk's remote dial files carry `!ios_extension && !js && ((ios && !macos) || android)` (sidecar_remote_dial_mobile.go) and `!ios_extension && !js && (!ios || macos) && !android` (sidecar_remote_dial.go), and the root's daemon client files that carry `!ios` add `|| macos` the same way, the daemon's server files staying out through `!sdk_mobile_bind`, so both configurations select the desktop dial and the daemon client, and the macOS app's `NewSidecarRemote` reaches `ur daemon` (18.4, 18.5, R-SDK-9) from one xcframework ([owner decision 493](#od-493)). The compiled archive selected them before these tags, so the macOS app's remote mode works as linked; the tags make the binding step agree, and §4.7's legs hold both configurations, the root's desktop client files checked to build in each, so a later divergence between them fails `make check` rather than the bind ([owner decision 554](#od-554)). Should the daemon client not build under GOOS=ios, a separate GOOS=darwin bind is a new question ([owner decision 493](#od-493)).
- **iOS.** From M4, §4's `make size` holds the `ios_extension` leg to the forwarding leg's budget above (owner decisions [215](#od-215), [491](#od-491); D-SDK-20); memory is measured on surrogates only ([owner decision 100](#od-100)).
- **wasm (D-SDK-19).** A connect-only js/wasm main is already 55.0 MB unstripped (53.2 MB stripped; 2026-11-03), since Go links every imported package's `init` functions and initialized variables, connect's IP stack included (42 gVisor packages, §4.6). The page Worker's `sidecar.wasm` therefore leaves out the root's connect-facing files, and though the root's `Id` aliases operator-core's, which imports connect, on every other leg, this leg keeps a twin of it, the root's own `[16]byte` type with the same methods and encodings, so it links no connect package (§4.4; [owner decision 276](#od-276), amending 251 for this leg). `make size` measures it at about 57.8 MB unstripped, so the goal below is a recorded slip and the miss rule's gate stands; the Q-SDK-1 spike before M4's entry decides C17 for the extension only ([owner decision 22](#od-22)):

```text
leg         js/wasm, -tags sidecar_http, main sdk/js/cmd/sidecarwasm, importing only the sidecar root and
            protocol (not sdk); its entry type is sidecar.Sidecar from this leg's NewSidecar, with no
            components and a SidecarHost of Store over IndexedDB, KeyStore over the WebCrypto key and a
            nil TokenSource, so §5.6's sidecarTokenManager refreshes (§5.4)
excluded    the root's connect-dependent files (client generations and SidecarEnv, Subprotocol and
            streams, remote search's search_remote_*.go, sockets dial and listen, bridge, tls and smtp
            listeners) and the engine host
            interfaces (host_*.go), since no server engine (§4.4) runs in the page Worker, each //go:build
            !sidecar_http; only they import connect or name a connect type, connect.Id included, or the
            root's Subprotocol
kept        identity, keychain, config verification and ACL evaluation, mls_ and the key ladder, evs head
            reads and writes over HTTPS, records and approval views, search (x/text normalization, about 0.6
            MB unstripped; no zstd), the long-poll, and the token path over SidecarApi: POST /sidecar/bind,
            GET /auth/refresh with §5.6's DPoP proof (crypto/ed25519), and the token exchange for evs and gkm
            (§7.8)
types       §5.4's every-leg types: the root's Id (here its own twin of operator-core's, owner decision 276),
            Logger, MonitorValue and CallbackList, and the net/http SidecarApi (bearer plus DPoP signer), so its
            events, actions, binding and Sign link here; connect-facing files convert at that boundary
make check  from M1: no root file of this leg imports a github.com/urnetwork/connect package, and its go
            list -deps holds no connect, operator-core or gVisor package (owner decision 276)
gate        41,943,040 B unstripped (owner decision 22's goal), measured from M2; estimated at 13-21 MB (Go's
            js runtime, net/http's fetch transport, protobuf, crypto/hpke, mls_, search), and measured at
            about 57.8 MB once the twin Id took connect's IP stack back out (owner decision 276)
threads     js/wasm runs one thread: MLS and X-Wing are pure Go in the Worker, and an operation over 50 ms
            yields between steps, so a long-poll's fetch and page requests interleave
gc          the loader sets go.env = {GODEBUG: "gcstoptheworld=1"} before go.run, the one variable make
            check's Worker harness gives its programs: with one thread and no preemption, Go's background
            mark worker runs only when the program blocks, so a long CPU-bound call (an MLS commit over a
            large group, decrypting a large repository) could leave a cycle open while linear memory, which
            never shrinks, grows; under it the goroutine that starts a cycle yields to a dedicated worker
            that marks to the end before anything else runs; the page Worker's boot test holds a planted
            allocation loop (a 4 MiB heap of pointers, then 256 MiB in 64 KiB blocks) under a bound on linear
            memory, and sdk's test harness gives its binaries the same environment; no GOMEMLIMIT or yield
            rule (owner decision 492)
C17         no longer gates the page Worker; it stays for the extension's streaming Worker (C4, Later)
miss        if the leg still exceeds the goal at M4's entry, RS1 ships it under today's 74,965,628 B sdk.wasm
            gate, a size ur.io already serves, and Gn-in records the slip; never a hosted sidecar
```

### 18.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full sidecar in network processes | always on | iOS: 4,690,096 B headroom, 32 MiB shared, jetsam kills the VPN; desktop: root, LocalSystem or sandboxed processes (apple/app/app.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:1291) hold content | rejected (owner decisions [87](#od-87), [197](#od-197)) |
| The keyless device role: the app compiles the rules and signs each link's delegation | no key or config reader in the tunnel; a 1 MiB budget | new rules and new links wait for the app, and a sleeping app stalls links | not taken ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) |
| A file allow-list of the forwarding files alone | a short list | the root's files are not layered: the closure was 269 of 428 files when first computed | not available without seam work: a computed list, tags on the rest, and the linker (18.10; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4) |
| The follower kept resident in the tunnel | no reload at a compile | 10.5 MB decoded at 5,000 devices | rejected: transient compiles (18.6; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 4) |
| A forwarding sidecar of its own in the VPN component, admitted as a device | hosts verify as today | two sidecars per app device in policy, `ur devices` and admissions; filings signed for a sidecar the app does not hold; with self_admit off an admin admits every phone's | rejected: a forwarding Delegation of the device's own sidecar (D-SDK-32) |
| A second, minimal follower, policy evaluator and compiler in `sidecar/device` | keeps the tunnel near 1 MiB | two implementations of security-critical rules to keep equal | not chosen ([owner decision 215](#od-215)) |
| A forwarding Delegation that expires within 90 days, as an auth key's | bounds a copied forwarding key with no revocation | forwarding stops where the app has not run for 90 days | rejected: it ends with its sidecar, its revocation or a newer one ([owner decision 197](#od-197)) |
| Forwarding in the root package, linked whole | no new package | links every root `init` and `protocol` descriptor into the jetsam-bound tunnel | rejected: `sidecar/device` with the listed root files (Q-SDK-5; D-SDK-20) |
| Hosted sidecar like ProxyDevice | no install | keys and plaintext on servers | ruled out (owner directive 2026-11-03; [owner decision 26](#od-26)) |
| No browser sidecar before M8 | smaller M4 | ur.io/recurd and the console decrypt nothing (owner decisions [15](#od-15), [46](#od-46)) | rejected (18.8) |
| Keys in the `https://ur.io` origin | no frame or messages | any ur.io XSS uses the key and takes the token | rejected (D-SDK-18) |
| Poll lease in `network_client.auth_time` | no new table | non-HOT writes over ~10 indexes at 12 times server's hourly cadence; a reap keyed on it revokes a long-connected agent within 60 s of a blip | rejected (D-SDK-17) |
| Phones keep all in the background on any network | older results at once | tens to hundreds of MB over cellular, and battery | rejected (D-SDK-21) |
| Browser tabs missing a condition prefetch all on a guessed Wi-Fi and charging state | parity with phones | Safari and Firefox expose no battery state, and desktop browsers no network type (MDN); a wrong guess spends cellular data | rejected (D-SDK-21) |
| Phones download all at "search more" only for the fallback, asking a designated indexer first | no first download of ~110-165 MB for a five-year mailbox; verified hits | relays see when each search and page runs; the indexer's holder sees the words | chosen once an indexer is designated (D-SDK-26; owner decisions [175](#od-175), [178](#od-178)) |
| Hedging requests to other members' indexers | lower tail latency | the query reaches more devices | rejected: only the first two own indexers are asked at once (D-SDK-27) |
| Other members' indexers by default, with no notice | [owner decision 175](#od-175)'s literal default | silent cross-member disclosure of search intent | rejected: one notice per answering member (D-SDK-26) |

### 18.12 Decisions proposed

**D-SDK-1 (proposed).** Two roles (18.4): the sidecar role in the app or `ur daemon`, and in every app's VPN component only forwarding, which holds its own forwarding key and nothing else of sidecar. *Why:* owner decisions [4](#od-4), [87](#od-87), [197](#od-197); tunnel budgets.

**D-SDK-2 (proposed).** One `sdk.Sidecar` with local and remote backends and 18.5's gates. *Why:* PLAN.md:28 within gobind limits.

**D-SDK-3 (proposed).** 18.6's seam, setup and mirror; app devices host, serve and map nothing before C16 (M4; D-BRIDGE-5), and then only on the device client's sdk provider, in that client's network. *Why:* Go types stay off bindings; the Opportunistic device client (sdk/device_local_provider.go:258) may reply in plaintext; the device client exists only in its own network.

**D-SDK-4 (proposed).** The sdk Api session owns the token and injects 18.7's services. *Why:* one refresh per process.

**D-SDK-5 (proposed).** 18.4's budgets are carved out of each process limit. *Why:* message pools and the soft limit are process-wide (sdk/sdk.go:554-571).

**D-SDK-6 (proposed).** The browser sidecar is phased per 18.8; its Workers are member devices, the page Worker admitted `read_only`, and the quick burner a wrapped reader. *Why:* owner decisions [15](#od-15), [26](#od-26), [76](#od-76), [114](#od-114).

**D-SDK-7 (proposed).** Cloud hosts climb 18.9's rungs against its host list. *Why:* [owner decision 49](#od-49); connect proxies only over SOCKS5.

**D-SDK-8 (proposed).** Adopt 18.10's gates. *Why:* 18.3's iOS headroom and 18.10's wasm sizes.

**D-SDK-9 (proposed).** Apps decide approvals, admissions, alarms and recovery vetoes through `SidecarApprovals`; control mode signs `approval` only as `device` evidence for another sidecar's request, after the person confirms at the host. *Why:* I-4, I-8; owner decisions [112](#od-112), [126](#od-126), [127](#od-127), [149](#od-149).

**D-SDK-10 (proposed).** Wakes carry only a topic class and version (18.7), from M8. *Why:* [owner decision 88](#od-88); §2.8 ext-8.

**D-SDK-11 (proposed).** The desktop app and extension releases adopt 18.7's credential rules before §7.4's stage 2 (M3). *Why:* I-6; [owner decision 45](#od-45); same-user agents read both stores.

**D-SDK-12 (proposed).** ur.io's hosted DeviceLocal runs no sidecar or bridge, and 18.3's hosted check marks it for §8.10's gate. *Why:* I-10.

**D-SDK-13 (proposed).** The forwarding role takes rules and names only from the `BridgeState` its own compile of the verified config produces and the anchored deltas after it, persists its posture (legacy, pending, enforcing), restoring enforcing state before the first packet, and signs each window client's `WindowDelegation` itself, with its forwarding key or a share's current `BridgeShareSigner` (18.6); its posture applies denials at once and opens only on a compiled state, and a narrowing entry it cannot check never makes it pending: the last compiled state stays in force and `bridge_alarm` is raised at 10 minutes, again at doubling intervals to once a day and for each newly overdue entry, until a compile judges it (owner decisions [216](#od-216), [487](#od-487)). *Why:* owner decisions [3](#od-3), [85](#od-85), [197](#od-197); forwarding must never wait on the app, a restart plus an unsigned `has_document = false` must not reopen a LAN, and §17.9's hosts admit only delegated window clients.

**D-SDK-14 (proposed).** Transport rejections are generation-bound and map to Unenrolled with a reason; only a verified `SidecarRevoke` maps to Revoked. *Why:* a lost or expired client is not a revocation (D-CORE-8), and a stale callback must not end a new pairing.

**D-SDK-15 (proposed).** `SidecarKeyStore` returns status codes and a `SidecarSecret` struct (18.5). *Why:* gobind carries no error type, and a crossing panic exits the app.

**D-SDK-16 (proposed).** Wakes follow 18.7: a slot-local script, a separate enqueue for token holders, client acks from connect's frame ack, a deferred check while live, and per-slot sentinels that reconcile a restarted master's tokens. Token projections follow each row's revision: every change, a removal's tombstone included, raises it in Postgres; a slot-local script applies a revision only above `tokrev` and within 60 s of the TIME its writer read before the transaction; a slot whose master changed is reconciled 90 s after the pass that found it; and each pass re-applies the rows changed since the last one. *Why:* Redis Cluster refuses cross-slot transactions, a stale live marker must not drop the only wake, and masters have no replicas and restart from their last RDB dump; a post-commit SET lands in no order that a Postgres commit or row lock sets, so an older POST's SET could replace a newer token or revive a removed one until the next launch (meta review F15).

**D-SDK-17 (proposed).** An ephemeral client's polls refresh its narrow `network_client_lease` row at most once per 5 min; it is reaped only with no open connection once that lease and its newest disconnect are both over 35 min old, 30-36 min after the later, and an unload beacon closes it early by a 128-bit capability (18.8). *Why:* no resident measures an HTTPS-only host's disconnect; `auth_time` refreshes hourly over `network_client`'s ~10 indexes, so a reap keyed on it revokes connected agents on any blip; `sendBeacon` sets no Authorization header, and the token stays in the Worker.

**D-SDK-18 (proposed).** Browser keys, tokens and the Worker live in a key origin that ur.io pages frame and message by exact origin, one Worker per network under a Web Lock. *Why:* one shared origin would let any ur.io XSS take the key, and two tabs' Workers over one IndexedDB would race refreshes, commits and keychain writes.

**D-SDK-19 (proposed).** The page Worker builds the root with `-tags sidecar_http`: connect-facing and engine host (`host_*.go`) files are `!sidecar_http`, and the rest, token path included, use only §5.4's root types and `SidecarApi`. The root's `Id` aliases operator-core's, which imports connect, on every other leg; on this one it is a twin with the same methods and encodings, so the leg links no connect or gVisor ([owner decision 276](#od-276), amending 251), and at about 57.8 MB it misses 18.10's goal, a recorded slip under the miss rule's gate. Its loader starts `sidecar.wasm` with `GODEBUG=gcstoptheworld=1` ([owner decision 492](#od-492)). *Why:* the page Worker runs no connect client, engine or `Env`, and connect's IP stack puts the 40 MB goal out of reach without C17; on js/wasm's one thread the background mark worker runs only when the program blocks, so a long CPU-bound call could leave a GC cycle open while linear memory, which never shrinks, grows.

**D-SDK-20 (proposed).** The forwarding role is `sidecar/device`, importing connect and `sidecar/protocol/bridge` only, with the root files on the `ios_extension` leg's list, a computed closure every other root file is tagged out of, whose list, refused modules and descriptors `make check` holds and whose stripped size `make size` holds (18.10); through the root's `Id` the leg also links operator-core ([owner decision 251](#od-251)), and with the replaying config head reader every leg runs it is held to 7.5 MiB, the budget [owner decision 491](#od-491) set from the measurement [owner decision 251](#od-251) asked for, amending 215's 6 MiB. *Why:* [owner decision 197](#od-197) puts the config follower and compiler in the VPN component, and only an allow-list keeps every other root init and descriptor out of the jetsam-bound tunnel.

**D-SDK-21 (proposed).** Every host that searches a repo keeps its two latest buckets synced, phones' team directory aside (D-SDK-28). Desktops and indexers keep all in the background; phones fetch it at "search more" for repos no designated indexer answers and browser tabs at "search more", both also on Wi-Fi while charging, phones in OS windows, and tabs while open only where their browser reports both conditions; ephemeral agents fetch it only at "search more"; each device may override per repo, within 18.4's caps. A condition an app or browser has not reported counts as metered and not charging. *Why:* owner decisions [154](#od-154), [177](#od-177) and [178](#od-178); 154's per-device override covers browsers, since Safari and Firefox report neither condition and desktop browsers no network type, and ephemeral agents, whose in-memory caches would re-download all at every start; only OS windows let a backgrounded phone download tens to hundreds of MB.

**D-SDK-22 (proposed).** Apps search through `SidecarSearch` (18.5): one call streams replacing pages of hits labeled verified, confirmed, possible, near or unmatched, each naming the indexer that verified it if one did, with progress that names the bytes to fetch, any metered wait and the remote state. *Why:* gobind's limits; one implementation of masking and ranking on every host.

**D-SDK-23 (proposed).** Hosts report network and power conditions and the foreground, apps through `SetConditions` and `SetForeground` and browsers through the key-origin frame's network, battery and tab visibility, and apps grant background time through `RunBackgroundSync`; the Go core reads no platform API. *Why:* none is portable across gomobile, the C ABI and js, the OS decides when a backgrounded app may run, and without a foreground report each search opens its own contract, the timing [owner decision 188](#od-188)'s windows exist to hide.

**D-SDK-24 (proposed).** The page Worker links the search engine and keeps its search cache in its own IndexedDB store, written only by the Web Lock holder; pages receive hit views only, and the quick burner searches its buckets in memory and never fetches all. *Why:* [owner decision 76](#od-76)'s one browser runtime; eviction and Safari's 7-day rule make the cache disposable by design.

**D-SDK-25 (proposed).** Search meets 18.4's warm targets and §16.10's cold contract on phones, desktops and the page Worker, each search's masks inside its working set; §22 measures them on surrogate phones ([owner decision 100](#od-100)) and in Safari's wasm engine before M10's exit ([owner decision 169](#od-169)), and the remote targets on surrogates from the later of M10's and M8's exits. *Why:* the research left decryption rates on phones and in Safari's wasm unmeasured; a cold download's first hit depends on where the match lies, so only its progress, arrival and completion can be bounded.

**D-SDK-26 (proposed).** Where its network designates a search indexer that may answer, none being designated by default ([owner decision 177](#od-177)), app hosts ask it at "search more" by default. The mode is per device and network: `on` (own indexers, then other members' that §11.14 allows, each new answering member only after the app's notice), `own` or `off`, kept in §5.9's non-derived search state, never in the config repo.
