### 19.11 Environments, gates, rollout

**local:** all, in server/local (postgres:18, redis:8; README.md:36), plus MinIO, Pebble ACME, an SMTP sink and a test dns edge. **canary:** none to build for ([owner decision 499](#od-499)): config/canary/ was deleted in 2023 and no build leg or host serves it, so only its cheap parts are built (the `sidecar_pending` tag leg, a `config/canary/` a host could use, canary kept in `sidecarPendingAllowed`); no canary deploy counts as evidence, T3 and M2's staging cluster proving stores and hosts, and the tier leaves the design unless the owner buys hosts for it. **main:** all, dark first, edges and mail for internal networks and design partners until launch ([owner decision 91](#od-91)); T6 on test roots and LE staging (§12.4). **community:** none.

**Gates (D-OPS-10).** `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` is optional and inert when absent, like config/main/onboarding.yml:3-6:

```yaml
sidecar:
  evs: {enabled: false, writes: true, networks: [], percent: 0, blocks: <n>}  # blocks: the env's evs block
                             # count, set with services.yml's; each process paces a spent network's reads at
                             # evs_unpaid_read_rate / blocks; none, or below 1, and an enabled block will not start
                             # (19.4; owner decision 500)
  format2: {enabled: false, networks: [], percent: 0, purge: observe, drop: observe}  # §11.6: networks whose
                             # pushes may carry format 2, each repo migrating at its first such push; purge: observe
                             # logs each candidate and deletes nothing, purge: on deletes, after D-TEST-12's soak (§22),
                             # the turn-on pass waiting, retrying, until its taskworker reads on (owner decision 412);
                             # drop: observe runs drop jobs through verify and deletes nothing (§11.13), drop: on
                             # deletes, after D-TEST-18's soak; until both are on and D-TEST-13's production check
                             # passes, the gate admits only listed internal networks and design partners (percent 0)
  gkm: {enabled: false, networks: [], percent: 0}   # sockets, tlsedge, mxedge, smtpedge alike
  dns: {enabled: false, writes: true}
  push: {enabled: false}     # §6 EnableSidecarPush
  wake: {enabled: false}     # 19.4's push sender
  bridge: {enabled: false}   # §17 EnableBridge
  escrow_draw_order: {enabled: false}  # §20.9 (D-QUOTA-9): every draw and return site (connect's CreateContract,
                             # the edges' leases, taskworker's closes); on only once M6's Gn-out registers
                             # MG6's index (19.7), never off while a team_credit balance is in window
  reseed: false              # 19.10, site loss only
  restore_hold: false        # 19.10's restore: while true, api answers every public route but its status route,
                             # the token exchange among them, 503 with Retry-After 60, and connect's CreateContract
                             # answers ContractError.Setup; open streams, sockets and edges run on, the dns and api
                             # steps run as jobs behind it, the runbook's first step sets it and the api step's end
                             # clears it; a reader that cannot read the file keeps its last answer
  place_new: meta-1          # 19.9: the metadata cluster that takes new repos; absent, the first
  drained: []                # W1: lb interfaces the dns edges and warpctl dns's <env>-lb sets leave out
  certs: {enabled: false}    # §13.15's two installs, api's and taskworker's: off, nothing of certs runs, so the
                             # first real CA order is the owner's act (owner decision 429)
  preview_networks: []       # §7.4 (D-PHASE-3): networks that enroll sidecars before stage 2
  sockets_control_qps: {rate: 50, burst: 500}  # §9.10 (D-SOCK-15), per process and calling client; edges: W2's 2,000 Finds/s
  urnetwork_edge: <network_id>                 # §6.10.1, §9.6: the urnetwork-edge platform network's id
  file_clusters: {<cluster id>: {settle_passed_build: <commit>, hdd_capacity_ops: <n>}}  # 19.6: the build that
                             # passed the settle suite, recorded by the operator after filecluster-suite passes,
                             # and the hdd run's measured capacity, published in {nvb_<cluster>}
```

A network is in when listed or when hash(network_id) mod 100 < `percent`, hash(network_id) being the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the id's 16 bytes, big-endian, in one function every gate shares, the format2 gate's included. No key enforces §7.4's stage 1 or D-TEAM-14, which refuse in code from M1 whatever the file holds, so it carries no `p0_enforce` ([owner decision 510](#od-510)). A disabled service stays ready and answers 503 with Retry-After; `writes: false` is the incident switch. Services reread the file every 60 s; sidecars learn their set from §6's `core` topic. A process whose first read fails, the file there but unreadable or unparsable with no earlier read to keep, marks that read until its first good one: taskworker's idle marking holds off (§13.6; [owner decision 622](#od-622)), api's removal owes the `rev/` object of each removed client on an edge device, found by its device spec (§9.8; [owner decision 641](#od-641)), and a connect resident settles an edge end's contract by the ordinary rules, an accepted gap (§6.10.1).

**Classes (D-OPS-11).** Staged with `--only-older` (build/all/deploy-rollout.zsh:33): evs, gkm, sockets, dns (on Q-OPS-5's conditions), tlsedge, mxedge, mxedge-platform; single pass (:24): smtpedge, and the `dnsedge` class's two services one host at a time, `dnsedge-1` first, then `dnsedge-2` once Q-OPS-5's stop rule holds (the canary signature clean, the NS serials equal): server/cli/dnsedge builds one image, which build/all/run.sh imports under each name, as it does for manager to app (run.sh:3554), and warp's core does not change. Classes land at once, and each service joins `staged_services` only in the milestone its block lands, since `warpctl deploy` panics on a service with no blocks; the staged list (:87) becomes `mmm lb taskworker api connect web app mcp dns gkm evs sockets tlsedge mxedge mxedge-platform`.

**Order** (§23 sets milestones; groups merge per 19.7):
1. M0: MG0 (D-PHASE-3's early merge), with D-OPS-18's daily dump and the main dump's exclude list from its Gn-out, restore-drilled before M3's pilot; W5, on warp's `sidecar` branch ([owner decision 196](#od-196)), built but unused ([owner decision 494](#od-494)); W6's recipe; the hardware order (19.6; owner decisions [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[139](#od-139)); HE's port-25 and reverse-delegation request (§14).
2. M1-M4: MG1-MG4; chrony on the evs, gkm, taskworker, Redis and storage hosts before evs serves (19.6); evs and gkm dark at M2 on a staging cluster on the production hosts, so they and their PM9A3 set arrive before M2's exit (D-TEST-11), rebuilt empty and SMART-rechecked before M3 under D-PHASE-7's data rule; then production (M3) with the write budget, the protection states and the pager ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); W2, W8, publishers; W10 at RS1.
3. M5: dns edges (W9), signed from the first deploy ([owner decision 109](#od-109)), then the ur.network move ([owner decision 13](#od-13)); sockets, which takes service tokens and so waits on no owner step: the revocation record's switch stays vault's, for api's own paths, and no JWKS export is run ([owner decision 588](#od-588)); certs and tlsedge with W1, W7 and the LE override; the platform listener with W11; the pager's notice class (19.8).
4. M7: mxedge's router (W4); M8: the push sender; M9: smtpedge, once its PTR and HELO names resolve (W11).
5. M10: after M10's Gn-out the `format2` gate opens to internal networks and design partners (percent 0), purge and drop in observe; purge turns on after D-TEST-12's soak and drop after D-TEST-18's, which `sidecarctl evs observe-report <env>` prints from monitor's counter and the repos' drop tables, only reading, so turning them on stays an operator's act ([owner decision 513](#od-513)); D-TEST-13's production confirmation runs while the gate holds percent at 0 ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); only then does the gate open by percent (§23.9). §22.8's M10 `hdd` run uses a bucket of its own on the production segment cluster in a low-load window, under 19.6's 50% drive-operation pause, its bucket emptied after.

### 19.12 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| MinIO pools for metadata growth | one endpoint; rebalance | a PUT checks its precondition only in the pool it picks (§11.3) | rejected ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) |
| Redis as the metadata store of record | no NVMe wear | a failover loses acknowledged commits; no replicas | rejected ([owner decision 136](#od-136)) |
| Every drive acknowledges each write | no degraded objects | one host's outage stops writes; MinIO has no such setting | rejected for 19.6's states |
| MinIO's warm tier for history past 24 h | no evacuation | a tiny HDD object per batch or log page | rejected for §11.13's packs |

### 19.13 Decisions proposed

**D-OPS-1 (proposed).** Host the engines and jobs per 19.4, the push sender in taskworker; only api's oauth issuer mounts signing keys. *Why:* hostile-facing processes hold only their own secrets.

**D-OPS-2 (proposed).** gkm is its own service, `server/cli/gkm`, from v0; its reconciler runs in taskworker. *Why:* api's daily deploys cannot stall MLS commits.

**D-OPS-3 (proposed).** Build W1, W2 and W4-W11; keep the 16 MiB limit. *Why:* 19.5's consumers need them.

**D-OPS-4 (proposed).** The file clusters are LAN-only, unshared and without presigned URLs. *Why:* conditional writes order evs and gkm; direct access exposes client IPs.

**D-OPS-5 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 94](#od-94): no off-site copy of the file clusters; D-OPS-18 covers Postgres-held sidecar rows.

**D-OPS-6 (proposed).** Migrations follow 19.7: a group is pending under `sidecar_pending` until its own Gn-out registers it. *Why:* the catalog refuses renumbered identities, and two tracks share one `sidecar` branch.

**D-OPS-7 (proposed).** Redis holds only rebuildable state (19.7); switches go to Postgres first. *Why:* masters have no replicas, and the clusters stay the only commit point ([owner decision 136](#od-136)).

**D-OPS-8 (proposed).** Metrics and logs carry no identifying labels, names or query strings (19.8). *Why:* I-13.

**D-OPS-9 (proposed).** Adopt 19.8's SLOs and page classes, which page out of hours from M3 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)) through a commercial pager service ([owner decision 498](#od-498)); budget burn stops rollout steps, as does a burn state monitor cannot read, an operator overriding a stop by name. *Why:* each percent step needs a stop rule, and owner decisions [89](#od-89) and [116](#od-116)'s 4 h RTO a responder at any hour.

**D-OPS-10 (proposed).** Gates, the placement target, the restore hold and the owner's switches live in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml`. *Why:* §4.8 merges code dark, and a new cluster takes repos without a deploy.

**D-OPS-11 (proposed).** Classify and order releases per 19.11. *Why:* an unclassified service exits 64.

**D-OPS-12 (proposed).** A builder job renews platform certificates at two thirds of their lifetime, by ARI, with goacme/lego v4.35.2, the release `warpctl certs issue` runs, both commands moving together to lego v5, the target, with RFC 9773's `replaces`, once someone allowed to fetch it has read its CLI ([owner decision 502](#od-502)); the daily lb deploy brings them, W5's swap built but unused ([owner decision 494](#od-494)). *Why:* manual renewal (xops/certs/renew.md:3-20) fails at 45-day lifetimes, due 2028-02-16 (https://letsencrypt.org/2025/12/02/from-90-to-45/).

**D-OPS-13 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 34](#od-34): no dedicated mail or tlsedge addresses.

**D-OPS-14 (proposed).** Durability is 19.6's, judged per object by the shards it holds: quorum writes, the protection states, which the in-house build's partial-write queue export lets leave `degraded` ([owner decision 496](#od-496)), the cold spare and D-OPS-18's daily sidecar dump off site. Postgres and site loss take 19.10's restore. *Why:* owner decisions [89](#od-89), [90](#od-90) and [94](#od-94) leave devices and dumps as the only copies, and 116 adds the spare.

**D-OPS-15 (proposed).** Addresses and dns edges follow 19.4 and 19.5. *Why:* owner decisions [34](#od-34), [69](#od-69), [71](#od-71), [123](#od-123) and [124](#od-124); RRL needs resolver addresses.

**D-OPS-16 (proposed).** The Redis bundles leave out 19.7's sidecar families: bringyour-backup.sh filters them from each node's rdb before sealing (xops/main/ansible/host_files/by-us-fmt-5-edge-6/backup/bringyour-backup.sh:8-13), loading each dump into a scratch redis-server of the pinned version, deleting the families, saving, then compressing, one node at a time and publishing nothing on any failure; its prefixes follow 19.7's tags, `{sso_}`, `{oauthdev_}` and `{oauthuser_}` among them ([owner decision 508](#od-508)). *Why:* they rebuild or expire within 48 h; no backup may outlive a published ttl (D-TRUST-7).

**D-OPS-17 (proposed).** Size the metadata tier by drive writes, objects and bytes, which §22.8's runs measure per push, per object and in records per batch per cluster; [owner decision 136](#od-136)'s triggers (50% raw, 40% inodes, 0.5 DWPD), or monitor's projection of one within the lead time, order the next metadata cluster ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), on new hosts after the second (19.9); each cluster that no longer takes repos is planned by its own cohort's projection (19.9's cohorts row), which dates the move tool. HDD sets join only through a segment placement that keeps §11.13's receipt check and moves upload load, never as a pool, ordered by 19.9's hdd trigger, monitor's trends of `hdd_ops` and `hdd_puts`, ahead of year two's HDD load, whose PUTs alone fill the 50% admission line by 19.6's model. *Why:* every drive takes every write, endurance binds before IOPS ([owner decision 140](#od-140)), a pool checks preconditions only inside itself (19.9), and placed repos never move without the tool ([owner decision 145](#od-145)), so free space elsewhere relieves no cohort; refused uploads are not throughput.

**D-OPS-18 (proposed).** The tables 19.7's groups create, with the network, user and client rows they name, have a daily, off-site dump from MG0's Gn-out, and the main dumps exclude those tables (19.6); the primary's physical working copies, edge-6's `pg-base` and edge-5's `main-pgbase-<date>`, are each refreshed or destroyed within 7 d, and the 24 h edge records' partitions are UNLOGGED ([owner decision 210](#od-210)). *Why:* owner decisions [2](#od-2) and [18](#od-18) moved storage, not identity, naming, mail routing, abuse or billing, out of Postgres; [owner decision 94](#od-94) bars an off-site copy of the file clusters, not of these rows; and the named rows keep a network newer than the twice-weekly main dump attached to its rows, log and repos.

**D-OPS-19 (proposed).** The metadata set runs 19.6's XFS and MinIO settings, and each storage host exports its metadata drives' write counters and SMART wear, and its HDDs' operation counters, to monitor, §11.13's write budget and its HDD share (19.6). *Why:* the drives' endurance is the binding budget, and only drive counters measure it ([owner decision 140](#od-140)); the HDD sets' operations bind before their space (Q-OPS-2).

**D-OPS-20 (proposed).** Both clusters run an in-house MinIO build, from the `urnetwork/minio` fork's `sidecar` branch ([owner decision 195](#od-195)), with 19.6's deadline and settle rules: every request but a streamed segment or pack PUT carries its deadline, which the build checks where it takes the key's lock and at each drive commit; each drive commit applies only while no commit was applied to its key on its drive since the coordinator read it under the lock; a PUT releases its key only once it holds a write quorum or can never reach a read quorum, and a DELETE only once it holds a write quorum or no drive holds anything of it, each reverting every drive that took it, another host settling a dead coordinator's write; a DELETE may name the LastModified of the object it means, as GC's and a drop job's do (owner decisions [203](#od-203), [225](#od-225)); a DELETE's stash stays in `.minio.sys/settle`, which nothing wipes, until its key is released; a LIST is answered only when it is whole ([owner decision 226](#od-226)), and a read answers 404 only on a read quorum's absence, else 503 ([owner decision 511](#od-511)); it exports each set's partial-write queue ([owner decision 496](#od-496)); and it refuses to start a one-process cluster in settle mode ([owner decision 504](#od-504)). *Why:* in the deployed build a cancel reaches no drive on another host and the lock is released first, and even a lock held to the 30 s drive timeout releases a commit that stalled after its last check, so a cancelled or timed-out write can land after a later request on its key read it or passed its precondition, breaking §11.7's marker collection, v1's versionless purge and drop jobs (§11.13) and every conditional write's atomicity; absence is not a version, so a drive's contents alone cannot tell a commit from before a DELETE from one after it, nor one failed DELETE's leavings from another's; holding a key while such a write settles is the cost, paid only when a host fails during a write that has not reached its write quorum, and for a DELETE stalled on a frozen host until that host answers or its drives are replaced, which only background jobs' unconditional DELETEs pay ([owner decision 501](#od-501)); a fork, not a patch series in warp, keeps MinIO's AGPL source in one public place.

**D-OPS-21 (proposed).** Drop jobs are P2 taskworker work, one per segment cluster at a time, each reading at most 32 MB/s and deleting at most 10 objects a second, paused while HDD drive operations exceed 50% of measured capacity (19.6). *Why:* [owner decision 173](#od-173)'s scan of every ref must not starve customers' reads or the HDD sets' heal and evacuation.

**D-OPS-22 (proposed).** Until the move tool exists, a metadata cluster at 80% raw or 70% inodes takes only what §20.7's storage limit accepts, refusing the rest 507 CLUSTER_FULL (19.9's cohorts row), and monitor projects each cluster's exhaustion from its own cohort's slopes, the first cluster's control plane apart, dating the move tool by the earliest. *Why:* a full cluster would refuse deletions and erasures too, and the estate's free space cannot take a placed cohort ([owner decision 145](#od-145)).

### 19.14 Open questions

**Q-OPS-1.** [X13] What is the "new file cluster" (PLAN.md:61), and where does ordering live? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [18](#od-18), [20](#od-20), [21](#od-21), [94](#od-94)):** (a), 19.6's MinIO clusters at one site, ordered by the store ([owner decision 2](#od-2)). **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 (owner decisions [116](#od-116), [136](#od-136)-[140](#od-140), [145](#od-145)):** 19.6's parity, cold spare, drives, write budget and Redis soft state, and growth by whole clusters; the load inputs stay an engineering estimate. *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-2.** Cross-cutting (§10.6, §11.13). Should small objects pack? Y2's HDD mix needs ~32,000 drive operations a second against ~8,000-12,800 (19.6). **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (b) in v0, with (a) a switch: format 1 freezes content-id segment ids, the reserved `spidx/` family and lookup order, and reserved locator kinds 3 and 4, never a physical address; after §22.8's `hdd` row (M3), (a) turns on for segments under 1 MiB and older than 7 days, never kind-5 segments, which stay deletable one by one, once HDD drive operations pass 50% of measured capacity; ~25,600 of Y2's ~32,000 drive operations a second are GETs, which packing does not reduce, so the page cache serves most and (c) HDD sets per D-OPS-17 the rest, which must land before year two's load, since its PUTs alone (~6,400) fill the 50% admission line (19.6, 19.9's hdd trigger); history leaves the batches hourly, so each day everything older than 24 h leaves them ([owner decision 136](#od-136)), and a small repo's parcels within 7 d; gkm's `gen/` takes §10.16's gen packs, which keep every generation for the repo's life (D-KEYS-20), count as gen/ for shreds, their 10-minute repeat and re-seeds, and hold no slot, so erasure is unchanged; they start on a cluster at 19.9's gen trigger, projected from §22.8's M2 count. *Residual:* 19.9's hdd trigger, from §22.8's admitted hdd run, and the segment placement, whose design Q-OPS-11 leaves to engineering ([owner decision 550](#od-550)).

**Q-OPS-3.** Where does Postgres-held sidecar metadata live without a replica? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by owner decisions [2](#od-2), [18](#od-18)):** moot for storage, which left Postgres. **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** D-OPS-18 and 19.10's reconcile: the sidecar rows, which are not storage, and the network, user and client rows they name take a daily off-site dump, so the dumped sidecar rows (a table whose ttl is at most 7 d is in no dump) come back to ≤ 24 h plus the run (≤ 20 min) at a primary's loss and ≤ 26 h at the site's while each nightly run completes, a day more per skipped or aborted run, whatever the main dump's age; the platform's other rows come back to the main dump's (19.3). *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-4.** Where are edges and mail tested? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 91](#od-91)):** (b), dark in main for internal networks and design partners, no canary stage. *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-5.** Should `dns` deploy staged (`--only-older`, stopping at 25%) or in one pass like `dnsedge`? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), staged: N and N+1 read each other's journal rows and snapshots, N+1's unreadable writes gated until 100%; `dnsedge` single-pass, one host at a time, serving only self-checked snapshots; rollout stops on a canary-signature failure or an NS serial divergence; FS-52 rolls N+1 back to N in T3. *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-6.** Must backups delay erasure? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 90](#od-90)):** (c), no backups of key metadata (19.6). *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-7.** What RPO and RTO apply, at how many sites? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (owner decisions [89](#od-89), [94](#od-94)):** (a), one site; the targets cover drive and host failures (19.6), and site loss recovers from devices (19.10). *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-8.** Cross-cutting (§4.8, §23.9). How do migration groups reach server's `main` when M3 pilots on production? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 118](#od-118)):** each group's SQL merges to `main` with its milestone's code at Gn-out (19.7), so M3 pilots on production. *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-9.** Cross-cutting (§12.6, §21.8). Do page-class infrastructure alerts page out of hours from M3, so owner decisions [89](#od-89) and [116](#od-116)'s 4 h RTO and 19.8's SLOs hold at all hours? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)):** (a), a two-person rota on one pager service from M3, with 30-minute acknowledgment and escalation, for 19.8's page classes only; [owner decision 134](#od-134)'s notices join the same pager at M5. The RTO and the SLOs hold at all hours, as §22.8's host drill (FS-50) measures. *Residual:* none.

**Q-OPS-10.** Cross-cutting (§10.6, §11.8). How does the metadata tier grow past one set, when a multi-pool PUT checks If-Match and If-None-Match only in the pool it picks by free space (§11.3)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 145](#od-145)):** (b), only by adding metadata clusters, never pools: each new repo and its gkm group are placed at creation by a create-only `place/<repo_id>` on the first cluster, whose If-None-Match decides a race (§11.8), and all their objects stay there. The triggers stay (19.9). Year two needs five to six clusters: batches are per evs process and cluster (§11.8), so at ~8 processes a set near capacity holds ~1-1.6 records a batch and sustains ~400-450 pushes/s (~530-600 on 1 KiB blocks) at ~27-43 KiB of drive writes a push (Q-EVS-9); [owner decision 145](#od-145)'s record first carried ~490-650 a set and four to five sets, which assumed batches shared across the whole load; per-cluster placement rules that out (19.9), and the record was corrected on 2026-11-05 to this sizing. *Residual:* none; a move tool is later (19.18).

**Q-OPS-11.** Cross-cutting (§11.22, §23.7). When does the segment placement, which §19.9's hdd row needs before year two's HDD load, get a design and a home, and what is its lead time? **Decided by owner 2026-11-06 ([owner decision 550](#od-550)):** (a), a tracked item now, as the next metadata cluster has: §23.7 gives it (due before the crossing 19.9's hdd trigger projects; start at M3's exit, when the hdd run first gives an admitted throughput) and a lead time of 26 weeks, monitor's `hdd_trigger_lead_days` = 182, §23.4's Later list and 19.18 name it, and the rota owns the page. Deciding at M3's exit on the measured rate, (b), and operators' judgment, (c), were not taken. *Residual:* the placement's design, which engineering writes within 8 weeks of M3's exit, keeping §11.13's receipt check and moving upload load (19.9).

### 19.15 Departures from PLAN.md

None: owner decisions [18](#od-18), [94](#od-94) and [145](#od-145) keep MinIO, in new clusters (PLAN.md:61).

### 19.16 Interfaces

- **Provides:** 19.4-19.11's blocks, push sender, W items, addresses, clusters and their growth, the store request deadline, settle rule and read rule, host clocks and each process's offset, protection states, drive counters and SMART wear, the `{nvb_<set>}` allowances, accounts and wallet, the class liabilities, each cluster's cohort projection and limit, and each segment cluster's drive operations and capacity, the sidecar dump, recovery, gates (`format2`'s purge and drop modes included), pager, SLOs, runbooks.
- **Consumes:** engines (§4, §9-§15); §7.8's `rev/` and re-seed mode; §7.9's log, verified cache and site-loss resumption; §8.9; §10.6, §10.8, §10.16's gen packs; §11.8's placement and clock rule, §11.13's mix, write budget, HDD share, v1's purge, sweep and drop jobs and the search index's costs; §11.14's search index; §16.11's directory; §12.6's restore step and `/dns/internal/reload-diff`; §13.4; §14.6; §15.4; §18.7; §20's jobs and draw order; §21's tables, `hold/`, intake and abuse mailbox (§21.10); §22's tests; X15 (§23).
- **Subprotocol messages:** none. **API routes:** none new but §8.9's internal `/internal/gate/` routes and §20.14's quota routes on them, which take a caller class's bearer and no client token. **Tables:** none owned; 19.7 summarizes; the push sender reads `{scp_<C>}tok`, `{scp_<C>}tokrev`, `{scp_<C>}ack` and `{wakeq_<shard>}`, and taskworker reconciles tokens per hash slot by `{tokgen_<n>}` and re-applies changed rows each pass (19.4; §18.7's steps 5 and 6).
- **Services and config:** services.yml blocks, two dns edge hosts; `sidecar.yml` (gates, evs's `blocks`, `place_new`, `drained`, `preview_networks`, `sockets_control_qps`, `urnetwork_edge`, `restore_hold`, `file_clusters`); `db.yml` and `redis.yml` caps; vault JWKS, ZSK, APNs, FCM and feed credentials, the gate caller classes' bearers and the sockets ticket key file, which `sidecarctl sockets ticket-keygen` writes once a year (§9.8; [owner decision 590](#od-590)); receipt keys in evs's secret files; D-OPS-20's MinIO build from `urnetwork/minio`; xops's `file-clusters` with 19.6's XFS and MinIO settings, the storage hosts' Fluent Bit and their 5 s counter process, chrony on the evs, gkm, taskworker, Redis and storage hosts with the Redis hosts' offset exporter, the daily sidecar dump, the main dump's exclude list and planetoid's pg-sidecar stream (D-OPS-18), the bundle filter (D-OPS-16); the pager service and `pager.Sink`; each block's own credential files (`file-clusters-<service>.yml`, `grafana-push-<service>.yml`, `pg-<service>.yml`) and its fragment in `warp/services/sidecar-blocks/`.
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §7.8's re-seed mode mints only `repo:<id>:admin` for evs's `/reseed` and gkm's GroupForm, which §11.12 also admits for a repo re-seeded as deleted; §7.9 resumes the log from member devices' verbatim entries, each adopted once two members' devices hold it, FS-41 checks that readers see no FORK, that one member's forged TICK takes no position and that a Team whose other members hold only read_only devices resumes, and FS-42 restores both dumps in each order of their snapshot times, keeping the newer one's rows, and checks that revocations between or after the dumps hold once api's replay ends, their TLSA (M7) and DKIM selectors (M9) gone, that a network newer than both takes the deleted-network path, that actions and lifts mailed after the dump hold (§21.10), and that a dns write, an ACME challenge, an NS that missed the SOA read and a custom host after the restore behave as 19.10's dns step says, which runs §12.6's restore step; §10.6, §11.7, §11.8 and v1's purge and drop jobs (§11.13) rely on 19.6's request deadline, which the Blobs client sends as x-ur-deadline-ms, and its settle rule, which §22's suite checks (FS-114); §11.13's HDD admission and drop jobs read 19.6's published HDD drive operations and capacity, and the versionless sweep HEADs each candidate before its DELETE (19.8); while 19.6's clock offset is unknown or over 50 ms, §11.8's evs answers pushes 503, and taskworker raises no evacuation fence and GC deletes nothing; §11.10's restarted push sequence relies on 19.6's chrony on the Redis hosts; §20.9's draw sites read `escrow_draw_order`; §11.8 places new repos on `place_new`, and §11.22 lists a segment placement that keeps the receipt check before any added HDD set (19.9); §11.13's accounts debit P1 admissions from A1 at full price, moving their deferred P2 work into the wallet W, funded P2 spending only W and P1 and unfunded P2 only T, while P0 issues at once, its measured bytes draining the bucket down to its floor at zero, past which they are its forgiven excess ([owner decision 190](#od-190)), and no other class issues while the bucket is empty; §10.6's acks and §11.10's leases and push sequence live in Redis; §18.7's trigger feeds `{wakeq_<shard>}`, and its sentinel pass re-projects the slots of a master lost or restarted; §21.8 feeds 19.8's pager; §22.8 measures §11.13's mix, §10.6's sizes, bytes per object and push, records per batch per cluster, and rotations and path-epoch copies, expiry-driven ones included, and its `hdd` row the segment cluster's capacity by 19.6's HDD counters; HE allows port 25.

### 19.18 Phasing

- **v0 (M0-M5, M7-M9):** 19.11's order, dark first; D-OPS-20's MinIO build on both clusters; one PM9A3 set of 8 drives and 2-4 spares, with 19.6's settings, counters, write budget and HDD capacity; the sidecar dump from MG0's Gn-out, with a restore drill and a re-seed drill before M3's pilot; infrastructure paging from M3 ([owner decision 143](#od-143)); business-hours abuse review, plus M5's notice pager ([owner decision 134](#od-134)).
- **v1 (M6):** MG6, then `escrow_draw_order` on (§20.9); the team directory (§16.11), whose pushes enter 19.6's load and 19.9's projection; 24/7 review.
- **v1 at M10 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)):** 19.11's `format2` gate with its purge and drop modes, each observe then on, with their metrics (19.8), the sweep (§11.13) and D-OPS-21's bounds; storage format 2's search index (§11.14), whose load enters 19.9's projection from D-TEST-13's computed cost, confirmed on production after the freeze ([owner decision 174](#od-174)).
- **Later:** [Q-OPS-2 (a)](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-small-object-packing) at its triggers; §10.16's [gen packs](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-gen-packs) at 19.9's gen trigger; [the next metadata cluster](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-next-metadata-cluster) at 19.9's triggers, a tracked year-one item (D-OPS-17; [owner decision 145](#od-145)), and later ones on new hosts; [a tool that moves placed repos between clusters](DESIGN-DEFER.md#evs-repo-move-tool), keeping one commit point, built by 19.9's cohorts row before the earliest projected cohort exhaustion; [a segment placement](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-segment-placement) before any HDD set, ordered by 19.9's hdd trigger, a tracked item whose lead time and page §23.7 gives and whose design is Q-OPS-11's residual ([owner decision 550](#od-550)); [a second site or an off-site copy](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-second-site), from operating data (owner decisions [89](#od-89), [94](#od-94)).
- **Deferred:** DESIGN-DEFER.md holds an entry for each Later item, linked above, and for [this section's v1 set](DESIGN-DEFER.md#ops-v1) ([owner decision 587](#od-587)).
- **Blocking:** the hardware's lead time (ordered in M0; the hosts and their PM9A3 set before M2's exit, for staging, and production at M3); §22.8's M2 drive-write run, which gates format 1 (D-TEST-11); the production cluster's write budget with its class liabilities in monitor, §22.8's `hdd` capacity and admitted-mix run, FS-119's cohort drill, the rota and the sidecar dump's restore drill (M3); the dns edge hosts and the pager's notice class (M5); HE's port 25 and reverse delegation (M9); the next metadata cluster's lead time, which sets 19.9's projection window.

## 20. Tiers, quotas, metering, and billing

### 20.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns tiers, prices, limits with their enforcement points and counters, the stored-byte count (with §11.13), client counting (X10, with §5), the payer of sidecar traffic (X11), Team billing and the escrow draw order, downgrade, and pricing conflicts (X16). §6.10.1 owns contract modes; §9-§17 own mechanisms and abuse-cap defaults, which §21 tightens.

### 20.5 Entitlement model

```go
// server/model: pro.go, pro_model.go
type NetworkTier string // "free" (Community), "pro", "team"
func (self *ProConfig) TierFor(tier NetworkTier) *ProTier // Tier(pro bool) remains
func NetworkTierOf(ctx context.Context, networkId server.Id) NetworkTier // highest in-window tier, Pro's cache
func NetworkSidecarLimits(ctx context.Context, networkId server.Id) *ProSidecarLimits // tier, then overrides
```

**Source.** The Team grant writes an in-window balance with `pro=true` and a new nullable `tier='team'`, so `pro` readers stay correct. Its renewal is `subscription_renewal`'s `SubscriptionTypeTeam` ("team"), its grant kinds `team` and `team_credit` join `grantGrace`, and the credit line carries `pro=false` and no `tier`, so it never confers the tier. A network's downgrade clock, `NetworkDowngradeTime`, is when its entitlement ended: the end_time of the newest window, already ended, of a `transfer_balance` whose `tier` conferred the tier the network left (MG6), for a Team its last `team` grant's end with its one-day grace and for Pro its last `pro` grant's, so one rule serves both ([owner decision 523](#od-523)).

**Overrides.** `network_sidecar_limit` rows raise a limit (ops) or tighten one (§21), snapshotted only for networks with rows, like Embed-plan rows (server/model/network_client_limit_model.go:13-25). A row never takes `evs_closure_bytes_per_day` below `evs_closure_bytes_floor`, and none overrides the floor or `evs_closure_uploads_per_s`: §21's `POST /abuse/action` refuses such a row, and `NetworkSidecarLimits` clamps to the floor ([owner decision 146](#od-146)) and ignores a pacing row, which every eraser's turn needs (20.7).

**Switch and zero.** Refusals ship dark behind `enforce_sidecar_limits`, like `enforce_concurrent_clients` (config/all/pro.yml:46-57), though an empty balance refuses as escrow does. `QuotaLimits` carries `enforced`, which api sets from the switch while the body keeps reporting the plan's tier and limits, so `ur status` and an app show them before enforcement starts; a daemon or reader that applies limits locally (§16.11's `directory_*` keys, §7.10's cleanup row, any other local pre-check) refuses only while `enforced` is true, an absent field reading false, and applies the closure floor and pacing whatever it says, since they hold while a network is spent, which is never dark ([owner decision 520](#od-520)). A mail receiver's three keys, `mail_inbound_message_bytes`, `mail_inbound_recipients` and `mail_inbound_repos_per_message`, also hold whatever it says, since they size a session's resources rather than refuse a creation and mxedge holds the same message cap whatever the switch: the receiver advertises SIZE at the first, answers `452 4.5.3` past the other two and refuses the EHLO with `451 4.3.0` when one reads 0 or -1, never advertising an unbounded SIZE, while the switch is off too (§15.5; [owner decision 580](#od-580)). While the switch is off, a rate whose limit only pro.yml sets, with no floor (`evs_drops_per_day`, `evs_drop_previews_per_day`, `evs_read_receipts_per_repo_day`), neither counts nor refuses and makes no Redis call ([owner decision 522](#od-522)). Enforced, zero means "not included": it refuses creation, never activation, reads, deletes, erasure, export or maintenance pushes (20.7; :23-30); a missing price withholds its overage (:17-21). server/model/pro_absent_test.go pins both states.

**Seats** are `network_member` rows (§7) active within 30 days, except Auditor and Billing admin: a member is active while any client under its `member_id` has an `auth_time` within 30 days, as the billing terms state, so an always-on device or a member's agent keeps its seat billed ([owner decision 515](#od-515)).

**Becoming Team.** `POST /network/team-create` (§7), then `POST /network/team-checkout`; the first `invoice.paid` writes the `team` renewal and the first period's grant and credit line and calls `UpdateProNetwork`, and each later period's `team` grant and `team_credit` line are `RefreshTeamTransferBalances`'s, at the period's anchor (20.9; [owner decision 514](#od-514)). Invoiced teams use market `manual`; lapse follows Pro.

### 20.6 X11: what counts toward the transfer balance

Decided (Q-QUOTA-2, Q-QUOTA-5, Q-QUOTA-6).

| Traffic | Mode | Payer |
|---|---|---|
| Sidecar↔sidecar, bridge, forwards and remote search (§11.14), one network | Network | the network: reserved at CreateContract, debited from close reports, while relayed, a requester-indexer pair as any peer's ([owner decision 609](#od-609)) |
| tlsedge→listener, mxedge→receiver | Service (C9) | listening network, by lease |
| sidecar→smtpedge | Service (C9) | sending network, by lease |
| evs transfer (HTTPS) | — | caller's network, by usage batches |
| Cross-network share | FriendsAndFamily | dialer's network, escrowed as Public |

**Leases**, one per edge process and active (network, meter), draw on escrow's per-balance Redis reservations, so both see one balance; they name no host or peer (§13.9 keeps per-host bytes 24 h). `Quota.Lease` handles are ref-counted over that one lease, and the last `Close` settles.

```text
edge (tlsedge, mxedge, smtpedge)   Redis: per-balance reservations      taskworker
 Lease(network, meter) --------> reserve a draw (below) in 20.9's draw order
 Spend(n): atomic add, no I/O
 renew ------------------------> reserve the next draw
 every 60 s: carve, then a UsageBatch ------------------------------> service_debit_journal
 Close or expiry: release -----> return the unused rest, in reverse     FlushServiceDebits debits, no
                                 draw order                             payout, and releases each token
draw     64 MiB (16 MiB on Community), or, when that is more, 4 s of the lease's own measured rate rounded up to a
         multiple of it, at most 16 times it (1 GiB; 256 MiB on Community), renewed with a quarter of the draw or
         2 s of traffic left, whichever is more: a slow lease draws as before and a fast one renews about once
         per 4 s with 2 s to do it, holding up to 4 s of its traffic unspent, which a Redis loss can over-admit
         (owner decision 518)
tokens   a lease's are lease/<lease_id>/<n>, each a reservation, living 15 min and extended every 5 min while the
         lease lives, the host spending none of a token's bytes 30 s before it could lapse; a carved debit's is
         svc/<usage_id>, living 24 h until its flush releases it (owner decision 517)
grant    a reservation is granted against the lower of the caller's reading of the balance and the balance's
         floor in Redis, {escrow_<balance_id>}approx_floor, the lowest credit shown in the last 2 min, which each
         flush lowers to the balance its debit left in the script that releases the debit's token; a host uses a
         reading for at most 30 s
carve    at each 60 s window one branch of the reservation script moves the window's used bytes, per balance in
         draw order, out of the lease's tokens into svc/<usage_id>, the journal row's usage id, a no-op if that
         token exists, so a carve runs once; the host sends (usage_id, balance_id, bytes) with the batch on the
         internal wire, so UsageEvent stays as engines see it, and posts a batch only once its carves answered;
         bytes whose reservation was gone are dropped from the event, counted in
         urnetwork_quota_lease_unbilled_bytes_total and alerted, and ApplyUsageBatch refuses a lease meter's event
         its carves do not cover (owner decision 517); no new table, column or Redis family
flush    FlushServiceDebits debits the journal with no payout and releases what each row reserved: evs rows
         nothing, relay rows their contract id, which is their usage id, and tls, mx and smtp rows svc/<usage_id>,
         releasing a token that is gone being a no-op; it takes no claim share in taskworker's claim admission,
         its chains registered in the production workload profile only and running on the ordinary queue and
         their function's lane, since the four existing shares at period 8 already spend the half of ordinary
         claim turns the scheduler allows; once service debits carry production volume (M5's tls leases at the
         earliest), the shares are rebalanced from a measurement, FlushTransferDebits, AdvancePayment and
         FlushServiceDebits at period 12 each and the totals lane and its drain at 8 (owner decisions 521, 522)
```

**Usage batches** (§11.13, edges' leases): every 60 s each producer sends one `UsageBatch` (20.7) of at most 1,000 events, a larger window splitting into several batches each under its own id, applied once by `batch_id` and flushed on SIGTERM; its stored-byte deltas move 20.7's nightly count; evs re-reads `OverLimit` every 5 s, so writes overshoot by about a minute, an answer past 200,000 networks (a setting) being cut and counted, the rest reading as not over (owner decisions [522](#od-522), [524](#od-524)).

```text
adds     an upload adds its segment's size, a committed push its record's length; evacuation moves records into
         parcels and packs, changing the count only by the log pages packed with them
purge    from format 2, a replaced versionless version's content leaves once deleted or kept only by a hold: the
         committing evs process reports kind-5 segments at seg/ (a staged version's only once its batch was
         evacuated), taskworker staged records as their batch is deleted; the sweep reports nothing, and the
         nightly count catches what only it freed
drop     from format 2, taskworker's drop job subtracts each seg/ object it deletes or moves to held at its stored
         size, within 60 s and once: its batch ids derive from (scan id, cursor range), not from its instance and
         window, and a held object's DELETE after its hold reports nothing; slots, outside the count, report
         nothing, and inline records and packed segments count until a later compaction, unscheduled (20.7, §11.13;
         owner decision 247)
apply    api inserts service_usage_batch(batch_id) with the batch's service_debit_journal rows and
         network_quota_state deltas in one transaction, the linearization point; a batch_id already present is
         a no-op answering 200; a batch naming meter relay is refused whole, relayed bytes settling by contract;
         a debit draws, in draw order, in-window balances (start_time <= now < end_time by the batch's caller's
         clock, depleted ones included), each up to its room, its balance_byte_count less the unapplied rows of
         both journals, Redis reservations not subtracted, and the rest overdraws the last in-window balance,
         or, with none in window, goes unbilled, counted in urnetwork_quota_unbilled_bytes_total; a carve names a
         network and meter the batch's events name, never passes its event's transfer bytes, leaves the rest to
         draw at apply, and is the carve already journaled under its (balance, usage id) (owner decision 522)
retry    a producer retries an unanswered batch for at most 10 min, then drops it, counted and alerting
         (under-billing only); batch rows live 24 h, past that horizon: one row per producer a minute, not one
         per network
loss     bytes are lost only by an unclean exit (its open window, <= 60 s of that process's metered bytes), by
         any batch dropped after 10 min unanswered, as in a Postgres outage over 10 min (§19.10), and by bytes a
         lease spent under a reservation that lapsed, at most one window's a host while Redis is lost to it; no
         byte counts twice; a lease's reserve behind lost bytes returns within 15 min, a carved window's within
         24 h (owner decision 517); 20.7's count corrects stored bytes
```

**Relayed bytes ([owner decision 10](#od-10)).**

```text
when     CreateContract for a Network-mode contract between two marked sidecar clients of one network, unless
         the pair already rides a P2P stream (server/model/contract_stream_binding.go); P2P bytes never count
mark     the contract's one INSERT sets payer_network_id: a payer, no transfer_escrow row and positive bytes
         name a relayed contract, since zero-escrow contracts set no payer; at close the payer's balances and
         each one's token are read before the close transaction, and the reservation's fence recovery and
         free-settlement check take that shape (§2.8 connect-1)
reserve  before the contract transaction, from the network's balances in 20.9's draw order, through the
         per-balance Redis reservations escrow and edge leases use (server/model/subscription_redis_admission.go);
         grant = min(requested, MaxContractTransferByteCount, max(MinContractTransferByteCount,
         available / 8)), signed into the contract, which clients size from (server/controller/
         connect_controller.go:43-58, :1291-1294); the reservation succeeding is the linearization point, and
         its pending marker the retry identity
refuse   no available balance: the network is spent (below), and CreateContract answers InsufficientBalance
         (connect/protocol/transfer.proto:539)
settle   the settled count (the mean of both parties' close reports) debits once, keyed by contract_id in
         service_debit_journal; the rest returns; a contract later bound to a P2P stream returns all of it
bound    overshoot past the balance is only what Redis loss over-admits, as for leases (20.15); grants shrink as
         the balance nears zero, so 380 pairs at Community's 20 sidecars cannot overdraw 30 GiB
cost     one Redis script per relayed contract (one per 1-256 MiB moved); no Postgres round trip added on a warm
         cache, credit read from a per-process draw-order cache of 5 s, and one read on a cold one
```

**Empty balance.** A failed lease or relayed reservation, or an evs debit that finds no balance, marks the network *spent*: new streams get `quota` (§9.6), open ones reset as leases run out (§6.7), mxedge answers temporary failures (§15.6), evs refuses payload-adding uploads and pushes (20.7), and CreateContract refuses relayed sidecar contracts, so remote searches over them fail and phones search what they hold (§11.14); a taskworker pass every 60 s (a setting), registered in the production workload profile only, clears the mark once an active in-window balance has room past its pending debits, Redis reservations aside, so a new grant reopens the network within about a minute, and a lease refused while Postgres shows room marks it again; the refusal carries `limit_key` `data`, `upgrade` true and limit and used 0, whatever the cause ([owner decision 522](#od-522)); the network reads its own repos at `evs_unpaid_read_rate`, a per-process token bucket per network at that rate divided by evs's blocks, so the network as a whole stays at the published rate, as §13.9's caps divide by blocks, a phone's fallback download of all included, others' not at all.

### 20.7 Enforcement points, counters, downgrade

**Counters.** Capacity other than storage is exact, recounted nightly: rows (entries, custom domains, clients, members) count in their transaction under a transaction-scoped per-network lock (PgBouncer-safe), and grants, admissions and ACL heads as api verifies them (§7.9). Storage counts from objects, below. Rates use one all-or-none Lua script per `{sq_<network_id>}` and `debit_id` (48 h keys), failing open for one window if Redis is lost: a call Redis does not answer, or whose answer cannot be read, passes and counts `urnetwork_quota_rate_fail_open_total`, and a caller whose own context ended gets that error. A debit id that passed answers pass again and counts nothing, and one that was refused recorded nothing and is judged afresh, so a caller asking again after a refusal's `retry_after_ms` keeps its debit id ([owner decision 516](#od-516)); a key names no day, the Quota windowing each count by its own clock, and a class-only key, as §11.12's erasure push rate, is counted in a call of its own, since under all-or-none its refusal would stop the call's other keys ([owner decision 524](#od-524)). `ReconcileSidecarCounters`, nightly, recomputes `storage_over`, the connected set and spent marks, and reports row-counted capacities over their limits as a metric, refusing nothing. Producers cache limits 5 s.

| Limit | Checked at | At the limit | On downgrade |
|---|---|---|---|
| `storage` | evs's over-limit list (20.6) over the nightly stored count (below) | uploads and pushes adding payload refused (Team: above 2 TiB, metered above 200 GiB); maintenance pushes, an erasure's bounded CLOSURE push and its uploads, re-seeding, config and mailcfg pushes within §7.9's limits, reads, deletes and export work | read-only |
| `tls_endpoints`: publish grants per (host, port) | grant activation; `ValidateListen` (§13.9) | refused | grants expire; standing names over quota suspended after 14 days by `model.SetTlsSuspension` with reason `quota:downgrade` and no `abuse_case`, lifted on renewal: no §21 action, so not mailed, not counted toward `restricted` or escalation, and re-derived by a restore |
| `dns_entries`: user RRsets | record CAS (§12.8) | refused | newest over quota withheld after 14 days |
| custom domains, mail From included (§14.6) | `custom-host-add` (§12.8) | Team only | web hosts and mail From withheld after 14 days; mail hosts keep MX, TLSA and routing |
| `config_admissions`, `acl_*` | the writer's validation, api's verifier (§7.9, §8.8); from 90% of `config_admissions`, admins' devices' cleanup list (§7.10's `cleanup` row) | delta or head refused | existing ones stay; new ones must fit |
| `smtp_*` | smtpedge `{smq_}` script (§14.7) | QUOTA; mail stays queued | next preamble |
| `sidecar_clients`: connected | enrollment and connect, as `concurrent_clients` (server/connect/resident.go:1170-1187), by one ZCOUNT from now to +inf of `{sq_<network_id>}connected_sidecar`, a sorted set of every marked client scored by its expiry ms, written and refreshed on the resident poll as `{np_}connected` is, its 48 h ttl refreshed at each write | refused; 4001 at connect | connected clients stay |
| members, SSO (§7.5, §7.6) | §7.5's Team routes, by `NetworkTierOf` | Team only | frozen: sign-in, data kept; invites, roles, IdP, SCIM refused |

**Downgrade clock.** A downgrade's 14 days count from `NetworkDowngradeTime` (20.5): a Team whose cycle invoice never pays keeps `team` for the period `RefreshTeamTransferBalances` granted at its anchor plus the grace, and its 14 days of withholding, and with them DNS's (§12), count from the moment `NetworkTierOf` drops, so day 13 changes nothing for a Team as for Pro ([owner decision 523](#od-523)).

**Stored bytes and maintenance at the limit (D-QUOTA-3).**

```text
stored   a repo's stored bytes are those §11.13's bytes row counts, with no payload reads: ciphertext as stored,
         padding and history included, the search index's files too (§11.14), in GiB (20.4); a deleted repo counts
         until shredded (§11.12), group mail once (§15.7), and a replaced versionless version's content only until
         the purge deletes it, a minute after its replacement, or while its batch lives when staged (at most 26 h;
         §11.13), the purge moving the count by usage batches, the nightly pass for what only its sweep frees (20.6;
         owner decision 165); a drop's listed content counts through its window until its job deletes it, the
         objects only a hold keeps leaving the count as above, so a held drop reads and bills as finished (owner
         decision 184), and its inline records and packed segments count until a later compaction, unscheduled
         (§11.13; owner decision 247); the team directory counts like any repo, and its reads debit transfer (20.6),
         with no exemption (owner decision 10)
count    taskworker's nightly pass over each repo's prefixes on its metadata cluster (the one its place/ names,
         owner decision 145) and on the segment cluster is the one segment GC makes (§11.13), so one LIST of each
         prefix serves both; a version counts from head windows and log pages while its batch exists, then from
         the parcel or pack that holds it, or, staged versionless content, from the segment evacuation writes for
         it, if any, so a record mid-evacuation counts twice only until its minute's batches are deleted, and the
         next pass corrects it; the pass runs as shard jobs, each replacing its per-network sums for the night in
         Redis {evsn_<night>} (48 h), and a closing job, once every shard of every metadata cluster has reported,
         writes each network's sum, zero for a network with a count and no sums, while a night that some shard
         never finished, or whose sums Redis lost, leaves the old count (owner decision 198); the pass writes an
         absolute count, deltas landing during it are not replayed, and the next pass corrects them; usage
         batches move the count between passes (20.6); §11.13 gives its cost
limit    at the storage limit, a network being over once its count reaches it (count >= limit, so a zero refuses the
         first upload; Team's limit is storage_overage_max while storage_gib_month is priced, or a larger storage a
         row sets, and storage while it is unpriced; owner decision 522), and while spent, evs refuses new payload,
         segment uploads and pushes naming a new segment or inline record alike; it accepts maintenance pushes, which
         add no payload (CONSUME, BASE, ERASE, PATH_EPOCH and its maps, DELETE, deletion and restore, EvsReseed), a
         CUT, whose one staged record only replaces its ref's erasure set (§11.12), and re-seed uploads; an erasure's
         CLOSURE push, bound to its ERASE and re-keying existing derived-field chains under §11.12's rekey rule, each
         new chain within Padmé of the one it replaces, with its payload and its ?closure=1 segment uploads, within
         the closure bounds below; and config and mailcfg pushes within §7.9's limits; so a full network can still
         erase and change policy; the search index's heads stop with the content pushes they ride, and its merges,
         roll-ups and builds add payload and wait until the network is under the limit and not spent, search
         answering from its partitions as they stand; removing its files is a deletion, accepted, and the settings
         version that turns it off, a new record, lands once under the limit and not spent (§11.14); accepted bytes
         count and debit as usual; in v0 an erasure frees no stored bytes; from format 2 (v1), deleting versionless
         files adds no payload, so it is accepted at the limit and frees their bytes a minute later, staged ones with
         their batch, and a DROP push that uploads no segment (its written checkpoints inline within §11.12's rekey
         bound, chunk sets re-cited, or boundaries removed) is accepted as maintenance, its index rewrites waiting as
         merges do, while one whose written checkpoint needs an upload gets QuotaRefusal and a cancel, adding no
         payload, is accepted (§11.13); other ciphertext stays until a later compaction, unscheduled (§11.12; owner
         decision 247)
closure  at the limit and while spent, §11.12's rekey row takes an eraser's ?closure=1 uploads, each at most
         1,088 KiB, one padded §15.7 i/ segment or §11.14 index file (else QuotaRefusal), only within its own
         evs_closure_uploads_per_min (60, fixed, read with a floor of 60), which {sq_} counts per eraser (the
         erasing sidecar, its token's ur_sidecar_id, §11.8), and within its turn of the network's pacing, R being
         evs_closure_uploads_per_s (4): each asking eraser holds a seat, a cell 1/R s wide at the tail of the
         network's seats, good from its instant to the end of its second; a seat is handed out only in a second
         with a free cell, so the network takes at most R uploads a second whatever asks arrive and in whatever
         order; with k erasers asking, each takes one every k/R s; an eraser that misses its seat's second is
         seated again, at once while the second has a free cell and else one round later (owner decision 516);
         past either it answers that upload 429 with retry_after_ms, the pacing's refusal naming
         evs_closure_uploads_per_s with its limit, the uploads the network took in that second and the wait to its
         seat or the next second; {sq_} counts the network's ERASE, CUT and CLOSURE pushes against
```
