```text
FI-1   closure: a committed head's dependency closure (statements, records, entries, segments, slots, maps, wraps of
       its generation) is retrievable, from the one metadata cluster its place/ names or the packs evacuation made,
       and decrypts for a current reader, except what a durable, visible, authorized erasure, shred or executed drop
       removed (§11)
FI-2   outcomes: each operation ends committed, aborted or unknown; unknown never triggers destructive cleanup; a
       retry of a committed operation returns its original result, and a refusal a client received stays true:
       once any attempt of a push id is answered a refusal, no attempt of it commits, whenever it reaches evs,
       save one validated before its repo's shred began, which the shred destroys (I-EVS-3); a reclaimed
       preparation never commits later (§11, §16)
FI-3   commit-point authorization: every head transition carries, and the oracle re-verifies, the authorization pin,
       generation pin, path epoch and lifecycle state current at its head CAS, retries and seals included; nothing
       committing later than §10.6's window after a gate closes uses an excluded generation (§8, §10, §11)
FI-4   one ladder: each generation has one authenticated parent and commitment C_g, whichever path raised it; every
       reader converges on it; none regresses (§10)
FI-5   lifecycle: restore and shred have one winner; a restored repo holds its whole key closure; a shredded or erased
       object never returns, a stale re-seed included, unless no surviving device holds the ERASE (§11.12's
       residual), which §19.10's close report flags by repo, and a dropped object never returns, a stale re-seed
       included, except as FI-27 bounds it (§11, §19)
FI-6   visibility: nothing uncommitted evicts a file's newest committed version, which readers find in its entry or
       the head window, and no directory delta leaves the window before its name table holds it; every uncommitted
       object (a dead record with its slots, an unadopted segment, a staged wrap, an abandoned path map) becomes
       reclaimable after its deadline, found without the log, but a slot whose origin names a statement no
       batch, container or head names, its attempt dead between its slot round and its record (owner decision
       400), and, while evacuation's delete of them is off, a dead record's slots (owner decision 399); nothing
       committed or unknown is reclaimed (§11)
FI-7   effects: an approval use is reserved before its effect and stays consumed or explicitly uncertain after any
       crash; no second effect; run taint and requester bindings survive restarts (§16)
FI-8   attribution: a run restore changes only state attributable to its run, or reports ambiguity, and checks its
       preview on the bytes it moves aside, never on an earlier read, discarding no others (§16)
FI-9   git: an acknowledged push has the declared ref, tree, ancestry and per-ref outcome; stock clients see standard
       non-fast-forward errors; a git-mode tip commits only once ur/lfs holds every git-lfs object it requires, safe
       from every prune, and no prune removes an object a current tip requires (§11)
FI-10  witnesses: a witness names exactly the state it compared; stale peers cannot manufacture freshness; a fork
       under one epoch alarms or reads unwitnessed (§2, §6)
FI-11  path integrity: no application byte reaches a backend before its audience check, whatever the SNI or ALPN, nor
       a target after its flow's revocation (§17.6, D-BRIDGE-21), and no flow opens, or stays open past its close,
       under a rule the host has durably judged revoked, across late compiles, new client generations and restarts
       (17.8's engine; DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 12); a proof accepts only what the MX's own state machine accepts
       (§13, §14, §17)
FI-12  recovery: after a Postgres or site loss, the newest copy a device or dump holds comes back exactly (oids, C_v,
       decryptability, identities, labels), save what §19.10's postgres step lists in the incident (a suffixed
       network name, a login left for a reset) or keeps at the main dump's age (rows the sidecar dump does not
       name), and nothing erased or dropped (but as FI-5 allows), shredded or revoked returns; an object whose every
       shard exists survives a second host (§19)
FI-13  accounting: (a) every metered byte debits at most once and, barring an unclean producer exit, a batch dropped
       past its 10-min retry horizon, or a network with no in-window balance, exactly once; (b) a period's billed
       quantity equals its rows' newest values; (c) after each nightly pass, stored bytes equal the seg/, pack/ and
       hp/ objects' sizes plus the lengths heads and log pages give for records still in batches, less objects only a
       hold keeps, objects held for a drop included, and containers whose every record a newer container's pidx/
       entry names (20.7); (d) 20.9's E-a to E-e (§20)
FI-14  write budget: (a) with the budget on, on each metadata set's busiest drive not under heal (§19.6's governor
       skips one), the writes of classes other than P0 over any 24 h stay within 24 h of refill plus the bucket's
       depth (0.8 DWPD) and one 5 s interval's issue times the pricing error, less the P0 writes the bucket held in
       those 24 h, which are P0's measured writes less its forgiven excess, the bytes past what the bucket held (owner
       decision 190), so the drive writes past that only by the forgiven excess; P0's bytes and forgiven excess are
       measured and reported by kind (§19.8), not bounded (owner decision 186); (b) conservation: each interval's P1
       and unfunded P2 debits stay within T, funded P2 spends only the wallet W, W never exceeds the priced funded

       refused; (d) a network is refused only while one with less queued priced bytes per weight is served, or,

       later names it; unknown and refused pushes purge nothing; every path's newest committed version keeps all its

FI-17  versioning: a committed version names a kind-5 segment only as §11.7's citation rule allows, a staged

FI-18  index results: for every scope, device and sync state, the candidates for a normalized query include every

FI-19  index erasure: once the erasure of a document completes, no committed version of an index file that a current

FI-20  roll-up: each expired bucket of a ref is rolled into all by at most one committed roll-up, whose plaintext

FI-21  search scope and taint: every hit is from a repo the caller's subject may read by §8's local evaluation and
       §8.5's consent, an EvsShare or audit reader having deposited, and evs having acknowledged, a read receipt

       leaves the device except a remote search's, sealed end to end to an indexer FI-24 allows (§16, §2)
FI-22  determinism: every index object's plaintext is a function of its format version, normalization version,
       extractor version and inputs alone, byte-equal on every build leg; decoders accept only canonical encodings, so
       re-encoding what one decoded reproduces its bytes; plaintext hashes are taken before encryption, and nothing is
       compressed (§11)
FI-23  fetch privacy: the index objects a search fetches, and their order, depend only on the device's sync state, its
```

Beyond the schedules:

- **lb drain (warp/warpctl/run.go:1453); Redis failover; Postgres or PgBouncer restart; resident migration; 60 s ack timeout:** clients retry streamed PUTs, which nginx cannot (warp/warpctl/config.go:2307); sockets heal; halts reload; streams reset TRANSFER_FAILED; RPC retries.
- **Clocks ±10 min; migration N+1 before code; sidecar N vs server N±1:** tickets, skew and expiry hold; explicit VERSION or UNIMPLEMENTED.
- **Kills mid-keychain write:** the keychain opens at its old or new state (§5.9).

### 22.9 Conformance and platform budgets

- **git** (2.34, Ubuntu 22.04's, https://ubuntuupdates.org/package/core/jammy/main/base/git; 2.43, Ubuntu 24.04's and Claude Code cloud's; latest; Windows, Xcode; go-git, JGit, libgit2; OpenSSH): through the local tier, and `git-remote-ur` without a prior mount, oids equal a reference; stock non-fast-forward errors, sibling pushes from one base giving one; `git push --atomic` fails before any write; a two-ref push reports per-ref statuses; a daemon killed between the remote commit and update-ref reconciles from its journal; foreign new commits refused, signed imports accepted; a sha256 repository refused, naming it, before any evs write ([owner decision 249](#od-249)).
- **git-lfs** (3.x as Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 ship it, and the latest; `lfs.standalonetransferagent`; `GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE`): FS-73's flows with stock clients, whose T3 test runs in server's evshost ([owner decision 548](#od-548)), pointer files byte-exact and export's oids equal to git's, its tip check included over http, ssh and `git-remote-ur`, with no skip option set and with `--no-verify` and `GIT_LFS_SKIP_PUSH`.
- **Restore** (darwin on APFS; linux on ext4, xfs and an NFS mount; windows on NTFS; a FAT volume on each; symlinks on each, Windows with and without the symlink privilege): FS-115's apply through each volume's no-replace rename, its hard-link fallback, and `unsupported` where it has neither, with Windows's in-use refusal.
- **File clusters** (D-OPS-20's in-house MinIO build, every cluster, each build, upgrade and new cluster; D-OPS-4): stale conditions refused with a host or quorum lost (§11.3); §19.6's deadline and settle rules, by FS-114's late-drive cases: a request past its x-ur-deadline-ms, sent late by the clock rule's margin (sidecartest/blobsuite's `Settle.LateBy`, 200 ms by default; [owner decision 545](#od-545)), refused where it takes its key's lock, no drive commit begun past it, and a PUT or DELETE whose drive commits are held after their checks past the 30 s drive timeout, its coordinator killed, taking effect before the next request on its key or never, the newer acknowledged state surviving release and a full heal, since a removal marker's collection deletes unconditionally ([owner decision 148](#od-148)), as from v1 do the versionless purge's and the marker collection's kind-5 and slot DELETEs and a drop job's DELETEs; the lag from a cancel to a write's last drive answer, measured and reported, which no margin relies on; no heal resurrects a deleted object or spreads a version fewer than a read quorum of drives hold; read-after-write consistency, and a LIST answered whole or 503 ([owner decision 226](#od-226)); a read answering 404 only on a read quorum's absence: a DriveMiss'd object with two hosts down reads 503, and while a host reconnects every host serves it or answers 503, never 404 ([owner decision 511](#od-511)); checksums; ranged GET; Delete, and a DELETE naming its object's LastModified refused 412 for a newer one ([owner decision 225](#od-225)); no lifecycle rule set on either bucket; one pool per cluster (FS-63).
- **MTAs** (Postfix (may, dane), Exim; Gmail, Outlook.com, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, iCloud, SES, Proton, Fastmail): in, D-MAIL-9's census with nothing lost; out, §14.4 levels, DKIM, strict DMARC, which B's selector fails for A's network and burners, FCrDNS, JMRP and CFL joins; aggregate reports as FS-39, a one-connection, ten-recipient send raising no alarm.

- **Index determinism** (darwin/arm64, linux/amd64 and arm64, windows/amd64, gomobile android/arm64 and the iOS settings, js/wasm in Node and, through Playwright, Chrome, Firefox and Safari): testdata/index/, its extraction (mail, files, the character-reference table, the charset labels) and search body sizes included, reproduces byte-equal plaintext and hashes under GOMAXPROCS 1 and 16, repeated runs (Go randomizes map order) and changed TZ and locale; the linked `norm.Version`, `cases.UnicodeVersion` and `unicode.Version` equal the format's normalization version and x/text's linked module version equals `IndexFileHeader` field 14's, so a toolchain or x/text bump fails until a new one is assigned (D-TEST-15).

### 22.11 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mock engines | fast | hide wire bugs | fakes at store interfaces |
| Random interleavings without named barriers | no hooks at protocol steps | a found race cannot be replayed; no commit point is held at its lost response | rejected: fixed schedules plus a seeded explorer (D-TEST-10) |
| Search results checked by the index's own decoder | simple | shares the index's bugs | rejected: an oracle written apart (D-TEST-14) |
| Purge or drop deletes on from format 2's first day | storage freed at once | a purge or drop bug destroys content no check restores | rejected: observe first (D-TEST-12, D-TEST-18) |

### 22.12 Decisions proposed

**D-TEST-1 (proposed).** T1, T2, T4 and T3's store suites gate merges, T3's FS rows running nightly and at each Gn-out (22.8's cadence), `sidecar/test.sh` running in RUN-ALL after connect; server tests of sidecar engines set `WARP_TEST_ENV_FAIL_FAST=1`; sidecar tests follow connect/CODESTYLE.md:200-217. *Why:* R-TEST-1, R-TEST-9.

**D-TEST-2 (proposed).** `sidecartest` rebuilds connect's helpers from exported API and ships fakes whose store suites server also runs on real stores. *Why:* the helpers are unimportable (Q-TEST-1); shared suites keep fakes honest.

**D-TEST-3 (proposed).** 22.5's gates and 22.9's budgets fail the build; raising one needs a reviewed change (sdk/build/APPLE_EXTENSION_MEMORY_BUDGET.md). *Why:* I-12; 4,690,096 B of iOS headroom.

**D-TEST-4 (proposed).** Every 22.6 target ships seeds and, given a second implementation, a differential oracle. *Why:* parsers face hostile peers, and protobuf encoding is not canonical (https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding/#field-order).

**D-TEST-5 (proposed).** Every scenario runs 22.7's harness and guard; later (22.17's Later, beyond M0-M10), a synthetic main network repeats S2 and S5-S7 hourly. *Why:* R-TEST-3 is a system property.

**D-TEST-6 (proposed).** The revocation suite runs with evs's gate off, through `Net.SetEvsGate`, which only a sidecar_testhooks build carries (22.4). *Why:* server refusal is defense in depth (I-5).

**D-TEST-7 (proposed).** 22.8 runs per milestone and its soak before each release; conformance peers are pinned and rerun per pin change. *Why:* fan-out fails only under load; peers change silently.

**D-TEST-8 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 99](#od-99): no external review gates a freeze or the claim.

**D-TEST-9 (proposed).** Freezes pass 22.10's gates in D-PHASE-7's two steps. *Why:* one conditional write orders storage ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), and nothing is audited ([owner decision 99](#od-99)).

**D-TEST-10 (proposed).** Every state machine of §7-§21, and §5.6's device revocation, is tested by deterministic fault schedules (FS-1 to FS-126), each run on the tiers its row names (T2's fakes, T3's real stores) against FI-1 to FI-30, beside TLA+ models of the separate durable objects (`EvsCommit.tla`), of the index roll-up (`IndexRollup.tla`) and of the store's settle rule (`StoreSettle.tla`) and a Porcupine check, in server's tests, of T3 histories with unknown outcomes, T3 moving stores' time in one reviewed file (22.8's real rule). *Why:* single-object conditional writes order storage ([owner decision 2](#od-2)) and no transaction spans objects, so every commit point, retry and cleanup must be shown under lost responses, crashes and stale processes, and the roll-up is a multi-push protocol whose lock, CAS and erasure race no schedule alone exhausts; nothing is audited ([owner decision 99](#od-99)).

**D-TEST-11 (proposed).** §22.8's `nvme` run on the PM9A3 set gates M2's exit and format 1's freeze: at 2× year one's mix with the write budget on, refilled at 0.8 DWPD for the run, the budget refuses no push, at most 43 KiB is written per push per drive, its P2 work included and charged once from the wallet (FS-116, which runs first, on exact costs), P0's bytes by kind are measured against the refill, setting §19.8's P0 warn line at four times their hourly share, at most half the refill, with the P0 page silent at that mix (P0 past the refill is FS-117's, [owner decision 186](#od-186)), and writes stay within 50% of rated write IOPS, on 1 KiB XFS blocks, or on 4 KiB only if format 2's projected mix (format 1's measured price table applied to §11.13's per-push index operations, the index on in every eligible repo) also fits there; its per-operation costs become §11.13's price table. *Why:* [owner decision 140](#od-140)'s binding limits, at most 0.8 DWPD and 50% of rated write IOPS, which the design meets at ~27-43 KiB a push, 43 KiB being 0.8 DWPD at 400 pushes/s; the run refills at that limit, not production's 0.768, which leaves room for the bucket's 1 h of depth (§11.13); the head's If-Match overwrite alone writes ~14 KiB ([owner decision 2](#od-2)), so the record's first ~10-15 KiB estimate was withdrawn (Q-EVS-9, decided); mkfs fixes the block size for format 2 too: at 2× year one format 1 writes ~40-43 KiB a push on 4 KiB blocks (~30-33 on 1 KiB), and the default-on index ([owner decision 156](#od-156)) adds ~4 on 1 KiB blocks at one companion push a minute per writer, and ~2 on 4 KiB blocks at one every 5 minutes ([owner decision 172](#od-172); §11.13).

**D-TEST-12 (proposed).** The versionless purge ships in observe mode (§19.11's `purge: observe`), logging candidates and deleting nothing while taskworker checks that no retained version names one; deletes turn on once FS-64 to FS-71 pass on their rows' tiers and a production soak after the final freeze (at least 14 days and 10,000 candidates) finds none that a retained version names, and until then the gate admits only internal networks and design partners (D-PHASE-10), so later networks get [owner decision 161](#od-161)'s purge from their first format-2 push. *Why:* a purge bug destroys content no other check restores, and only production shows real clients' citations.

**D-TEST-13 (proposed).** Format 2's bytes freeze only when its drive-write cost, projected from §22.8's M2 price table (D-TEST-11) and the M10 `index` row's T3 operation counts, with the index on in every eligible repo, purges and staging on and each companion push charged to the content pushes it indexes, meets D-TEST-11's gate; after the freeze, while §19.11's `format2` gate holds format 2 to internal networks and design partners, production's write budget must show measured over priced drive bytes within 10%, and a larger ratio holds the gate there until §19.9's next cluster or a later format change restores the fit; runs with the index off attribute each increment. *Why:* [owner decision 174](#od-174), which buys no staging drives and accepts that a miss found after the freeze costs more clusters sooner ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) or a format change; [owner decision 140](#od-140) binds format 2 too, and at [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s cadence §11.13's costs put a push, with the default-on index, at ~34-37 KiB at 2× year one on 1 KiB blocks but ~42-45 KiB on 4 KiB blocks, against the gate's 43.

**D-TEST-14 (proposed).** Every search schedule checks its results against `SearchOracle` (22.4), which shares no index code: a desktop's text-verified hits equal its set, every device's candidates include its covered set, and each uncovered document is found from local text or reported not yet searchable; the index schedules also search from a fresh cache after the purge has taken every replaced index version. The oracle's extractor and the index's are held to one set of conformance vectors and to equality under a fuzz target, since on damaged mail two readings of the same rule are the likeliest way for the two to differ (DESIGN-DETAILS.md section 11). *Why:* completeness needs extraction, masking, coverage and roll-ups all correct, and an oracle sharing their code shares their bugs; a warm cache or an uncollected version can hide a lost tombstone.

**D-TEST-15 (proposed).** testdata/index/ fixes vectors with plaintext hashes (normalization, extraction (mail, files, the character-reference table, the charset labels), trigram sets, head files, seals, merges, roll-ups, doc and tombstone tables, a roll-up promoting a carried entry into a newer bucket's shards, and search body sizes) that every test.sh reproduces byte for byte on every leg, js/wasm and gomobile included; decoders accept only canonical encodings; every leg builds with one Go toolchain, since x/text picks its Unicode 15.0.0 or 17.0.0 tables by toolchain (.gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.43.0/unicode/norm/tables15.0.0.go:3, `//go:build !go1.27`; connect/go.mod:3 and sdk/go.mod:3, `go 1.27.4`), and the vectors check the linked `norm.Version`, `cases.UnicodeVersion` and `unicode.Version` and x/text's module version (`IndexFileHeader` field 14), and include examples of the 19,960 two-rune strings that v0.40.0's and v0.41.0's NFC compose wrongly under go1.27.3: the four Hebrew pairs (U+05D2 U+0307, U+05DA U+0307, U+FB32 U+0307, U+FB3A U+0307) and a supplementary letter, U+10044 U+0307, which v0.40.0 composes to U+1E0A (§4.7); v0.40.0, which connect/go.mod:33 requires, keys recomposition on runes clipped to 16 bits (.gomodcache/golang.org/x/text@v0.40.0/unicode/norm/forminfo.go:217; tables17.0.0.go:8070-8071 map 0x05D20307 to U+105C9 and 0x05DA0307 to U+105E4), while v0.43.0, which server/go.mod:59 requires, keys full runes (forminfo.go:217), and both report Unicode 17.0.0. *Why:* convergent roll-ups, local reproduction and the indexer's checks rest on determinism (FI-22), which map order, a toolchain or x/text's tables and code break silently.

**D-TEST-16 (proposed).** Remote search is checked against `SearchOracle` as local search is, and its privacy by a relay capture: one frame-size sequence per kind whatever the query, results or post-parse failure, and equal evs request logs on both devices with and without it (FS-83, FI-24); the pair's contracts are accounted like any peer's, so no sweep holds a window's reports ([owner decision 609](#od-609)). *Why:* fixed sizes and evs's blindness are [owner decision 175](#od-175)'s whole privacy claim, and one optimization would break either silently: an early short reply, or a sync before answering.

**D-TEST-17 (proposed).** FS-86 gates the directory against §16.11's cost table: its M6 case on announce entries at M6's Gn-out, and its card case at the later of M6's and M10's, each at 500 members in physical time on T3 and, as fake-clock days with one physical peak hour at 3x bursts beside §22.8's 1x year-one mix, at the Team limit (2,000 members, 5,000 admissions) and at a 5,000-member stress case; a golden schedule (`DirectoryCostOracle`) computes each reader's expected requests, path reads and ciphertext bytes from the events and sync times alone, the measured ones staying within 1.25 times them per reader-day and per team-day, and disabling coalescing, head reproduction or unchanged-card suppression fails that check; the cards ref's commits meet the table's p99, rerun and 429 ceilings on T3's 4-host file-cluster layout with nothing else running on the machine, over a whole peak hour at the Team limit's rate, the local stack's run being a reduced-scale form that logs a miss and fails nothing ([owner decision 598](#od-598)), and injected store delays fail them; the year-one mix keeps its p99; a cold phone past 8 MiB on a metered link shows partial coverage it can continue; priced NVMe bytes per push per drive meet §11.13's price table, and the directory's pushes join format 2's computed write gate, which production confirms after the freeze (D-TEST-13; [owner decision 174](#od-174)). A miss at the Team limit blocks its gate, and the owner hears then. *Why:* reader transfer, per-stream reads and one ref's head are the directory's binding terms, and a number recorded with no ceiling cannot fail.

**D-TEST-18 (proposed).** Drop deletes ship in observe mode (§19.11's `drop: observe`): jobs run every phase and record their delete sets, deleting nothing, while the drop oracle (taskworker's verify, written apart from mark) checks each set against every retained version. Deletes turn on only once FS-89 to FS-96 pass on their tiers, TLC checks I-EVS-15 and FI-27, and a production soak on internal networks and design partners of at least 30 days and 200 jobs, half of them on repos with renames and cross-ref copies, finds no delete-set member that a retained version names. *Why:* a drop deletes keep-forever content ([owner decision 173](#od-173)), the costliest bug class, and observe mode shows its sets on real histories first.

### 22.13 Open questions

**Q-TEST-1.** Cross-cutting (X9, §4): copy connect's test helpers or export them? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a), `sidecartest` builds on connect's exported API; every T2 scenario using the fake contract issuer or ControlId sink also runs in T3 on server's exchange (server/connect/resident.go:902), and a divergence fails; a connect pin change reruns both tiers; a recurring drift, or a helper needing unexported state, raises an X9 row for `connect/connecttest` to the owner. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-2.** The local stack lacks an object store, and its one Redis node accepts cross-slot commands production's cluster rejects. **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (a) plus (b), in 22.4's topologies: locally a 3-master Redis Cluster on 8.10.2 and one 8-drive MinIO at EC:4 from the production source; in T3 and at the release gate the same cluster and MinIO as 4 × 2 at EC:4 and 4 × 4 at EC:8; a runtime and static CROSSSLOT lint; canary is no substitute. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-3.** Who reviews externally? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 99](#od-99)):** nobody for now; 22.10's gates stand in. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-4.** How is the iOS tunnel's footprint verified without an iPhone (connect/MEMSTEADY.md:18)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 100](#od-100)):** (b), surrogate cells only (22.9), accepting 22.16's jetsam risk. *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-5 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 24](#od-24); §11 holds the residual.

**Q-TEST-6.** Does §6.11's `oneof` ban cover every sidecar proto or only envelope, stream and push messages? **Closed by peer review 2026-11-04:** (b). No `oneof` appears in envelope, stream or push messages, or in any message they carry transitively; 22.5's descriptor lint walks from those roots over the released descriptors and fails on a oneof outside its explicit allowlist, empty in v0; other protos may use one. The reason is allocation: protobuf-go allocates a wrapper for each set oneof field, and hot-path decodes stay allocation-free (§10.4's `UrMlsCredential` has none). *Residual:* none.

**Q-TEST-7.** Where does continuous fuzzing run? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 101](#od-101)):** (c), nowhere; seeds run as Go tests (22.6). *Residual:* none.

### 22.14 Departures from PLAN.md

None. PLAN.md says nothing about testing.

- **Consumes:** §2.8's list; `make check` (§4); `testHookSecret` sites (§5, §9's `K_sock`, `K_tok` and `K_seal`, §10, §11, §13-§15, §17's ShareKey and ShareSigner seeds) and `testHookBarrier` sites at every linearization point (§7-§21, and §5.6's revocation posts); §5-§21's targets; §19's environments, W2, drive counters and M2's staging cluster (§19.11); §23's milestones and gate map; from M6, §16.11's directory; from M10, the barriers of the purge, the sweep, evacuation's staged decision, seals, merges, the roll-up lock, the migration and the drop job (§11), §11.14's remote search, §16's search tools, §18's injected network and charging state, RECORD.md's search fields and, after format 2's freeze, production's write-budget counters ([owner decision 174](#od-174)).
- **Subprotocol messages, API routes, tables:** none; release builds carry no test route.
- **Services and config:** server/local's 3-master Redis Cluster and 8-drive MinIO, T3's MinIO clusters (22.4); RUN-ALL, TEST-PERF and test-main cells; the nightly form, `sidecar/test.sh --cadence nightly`, run by a launchd job on a host the owner names, with T3's private stores on that host, each gate sweep of the build running that form, and never taking tests/network-intensive-suite-lock.sh ([owner decision 539](#od-539)).
- **Assumptions about other sections:** §19 runs T6 with test roots and LE staging, runs M2's staging cluster on the production hosts' PM9A3 set with §19.6's settings and counters, rebuilt empty and SMART-rechecked before M3 (§19.11), runs 22.9's file-cluster suite on every new cluster before `place_new` names it, and gives §19.11's format2 gate a purge mode and a `drop` mode (observe, on) that admit only internal networks and design partners while observing (D-TEST-12, D-TEST-18); §23.8 gates freezes in D-PHASE-7's two steps, the escrow order at M6's entry on FS-46 and 20.9's benchmark, and burners on D-MAIL-9; §23.4's M2 exit names FS-57 to FS-63, FS-113, FS-114's head and marker cases, FS-116 to FS-118 and FS-72's and FS-95's format-1 cases, and §23.6's gate map lists each FS at every gate its row names, later parts included (FS-19, FS-23, FS-30, FS-38, FS-39, FS-41, FS-42, FS-47, FS-66, FS-69, FS-76 to FS-78, FS-80, FS-83 to FS-88, FS-92, FS-97 to FS-101, FS-106, FS-109 to FS-112, FS-114, FS-124 and FS-125; FS-82's mail and coverage cases at M7 and M8), FS-63 and FS-119 again at each next metadata cluster, FS-119 first at M3-out, M10's schedules, and S7's SNI-less abuse@`<root>` case at M5; every index file an erasure rewrites fits §11.12's closure upload bound; each owning section names a barrier at each linearization point (22.8's rules).

### 22.16 Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unaudited novel crypto passes every test, 0x0010 having no vectors ([owner decision 99](#od-99)) | Medium | Critical | 22.10's interop artifact; §10.4's mapping and KATs; its disclosure ([owner decision 119](#od-119)) |
| A scanner gap lets a leak pass | Medium | High | decompression, self-test, schema guard |
| A race no schedule names passes every test | Medium | High | barriers at every linearization point; the seeded explorer; TLC and Porcupine (D-TEST-10) |
| Measured drive writes miss D-TEST-11's gate (format 1) or D-TEST-13's (format 2, the index on everywhere) | Medium | High | 1 KiB blocks and §19.6's settings, chosen at M2 on format 2's projection too; [owner decision 172](#od-172)'s companion cadence; M2's exit and each freeze wait for their gate, format 2's on D-TEST-13's projection, confirmed on production after the freeze ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |
| The governor's accounts charge P2 twice, let a class other than P0 issue while P0 holds the bucket empty, or keep the other classes stopped after a P0 storm ends, so pushes are refused early or the drives wear past the budget by more than P0's forgiven excess | Low | High | one conservation equation and FI-14 (a) and (b), checked after every step; FS-116's exact-cost schedule and its mutant before D-TEST-11's hardware run; FS-117's day of P0 alone past the refill, the day after it, and its mutants |
| HE refuses port 25, blocking outbound conformance | Unknown | High | asked in M0 (§23.7) |
| Test hooks reach a release, exposing keys or stalling steps | Low | Critical | build tag; `make check` |
| A jetsam regression reaches users | High | High | surrogates; `make size` |
| A purge bug deletes a newest version's content | Low | Critical | observe mode and its soak (D-TEST-12); FI-16 model-checked; FS-64 to FS-71 |
| The oracle shares a normalization bug with the index | Medium | Medium | written apart, sharing only the published tables; fixed vectors; 22.6's reference extractor |
| A phone's "search more" leaks the query through what it fetches | Low | High | FI-23's trace equality; no body fetched before an open; a remote search's sizes and evs logs are FI-24's |
| A malicious server injecting mail reads trigram presence from padded sizes (DBREACH) | Medium | High | no compression; Padmé and §11.14's keyed pad; 22.7's fixture fails the build on a recovered code |
| A drop bug deletes live content | Low | Critical | D-TEST-18's observe soak; FI-27 and I-EVS-15 model-checked; FS-89 to FS-96 |

### 23.1 Purpose and scope

This section owns X15: milestones M0-M10 on two tracks, staffing, exit criteria, the gate map, freezes, lead times, publication and merges. What each milestone builds belongs to §4-§18 and §21; environments, hardware and releases to §19; tests and gates to §22.

### 23.3 What exists today

- No repo has a `sidecar` branch; sidecar is PUBLIC since [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip, its two `main` commits holding only documents (§4.3).
- Releases check out `main` in every repo (build/all/run.sh:666-671, :825-876). server's lock pins each sibling's commit (server/local/source-graph/lock.yml:7-39), checked against each HEAD (server/local/source-graph/source_graph_test.go:135-141); sn builds server's packages and repeats its replaces, which Go does not inherit (sn/go.mod:212-215).
- A migration's version is its slice index plus one (server/db_migrations.go:163-165), so an applied migration cannot move.

RS1-RS3 are recURd's stages (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:892-904; RECORD.md, §16.8), each released once its last item lands; BS1 is the burner launch. **v0** is what personal networks get, M0-M5 and M7-M9, with app hosts at M8; **v1** is M6, M10 and M7-M9's Team items, M10 bringing versionless objects and search to every network ([owner decision 163](#od-163)); **Later** follows M9 and M10. `sidecar` branches start at M0 in every touched repo ([owner decision 196](#od-196)): sidecar, connect, server, sdk, build and sn, which must repeat server's sidecar replace (23.3); xops for D-OPS-18's dumps; warp for §19.11's W5, W2 and W8; mmm; config (pro.yml's `sidecar:` blocks, `preview_networks`); vault; and the minio fork for D-OPS-20's build ([owner decision 195](#od-195)). M0-M10 build straight through on those branches, in dependency order; 23.8 says what happens at a gate the build cannot meet ([owner decision 194](#od-194)).

### 23.5 X15: two tracks and staffing

Team A (recURd) builds M0-M4 and M6; team B (mail and burner, [owner decision 9](#od-9)) builds M5 and M7-M9, with four engineers by M2's exit: one from M0 on `smtpproof`'s BDAT and DATA proofs ([owner decision 125](#od-125)) and mail's lead times, then one each for edges and DNS, mail ingress and receivers, and app seams. M5 is on track B because M7 needs its dns edge, DNSSEC soak, C9 and abuse intake, and RS2 its TLS edge. If team B is not staffed by M2's exit, team A builds M5 before M6, M7-M9 follow M6, and the owner hears then.

M10 is track A's ([owner decision 169](#od-169)): about three more engineers, hired from M3's entry, build §11's format 2, the index and the search tools from M4's exit beside M6, about 9-12 engineer-months by inference; its hold, team, mail and phone cases wait for M5, M6, M7 and M8 (D-PHASE-8). If the engineers are not there by M4's exit, M10 follows M6, and the owner hears then.

M2's critical path is §10.4's subset ([owner decision 43](#od-43)'s 2-4 engineer-months) and §22.10's 0x0010 interop; §7.9, §11 and gkm build in parallel against a fake of the subset, and D-TEST-11's run needs the production hosts and their PM9A3 set before M2's exit (23.7). If either slips, M2's exit and every later milestone's exit slip with it, since both tracks share M0-M2; the build goes on, with formats unfrozen ([owner decision 194](#od-194); 23.8).

### 23.8 Review gates

- **G0.** Peer review of DESIGN.md; the density rule: no content duplicated across sections (each item in its owning section, cited elsewhere), except §2.8's published list, §3.7's flows and Requirements rows ([owner decision 551](#od-551)), normative formats and state machines in fenced blocks, prose dense; D-ARCH-4's assembly check passes; 23.6's M0-M2 items settled; RECORD.md reviewed here or by M2's entry. The density rule replaced the OUTLINE word ceilings (+10%) on 2026-11-04: the normative formats and state machines peer review required put every section over its ceiling (the assembly's word table), and a ceiling cuts normative content where this rule cuts repetition. The owner signed G0 on 2026-11-06 ([owner decision 193](#od-193)). A reviewer's re-check of the 21 items DESIGN-REVIEW-RESPONSE.md places at G0, the density review and RECORD.md's draft run beside M0's bootstrap, and their findings return as Q- items (D-PHASE-2), so a finding can change something already built.
- **Freezes.** With no external review ([owner decision 99](#od-99)), each format freezes twice: its specification at Gn-in, its bytes at Gn-out on 22.10's evidence, whose FS rows are 23.6's schedules for that gate (D-PHASE-7). At M2: §7.9's records, its presence row and §6.9's countersignature fields among them (owner decisions [185](#od-185), [187](#od-187), [189](#od-189), [192](#od-192)); format 1, whose bytes, D-PHASE-9's reservations included, also wait for D-TEST-11's nvme gate, its erasure and deposit bytes freezing on §22.5's §11 tests, FS-23 and FS-47 while FS-13, FS-23's mailbox case and FS-47's mail case keep their M7 gates; credential 0xF552, suite 0x0010 and D-KEYS-10's delivery wire (ReaderKey, KeyDelivery and gkm's wrap and recovery paths), whose bytes freeze with §22.10's 0x0010 interop artifact, a gap in any step it requires holding the freeze unless a second peer covers that step; under [owner decision 610](#od-610) that interop artifact and the MLS legs of FS-15, FS-20, FS-24 and FS-104 count toward nothing at M2: the four rows stay at M2 running their drafted schedules, whose delivery legs are M2's evidence, the gate's sweep saying in an open item what does not count, no epoch-retention resync test is built, v0 having no epochs or acks, and this line, §22.8's four rows, §22.10's table, 23.6's M2 row and D-KEYS-10 keep their MLS wording until KEYS's review-phase rework moves the rows onto deliveries ([the fold that waits with MLS's](DESIGN-DEFER.md#keys-mls); [owner decision 627](#od-627)). At M3: `record.proto`, [owner decision 142](#od-142)'s tainted-run rule and CanonicalAction's reserved field 37 included. At M6: the escrow order (D-QUOTA-9), frozen at M6's entry once FS-46 and 20.9's benchmark pass on M4's dark build, the benchmark rerunning at its exit; `directory.proto`'s announcement, request, decision and notice messages, specified at M6's Gn-in, bytes at its Gn-out. At M9: `smtpproof/SPEC.md`. At M10: format 2, with the DROP payload and `directory.proto`'s cards, its bytes also waiting for D-TEST-13's computed gate ([owner decision 174](#od-174)), repos migrating only after it (23.9); `search.proto`'s messages, types 0x1404 and 0x1405 and Hello's feature bits 0 and 1, additive to M2's wire.
- **Gn-in.** 23.6's design closure for the gate; specifications freeze; changes since G0 and §22's exit-test plan reviewed.
- **Gn-out.** Exit criteria shown, with 23.6's schedules passing, each gate's sweep naming every row's tests where they run, FS-5's, FS-73's and FS-72's rollback case's T3 tests in server's evshost, and a row reading missing until a sweep names its test ([owner decision 548](#od-548)), as each sweep names every other case whose T3 test runs outside server's sidecart3, the convention's T3 tags carrying the local stack's (§22.8's gates line; [owner decision 625](#od-625)), a case passing only with every clause registered for it ([owner decision 626](#od-626)), and a gate's list check running nothing, a row's commands and the operations matrix's alike reading listed (QD-1082); formats freeze; §22's privacy assertions pass; §2.8's list updated (I-18); `commit-msg --scan main..sidecar` clean (connect/CODESTYLE.md:83); the owner approves the deploy and merges (23.9).
- **Gates the build cannot meet.** M0-M10 build straight through in dependency order on the `sidecar` branches, with no stop at a Gn-out ([owner decision 194](#od-194)). Each gate's local checks run and are reported, and anything needing hardware, production or people stays listed open: M2's format-1 freeze on D-TEST-11's PM9A3 run, M0's and M1's stages in production, each Gn-out's approval to merge. This changes how the milestones are executed, not what freezes when: the Freezes order above still decides what may reach a production store (D-PHASE-7). Formats stay unfrozen meanwhile, so a later hardware miss can force rework in later milestones. The draft's own constant limits move into settings objects in the review phase's sweep, area by area as the review reads each area, the build's code in server, connect and sdk included, while new code follows §6's bounds and each change moves the constants in the files it touches (owner decisions [297](#od-297), [552](#od-552)).
- **Releases.** D-TRUST-3 holds; RS1's copy discloses I-10's no-policy allow-all ([owner decision 120](#od-120)); "end-to-end encrypted" waits only for D-TRUST-4's document, §21.11's canary and §2.18's unaudited-cryptography disclosure (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:932-934; owner decisions [77](#od-77), [119](#od-119)); BS1 waits for 23.6's census call and M8's mail-indexer readiness, never for a user's indexer ([owner decision 12](#od-12)).

### 23.9 Branches, merges, and the source-graph lock

1. **Publication.** sidecar is public from [owner decision 118](#od-118)'s flip (2026-11-04), as it is ([owner decision 117](#od-117)); every `sidecar` branch uses its repo's normal remote (§4.8).
2. **Merges.** At each Gn-out, every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` in §4.8's order (D-REPO-5), minio's `master` playing `main` ([owner decision 270](#od-270)), re-pinning the lock (23.3). The merge takes the commit set recorded when that gate's local checks were reported, never the tip, a later milestone's merge bringing the rest and a group's migration registration the one commit on top; connect's merge first passes `check/`'s X9 gate (§4.8); deploys, pilots and releases build from `main`, gated in `config/<env>/sidecar.yml` (D-OPS-10).
3. **Migrations.** §19.7's groups stay pending under `sidecar_pending` (D-OPS-6) until their own Gn-out registers them, and never change after (23.3), so one track's merge never applies the other's group (FS-54) and M3's pilot runs on production ([owner decision 118](#od-118)).
4. **Format 2.** After M10's Gn-out, §19.11's `format2` gate opens to internal networks and design partners; admitted networks' repos migrate as §11.6 states; the purge runs in observe mode until D-TEST-12's production soak shows no candidate a retained version names, then deletes; drops run in observe mode until D-TEST-18's soak, then delete (D-PHASE-12); D-TEST-13's production confirmation runs while the gate admits only those networks, a miss holding it there ([owner decision 174](#od-174)); and only then does the gate open by percent (D-PHASE-10).

### 23.10 Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Merges held until RS1 on private mirrors ([owner decision 107](#od-107)) | no unreleased server code public | pilot and edges wait or run on canary | rejected ([owner decision 118](#od-118)) |
| One freeze per format | one review | at Gn-in, no implementation evidence; at Gn-out, no fixed specification for M2's parallel work | rejected (D-PHASE-7) |
| Format 2 inside M6 | v1 as defined today; one fewer milestone | RS2 waits for an unrelated feature; M6 grows by ~9-12 engineer-months | not taken ([owner decision 169](#od-169)) |
| Versionless fields in format 1 at M2, their collection later with the index | the cheapest format change | the owner chose v1 with a new format ([owner decision 163](#od-163)) | ruled out |
| D-TEST-13's gate computed from M2's price table and T3's counts, confirmed on production after the freeze | no hardware bought early | a miss found after the freeze costs clusters sooner or a format change | chosen ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |
| The next cluster's 8 × PM9A3 as M10's staging set | measured before the freeze | drives bought ahead of the trigger, its model fixed early | not taken ([owner decision 174](#od-174)) |

### 23.11 Decisions proposed

**D-PHASE-1 (proposed).** Build 23.4's milestones in dependency order, straight through on the `sidecar` branches ([owner decision 194](#od-194); 23.8), staffed as 23.5 proposes, releasing each recURd stage once its last item lands. *Why:* R-PHASE-4, whose stages ship whole (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:907), and R-PHASE-10; the sections' Phasing share these dependencies; and several gates need hardware, production or people the build does not have, where stopping at each Gn-out and building M0-M2 then re-planning were not taken.

**D-PHASE-2 (proposed).** No code is written before G0, which the owner signed on 2026-11-06, its re-checks, density review and RECORD.md draft running beside M0's bootstrap ([owner decision 193](#od-193); 23.8); an unsettled blocker defers what it blocks; until the owner decides an open question, text written at its recommendation is marked "(proposed; Q-...)" (D-ARCH-4); and an implementation finding that changes a D- item returns to review as a Q- item, as do those re-checks' and that review's findings. *Why:* R-PHASE-1; owner rule 8.

**D-PHASE-3 (proposed).** §7.4's stage 1 and D-TEAM-14 reach production log-only at M0's Gn-out, so the 14 log-only days overlap M1; the desktop app and extension releases with §18.7's credential rules, then stage 2, a deploy of an api built with the tag `sidecar_stage2` that no config push turns on or off (§7.4; [owner decision 328](#od-328)), reach production before M3's pilot; until stage 2 is live, sidecar enrollment is limited to `config/<env>/sidecar.yml`'s `preview_networks`. *Why:* D-TRUST-3, kept off the critical path.

**D-PHASE-4 (proposed).** 23.7's M0 items, and §10.4's MLS subset with its X-Wing KAT, start in M0. *Why:* each is slow or unpredictable to finish, and the subset is M2's critical path (23.5).

**D-PHASE-5 (withdrawn).** Superseded by [owner decision 118](#od-118): every touched repo merges `sidecar` into `main` at each Gn-out (23.9).

**D-PHASE-6 (proposed).** The design-partner pilot starts at M3's exit; its measures (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:913-920) feed M6's entry review, which may re-plan the recURd track. *Why:* "Rework the developer hook before building the team layer" (:915).

**D-PHASE-7 (proposed).** Each frozen format freezes twice: its specification at its milestone's Gn-in and its final bytes at its Gn-out, on 22.10's evidence (23.8); no production store holds a format before its final freeze. The escrow order (D-QUOTA-9) is the one Gn-in that needs implementation evidence: M4 builds it dark, and M6's Gn-in freezes it on that build (23.8). *Why:* an entry review cannot show implementation evidence unless an earlier milestone built the code, and [owner decision 92](#od-92)'s hot-path benchmark must pass before M6's billing builds on the order; data on local, T3 and the staging cluster is rebuilt, as a canary's would be were its hosts bought ([owner decision 499](#od-499)), so a change between the two freezes costs no migration.

**D-PHASE-8 (proposed).** Format 2 is milestone M10 (23.4), built on track A from M4's exit beside M6 with its own entry and exit reviews; no recURd stage waits for it, and its hold, team, mail and phone cases run at the later of M10's exit and, respectively, M5's, M6's, M7's or M8's. *Why:* [owner decision 169](#od-169) places it, and [owner decision 163](#od-163) puts all of it in v1; RS2's items (sidecar/design/pitch5.html:897-899) do not include search, so holding RS2 for format 2's freeze would delay a release for another feature.

**D-PHASE-9 (proposed).** A format that freezes reserves the numbers a decided later format or milestone needs. Its code refuses data that uses a later format's numbers as needing that format, never as tampering; knows a reserved kind, applying its fixed kind default (the `directory` kind's readers and writers, §8.5, D-ACL-24); ignores a field that only guides writers; and from the freeze honors a reserved access limit and evaluates a reserved policy atom, as the implicit document's directory rule names `autogroup:dst-owner` from M2, Team documents from M6 (§8.4, §8.5). Format 1 reserves at M2 format 2's numbers, the drop's and the erasure cut's among them (EvsPush flags 256 and 512 and fields 33 and 34, flag 1024 joining them as a completion ERASE's before M10's freeze ([owner decision 658](#od-658)), EvsHead's index_epoch, window bit 5, the read states `drop_pending` and `dropped`, EvsReadPathState's 2 and 3, which join the reservation lint, as do the enums that name values uint32 fields carry, EvsPushFlag, EvsLocatorKind, EvsVersioning, EvsWindowFlag, SmtpPreambleCode and SmtpProofCode, which add no number, their fields staying uint32 on the wire), and M6's directory's: the `directory` kind, acl.proto's `autogroup:dst-owner` atom and `EvsShare.expires`, and config.proto's `ServiceSettings.directory` (§7.9, §8.4, §8.8, §10.5, §11); the search index's own encoding (`evsindex.proto`, sealed inside the versioning-2 files format 1 reserves), its tombstone tables and diff rules included, needs no number at M2 and freezes with format 2 at M10 (§11.14); `record.proto` reserves CanonicalAction's field 37 at M3 (§16.8); no number is reserved for keep-last-n ([owner decision 165](#od-165)). *Why:* [owner decision 163](#od-163), and the directory (owner decisions [171](#od-171), [180](#od-180)) writes into formats that freeze at M2; an upgrade must not raise fork or missing-segment alarms on older devices, a config field or atom that older devices refused would stop the network, and a reader that ignored a share's expiry would widen access.

**D-PHASE-10 (proposed).** Format 2 reaches production only after its final freeze, through §19.11's `format2` gate in 23.9's order, and deletes replaced versionless content only after D-TEST-12's soak and dropped history only after D-TEST-18's (D-PHASE-12). *Why:* D-PHASE-7's data rule; a purge or migration bug must surface on internal data first.

**D-PHASE-11 (proposed).** The directory ships at M6 on format 1: announce, request, decision, erasure request and coordination entries in its streams, read 64 to a request (§11.9), and versioned notices; its erasure takes `admin` in M2's code, as every repo's (§11.12). It moves to cards, repo files and its index with M10, its format-2 cases running at the later of M6's and M10's exits. M2 reserves its kind, atom and fields (D-PHASE-9). *Why:* [owner decision 169](#od-169) keeps RS2 off format 2, and [owner decision 170](#od-170)'s announcements need only streams.

**D-PHASE-12 (proposed).** Drop deletes reach production only after D-TEST-18's soak, through §19.11's `format2.drop` gate in 23.9's order. *Why:* as D-PHASE-10, for the costlier delete path ([owner decision 173](#od-173)).

**Q-PHASE-5.** When do external reviews run? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by owner decisions [99](#od-99), [102](#od-102)):** moot; 22.10's gates stand in. *Residual:* none.

**Q-PHASE-6.** Which burner root and label size does M8 use? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 (implied by [owner decision 32](#od-32)):** moot. *Residual:* none.

**Q-PHASE-7.** How is token expiry enforced before the first sidecar? **Decided by owner 2026-11-03 ([owner decision 103](#od-103)):** (b), D-TEAM-14's hard 7-day `exp`, shipped with the P0. **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 131](#od-131)):** only sidecar-held child and admin-refused tokens get it, and the sdk's window clients keep today's lifetime until app adoption (§7.4). *Residual:* none.

**Q-PHASE-8.** When does sidecar go public (Q-REPO-4)? **Decided by owner 2026-11-04 ([owner decision 118](#od-118)):** now, as it is ([owner decision 117](#od-117)), superseding [owner decision 107](#od-107); every touched repo merges at each Gn-out (23.9). *Residual:* none.

**Q-PHASE-9.** Where in v1 does format 2 go, and who builds it? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 169](#od-169)):** (b), its own milestone M10, on track A from M4's exit beside M6, with about three more engineers hired from M3's entry; RS2 does not wait, and M10's team-record, mail and phone cases run at the later of M10's exit and M6's, M7's or M8's (D-PHASE-8). Options (a), inside M6, and (c), after M6, were not taken; (c) stays 23.5's contingency if the hires slip, and then returns to the owner. *Residual:* none.

**Q-PHASE-10.** Cross-cutting (§19.6, §22.8). Which drives run D-TEST-13's drive-write gate before format 2's bytes freeze? **Decided by owner 2026-11-05 ([owner decision 174](#od-174)):** (b), none: the gate is projected from M2's measured price table (§22.8) and T3's operation counts with the index on in every eligible repo, then confirmed on production after format 2's freeze, while §19.11's `format2` gate admits only internal networks and design partners (23.9), by the write budget's measured-over-priced ratio staying within 10% (D-TEST-13); no staging drives are bought early, and a miss found after the freeze costs more metadata clusters sooner ([owner decision 145](#od-145)) or a later format change. Options (a), early staging drives, and (c), synthetic repos on production, were not taken. *Residual:* none.
